articles.title: 1 milliard de dollars ! TSMC prêt à investir dans Anthropic et OpenAI
articles.text:
Le géant de la fonderie des semi-conducteurs va engager des investissements dans les leaders de l'IA. Preuve de confiance, ou inquiétude d'un énième investissement circulaire ?
Si le monde de l'IA est plein d'argent aujourd'hui, c'est autant dû aux grands investisseurs institutionnels qui ont longtemps ouvert grand leurs coffres - même si ça commence à caler - qu'aux investissements consentis par ceux qui bénéficient directement de cet essor. On avait ainsi eu récemment l'exemple d'un contrat entre Anthropic et Broadcom. Et aujourd'hui, on pourrait en avoir une autre illustration avec TSMC.
TSMC veut mettre 1 milliard de dollars sur les deux géants américains de l'IA
Chez TSMC, on vit une période bénie ces dernières années grâce aux immenses commandes pour la fonderie de semi-conducteurs passées par les entreprises comme NVIDIA. Et on a confiance dans la pérennité de ce secteur du côté du géant taïwanais.
En effet, comme nous l'apprend Reuters, TSMC, qui va connaître une année faste (avec une chiffre d'affaires en hausse de 44%), va aussi investir à son tour dans les start-ups IA. Une enveloppe de 1 milliard de dollars va ainsi être allouée à l'investissement dans Anthropic et OpenAI.
Le géant taïwanais va participer à l'IPO d'Anthropic
Plus exactement, TSMC va acquérir pour 500 millions de dollars d'actions privilégiées, quand une autre enveloppe de 500 millions d'euros sera utilisée pour participer à l'IPO à venir d'Anthropic. Celle-ci devrait donner une action dont le cours sera compris entre 70 et 78 dollars, avec une valorisation qui devrait atteindre les 1 400 milliards de capitalisation.
Il faut d'ailleurs noter qu'Anthropic va, dans le même temps, lever une somme conséquente de près de 26 milliards de dollars, dans le cadre d'un placement privé distinct. Participeront notamment Microsoft, Google, NVIDIA ou AMD - soit autant de parties prenantes de l'explosion de l'intelligence artificielle. Jusqu'à quel point ce genre de financements seront-ils considérés comme de simples investissements, et non pas des investissements circulaires ?
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Blind Eagle Uses Fake Court Notices to Deliver Remote Access Trojan Across Latin America
articles.text:
The threat actor known as Blind Eagle has resurfaced with a new campaign targeting organizations in Latin America through judicial and administrative-themed phishing lures to deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) that shares its lineage with AsyncRAT and DCRat.
"The campaign uses Portuguese and Spanish lures that resemble court notifications, fiscalía notices, tutela proceedings, and administrative documents," Zenox said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
Assessed to be a Spanish-speaking group and active since 2018, Blind Eagle (aka APT-C-36) has a track record of using spear-phishing lures to distribute commodity RATs like AsyncRAT, BitRAT, Lime RAT, NjRAT, Quasar RAT, and Remcos RAT.
Attack chains begin with phishing emails targeting individuals who handle cases, contracts, judicial, or institutional service requests to trick them into opening a malware-laced attachment.
One email containing a Colombian judicial-themed XHTML file has been identified as a weaponized Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) image that renders a bogus web page impersonating Colombia's Fiscalía General de la Nación, also referred to as the Office of the Attorney General.
The web page, for its part, employs a technique known as HTML smuggling to assemble the next-stage ZIP archive payload locally in the web browser using ZipCrypto, thereby circumventing email security controls.
Present within the ZIP archive is a JavaScript dropper that masquerades as Network Configuration Auditor version 2.7.298. The JavaScript code conducts environment reconnaissance, and collects details such as system version, network profile, installation date, memory size, computer name, environment variables, and directories localized in Portuguese and Spanish.
Upon execution, it launches a Visual Basic Script that performs Windows Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) and Event Tracing for Windows (ETW) bypass, while displaying a fake criminal-citation page as a distraction mechanism.
In parallel, the malware also takes steps to delete the original XHTML artifact, clears Mark of the Web (MotW) metadata, and sets up persistence on the host under the Windows Startup folder so that it's automatically executed on system startup.
The attack culminates with the use of PowerShell to decode and launch the final RAT payload in memory. The trojan is an AsyncRAT fork with DCRat lineage based on code structure, configuration, build characteristics, and observed behavior.
"The targeting of judicial, fiscal, administrative and educational organizations gives the operation access to highly sensitive legal, financial and institutional information," Zenox said.
"Combined with the Portuguese and Spanish lures, Brazilian infrastructure, operational timezone and regional victimology, these elements establish the campaign as an APT-C-36 operation conducted through a Brazilian operational cluster."
Zenox told The Hacker News that it could not confirm whether any of these attacks had succeeded against real-world targets. However, during the campaign period between late October and early November 2026, it observed a large-scale wave of targeted phishing involving nearly 3,300 malicious emails.
While not all of these messages targeted organizations in Colombia, the country continues to remain a priority target for Blind Eagle for a combination of reasons.
"The repeated targeting of Colombia likely reflects multiple factors, with one of the main enabling factors being the structural vulnerabilities and uneven security maturity across parts of the country's critical, public, financial, and private-sector infrastructure," Zenox security researcher Gabriel Alves said.
"These conditions may increase the likelihood of successful compromises and offer greater opportunities to monetize access, steal sensitive data or funds, or reuse compromised credentials against critical systems. This is further supported by regional actors' familiarity with the Colombian context and is consistent with patterns observed among Latin American threat actors."
(The story was updated after publication to include additional insights from Zenox.)

articles.title: ‘Get you out of your device and back to your vacation’ — Disney’s new AI experiment with Ray-Ban Meta could change how you explore Disneyland
articles.text:
‘Get you out of your device and back to your vacation’ — Disney’s new AI experiment could change how you explore Disneyland, whether you’re using an iPhone, Ray-Ban Metas, or AirPods
It's coming soon for Magic Key Holders first
- Disney's new AI guide could make navigating Disneyland easier
- Works with Ray-Ban Metas, AirPods, and your iPhone
- Coming soon in beta for Magic Key holders through Imagineering Labs
When you're at a Disney park, or really any theme park, the idea is to be immersed in the experience, right? But there's also no sugarcoating the fact that a phone, especially one equipped with the Disneyland app, My Disney Experience for Walt Disney World, or any other park app, is pretty essential for planning and making the most of your day.
The app is essentially the brain of your visit, letting you check wait times for attractions, meet-and-greets, and other experiences, but also helping you find your way to food — I mean, we're all after a corn dog or a churro, right? — other services, and entertainment. But as we've heard from Disney Parks leaders in the past, constantly looking down at your phone can break the immersion.
Now, we're getting a glimpse at a potential alternative, and it's coming soon for a select group of Disneyland guests through a new Disney Imagineering app that's set to offer a rare peek behind the curtain.
Dubbed Imagineering Labs, the opt-in experience won't replace the main Disneyland app, but it will give guests the chance to try select experiences before they're fully developed or even guaranteed to launch. It's a pretty exciting approach, especially since feedback from guests could help shape what Imagineers ultimately bring to life.
The first experiment is an augmented reality Star Wars adventure called Secrets of the Spire, which is decidedly entertainment-focused and uses your iPhone's camera to overlay digital elements onto the environment and trigger physical reactions throughout Galaxy's Edge.
But the Disneyland Enchanted Guide is a bit more utility-focused, and it's seriously piquing my interest. It's an AI-powered assistant that lets you ask questions in natural language, like, 'Where's the nearest Dole Whip?' 'How long is the wait for Rise of the Resistance right now?' or whether you should come back later if the line is too long. It's also multimodal, meaning you can point your phone's camera at something in the park and ask about it.
Asa Kalama, Vice President and Executive Creative Director at Walt Disney Imagineering, described the thinking behind it to TechRadar: “Some of us are lucky enough to have that, you know, big Disney Parks fan as a friend, and there's no better park-going adventure than alongside them. They know all the tips, they know all the tricks, they can help you navigate your day. Well, what if we were able to provide that to every single guest that came to the park?”
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
And that's really the idea here. Rather than digging through menus or bouncing between different parts of an app, you can simply ask the Enchanted Guide and get an answer.
The interface is pretty neat, too. Rather than a traditional chatbot screen, the Enchanted Guide puts a familiar Disneyland map front and center, complete with attraction wait times and a glowing Mickey-shaped button at the bottom for asking questions. There are also buttons to type or use your camera, and the Guide can take into account your location, plans, and details you choose to share to make its recommendations more useful throughout the day.
It's using a combination of AI models to power the intelligence behind the Enchanted Guide, but there's been a whole host of customizations to make it feel uniquely Disney. Kalama explained that the team has worked to ensure the information comes from Disney's trusted sources, including real-time park information, and is delivered in a way that feels like the Disney voice, both literally and figuratively. From the pre-recorded preview I saw, it almost feels like chatting with a Cast Member you might stop on Main Street.
It gets even more interesting, though, when you can use another device to interact with it.
You might recall that at Meta Connect 2025, Disney Imagineering showed off an early tease of an experience at Disneyland using Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses, letting guests look at their surroundings, ask questions, and hear responses through the glasses. And while that was just an early glimpse, the Disneyland Enchanted Guide is bringing that idea to life, letting you interact with Disney's new AI assistant without constantly reaching for your phone.
Essentially, you can connect the Disneyland Enchanted Guide within the Imagineering Labs app to compatible Meta smart glasses using Meta's Wearables Device Access Toolkit. Once that's enabled and you're rocking the shades, you can chat with the Guide through the glasses without necessarily needing to pull out your connected phone.
The Enchanted Guide can make use of the glasses' microphones, speakers, and cameras. That means you could look at an attraction, ask about it, and get real-time information without even knowing its name.
Speaking with TechRadar, Chris Barbour, Director, Content & Ecosystem, Meta, explained that the partnership with Disney Imagineering started with a pretty simple idea: “The best of keep me immersed, keep me not having to look down at my phone, but also give me all the advantages of the technology being present for me.”
As Chris explained, one of his favorite parts is “being able to look at an attraction and get real-time information about that,” with the Guide using what the camera sees to understand what you're asking about.
On paper, and without having tested it yet, that could be incredibly handy within the park.
For instance, Asa shared a few examples, from checking the current wait time for an attraction to something a little more useful, like getting an alert when that wait drops below a certain threshold.
“Can you let me know when Dumbo the Flying Elephant has a wait time of under 10 minutes?”
The Enchanted Guide could then deliver a notification when that condition is met, leaving you free to enjoy other parts of the park in the meantime.
Imagine if it could also remind you when your next Lightning Lane reservation is coming up or if a slot opens for an attraction you want to experience. That's the kind of functionality I'd love to see. While Asa didn't confirm either capability, he did note that some features, including actually making Lightning Lane reservations, still live within the core Disneyland app. For now, the Enchanted Guide can explain how Lightning Lanes work, but will send you over to the main app when it's time to book one.
“There are certain capabilities that are on our roadmap that aren't yet currently implemented,” Kalama explained.
And while the Meta Ray-Ban integration is especially interesting, you don't necessarily need smart glasses to go hands-free with the Enchanted Guide. Bluetooth earbuds, including Apple's AirPods, will also work, letting you keep your iPhone tucked away while exploring Disneyland. AirPods won't support multi-modal on their own, as they don't have cameras ... yet.
Of course, wearing camera-equipped smart glasses in the parks could raise some privacy concerns. Meta Ray-Ban glasses have a built-in capture LED that indicates when the camera is in use, but that might not be immediately obvious to everyone around you. Guests are already accustomed to seeing phones and earbuds throughout the parks, so just be prepared for some looks.
There will even be a dedicated wake word for the Enchanted Guide, though it's still being finalized ahead of launch. That means you won't need to pull out your phone and tap the Mickey-shaped microphone button every time you want to ask a question. I'm especially curious to see what Disney lands on for the wake word.
And given that this is an AI assistant capable of understanding images and voice prompts, privacy is another important consideration. Both prompts and images are processed and then deleted, and the Enchanted Guide doesn't support video. So while it can use a camera to understand what you're looking at, it isn't designed to continuously analyze a live video feed.
Of course, this is still an experiment, and there's plenty we don't know about how well it will all work. I'm especially curious to see how quickly the Enchanted Guide responds, how accurately it understands what's happening around you, and whether it really can make navigating Disneyland easier.
And we'll have to wait a little longer to find out.
The Disneyland Enchanted Guide is still listed as coming soon within Imagineering Labs, and when it does launch, it'll initially be limited to Disneyland Magic Key holders. The experience will live within the Imagineering Labs app, where you'll sign in with your Disney account. With an eligible Magic Key linked to your profile, you'll be able to access the Guide once it's available for testing.
There will likely be some bugs, hiccups, or slowdowns along the way, but that's part of the whole Imagineering Labs approach. Rather than waiting until an experience is completely finished, Disney is opening up the development process and letting guests help shape what comes next.
A wider rollout is planned, though there's no firm date just yet, and for now, this is very much a Disneyland-focused experience.
But the goal behind it all is one that I think makes a lot of sense.
As Kalama put it, “The goal here really is to keep you invested and engaged with the physical world around you and the friends and family that you've brought to the park, to get you out of your device and back to your vacation as quickly as possible.”
And that's what has me excited about the Disneyland Enchanted Guide. Disney isn't trying to replace the magic of being in the parks with another screen or another digital experience. Instead, it's exploring how technology can help you make the most of your day without constantly having to reach for your smartphone.
There's still plenty to prove, especially when it comes to how well the AI works in a busy, sometimes unpredictable theme park environment. But if Disney can pull this off, the Enchanted Guide could become the kind of park companion you don't realize you need until you've spent a day with it.
And if it means more time enjoying Disneyland and less time staring at my iPhone, I'm all for it.

articles.title: Truco para duplicar la pantalla de un Android en cualquier televisor sin cable HDMI
articles.text:
Duplicar la pantalla de un celular Android en un televisor sin cable HDMI ni aplicaciones externas es posible cuando ambos dispositivos cuentan con funciones de transmisión inalámbrica y comparten la misma red WiFi.
Una función nativa en el teléfono permite llevar a la pantalla grande videos, diapositivas, películas, juegos y otros contenidos del teléfono. A la par, hay funciones propias dentro de aplicaciones como YouTube y Netflix, que envían el contenido al televisor sin mostrar necesariamente toda la interfaz del celular.
Qué se necesita para duplicar la pantalla de un Android al TV
El primer requisito es que el celular Android y el Smart TV están conectados a la misma red WiFi. Si cada dispositivo utiliza una conexión distinta, el teléfono no podrá detectar el televisor ni iniciar la transmisión.
El televisor debe incluir alguna tecnología de conexión inalámbrica, como Chromecast integrado, Miracast o compatibilidad con DLNA. Muchos modelos recientes de Samsung, LG, Sony, Philips, TCL y Hisense incorporan alguna de estas opciones, aunque las funciones disponibles pueden variar según el modelo y el sistema operativo.
Dónde está la opción “Emitir” en Android
En la mayoría de los teléfonos Android, la función aparece como “Emitir”, “Cast”, “Transmitir pantalla” o un nombre similar. Para encontrarla, hay que deslizar desde la parte superior de la pantalla hacia abajo y abrir el menú de accesos rápidos, donde suele figurar un ícono de rectángulo con ondas en una esquina.
Si el acceso no aparece de inmediato, es posible que esté oculto entre los botones disponibles. En ese caso, se puede editar el panel de accesos rápidos y agregarlo. Algunos fabricantes incluyen esta función dentro de Ajustes, en los apartados Conexiones, Dispositivos conectados o Pantalla.
Cómo conectar el celular al televisor
Al tocar “Emitir”, el teléfono buscará los televisores compatibles dentro de la red doméstica. El nombre del dispositivo debería aparecer en una lista pocos segundos después. Para evitar confusiones, se debe verificar el nombre configurado en el Smart TV antes de seleccionar una opción.
Tras elegir el televisor, Android puede solicitar una confirmación en la pantalla grande o en el celular. Cuando se aprueba la conexión, la imagen del teléfono se proyecta en el televisor. Desde ese momento, se pueden abrir aplicaciones, reproducir videos o mostrar una presentación desde el celular.
Cuáles opciones tienen las aplicaciones del celular para proyectar pantalla
YouTube cuenta con una función propia para enviar un video al televisor. Dentro del reproductor, el ícono de transmisión aparece como una pequeña pantalla con ondas. Al pulsarlo, la aplicación muestra los televisores, dispositivos Chromecast y otros dispositivos compatibles que detecta en la red WiFi.
Una vez elegido el TV, el contenido se reproduce directamente en la pantalla grande y el celular queda como control remoto. Desde allí se puede pausar, adelantar, retroceder, modificar el volumen o elegir otro video. Este método evita que las notificaciones y otras aplicaciones del teléfono aparezcan en el televisor.
Asimismo, la aplicación de Netflix ofrece un sistema parecido. Al abrir una serie, una película o un documental, suele aparecer el ícono de transmisión en la esquina superior derecha. Al tocarlo, el teléfono busca los dispositivos conectados a la misma red y muestra las alternativas disponibles.
Después de seleccionar el televisor, la reproducción pasa a la pantalla grande y el móvil permite gestionar la reproducción. El usuario puede pausar el contenido, cambiar de episodio, activar subtítulos o ajustar el volumen desde el celular. La plataforma envía el material de forma directa al televisor compatible.
Qué hacer si el nombre del Smart TV no aparece o la conexión falla
Si el Smart TV no figura en la lista, el primer paso es comprobar que ambos dispositivos utilicen la misma red WiFi. Puede ser útil reiniciar el teléfono, apagar y encender el televisor o desactivar la conexión WiFi durante unos segundos antes de volver a conectarla.
La estabilidad de la red influye en la calidad de la transmisión. Una conexión débil puede provocar cortes, demoras o pérdida de imagen. Siempre que esté disponible, conviene utilizar una red de 5 GHz, que suele ofrecer mayor velocidad y menos interferencias que una de 2,4 GHz.

articles.title: New 'BluePhishing' scam sees criminals spoof AI agents to get access to corporate environments
articles.text:
New 'BluePhishing' scam sees criminals spoof AI agents to get access to corporate environments
Be careful which agents you approve
- Researchers showed Microsoft Entra Agent ID blueprints can be abused to socially engineer malicious AI agents into organizations
- A single approved blueprint can spawn hundreds of agent identities with access to corporate resources
- Defenders should restrict third-party agent consent, apply least-privilege controls, and monitor agent creation events
When Microsoft first introduced Entra Agent ID as a way organizations can identify and monitor AI agents, it most certainly did not think it would be used to smuggle malicious agents into corporate environments. Yet, that’s where we are today.
Entra Agent ID is an extension of Microsoft Entra. It’s a system that allows companies to create AI agents, give them digital identities, and then decide which services and what data they can access. Expecting organizations to deploy dozens (if not hundreds) of these agents, Microsoft also introduced “agent blueprints”, essentially templates companies can use to create multiple AI agent identities, each with their own permissions.
In a new report, security researchers Proofpoint laid out how a threat actor could create a malicious blueprint in their own Microsoft environment and then - using classic social engineering techniques - convince a victim to approve it in their own environment. To make matters worse, when a malicious agent enters the environment, they can “clone” themselves, creating multiple additional identities, all tasked with doing different things.
How the attack plays out
Proofpoint found the attack starts with the attacker setting up a blueprint in a Microsoft Entra environment they control. They can configure its credentials and the permissions they want it to receive and also make sure it can be authorized by other organizations.
Then, they create a link that leads to a genuine Microsoft authorization page. Unlike your run-of-the-mill phishing attack, this one is different because the login page doesn’t need to be fake and spoofed. The attacker does, however, need to have some basic information about the target organization, such as their tenant ID and details about an existing user they can specifically target.
Then comes the fun part: the victim is presented with the link (this can be done via email, social networks, instant messaging platforms) which asks them to approve the blueprint and its permissions. The link is legitimate, and so is the popup prompting the approval - nothing suggests this is actually a highly sophisticated phishing scam.
If they click the link and approve the blueprint, the malicious AI is added inside their organization.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The higher-authority the target - the bigger the potential damage, since for organization-wide application permissions, the person approving must have the necessary admin privileges. Ordinary users may be able to approve certain delegated permissions, depending on company policy.
One of the first things the AI agent receives, once installed, is a permission called AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager. This allows the threat actor to create additional identities linked to the blueprint that’s now inside their target’s environment. A single blueprint can support up to 250 agent identities, which means there can be a swarm of malicious bots running around at the same time.
Raising awareness while limiting access privilege
The attacker then obtains access tokens for those identities, making them valid members of the company with approved access to different resources which they can then exfiltrate as they please.
“Organizations should raise user awareness of the risks associated with agent consent, particularly when granting permissions to ‘third-party’ agents from untrusted sources,” Proofpoint warned. “Much like user consent settings limit users from granting consent to third-party apps, these settings also extend to agent blueprints and their agent identities.”
Proofpoint stressed agent blueprint ID is consistent across all tenants that give their consent, which is a common indicator to detect or remove known malicious agents. Applying the principle of least privilege will help limit the impact, the researchers concluded, utilizing controls like Conditional Access policies for agents and Entra ID protection for agents. “For monitoring, agent and blueprint events are surfaced in the audit log, in a similar way to app consent operations,” the report concludes.

articles.title: Fireworks AI Confirms Wider Breach Affecting Customer Datasets, Model Weights and Notion AI Chats
articles.text:
Fireworks AI disclosed on Monday that its investigation into a security incident first reported early last month uncovered further malicious activity, affecting account and billing information, alongside secrets, datasets, and incomplete models for a "limited set of accounts."
In a notice published on October 10, 2026, the company said it detected unauthorized use of internal Fireworks credentials that allowed an unauthorized third-party to access environment variables used in evaluation jobs in a limited number of customer accounts. The activity was detected on October 6, 2026, at 9 a.m. PDT.
At that time, the AI infrastructure provider said it only found evidence that environment variables, including API keys and tokens stored as secrets, were captured in certain affected accounts, adding that there were no signs that customer models, datasets, training data, inference traffic, or personal information were accessed.
In response to the incident, Fireworks AI took the step of revoking the compromised internal credentials and rotating service account tokens, along with affected Fireworks API keys and keys created by the threat actor.
The latest bulletin from the company reveals that the scope of the breach may have been broader than previously thought. The company said attackers reached its development environment via an unnamed third-party cloud provider that hosted Fireworks research and development (R&D) machines on October 23, 2026.
"On October 24, the unauthorized third party used it to reach Fireworks development machines and then run an unauthorized workload that led to additional customer data impact," it added. "As of October 25, we have not detected further evidence of successful unauthorized access by the threat actor on the Fireworks platform customers use."
The breach is said to have provided access to the following types of information -
- Resource metadata: Fireworks resource identifiers, display names, descriptions, and creation time
- Billing information: billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment history, account balance, and credit usage
- Model weights and datasets: a subset of incomplete model weights and datasets for certain customers
Fireworks AI said payment card numbers are not stored by the company and were not impacted by the security incident. It also said it's alerting customers whose data was impacted.
The company also noted that it has implemented security hardening procedures, such as credential revocation and rotation; isolating affected systems to prevent further unauthorized activity and lateral movement; tightening access controls; and improving its logging and monitoring systems.
"The evidence indicates links to a cybercriminal threat actor group, which is financially motivated and aimed at selling tokens from unauthorized access to large language models (LLMs) to illicit routing gateways," it said.
The activity is assessed to be part of an emerging threat known as LLMjacking, which refers to the act of hijacking a victim's LLM through stolen credentials to fuel a criminal enterprise that thrives on peddling the access to other threat actors, while leaving the legitimate owner to pay the bill.
Last week, Google issued a warning that threat actors are increasingly targeting AI infrastructure for LLMjacking in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors.
Notion Impacted by Fireworks AI Incident
Popular productivity and note-taking application Notion has disclosed that the security incident targeting Fireworks AI impacted "fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces." In a post shared on Reddit, one user said: "looks like all of us are part of that <1%."
While the initial assessment was that the breach allowed the threat actor to access Notion AI synthetic testing data, it has since come to light that it may also have involved potential customer data.
"Upon analysis of the new data, we discovered that it included Notion AI chat transcripts used for the Insights feature, which for the vast majority of impacted workspaces were unattributable," it said. "'Unattributable' means the chats weren't labeled with who wrote them or which workspace they came from, and the transcripts did not contain tool call results."
Notion has also emphasized that no other features across its platform were affected by the incident. The Insights feature has since been disabled as it continues to investigate the breach and the company is no longer serving open-weight models through Fireworks.
Affected customers are advised to review the impacted data securely inside their workspace. If those with affected workspaces have pasted sensitive information, passwords, API keys, or other credentials during the attack window, it's recommended to rotate them with immediate effect.

articles.title: Et si l'IA pouvait prouver qu'un logiciel est sécurisé ? Google DeepMind a tenté l'expérience avec Signal
articles.text:
Durant quatre semaines, Google DeepMind a utilisé une nouvelle IA pour vérifier plusieurs garanties cryptographiques du protocole Signal. Une expérience qui pourrait changer la manière dont les chercheurs contrôlent la sécurité des logiciels.
On peut tester un programme des milliers de fois sans avoir exploré tous les scénarios possibles. Alors comment s’assurer qu’il respecte bien les garanties de sécurité qu’on attend de lui ? En produisant des preuves mathématiques. C’est le principe de la vérification formelle, une méthode qui existe depuis longtemps. Sauf que ces démonstrations représentent une somme de travail considérable. Google DeepMind a donc voulu savoir si l’IA pouvait accélérer les choses, en choisissant un terrain d’essai de taille : le protocole de chiffrement Signal, utilisé pour protéger les communications de Signal, WhatsApp et Google Messages.

Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Le protocole Signal à l’épreuve d’AlphaProof Code
Pour relever le défi, les chercheurs ont utilisé AlphaProof Code, un nouveau système reposant sur des agents IA capables de participer à la construction de démonstrations mathématiques. Leur mission n’était pas de chercher des failles dans Signal, mais d’aider à prouver que plusieurs propriétés de son chiffrement étaient bien respectées, y compris dans le code chargé de les appliquer. Car un protocole peut être correctement conçu sur le plan théorique et présenter malgré tout des erreurs dans son implémentation.
DeepMind a donc travaillé sur une version compilée de libsignal, la bibliothèque de référence du protocole, pour pousser les vérifications jusqu’au code machine. Les agents chargés des preuves, reposant sur Gemini 4 Carbon, ont pu explorer différentes pistes, revenir sur leurs erreurs et ajuster leurs raisonnements, sous la supervision des chercheurs aux étapes décisives. Les preuves obtenues ont ensuite été contrôlées par Lean, un logiciel capable d’en vérifier la validité mathématique.
Les résultats se sont révélés encourageants. Selon WIRED, il n’a fallu que quatre semaines à DeepMind pour démontrer plusieurs garanties cryptographiques essentielles du protocole, parmi lesquelles la confidentialité des messages, l’authentification des correspondants et certaines protections en cas de compromission des clés, sans découvrir de nouvelle vulnérabilité dans les parties examinées.
Pour pousser l’expérience plus loin, l’équipe a ensuite réintroduit dans le code de Signal deux anciennes vulnérabilités, corrigées depuis longtemps. L’outil a alors permis de démontrer mathématiquement que les versions ainsi modifiées ne respectaient plus les garanties de sécurité examinées.
Les chercheurs ont néanmoins bénéficié d’un point de départ précieux. Des travaux de vérification formelle existaient déjà sur certaines parties du protocole Signal. DeepMind a donc pu s’appuyer sur ces analyses pour étendre les démonstrations à son implémentation, jusqu’alors beaucoup plus difficile à vérifier.
Une avancée prometteuse, mais pas un certificat de sécurité universel
Il serait toutefois exagéré d’en conclure que Google a mathématiquement prouvé l’absence de vulnérabilités dans Signal. La vérification formelle porte sur des propriétés précises, dans un cadre défini à l’avance, et dépend des hypothèses retenues pour construire les preuves. Dans le cas de Signal, les chercheurs ont notamment supposé que certaines fonctions cryptographiques étaient sûres, sans vérifier directement leur code. Une preuve valide garantit donc le respect des propriétés examinées dans ces conditions, mais ne dit rien des éventuelles failles dans les fonctions qui n’ont pas été analysées.
Les chercheurs n'ont d’ailleurs pas vérifié l’application Signal dans son ensemble. Leurs démonstrations concernent les échanges individuels, sans couvrir les conversations de groupe ni les usages sur plusieurs appareils. Certaines garanties de résistance aux attaques quantiques restent également en dehors du périmètre vérifié. Ils n'ont pas non plus examiné WhatsApp ou Google Messages, même si les deux messageries utilisent ce protocole pour chiffrer leurs échanges.
Les chercheurs de DeepMind espèrent désormais utiliser cette méthode pour contrôler des logiciels entiers, ainsi que les programmes et bibliothèques dont ils dépendent. De telles preuves pourraient ainsi servir aux banques et aux organisations qui exploitent des systèmes critiques pour confirmer mathématiquement le respect d’exigences de sécurité précises. Mais cela suppose qu’AlphaProof Code puisse examiner des logiciels beaucoup plus volumineux, ce qui reste à démontrer. Google n’a pas non plus communiqué le coût de l’expérience menée sur Signal, ni même indiqué si l’outil pourrait un jour être proposé aux entreprises.
Les spécifications et les preuves produites durant ces quatre semaines ont toutefois été publiées en accès libre. D’autres équipes peuvent désormais les examiner, reproduire les vérifications et évaluer plus précisément la portée des résultats annoncés par DeepMind.

articles.title: GTA 6 ya se puede descargar en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S: necesitarás 212 GB de espacio libre
articles.text:
Los jugadores que reservaron digitalmente Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) ya pueden descargarlo en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games habilitó la precarga para que los usuarios adelanten la instalación y estén listos cuando el juego se estrene el 19 de noviembre. El título requiere hasta 212 GB de espacio disponible, según el dispositivo.
La descarga anticipada no permite jugar antes del lanzamiento. Los archivos del juego se instalan en la consola, pero el acceso se habilitará en la fecha oficial. La precarga busca reducir la cantidad de contenido que deberá descargarse ese día y puede ayudar a evitar que los jugadores tengan que esperar mientras se baja el juego completo.
Rockstar anunció que la precarga para PlayStation 5 comenzó a la medianoche local del 10 de noviembre. En Xbox Series X|S, la ventana de inicio se estableció para ese mismo día a las 00:00 GMT, según la información de la compañía. Los horarios pueden corresponder a momentos distintos según la zona horaria.
Qué es la precarga y cuándo se podrá jugar
La precarga permite descargar e instalar un juego antes de su fecha de estreno. En el caso de GTA 6, quienes tienen una reserva digital pueden adelantar la descarga de sus archivos y esperar a que se desbloquee el acceso el 19 de noviembre. Es posible que el día del lanzamiento todavía sea necesario descargar una actualización o archivos adicionales.
La preparación puede resultar útil para quienes cuentan con una conexión lenta o tienen que compartir la red con otras personas. También evita comenzar desde cero la instalación en medio de la alta demanda que suele acompañar a un lanzamiento esperado. Sin embargo, la precarga no garantiza que no haya demoras por problemas de conexión, actualizaciones pendientes o saturación de los servicios.
El juego solo podrá iniciarse cuando llegue la hora de lanzamiento correspondiente a la región del usuario. Por tanto, tener los archivos instalados no equivale a obtener acceso anticipado: el desbloqueo se mantiene ligado a la fecha oficial.
Cómo preparar la consola
Para descargar el juego, el usuario debe haber reservado la versión digital con la cuenta de PlayStation o Xbox que utilizará para jugar. También necesita comprobar que dispone de espacio suficiente. Rockstar indica que el requisito puede llegar a 212 GB, aunque el tamaño exacto puede variar según el dispositivo.
En PS5, la descarga debería aparecer en la biblioteca del usuario, dentro de la colección de juegos o en la página de la reserva. Si está activada la descarga automática, la consola debe permanecer encendida o en modo de reposo para que pueda instalar los archivos. PlayStation también recomienda tener disponible el espacio requerido antes de que comience el proceso.
En Xbox Series X|S, la opción de instalación estará disponible para las cuentas que hayan reservado el título. Conviene verificar que las descargas automáticas estén habilitadas y dejar la consola encendida o en suspensión, además de revisar el almacenamiento interno o la unidad compatible.
El espacio puede ser el principal obstáculo
Los 212 GB representan una parte considerable del almacenamiento de una consola, especialmente si ya hay varios juegos instalados. Quienes necesiten liberar espacio pueden borrar títulos o aplicaciones que no utilicen y volver a descargarlos más adelante, siempre que los datos guardados estén sincronizados o respaldados.
Rockstar recomienda reservar el juego mediante canales autorizados y revisar las instrucciones de instalación correspondientes a cada plataforma. Con la precarga completada, los jugadores podrán iniciar GTA 6 cuando se habilite el acceso el 19 de noviembre, siempre que la consola tenga los archivos necesarios y conexión a internet para las actualizaciones que puedan publicarse.

articles.title: Smart locks and cameras don’t have to be a hassle — Wyze just launched a lock that you can install with just a Philips screwdriver, plus a solar security camera that stays charged on just an hour of sunlight per day
articles.text:
Wyze just launched a smart lock that you can install in moments with a Philips screwdriver, plus a solar security camera that stays charged on an hour of sunlight per day — and they're both surprisingly cheap
- The smart Wyze Lever Lock is easy to install, and has built-in Wi-Fi
- The 2K Wyze Solar Cam comes bundled with a photovoltaic panel
- Both are affordably priced, and subscription plans aren't mandatory
Installing smart locks can be a hassle — you often have to drill new holes in your door, and usually spend time setting up a separate Wi-Fi hub to connect the lock to your home network too. It doesn't have to be that way, though.
Wyze — a tech company that's made a name for itself in affordable home security — has launched a new lever-operated smart lock that you can fit with nothing but a Philips screwdriver. Just unscrew your existing door handle, screw the Wyze Lever Lock into place, and you're done.
Most of the best smart locks we've tested here at TechRadar are deadbolts designed for your front door, but the Wyze Lever Lock is made for the other entryways that you might actually use more often, such as garage-entry doors and side entrances. You can use it on internal doors too, so you can protect your home office (and any expensive IT equipment and sensitive documents therein).
Your opening options include a fingerprint scanner (which Wyze claims will release the lock in 0.5 seconds), a touch-sensitive numeric keypad, and a pair of physical backup keys for emergencies.
The Smart Lever Lock has built-in Wi-Fi connectivity, so there's no need for an additional hub, and runs for 12 months using eight AA batteries. It's available now for $99.98 direct from Wyze, with free shipping.
2K recording, no wires
So you've secured your doors — now what about home surveillance? Wyze has you covered there as well. Last month the company launched a wireless outdoor security camera that you can fit anywhere, and is powered by just an hour of sunlight per day.
The Wyze Solar Cam comes bundled with a photovoltaic panel, which you can mount right beside the camera or up to 10 feet away so it catches as much sunlight as possible.

The camera has impressive recording chops too, streaming 2K video footage in wide dynamic range, revealing extra detail in bright areas and deep shadows.
Like the Lever Smart Lock, the camera is surprisingly affordable, with a list price of just $69.98 for a single camera direct from Wyze. If you don't need the solar panel, you can pick up the camera by itself for $59.98. Best of all, there's no monthly subscription necessary, though if you want cloud recording and AI features, plans start at $2.99 per month.

articles.title: TSMC, el mayor fabricante de chips del mundo, invertirá hasta USD 1.000 millones en Anthropic y OpenAI
articles.text:
El directorio de TSMC, el mayor fabricante de chips por contrato del mundo, aprobó el 10 de noviembre invertir hasta USD 500 millones en acciones de Anthropic y hasta USD 500 millones en acciones preferentes de OpenAI. Así lo señaló la empresa en un documento presentado ante el regulador bursátil de Estados Unidos.
En el caso de Anthropic, la compra se hará al precio de su oferta pública inicial, es decir, el valor al que las acciones se venden por primera vez al público. En el de OpenAI, serán acciones preferentes, que dan prioridad en el cobro de dividendos frente a las comunes.
Los montos son topes: el documento dice que la inversión en cada una no superará los USD 500 millones. La misma reunión autorizó hasta USD 500 millones para crear una sociedad de inversión estratégica en la industria de semiconductores y su entorno.
Asimismo, el directorio aprobó asignaciones de capital por unos USD 40.927 millones, sobre todo para ampliar la capacidad de fabricación y empaquetado de chips, construir plantas e invertir en investigación durante 2027.
Coincide con el debut de Anthropic en bolsa
El anuncio llega el día en que Anthropic fijó el rango de precio de su debut en bolsa en USD 70 a USD 78 por acción, lo que implica un valor de hasta USD 1,4 billones, según Reuters. La agencia lo describió como uno de los mayores estrenos bursátiles registrados.
La empresa que desarrolla Claude reúne USD 26.000 millones en una colocación privada, con inversores como Google, Nvidia, AMD y Microsoft, según Reuters. TSMC se suma a ese grupo como accionista de uno de los dos laboratorios.
TSMC fabrica los chips que usan las principales empresas de IA, entre ellas Nvidia, cuyos procesadores gráficos sostienen buena parte de los modelos actuales. Nikkei Asia señaló que la compañía rara vez invirtió en clientes, proveedores u otros actores de su entorno.
Reuters interpretó el movimiento como una señal de confianza en la demanda de largo plazo por la inteligencia artificial (IA), incluso mientras crecen las dudas sobre el gasto en esa tecnología. TSMC pasará de abastecer la infraestructura a ser dueña de parte de dos de los desarrolladores más influyentes.
Una empresa con ganancias récord
En su informe del tercer trimestre de 2026, TSMC declaró ingresos consolidados por NT$1,49 billones (dólares taiwaneses) y una ganancia neta de NT$763.060 millones. El directorio también aprobó un dividendo en efectivo de NT$9 por acción para ese período.
El mes pasado, la compañía declaró una sexta ganancia récord consecutiva y dijo que la demanda de chips para IA seguía siendo “extremadamente sólida”, según Reuters. Prevé un crecimiento de ingresos de cerca del 44% en 2026 y afirmó que la demanda supera su capacidad de producción.
Para 2027, en cambio, la empresa adoptó una perspectiva más prudente. Tiene en marcha una inversión de USD 265.000 millones en plantas en Arizona y evalúa proyectos en Texas.
El dividendo aprobado se pagará el 8 de abril de 2027 a los accionistas que figuren en el registro al 17 de marzo, según el documento presentado por TSMC.
Qué buscaría TSMC al convertirse en accionista de OpenAI y Anthropic
La decisión amplía la posición de la compañía dentro de la cadena tecnológica. La empresa taiwanesa ya produce chips para compañías como Nvidia, cuyos procesadores gráficos se utilizan para entrenar y ejecutar modelos de inteligencia artificial.
Con las inversiones tendrá participación en dos desarrolladores de modelos de IA que concentran buena parte de la competencia.
La operación ocurre mientras TSMC acelera sus desembolsos para aumentar su capacidad de fabricación y empaquetado de semiconductores. El directorio aprobó asignaciones por USD 40.927 millones para 2027 y la compañía mantiene proyectos industriales en Estados Unidos, incluida una inversión de USD 265.000 millones en Arizona y posibles instalaciones en Texas.

articles.title: Binance Warns of iOS Sandbox Escape That Could Expose Crypto Wallet Keys, No Fix Confirmed
articles.text:
An iOS sandbox escape published on GitHub lets an app read other apps' files on iPhones running iOS 26 and 27. That puts seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk of exposure to malicious apps, Binance warned today. Apple's updates for iOS 26 and 27, released yesterday, do not list a fix.
A researcher who goes by forcequit, in collaboration with 0xjohnny, released the escape, called worse_query, on Sunday, a day before those updates came out. Neither the exchange nor the researcher reported any attacks or thefts involving it.
The exchange told users to delete apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed apps, and to update iOS and all their apps. No fix for the escape has been confirmed.
For anyone who suspects a breach, the exchange's security warning advises moving funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and resetting all active login sessions.
The researcher's proof-of-concept code can reach every app's data container on an iPhone, and some system folders on iOS 27. To use it, an app has to set up an App Group container.
He says the code is for developers and "isn't useful by itself." Other developers have built apps on it that people can install.
One of them is WQ Files, a file manager that developer Christoph Kolbicz built on worse_query. It reaches other apps' data without a jailbreak or a kernel exploit, and it can edit, delete and clear that data.
WQ Files installs via sideloading tools such as AltStore and SideStore, which automatically create the App Group it needs when used with an Apple ID. No one involved has said whether an app from the App Store could use worse_query.
The three versions in the exchange's warning are the ones listed as tested in the WQ Files release notes. The researcher gives a wider range.
Of these sources, only Erosion's developers list iOS 27.2.1, which came out yesterday, and none lists iOS 26.7.3. They added 27.2.1 this week in a README change with the note "pretty sure 27.2.1 is supported".
Yesterday's updates, iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3, fixed two iMessage flaws and several Bluetooth bugs. The security notes for iOS 27.2.1 do not mention worse_query or any sandbox issues, nor do the iOS 26.7.3 notes. Apple does not disclose, discuss, or confirm security issues until it has investigated and a patch or release is available, the notes say.
In a reply on X, the researcher wrote that he had not planned to release worse_query early. He added that "Apple was stalling on responding to me and people started larping with it on here."
The exchange did not name any wallet app as exposed, and neither did the researcher nor the developers of the apps built on worse_query.

articles.title: Votre ancien téléphone Android peut encore vous être utile : 5 idées à tester avant de le recycler
articles.text:
Vous venez de remplacer votre smartphone par un modèle plus récent ? Ne reléguez pas l’ancien dans un tiroir, il peut encore vous être utile !
Google peaufine régulièrement son système d'exploitation mobile. Récemment, Android 17 QPR1 a modernisé l’interface de vos smartphones et amélioré leur confidentialité. Le géant de Mountain View a aussi corrigé 216 failles début novembre. Autant de mises à jour que votre vieux mobile ne verra probablement jamais, mais il ne faut pas le condamner à l’oubli pour autant.
Faute de pouvoir en faire un robot humanoïde comme les chercheurs de l'UCLA, voici 5 idées pour lui donner une seconde vie.
Offrez un nouveau système à votre vieux smartphone
Votre smartphone doit tirer sa révérence. Pourquoi ne pas prolonger son existence en le dotant d’une ROM communautaire ? En installant une distribution open source comme LineageOS ou GrapheneOS, vous pourrez prolonger vos mises à jour et vous doter d'un téléphone secondaire. Le hic ? Il faudra dire adieu aux fonctions maison de Google et à la plupart des applis bancaires.
Recyclez les capteurs photo
En branchant votre vieux portable à un ordinateur, vous pouvez l’utiliser comme une webcam et participer à des visios sur Zoom ou Meet. Il est même possible d’aller plus loin et de transformer votre mobile en caméra de surveillance avec Alfred Camera.
Transformez votre vieux portable en console
Si vous êtes fan de retrogaming et que le processeur de votre ancien téléphone tient encore la route, n'hésitez pas à installer des émulateurs comme RetroArch pour faire tourner des jeux Super Nintendo ou PlayStation 1. En passant par xCloud ou GeForce Now et en connectant une manette mobile, vous pourrez aussi déléguer le calcul à des serveurs distants et faire de votre portable une véritable console de poche.
Ajoutez un écran multimédia à votre véhicule
Saviez-vous qu’il était possible de transformer votre vieux téléphone en interface de type Android Auto ? Téléchargez une application comme Open Headunit, installez votre portable sur votre tableau de bord et le tour est joué !
Utilisez votre mobile comme connexion de secours
Si vous avez de temps à autre des soucis avec votre connexion principale, pensez à utiliser votre ancien mobile comme point d’accès Wi-Fi secondaire. Seul problème, il faudra payer un second forfait pour obtenir cette connexion de dépannage : à vous de voir si cela vaut le coup de dépenser un peu plus.
Source : Android Police

articles.title: Nvidia GPU price hike rumor suggests RTX 5070 Ti could end up at almost triple its MSRP — seriously bleak times could be ahead for PC gamers
articles.text:
Nvidia RTX 5080 to cost $3,000 and the RTX 5070 Ti at $2,000? Rumored GPU price hikes could be the finishing blow for high-end PC gaming in the RAM crisis
We could be looking at triple the MSRP for both GPUs in the US, and equivalent huge price hikes elsewhere
- A rumor claims MSI is planning some big price increases for Nvidia GPUs
- The RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti could be hit with price rises of around $1,200 and $600 respectively
- Admittedly those are the worst-case scenarios, but with big price rises already in place, these GPUs are already pretty much unaffordable anyway – so even more modest bumps in cost are going to hurt
If you thought Nvidia's higher-end GPUs were pricey enough, you'd be spot on there – but they are going to get a lot more costly still based on the latest from the rumor mill.
Wccftech highlighted that leaker Harukaze5719 on X flagged up a post on ChannelGate (a common source of supply chain rumors in Asia) with details of what's supposedly a set of big prices increases from MSI.
We're told that the RTX 5080 could be visited with a price hike of between 1,300 to 8,000 Yuan this month in China, which equates to a jump of about $200 at minimum in the US, or $1,200 in the worst-case scenario (or the equivalent across other regions).
Yes, that isn't a typo, the claim is that MSI's RTX 5080 could jump by over a grand – the MSRP of this graphics card – towards the upper end of this predicted price increase.
The rumored hike for the RTX 5070 Ti is almost as frightening and could be from $120 all the way up to a potential $600 rise.
The source further claims a rise of between $75 and $150 for the RTX 5070, and smaller price bumps of around the $50 mark for the RTX 5060 and 5060 Ti. It's mostly the higher-tier GeForce GPUs which are being hit here, though, and possibly in a really nasty way.
Analysis: a pricing shambles
Previous buzz from ChannelGate (last week, as TechPowerUp noticed) regarding several other board makers suggested price rises in the order of $400 (in the US) for the RTX 5080 and $150 for the RTX 5070 Ti, which particularly in the latter case is at the lower-end of these fresh predictions. Keep a firm grip on that saltshaker, in other words, but everyone seems agreed that there are some major hikes coming to Nvidia GPUs in Asia, and those same pricing pressures will surely apply across the globe.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
We'd better hope that the higher-end of these new forecasted hikes don't become a reality, anyway, as they'd leave the GPU market in a pricing shambles, frankly.
To take the US market for example, the RTX 5080 is already $2,000, so are we looking at it being nearer $3,000 come the end of November? It certainly seems like it's heading towards $2,500, which is a frankly astonishing amount for a non-flagship GPU. (Although given the RTX 5090's vanishing act, it is the de facto flagship at this point I suppose).
The RTX 5070 Ti is the more worrying prospect here, though, because the RTX 5080 has always been an expensive card – most folks won't fork out a grand (the MSRP) for a GPU anyway, as that's the budget for the whole PC (or most of it) for the majority. Whereas the RTX 5070 Ti is a realistic buy at its MSRP, but the GPU has already entered effectively unaffordable territory even now thanks to more recent price rises.
Currently in the US you'll pay at least $1,400 for an RTX 5070 Ti from big-name retailers like Newegg or Micro Center (and more for the beefier cards). If a $600 rise is inflicted on this graphics card, you're looking at $2,000, or closing on it, for the privilege of owning one. And this is supposed to be a mainstream mid-range (well, upper-mid-range) GPU, remember.
I was already prepared for this to happen – which is why I've been recommending buying a GPU sooner rather than later, if you need one, as this year has rolled on – although I wasn't expecting this kind of steep spike (and certainly not so suddenly).
This new rumor may be wrong, or the heftier price increases this leak is theorizing may not come to pass, but I'm pretty certain we are going to see all GPUs get bumped up in price as 2027 begins, and I fear there may yet be worse to come. (Certainly the broader RAM crisis is predicted to intensify next year).
Still, at least you might be able to get some money back on your purchase by letting Microsoft use your shiny new Nvidia GPU to train its AI (in one possible future timeline, that is).

articles.title: Beyond the Alert: The Case for Rich Network Data
articles.text:
At some point your security will fail. This isn’t pessimism. It’s not because your team and tools aren’t sophisticated enough. It’s the reason we have detections in the first place. And, it’s why once we accept that prevention has its limits, we arrive at an interdiction strategy: finding and disrupting what got in.
After the alert
The alert tells you something happened. However, gaining access to your network doesn’t necessarily mean attackers have stolen data or disrupted the systems they were targeting. They may need to obtain additional access, move to another machine, or further explore the network. Being able to see and understand that activity is the intervention opportunity.
People naturally gravitate toward detections during product evaluations. They’re tangible, easy to compare and quantify, and address the question everyone wants an answer to: Will they catch the attack? There’s often an assumption that the rest will follow, meaning, if the detections are good, surely the investigation will be as well, right?
Whether you can trace the attack, understand the scope, and respond in time to intervene depends largely on the data behind that detection. In network security, a product can have good detections and still leave an analyst struggling to investigate. Perhaps the analyst can see the connection that triggered the alert but can’t follow what happened next. If a search returns nothing, does that mean the activity didn’t happen or that you weren’t collecting the evidence needed to see it?
This, and the arrival of AI defense, is why data quality has recently been getting so much attention.
Data vs. data
Investigation success takes knowledge of both attacker behavior and your own environment. You need to understand what you’re looking for, but also what your data can actually tell you.
The difference in network data shows up when investigating an alert. Both shallow and rich data provide investigations with a starting point, but one can rapidly lead to a dead end. Shallow data is often just composed of timestamps, IPs, and basic connection information. Rich data retains greater transaction details and adds context. It correlates and lets you pivot and reconstruct, answering not just what triggered the alert but what happened before, after, and elsewhere.
To evaluate the data quality of a security tool, consider key questions such as:
- Are full transaction details provided or just a summary?
- Is packet content or file extraction available?
- How far back can we search, and how fast?
- Can I follow a connection across hosts and time?
AI <3 data
AI-powered SOC tools can now process data at a scale that human teams simply cannot match. The more data points AI has, the more effectively it can surface events. While shallow data limits what AI can correlate, richer data allows it to identify subtle patterns across hosts and behaviors, potentially exposing previously unseen indicators of compromise or providing opportunity to intervene before an attack escalates.
AI can help when something unfamiliar is encountered. Nobody knows every service, process, or log format. An assistant can help explain what you’re looking at, suggest questions to pursue, or write a script to make a large set of data easier to examine. That can save a lot of research time. It can also help an analyst get past a point where they would otherwise be stuck.
But we’re certainly not at the point where we can trust what AI claims 100% of the time. You still need to test what it gives you. If an assistant suggests an explanation, check whether the evidence supports it. If it produces a query or script, test what it does. And before running a suggested command, ask what else it might affect. A model can be so focused on solving the immediate problem that it overlooks the rest of the system.
As AI takes on more investigative work, the ability to inspect the underlying evidence becomes another essential aspect of modern data quality.
Unfamiliar territory is the test
When evaluating data from network security products—NDR in particular—take an alert from a demonstration and investigate it properly. But don’t follow the guided path. Dig deep and put yourself in unfamiliar territory. You’ll get a much better sense of how the product helps analysts when they’re dealing with an event they haven’t seen before.
- Look at the transactions behind the alert
- Ask what packet content or extracted files are available
- Follow the activity backwards and forwards in time
- Ask a question that wasn’t anticipated
These questions and tasks probably won’t be part of a typical demo. That’s the point. They’ll let you see if the data provides the fidelity, reach, and context to actually solve investigations or just a starting point with nowhere to go.
Detections get the attention, but data determines the outcome. The real question is can your team use the data to fully understand an incident and decide what to do?

Corelight network detection and response (NDR) delivers data that’s open, transparent, and explainable—helping detect evasive threats, reduce triage time, and enable agentic AI throughout the SOC. Corelight’s structured network evidence preserves protocol-level context to produce a more complete dataset for investigation and AI. When analysts and AI can reason from evidence instead of isolated alerts or metadata, they can validate findings, reconstruct activity, and reach more reliable conclusions. articles.title: “Get ready with me” oculta riesgos para niños y adolescentes: perfiles falsos y suplantación de identidad
articles.text:
Los videos que muestran rutinas de maquillaje, cuidado de la piel o preparación para salir de casa se multiplican en las redes sociales. Pero la tendencia “Get ready with me” puede exponer a niños y adolescentes a perfiles falsos, suplantación de identidad y contactos engañosos, según alertaron expertos en ciberseguridad.
Un uniforme escolar, el nombre de un amigo, una vista desde la ventana o la calle que aparece detrás de la cámara pueden revelar más de lo previsto. Kaspersky advirtió que la suma de esos datos facilita que desconocidos reconstruyan aspectos de la vida cotidiana de un menor y los utilicen para intentar acercarse a él.
Qué información puede quedar expuesta en un video publicado en redes sociales
El formato “Get ready with me” consiste en grabar una rutina mientras la persona conversa frente a la cámara. En ese contexto, los menores suelen mostrar productos, ropa, accesorios y espacios de su hogar sin advertir que el contenido del fondo puede aportar datos sensibles.
Un logotipo en una mochila, el uniforme de una institución educativa, una calle identificable o referencias a horarios y actividades permiten detectar lugares frecuentes. Aislados, esos elementos pueden parecer irrelevantes; juntos, pueden dar pistas sobre la identidad, los movimientos y el ambiente social de quien publica el video.
Los especialistas relacionaron este fenómeno con el oversharing, o sobreexposición de información personal. Cada publicación, comentario, perfil o interacción deja rastros que conforman la huella digital, un conjunto de datos que puede permanecer disponible incluso después de que el contenido deje de circular en la cuenta original.
Un video puede descargarse, reenviarse o vincularse con publicaciones de otras plataformas. Las cuentas antiguas, los nombres de usuario y las fotos que ya no se consultan pueden aportar información. Por eso, eliminar una publicación puntual no siempre alcanza para recuperar el control sobre los datos que quedaron expuestos.
Cómo aprovechan los ciberdelincuentes los videos publicados en redes sociales
La información obtenida a través de las redes puede utilizarse para crear mensajes de phishing más creíbles. Conocer el colegio, los intereses, los pasatiempos o el grupo de amigos de un menor permite que un atacante redacte comunicaciones que aparenten provenir de alguien cercano o de una institución conocida.
Además, ese material puede servir para crear perfiles falsos y casos de suplantación de identidad. Los ciberdelincuentes pueden copiar fotos, nombres, videos o expresiones habituales para simular una cuenta auténtica y contactar a familiares, amigos u otros usuarios.
La finalidad puede ser obtener más datos, pedir transferencias de dinero o establecer conversaciones privadas bajo una identidad falsa.
Qué pasa cuando un desconocido busca generar confianza de un menor
La exposición frecuente puede producir una sensación de cercanía entre quien publica y personas que en realidad no conoce. Ese vínculo aparente abre la puerta a maniobras de manipulación, sobre todo cuando un adulto o un perfil falso utiliza datos personales para presentarse como alguien confiable.
“Uno de los mayores riesgos es que los menores no siempre son conscientes de quién puede acceder a sus publicaciones ni de cómo esa información puede utilizarse en su contra”, señaló Fabiano Tricarico, director de Productos para el Consumidor para Américas de Kaspersky.
El ejecutivo advirtió que un contenido compartido inicialmente con amigos puede llegar a manos de desconocidos que intenten ganarse la confianza de los menores mediante engaños.
Tricarico dijo que los adultos responsables deben conversar con niños y adolescentes sobre las interacciones sospechosas. Sugirió explicarles qué medidas tomar cuando alguien solicita información personal, propone trasladar una conversación a un espacio privado o intenta obtener imágenes y datos fuera de los canales habituales.
Cuáles medidas deben tomar las familias antes de publicar en redes sociales
La primera pauta consiste en revisar cada video antes de subirlo. No alcanza con controlar lo que se dice ante la cámara: conviene observar el fondo, los objetos visibles y cualquier referencia que permita inferir una ubicación, un nombre o una rutina.
Asimismo, es clave buscar de forma periódica nombres, apodos y perfiles en internet para detectar cuentas olvidadas o publicaciones antiguas. Las familias pueden revisar las opciones de privacidad, limitar quién ve el contenido o envía mensajes y eliminar perfiles que ya no se usan.
Cuanta menos información personal permanezca disponible, menor será la exposición ante una cuenta comprometida o una maniobra de engaño.

articles.title: NVIDIA May Cut TSMC Chip Orders Amid Mounting Pressure, Report Claims
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
NVIDIA May Cut TSMC Chip Orders Amid Mounting Pressure, Report Claims
NVIDIA may be slowing down its chip orders at TSMC, according to a new report from Taiwan's Commercial Times. The outlet cites unnamed supply chain sources but doesn't name a product, node, size, or timeline. Neither NVIDIA nor TSMC have commented so far, and the claims are single-sourced for now. The report frames this as NVIDIA being squeezed from inside and out. On the inside, there's Jensen Huang's November 8 email to staff, in which he apologized for an extramarital affair, and the board's independent investigation into reports that he was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board has said it has no reason to believe national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised. 
The outside pressure mostly comes down to export controls. The report points to tighter export reviews and H200 chips reportedly stockpiled in Hong Kong, both of which it says raise the risk of NVIDIA scaling back orders. It also cites foreign media reports suggesting that some firms approved to handle H200 could be shell companies, which feeds concerns that chips might reach China through fronts like these or middlemen in other countries. The report presents that as a suspicion rather than a finding, and if cuts do happen, upstream suppliers such as TSMC and ASE are the most exposed.If NVIDIA does give up wafer capacity, the report expects AMD and custom chip designers to snap it up. AMD's data center revenue hit a record $8.5 billion last quarter, up 97% year-over-year, as Helios production ramps. Meanwhile, MediaTek, Alchip, and GUC are named as possible winners on the ASIC side, and ASIC vendors reportedly told the outlet their customers would take all the capacity TSMC can offer. Leading-edge supply is tight as it is, with TSMC reportedly also weighing CoWoS price hikes of up to 20%. For now, this information is best treated as a rumor.

articles.title: IPVanish quietly brings quantum-resistant WireGuard to iPhone and iPad — here's all we know
articles.text:
IPVanish quietly brings quantum-resistant WireGuard to iPhone and iPad — here's all we know
The provider's latest iOS release adds post-quantum protection to WireGuard, but key questions remain
- IPVanish has added post-quantum encryption (PQE) in latest iOS update
- PQE protects your data against "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks
- The release notes don't yet reveal how IPVanish's PQE works
IPVanish has rolled out post-quantum encryption (PQE) in its iOS app, becoming the latest VPN provider to prepare for a future where quantum computers can crack today's encryption.
Version 4.33.2 of the IPVanish app landed on the App Store on Monday, and its release notes confirm in a single line that PQE has been added to the WireGuard protocol.
The move puts IPVanish alongside a growing list of best VPN providers already offering quantum-resistant protection, including NordVPN, Surfshark, ExpressVPN, and Mullvad.
IPVanish — an ever-evolving VPN
IPVanish may not quite match the market leaders, but it is still a strong all-round VPN with plenty of features, high speeds, and better unblocking capabilities than most VPNs. Well worth a try, especially as it keeps improving its infrastructure, speed performance, and feature offerings.
What we know about IPVanish's post-quantum upgrade
Right now, the facts are limited. According to the App Store listing, PQE applies to WireGuard on iOS. The notes don't mention OpenVPN or IKEv2, and there's no word yet on Android, Windows, macOS, or IPVanish's TV apps.
Several key questions remain, including which algorithm IPVanish is using, whether the setup is hybrid or fully post-quantum, whether it's switched on by default, and when other platforms will follow.
We've contacted IPVanish and will update this article when we hear back.
That said, the upgrade has been in the works for a while. Back in September 2025, IPVanish's Chief Commercial Officer Subbu Sthanu told TechNadu that post-quantum readiness was a major focus for its R&D team, which was exploring hybrid encryption for both WireGuard and OpenVPN.
At the time, Sthanu said the team was "building custom implementations rather than relying on off-the-shelf patches."
The rollout also caps a busy few months for the provider, which recently passed its third independent no-logs audit and continues to expand its RAM-only server network.
Hybrid or full? Why the details matter
WireGuard isn't quantum-safe out of the box, as its key exchange relies on elliptic-curve cryptography. Providers usually fix this by running a separate post-quantum handshake, typically with the NIST-standardized ML-KEM algorithm, and feeding the result into WireGuard's pre-shared key slot.
Most VPNs, including NordVPN, take a hybrid approach that layers post-quantum protection on top of classical encryption, so a flaw in the newer algorithm wouldn't leave your data exposed.
Some providers are now pushing further. In October 2026, Surfshark added ML-DSA authentication to WireGuard, claiming full post-quantum coverage of encryption, key exchange, and authentication. Without quantum-resistant authentication, a future attacker could, in theory, impersonate a VPN server. NordVPN is also working on post-quantum authentication.
Knowing where IPVanish sits on this spectrum will tell us how complete its protection really is.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance. Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
Why post-quantum encryption matters for you
Quantum computers aren't yet powerful enough to break modern encryption, but experts expect that moment, dubbed "Q-Day," to arrive eventually.
The risk is already here, though, as bad actors are already deploying so-called "harvest now, decrypt later" attacks to collect encrypted traffic today and store it until they gain the tools to unlock it.
For most people, this isn't cause for panic. But if you send sensitive information that needs to stay private for years, such as financial, medical, or work data, PQE adds a valuable layer of future-proofing.

GPUs are her main area of interest, and nothing thrills her quite like that time every couple of years when new graphics cards hit the market.
She built her first PC nearly 20 years ago, and dozens of builds later, she’s always planning out her next build (or helping her friends with theirs). During her career, Monica has written for many tech-centric outlets, including Digital Trends, SlashGear, WePC, and Tom’s Hardware.
