articles.title: Nuevo tráiler de ‘GTA VI’ y ya sabemos lo que significa eso de “mejor en PS5” y cómo poder jugar en Xbox One
articles.text:
Queda poco más de una semana para que podamos jugar a 'GTA VI' y Rockstar, que durante mucho tiempo se mantuvo en un perfil bajo, lleva tiempo con la maquinaria del marketing a toda potencia. Hoy han soltado un nuevo tráiler con alguna secuencia nueva, pero sobre todo han arrojado algo de luz a tres temas importantes.
Entre ellos, las mejoras de 'Grand Theft Auto VI' en PS5 Pro y, para variar, detalles sobre la versión de Xbox.
'GTA VI' en PS5 Pro
Hasta ahora, el contenido que hemos visto del juego se ha mostrado en una PS5. La consola de Sony es la base en la promoción del título y ya sabemos cómo suele funcionar esto: si hay acuerdos de por medio, las versiones de otras plataformas se mencionan lo mínimo posible.
Además, todo apuntaba que lo que habíamos visto hasta ahora era en la PS5 base, la consola de 2020, por lo que había quienes nos preguntábamos qué mejoras tendría en PS5 Pro. Han tardado, pero por fin han dado respuesta:
"La experiencia visual en PlayStation 5 Pro no tiene parangón, ya que presenta una mayor claridad de imagen gracias a PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) y sombras con trazado de rayos, disponibles exclusivamente en PlayStation 5 Pro".
Dentro del marketing de "mejor en PS5", y al margen de las mejoras visuales en PS5 Pro, Rockstar ha confirmado que esta versión tendrá retroalimentación háptica gracias a las capacidades del mando de la consola, renderización de audio espacial mejorada y tiempos de carga reducidos que aprovechan el SSD de la máquina.
También señalan que han llevado todas las plataformas "al mismísimo límite", por lo que en Xbox Series X podremos disfrutar de la misma experiencia puntera a nivel visual.
'GTA VI' en Xbox One con la nube
Por otro lado tenemos la mención directa a Xbox. Aquí, el comunicado se centra en el juego en la nube.
Estará disponible en Xbox Cloud Gaming tanto en Series X como en Series S, pero también en Xbox One. Esto es una novedad interesante porque si no habías dado el salto y tenías una Xbox One X (o una One normal) que sigue ofreciendo una calidad brutal en la imagen en muchos juegos, es la forma de jugar a 'GTA VI' sin comprar una consola nueva.
Ahora bien, el asterisco es que los ajustes visuales de esta versión en la nube, se juegue en la consola en la que se juegue, será la de Xbox Series S. Aquí se cumple eso de "una de cal y otra de arena" debido a que la de Series S, por pura potencia de la máquina, será la versión más recortada del juego.
Y si lo que quieres es jugar en Remote Play de PlayStation, han confirmado que también será compatible.
En fin, quedan nueve días para tener el juego más esperado de la generación en nuestras consolas y sólo queda ver si cumple con unas expectativas que están por la estratosfera.

articles.title: Microsoft lobbies against potential ban on Chinese optical networking gear for AI data centers as FCC mulls restricting imports — industry group says move could grind data center rollout to a halt
articles.text:
Microsoft lobbies against potential ban on Chinese optical networking gear for AI data centers as FCC mulls restricting imports — industry group says move could grind data center rollout to a halt
The supply of this tiny module (or lack thereof) could derail the hundreds of massive data centers planned in the U.S.
Microsoft, the tech giant that is building 35 data centers around the U.S. and has plans for 134 more, has reportedly met with the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy and the National Security Council as the FCC is considering an import ban on Chinese optical transceivers. According to Reuters, the company, alongside the Information Technology Industry Council (ITI), is lobbying against the move.
“It really threatens to arguably grind (the data center rollout) to a halt,” ITI Executive Vice President of Policy and General Counsel John Miller said. He also added, “Those chips, without optical transceivers, literally could just sit there waiting around unutilized until you actually have the transceivers to essentially connect them together,” referring to the AI chips that data centers use.
Optical transceivers are tiny modules plugged into hardware that convert their electrical signals into light signals, allowing data to be transmitted as light pulses across fiber optics. Data centers increasingly use optical transceivers and fiber optics to transmit data between AI GPUs and server racks, as they’re faster, offer lower latency, require less power, and generate less heat compared to traditional copper connections. However, Chinese companies currently supply 66% of the global market, meaning banning them from supplying data centers in the U.S. would more than halve the available supply, thereby exacerbating the various shortages that have been pummeling the industry.
However, there are concerns that some of these transceivers could be compromised by Beijing and be used to steal data, install malware, or remotely disrupt American data centers, which is why the FCC is considering the restriction, just like how it banned Huawei from the U.S. telecommunications network. But unlike Huawei, which had many established competitors in the telecommunications hardware industry, only two U.S.-based companies produce optical transceivers that data centers need — Coherent and Lumentum. While these firms could produce optical transceivers to compete with Chinese offerings, they simply do not have the scale to make up for the shortfall if the FCC bans Chinese imports today.
One compromise floated by the Trump administration is that it would only ban Chinese optical transceivers capable of hitting 3.2 terabits per second. While this technology already exists, its production isn’t expected to expand until 2028, with installation not beginning until 2029. This should give American producers time to ramp up their own output, although the suggestion is still under consideration.

articles.title: Keychron Launches G25 HE 46 g Gaming Mouse with Razer Viper Mini Shape and Analog Switches
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
Keychron Launches G25 HE 46 g Gaming Mouse with Razer Viper Mini Shape and Analog Switches
Following the release of the Keychron G6 HE, the brand has been steadily expanding its portfolio of models with Hall effect switches for adjustable actuation and rapid trigger support. The G25 HE is Keychron's latest HE mouse model, recently announced in an X post, and it takes the Hall effect switch tech and the flagship internals of the G6 HE and puts it all into a smaller shape that bears an uncanny resemblance to the Razer Viper Mini and Cobra shapes. Keychron has yet to provide a full spec sheet or product page for the G25 HE, but the mouse has been scanned and submitted to EloShapes for comparisons, where its specs and features are also available. 
The Keychron G25 HE measures in at 120 × 63 × 39 mm and weighs 46 g, which is on the lighter side for a wireless mouse, but not the lightest by any means. It is also a symmetrical shape with right-side programmable thumb buttons and a partially open bottom plate. The G25 HE is powered by a PixArt PAW 3955 optical sensor and a Nordic 54LM20A MCU, which means it has a peak DPI of 40,000, up to 8 kHz polling rate, and can track at up to 750 IPS and 60 G of acceleration. The star of the show, and the mouse's namesake, are the MagOpt switches which feature both optical and Hall effect magnetic sensing, although the switches still have a click leaf and a distinct tactile bump, which has been largely considered to have a negative impact on the mouse's adjustable actuation trickery.The G25 HE, like Keychron's other mice, will feature both Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz wireless connectivity, with a supplemental detachable USB Type-C cable for wired gaming if players are so inclined. No battery life specs have been published yet. 
Button mapping, actuation distance, and rapid trigger can all be configured in the Keychron Launcher web driver, after which settings are saved to the mouse's internal memory, so that nothing needs to be running in the background to keep the custom settings applied. An exact price hasn't yet been announced for the Keychron G25 HE, but if previous mouse launches have been any indication, it will launch somewhere around the $60-80 mark.

articles.title: La cadena de hoteles Wyndham expuso datos de clientes al dejar una contraseña dentro de su aplicación para Android
articles.text:
La cadena de hoteles Wyndham reconoció un incidente de ciberseguridad después de que un investigador descubriera una contraseña dentro del código de su aplicación para Android. La clave daba acceso a una base de datos interna con nombres, correos y números de miembro de clientes, según TechCrunch.
El investigador Robert Wiggins, de la firma What Security, dijo a TechCrunch que la contraseña abría una base de datos de la empresa alojada en Salesforce, una plataforma de gestión de clientes. Cualquier persona con una copia de la app podía extraerla.
Además de los datos personales, la base guardaba los tokens de inicio de sesión de los clientes. Son códigos que mantienen abierta la sesión en la app sin pedir la contraseña cada vez. También contenía archivos y documentos de Wyndham.
Wiggins calculó que había millones de registros, pero no pudo determinar cuántos pertenecían a clientes. Wyndham afirma tener unos 129 millones de miembros inscritos en su programa de recompensas.
La empresa anuló la clave, pero dejó dudas sin responder
Según Wiggins, Wyndham no ofrece un canal para reportar fallas de seguridad, así que pidió ayuda a TechCrunch para avisar a la compañía. Poco después de que el medio contactara al grupo de ciberseguridad, la credencial fue revocada y el acceso se cerró.
Un portavoz de Wyndham dijo que su equipo tomó medidas para resolver el problema y que sus expertos de seguridad no tienen evidencia de accesos no autorizados. No dio detalles que respalden esa afirmación.
La empresa tampoco quiso decir si cuenta con registros del servidor que permitan saber si alguien entró a la base antes del hallazgo. Wiggins señaló que, sin esa visibilidad, un atacante pudo haber filtrado grandes cantidades de datos de clientes.
El portavoz no precisó cuánto tiempo estuvo la contraseña dentro de la app ni cómo se corregirá de forma definitiva. Tampoco respondió si avisará a los clientes expuestos ni si informará a reguladores como la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos (SEC), que exige a las empresas que cotizan en bolsa divulgar incidentes de ciberseguridad relevantes.
Un error simple que la IA ayuda a encontrar
Incluir contraseñas dentro de una aplicación, práctica conocida como hardcoding, es algo que los desarrolladores suelen evitar. TechCrunch explicó que muchos casos de este tipo reciben la máxima calificación de gravedad por lo sencillo que resulta abusar de ellos.
Para Wiggins es el segundo hallazgo público de credenciales incrustadas en dos semanas, tras una falla casi idéntica en la app de la cadena de restaurantes Applebee’s que expuso datos de clientes. En ambos casos usó herramientas de IA, que revisan miles de líneas de código descompilado por segundo.
Wyndham no dijo si creará un programa para que investigadores externos informen fallas en privado. Michael Francess, director de ciberseguridad de la empresa, indicó a medios que los investigadores pueden escribir al correo del hotel.
No es el primer problema de seguridad de la cadena. En 2024, un investigador halló que varias recepciones de hoteles Wyndham tenían instalado un programa espía, pcTattletale, que filtraba capturas de pantalla con datos de huéspedes y reservas. Tras esa publicación, la empresa del programa fue hackeada y su dueño, Bryan Fleming, cerró el negocio; luego fue arrestado y condenado por fabricar y vender spyware ilegal.
Qué riesgos enfrenta una cadena de hoteles tras una filtración de datos
Los atacantes podrían usar nombres, correos y números de membresía para enviar mensajes fraudulentos que imiten comunicaciones del hotel y busquen obtener contraseñas o datos bancarios.
Si los tokens de sesión siguen activos, una persona no autorizada podría acceder a cuentas sin conocer la clave. Eso expone reservas, información de contacto y posibles beneficios del programa de fidelidad.

articles.title: Rebelote ! Le vol inaugural de cette fusée, véritable espoir du spatial européen, est repoussé à 2027
articles.text:
Elle devait décoller cette année depuis l’Écosse, mais il faudra finalement patienter. La fusée allemande RFA One ne s’envolera pas avant l’année prochaine. Elle n’en reste pas moins très prometteuse.
Basée comme son nom l’indique à Augsbourg, en Allemagne, Rocket Factory Augsburg (RFA) fait partie des jeunes pousses qui veulent offrir à l’Europe un accès souverain à l’espace. Son pari : un petit lanceur, RFA One, conçu pour envoyer des satellites en orbite à moindre coût.
Et l’entreprise, détenue à 65,1 % par le groupe spatial OHB, n’est pas seule sur ce terrain. Sa compatriote Isar Aerospace a franchi le cap début septembre, en devenant la première une fusée privée à rejoindre l’orbite depuis l’Europe continentale. RFA, elle, va devoir s’armer un peu plus de patience, révèle European Spaceflight.
Le calendrier a glissé
En effet, la start-up vise désormais 2027 pour le vol inaugural de son fleuron. Tout semblait pourtant bien engagé pour 2026 : en mars, RFA annonçait avoir livré les deux premiers étages à SaxaVord, dans les îles Shetland, au nord de l’Écosse. La fusée était même assemblée sur son pas de tir en juillet, prête pour un essai d’allumage du premier étage.
Mais un problème est survenu pendant les tests, poussant la firme à revoir ses plans. Si en août, Marco Fucks, P.-D.G d’OHB, assurait encore que le premier vol restait prévu « plus tard cette année », force est de constater que cette deadline ne sera pas tenue.
Haute de 30 mètres, RFA One compte trois étages, dont le premier est voué à devenir réutilisable. Elle sera en mesure d’emporter jusqu’à 1 300 kilogrammes de charge utile en orbite héliosynchrone, ou orbite polaire basse, très prisée pour l’observation de la Terre. Et pour tenir les coûts, RFA a fait des choix audacieux. Sa fusée dispose, par exemple, de réservoirs en inox issus de l’industrie des boissons et de pièces issues de l’automobile et de l’énergie, produites en grande série.
Espoir intact pour le spatial européen
RFA One compte parmi les trois fusées sélectionnées dans le cadre de l’European Launcher Challenge de l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA). Signé en août, il doit accorder plus de 540 millions d’euros à l’entreprise allemande, ainsi qu’à Isar Aerospace et l’espagnole PLD Space pour accélérer le développement de leurs lanceurs respectifs. Objectif : moins dépendre des États-Unis et surtout, d’une certaine SpaceX.
D’ailleurs, PLD vise aussi un vol inaugural en 2027 pour sa fusée moyenne Miura 5. Celui-ci aura lieu depuis le centre spatial de Kourou, en Guyane française.

articles.title: GTA 6 chegará ao Xbox Cloud Gaming no lançamento • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
GTA 6 chegará ao Xbox Cloud Gaming no lançamento
Streaming estreia junto com o jogo em 19 de novembro. Consumidores já podem fazer pré-download nos consoles.
A Xbox anunciou nesta terça-feira (10/11) que GTA 6 estará disponível no Xbox Cloud Gaming, serviço de nuvem da empresa, já no lançamento. Com isso, jogadores poderão rodar a nova sequência da franquia da Rockstar por streaming no dia 19 de novembro, inclusive no Xbox One. A estreia está marcada para as 3h da manhã (horário de Brasília).
A novidade foi anunciada pela Microsoft junto a novos detalhes sobre o lançamento. O streaming utilizará uma versão equivalente à do Xbox Series S nos servidores e, inicialmente, será restrito aos consoles Xbox.
Essa restrição pode ser temporária, mas, pelo menos por ora, usuários do Game Pass em PCs, celulares, navegadores e Smart TVs, que geralmente também possuem acesso ao Cloud Gaming, ficarão de fora.
De acordo com o diretor de estratégia do Xbox, Matthew Ball, a parceria não impede que GTA 6 chegue a outros serviços de streaming futuramente. Mais cedo nesta terça-feira, a Rockstar liberou o pré-download do jogo e um novo teaser com imagens inéditas da gameplay.
A liberação dos arquivos do jogo já começou a levantar novas teorias. Segundo o GameSpot, jogadores que iniciaram a instalação encontraram o modo história listado como um pacote separado.
A divisão chamou atenção porque, segundo o site, pode facilitar a distribuição de outros conteúdos do jogo. A Rockstar ainda não anunciou oficialmente um novo modo online.
A chegada do jogo ao Xbox Cloud Gaming não é a mesma coisa que a adição do jogo ao catálogo do Xbox Game Pass. Para jogar pela nuvem, além da assinatura, ainda é necessário que o usuário compre uma cópia digital do título.
No Brasil, os planos do Game Pass vão de R$ 43,90 a R$ 76,90 por mês, permitindo entre 5 a 15 horas de gameplay na nuvem mensalmente. A partir desta quarta-feira (11/11), porém, a Microsoft também permitirá adquirir horas avulsas de uso do serviço, mesmo sem exigir uma assinatura mensal.
Notavelmente, ficam de fora da brincadeira os assinantes do Game Pass somente para PC, que custa R$ 59,99 por mês. Rumores passados, rapidamente desmentidos pela Microsoft, indicavam que os direitos de streaming do jogo seriam exclusivos da Micrososft e permitiram o acesso do título nos computadores. Fontes na indústria, no entanto, adiantam que o jogo pode chegar à plataforma mais cedo do que se imagina.
Além do novo jogo, outros títulos da Rockstar devem chegar à plataforma. Grand Theft Auto V e Red Dead Redemption 2 estão entre os jogos previstos para chegar ao Xbox Cloud Gaming nos próximos meses.
A Rockstar também confirmou que GTA 6 será executado a 30 quadros por segundo em todas as versões para consoles, incluindo o PS5 Pro. A confirmação contraria rumores anteriores que indicavam a possibilidade de desempenho com taxas de quadros diferentes.
No entanto, o console mais potente da Sony deve receber melhorias gráficas em relação ao PS5 convencional. Uma delas será o uso de sombras com ray tracing. O console também terá suporte ao PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), tecnologia de reconstrução de imagem da Sony.

articles.title: ‘It feels like working with another staff-level engineer’: Anthropic lifts the veil on the latest features for Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 built ‘for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work’ — and it's already built an operating system from scratch
articles.text:
‘It feels like working with another staff-level engineer’: Anthropic lifts the veil on the latest features for Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 built ‘for the most ambitious, open-ended technical work’ — and it's already built an operating system from scratch
The latest Fable and Mythos releases are cheaper and more accurate
- Anthropic releases Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 designed to help solve complex problems and ambitious projects
- Both offer a 20% cheaper token cost than previous versions
- The models are highly capable across coding, biology scientific and mathematics research
Anthropic’s latest Fable and Mythos releases have been unveiled, offering users superior outputs that are more accurate at a cheaper token cost than previous versions.
Fable 5.2 is available for all users and couples its improved inference with an improved set of cybersecurity and biology safeguards. But to get your hands on the expanded capabilities of Mythos 5.2, you’ll have to apply through Anthropic’s Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.
Anthropic totes the new Fable and Mythos versions as being perfect for “ambitious, open-ended technical work” rather than as a “daily driver” — for which Anthropic recommends sticking to Opus 5.5.
Cheaper, quicker, and more accurate
The latest Fable release promises more bang for your buck over the 5.1 release. Anthropic says that 5.2 usage will sit at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens — around 20% cheaper than the previous version.
But if you’re on a deadline or just want something done quickly, Anthropic is introducing an optional “fast mode” that increases token generation speed by up to 2.5 times at an increased cost of $16 (input) and $80 (output) per million tokens.
Across almost every benchmark task, Anthropic says Fable 5.2 is more accurate than Opus 5.5, delivering results faster and more accurately with a significantly reduced token cost per task.
But Anthropic says users will be best served by taking a balanced approach to model use, using Opus 5.5 to get tasks started with Fable 5.2 coming on board as an “advisor” for more difficult tasks.

To demonstrate its capabilities, one of Anthropic’s engineers gave Fable 5.2 the task of designing a prototype operating system. Over the course of eight days over 1,000 agents were writing, testing, and reviewing code, from which the model produced a working operating system that boots and contains all the necessary bells and whistles including built-in Claude functionality.
“Claude Fable 5.2 is great for taking a loose idea and refining it. Its answers are really well considered, and within a few turns I can almost always say “ok, go do that,” and trust that it’ll complete it with little intervention,” said Tom Pritchard, Staff Engineer, Shopify. “It feels like working with another staff-level engineer.”
Anthropic’s engineers demonstrated Fable’s capabilities across science and mathematics using a range of tasks. According to Anthropic, Fable 5.2 was able to formalize the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours, designed a home voice-assistant hub, a USB speakerphone, and a handheld virtual pet from scratch, and solved two open problems in black hole physics.

articles.title: AI agent infrastructure: Red Hat's Kubernetes strategy - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
The next chapter for Red Hat: AI agents rewrite the cloud-native playbook
Red Hat LLC has spent years making Kubernetes manageable for enterprises that would rather run applications than tend clusters. As AI agents move into production, the company is extending that experience to a new generation of workloads. AI agents don’t just consume infrastructure. They execute commands, call external tools, access enterprise systems and take actions that can affect the business. The next phase of AI agent infrastructure requires enforceable security boundaries alongside efficient resource management.
Red Hat arrives at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City this week with a growing portfolio of technologies addressing those requirements. OpenShift provides the Kubernetes foundation; its work with Nvidia Corp. on OpenShell addresses agent execution and security; and the llm-d project has reached version 1.0 with capabilities for serving the context-heavy workloads agents create. Together, these developments position Red Hat to help enterprises manage agentic AI through open, Kubernetes-based infrastructure.
Unlike conventional applications, autonomous agents can generate commands, invoke tools and delegate work across multiple systems. That flexibility creates opportunities for automation while increasing the importance of consistent access controls and oversight.
This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exploration of how cloud-native infrastructure is evolving to support enterprise AI, with Red Hat and the broader Kubernetes ecosystem addressing the security, operational efficiency and scalability requirements of autonomous agents. (* Disclosure below.)
Red Hat advances Kubernetes-native security for AI agents
The rapid adoption of OpenClaw has brought renewed attention to agent security. An agent that can read files, run shell commands and make network calls needs clearly defined permissions and isolation to operate safely within enterprise environments.
Red Hat’s response centers on its collaboration with Nvidia around OpenShell, a runtime that places agents inside isolated execution environments and applies policy to their access. Nvidia developed OpenShell; Red Hat is working with Nvidia and the wider community to integrate the technology into Red Hat AI and its open hybrid cloud platform. Red Hat’s announcement describes the work as part of a broader effort to bring security-focused agentic AI capabilities to enterprise infrastructure.
OpenShell uses sandboxing, process-aware policy and controls over network access and credentials. Red Hat has also described how OpenShell can work with OpenShift’s sandboxed containers, adding application-level restrictions inside a virtual-machine boundary. These complementary layers govern agent behavior and isolate the environments in which agents operate, as Red Hat explains in its technical overview of layered sandboxing.
The distinction matters because sandboxing does not make an agent trustworthy. It limits the damage an agent can cause when its instructions, generated code or external inputs lead it somewhere they should not.
In a recent interview with theCUBE, Pete Cheslock, principal AI community architect at Red Hat, described how OpenShell builds on Kubernetes infrastructure: “The agent sandbox is one of them, so that you can deploy these agents in a secure way using Kubernetes native APIs.” His comments get to the central issue: enterprises cannot delegate authority to agents without defining and enforcing its limits.
Red Hat Chief Technology Officer Chris Wright also emphasized the importance of agent isolation in a May interview with theCUBE. Agents that can take real actions in a business need sandboxing and least-privilege protections, he explained.
“You’ve got to give it the right sandboxing. You’ve got to put protections around the agent, give it least privileges so it doesn’t think about read versus read-write — very big difference,” Wright said in SiliconANGLE’s coverage of Red Hat Summit.
Beyond sandboxing, enterprises must manage agent identities, data permissions, tool access and authorization. That distinction is reinforced by Paul Nashawaty, practice lead and principal analyst for application development, modernization and cloud native at theCUBE Research, whose September analysis of AI agent governance examines the difference between observing what agents do and proving what they were authorized to do. The research identifies runtime enforcement, delegated authority and verifiable audit evidence as requirements that become more important as autonomous systems move into production.
“This creates an opportunity for platforms that can unify application development, infrastructure orchestration, security and observability rather than adding another layer of disconnected tooling,” Nashawaty said.
Red Hat’s llm-d extends Kubernetes infrastructure for AI inference
Beyond security, agents create new requirements for inference infrastructure. An agent may call a model, retrieve information, invoke a tool and return to the model with additional context. Each interaction consumes compute, memory and network capacity, while the system must preserve enough context to continue efficiently.
Red Hat’s llm-d project addresses part of that problem. Founded by Red Hat, IBM Corp., Google Cloud, CoreWeave Inc. and Nvidia, and now governed by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, llm-d uses Kubernetes-native components to distribute inference across accelerators and manage traffic between them.
The project reached version 1.0 on Oct. 20, adding session-aware routing, turn-priority scheduling, multi-tenant quality-of-service controls and high-availability operations. Those features aim to keep multi-turn requests close to cached context, prioritize latency-sensitive work and reduce disruption during maintenance. The Red Hat release announcement and Google Cloud’s technical overview describe the release.
The architecture provides operators with additional options for coordinating inference workloads and managing accelerator resources within Kubernetes.
Red Hat Senior Vice President and AI Chief Technology Officer Brian Stevens described one of llm-d’s central architectural decisions in SiliconANGLE’s report on Kubernetes inference: “We can independently scale the processing of the input from the production of the tokens.”
Other infrastructure providers are addressing complementary requirements. ScaleOps Labs Ltd. focuses on GPU utilization and resource optimization across Kubernetes workloads. Vultr Holdings LLC offers GPU infrastructure and Kubernetes-based model deployment, while Broadcom Inc. positions VMware Cloud Foundation as a private-cloud platform for Kubernetes and AI workloads. Together, these offerings reflect expanding enterprise choices for resource optimization, accelerator capacity and private-cloud operations.
The operational gap appears in theCUBE Research’s “Day 0 Build, Test Survey Research Report.” Based on a survey of 375 IT, development, operations and platform engineering professionals, the research found that cloud-native adoption is widespread but maturity remains uneven. Inconsistent automated testing, fragmented developer tools and gaps in rollback capabilities continue to complicate production deployment.
“Ninety-two percent of organizations are integrating AI into at least one stage of the software development lifecycle, while 79% expect full-scale AI agent adoption within the next three years,” Nashawaty said, adding that approximately 30% still face operational readiness challenges.
The broader industry is also moving toward production-scale infrastructure. The CNCF’s 2026 annual cloud-native survey found that 82% of container users run Kubernetes in production and that 66% of organizations hosting generative AI workloads use Kubernetes for some or all inference. Those figures reinforce Kubernetes’ expanding role as enterprises adopt AI workloads.
Open-source collaboration expands Red Hat’s AI infrastructure opportunities
The open-source ecosystem is expanding alongside agentic AI adoption. On Nov. 5, Google announced the donation of Agent Substrate, gVisor and OpenRL to the CNCF following their acceptance into its Sandbox program in October. The projects address agent execution, isolation and reinforcement-learning workflows. Agent Substrate separates agent sessions and identities from active compute, allowing idle environments to pause and resume; gVisor provides an additional isolation boundary for untrusted code; and OpenRL supports reinforcement-learning post-training on Kubernetes. Google’s announcement describes the projects and their transition into CNCF governance.
These contributions complement broader efforts across the Kubernetes community. Red Hat is a co-founder of llm-d and is integrating Nvidia’s OpenShell into its enterprise AI platform, while Google is contributing technologies related to runtime and training requirements. The common emphasis on open infrastructure creates opportunities for interoperability as enterprise AI systems mature.
Broadcom added another development on Nov. 9, announcing that its VM API project had been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. The project aims to let organizations manage virtual machines through Kubernetes application programming interfaces across different infrastructure providers. This extends the Kubernetes conversation to managing virtual machines alongside containerized workloads.
Project Lightwell adds another dimension to Red Hat’s enterprise strategy. Announced with IBM in May, the $5 billion initiative aims to use AI-assisted vulnerability identification and validated fixes to strengthen open-source software supply chains. The initiative extends security efforts to the software dependencies supporting production workloads.
Sam Weston, industry analyst for enterprise applications, development and modernization at theCUBE Research, points to the infrastructure mix enterprises already operate.
“With our data showing 61.8% of enterprises run hybrid deployments and an additional 10% operate across multi-cloud environments, Red Hat’s hybrid-first platform strategy aligns closely with where enterprise infrastructure lives today,” Weston said.
Red Hat’s established OpenShift footprint provides a foundation for connecting these developments. As enterprises deploy more autonomous workloads, the company is positioned to combine Kubernetes orchestration, agent isolation and distributed inference within its broader hybrid cloud strategy.
The opportunity extends beyond any individual project. OpenShift, llm-d and OpenShell illustrate how Red Hat is contributing to an open infrastructure model that accommodates both conventional applications and emerging AI agents.
For enterprises, the objective is to make AI workloads secure, efficient and manageable without losing control over how autonomous systems operate. Red Hat’s work across the Kubernetes ecosystem reflects how that foundation is taking shape.

articles.title: Un error informático incluye a los mayores de 70 años en el sorteo de las mesas electorales de Vigo
articles.text:
A veces las listas fallan en dos direcciones. Japón revisó su censo y descubrió que le faltaban 3 millones de personas. Pero en Vigo el fallo fue el inverso: el sorteo de las mesas del 29N incluyó a gente que la ley debería dejar fuera por edad. El primer síntoma fueron las llamadas y visitas de mayores, algunos de más de 90 años, a la Junta Electoral de Zona. Allan Karlsson, el centenario que se fugó por la ventana para no ir a su fiesta de cumpleaños, habría hecho lo mismito con la carta.
Qué dice la ley. Partamos de lo básico, para no perdernos. Una mesa electoral la forman un presidente y dos vocales. Cada cargo tiene 2 suplentes. En total, 9 personas por mesa. Los ayuntamientos las eligen por sorteo público, bajo la supervisión de la Junta Electoral de Zona. El artículo 26 de la ley electoral limita el bombo a los electores de cada mesa que sepan leer y escribir y sean menores de 70 años. A partir de los 65 se puede renunciar en 7 días.
Más datos: el sorteo siempre cae entre el día 25 y el 29 posteriores a la convocatoria: este año ha sido del 31 de octubre al 4 de noviembre, con casi 550.000 personas convocadas en toda España para las elecciones del 29 de noviembre. El INE fijó el periodo electoral entre el 6 de octubre y el 29 de noviembre.
El fallo. Vigo celebró el sorteo el 2 de noviembre, a las 10:00, en pleno extraordinario. La parte pública fueron 9 números que sacó un programa informático. Según el Concello, un “error informático” impidió aplicar bien el filtro de edad y entraron en el sorteo ciudadanos de más de 70 años. La aplicación del INE que usan los ayuntamientos descarta a esos electores de forma automática, aunque algunos municipios tienen su propia herramienta. Pero se desconoce cuál usó Vigo y en qué punto falló el filtro.
La carta. La ley da 3 días para notificar. Las cartas, que reparte habitualmente Policía Local, empezaron a entregarse el jueves 5. Ese mismo día y a lo largo del viernes y el lunes 9, numerosas personas mayores telefonearon o se presentaron en la Junta Electoral de Zona, en la Ciudad de la Justicia. Hubo casos de más de 80 y de más de 90 años.
En algunos casos, llamaron familiares extrañados. Y claro, entre las consecuencias de ignorar una designación figura el artículo 143, así que preguntar es lo sensato. ¿Y qué hizo el Concello? Detectó la incidencia y generó un nuevo listado. La Policía Local sigue notificando “de forma ordinaria”, en comunicación continua con la Junta. Si bien desconocemos cuántos mayores de 70 salieron elegidos, sí hubo que repetir el sorteo.
Las 8:00, para todos. Eso sí, el cargo es obligatorio. El artículo 80 cita a presidente, vocales y suplentes a las 8:00 en el colegio, una hora antes de abrir las urnas. Ser segundo suplente no te libra del madrugón (y encima sin bocata ni cobro). La mesa no se constituye sin tres titulares: si falta alguno, entra un suplente. Si llegan los tres, los suplentes solo actúan si hacen falta. La dieta suelen ser unos 75 euros y se goza de permiso laboral si ese día de toca trabajar.
El precio de faltar. El artículo 143 castiga a titulares y suplentes que no acudan, abandonen sin causa legítima o incumplan la obligación de excusa o aviso previo. La pena: prisión de 3 meses a 1 año o multa de 6 a 24 meses. Para evitarla existe la excusa, que se presenta ante la Junta Electoral de Zona y ella decide en 5 días sobre las alegaciones registradas.
¿Cuántas son? Entre las presentadas en persona, por correo electrónico y en la web mesaselectorales.es, para ayer lunes 9, la Junta ya superaba las 300 excusas (no en vano Galicia es casi una zona cero en términos de baja natalidad y la pirámide poblacional está invertida hasta una tasa de reemplazo de 1.1). Son más de las que acumulaba a estas alturas en julio de 2023, cuando el verano disparó las renuncias por vacaciones. El plazo para alegar seguía abierto.

articles.title: Intel and Altera Partner for Edge and Physical AI Development
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
Intel and Altera Partner for Edge and Physical AI Development
Intel and Altera today announced a collaboration to develop a flexible, real-time sensor bridge for a range of Edge & Physical AI industries including healthcare, aerospace and defense, and robotics applications. By combining Intel compute, connectivity and software with Altera FPGAs, the companies aim to help original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) address the growing complexity of connecting, processing and acting on real-world data across increasingly sensor-rich edge environments.
Edge and Physical AI systems can require data from different sensors and interfaces to be brought together while meeting requirements for timing, performance, power and cost. Some applications also require very high bandwidth or flexible form factors in which input/output (I/O) is located away from the compute board. Sensor data must then be streamed rapidly into memory for the host Intel processor to use across edge, robotics and other workloads.Intel and Altera plan to address these challenges through modular reference solutions that combine programmable hardware with a consistent Intel compute and software foundation. The goal is to give OEMs greater flexibility as applications, sensors and workloads evolve, while helping them move more efficiently from prototype to deployment.
Dan Rodriguez, corporate vice president and general manager, Edge Computing Group, IntelAs sensors multiply at the edge and through Physical AI systems, our customers need a simpler way to turn real-world data into timely action. Together with Altera, we aim to give OEMs a flexible foundation that simplifies integration and helps them move faster from prototype to market deployment while meeting their needs across performance, power and cost.
Farhad Shafai, head of business solutions and marketing at AlteraPhysical AI systems have to sense, decide, and act in real time, and the physical world demands accuracy, reliability, and safety. Altera FPGAs provide the sensor connectivity, data processing, and deterministic control that machines need to respond to the physical world, and they stay programmable as sensors and AI models evolve. Combining that with Intel's compute and software is intended to give OEMs a flexible foundation to tailor systems to their needs.
Applying programmable, real-time processing across edge markets
Intel and Altera plan to apply the collaboration across multiple markets where real-time processing and programmable computing matter most. These capabilities will be accessible to developers through Intel's Open Edge Platform SDK and an Altera SDK.
- Healthcare: The companies are jointly developing a reference solution targeting the stringent latency and real-time requirements of advanced healthcare equipment.
- Aerospace and defense: Intel and Altera are collaborating on reference solutions for next-generation mission systems, with a focus on size, weight and power requirements for converged AI and signal-processing workloads.
- Robotics: Intel and Altera plan to combine Intel compute, connectivity and robotics software with Altera FPGA technology to help address the increasingly complex sensing, timing and real-time processing requirements of intelligent machines.
Together, Intel and Altera aim to help OEMs move faster from prototype to deployment with programmable real-time sensor bridge reference solutions that are designed to reduce integration complexity while addressing performance, power and cost requirements across a range of edge applications.

articles.title: AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’
articles.text:
AMD VP and chief Zen architect rebuke claims that Nvidia and Arm made CPUs for agentic AI — ‘We didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing’
AMD’s new Venice chips aren’t agentic CPUs, but they’re the best CPUs for agentic AI, says AMD.
Two prominent voices within AMD agree that the company didn’t design its new Zen 6 family, codenamed Venice, explicitly for agentic AI in a clear shot at Nvidia and Arm, who’ve both described their latest data center CPUs as “agentic” in nature. In separate talks, AMD’s chief Zen architect Mike Clark and corporate VP Madhu Rangarajan said that the company didn’t predict the agentic wave when Zen 6 development started.
We just wrapped up testing AMD's Venice CPUs, which you can read more about in our Zen 6 benchmarking article.
CPU development cycles are measured in years, and given that the agentic frenzy around CPUs hit around March of this year, it’s unreasonable to expect that anyone has developed silicon specifically for agentic AI, much less a general-purpose data center CPU. And still, Nvidia claims its Vera CPU was “purpose-built” for agentic AI, while Arm says its AGI CPU was “designed for the demands of agentic AI.”
“We think that the EPYC 9006 CPU is the best CPU for the agentic era, and spoiler alert, we didn’t magically know four years ago that agentic was going to be a thing and purpose-built something for agentic,” said Rangarajan in a session with media. “The reality is an agentic workflow is a diverse set of tasks… and in order to execute those tasks well, you need compute that is able to handle a diverse set of workloads with a full portfolio.”
Introducing the Zen 6 microarchitecture, Mike Clark agreed with the sentiment: “I’m not going to mislead and act like I knew agentic computing was coming, or we knew it, but we did strongly believe that the CPU would always have a place in the software ecosystem of AI… And as agentic [has] blown up, we [are] able to now deploy that for agentic compute workloads.”
As AMD rolls out its next-generation microarchitecture with Venice CPUs, it’s targeting the messaging from Arm and Nvidia, which have posed the most direct threat to AMD’s continued rise in the data center on the back of agentic workloads. And indeed, there are performance vectors where Nvidia’s Vera looks strong for agentic workloads, as you can see in our Nvidia Vera testing. AMD’s argument, however, is that agentic AI calls for a broad range of CPUs just as general-purpose workloads do, pushing back on the single-SKU approach of Nvidia and Arm.
Our testing of two AMD Venice chips supports that argument, as well, with the dense EPYC 9996 with its 256 cores and 512 threads offering peak throughput performance, while the frequency-optimized EPYC 9686F goes toe-to-toe with Vera in the role of an AI host node. AMD is launching two additional ranges next year, with Venice-X targeting HPC with its 3D-stack cache, and Verano going directly after Vera as an AI host node with an LPDDR5X memory system.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Although the workload characteristics of agentic AI are still in the process of being defined, we have a better understanding of how those loops work now than we did at the beginning of the year. And like all complex topics, the answer to what is important in a CPU for agentic AI is the always-disappointing “it depends.”
As we break down in our early testing procedure for agentic AI, the workload characteristics and demand on the CPU/memory are defined by what the agent is doing, and in the data center, what several agents are doing at high concurrency when sandboxed. A coding agent will generally call more tools that are taxing on the CPU than a web browsing agent, for example, while an agent that queries a database may call for strong memory performance.
Of course, there are some vectors of performance that can’t be addressed with different SKUs (such as that strong memory performance). However, the potential diversity of agentic workloads certainly makes an argument for CPU variety. At a most basic level, an agentic loop allows the LLM to understand functions you’ve defined, and then pass arguments to those functions to execute them. We’re talking about a workload as broad as what you can define in a function in languages like Python and Rust.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Jake Roach is the Senior CPU Analyst at Tom’s Hardware, writing reviews, news, and features about the latest consumer and workstation processors.

Alors, quitte à vous équiper, autant vous tourner vers un modèle doté d’un grand écran. C’est ce que propose la tablette Teclast T65, qui dispose d’un écran IPS de 13,4 pouces. Pourquoi choisir la tablette Teclast T65 ?
- Pour son grand écran : les 13,4 pouces offrent une surface confortable pour regarder des vidéos, surfer sur Internet et consulter des documents.

Une tablette aussi grande que certains PC portables

Un grand format en entrée de gamme
La Teclast T65 fonctionne sous Android 16 et donne accès à un grand écran pour un prix raisonnable. En contrepartie, elle pèse assez lourd avec ses 720 g, et ses performances restent globalement modestes, notamment pour jouer à des titres gourmands.

❌ Les limites

articles.title: Google dévoile Gemini 4 Carbon, l'IA qui veut repousser les limites de l'IA
articles.text:
Dix jours seulement après avoir dévoilé Gemini 4 Argon, Google est de retour avec un nouveau modèle baptisé Gemini 4 Carbon. L’entreprise américaine assure qu’il est question de son modèle « le plus puissant » à ce jour. Selon Google, Gemini 4 Carbon « offre des performances de pointe dans les workflows agentiques de longue durée, notamment pour les tâches complexes liées à la connaissance, l’ingénierie logicielle, la cybersécurité et le raisonnement scientifique ».
Un modèle taillé pour les tâches complexes
Autant dire que Gemini 4 Carbon est un modèle très haut de gamme. Google explique qu’il « est conçu pour les tâches qui mettent à l’épreuve les limites de l’intelligence d’un modèle, comme le développement et le débogage complexes en plusieurs étapes, ainsi que la recherche et la découverte scientifiques ouvertes ». Ses capacités de raisonnement en mathématiques, en physique et dans les sciences de la vie seraient particulièrement avancées.
Ce modèle serait capable de prendre en charge des projets particulièrement complexes comme la conception architecturale, la coordination et l’audit du code. Il serait aussi capable de gérer des projets de développement complexes, de détecter et corriger des erreurs et de vérifier lui-même le fonctionnement des applications créées. Gemini 4 Carbon serait également plus performant en conception 3D et en développement de jeux vidéo. Google en a aussi profité pour dévoiler la fonctionnalité /swarm dans Antigravity. Son principe est simple : transformer une simple instruction en une équipe d’agents IA capable de se coordonner pour mener un projet à bien.
Un modèle pensé pour la cybersécurité
À l’heure où les découvertes de failles critiques et les cyberattaques se multiplient, Google explique que Gemini 4 Carbon « fournit aux équipes de sécurité les capacités d’analyse de bout en bout dont elles ont besoin pour protéger les logiciels critiques ». L’entreprise américaine précise que ce modèle « peut notamment inspecter des logiciels, retracer la manière dont des failles peuvent être combinées entre différents systèmes et générer des correctifs vérifiés s’attaquant à la cause profonde des problèmes ». En résumé, Gemini 4 Carbon pourrait permettre de limiter le nombre de cyberattaques.
Alors que les cas d’IA échappant au contrôle de leurs concepteurs se multiplient, qu’en est-il de la sécurité de Gemini 4 Carbon ? Google assure avoir mis en place de « solides mécanismes de sécurité » afin de renforcer sa résistance aux utilisations abusives et aux injections de prompts. Google explique avoir également travaillé sur l’alignement de Gemini 4 Carbon afin de limiter les comportements imprévus et de garantir que le modèle respecte les consignes qui lui sont données. Espérons que cela soit bel et bien le cas.
Gemini 4 Carbon est disponible dès maintenant pour les développeurs et les entreprises. Le grand public peut également y accéder, mais uniquement avec un abonnement Google AI Ultra, depuis l’application Gemini et le mode IA de Google Search.

Les Anneaux de pouvoir : quand sortent les épisodes de la saison 3 sur Prime Video ?
Sauron, Elrond, Gandalf, Galadriel et le reste de la Terre du Milieu reviennent sur Prime Video dans la nouvelle saison des Anneaux de pouvoir. Voici quand retrouver les nouveaux épisodes de la série sur le service de streaming d'Amazon.
Deux ans après une saison 2 qui avait donné aux spectateurs et aux fans quelques frissons et des motifs d'espoir pour la suite, la prestigieuse série Les Anneaux de pouvoir revient enfin sur Prime Video pour une très attendue troisième saison.
Mais attention, la sortie des épisodes de cette nouvelle saison est faite de manière bien particulière. C'est pour cela que Les Numériques vous présente ici le calendrier de diffusion précis, pour que vous ne ratiez rien de ce retour en Terre du Milieu.
Quelle est l'histoire de cette saison 3 des Anneaux de pouvoir ?
Cette troisième saison se déroule cinq après les événements de la saison 2, qui a vu la chute d'Eregion après que Celembrimbor a aidé Sauron à forger les anneaux de pouvoir. Les armées du Seigneur des Ténèbres ont conquis une grosse partie de la Terre du Milieu, et seuls quelques bastions isolés - Khazad-dûm, Lindon, Fondcombe... - résistent encore à la victoire de Sauron.
Les Elfes, les Nains et les Hommes vont tenter d'unir leurs forces pour lutter contre l'armée du Mordor, mais dans sa tour de Barad-dûr tout juste achevée, le Seigneur des Ténèbres travaille sans relâche, obsédé par la volonté de maîtriser un pouvoir capable de mettre ses derniers ennemis à genoux : un Anneau unique pour les gouverner tous...
Combien d'épisodes pour cette saison 3 ?
Tout comme la première et la deuxième saison, ce nouveau chapitre est composé de huit épisodes. Les durées de ceux-ci oscillent entre 51 minutes et 1 heure et 10 minutes.
Mais contrairement aux programmes Netflix, dévoilés en un seul coup en format "binge", ou à ceux de la chaîne HBO qui privilégie une diffusion hebdomadaire, Prime Video a fait le choix d'une sortie un peu spéciale des épisodes, comme on vous le détaille ci-dessous.

articles.title: Nvidia e CEO são processados por omitir caso com executiva chinesa • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nvidia e CEO são processados por omitir caso com executiva chinesa
Acionistas dizem que empresa não informou riscos ligados à relação de Jensen Huang com Alice Huang, ex-executiva da Megaspeed.
A Nvidia e seu CEO, Jensen Huang, foram processados por acionistas que acusam a empresa de esconder do mercado riscos relacionados à suposta relação do executivo com Alice Huang. Ela é ex-executiva da Megaspeed, companhia investigada nos EUA por possíveis violações das restrições à exportação de chips para a China.
A ação coletiva foi apresentada nessa segunda-feira (09/11), alegando que a falta de transparência ajudou a manter as ações da Nvidia artificialmente valorizadas.
O processo parte de uma investigação aberta pela própria empresa para descobrir se Huang foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência estrangeira. As suspeitas foram levantadas após o CEO admitir ter sido infiel à esposa. Ele, porém, não confirmou publicamente o relacionamento com Alice.
A ação é liderada pelo acionista Mark Kistenmacher. Segundo o processo, Nvidia e Huang fizeram declarações enganosas ou deixaram de informar fatos relevantes que poderiam afetar a avaliação dos investidores sobre a companhia. Os acionistas argumentam que o possível relacionamento com Alice pode representar riscos regulatórios, comerciais e de segurança nacional.
Com a revelação do caso extraconjugal, as ações da fabricante fecharam a segunda-feira em queda de 4,3%, eliminando cerca de US$ 190 bilhões (cerca de R$ 1 trilhão) em valor de mercado.
A Nvidia é uma das empresas mais expostas às restrições impostas por Washington à venda de chips avançados para a China. Os Estados Unidos restringem há anos a exportação dos aceleradores mais potentes da empresa ao país, por receio de que eles sejam usados no desenvolvimento de sistemas militares.
Huang construiu nos últimos anos um papel de articulador no setor, se posicionando abertamente contra restrições à indústria. Em maio deste ano, o executivo revelou que a participação da companhia no mercado de IA da China havia despencado a 0%, alertando que isso incentivaria a indústria interna da China a atingir autossuficiência tecnológica através de concorrentes como a Huawei.
Antes mesmo do processo, o conselho de administração da Nvidia criou um comitê independente para apurar o caso. A investigação busca determinar se Huang foi deliberadamente alvo de uma operação de inteligência e se houve exposição de informações da Nvidia ou dos Estados Unidos.
Até agora, a empresa afirma que não encontrou motivos para acreditar que segredos comerciais tenham sido comprometidos. Huang disse aos funcionários que cooperará com a investigação e reconheceu apenas a infidelidade.

articles.title: 'Designed to blend in, not stand out': This Dolby Atmos soundbar uses a fabric design to fit into your room's decor — and it has Denon and Marantz heritage behind it
articles.text:
This powerful new Dolby Atmos soundbar has 14 speakers and a fabric design that's meant to blend into the room — and it comes from a brand-new company with Denon and Marantz heritage behind it
The Knit Form is a home theater soundbar unlike any other
- 14-channel Class D amplification and Dolby Atmos 5.1.2
- Five colors of Threadform fabric to blend with your decor
- $999 (about £745 / AU$1,422)
For as long as there have been speakers, there have been attempts to make them look less speaker-y — but as far as I know, there's never been an attempt to make them look like someone knitted them. Enter the Knit Form, a serious soundbar with a very unusual design. It's intended to blend in, not stand out.
As you can see, it's very different to its rivals: if you look at our current best soundbars line-up, there's a lot of long black-grilled lozenges out there. This is much more colorful.
The Knit Form comes from the mind of Joel Sietsema, formerly senior product and brand leader at Denon and Marantz's parent company, Sound United. But its unique selling point comes courtesy of his wife, an interior designer, whose response to his speaker concepts was to want every one of them hidden. The Knit Form is the result of that, Sietsema says. "Form is what happens when you design for the home first. It should look like furniture, sound incredible, and be easily integrated into the technology you’ve already welcomed in your space.”
It may look like a draught excluder but this is a high-end soundbar with a serious specification, serious backers and serious audio expertise. And that fabric isn't exactly ordinary either.
Knit Form soundbar: key features and pricing
Let's start on the outside. The fabric is Threadform, an acoustically transparent textile that keeps its color and lasts a long time. It's available in five different colors on the Form.
Beneath the Threadform there's a 14-channel, class D amp delivering 5.1.2 Dolby Atmos via its internal drivers, center dialog speaker and dual subwoofers. It has Bluetooth 5.3 input with AirPlay, Google Cast and Spotify Connect, and it also transmits audio over Auracast. There's a single HDMI ARC/eARC for the TV and an optional smartphone app that enables you to customize the sound settings.
The Knit Form is designed to get out of the way of your entertainment. There's no front-facing logo; the status lights turn off during viewing; and the five colors are "designed to complement a space rather than compete with it." I really like it, especially in the terracotta-ish Ember colorway. It's recommended for TVs 55 inches or over.

articles.title: SoftBank, inversora en OpenAI, perdió USD 7.000 millones en tres meses y sorprendió a los analistas
articles.text:
El grupo japonés SoftBank informó una pérdida neta de 1,1 billones de yenes (USD 7.000 millones) en el trimestre de julio a septiembre. El resultado contrasta con la ganancia de 2,5 billones de yenes del mismo período del año anterior y quedó muy por debajo de lo que esperaban los analistas.
Según Reuters, tres analistas consultados por LSEG proyectaban entre una ganancia de 233.000 millones de yenes y una pérdida de 113.000 millones. Bloomberg indicó que el promedio de ocho analistas apuntaba a una ganancia de 129.000 millones de yenes. Es la primera pérdida neta de la compañía en casi dos años, de acuerdo con Bloomberg.
SoftBank es uno de los principales inversores externos de OpenAI, la empresa creadora de ChatGPT. Hasta septiembre había aportado USD 54,6 millones de millones...
Pagos adelantados por equipos que ya no usará
El informe financiero de la empresa atribuye una parte central del golpe a una pérdida de 597.200 millones de yenes (unos USD 3.700 millones) registrada en el semestre. Surgió de reajustar las compras de equipos de generación eléctrica para proyectos de centros de datos de IA en Estados Unidos.
De ese total, 457.000 millones de yenes corresponden a pagos adelantados que no se pueden recuperar y 140.200 millones a modificaciones de contratos y acuerdos de compensación. Reuters precisó que una filial de SoftBank había invertido en ese equipamiento y que los planes se revisaron después.
El segundo factor es el costo de la deuda. Los gastos financieros del trimestre llegaron a 461.900 millones de yenes, más del doble que un año antes, por un préstamo con garantía en acciones de Arm, emisiones récord de bonos y tasas de interés más altas, según Investing.com.
En el semestre, el informe de la empresa muestra gastos financieros de 790.700 millones de yenes. SoftBank realizó importantes colocaciones de bonos y devolvió por anticipado USD 25.900 millones de un préstamo puente que había pedido en marzo para financiar su aporte a OpenAI.
Los fondos de inversión y el valor de OpenAI
El segmento de los Vision Fund, los fondos con los que SoftBank invierte en cientos de startups, registró una pérdida de 81.580 millones de yenes en el trimestre, frente a una ganancia de 2,38 billones un año antes, según CNBC. La caída de acciones como Coupang y Grab pesó sobre el resultado del segmento.
Bloomberg agregó que las bajas de Arm e Intel, empresas en las que SoftBank tiene participación, también pesaron en el resultado. Las ventas del semestre subieron 13,3%, hasta 4,24 billones de yenes, impulsadas por telecomunicaciones y por el negocio de cómputo para IA, según la empresa.
SoftBank valuó su participación en OpenAI en USD 99.600 millones, sin cambios desde el cierre del año fiscal anterior. La compañía completó en octubre los USD 30.000 millones de inversiones adicionales que había acordado en febrero, con lo que su aporte acumulado asciende a USD 64.600 millones y su participación a cerca de 13%.
Las acciones cayeron más de la mitad desde junio
Pese al resultado, las acciones de SoftBank cerraron con un alza de 13,9% el martes, en un día de rebote de las tecnológicas asiáticas, según CNBC. Bloomberg indicó que el título acumula una caída superior a 50% desde su máximo de junio, por el temor a la deuda tomada para apostar por la IA.
El 6 de noviembre, Reuters informó que el costo de asegurar la deuda de SoftBank contra un incumplimiento llegó a su nivel más alto en cuatro años. Ese día las acciones habían caído 11%. Bloomberg sumó que los inversores temen que el triunfo demócrata en las elecciones legislativas de Estados Unidos frene proyectos del fundador, Masayoshi Son.
La salida a bolsa de OpenAI, que permitiría a SoftBank convertir su participación en dinero, se postergó hasta 2027, según Reuters.

articles.title: Staera launches with $4.6M to develop an optical interconnect for chiplets - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Staera launches with $4.6M to develop an optical interconnect for chiplets
Staera Semiconductor Inc., a startup that develops technology for linking together chiplets, launched today with $4.6 million in pre-seed funding.
Singaporean fund Openspace Capital led the investment. It was joined by SGInnovate, Black Kite Capital, 28 Holdings, In Group and financial software company Decimus Technologies.
High-end artificial intelligence accelerators comprise multiple chiplets, silicon dies that each perform a narrow set of tasks. They’re linked together by a kind of miniature network that also functions as the host accelerator’s base layer.
That miniature network takes the form of an interposer, an advanced device that sometimes includes computing circuits, or a bridge. A bridge is essentially a small interposer that costs less to make.
Interposers and bridges both use tiny copper wires to move data between the chiplets they connect. San Francisco-based Staera hopes to replace those copper wires with optical links. According to the company, optical technology is faster and uses less power. It can also transmit data over longer distances without slowing down, which enables chipmakers to build bigger accelerators.
“Copper performance plummets over the millimeter-to-meter distances that matter most in AI accelerators, and bolt-on optics add power and complexity.” said Chief Executive Officer Andrew Kim. “We build the light into the chip, the entire optical link inside a chip, so the connection gets smaller, cooler and faster with each generation.”
Staera’s first product is called Lightwire. It transmits data over optical links, or waveguides, made of a transparent material known as silicon nitride. Light beams can only travel through a transparent material if their wavelengths fall within a specific range. Silicon nitride supports a larger range of wavelengths than many alternatives and causes less light loss, which boosts connection speeds.
The light beams into which Lightwire encodes data traffic are produced by miniature LEDs. Those devices are made of gallium nitride, a compound that is widely used in optical systems because it has a direct bandgap.
The electrons that orbit an atomic nucleus have different energy levels known as bands. Light is produced when an electron jumps from one band to one another and then collides with a quasiparticle called an electron hole.
Usually, the process also involves a second quasiparticle known as a phonon. Direct bandgap materials such as gallium nitride don’t require a phonon, which makes the light generation process more efficient.
Staera says Lightwire transmits data between an AI accelerator’s chiplets at a rate of up to 8 gigabits per second. The technology can provide more than 600 optical links per square millimeter. In practice, that means a Lightwire-powered HBM4 memory stack can move up to 24 terabits of data per second instead of the 2.8 terabits supported by current technologies.
Staera’s funding round will advance its commercialization efforts. It will enhance Lightwire, grow its U.S. team and build out a manufacturing supply chain. The company hopes to begin commercial shipments in 2030.
