articles.title: Motorola deixa escapar nome de novo dobrável "passaporte" • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Motorola deixa escapar nome de novo dobrável “passaporte”
Flex aparece em página de suporte da fabricante com referência a 2027, mas ainda não foi anunciado oficialmente.
Resumo
- Motorola deixa escapar o nome Razr Flex em seu site de suporte na Austrália.
- Registro menciona 2027, mas não confirma uma data de lançamento.
- Novo dobrável deve ter formato de passaporte e tela interna de 6,92 polegadas.
A Motorola deixou escapar o possível nome de seu próximo celular dobrável em formato de passaporte: será Motorola Razr Flex. Uma página de suporte da fabricante na Austrália antecipou informações e revelou o nome do produto.
A referência identificada pelo Android Authority apareceu em uma área de testes do site da Motorola, incluindo uma seção de atualizações de segurança destinada aos smartphones da linha Razr. A página ainda apresenta informações provisórias.
Razr Flex deve ter tela de 6,92 polegadas
A Motorola já havia antecipado um novo celular dobrável em setembro, poucas horas depois da apresentação do iPhone Duo. Na ocasião, a fabricante publicou um vídeo mostrando a silhueta de um aparelho mais largo, com proporções semelhantes às de um passaporte.
O formato é diferente dos modelos Razr tradicionais, que se dobram verticalmente. A proposta seria oferecer um celular compacto quando fechado, mas com uma tela mais ampla ao ser aberto, seguindo a tendência de aparelhos como o iPhone Duo e o Galaxy Z Fold 8.
Segundo vazamentos anteriores, o Razr Flex poderá ter tela interna OLED de 6,92 polegadas, com taxa de atualização de 165 Hz, e display externo de 4,97 polegadas. O aparelho seria menor que o Razr Fold, apresentado pela Motorola em janeiro com tela interna de 8,1 polegadas.
Já os esboços revelados pelo site Android Headlines mostram uma barra de câmeras horizontal centralizada na traseira, que poderia evitar que o aparelho balance quando apoiado sobre uma mesa. Os desenhos também indicam uma câmera frontal na tela externa e outra no canto superior direito do painel interno.
O projeto também teria acabamento em vidro 3D e uma tela dobrável com vinco menos aparente, conforme informações atribuídas a documentos internos da fabricante.
As especificações ainda não confirmadas incluem processador Snapdragon 8 Gen 5, 12 GB de RAM e bateria de 5.000 mAh. O conjunto fotográfico poderá reunir duas câmeras traseiras de 50 megapixels, além de sensores frontais de 32 megapixels.
Motorola ainda não confirmou lançamento
A referência a 2027 reforça a possibilidade de que o novo dobrável seja apresentado no próximo ano. Vazamentos anteriores indicavam até uma possível estreia ainda em dezembro de 2026. O número também pode fazer parte da identificação da geração do produto, como ocorre com outros smartphones Razr. Portanto, não é possível afirmar que a página de suporte confirme uma data de lançamento.
A expectativa é que o Razr Flex complemente o catálogo de dobráveis da Motorola, oferecendo uma alternativa menor ao Razr Fold. A fabricante ainda não confirmou as especificações, o preço ou os mercados que receberão o novo aparelho, incluindo o Brasil.

articles.title: Who Pays for AI Data Center Power Costs? How the U.S. and China Compare - EE Times
articles.text:
In 40 of 41 local ballot contests across 10 U.S. states on Nov. 3, voters favored limiting data center development.
The measures included bans, moratoriums, rejected zoning proposals, and nonbinding votes. Their legal consequences vary, but they signal growing scrutiny of the electricity, land, and public resources required by large computing facilities.
Meanwhile, developers are competing to secure power capacity years before their facilities will operate.
The U.S. relies on utilities, regulators, and local governments to negotiate these commitments. China coordinates computing infrastructure and energy resources through national development programs.
Both face the same uncertainty: How much infrastructure should be built before future computing demand is known, and who pays when forecasts prove wrong?
Computing moves faster than the grid
The International Energy Agency projects global data center electricity consumption rising from approximately 485 terawatt-hours in 2025 to 950 TWh by 2030. Consumption at AI-focused facilities is expected to triple.
AI accelerator generations change within years. Substations, transformers, and transmission connections are designed to operate for decades. Utilities must therefore finance long-lived infrastructure against demand forecasts shaped by a much faster technology cycle.
The challenge also involves power characteristics. Training, inference, and facility-level power management create different load profiles. On-site systems can buffer fluctuations, but utilities still need to plan for the facilities they connect.
A 500-megawatt request may require substations, transmission upgrades, and additional generation capacity before the developer consumes its first megawatt.
If the project is delayed or canceled, those costs do not disappear.
Ohio’s answer: make developers commit
In July 2025, Ohio regulators approved a dedicated tariff for large data centers served by AEP Ohio.
Qualifying developers must enter agreements with a ramp-up period of up to four years followed by eight additional years. Minimum monthly billing demand reflects contracted capacity and historical usage, subject to the tariff’s 85% contracted-capacity limit.
Developers failing specified credit-rating and liquidity tests must provide qualifying guarantees or collateral equal to 50% of minimum contractual charges over the agreement. Cancelation or substantial delay before connection can also trigger reimbursement obligations.
By February 2026, AEP Ohio reported 5,642 MW of binding contracts under the new tariff, alongside 12,219 MW contracted previously. These are commitments, not operating demand.
The tariff reduces the risk that existing electricity customers will finance infrastructure for projects that never materialize.
It also changes the economics of competition.
A hyperscaler can support long-term electricity commitments through its balance sheet. A smaller developer may need project financing, customer contracts, and external guarantees before securing comparable capacity.
Electricity access could reinforce the advantages that large technology companies already enjoy in semiconductor procurement and capital markets.
Who receives the benefits, and who pays?
PJM Interconnection operates a wholesale electricity market across parts of 13 states and Washington, DC.
In July 2026, PJM’s independent market monitor, Monitoring Analytics, estimated that data center demand accounted for approximately $6.3 billion of $16.4 billion in capacity charges associated with the latest auction. Across four auctions, it attributed $29.4 billion of $63.6 billion in total capacity charges to that demand.
These are the market monitor’s estimates of the contribution of existing and forecast data center demand to wholesale capacity charges, not amounts billed directly to data center operators or households. Actual cost recovery depends on market arrangements and retail tariffs.
Local governments see a different balance sheet.
Fairfax County, Virginia, estimated approximately $110.6 million in data center-related general fund tax revenue for tax year 2026.
Those revenues benefit the county, while electricity infrastructure costs may extend across a wider network. The Fairfax and PJM figures cover different jurisdictions and do not establish a direct subsidy.
They illustrate a structural problem: The institutions approving projects and collecting tax revenues are not necessarily those allocating electricity infrastructure costs.
Regulation becomes a competitive variable
In June 2026, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued orders requiring six regional grid operators to justify or propose reforms to rules for connecting large electricity users and allocating associated costs. The proceedings do not themselves impose new tariffs.
Developers must increasingly evaluate collateral requirements, connection charges, and regulatory uncertainty alongside land prices, fiber connectivity, and computing equipment.
There is no cost-free solution.
Weak commitments expose electricity customers to speculative projects. Strict requirements can favor companies with stronger balance sheets, potentially excluding viable competitors.
America’s decentralized system permits local scrutiny and commercial discipline, but coordination across utilities, markets, and regulators can be expensive and slow.
China is testing a different model.
China’s coordinated approach
China’s Eastern Data, Western Computing initiative uses nationally coordinated computing hubs and data center clusters to align infrastructure investment with regional electricity resources, land, and network connectivity.
Suitable workloads are encouraged toward resource-rich western regions, while latency-sensitive services remain closer to major economic centers.
That distinction matters technically. Training and inference have different requirements for latency, bandwidth, and data movement. Cheap electricity does not make every location suitable for every workload.
China can coordinate electricity infrastructure, industrial development, and state-owned investment more directly than the U.S. This may reduce barriers created by fragmented planning and approval processes.
But coordination does not guarantee productive demand.
Infrastructure built around development targets can remain underutilized. When commercial demand disappoints, losses may be absorbed by state-owned enterprises, lenders, or institutions supporting the projects.
America risks delaying viable capacity or concentrating development among financially stronger companies. China risks committing capital to capacity that customers cannot use economically.
The outcome cannot be judged by the number of announced projects or installed megawatts alone.
Four tests for 2030
The competition between these infrastructure models should be evaluated against four measures:
- Time to operation: How long does it take to turn an electricity request into a commercially operating computing facility?
- Delivered cost: What is the total cost of securing reliable power, including network investments, financing, and contractual commitments?
- Utilization: How much installed computing capacity generates productive workloads rather than remaining idle or constrained?
- Financial exposure: Who absorbs losses when demand forecasts fail?
Differences in electricity pricing, financing structures, and public reporting will complicate comparisons, but these questions reveal more than headline investment announcements.
By 2030, leadership in AI infrastructure may depend as much on electricity access and financial capacity as on processor performance.
For both the U.S. and China, the decisive measure will be how efficiently investment in electricity infrastructure becomes computing capacity that customers use.

articles.title: UAE's Wafr attracts angel investment to digitise sukuk issuance and settlement
articles.text:
UAE's Wafr attracts angel investment to digitise sukuk issuance and settlement
- UAE-based fintech Wafr has secured an undisclosed pre-seed funding round, with participation from angel investors Coen Jonker, co-founder of Tyme Group, and Neal Cross, former chief innovation officer at DBS Bank.
- Co-founded by Mahmoud Bouchelif and Anthony Murphy in 2026, Wafr is developing a global Islamic finance platform offering Shariah-compliant financial services to individuals, businesses and financial institutions.
- The company has launched WafrChain, a permissioned blockchain platform designed to manage sukuk issuance, distribution, settlement and profit payments. It supports settlement in fiat currencies and stablecoins, with Shariah approvals recorded on-chain.
- Wafr plans to expand its institutional offering into fund tokenisation, tokenised deposits, trade finance and B2B settlement, alongside future consumer services including international accounts, cross-border remittances and payment cards, subject to regulatory approvals.
Press release:
Wafr, a financial technology company building a global Islamic financial platform, today announces its pre-seed funding round and the launch of WafrChain, its first product for on-chain Shariah-compliant sukuk, with sukuk tokenisation now live on the platform.
The round brings together individual investors, including Coen Jonker, co-founder of Tyme Group and former Commonwealth Bank of Australia Group Executive, and Neal Cross, co-founder of PictureWealth and former Chief Innovation Officer of DBS Bank.
Wafr’s co-founding team includes Chief Executive Officer Mahmoud Bouchelif, a former Islamic banker and founder of LeanTech SG, and Chief Product Officer Anthony Murphy, whose experience includes launching digital banking products at AMP, Commonwealth Bank of Australia and Macquarie Bank. Bouchelif built LeanTech SG into a profitable business with 7-figure revenue, without external funding, and has advised GCC banking leaders on digital transformation for approximately a decade.
Wafr’s purpose, “Abundance for everyone”, reflects its ambition to make fair, transparent and ethical financial services accessible across borders. The company is building towards a global financial platform rooted in Shariah-compliant principles and open to people of every faith, connecting institutional infrastructure with services for individuals and businesses.
Sukuk remain one of the most complex instruments in Islamic finance to bring to market. A single issuance typically involves eight separate parties, including the issuer, the trustee, arrangers, the Shariah board, custodians, the paying agent, distributors and investors, each keeping its own record of the same instrument. Every transfer, profit payment and corporate action is re-keyed and reconciled between them, adding cost, delay and the risk of error to each issuance, which can take many months and in some cases more than a year to bring to market.
WafrChain is a private, permissioned blockchain designed to connect the institutions involved in the sukuk lifecycle through a shared record. Instrument terms, including unit price, profit schedule and maturity, are recorded on-chain alongside the approval of the issuer’s own Shariah board before distribution, while Wafr’s Shariah board works with each issuer to confirm that the structure is compliant. The platform connects issuers with distributors and institutional buyers and uses smart contracts to route profit payments. Settlement can take place in fiat currency, through local real-time gross settlement systems and SWIFT, or in stablecoins, and institutions can integrate WafrChain with their existing systems through a single API.
The network has been built for the speed and confidentiality that financial institutions require. Transactions reach finality in 300 milliseconds, and each participant can see only its own activity, so issuers, distributors and investors keep their positions private from one another. WafrChain is also designed to continue operating with only a third of its nodes active.
Mahmoud Bouchelif, co-founder and chief executive officer of Wafr, said:
“Islamic finance can bring abundance to people, businesses and economies, yet access to services that reflect its principles remains uneven. We are building Wafr for everyone who believes finance should be fair, transparent and ethical, whatever their faith. WafrChain is our starting point, giving institutions a foundation for bringing Shariah-compliant assets on-chain while we develop the services people need to manage their financial lives across borders.”
Anthony Murphy, Co-Founder and Chief Product Officer of Wafr, said:
“At Wafr, we start with the problems people and businesses are actually facing and focus on how we can solve them in a practical way. We believe technology is critical if we are going to make Shariah-compliant and ethical financial services simpler, more accessible and more relevant to how people manage their money today, while bringing the principles behind Islamic finance to more people around the world. WafrChain is the first product built with that thinking, and it sets the direction for how we want to build at Wafr.”
Coen Jonker, co-founder of Tyme Group and an angel investor in Wafr, said:
“I have long believed that someone will build a truly global digital finance business for the Muslim world. The need is clear, the opportunity is enormous, and the technology now makes it possible to think beyond traditional banking models. Wafr is pursuing that ambition with a clear sense of purpose, and I’m excited by Mahmoud’s determination and his co-founders to make it happen.”
Neal Cross – Co-founder of PictureWealth, ex-DBS Chief Innovation Officer – added:
“Everyone talks about what blockchain could do for finance. Wafr is one of the few teams starting with the customers who need it most. Islamic finance was built on trust, transparency and shared risk, which is exactly what blockchain does best. Add founders like Mahmoud and Anthony, who don’t build things for show, and backing them was an easy decision.”
According to the ICD–LSEG Islamic Finance Development Report 2026, global Islamic finance assets reached $6.5 trillion in 2025, up 9% year on year. Sukuk outstanding stood at $1.14 trillion, while annual issuance rose 14.5% to $291.4 billion.
Beyond sukuk, Wafr’s institutional roadmap includes fund tokenisation, tokenised deposits, trade finance and business-to-business settlement. Its consumer plans span global accounts, cross-border remittances and cards, with agentic AI and stablecoin-enabled settlement forming part of its wider development strategy. These plans support Wafr’s ambition to expand financial access for unbanked and underserved communities across markets. Wafr’s consumer services will be introduced in line with the applicable regulatory processes and approvals, working with licensed partners where required.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI Runs at 30 FPS, PS5 Pro Gets PSSR and Ray Tracing
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
Grand Theft Auto VI Runs at 30 FPS, PS5 Pro Gets PSSR and Ray Tracing
Grand Theft Auto VI is now available for pre-load for gamers who pre-ordered the game, allowing them to start the download. With the game launching on November 19, Rockstar has confirmed that it will run at 30 frames per second on consoles, utilizing their integrated graphics for maximum visual fidelity. This means that while the studio has invested significant resources to maximize the performance of these console graphics cards, the game will be capped at 30 FPS to ensure stability and optimal visual quality. Current generation consoles are limited to 30 FPS, although some will receive additional features.
For instance, Sony's PlayStation 5 Pro will offer gamers PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows, exclusive to that console. Although the standard PlayStation 5 supports a similar technology called Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), a simplified version of PSSR, it will not be implemented at launch. Only the more powerful PS5 Pro will feature PSSR and ray tracing.The PlayStation 5 version will also support the DualSense controller's haptic feedback throughout gameplay, with adjustments available in the accessibility settings. Other features include enhanced spatial audio using Tempest 3D Audio and faster loading times. The Xbox Series X|S won't receive any special treatment, but Xbox One users will be able to stream the game through Xbox Cloud Gaming, using Xbox Series S graphics settings. Streaming performance will depend on connection quality and other technical factors, which may affect the experience compared to running the game locally. Grand Theft Auto VI will also support Remote Play on both PlayStation and Xbox.

articles.title: OpenAI rolls out new business profiles, making ChatGPT just a little bit more like Google | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In an effort to make ChatGPT an even better consumer discovery engine, OpenAI is launching a host of new features designed to help companies control how users interact with their businesses.
On Tuesday, the company rolled out a Business Hub that will serve as a place where companies can create business profiles that — in a feature that greatly resembles the kind of profiles that Google and other search engines already offer — allow enterprises to verify and update information about their products and services. The feature is currently in beta.
Eligible companies will also be able to create and launch a specialized business agent, which gives ChatGPT users the ability to ask questions about the business and its products.
“As people turn to AI to discover products, compare options and make decisions, ChatGPT has become the platform for people and businesses to connect through AI,” the company said on Tuesday. “Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT.”
In a move that calls to mind Google Analytics, the Business Hub will also give users access to limited business insights. These insights will reveal how ChatGPT users interact with their products — including profile views, business mentions, website clicks, and other metrics.
Businesses will have to verify their profiles through a formal process, although the company did not share specifics of what that process would entail. Benji Shomair, OpenAI’s VP of Monetization, told journalists on Monday that there are “multiple verification methods that we use for different types of business in different markets.”
OpenAI previously tried to position ChatGPT as an e-commerce hub by which users could buy products directly. This effort — which used a commission fee system — was viewed as a potentially huge source of revenue and a way to make ChatGPT a more direct Amazon competitor. However, that project ultimately failed to take off and, in March, the company retired the effort, which had even included a “checkout cart” feature.
With the integration of business profiles and intelligence, ChatGPT seems to be attempting to become more like Google, which — since the advent of the internet — has been the place where web users go to understand the companies they want to shop at. It remains to be seen whether this initiative will bear better results than the one that sought to make ChatGPT a direct e-commerce hub.

articles.title: Honda invests $166M to upgrade Ontario plant to make hybrids
articles.text:
Honda Canada has announced that it will invest C$166 million into retooling and expanding its Alliston, Ont. plant, which will provide more than 4000 jobs and expand its hybrid-electric production.
As noted by CP24, the announcement is part of a broader $867 million commitment to bolster its North American manufacturing network and to meet the growing demand for hybrid vehicles.
Now, this announcement comes following Honda’s decision to indefinitely pause its $15 billion EV expansion in Alliston, and after the automaker reported a $2.7 billion full-year loss, which the company says was attributed largely to the high costs of developing electric vehicles and shifting market conditions — choosing instead to focus on hybrids.
Speaking of hybrids, when Honda announced that it was shifting away from its EV plans, the company shared that it plans to launch 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by the year 2030, with North America as a key market.
The company says that investments in manufacturing facilities across Canada, Ohio, Alabama, and Georgia will help support production of these vehicles in North America.
Specifically, the Ohio plant (built between Honda’s existing East Liberty and Marysville assembly plants) is set to open in 2029 pending final government approvals, and will be able to manufacture nearly 240,000 vehicles annually.
Honda also shared that it is working with both the federal and Ontario governments on the project.
Source: CP24

articles.title: Going deep on local AI performance benchmarking with Apple’s Mac Studio with M5 Ultra taking on Nvidia DGX Spark — inference engine recipes mandatory for bigger models as MLX stack matures
articles.text:
Going deep on local AI performance benchmarking with Apple’s Mac Studio with M5 Ultra taking on Nvidia DGX Spark — inference engine recipes mandatory for bigger models as MLX stack matures
Is a Mac Studio a better investment than a DGX Spark?
Apple’s updated Mac Studio with the M5 Ultra SoC has already proven itself as one of the most powerful systems around, thanks to its 36-core CPU and 80-core GPU with Neural Accelerators for the matrix math operations that drive AI compute. Beyond that raw power, options for up to 512GB of unified memory have many local AI enthusiasts lining up for the 13 to 15 weeks it’ll take for Apple to ship one right now.
But is our tested Mac Studio config worth a whopping $12,300 or more for those folks? We already tested the maxed-out M5 Ultra chip with the popular Qwen 3.8 27B in our initial review, but that compact dense model doesn’t come anywhere close to exercising 256GB of memory. We wanted to fill that pool to the brim with cutting-edge large models like DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM 5.3 Flash.
We also have some new benchmarks at our disposal to see how the Mac Studio stacks up in agentic tasks on the GPU side in the wake of our review of the Microsoft Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia’s RTX Spark chip. So there's much to dig into.
Agentic AI performance and power efficiency
We started our more detailed local AI testing with Artificial Analysis' AgentPerf-Local benchmark. This test plays back recorded inference traces with certain models across a range of agentic AI workloads to gauge performance. Artificial Analysis provides a full breakdown of this workload, but the bulk of its work takes place in prompt processing rather than token generation. As a result, it should favor systems with lots of raw compute, which both GB10 and the M5 Ultra have at their disposal.
The M5 Ultra's 80-core GPU dwarfs GB10's 48 Blackwell SMs at a high level. Even without detailed info on clocks, it would be extremely difficult for GB10 to outgun the M5 Ultra in this test. And the Mac's 1.2 TB/s of memory bandwidth gives it just over four times as much decode bandwidth as GB10's 273 GB/s. But as our past tests have shown, raw specs aren't as important as delivered performance with AI. Delivered performance can vary greatly from paper specs.
We continued to use the dense Qwen 3.8 27B for this test. We used llama.cpp as our inference backend on both the Mac Studio and a single Dell Pro Precision GB10 box, which is nearly identical to the DGX Spark. We further enabled Qwen 3.8 27B’s native multi-token prediction (MTP) support for a decode speed boost on both platforms.
Versus a single DGX Spark-like system, the M5 Ultra Mac Studio finishes this agentic test in just under half the time, an extremely impressive result. One might think this is a silly comparison given the imbalance in compute resources and memory bandwidth between these two systems, but the cost of a single 4TB Dell Pro Precision GB10, like the one we tested, is now a whopping $10K, so comparing it to the $12K Mac Studio head-to-head isn’t actually that far-fetched.
Because AgentPerf-Local performs a fixed amount of work on every system, we can also directly compare power efficiency between platforms by recording the wall power consumed by a single Spark and the Mac Studio and converting it to task energy in kilojoules.
At least with llama.cpp, the Mac Studio not only finishes the AgentPerf-Local test much faster than the DGX Spark, but it also consumes less task energy overall — about 16% less. A different inference engine might produce a more favorable result for the Spark-like system, but apples-to-apples, this test looks fantastic for the Mac Studio.
We can multiply both task time and energy consumed (in kilojoules) together to arrive at the energy-delay product (EDP) for each system. A lower EDP wraps up a fast time to completion and a low task energy into a single comparable figure for efficiency.
The Mac Studio’s EDP is under half that of the DGX Spark in this test, once again indicating its impressive efficiency and performance with this dense model and workload.
Going big with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 and GLM 5.3 Flash
Of course, Qwen 3.8 27B doesn’t need 256GB (or even 128GB) of RAM to do its thing. To really stretch the legs of the Mac Studio, we chose two larger open models that are near the top of capability benchmarks right now: GLM-5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017.
The M5 Ultra Mac Studio can natively fit quantized versions of these models (a four-bit quantization in the case of GLM 5.3 and a two-bit quantization courtesy of Unsloth for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash) in its 256GB of RAM, but there’s no way even those quantizations will fit on a single 128GB DGX Spark.
That’s where the clustering capability of Nvidia’s platform comes in. We’ve already seen how pairing up Sparks can scale up one’s local inference capacity, and that capability is critical when evaluating them against a Mac Studio like this.
But the rapidly rising prices of GB10 systems have frustrated our value analysis during the course of this testing. For just one example, Lenovo set all of its ThinkStation PGX systems to a “coming soon” status during our tests. And as we’ve already mentioned, the Dell Pro Precision GB10s we’re clustering here are an eye-popping $10K each. We have no reason to believe the rest of the GB10 systems on the market will be that much cheaper once this current volatility shakes out.
No matter how you slice it, getting even a pair of DGX Sparks with 4TB SSDs is going to end up costing quite a bit more than this single Mac Studio, even if $20K for a dual-Dell cluster is at the top end of the market. $15K or more is a relatively more reasonable benchmark, but even then, that’s 25% more money than a single M5 Ultra Studio.
We don't yet have end-to-end agentic tests for these larger models, but directionally, we can still consider prompt processing and decode performance to see which of these systems would deliver faster agentic turnaround.
Because of the limited choice of compatible inference engines for Apple Silicon, we have to use llama.cpp for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. Worse, the Mac Studio can't hold both the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 model weights and the DSpark speculative decoding model required to boost token output even with a two-bit quantization, so we’re forced to leave performance on the table.
In contrast, the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash serving recipe for our Spark cluster can take advantage of DSpark speculative decoding and the TensorFold inference engine, which can deliver higher performance than llama.cpp.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Even with MLX support, llama.cpp performance with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on the Mac Studio is pokey next to the DGX Spark cluster. Between its slower prompt processing speed and unaugmented decoding, it would end up at a disadvantage in agentic work with this model.
The community two-Spark serving recipe from Mia’s AI Lab with TensorFold is a major asset for owners of those systems, even accounting for the bit of extra work involved in setting up and managing a Spark cluster.
Where the Mac running llama.cpp needs anywhere from 10 to 25 minutes to digest the longest context lengths we tested for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, the Spark cluster needs under five minutes at most to do the same jobs with this recipe — and the TensorFold inference engine is much faster on the decode side, too. If you want to run this model locally, a pair of Sparks is the clear winner right now.
With DeepSeek out of the way, let’s consider GLM 5.3 Flash, another leading open model for local intelligence. Because MTP with GLM 5.3 Flash doesn't require a separate drafting model, we can give it a decode boost on the Mac Studio without the memory headroom issues we saw with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. For our Spark cluster, we chose to run GLM 5.3 Flash using a recipe cooked up by Mia's AI Lab.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
GLM 5.3 Flash runs much better on llama.cpp than DeepSeek V4.1 Flash does, but even so, the DGX Spark cluster delivers much faster prompt processing times across the board. The M5 Ultra's memory bandwidth advantage means the Mac is delivering higher tokens per second on the decode side, but it’s likely that any agentic turn would still finish faster on the Spark cluster.
Because a TensorFold serving recipe is available for GLM 5.3 Flash on Apple Silicon, however, we can see just how much extra performance is available from an MLX-specific four-bit model quantization and a theoretically higher-performance inference engine.
This serving recipe turbocharges the Mac Studio’s performance compared to llama.cpp. Prompt processing times with TensorFold get much closer to those of the Spark cluster, and decode throughput is a startling three times faster, on average.
We expect (and can only hope) that improved inference engine support and serving recipes for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 on the M5 Ultra will arrive in time as community members unleash their coding agents on this hardware, because the performance potential is clearly there for Apple Silicon.
Bottom line
A single M5 Ultra Mac Studio can deliver incredible local AI performance and power efficiency versus a single DGX Spark when all the puzzle pieces fall into place. And that's not as absurd a comparison as it might seem.
Prices for unified memory systems are ballooning to the point that a single Dell Pro Precision GB10 system with a 4TB SSD is now over $10K, closing in on the $12K-ish price of the Mac Studio configuration that we tested. We expect those trends will only continue as the RAM and NAND supply crunch becomes more acute.
But our broader experience shows that the M5 Ultra's impressive performance isn't assured from every model and inference engine, especially from the bigger and highly intelligent models you'll want to put in 256GB of RAM.
This Mac's prompt processing speeds can really rip with llama.cpp and smaller models like Qwen 3.8 27B, but you really want to ensure that you have a higher-performance serving recipe at your disposal for bigger models like GLM 5.3 Flash and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017. The TensorFold engine runs GLM 5.3 Flash incredibly well, but it doesn’t support DeepSeek at all yet.
As we emphasized in our review of the M4 Max Mac Studio, memory bandwidth is just one factor in AI inference performance. You need to take the entire hardware-software stack into account in order to wholly judge the performance and model compatibility available from these extremely pricey unified memory setups.
Even as Apple closes the performance shortfalls of its hardware for AI inference, development and support around the MLX stack has a ways to go before it catches up with the maturity and performance, as well as the model and inference engine options, available on Nvidia hardware.
The enduring value of the DGX Spark platform beyond its raw performance and scalability is that the breadth and velocity of community software development and support around the platform has gotten to the point that you're virtually assured of a way to run a hot new model soon after its weights hit Hugging Face (at least assuming you have enough Sparks to cluster to provide the memory capacity necessary).
That assurance of community software support and ongoing development, along with the DRAM and NAND supply crunches, means high demand and ever higher prices for 128GB GB10 boxes. Two such Sparks with 4TB drives will run you an eye-watering $15K to $20K+, depending on the partner system and storage configuration you choose. And those prices are likely to continue rising, making a single Mac Studio a potentially appealing option as long as Apple doesn’t jack up its prices for these systems in turn.
If strong local AI performance is just one thing you need from a personal workstation, and you also want one of the world's fastest CPUs and a powerful GPU for general-purpose work in one well-rounded, efficient, and quiet compact chassis, the Mac Studio is a remarkable system.
If you can wait for software to catch up to this system’s incredible performance potential for local AI and don’t mind the possibility of narrower model and inference engine support compared to a DGX Spark setup, get in line, as lead times for these systems stretch into February 2027 as of this writing.
But if you're thinking about dropping well over $10K specifically for the purpose of building a local AI inference setup right now, perhaps for yourself or a small office, clustering a pair of Sparks gets you both the memory capacity and compute horsepower you need with the robust software support and broad model compatibility you’d expect for that outlay to be worthwhile. Those assurances may be worth the lower raw performance potential of such a cluster compared to the Mac Studio.
As the Senior Analyst, Graphics at Tom's Hardware, Jeff Kampman covers everything that has to do with graphics cards, gaming performance, and more. From integrated graphics processors to discrete graphics cards to the hyperscale installations powering our AI future, if it's got a GPU in it, Jeff is on it.

articles.title: Cowbell unveils AI liability insurance for small businesses that deploy AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cowbell unveils AI liability insurance for small businesses that deploy AI agents
Cyber insurance provider Cowbell Cyber Inc. today unveiled Cowbell AI Liability Insurance, a standalone policy for U.S. small and midsized businesses that covers losses caused by the artificial intelligence agents they deploy.
The new policy is meant to deal with a problem that arises when businesses let agents move money or change customer records with nobody signing off first. Coverage hinges on a trigger the company calls an “AI Incident.” The definition takes in model drift and attacks that manipulate an agent, not just software acting without approval.
Cowbell describes an accounts payable agent misreading approval statuses and paying a supplier twice with no human check. Part of that money disappears when the supplier goes into liquidation.
Unrecovered funds like those can be covered, and the policy also pays to investigate what happened and take the agent offline. Inaccurate or unsafe output can be corrected or withdrawn at the insurer’s expense, with recipients notified.
Usage charges an agent racks up without authorization are covered too, such as when a loop goes unchecked. Cowbell also covers LLMjacking, where an outsider uses stolen credentials or application programming interface keys to run AI workloads and leaves the business holding the bill.
Claims brought by customers fall on the third-party side. Cowbell’s example there is a bookkeeping firm whose agent files client tax returns using outdated rates, and the clients sue once the penalties and interest arrive.
In a case like that, the policy can pay defense costs and any damages or settlements, and the same goes for suits alleging algorithmic discrimination or bodily injury caused by reliance on AI output. Regulatory proceedings are also covered, and where the law allows it so are certain fines and penalties.
Cowbell Chief Commercial Officer Simon Hughes said AI liability is “no longer only about people using AI,” pointing to agents that act with no human in the decision-making chain. When one goes rogue, he said, a business can take its own losses and face customer claims at the same time. Hughes said the policy was written with that double exposure in mind.
Underwriting draws partly on three AI-specific Cowbell Factors covering observability, autonomy and governance. They show underwriters how closely a business monitors its AI tools and how much authority those tools have to act on their own.
Cowbell’s Risk Advisor agent, launched in October, uses the factors to explain risk signals to policyholders. Businesses can see their own scores by connecting Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT and other tools through Cowbell Connectors.
Cowbell already sells some AI coverage. Prime One, which it launched in April for U.S. companies with $250 million to $1 billion in annual revenue, includes affirmative coverage for AI-related incidents inside a cyber policy. The new product is sold on its own and aimed at smaller businesses.
Cowbell AI Liability Insurance goes on sale Jan. 1, 2027, and will be available only through wholesale brokers on a non-admitted basis. Cowbell is a venture capital-backed company that has raised more than $200 million, including a $60 million Series C round from Zurich Insurance Group Ltd. in July 2024.

articles.title: Mass Effect 1 and 2 composer says ‘cinematic moments that propel the story forward’ are a ‘favorite’ part of writing since ‘the music won’t change in those moments depending on the gameplay as they are baked into the visuals’ — ‘They are wonderful pauses for the player to take it all in. Especially for a game like Mass Effect’
articles.text:
‘This is our opportunity to give the player goosebumps’ — Original Mass Effect composer says ‘cinematic moments that propel the story forward’ are a ‘favorite’ part of the writing process since the music is ‘baked into the visuals’
Jack Wall says Mass Effect "was one of the most exciting sci-fi stories I’d ever heard," when he was hired
- Original Mass Effect composer Jack Wall explains why the cinematic music was one of his "favourite" parts to write
- He says cinematic moments help "propel the story forward"
- Wall adds that cinematic music is "our opportunity to give the player goosebumps"
Jack Wall, the composer for Mass Effect and Mass Effect 2, has explained how the game's cinematic music acted as an integral part of each narrative.
In an interview with TechRadar Gaming, where the composer discussed BioWare's closure and how orchestral and synth music influenced the series, Wall said, "One of my favorite parts of being a composer for any game is the cinematic moments that propel the story forward."
He explained that cinematic moments accompanied by tracks are vital to the story, and "This is our opportunity to give the player goosebumps."
Wall explained that he wrote the music to be specifically connected to "both to places/environments and characters — always driving the story forward."
"The music won’t change in those moments depending on the gameplay as they are baked into the visuals," Wall added. "They are wonderful pauses for the player to just take it all in. Especially for a game like Mass Effect where those cinematics are generally rewards for getting to the next phase of gameplay."
Interestingly, Wall revealed that after he was hired for Mass Effect, BioWare divulged the entire story to him "along with the full arch of time, the Reapers, etc," providing him with a creative direction for the soundtrack.
"It was one of the most exciting sci-fi stories I’d ever heard," he said.

articles.title: Multipolitan raises $2 million to develop cross-border mobility platform
articles.text:
Multipolitan raises $2 million to develop cross-border mobility platform
- UAE-based travel and global mobility technology startup Multipolitan has raised $2 million in pre-seed funding, led by EmergentX, at a pre-money valuation of $25 million.
- Founded in Singapore in 2024 by Nirbhay Handa and Lee Smith, Multipolitan develops a platform that combines immigration, visa, travel and personal document management services. The company plans to launch its consumer application in December 2026.
- The funding comes ahead of the company's planned consumer launch, with its platform designed to help internationally mobile individuals and families manage travel documentation, visa requirements and residency compliance.
Press release:
UAE-based global mobility technology startup Multipolitan has raised $2 million in a pre-seed funding round led by EmergentX, at a pre-money valuation of $25 million (AED 91.81 million).
Founded in 2024, Multipolitan develops technology to help individuals and families manage international travel, immigration requirements and cross-border relocation. The company plans to launch its consumer application in December 2026, bringing together visa, travel and personal document management services on a single platform.
The forthcoming application will allow users to manage passports and visas, receive document expiry alerts, check travel and entry requirements, track flight updates and monitor residency periods to comply with immigration rules.
Multipolitan's technology is built around three proprietary systems: INREX, which analyses immigration information; FlightIQ, which provides real-time travel and flight data; and Visa Connect, which supports AI-powered visa management.
The company said revenue from services provided to private-sector clients has exceeded $4 million in less than two years. It aims to use its existing business operations and technology infrastructure to develop a consumer platform targeting internationally mobile individuals, entrepreneurs, digital nomads and families.
Headquartered in the UAE, Multipolitan holds an innovation accreditation from Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM). The company employs more than 40 people across the UAE, India and Singapore and plans to expand its team.
The investment comes ahead of Multipolitan's planned December launch, although the company has not disclosed a detailed allocation of the new capital or specific geographic expansion targets.

articles.title: Un investigador usó IA de Anthropic para hallar más de 100 fallas graves en el código del gobierno británico
articles.text:
Un investigador de seguridad encontró más de 100 vulnerabilidades graves en código que el gobierno del Reino Unido publica abierto en internet, según informó Wired. Chris Nesbitt-Smith, de la empresa ControlPlane, revisó 349 repositorios de código de 33 organizaciones públicas y halló fallas en cerca de dos tercios de ellos.
Nesbitt-Smith usó los modelos Opus y Sonnet de Claude, de Anthropic, en una computadora portátil y con versiones disponibles para cualquier usuario. Dijo a Wired que muchos de los problemas habrían salido a la luz en una revisión informática de rutina: “Nada de esto tiene el nivel de sofisticación que preocupa a los medios generales en materia de ciberataques”.
El caso más grave fue el de la Inspección de Planificación (Planning Inspectorate), el organismo que tramita asuntos de uso del suelo en Inglaterra. Había subido por error a GitHub, un sitio donde se comparte código, una credencial de acceso, y no la eliminó por completo.
Según el investigador, la credencial no parecía vencer y daba un acceso muy amplio, lo que la hacía “particularmente peligrosa”. Con ella se habría podido leer y modificar todos los sitios de SharePoint y las cuentas privadas de OneDrive de los empleados (servicios de Microsoft para guardar archivos), incluidos registros de recursos humanos.
El organismo dice que lo corrigió en 20 minutos
La clave también habría abierto bibliotecas con pruebas protegidas por orden legal para investigaciones y apelaciones de planificación. “La opción de infectar todo con un programa que cifra los datos o de robarlos estaba ahí”, dijo Nesbitt-Smith.
Un portavoz de la Inspección de Planificación respondió a Wired que sus herramientas de vigilancia detectaron la actividad del investigador en agosto y que ya trataba el hecho como un incidente informático cuando ControlPlane se comunicó. Afirmó que corrigió la falla 20 minutos después del aviso y que comprobó que no hubo robo de datos.
Amanda Brock, directora ejecutiva de OpenUK, un grupo sin fines de lucro del sector, sostuvo que el problema no es del código abierto sino de la gestión interna: “Esos datos quedaron expuestos por no seguir un buen proceso”.
Otras fallas aparecieron en el Departamento de Educación de Inglaterra. Wired menciona un servicio de compras que usan las escuelas, un servicio de solicitudes de docentes con datos personales, títulos, historial laboral y documentos de identidad, y el principal registro de proveedores de formación y aprendizaje financiados por el Estado.
Además, otra falla afectaba a un portal de datos abiertos del gobierno de Escocia. ControlPlane explicó en su informe que una clave de administrador sin fecha de vencimiento había quedado dentro del código que se descarga al abrir la página, de modo que cualquier visitante podía leerla y usar las funciones de administración sin iniciar sesión.
Cerrar el código no resolvería el problema
El gobierno británico publica de forma abierta el código que produce con dinero público desde hace unos diez años, según Wired. Eso incluye al Departamento de Salud y Asistencia Social, al Ministerio del Interior y a autoridades locales. La revista añade que los recortes de presupuesto llevaron a varios departamentos a descuidar el mantenimiento de su infraestructura tecnológica.
Wired recuerda que hay voces a favor de dejar de publicar código ahora que la IA acelera la búsqueda de fallas, y que el servicio público de salud (NHS) habría ordenado en mayo a sus equipos abandonar el código abierto por esas dudas de seguridad.
Nesbitt-Smith advirtió que cerrar los repositorios sin arreglar antes los errores sería el “peor escenario”. Es probable, dijo, que un atacante ya tenga copias de ese código y conserve el acceso, y que cerrarlo atraiga más atención sobre los puntos débiles.
El portal escocés se dio de baja de forma definitiva tras el aviso: ControlPlane lo reportó el 23 de junio por el programa de divulgación de fallas del gobierno de Escocia y el dueño del sistema lo retiró el 25 de junio, al concluir que ya no hacía falta. Wired informó que las demás organizaciones también resolvieron los problemas.

articles.title: Anthropic targets upto $1.4T valuation with $70 to $78 IPO price range
articles.text:
Anthropic targets upto $1.4T valuation with $70 to $78 IPO price range
Anthropic will be valued at $1.41 trillion at the upper end of its IPO price band and the shares will be traded on Nasdaq.
AI company Anthropic has set $70 to $78 as the price band for its initial public offering (IPO) which potentially values the company in the range of $1.26 trillion to $1.41 trillion.
The company will be offering 825 million shares. According to the filings, leading technology companies such as Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom will be purchasing $26 billion worth of shares in Anthropic through a private placement. Reports suggest that the company could raise in excess of $100 billion.
The report also said Anthropic will be pricing the shares of its IPO on November 18 and trade on November 19. The shares will be traded on Nasdaq stock exchange.
Anthropic, which has raised a total of $130 billion in funding, was last valued at $965 billion.
The AI company's valuation comes at a time when investors are questioning the valuation of AI companies. Anthropic, which was founded by Dario Amodei and others in 2021, was earlier seeking a valuation of $2 trillion. In comparison, the company reported revenue of $1.16 billion and losses of $12.96 billion in the first half of 2025.
Anthropic’s growth has been remarkable, with revenue rising from just $41 million in 2023 to $4.5 billion in 2025.
In its IPO filing, Anthropic said, “We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history. If managed well, it could rapidly accelerate scientific innovation, greatly increase economic growth rates, bring cures for major diseases within reach and solve problems that have resisted generations of human efforts.”
“Anthropic aims to realise these while navigating and preventing the risks that come with a technological revolution this fast and this powerful.”
Anthropic believes the diffusion of AI through the global economy represents one of the largest opportunities in history to improve how humans live and work, and it is just beginning. It further noted that the world has only begun to use the capabilities of today’s frontier models, and the gap between what Claude can do and how broadly it is used represents one of our largest growth opportunities, alongside continued advances at the frontier.

Pliable, résistant à la pluie et équipé de ports USB-A et USB-C, le panneau solaire Anker SOLIX PS30 de 30 W passe à 54,14 € chez Amazon, soit près de 26 € de moins.

articles.title: Le nouveau Claude a un gros problème : l'IA d'Anthropic est beaucoup plus facile à piéger
articles.text:
Le 9 novembre, Anthropic a mis en ligne Claude Fable 5.2, son modèle le plus capable à ce jour, avec des tarifs en baisse de 20 % et une entrée en Bourse en toile de fond. Comme ses prédécesseurs, il partage son moteur avec Claude Mythos 5.2, version réservée à des organisations vérifiées. La copie publique y ajoute des filtres qui bloquent les requêtes sensibles en cybersécurité, en biologie et sur quelques chantiers d’IA de pointe. La fiche technique publiée le même jour chiffre, au fil de 264 pages, le prix de cette architecture.
Un filtre qui confie les requêtes piégées au modèle le moins armé
Quand une requête touche à la cybersécurité offensive, le filtre détourne la conversation vers Claude Opus 4.8, un modèle sorti le 28 mai (disons-le, une éternité dans le monde des LLM). La bascule est automatique dans les applications d’Anthropic, sur option pour les développeurs qui passent par l’API, tandis que la biologie sensible et certains travaux liés aux modèles de pointe partent vers Opus 5. Comme sur la génération précédente, un bandeau devrait signaler le changement, et la conversation resterait ensuite sur le remplaçant tant que l’utilisateur ne revient pas en arrière.
Mais il y a un hic : Opus 4.8 résiste nettement moins bien que ses cadets aux injections de prompt. La technique consiste à glisser des consignes dans un contenu que l’agent lit en travaillant, un mail ou une page web, et le modèle les exécute comme si elles venaient de l’utilisateur. Le détour par l’ancien modèle ouvre donc une voie d’attaque que Fable 5.2, seul, aurait fermée.
Sur le banc d’essai Gray Swan, qui pousse un agent à exfiltrer des données privées, détruire des fichiers ou déclencher un paiement que personne n’a demandé, 4,09 % des attaques aboutissent après quinze tentatives. C’est quatre fois plus que contre Fable 5.1 (1,02 %) ou Opus 5.5 (0,96 %), deux modèles que Fable 5.2 surclasse pourtant presque partout ailleurs. Dans le détail, 53 % des tentatives ont été servies par Opus 4.8, qui cède une fois sur vingt (5,17 %), quand Fable 5.2 tient à 2,05 % sur les requêtes qu’il traite lui-même.
Un attaquant automatique, entraîné à raffiner ses essais et doté de 200 tentatives par scénario, atteint 89,82 % de réussite sur des tâches de code ; 99,5 % des réponses venaient alors du remplaçant. Aucune des 43 réponses données par Fable 5.2 en personne n’a cédé. Les sondes anti-injection déployées dans les produits ramènent le score à 28,16 %, trois fois le niveau mesuré sur Fable 5.1. Même profil en pilotage d’ordinateur, où 38 des 40 attaques réussies étaient passées par la bascule.
Faut-il couper la bascule automatique ?
Le phénomène figurait déjà dans la fiche de Fable 5.1, publiée en septembre, et Opus 4.8 a été durci depuis. Anthropic ajoute des protections autour du dispositif : des sondes inspectent ce que lit l’agent avant qu’il n’agisse, et un classificateur bloque les commandes dangereuses dans le mode d’exécution par défaut de ses outils de code.
Pour qui confie sa boîte mail ou sa navigation à un agent, un réglage documenté jusqu’ici pour les versions précédentes remplace la bascule par une pause. La requête signalée attend d’être reformulée, et rien ne part vers le modèle le moins armé. Les professionnels dont le travail légitime déclenche les filtres, chercheurs en sécurité en tête, peuvent par ailleurs demander un accès vérifié aux modèles moins bridés.
Dès octobre 2024, l’Anssi et son homologue allemand rangeaient l’injection de prompt parmi les risques des assistants de code, en appelant à garder un humain dans la boucle. Deux ans plus tard, le conseil s’applique plus que jamais… au produit le plus avancé du marché. Un garde-fou appartient à la surface d’attaque, et blinder la porte ne protège pas grand-chose quand les visiteurs suspects sont raccompagnés vers une entrée moins surveillée.

articles.title: AEMET ha confirmado que Charles superará el umbral de ciclogénesis explosiva y el problema no es la lluvia: son las rachas de viento de hasta 140 km/h
articles.text:
A las 05:40 del 28 de enero de 2026, una estación meteorológica situada en un parque eólico al suroeste de Coimbra marcó una racha de 208,8 km/h. Es, hasta la fecha, la velocidad más alta que se ha registrado en el interior de la península Ibérica. Pues bien, si todo sale como dicen algunos modelos, ese récord podría estar a punto de romperse.
Por si acaso, Portugal ya ha ordenado cerrar sus colegios este miércoles y muchas escuelas a este lado de la raya han seguido el mismo camino. El motivo no es Charles, como tampoco lo fue Kristin aquel 28 de enero: es un fenómeno conocido como 'chorro en aguijón'. El problema es que una ciclogénesis explosiva como la que tenemos encima es un terreno abonado para que se repita.
Y, aunque no lo haga, rachas de 140 km/h en superficie sobre la Península es algo muy poco habitual (más allá de cabos y cumbres). Y extremadamente peligroso.
Lo que está confirmado. AEMET explicaba este martes que la presión en el centro de Charles va a caer 19 hectopascales en 24 horas. A las latitudes por las que se mueve (entre 35 y 38° N) el listón de la ciclogénesis explosiva está entre 15,9 y 17,1 hPa; así que lo salta. No de forma extremadamente llamativa, pero lo hace.
La agencia habla de "vientos huracanados" y, pese a las apariencias, hablamos de rachas de viento. No de vientos sostenidos. Es justo lo que hablaba sobre el 'chorro en aguijón': una corriente de aire que cae desde la parte alta de la borrasca hasta el suelo generando periodos de viento de altísima intensidad. En Coimbra, aquel episodio de rachas duró 80 minutos.
¿Y qué significa todo esto? El Gobierno portugués ha declarado la situación de alerta en todo el territorio continental desde las 00:00 hasta las 23:59 del miércoles. Eso son colegios y servicios públicos no esenciales cerrados, actos al aire libre suspendidos y parques clausurados a cal y canto. España espera, en condiciones normales, rachas menos fuertes; pero Castilla y León y Extremadura ya se están moviendo hacia el mismo lugar.
Sobre todo, porque nadie sabe qué va a pasar. Ni dónde, ni cómo. Lo que sabemos es que las tormentas que se profundizan muy pronto tienden a romperse: el frente frío se separa del cálido y se enrosca. Ahí es cuando, según la revisión de referencia, puede descolgarse una corriente que baja desde los niveles medios de la atmósfera durante unas pocas horas y llega abajo acelerada. Ese es el problema. Lo que todos tememos.
Lo malo es que es un fenómeno pequeño y caprichoso. Además es poco frecuente y no lo podemos predecir con exactitud: cuando se rompe la tormenta, el viento puede salir por muchos sitios.
¿Y qué hacemos? Esperar. Es lo único que podemos hacer: esperar los radares y los satélites del miércoles e ir preparándonos para lo que pueda ocurrir.

articles.title: Orange lance une appli gratuite pour utiliser Claude, Gemini, GPT et Mistral, même si vous n’êtes pas client
articles.text:
Orange va lancer le 19 novembre ses super-apps Orange et Sosh, avec Orange IAs, un service qui donne accès à Claude, Gemini, GPT et Mistral. Sa version de base est gratuite, y compris pour les clients des autres opérateurs.
Cette fois ça y est, Orange n'a pas un, mais les deux pieds dans l'intelligence artificielle ! L'opérateur historique a présenté ce mardi 10 novembre Orange IAs, un service d'intelligence artificielle intégré à ses nouvelles super-apps Orange et Sosh, qui remplaceront « Orange et moi » et « MySosh » à partir du 19 novembre 2026. L'opérateur y réunit plusieurs grands modèles d'IA, consultables depuis une même application, avec une formule gratuite et une offre premium réservée à ses clients. Les deux applications regroupent aussi la gestion du compte, des outils de cybersécurité et une sélection de services partenaires. Un véritable festival, pour Orange.
Orange IAs : tout savoir sur le service d’IA gratuit d’Orange avec Claude, Gemini, GPT et Mistral
On peut considérer qu'Orange IAs Découverte est la porte d'entrée des consommateurs sur l'intelligence artificielle, en plus d'être gratuite. Depuis l'application, on peut interroger Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), Mistral ou GPT, le modèle d'OpenAI qui fait tourner ChatGPT. Trois options s'offrent à l'utilisateur. Il peut choisir lui-même son interlocuteur, laisser l'outil désigner celui qui lui paraît le plus adapté, ou poser la même question à plusieurs IA pour comparer leurs réponses. Un compte unique et un historique partagé permettent de passer d'un modèle à l'autre sans repartir de zéro.
Ce qui est intéressant, c'est que vous n'avez pas besoin d'être client Orange pour en profiter, puisque le service est ouvert à tous les particuliers, quel que soit leur opérateur (Free, SFR ou Bouygues Telecom). Les néophytes peuvent s'appuyer sur des assistants prêts à l'emploi, pensés pour des tâches concrètes comme rédiger un courrier, résumer un document ou préparer un voyage. Ceux qui préfèrent un interlocuteur en chair et en os peuvent suivre des ateliers numériques en boutique. Et côté vie privée, Orange s'engage à ne pas transmettre l'identité des utilisateurs aux fournisseurs des modèles, tout en assurant que les conversations ne servent et ne serviront pas à entraîner ces derniers. On sait toutefois que le catalogue d'IA pourra évoluer, et que l'usage est soumis à une limite quotidienne fixée dans les conditions générales, inconnues pour l'heure.
Les clients Orange et Sosh qui en veulent davantage peuvent souscrire Orange IAs Plus, à 10 euros par mois sans engagement. La formule débloque des modèles plus avancés, des images plus soignées et l'analyse de documents jusqu'à 20 Mo. Elle donne aussi accès à une assistance téléphonique assurée par des spécialistes d'Orange IAs. Une jauge permet de suivre sa consommation en temps réel, et l'appli affiche même une estimation de l'impact carbone de ses usages. Les plus attentifs à la planète activeront le mode Éco, qui privilégie automatiquement le modèle le moins émetteur de CO2. Pour comparaison, lors des offres lancées début 2025, ChatGPT Plus passait à 23 euros par mois après l'année offerte chez Orange, Le Chat Pro de Mistral était annoncé à 17,99 euros par mois chez Free, et Perplexity Pro était habituellement facturé 22 euros par mois.
Une super-app qui ne s'arrête ni à l'IA, ni aux abonnés Orange
Orange IAs n'est qu'une brique des nouvelles applis Orange et Sosh. L'opérateur les présente comme des super-apps, c'est-à-dire des applications qui en regroupent plusieurs, et il prend le terme au pied de la lettre. À l'intérieur, on y gère ses contrats, ses factures, sa consommation et ses équipements, et on y accède à sa messagerie Orange, à la TV et à l'actualité. Un assistant niché dans la barre de recherche répond aux questions sur son offre, ses équipements ou sa facture. La cybersécurité va compter, avec un assistant gratuit, lui aussi dopé à l'IA, chargé de passer au crible un SMS, un MMS, un QR code, un numéro ou un lien douteux, et un service identifiera les appels indésirables. Des quiz, des contenus de sensibilisation et des ateliers s'y ajoutent.
Notez que les abonnés à l'option Orange Cybersecure (payante 7 euros par mois) y retrouvent leur protection, qui peut couvrir jusqu'à dix appareils de la famille, avec des spécialistes joignables 7j/7. Viennent enfin une Marketplace de produits high-tech neufs ou reconditionnés et un fil « News » façon réseaux sociaux. Cinq services partenaires sont aussi utilisables sans rien télécharger, avec Deezer Hits, ViaMichelin, AlloCiné Mini, Playzer Originals et Quizz de Génie. Les clients Orange disposent en plus de l'espace fidélité « Orange Merci ». Pour le reste, l'assistant cyber, la Marketplace, News et les services partenaires sont ouverts à tous.
Jusqu'ici, les opérateurs français voyaient surtout l'IA comme une sorte de cadeau glissé dans le forfait. En février 2025, Free offrait un an de Le Chat Pro, l'assistant de Mistral AI, à ses abonnés mobiles, et Bouygues Telecom répliquait avec douze mois de Perplexity Pro. Un mois plus tard, Orange emboîtait le pas en offrant un an de ChatGPT Plus avec son forfait Série Spéciale 180 Go 5G+. À chaque fois, un seul partenaire et une gratuité limitée à douze mois. L'opérateur historique avait déjà mis un pied dedans, en lançant il y a quelques mois Sharlie, un assistant vocal capable de régler les soucis de facturation des abonnés Sosh. Il présentait aussi Maia, l'IA qui épaule déjà plusieurs milliers de conseillers commerciaux pendant leurs appels.
Et ça bouge un peu partout, puisque la semaine dernière, Bouygues Telecom a pris un tout autre chemin en installant ses offres directement dans ChatGPT. Orange fait le contraire. Plutôt que d'aller frapper à la porte de l'IA, il invite les IA chez lui, dans une appli ouverte aux clients de ses concurrents. L'idée d'un agrégateur de chatbots n'est pas nouvelle, mais elle gagne ici la caution d'une marque que tout le monde connaît, et des boutiques pour accompagner les moins à l'aise. Jérôme Hénique, le patron d'Orange France, promet que chacun y trouvera « le service ou l'IA qui lui convient ». Rendez-vous le 19 novembre sur l'App Store et Google Play. Ceux qui ont activé les mises à jour automatiques n'auront rien à faire.

articles.text:
Aproveite: PlayStation 5 Slim cai de preço em até 12x antes da Black Friday
PS5 Slim Edição Digital traz controle DualSense e suporta ray-tracing; console da Sony sai 19% mais em conta no prazo com cupom em oferta do Magalu no AliExpress
O PlayStation 5 Slim Digital está saindo por R$ 3.739 com cupom AEMEGA18 em até 12x sem juros na loja do Magalu no AliExpress. O console da Sony, que suporta gráficos com ray-tracing e traz um controle DualSense, recebe desconto de 19% sobre o preço base de R$ 4.599, reajustado recentemente.
Como o gadget não costuma entrar frequentemente em promoção, esta é oportunidade rara de adquiri-lo com desconto durante a Black November 2026.
O PS5 Slim é a versão básica atual do console lançado em 2020, apresentando um design compacto com a mesma performance. Seu SSD interno de 825 GB e os 16 GB de RAM carregam games de forma quase instantânea, mas é possível expandir o espaço interno com um SSD externo e/ou um M.2.
O console reproduz gráficos em 4K a até 120 fps em TVs compatíveis, enquanto a tecnologia de ray-tracing permite a renderização de reflexos e sombras mais realistas, para maior imersão durante sessões de jogo.
Seu controle sem fio DualSense, um dos mais avançados do mercado, possui feedback háptico para oferecer tensão e resistência nos gatilhos conforme a interação, enquanto respostas táteis e de áudio via alto-falantes embutidos fazem o jogador se sentir na pele do personagem no game.
O PS5 Slim é compatível com todos os jogos do PS4, mas não vem com leitor de mídia física; o acessório, também compatível com o PS5 Pro, precisa ser adquirido à parte.
Este sistema suporta Wi-Fi 6 e Ethernet para acesso à PlayStation Store, que oferece jogos digitais e vários apps de streaming, como Netflix e Amazon Prime Video.
O PlayStation 5 Slim Digital (R$ 3.739 com cupom AEMEGA18 em até 12x sem juros) tem duas portas USB-C e duas USB-A para acessórios e carregar o DualSense.
Black November é o mês da Black Friday 2026, que acontece no dia 27 de novembro, em que o varejo já oferece promoções e cupons com condições especiais em eletrônicos, disponíveis ao longo do mês.

articles.title: Elon Musk’s Terafab targets 1 million wafers a month after 2032 — planned 700,000 monthly memory wafers could rival Samsung’s entire estimated DRAM production capacity
articles.text:
Elon Musk’s Terafab targets 1 million wafers a month after 2032 — planned 700,000 monthly memory wafers could rival Samsung’s entire estimated DRAM production capacity
Terafab’s procurement team reportedly has already been to Japan, asking some toolmakers to deliver within months.
Elon Musk’s Terafab, a joint venture of Tesla and SpaceX, has informally told equipment makers it is seeking to produce 1 million wafers per month after 2032, according to Financial News. About 70% of this output, or 700,000 wafers, is planned to go to memory, with more than 300,000 going to logic chips. Terafab’s procurement team has already visited Japan to ask some local toolmakers for delivery within months. The memory allotment would rival Samsung’s estimated DRAM production capacity if it were all of that type.
Samsung’s DRAM capacity was estimated last year at 650,000–700,000 wafers a month, while SK hynix is reportedly at about 550,000, with about 1 million a goal by 2030. The comparison has to be taken in context, as Terafab’s 700,000 measures all of its expected memory output, which could be NAND or DRAM, while the Samsung and SK hynix figures measure only DRAM. As it is, the memory portion alone would be 3.5 times the reported 200,000 at SK hynix’s Wuxi fab in China.
Many in the industry were skeptical when Musk announced the plans in March, but orders are now leading more companies to see a real business opportunity. The timeline is aggressive, as it usually takes three years or more to get from planning to volume at a leading-edge fab, and Terafab is targeting volume production in the second half of 2028. Procurement officials from the company reportedly visited Japan earlier this month to meet local suppliers and to work on details on bringing in equipment, with some suppliers asked to deliver within a few months.
The Elec also reports that Terafab representatives visited booths of about 10 Korean materials, parts, and equipment firms at SEMICON West, with some NDAs signed.
Logic chips are one thing — Jiji Press reports Terafab is working with Intel to adopt its 2nm and 1.4nm processes — but memory is another, and it’s not clear what type of memory is on the docket. Technical help from a Taiwanese company is under consideration for memory, but no partner has been named, leaving 70% of the planned wafers without a disclosed process technology.
Memory production tends to split between DRAM and NAND flash, the latter for non-volatile storage. A Tesla job listing for a Terafab Memory Process Integration Engineer, reported in August, covers end-to-end DRAM process integration and DRAM node development, and supports emerging memories such as MRAM, RRAM, and 3D DRAM. Terafab hasn’t said how its DRAM would be divided among products like HBM and LPDDR, both useful for AI and both mentioned in its job postings, or whether it expects to make and stack the DRAM itself or package chips it brings in.
Building a cutting-edge logic fab on U.S. soil is its own challenge, and Tesla and SpaceX lack chip-manufacturing experience. Even Musk, on a SpaceX call last month, called Terafab’s dates “very aggressive” and said he put “big error bars” on the timeline. The first SRAM test chip is targeted for around May or June 2027 at the Austin research facility.

How TSMC might fit in remains open. TSMC says any fab with its involvement has to be run by TSMC, while Musk said his own companies would build and operate Terafab, a scenario which could leave TSMC as a space tenant. At least the spending plans are known: $16.8 billion for the first phase in Grimes County, Texas, with total investment of up to $119 billion if later phases proceed. A pilot plant could be completed as early as July 2027.

articles.title: Sony ressort son mythique casque Walkman, avec une nouveauté
articles.text:
Lancé en même temps que le célèbre lecteur de cassette Walkman TPS-L2, le casque audio fait un retour inattendu. À rebours des gros casques à réduction de bruit, comme le WH-1000XM6, Sony relance le MDR-3R en conservant l’esprit minimaliste de ses débuts.
Un design vintage mais une connectique USB-C
Comme sur la version originale, on retrouve un arceau gris métallique réglable et des coussinets circulaires, deux coloris orange et bleu (une version Stranger Things est également proposée) qui nous replongent en 1979. Le MDR-3R garde sa connexion filaire, mais n’oublie pas que les prises jack ont déserté nos appareils en proposant une connectique USB-C.
À l’intérieur, le constructeur réutilise les haut-parleurs de 23 mm du modèle d’origine pour s’approcher au plus près de la signature sonore du modèle original. Selon nos confrères de Gizmodo, qui ont pu tester le produit, il tire son épingle du jeu en proposant des médiums et des aigus convaincants, accompagnés d’une bonne restitution stéréo. En revanche, le rendu se montre très léger dans les graves et l’absence de réduction de bruit ne passe pas inaperçue lorsque l’on passe des appels dans des environnements bruyants.
Le retour en force des écouteurs filaires
Les écouteurs filaires, les formats physiques et plus généralement les produits des années 80-90, font un retour en force. Sony ne s’y trompe pas en ressortant son casque MDR-3R, compatible avec les nouveaux Walkman qui ont aujourd’hui un écran tactile, tournent sous Android et coûtent une petite fortune. Le casque rétro de Sony ne cherche évidemment pas à rivaliser avec les casques modernes, mais il mise plutôt sur la nostalgie de ses clients les plus matures.

articles.title: Pixel Tag, Google's $30 Android-ready answer to Apple's AirTag, is now available | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s answer to Apple’s AirTag, the Google Pixel Tag, goes on sale starting Tuesday, allowing Android users to track items like their keys, wallet, or bag using their smartphone’s built-in Find Hub.
First announced in August, the $29.99 device takes cues from the AirTag and other lost-item finders by offering connectivity via Bluetooth and ultra-wideband for precision finding. This lets Android device owners, including Pixel Watch wearers, locate their missing items using a combination of visual distance and directional guidance.
Plus, the tag has a built-in speaker to play a chime that helps you locate your item if nearby. (Or, if you’ve lost your phone, you can press the button on the Pixel Tag twice to ring it, too.) You can choose between three different levels of loudness in the settings within the Find Hub, with the maximum volume around 80 decibels.
Though the Pixel Tag serves the same purpose as an AirTag, Google has opted for a different design. Instead of a small, round device, like Apple’s, the Pixel Tag is slimmer and more elongated.
Spec-by-spec, the Pixel Tag is 1.1-inches wide, compared to the AirTag’s 1.26 inches. As the Pixel Tag is oval-shaped, it’s 1.8-inches high from top to bottom. Thickness-wise, the Pixel Tag clocks in at a depth of 0.2 inches, compared with the AirTag’s 0.31 inches (which Apple calls its height). The slimness of the device might make it more appealing for some, particularly if they’re adding the tag to a small item, like a keychain.
The device weighs just 0.4 oz, with the battery included.
Unlike Apple, Google opted for a physical button you can press on the tag, which makes it more obvious how it’s meant to work.
Google didn’t originally say that the Pixel Tag included NFC when it announced the device in August. NFC is used by Apple’s AirTag to aid people who find lost items, as they can tap the side of the tag to launch a webpage that displays the owner’s contact information. Google uses the tap gesture to instead connect the user to the device’s settings.
Meanwhile, for lost items that are not nearby, the Pixel Tag relies on Google’s crowdsourced network of over a billion Android devices globally. The network, similar to competitive offerings from Apple and Tile, taps into the connectivity provided by other Android devices, which can identify and share the location of the lost item back to its owner. This location information is displayed on a map inside the Find Hub app.
While the person who found the item can’t tap it, as with NFC-enabled devices, Pixel Tags that are put into “Lost” mode will be able to share the owner’s email, number, and a short message so the person who finds the tag can contact you. When the tag comes back into range of the user’s phone, the item is automatically marked as found.
The Pixel Tag’s location can also be shared with up to 10 people in the Find Hub app, which could be useful for shared items like the family car keys, which multiple people might rely on.
Like AirTag, the Pixel Tag is powered by a user-replaceable coin cell battery (the CR2032), which makes the device reusable for the long term. (Google claims the device has up to one year of battery life to start.)
Meanwhile, the device itself is made from stainless steel and features IP67 water and dust resistance (maximum depth of 1 meter up to 30 minutes). It pairs with devices running Android 9 or newer via Fast Pair technology.
The Pixel Tag comes in two shades: silver and a pale green, and can be bought individually or in a four-pack for $99.99.
Alongside the launch, the company Bellroy is debuting its own keychain cases in a variety of colors and styles, which will also be sold on the Google Store.
Post updated after publication to note that the Pixel Tag now supports NFC, which was a surprise addition not mentioned at the time of its announcement.

articles.title: ASRock Updates VBIOS Flashing Utility Following Radeon RX 7900 XT/XTX Bricking Reports
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
ASRock Updates VBIOS Flashing Utility Following Radeon RX 7900 XT/XTX Bricking Reports
ASRock has released an updated version of the ASRVBFlash utility, version 1.0.6, which is intended to fix issues caused by the previous version, 1.0.5, for Radeon RX 7900 XT/XTX users. The earlier version led to reports of ASRock GPUs becoming bricked after users attempted to update the firmware with ASRVBFlash. ASRock has quietly released the 1.0.6 update without providing details on what changes have been made. We only know that this version aims to prevent the bricking of cards and instead properly update the GPU firmware to enhance security, which was the original intent.
The initial issue arose when users ran the ASRVBFlash 1.0.5 utility. During the process, Windows would start a reboot sequence, but the system would then fail to boot. At the time, a workaround involved reinstalling an older VBIOS, which some users downloaded from TechPowerUp's VBIOS hosting. Meanwhile, ASRock reportedly removed VBIOS version 1.0.5 from its download pages, although it remained accessible via FTP connections.With the release of the new VBIOS flashing utility, the problem of bricked GPUs should no longer occur. However, for those who updated their ASRock GPUs and ended up with bricked cards, the situation remains unclear. A customer in Japan was informed by ASRock that a card bricked by an official firmware update is covered under warranty, while a European customer was told that any self-attempted removal of the heatsink to access the VBIOS EEPROM chip would void the warranty. If your card is bricked, the best course of action is to pursue an RMA. For those still unsure if the new ASRVBFlash utility version is reliable, it might be wise to wait for feedback from the community.
