articles.title: 'Let's take all the intelligence out': How Ring finally built its home surveillance drone
articles.text:
'It’s loud — we think that’s a feature. This thing is not gonna sneak up on you': Ring CEO Jamie Siminoff on why Ring Drone Cam's sound is intentional
Everything you love about Ring, but in motion
- Ring is finally ready to ship its home-surveillance drone
- The Ring Drone Cam is lighter than some smartphones
- A cloud-based AI Pilot does all the driving
Third time may be the charm for Ring's long-gestating security drone efforts — and Ring CEO Jamie Simioff insists that the new Ring Drone Cam is just what his customers want.
"When people stop me on the street, it's what they ask, 'Where's the drone?'" Simioff told me.
After a decade of effort, which traces back to before Ring became a part of the giant Amazon device family, Ring is finally ready to deliver a home security drone that makes sense.
Sure, perhaps we've heard this before, and Siminoff wasn't shy about recounting Ring's abortive drone history. That history started with an idea in 2016, which led to a drone that Siminoff said launched in 2021 but not to customers. "They were in boxes and ready to go," he added (design trade-offs, limited flight time, privacy concerns, and other issues ultimately scuttled that launch). By 2025, Ring was ready with another attempt, but that drone also never shipped.
As Sminioff described it, Ring was overcomplicating the drones, building in too many capabilities. A smart drone — basically a flying robot with all the attendant sensors — was the wrong approach. So Ring went back to the drawing board but with a critical learning: "The more sensors you take off, the lighter you can go, because you’re using less power."
He said Ring decided to "take all the intelligence out" and shifted it to the cloud. The resulting security drone is ultra-light (around 160 grams) and has just a few native skills, which include knowing how to land and how to connect via Wi-Fi to the app.
The App connects to Ring's new AI Pilot, which uses cloud-based, silicon-powered agents to control the drone. Not that the drone is flying blind. It has a front camera, a base camera, and the guidance of the AI Pilot, which is using a brand-new home map.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Ring Drone Cam owners will be able to use the drone to walk through their home and build a detailed map, which Siminoff described as a "digital twin" of your space.
If, for instance, you detect a rear door open or a window ajar in your home (via one of Ring's sensors that they assume you'll have throughout your home), you can tap on the location in the digital house map and the Ring Drone Cam will lift off from its home charge base and fly directly to it.
The AI Pilot knows the map of your home, so it won't be bouncing off walls and, if someone does happen to be in the way, the Ring Drone Cam will know how to get around them. Siminoff admitted, though, that the drone is simply not smart enough to come up with an alternative route to get around, say, a group of people.
A relatively simple and lightweight flyer, the Ring Drone Cam is quite loud, and Siminoff says that's intentional. "It’s loud — we think that’s a feature. This thing is not gonna sneak up on you."
In fact, the use case he envisions is when nobody is home, though he agreed that if you're home asleep and there's movement downstairs, it could come in handy then, too. The sound alone might scare off intruders.
The Ring Drone Cam is not designed to go outside, but it can peer out of a window. Imagine that someone approaches your front door, and the Ring Doorbell detects them. The Drone Cam could get the alert, lift off, and shine its LED spotlights out the window.
I asked Siminoff if the Ring app would support split-screen, so you could see the Drone and Doorbell footage side-by-side. He said it didn't, but that he liked the idea.
In the app, Ring Drone Cam owners can schedule automated home patrols that include multiple floors, since this drone can traverse stairways. The drone keeps track of the ground below but has no sensor for the ceiling. It also depends on that Wi-Fi connection for navigation. If your home internet cuts out, the Drone will basically land where it is, assuming it's safe to do so.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Speaking of safety, all four propellers are inside cages, so even if the lightweight drone does somehow run into you, you're unlikely to get injured. Siminoff also said that the Drone Cam promises the same level of video privacy as you find on the brand's video doorbells, which includes two-factor authentication and encryption. Also, as soon as the drone lands, it stops filming, and the charging dock also covers the camera when the drone is settled inside.
As you might expect for such a small and lightweight drone, the Ring Drone Cam doesn't offer much flight time, cruising for roughly five to eight minutes on a charge (consumer drones can often fly for up to 30 minutes). Charging could take between 40 minutes and an hour, though I imagine its patrol flights might just be a minute or two, after which the drone would return to its charging base.
Assuming that this is the drone Ring finally ships, the Ring Drone Cam will be available in the US only (Ring hasn't announced any plans to expand the launch) from January 27 for $249.99 and will be available in dark gray. The white units I saw were all pre-production, and there are currently no plans to offer a white option.
The return of Astro
Remember Amazon Astro, the sort-of-cute patrol robot that Amazon launched in 2021 and discontinued in 2024? It's back, in a fashion.
Using Astro as a base, Ring rebuilt it, added a light tower, and rechristened it the Ring Rover Cam. And while the Ring Rover Cam could be used in a home, it's really designed for medium-to-small businesses — and at $999.99 it's priced for those customers, too,
The reimagined robot can autonomously map a space, perform 30-minute patrols (we watched it roll around a fake Amazon inventory space), and pop up its periscope camera, which can extend to about four feet.
Ring has added one hardware feature: a new light tower that shines up at the ceiling. If you lose visual track of where the Rover Cam is, you can just look for a blue circle on the ceiling. In the case of an emergency, the robot lets out a piercing alarm, and that blue light turns into a spinning ambulance-like red one.
The Ring Rover Cam ships in the US from December 16.

articles.title: Adobe expands AI assistant into creative workflows - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Adobe expands AI assistant into creative workflows
Adobe Inc. today announced an expansion of its CX Enterprise Coworker agentic artificial intelligence platform into its GenStudio content supply chain platform.
The company said the integration move allows creative professionals to bring AI agents into production workflows to develop, manage and deliver personalized marketing content at large scale.
The announcement, made at its Adobe MAX conference in Miami, extends CX Enterprise Coworker beyond its initial focus on customer analytics and marketing into content planning, creation and distribution. The technology provides a conversational interface for coordinating AI agents across Adobe applications and third-party systems.
Adobe said it’s aiming to reduce the manual work involved in producing marketing campaigns while maintaining human oversight and brand consistency. It’s also introducing several new capabilities across its GenStudio portfolio, including AI-assisted campaign planning, automated brand compliance, reusable creative workflows and expanded 3D product visualization.
Central to the initiative is Adobe Brand Intelligence, a machine learning system that captures an organization’s brand standards, including the unwritten practices and preferences that traditionally have resided inside employees’ heads.
“As we move to a world where creatives are directing agents, the context that’s locked in the hearts and minds of creatives is made available to agents so they can start to produce content that is on brand,” said Varun Parmar, Adobe’s senior vice president of GenStudio and Firefly for Enterprise.
Brand Intelligence will be integrated into Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign and Firefly Creative Production for Enterprise. New intelligent asset adaptation capabilities can automatically resize and rearrange campaign designs for different media formats while preserving brand standards.
The system also incorporates continuous learning to keep guidelines current as creative practices evolve.
“It’s ingesting reviews, approvals and rejections by the creatives,” Parmar said. “Based on that information, it’s able to infer the latest guidelines.”
Administrators can inspect and override those conclusions to prevent outdated or incorrect practices from becoming embedded in automated workflows.
Another addition is Ideation Space, a collaborative AI-powered canvas within Adobe Workfront. It combines historical campaign performance, audience information and other enterprise data to help marketers develop campaign briefs.
In a demonstration, Adobe showed how Coworker could retrieve project assignments, research audience characteristics, coordinate with an AI copywriting agent and evaluate proposed designs using synthetic audience simulations. The platform can also be used to run surveys of human respondents.
Adobe is extending Firefly Graph for Enterprise with a feature called Capsules that packages complex creative workflows into simplified applications that other employees can run without mastering the underlying tools. Another feature, Node Publishing, allows teams to share reusable workflow components.
New 3D Digital Twin capabilities enable enterprises to modify product imagery, materials, lighting and camera angles and generate animations without repeatedly photographing physical products.
CX Enterprise Coworker supports external applications and custom-built systems through the Model Context Protocol, enabling enterprises to connect their existing technology investments.
Adobe emphasized that the expansion isn’t intended to give AI agents unrestricted authority over creative decisions. “CX Enterprise Coworker enables human-led agent-accelerated work,” Parmar said. “At every step when the agent is making a decision, it’s coming back to the human and asking.”
Early deployments have accelerated audience definition, traditionally a time-consuming part of campaign development, according to Adobe, although executives provided no quantitative productivity figures. The company expects similar improvements in content production.
The new GenStudio integrations are being made available today, with some Firefly Graph capabilities remaining in beta test. Adobe said the expanded Coworker functionality won’t require additional charges for customers with existing subscriptions.

articles.title: Pennylane en panne ? Le numéro 1 de la facturation électronique rencontre des problèmes aujourd'hui
articles.text:
Pennylane connaît des difficultés ce mardi 10 novembre. L'éditeur français, en tête des raccordements au réseau Peppol avec plus d'un million d'entreprises référencées, reconnaît des problèmes de stabilité sur son application web. Ses équipes enquêtent sur l'origine de l'incident.
La matinée ne se déroule pas tout à fait comme prévu pour Pennylane. À 9 h 39, l'éditeur de logiciels comptables a publié une alerte signalant des dysfonctionnements sur son application. Les utilisateurs peuvent rencontrer des erreurs pendant l'utilisation du service, sans que l'on sache encore combien d'entre eux sont touchés ni quelles fonctionnalités sont précisément affectées.
Mise à jour du 10 novembre, à 15 h 30 : incident résolu
Pennylane a confirmé le rétablissement de son application à 14 h 40, après un peu plus de cinq heures de perturbations. L'éditeur avait signalé une amélioration dès 12 h 05, tout en prévenant que des dysfonctionnements ponctuels pouvaient encore survenir. L'incident est désormais officiellement clôturé et tous les services sont affichés comme opérationnels. Pennylane n'a pas précisé l'origine du problème.
Des erreurs sur l'application web, mais pas de panne générale annoncée
Sur sa page de statut, Pennylane évoque des problèmes de stabilité et indique que ses équipes techniques enquêtent sur l'incident. À l'heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, celui-ci reste classé « en cours d'investigation ».
L'application web, accessible à l'adresse app.pennylane.com, affiche des performances dégradées. En revanche, l'API, l'application mobile, le site vitrine, le centre d'aide et le support client sont toujours signalés comme opérationnels.
L'éditeur n'a communiqué ni sur la cause du dysfonctionnement ni sur une éventuelle heure de rétablissement. Rien ne permet non plus, à ce stade, d'affirmer que les échanges de factures électroniques entre plateformes agréées sont affectés.
Un acteur devenu central depuis la réforme
Si cet incident attire l'attention, c'est aussi en raison du poids pris par Pennylane dans la facturation électronique depuis le 1er septembre 2026. Cette première étape de la réforme impose à toutes les entreprises, assujetties à la TVA ou non, de pouvoir recevoir des factures électroniques, tandis que les grandes entreprises et les ETI doivent également en émettre.
Selon le baromètre Connect-Compta de Chift, Pennylane occupait au 2 novembre la première place du classement avec 1,07 million d'entreprises raccordées au réseau Peppol, loin devant ses concurrents.
Ce chiffre mesure toutefois les entreprises référencées pour recevoir des factures, pas le nombre de clients actifs de Pennylane. Il ne signifie évidemment pas qu'un million d'entreprises rencontrent aujourd'hui des difficultés.
Les dysfonctionnements de ce mardi sont par ailleurs distincts des problèmes d'interopérabilité entre plateformes agréées que nous évoquions récemment. Pour les professionnels confrontés aux erreurs de l'application, la question est désormais de savoir quelles opérations sont réellement perturbées et quand elles pourront reprendre normalement.

articles.title: With Jensen Huang under fire, Nvidia looks at sucession plans
articles.text:
With Jensen Huang under fire, Nvidia looks at sucession plans
The controversy over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s improper relationship with a Chinese citizen has raised national security concerns for the US.
The controversy surrounding Nvidia founder & CEO Jensen Huang has raised questions about the future leadership and succession planning at the company. At $4 trillion, the chipmaker is second only to Apple in terms of valuation.
A report in the The Wall Street Journal says that Huang runs a very flat leadership structure with about 60 direct reportees and there is no visible second rung of leadership or any potential successors in the company.
This has become an important question for Nvidia as Huang will come under increased scrutiny for his improper relationship with a Chinese national Alice Huang, who is allegedly a spy for the Chinese government. This relationship supposedly enabled China to get access to the high-end processors of Nvidia.
Also, reports quoting United States President Donald Trump said that the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is looking into the relationship between the Nvidia CEO and the Chinese national. Trump has defended Huang as a very "honorable" man.
In addition, the US Congress will also come into the picture seeking information on the kind of relationship and whether any sensitive technology has been passed onto China bypassing regulation.
However, reports also quoting an Nvidia spokesperson said, Jensen Huang is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption.
The Board of Nvidia has already stated that it would be investigating the entire matter.
The leadership question comes into picture as there is the angle of national security with regard to the CEO’s relationship with the Chinese citizen and this brings the government into the picture. This is not a leadership crisis which a corporate typically faces where the issues are generally around business challenges, shareholder dissatisfaction, and physical health of the CEO.
Jensen Huang has built a larger-than-life picture not just for Nvidia but also for the AI world. He is seen as an influential individual determining the contours of any new policy with regard to the AI industry. Along with this, he is also well networked with the various heads of States across the globe.
Though, it must be noted that both his children, Madison Huang and Spencer Huang work at Nvidia. Additionally, his son-in-law Nico Caprez also works with the company.
At this point of time, it is difficult to gauge the future direction of Nvidia as there are several elements in play. The improper relationship is one aspect, the bigger repercussion is whether technology was illegally acquired by a foreign country.
Although at the same time, some industry watchers see it as a proxy fight between the United States and China to gain the upper hand in the world of AI. China is seen as being close to matching the technology prowess of the United States and potentially overtaking it.

articles.title: Orange annonce une app gratuite tout-en-un qui permet de discuter avec ChatGPT, Claude ou Gemini
articles.text:
A partir du 19 novembre 2026, les applications « Orange et moi » et « MySosh » n’existeront plus. À la place, les clients pourront découvrir deux nouvelles applications : « Orange » et « Sosh ». L’opérateur veut ainsi centrer ses différents services au sein d’un même endroit. Par ailleurs, Orange a dévoilé deux nouvelles plateformes : Orange IAs et Orange IAs Plus. Ces deux services proposent un accès direct aux principaux modèles d’IA depuis un même espace.
Orange lancera bientôt deux nouvelles applications
Le 19 novembre 2026, Orange lancera deux nouvelles applications : « Orange » et « Sosh ». Celles-ci viendront remplacer « Orange et moi » et « MySosh ». Orange veut ainsi que ses clients retrouvent dans un même espace leurs principaux services (gestion de leurs équipements et contrats, consultation des factures, TV, etc.). Par ailleurs, il faut noter que ces deux applications intègrent un assistant cyber alimenté par l’IA. Disponible gratuitement, même pour ceux qui ne sont pas clients d’Orange, cet assistant cyber aide les particuliers à détecter des arnaques. Ainsi, si vous avez un doute, vous pouvez transmettre à cet assistant cyber un SMS, un MMS, un QR code, un numéro de téléphone ou encore un lien web. Il vous indiquera alors s’il s’agit potentiellement d’une arnaque. À noter que les deux applications donnent aussi un accès à la marketplace d’Orange.
Les nouvelles applications « Orange » et « Sosh » seront disponibles sur l’App Store et Google Play à partir du 19 novembre prochain. Les clients qui ont activé les mises à jour automatiques bénéficieront des nouvelles versions sans devoir effectuer de démarches particulières.
Orange dévoile un service qui centralise les principaux modèles d’IA
Orange a dévoilé Orange IAs, un service gratuit qui donne accès aux grands modèles d’IA du marché. Depuis une même application, l’utilisateur pourra avoir accès à Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), ChatGPT (OpenAI) et Mistral. Il peut choisir le modèle à interroger, se laisser orienter vers celui qui est le plus adapté à ses besoins ou comparer plusieurs réponses. Il est ici question d’un compte unique et d’un historique de requêtes commun, ce qui permet de faciliter le passage d’une intelligence artificielle à une autre. À noter qu’Orange IAs est également disponible pour les personnes qui ne sont pas clientes d’Orange.
Orange à également dévoilé Orange IAs Plus, une version premium qui donne accès à des fonctionnalités avancées. Moyennant 10 euros par mois sans engagement, les utilisateurs ont accès à des modèles IA plus avancés, à la création d’images de meilleure qualité, à l’analyse de documents jusqu’à 20 Mo et à un accompagnement téléphonique avec des spécialistes d’Orange IAs. Les clients de ce service payant peuvent par ailleurs suivre leur consommation en temps réel grâce à une jauge, consulter une estimation de leur impact carbone de leurs usages et activer un mode Éco qui privilégie automatiquement le modèle d’IA le moins émetteur de CO2.
Orange assure que « l’identité des utilisateurs n’est pas transmise par Orange aux fournisseurs des modèles d’IA » et que « leurs conversations ne servent pas à entraîner ceux-ci ».

articles.title: À la COP31, le bilan environnemental de l’IA fait l’objet de débats timides
articles.text:
À la COP31, le bilan environnemental de l’IA fait l’objet de débats timides
La 31e conférence internationale sur le climat qui s’est ouverte lundi 9 novembre à Antalya, Turquie, a été l’occasion de dévoiler une charte de bonne conduite environnementale sur le déploiement et l’utilisation de l’IA. Mais cette dernière manque de mordant.
L’intelligence artificielle est-elle une chance ou un risque pour le climat ? C’est la question que pose en creuxla charte d’Antalya présenté à l’occasion de la COP31. Profitant de la dynamique de cette conférence internationale pour l’environnement, la Turquie, pays hôte, a encouragé les différents états à s’engager dans une démarche plus durable vis-à-vis du développement de l’IA, note The Verge.
Reconnaissant l’appétit de l’IA pour "l’électricité, les infrastructures informatiques, l’eau, les terres et les matériaux rares" tout en expliquant que l’outil peut aussi "accélérer la mise en œuvre des politiques climatiques", le document tente de tracer un chemin de crête entre collaboration internationale, engagements environnementaux et développement technologique.
Plus d'IA pour plus d'écologie
Le ton est donné dès l’invitation au débat, il est question "d’intensifier les efforts visant à intégrer l’intelligence artificielle dans la lutte contre le changement climatique". Point de moratoire, de déploiement plus mesuré ou de décroissance. Il s’agit ici d’employer de l’énergie verte, de minimiser les prélèvements d’eau et de terres rares et de développer des "des normes multipartites, reconnues au niveau international" pour mesurer l’impact de l’industrie sur l’environnement.
Derrière ces mesures techniques, il est aussi question d’imposer plus de transparence aux différents acteurs du secteur, qui continue à jouer la carte de l’opacité malgré des pratiques écocidaires bien documentées, et de s’attaquer au sujet des déchets électroniques liés au développement de l’intelligence artificielle. Un souci rarement évoqué dans le débat public.
Une charte non contraignante
Seul petit hic, la signature de cette charte est basée sur le volontariat et ses objectifs sont "non contraignants", contrairement aux accords de Paris de 2015, qui prévoient des recours juridiques en cas de non-respect de mesures. En plus des pistes générales contenues dans la charte, une vingtaine de mesures additionnelles sont proposées, comme par exemple, assurer la recyclabilité d’un certain taux de composants. Malheureusement, ces idées ne sont pas plus contraignantes et peuvent même être choisies à la carte par les pays signataires.
Face à des pays comme les États-Unis ou la Chine qui font reposer de plus en plus de leurs économies sur le secteur de l’IA, pas certain que la charte parvienne à convaincre. Des représentants européens ont tout de même évoqué la possibilité de prendre part à cette initiative, qui a le mérite d’être un des premiers textes internationaux à s’intéresser de près à cette question.
Quelques jours avant, en France, le premier lobby du secteur souhaitait faire de l’Hexagone, "la première terre d’accueil pour les centres de données en Europe" et appelait à lever "plusieurs obstacles qui pourraient ralentir la concrétisation des investissements". Un discours un peu moins abrupt que celui porté par les lobbys européens, qui appelaient il y a quelques semaines à faire des compromis sur les engagements environnementaux des 27 au nom de "compétitivité, de la souveraineté et de la rapidité".

articles.title: Un ingeniero camerunés ha creado un enfriador solar que puede reducir la temperatura de una habitación en más de 20 grados
articles.text:
Un joven ingeniero de Camerún ha construido un enfriador solar de terracota capaz de bajar la temperatura de una habitación en más de 20 grados centígrados. Teniendo en cuenta el calor extremo del Sahel, podría ayudar a muchas personas a conseguir un entorno mucho más fresco en sus casas. Lo curioso es que el invento también carga móviles y cuenta con iluminación. Y su creador afirma que es lo suficientemente barato para cualquier hogar.
Una solución ecológica. La refrigeración es una necesidad básica en el Sahel, pero el aire acondicionado convencional es caro de comprar y de utilizar, y la electricidad de la red es poco fiable en muchos lugares. Didier Dinamou, ingeniero energético y fundador de la startup D.Y. Innovation, sostiene que la respuesta tampoco implica tecnología avanzada de climatización.
En una entrevista en vídeo con Brut Afrique en 2025, afirmaba que su sistema utiliza materiales locales de gran abundancia, lo que mantiene bajos los costes de producción. Para Dinamou es una solución accesible y ecológica para África.
Cómo funciona. El sistema se basa en la refrigeración evaporativa, con paneles solares que alimentan toda la unidad. Según Dinamou, el agua llena un depósito de terracota, donde la arcilla la mantiene fría de forma natural. Después, una pequeña bomba eleva el agua para humedecer los tubos de arcilla. Por último, un ventilador expulsa aire a través de las superficies húmedas. A medida que parte del agua se evapora, extrae el calor del aire y entra aire más fresco en la habitación.
Dinamou afirma que en su taller la habitación estaba a 36 °C mientras que el agua del sistema estaba a 20 °C. A diferencia de un aparato de aire acondicionado convencional, no hay compresor ni gas refrigerante, así que las únicas demandas de energía reales son una bomba y un ventilador, que un panel solar puede manejar fácilmente.
La vieja idea detrás de esto. En todo el Sahel, los hogares mantienen el agua potable fresca en jarras de arcilla, porque la terracota porosa permite que un poco de agua se filtre y se evapore, llevándose el calor consigo. Es similar a proyectos que ya hemos hablado en esta casa como TerraMound o Bloc. Dinamou declaraba a Brut Afrique que vio esto como una valiosa propiedad térmica que merecía la pena mejorar con tecnología moderna.
Según Energy Crossroad, el sistema comenzó como su proyecto de fin de carrera en la École Nationale Supérieure Polytechnique de Maroua, obteniendo una puntuación de 18,5 sobre 20.
En cifras. En las pruebas con una temperatura exterior de 48 °C, Dinamou cuenta que el sistema redujo una habitación de 30 metros cuadrados a 25 °C. Estimaba el coste en unos 90.000 francos CFA (unos 137 euros al cambio), describiendo el sistema como mucho más barato que el aire acondicionado convencional.
Más allá de enfriar. La unidad también tiene un puerto USB para cargar teléfonos y proporciona iluminación. Dinamou dice que los usuarios que más se pueden beneficiar de ello son los hogares y centros de salud del Sahel, donde el potencial solar es alto.
El inconveniente. La refrigeración evaporativa tiene límites, pues funciona mejor con aire cálido y seco, que es exactamente el clima del Sahel, y es menos eficaz donde la humedad es alta. También utiliza agua, un recurso escaso en gran parte de la región. Por no mencionar que, frente a un aire acondicionado, evidentemente no hay comparación posible.
Dinamou también describe otros obstáculos, pues afirma que el norte de Camerún carece de laboratorios para analizar la composición de la arcilla o realizar ensayos mecánicos y térmicos, y que pedir equipos especializados lleva mucho tiempo. La idea es comparar sus resultados con pruebas independientes, para después fijar un precio final y pasar de los prototipos de taller a un equipo viable para producción. Veremos si al final tiene recorrido el invento.

articles.title: GTA VI is ready to pre-load, but even the PS5 Pro tops out at 30 FPS
articles.text:
Something to look forward to: These days, paying extra for a PS5 Pro usually gets you a smoother version of the same game. Grand Theft Auto VI won't offer that, at least not at launch. Rockstar opened pre-loads for the game today and confirmed it targets 30 FPS on every console, Sony's pricier box included. Instead, the Pro's extra muscle is going toward sharper visuals.
Anyone with a digital pre-order on PS5 or Xbox Series can start downloading now. Xbox pre-loads opened globally at midnight GMT on November 10, while on PS5 they went live at midnight in each player's own time zone. Boxed copies only hold a download code, so those buyers will have to wait until retailers start selling them on November 12.
Everyone will need plenty of free space, too. Rockstar lists the pre-load at up to 212 GB depending on the console, and Thurrott reports the game takes up 209.86 GB on a Series X. That's the kind of download that made France's short-lived plan to tax every gigabyte look so costly for publishers.
As for the frame rate, Rockstar says in its announcement that the game was built from the ground up for current consoles. The studio is "pushing both platforms to their absolute limits" at 30 FPS to keep Leonida's crowds and visual detail intact. It hasn't shared resolutions for any console, though, or said whether other graphics modes will show up.
That's a little awkward for a console Sony originally pitched as a way to keep high frame rates without trading away image quality. Here, the PS5 Pro uses Sony's PSSR upscaler for a cleaner image, and it's the only console that gets ray-traced shadows. PSSR itself got a big overhaul earlier this year, when Sony rolled out a new version built on its Project Amethyst work with AMD – the same partnership behind FSR 4.
Regular PS5 owners still get DualSense haptics across the game, Tempest 3D Audio support and faster load times. Meanwhile, Xbox One owners aren't completely left out, since the game will stream through Xbox Cloud Gaming using Series S graphics settings.
There may be more to the Pro version than Rockstar is letting on, though. RockstarINTEL reports that PlayStation Store backend data for the game lists PSSR version 13.60. That's a newer build than the 13.00A Cyberpunk 2077 uses. The same listing mentions a 120Hz mode, too. That's got some fans hoping for a 40 FPS option, but Rockstar hasn't promised anything beyond 30 FPS ahead of the November 19 launch.

articles.title: KORA Introduces AI-Focused Operating System with Local AI and Agentic Workspaces
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
KORA Introduces AI-Focused Operating System with Local AI and Agentic Workspaces
There is a new player in the operating systems arena from KORA Systems Inc. Called KORA, this operating system is the first bottom-up OS designed specifically for AI PCs, enabling agentic workflows. It is one of the first concepts where a system is so heavily customized that AI workflows are native to it. The company developed this customized operating system on top of NixOS, using it as a foundational layer.
The customization includes the development of what are called neural workspaces and file systems, which replace traditional folders and desktop apps. While these traditional elements are still present, the workflow on KORA OS is organized around intent, context, and memory. Each workspace is divided based on user intent, and the OS manages the files accordingly. Security is robust, as KORA implements each workspace within a secured sandbox for applications and agents, with separate permissions. The memory and context of the workflow remain on the user's desktop, never leaving the machine. Features like semantic search and email are natively integrated, allowing you to search across your entire OS or email to find what you need.For its intelligence base, KORA uses a self-developed Cortex inference engine, which utilizes every chip in the machine—from CPU and GPU to NPU—to maximize compute power, allowing open-weight models to run locally without issue. Cortex is a hybrid engine, enabling every agent and application request to pass through it, and it decides what should be processed by a cloud provider or stay local. Cortex includes an inference engine called Lemma, built on top of llama.cpp, to provide high-performance inference token serving for maximum output.
KORA is also bundling a software translation layer for Windows applications, built using a custom-developed tool based on Wine and Proton, with local AI models handling the configuration of these applications. KORA is collaborating with Qualcomm on the Snapdragon X2 Elite platform, which is expected to be the first PC to support the new KORA OS. What is particularly interesting is that KORA is developing a base layer for HUMAIN OS, an enterprise version of KORA OS co-developed with HUMAIN, scheduled for launch in 2027. All modern x86 infrastructure, including AMD and Intel chips, will run KORA, and Qualcomm is the launch silicon partner for the Arm-based side of support. Other Arm-based chips will be supported over time, as KORA is not exclusive to Qualcomm.
The founders are already veteran OS developers, as KORA is their fourth project. They were part of the Cyanogen, Android, and GameOS releases, which means they have considerable experience in creating operating systems. The KORA team has about 20 engineers working on the project, and the founding team includes Kirt McMaster as chief executive officer, John Lagerling as chief business officer, and Franck De Girolami as chief technology officer.

articles.title: Mawsool raises pre-seed funding to develop AI-powered sales intelligence platform
articles.text:
Mawsool raises pre-seed funding to develop AI-powered sales intelligence platform
- Saudi Arabia-based sales intelligence startup Mawsool has closed an undisclosed pre-seed funding round, with participation from Parachute16, Ghassan Halawa, THANAWI, Advanced Elements Co. and Abdullah Al-Dosari, alongside other investors.
- Founded in 2023 by Osama Abdelhadi and Oday Ali, Mawsool develops an AI-powered B2B sales intelligence platform that helps companies identify potential customers, verify business contacts and generate sales leads.
- The company says its platform provides access to more than one billion verified business contacts, using AI-powered search and data verification to help sales teams identify prospective clients and streamline customer acquisition. The database size has not been independently verified.
- The funding will support further development of Mawsool's technology and sales intelligence capabilities, alongside efforts to expand its reach across Saudi Arabia and the wider MENA region.
Press release:
Saudi Arabia-based sales intelligence startup Mawsool has closed a pre-seed funding round backed by a group of angel and corporate investors, including Parachute16, Ghassan Halawa, THANAWI, Advanced Elements Co. and Abdullah Al-Dosari. The funding amount was not disclosed.
Founded in 2023 by Osama Abdelhadi and Oday Ali, Mawsool is headquartered in Riyadh and develops an AI-powered platform that helps businesses identify prospective customers, access company information and verify contact details.
The company provides B2B sales teams with access to a database it says contains well over one billion verified business contacts. Its technology uses AI-powered search and data verification tools to identify potential customers and reduce the manual work involved in sales prospecting.
Mawsool aims to help businesses streamline lead generation, identify commercial opportunities and improve their customer acquisition processes.
The new investment will help develop the company's technology and strengthen its sales intelligence capabilities. Mawsool also plans to expand its reach across Saudi Arabia and the wider Middle East and North Africa region.

articles.title: Linus Torvalds says that AI fixes drove most of the progress in latest Linux kernel — BPF saw more AI-written fixes than bug reports, possibly indicating a tidal shift for open-source maintainers tired of flood of junk reports
articles.text:
Linus Torvalds says that AI fixes drove most of the progress in latest Linux kernel — BPF saw more AI-written fixes than bug reports, possibly indicating a tidal shift for open-source maintainers tired of flood of junk reports
It would certainly be a welcome development for open-source projects everywhere.
Most open-source projects have meager resources, and the inrush of AI-provided bug reports and "fixes" has been a bane on their respective maintainers. However, the Linux kernel is well-manned, and code for it generally has a higher barrier to entry than in other places. Linus Torvalds thinks that the flood of AI bug reports may be settling, as the kernel's Berkeley Packet Filter (BPF) portion saw more AI fixes than reports.
Torvalds splits off the changes among three areas: graphics, networking, and sound drivers; networking and the BPF; and miscellaneous changes. He proceeds to state that "much of this was driven by various AI fixes," an apparent underscoring of his stance that AI-written contributions should be embraced rather than shunned — so long as they're subject to the same quality control.
The Linux maestro also relayed a note from Alexei Starovoitov, the BPF maintainer, who claims that this subsection actually saw a higher rate of AI-provided fixes versus reports. This might signal a tidal shift, at least where the Linux kernel is concerned, and would be exceedingly welcome news for other open-source maintainers everywhere tired of dealing with junk reports at the same time they have to handle a higher influx of legitimate bugs, thanks to AI-driven bug discovery.
In Torvalds' own words, "I think most other areas haven't reached that point yet, but it's at least a sign that we may be starting to see the tide starting to turn."
Anyone can make a pointless bug report, but it's hard to deny that the existence of powerful AI bots has prompted a renewed focus on cybersecurity most everywhere. Firefox fixed 423 security bugs in an April release, Chrome found and fixed 1,072 bugs in June — making for more fixes in 2026 than the project's previous eight years — and my personal "favorite," NodeJS, sadly fixed 50 vulnerabilities instead of announcing its closure.
Many open-source projects have complained about high-volume, low-quality AI-driven bug reports, with some even shutting down their bug bounty programs altogether, or placing additional verifications for issue reports. We'd venture that the Linux kernel has a much larger bug-triaging team than your average project, though, meaning it has more resources to sift through the junk.
This tentative conclusion popped up in a message sent yesterday to the kernel mailing list, wherein Torvalds briefly describes the overall shape of the kernel's 7.4-rc2 update. He says that despite the update looking large from a pure file-count perspective, it's actually mostly composed of one- and two-line fixes and is "very straightforward" to implement.

articles.title: 'That'll definitely bring in the year of the Linux desktop': Microsoft patent spotted for using spare GPU resources to train AI – but most Windows 11 users hate the idea already
articles.text:
Microsoft patent points to a future where your spare GPU resources could be used to train AI — but Windows 11 users would need a lot of convincing
Paid a stack of cash for your GPU? Microsoft patent suggests it could have a plan to help you earn some of that back
- Microsoft has a patent for a system which uses your spare GPU resources to train AI
- The graphics card would process micro-tasks in combination with other PCs
- You'd be paid some kind of reward for this, but there are issues, and many doubts and concerns, around how such a scheme would work
Microsoft has been granted a patent for a system whereby it could use the GPU in your PC to train its AI (given your consent, naturally), paying you in some way for the privilege.
German site PC Games Hardware noticed the Microsoft patent (via VideoCardz) which was originally flagged by Patentlyze, and is for an 'Opportunistic Micro-training on Edge Devices Using Spare GPU Utilization'. Which is technobabble for using your spare graphics card resources to run parts of AI training routines.
Microsoft has gaming PCs in mind here – given that they can run powerful GPUs, and when sat at the desktop in Windows 11, those graphics cards are doing very little – but the system could work with any device in theory.
As detailed by the patent, AI training tasks would be splint into small elements (or micro-tasks) which would be distributed across various participating PCs, and the results tied back together after those individual jobs had been completed. Various checks would be in place to detect errors or results that had been manipulated.
Any given micro-task would be appropriately assigned to a PC with a matching amount of spare GPU and system resources, as the patent states: "The system monitors end devices to detect available computing capacity and breaks down training tasks into independently trainable subtasks."
As to what payment you might receive for giving Microsoft the benefit of using your PC, that isn't made clear as you might expect, but there would be some reward – either a direct payment, or perhaps some form of credits.
Of course, there are already similar ideas out in there in the computing world, such as Folding@home whereby your PC contributes to medical research (and SETI@home before that).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Analysis: AI@home4Microsoft
There are a lot of issues with this plan, if Microsoft was ever to attempt to go ahead with it. For starters, I think the payment would have to be clearly worthwhile considering what you're giving Microsoft here – I'm not sure credits, or, say, Microsoft Rewards Points (to pluck a speculative example out of thin air) are going to cut it.
As we're looking at the future, Microsoft may well be thinking of credits for using AI (when it inevitably becomes pricier for everyone), but there's a degree of risk in this process which a lot of folks are already finding very off-putting or alarming. (Even though, as noted, this is just a concept, and nothing's happening with it – at least not yet).
That includes concerns around giving Microsoft the ability to monitor your system beyond Windows 11's standard telemetry and into deeper territory to ascertain what your GPU is up to and further data on system load.
The second potential stumbling block is that the AI training system would supposedly limit RAM usage, and ensure a GPU isn't overheating due to the load it's being put under – but do Windows 11 users trust Microsoft to do that reliably? Given the bugs in its operating system, I think there'd be more than a few worries about this side of the equation going awry. Cue posts on Reddit about 'Microsoft burnt out my graphics card' and so on. Doubtless something like game stuttering might be blamed on this tech, too (when it could be related to another entirely different problem – like a recent Windows 11 update, ahem).
There's also the cost of the power to ramp up the GPU, and whether that does actually balance out with whatever reward the user is being paid (which, as noted, we don't have a clue about yet). And finally, there's the wear-and-tear on your GPU, because with the card being used a lot more – and possibly being pushed more consistently – it won't offer nearly the same level of longevity as it would otherwise.
It feels like a seething nest of potential problems to me, and I'm skeptical Microsoft would ever move forward with such a scheme given that. Still, it is clearly an idea the company is mulling, so we shall see if we hear anything more about this in the future.
The idea is already sparking bad feelings on Reddit, with some folks having trust issues that it isn't a signal of Microsoft's broader intention to sneak in some kind of AI training routines with its hardware.
As this cynical Redditor said: "Oh great, SETI for AI training: 1. This is probably gonna happen on idle Xboxes whether you want it to or not. 2. They won't give you Battlepass for free or anything fun."
Another Redditor declared: "That'll definitely finally bring in the year of the Linux desktop."
To be fair, not everyone is so skeptical, and this commenter observed: "Honestly if it pays more than the electricity costs it could be a win."
Those who are more positive are the minority, though, and they are very much stressing that Microsoft would need to compensate PC owners well enough.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets.
The launch of Anthropic’s new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks.
With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.
The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says.
Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.
Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow.
As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines.
The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time.
When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says.
Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile.
The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet.
Anthropic says Claude handles the initial setup of trackers and budgets, while allowing teams to continue refining and updating the same spreadsheet. Each spreadsheet can include multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude also makes edits directly in cells alongside the team, and outlines each change so users can see what it did.
Claude Sheets is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile.
Anthropic also announced that Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The feature connects Claude to systems that companies use to keep their numbers, like a data warehouse or CRM. Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos.
Additionally, the company announced interactive connectors that open the full version of apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude. Anthropic notes that teams can now open these apps directly alongside their Claude conversations and ask the assistant to work within them, essentially bringing existing workflows into the same workspace.

articles.title: PuppyGraph raises $10M to let AI agents query enterprise data as a graph - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
PuppyGraph raises $10M to let AI agents query enterprise data as a graph
Graph query engine startup PuppyGraph said today it has raised $10 million in new funding to build out its enterprise go-to-market operation.
The round follows the general release of version 1.0 of its software. PuppyGraph provides a query engine that lets companies treat data already sitting in their warehouses and lakehouses as a single graph, without first moving it into a separate graph database. The company says artificial intelligence agents running on it can work across 3,000 enterprise tables and get graph query results back in under a second.
Agent projects tend to hit trouble once they leave the pilot stage, according to PuppyGraph. The company’s own example asks which critical systems an attacker could reach from a compromised account, a question that means tracing how identities and permissions connect across thousands of tables in several systems.
A proof of concept might cover 30 to 50. Teams that scale past that find schema descriptions alone eating into an agent’s context window, and PuppyGraph said queries running several relationships deep can stall until they time out.
Data teams setting up PuppyGraph 1.0 start from a schema that an AI-assisted tool drafts out of their existing tables. Once they have approved it, users can put questions to the graph in plain English.
PuppyGraph has its own agent for that, and the Model Context Protocol lets companies bring in the AI tools they already use. Agents are kept from guessing how the data fits together. Any agent that references a relationship nobody set up gets its query bounced, and the error that comes back is written for the agent to act on.
When PuppyGraph connects to Snowflake Inc. or Databricks Inc. it can obtain short-lived credentials tied to the user’s identity, so nobody has to hand over long-lived keys. Row-level permissions configured on the data still apply, and the company says it checks them at each hop of a traversal.
“The insights of enterprise data will soon be generated by agents,” said Weimo Liu (pictured), co-founder and chief executive of PuppyGraph. “Users will expect to ask questions that cross departments and systems, beyond the workflows someone built into a dashboard.”
PuppyGraph’s customer list includes Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Palo Alto Networks Inc., and the announcement also named Coinbase Global Inc., Datadog Inc. and Trend Micro Inc. as customers. Xinyu Liu, a staff software engineer at Coinbase, said that because the exchange connects straight to tables it already keeps in Snowflake and Databricks, “standing up a new graph is a schema definition, not a data migration.” Weimo Liu worked as a software engineer at Google LLC before co-founding the Santa Clara-based company.
PuppyGraph’s annual recurring revenue grew sevenfold over the past year, by the startup’s count. No dollar figure was disclosed.
Particle Future and defy.vc led the Series A round. It is the second time defy.vc has led a round for PuppyGraph, after a $5 million seed round in November 2024. PuppyGraph will also put some of the new money into engineering.
Amy Yin, a partner at defy.vc, said writing a query is now a job a user can hand to Anthropic PBC’s Claude. Executing it across billions of relationships still “takes serious engineering,” in her view.
Developers can download a free version of PuppyGraph with a single Docker command and no sign-up form, and the company says it takes about 10 minutes to go from deployment to a first query. Investors have now put $15 million into the startup.

articles.title: IIFL Finance to raise Rs 6,414 crore, with Blackstone leading Rs 5,000 crore primary infusion
articles.text:
IIFL Finance to raise Rs 6,414 Cr led by Blackstone
Funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity will invest Rs 5,000 crore ($535 million) in compulsorily convertible preference shares.
IIFL Finance has approved a Rs 6,414 crore ($686 million) primary capital raise, with Blackstone leading the round.
The board cleared the preferential issue at a meeting on Tuesday. The deal is one of the largest primary private equity infusions in a listed Indian non-banking finance company, according to IIFL.
Funds managed by Blackstone Private Equity will invest Rs 5,000 crore ($535 million) in compulsorily convertible preference shares, which will convert into equity at Rs 602 a share, in line with the regulatory price, within 18 months of allotment. The company said this would give Blackstone a stake of about 16 % on a fully diluted basis.
The promoters, Nirmal Jain and R. Venkataraman, will invest Rs 1,264 crore (135 million) through a preferential allotment of warrants, and will continue as co-promoters. Anchorage Capital is also participating, with a Rs 150 crore (16 million) primary equity investment. The company and its promoters have signed definitive agreements with both investors.
IIFL Finance said the entire sum will go in as primary capital. On a pro forma basis for September 2026, which would lift its capital adequacy ratio from roughly 17% to roughly 30%. The company said the money would support growth in its secured lending businesses, particularly gold finance, and could, over time, improve its credit ratings and lower its borrowing costs.
Nirmal Jain, founder and managing director of IIFL Finance, said: “We are delighted to welcome Blackstone as a partner in IIFL Finance. Their investment is a strong endorsement of the franchise our team has built, and of the opportunity to bring formal, secured credit to millions of underserved households and small businesses across India. Venkat and I are investing Rs 1,264 crores alongside Blackstone, which reflects our own conviction in the Company’s next phase of growth.
“This partnership is about more than capital. Blackstone brings deep experience in building market-leading businesses in India, strong governance discipline, and a global perspective. The investment strengthens our balance sheet and gives us the headroom to scale our franchises, invest further in technology, and deepen our co-lending partnerships with banks, while staying disciplined on risk and capital.”
IIFL Finance also expects to draw on Blackstone’s global network and operational expertise, including in technology, data and artificial intelligence. Blackstone representatives are proposed to join the board, which the company said would strengthen governance while preserving its entrepreneurial culture.
Mukesh Mehta, chief investment officer for India private equity and senior managing director at Blackstone, said: “We are pleased to invest in IIFL Finance, a leading retail lending platform in India with a strong franchise and commitment to serving underserved customers. Building great businesses has been central to our approach over more than two decades of investing in India, and we look forward to partnering with Nirmal, Venkat and the management team to support IIFL Finance’s continued growth.”
The transaction remains subject to customary regulatory and shareholder approvals. Trilegal advised IIFL Finance, while Khaitan & Co advised Blackstone.
IIFL Finance offers gold, business, home and microfinance loans, among other products, through 5,091 branches across urban and rural India. Blackstone, which says it manages nearly $1.4 trillion in assets, has been investing in India for 20 years."

articles.title: Cómo una tormenta solar extraordinaria expuso problemas en los sistemas de alerta en los vuelos, según un estudio
articles.text:
El 11 de noviembre de 2025, una tormenta solar desató el mayor pulso de radiación atmosférica en casi dos décadas, lo que activó un inédito despliegue científico para medir su impacto en el hemisferio norte. El fenómeno cósmico, originado por una potente erupción de clase X5, provocó un flujo repentino de partículas que penetraron la atmósfera hasta alcanzar la superficie terrestre.
Durante años, la seguridad de las rutas aéreas y los dispositivos electrónicos frente a estas tempestades dependió de simulaciones teóricas por computadora. La falta de registros físicos en tiempo real impedía calibrar la verdadera intensidad de estas dosis, una ausencia que dejaba abierta una incógnita crítica sobre los riesgos sanitarios para tripulaciones frecuentes y la vulnerabilidad técnica de los instrumentos de vuelo.
Para resolver esa falta de datos directos, la Universidad de Surrey coordinó una red internacional de sensores distribuidos desde la superficie hasta globos en la estratosfera para evaluar la radiación descendente, según reveló un estudio en Space Weather. El hallazgo comprobó que los niveles de exposición superaron los límites de seguridad en rutas privadas y supersónicas sin que los protocolos habituales emitieran ninguna advertencia operativa.
Los globos meteorológicos registraron niveles críticos sobre el Reino Unido
El operativo permitió lanzar sondas en globos meteorológicos durante el auge de la tormenta. Los instrumentos elevados desde las islas Shetland revelaron que la exposición superó el límite moderado fijado por la Organización de Aviación Civil Internacional (OACI) para aeronaves ejecutivas a 14.600 metros de altitud. A cotas superiores, propias de vuelos supersónicos a 18.000 metros, los registros superaron el umbral grave.
“El primer lanzamiento de globos desde Lerwick registró un entorno de radiación extraordinario en las capas altas de la atmósfera”, afirmó Fraser Baird, colíder del estudio e investigador del Centro Espacial de Surrey, según el comunicado de prensa. El especialista destacó la marcada variación geográfica de estos fenómenos y la necesidad de contar con vigilancia coordinada para evaluar el peligro en la aviación.
Las mediciones confirmaron un comportamiento marcadamente irregular, es decir, una notable disparidad en la fuerza del evento según la posición geográfica y la altitud analizada. Mientras los sensores en el norte del Reino Unido captaron registros superiores al mil por ciento sobre los valores normales de rayos cósmicos, los globos lanzados en el suroeste inglés y en De Bilt, en los Países Bajos, no mostraron variaciones de consideración.
Mediciones en vuelos comerciales y en tierra confirman la dispersión de la radiación
La investigación también analizó detectores en aviones comerciales que cruzaban el Atlántico durante el evento. Un Boeing 777 que cubrió la ruta Londres-Nueva York registró un aumento del 42,6 por ciento en la dosis acumulada de radiación ionizante respecto a viajes idénticos en condiciones normales. Aunque en cabina no se superaron los topes de peligro, los instrumentos mostraron que el flujo de partículas se elevó con rapidez en las rutas transatlánticas.
“Tener todos esos sistemas funcionando juntos durante el mayor aumento de radiación observado en casi veinte años nos brindó un conjunto de datos único y la imagen más completa que hemos tenido de este fenómeno”, afirmó Ben Clewer, investigador de clima espacial de la Universidad de Surrey, según el comunicado de prensa. Los científicos integraron estas lecturas con los datos de cuatro estaciones terrestres de neutrones en territorio británico.
La investigación destacó la necesidad de perfeccionar los sistemas de alerta mediante la combinación de observaciones directas y modelos numéricos. Actualmente, los esquemas de asesoramiento para la aviación dependen en gran medida de simulaciones teóricas guiadas por datos satelitales y terrestres. Frente a ese desafío, el trabajo concluye que los modelos informáticos poseen limitaciones por sí solos y requieren incorporar lecturas físicas en vuelo para calibrar con mayor precisión el riesgo operacional y proteger a tripulaciones y equipos.
La vigilancia coordinada busca prevenir incidentes en futuras tormentas solares
El éxito de la misión demostró la viabilidad de activar lanzamientos rápidos de sensores apenas se detecta una perturbación solar desde tierra. Dicho de otro modo, articular estaciones terrestres y globos estratosféricos permite seguir la evolución del peligro en minutos, lo que ofrece un margen de maniobra crucial para modificar rutas aéreas o descender temporalmente la altitud de crucero en zonas comprometidas.
“Esta es la primera vez que se recopilan datos de radiación a través de la atmósfera durante un evento de clima espacial de esta manera, lo que representa un gran salto científico y marcará una diferencia real en nuestra capacidad de pronóstico”, afirmó Krista Hammond, gerente de clima espacial del servicio meteorológico británico conocido como Met Office, según el comunicado de prensa.
Ante la vulnerabilidad de la microelectrónica frente a fallas provocadas por partículas energéticas, los investigadores plantearon incorporar sensores permanentes en la navegación comercial. El objetivo es consolidar una red de respuesta rápida capaz de alertar en tiempo real a las aerolíneas antes de que una tempestad de mayor magnitud afecte a las aeronaves en pleno vuelo.

articles.title: 24 milliards$ pour un data center géant et une centrale à gaz à Starbase : l'ogre SpaceX jamais rassasié
articles.text:
Décidément, l’appétit d’Elon Musk ne connaît aucune limite. SpaceX prévoit désormais de bâtir une centrale à gaz et un centre de calcul à Starbase, le complexe dédié, du moins jusqu’à maintenant, à Starship.
Il fallait peut-être s’en douter, alors que le géant spatial grignote doucement des terres aux abords de son complexe industriel texan. D’autant qu’en amont, Elon Musk multiplie les paris sur le gaz : turbines autour du supercalculateur Colossus, rachat du fournisseur APR Energy, centrale à gaz pour alimenter l’usine de puces Terafab… Et il ne compte visiblement pas s’arrêter là.
Starbase sera métamorphosée
Dans un avis d’audience publique, publié sur le site de la ville de Starbase, SpaceX présente en effet son ambition de construire et exploiter une centrale à gaz et un » centre de supercalcul », comprenez un data center géant, sur le site. Un projet titanesque estimé à 24 milliards de dollars dans ses premières phases, le chiffre pourrait donc grimper encore.
Selon Reuters, ce serait l’un des plus gros investissements privés jamais réalisés dans la vallée du Rio Grande, avec un chantier qui s’étendrait sur environ 180 hectares. Pas sûr que les riverains apprécient, alors que les plaintes se multiplient face à l’impact des lancements de Starship.
Mais cette nouvelle initiative témoigne des ambitions d’Elon Musk : alors que le réseau électrique est de plus en plus tendu outre-Atlantique, l’homme le plus riche du monde veut outrepasser les barrières réglementaires pour tout contrôler lui-même. Cela comprend, évidemment la chaîne du gaz.
- Accès aux données X en temps réel
- Bon outil de veille médiatique
- Moins biaisé politiquement que sa concurrence
Musk fonce sur le gaz
Car c’est désormais acté : Musk fonce sur les énergies fossiles. La tendance est telle que SpaceX prépare déjà Starpipe, un gazoduc d’environ 13 kilomètres attendu en janvier 2027. Celui-ci alimentera une usine de méthane liquide pour ses fusées Starship. En septembre, la société a aussi proposé un autre gazoduc à Cap Canaveral, en Floride, et recrute même des négociants en gaz à Starbase et en Floride pour ne plus dépendre de prestataires extérieurs.
Et l’entreprise peut se permettre de telles dépenses, elle qui a vu ses revenus bondir de 161 % au troisième trimestre. L'entreprise s’est également endettée de 40 milliards de dollars uniquement pour mettre la main sur de nouvelles puces NVIDIA, et vise la construction de 10 gigawatts de data centers rien qu’en 2027.
À noter que le recours au gaz devient légion chez les géants de l'IA, qui semblent avoir fait l’impasse sur leurs engagements environnementaux. Mais reste à voir s’ils pourront continuer de croître de la même manière, alors que les électeurs américains ont clairement voté contre la prolifération de data centers dans le pays lors des élections de mi-mandat. Au Texas, la future gouverneure Gina Hinojosa a d’ailleurs fait campagne sur la promesse d’encadrer leur construction.

articles.title: LEGO Star Wars : l'AT-AT en pain d'épices et son Dark Vador de Noël à 41,99 €
articles.text:
Le LEGO Star Wars AT-AT façon pain d'épices 40806 est à 41,99 € (-30 %)
Un AT-AT transformé en maison en pain d'épices, avec un Dark Vador de Noël : le set LEGO Star Wars 40806 de 697 pièces passe à 41,99 € chez Amazon, soit 18 € de moins.
Vendu et expédié par Amazon, ce set affiche 41,99 € contre 59,99 € pour le prix conseillé, soit une remise de 30 %. C'est un produit très demandé : Amazon indique plus de 500 achats le mois dernier.
Un marcheur impérial version Noël
LEGO revisite le célèbre AT-AT de L'Empire contre-attaque en maison de pain d'épices, avec des décorations festives. Ses pattes sont articulées, le cockpit s'ouvre et les panneaux latéraux se soulèvent pour accéder à l'intérieur.
On y découvre le siège de Dark Vador près d'une cheminée, une table avec une boisson et un biscuit, ainsi que des chaussettes de Noël et des cadeaux.
Une minifigurine de Dark Vador en pain d'épices
Le set inclut une minifigurine de Dark Vador façon pain d'épices, avec un sucre d'orge et un sabre laser rouge. Avec ses 697 pièces, il fait aussi une jolie décoration de saison une fois monté.
LEGO le conseille à partir de 10 ans, ce qui en fait aussi une idée de cadeau pour les fans de Star Wars de tous âges. Il est noté 4,6/5 sur Amazon.

articles.title: Der Asteroid 1998 KY26 schert aus der Bahn – warum die Theorie vom dunklen Kometen kippt
articles.text:
Asteroid im All beschleunigt – und stellt Wissenschaftler vor Rätsel
Der erdnahe Asteroid mit der Bezeichnung 1998 KY26 bewegt sich nicht allein nach den Gesetzen der Schwerkraft durch das All, sondern erfährt senkrecht zu seiner Umlaufbahn um die Sonne eine zusätzliche, sogenannte nichtgravitative Beschleunigung. Bislang vermuteten mehrere Wissenschaftler:innen hinter dieser Bahnabweichung unsichtbar verdampfendes Wassereis im Inneren des Himmelskörpers, doch wie in einer im Fachmagazin Icarus veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, erweist sich der Gesteinsbrocken für dauerhafte Eisvorräte als deutlich zu warm.
Für die Untersuchung haben die beiden Raumfahrtingenieure Korbin Hansen und Masatoshi Hirabayashi vom Georgia Institute of Technology in Atlanta im US-Bundesstaat Georgia ein dreidimensionales Computermodell eingesetzt, das die Wärmeleitung von der Oberfläche bis in den Kern des rund elf Meter großen Körpers berechnet. Ihren Simulationen zufolge liegt die Temperatur selbst an den kältesten Stellen im Durchschnitt eines Sonnenumlaufs bei mindestens 212 Kelvin, was minus 61 Grad Celsius entspricht, während Wassereis im Vakuum selbst unter einer schützenden Gesteinsschicht nur unterhalb von 145 Kelvin beziehungsweise minus 128 Grad Celsius über längere Zeiträume stabil bleibt.
Warum 1998 KY26 am Georgia Institute of Technology durch den Eis-Test fällt
In der Astronomie galt der Himmelskörper seit einigen Jahren als Kandidat für einen sogenannten „dunklen Kometen“, also einen Körper, der zwar äußerlich wie ein gewöhnlicher Gesteinsasteroid ohne leuchtende Staubwolke aussieht, aber durch ausströmendes Gas wie durch kleine Steuerdüsen aus der Spur gedrückt wird. „Den Ergebnissen unseres Temperaturmodells zufolge würde auf 1998 KY26 zu viel Wasser entweichen, als dass sich Eis im Untergrund halten könnte – das grenzt genauer ein, woraus der Asteroid besteht“, schreiben Hansen und Hirabayashi in ihrer Arbeit, über die auch Sciencealert berichtet.
Wenn verdampfendes Eis – in der Fachsprache durch den direkten Übergang vom festen in den gasförmigen Zustand als Sublimation bezeichnet – tatsächlich die Ursache für die gemessene Bahnabweichung wäre, müsste der Asteroid pro Sekunde rund 0,03 Gramm Wasser verlieren und hätte seine Vorräte bereits nach 62 Jahren restlos aufgebraucht. Selbst ohne diese Schubwirkung würde ein Wasseranteil von einem Prozent der Gesamtmasse bei den berechneten Temperaturen innerhalb von gut 2.000 Jahren verschwinden, zumal der schnell rotierende Brocken vermutlich ein zusammenhängender Felsblock, ein sogenannter Monolith, ist und die Sonnenwärme dadurch viel besser ins Innere leitet als ein lockerer Trümmerhaufen-Asteroid aus Geröll und Staub.
Sonnenlicht statt Wasserdampf: Wie Strahlungsdruck den Asteroiden 1998 KY26 antreibt
Dass Forscher:innen überhaupt auf die Idee eines verborgenen Eis-Antriebs kamen, lag an veralteten Annahmen über die Größe des Objekts, das seit Ende der neunziger Jahre auf etwa 30 Meter Durchmesser geschätzt wurde. Erst im September 2025 zeigten Beobachtungen unter der Leitung des Astronomen Toni Santana-Ros von der spanischen Universität Alicante an den Teleskopen der Europäischen Südsternwarte (ESO), die im Fachjournal Nature Communications erschienen sind, dass 1998 KY26 lediglich elf Meter misst und sich alle 5,35 Minuten einmal um die eigene Achse dreht.
Durch das rund zwanzigmal geringere Gewicht und eine helle, stark eisenarme Gesteinsoberfläche, die 55 Prozent des einfallenden Sonnenlichts zurückwirft, genügen bereits konventionelle physikalische Kräfte, um den leichten Brocken merklich von seinem Kurs abzulenken. Wie ein Team um den Wissenschaftler Davide Farnocchia vom Jet Propulsion Laboratory der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa im Fachblatt The Astrophysical Journal Letters vorgerechnet hat, lässt sich die rätselhafte Beschleunigung durch den mechanischen Strahlungsdruck des Sonnenlichts sowie den sogenannten Jarkowski-Effekt erklären, bei dem die verzögerte Wärmeabstrahlung der aufgeheizten Oberfläche einen schwachen Rückstoß erzeugt.
Raumsonde Hayabusa 2 der Jaxa steht 2031 vor einem schwierigen Manöver
Trotz der deutlichen Ergebnisse aus Atlanta bleibt eine Einschränkung bestehen, da auch das neue Wärmemodell auf Annahmen beruht und unklar ist, wie lange sich 1998 KY26 schon auf seiner heutigen, sonnennahen Umlaufbahn befindet, die ihn bis auf knapp unter den Abstand zwischen Erde und Sonne an unser Zentralgestirn heranführt. Endgültige Gewissheit über die Beschaffenheit soll im Juli 2031 die Raumsonde Hayabusa 2 der japanischen Raumfahrtagentur Jaxa liefern, die sich bereits auf dem Weg zu dem Kleinkörper befindet.
Für die Ingenieur:innen der Jaxa bringen die jüngsten Erkenntnisse handfeste Probleme mit sich, weil sie die Mission ursprünglich für einen rund dreimal größeren und halb so schnell rotierenden Zielkörper geplant hatten. Da auf dem elf Meter kleinen, trockenen Felsblock abseits der Pole die Fliehkraft stärker wirkt als die eigene Anziehungskraft, wird jedes Annäherungs- oder gar Aufsetzmanöver der Sonde zu einem riskanten Unterfangen, bei dem aufgewirbeltes Material oder ein unkontrollierter Abpraller die Instrumente gefährden können.

articles.title: President Trump says the FBI is investigating Jensen Huang’s affair — Nvidia also accused of intervening in Megaspeed chip smuggling investigation
articles.text:
President Trump says the FBI is investigating Jensen Huang’s affair with suspected Chinese spy — Nvidia also accused of intervening in Megaspeed chip smuggling investigation
This raises questions about the company’s influence on the U.S. government.
As more information about the ongoing situation at Nvidia unravels, U.S. President Donald Trump has confirmed that the FBI is investigating CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy days after he admitted to the indiscretion. According to the Associated Press, the president said this during a briefing at the White House, with one reporter asking him about his knowledge of Huang’s issue before it became publicly known. The news comes amidst a separate bombshell report from Bloomberg, which claims that Nvidia intervened in a US government probe of suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed, where Alice Huang was an executive.
“Well, I’ve been hearing about it, and I’ve been reading about it over a period of time, but, uh, not too long ago,” Trump said. “We’ll look into, I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something, and I think he’ll be in good shape.” He also said, “I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling alright, how you’re doing. He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”
It has been previously reported that U.S. intelligence services suspected that Alice Huang, who previously held an executive position at Megaspeed, had ties to the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS), which is one of the country’s intelligence services, and that they told the President about it over a year ago. However, it was reported he did not act on the information, as he reportedly did not want to jeopardize Nvidia sales or antagonize Beijing, especially after the White House approved the export of H200 chips to China with an attached 25% fee.
Congress has called Huang once to confront him about these rumors, with the CEO confirming his affair with Alice Huang shortly after. The committee said it has "concerns over Nvidia’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage and Mr. Huang’s reported ties to a Chinese intelligence-linked executive of a Singapore-based data center company.” Now, it seems that the FBI, which is the U.S.’s primary domestic counterintelligence agency, is looking into the situation, too.
While the infidelity of tech executives is usually outside the purview of politicians and law enforcement, Jensen Huang’s sensitive position as the head of the leading AI chip manufacturer that arguably single-handedly drove the global AI race has made him a prominent target. China has denied the accusation that Alice Huang is its agent, but a think tank suggests that “China is employing ‘attractive women’ posing as investors, business professionals, academics, or romantic partners to gain access to U.S. tech talent, networks, and research infrastructure.”
This is why Nvidia’s supposed intervention in the U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security’s (BIS) investigation into Megaspeed is becoming a concern. Megaspeed has been investigated for allegedly smuggling $2 billion worth of Nvidia AI processors into China, although Nvidia has claimed that it has done its due diligence and did not find any signs of diversions by the company. Despite that, Bloomberg reports that Nvidia executive vice president and general counsel Tim Teter reached out to U.S. Under Secretary of Commerce for Industry and Security and BIS head Jeffrey Kessler to ask about the administration’s investigation into the company and whether the BIS was involved in Singapore’s detention of Alice Huang at that time. Sources claimed that the U.S. agency was not involved in Ms. Huang’s apprehension by Singaporean authorities.
The publication reported BIS staff were told to route all Nvidia requests through Kessler or to seek approval from him for any outreach involving the company, which people say was highly unusual, and that Teter even supposedly reached out directly to BIS employees. When the affected employees forwarded the emails to Kessler and raised their concerns, the BIS chief instructed them to handle the case by the book. articles.title: Bluetti’s new emergency power pack is super slim, installs in minutes, and keeps your fridge running to protect your food and medications during a blackout
articles.text:
Be prepared for blackouts — Bluetti’s compact backup battery keeps your fridge running for nearly 22 hours, is easy to install, and even fast-charges itself when storms are forecast
Keep your food and medications chilled in an emergency
- The Bluetti FridgePower keeps your food and temperature-sensitive medications cold for almost 22 hours in the event of a blackout
- Adding extra power packs can extend that to four days
- It's available now for £899 / $999 / AU$2,299
If, like us, you've been a bit baffled by governments around the world suddenly telling us to stock up on tinned food, radios and bottled water, you might be interested in Bluetti's new power pack specifically designed for fridges. With blackouts apparently expected everywhere at any time, the Bluetti FridgePower can keep your food and temperature-sensitive medications cold, even when the electricity goes out.
The FridgePower is a super slim battery pack with an uninterruptible power supply that delivers up to 1,800W of continuous output, and a claimed 21.6 hours of fridge/freezer backup. If you want to keep your fridge running during a longer outage, you can add extra power packs to extend the protection to up to four days.
If you think that sounds impressive, you're not alone — the device has just been named as an honoree in the CES Innovation Awards 2027.
Bluetti FridgePower: key features and pricing
At 75mm thick, the FridgePower is designed to slide in beside your fridge or inside a cabinet, and it's wall-mountable too. It can send push notifications to your phone for peace of mind (notifying you of its charge level, and sending system alerts), and there will be an optional fridge-mounted display available early next year.
Perhaps most interestingly of all, the FridgePower can monitor local weather conditions and initiate fast charging when a storm is forecast to make sure it's ready if a lightning strike takes out mains electricity.
The standard capacity is 2,016Wh and you can add additional batteries to take that up to 8,064Wh. You won't notice it running either, as its noise output is just 30dB in Quiet Mode.
This might be worth considering even if there isn't an impending apocalypse, because home batteries can help battle ever-increasing energy bills: if you have a tariff with lower rates off-peak you can charge the battery then and use it to deliver power during the more expensive peaks. Come the spring and you'd also be able to charge it via balcony solar panels or a portable solar power pack.

The list price of the Bluetti FridgePower is £129.99, though it's currently discounted to £899. In the US it's listed at $1,599, but Amazon is offering it for $999. It's AU$2,299 in Australia, down from AU$2,499.
