articles.title: Lumbra gets $25M in backing to help intelligence community deploy reliable AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Lumbra gets $25M in backing to help intelligence community deploy reliable AI agents
When it comes to matters of national security, it’s vitally important to ensure that the right intelligence gets to the right decision-makers, but doing this in today’s complex information technology environments is challenging, to say the least.
Enter the artificial intelligence startup Lumbra Inc., which has just raised $25 million in early-stage A funding to develop specialist autonomous agents tasked with sorting through the most sensitive data of all. Today’s Series A round was led by Point72 Ventures and Ansa Capital, with participation from seed round investor Costanoa.
Lumbra was founded last year by former Central Intelligence Agency officer Aaron Brown and ex-special forces infantry officer Michael Hiebert. Together, they’ve built a platform called LumbraOS, which is designed to orchestrate AI agents within high-consequence and ultra-secure computing environments, where risks of any kind simply cannot be tolerated.
Brown explained that LumbraOS was built from the ground up as a “model-neutral platform” that allows operators to mix and match various proprietary and open-weight AI models, assigning them different national security- and intelligence-related tasks. The platform is built on three key pillars: Nebula, StarChart and Astrolabe.
Nebula is the component tasked with managing agent orchestration, and works by tracing every “claim” generated by AI agents back to the primary source data behind that claim, so that domain experts can validate their outputs before decisions are made. StarChart is a dynamic knowledge graph that links disparate insights across multiple datasets through embedded sensitivity tags. Meanwhile, Astrolabe enforces governance policies and continuously evaluates each agent after benchmarking their performance prior to deployment to monitor for any alarming behavior.
Traditional AI systems developers struggle for years to ensure they meet the most rigorous federal security standards, but Brown and Hiebert say they developed LumbraOS specifically for classified computing environments. Just two months after launching their platform, they quietly landed a multimillion-dollar contract with an unnamed U.S. intelligence agency, with their AI agents operating on a top-secret defense network within just six months.
Impressed with the startup’s technology, the Pentagon followed up by naming Lumbra as one of two companies that underpins its Agent Network project, and one of seven “pace-setting projects” within its broader AI Acceleration strategy.
Following this traction, Lumbra’s co-founders believe there is potential for LumbraOS to expand beyond the intelligence community. They’re targeting enterprises in high-stakes industries such as healthcare, finance and law, where sensitive data leaks are deal breakers.
Brown said most organizations in these industries only use autonomous agents for singular tasks, if at all. That’s because they lack the tools to make those agents controllable, transparent and reliable enough at large scale. With its traceable audit logs and strict governance controls, Lumbra thinks it can help organizations to deploy agents safely across their networks to automate more complex workloads.
“The organizations that get agents right will spend less time telling them what to do and more time deciding what they may touch and what their work must prove,” Brown said. “Thousands of agents working a question together can find an insight while there’s still time to act on it. Lumbra exists to give decision-makers an advantage at the moment of decision.”
To target the enterprise, Lumbra plans to use the funds from today’s round to expand its engineering and product development teams and accelerate its go-to-market operations.
Ansa Capital Managing Partner Marco DeMeireles said the problem of trust and verifiability is the biggest barrier to adoption for AI agents in high-stakes environments. “Lumbra has demonstrated its ability to bring these capabilities into production across some of the most demanding environments within the U.S. government,” he said. “We believe these same capabilities will become foundational to how the world’s most critical enterprises deploy AI.”

articles.title: Faster money transfers are coming to a bank near you
articles.text:
Canada is finally getting faster bank transfers. Payments Canada’s new Real-Time Rail (RTR) payment system promises speedier payments and fund transfers — so fast, it could save Canada billions over the next decade.
Payments Canada announced RTR this week, noting the payment system is built around international standards, though you might not see the benefits right away. Financial institutions and payment providers are expected to come aboard over the next year.
The big change with RTR is a shift toward real-time payment processing. Currently, payments are usually handled in batches, meaning they can take a while to process. Under the new RTR system, payments can be handled within seconds, and it works 24/7, including holidays and weekends.
Faster payments, real benefits
Payments Canada positions this change as something with real, tangible benefits to Canadians and businesses. RTR could enable faster fund transfers between bank accounts, credit card payments, business-to-business payments, and more. It could also impact how businesses pay employees, particularly gig, freelance, and contract workers, by enabling businesses to pay as soon as work is completed.
Payments Canada even said that RTR could help those living paycheque to paycheque by helping remove the need to rely on high-interest payday loans.
On top of the increased processing speed, the RTR platform will include protections like fraud reporting, fraud transaction “safety” scores, and confirmation of payee tools.
A memo from the C.D. Howe Institute to Canadian financial institution customers estimates RTR could save between $5.3 and $14.5 billion over 10 years.
Some banks already support RTR
Canada partnered with companies like CGI, Deloitte Canada, IBM Canada, and Interac to develop RTR. Work started in 2021. However, Canada will be the last of the G7 nations to implement RTR.
So far, there are only a small number of financial institutions taking advantage of RTR:
- Wealthsimple
- Questbank
- Peoples Trust Company
- Paramount Commerce
- KOHO
- DoBusiness.com
- Digital Commerce Bank
- Bank of America
However, other Canadian banks are expected to join RTR as well. RBC, for example, is expected to adopt RTR in Q2 2027.

articles.title: La guerra del chocolate: Toblerone demanda a una empresa de 10 empleados: “Esa es nuestra barra”
articles.text:
La multinacional estadounidense dueña de Toblerone (Mondelēz) ha llevado a los tribunales a Catherine’s Originals. Se trata de una pequeña empresa británica que elabora chocolates veganos. Los administradores están incluidos en la plantilla media de 10 personas. El motivo es que la barrita de chocolate que comercializa esta firma, llamada O’bar, según Mondelēz, tiene una forma muy similar a la de la marca suiza.
Mondelēz acusa a la pequeña firma de infringir sus derechos de marca. La fundadora de Catherine's Originals, Catherine Dodd, niega que esto sea así. Sostiene que el diseño curvo de su chocolate representa la O de Originals.
Catherine Dodd comenzó este negocio en 2021. La empresa está ubicada en West Sussex (Inglaterra). Recibe muchos de sus pedidos a través de Instagram. Tiene que defender ahora el diseño de uno de sus productos ante una multinacional que también es propietaria de Oreo y Cadbury y que cuenta con unos 91.000 empleados en todo el mundo.
Una disputa por la forma del chocolate
La fundadora admite que le da miedo tener que enfrentarse a este tipo de demandas. Niega las acusaciones y defiende que tiene derecho a proteger su creación. Cree que su tamaño no debe limitar su capacidad de defensa de su producto.
Mondelēz asegura que el contorno de Toblerone es un diseño distintivo que necesita protección. Afirma que ha intentado abordar el asunto directamente con Catherine’s Originals. Y lo ha hecho durante varios meses. Pero estas conversaciones no han llegado a ningún acuerdo. Hay un enfrentamiento entre ambas partes.
También en 2017 Mondelēz presentó una reclamación sobre la barrita Twin Peaks de Poundland. Esta cadena británica pospuso el lanzamiento de su producto tras la reclamación. Cambió el diseño de la barrita y también de su envoltorio.

articles.title: 3 Books to read instead of doomscrolling every day
articles.text:
3 Books to read instead of doomscrolling every day
Replace endless scrolling with meaningful reading. Discover three books that can help you reclaim your attention & build healthier digital habits.
How often do you pick up your phone to check one notification and end up spending the next hour scrolling through Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts or endless social media updates?
Doomscrolling has quietly become part of everyday life. What begins as a few minutes of entertainment can turn into hours of consuming content without much thought or purpose. While social media keeps us occupied, it can also leave us feeling distracted, mentally exhausted and dissatisfied.
One way to break this habit is to replace mindless scrolling with something that adds value to your life. Reading is a great place to start. Even dedicating 15–20 minutes a day to a good book can help you develop new perspectives, improve your focus, and use your free time better.
If you are looking for a reason to put your phone down, here are three books worth adding to your reading list.
3 Books to read instead of doomscrolling every day
1. Digital Minimalism by Cal Newport
If you constantly find yourself checking your phone without a specific reason, Digital Minimalism is a good place to begin.
In this book, Cal Newport introduces the idea of using technology intentionally rather than allowing it to dictate how you spend your time. He explains that digital minimalism is not about abandoning technology altogether. Instead, it involves identifying which digital tools genuinely add value to your life and reducing the ones that create unnecessary distractions.
One of the book's key ideas is a 30-day digital declutter, which encourages readers to step away from optional digital activities and gradually reintroduce only those that serve a meaningful purpose.
Why you should read it: This book can help you rethink your relationship with social media, set healthier boundaries with your phone and make more room for activities that genuinely matter.
2. Stolen Focus by Johann Hari
Have you ever opened an app for a few minutes, only to realise that an entire hour has passed? Or found yourself switching between multiple tabs while struggling to finish a simple task?
Stolen Focus explores the growing attention crisis and the factors that make it difficult for people to concentrate. Johann Hari investigates how technology, constant interruptions, information overload and other aspects of modern life affect our ability to pay attention.
Rather than blaming individuals for having poor self-control, the author examines the wider systems and habits that contribute to distracted living.
Why you should read it: If you want to understand why doomscrolling and constant notifications make it difficult to focus, this book offers an insightful look at the problem and how we can begin reclaiming our attention.
3. How to Break Up with Your Phone by Catherine Price
If you have tried reducing your screen time but keep returning to the same scrolling habits, this book offers a practical starting point.
How to Break Up with Your Phone explores how smartphones influence our attention, daily routines and relationships. Catherine Price encourages readers to examine their phone habits and understand what keeps them reaching for their devices.
The book offers a 30-day plan designed to help readers develop a healthier relationship with their phones. Instead of asking you to give up technology completely, it focuses on making more conscious choices about when and why you use it.
Why you should read it: This is a useful choice if you want practical steps to reduce unnecessary screen time, build better habits and spend more time enjoying life away from a screen.
Final thoughts
Doomscrolling can make us feel occupied without necessarily making our lives more meaningful. We consume hundreds of posts, watch countless videos and follow endless updates, yet often struggle to remember what we actually gained from all that screen time.
These three books offer different ways to understand and address the problem. While Digital Minimalism helps you use technology more intentionally, Stolen Focus explores why our attention is constantly under pressure, and How to Break Up with Your Phone offers practical steps to change your habits.
You do not have to stop using social media completely. Start by replacing just 15 minutes of scrolling with reading every day. Over time, that small change can help you build a more intentional and fulfilling routine.

articles.title: BYD vai conectar 200 mil carros no Brasil com eSIMs da TIM • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
BYD vai conectar 200 mil carros no Brasil com eSIMs da TIM
Parceria prevê a instalação de chips virtuais nos veículos da montadoranos e redes 4G/5G no complexo industrial de Camaçari, na Bahia.
A BYD fechou uma parceria com a TIM para conectar cerca de 200 mil carros no Brasil nos próximos 24 meses. O acordo prevê o uso de chips virtuais (eSIM) nos veículos da montadora chinesa e a instalação de redes móveis 4G e 5G dedicadas no complexo industrial de Camaçari, na Bahia.
A operadora também fornecerá a infraestrutura necessária para conectar funcionários, equipamentos e automóveis durante a fabricação.
As empresas não informaram quais modelos serão contemplados primeiro nem divulgaram um cronograma detalhado de implementação. Também não está claro se carros já vendidos poderão receber a solução.
O eSIM é um chip integrado ao equipamento que dispensa a instalação de um cartão SIM comum. Nos carros, a tecnologia permite manter a conexão com a operadora para serviços digitais, sem exigir que o motorista compartilhe a internet do próprio celular.
Entre as aplicações estão navegação com dados atualizados, entretenimento e funções remotas acessadas pelo smartphone. A BYD ainda não detalhou quais funcionalidades estarão disponíveis por meio do acordo.
A TIM informa que sua rede 4G alcança todos os municípios brasileiros e que o 5G está disponível em cerca de 1,1 mil cidades, ou seja, o acesso também depende da área de cobertura e das condições da rede. Também não foram divulgados preços de planos ou franquias de dados. Outra dúvida é se os serviços virão incluídos no valor dos veículos ou se haverá assinaturas separadas.
A operadora já possui experiência nesse mercado por meio da parceria com a Stellantis. Veículos como Jeep Renegade e Compass e Fiat Toro receberam conexão 4G com eSIM da operadora.
O contrato também prevê uma infraestrutura móvel dedicada no complexo industrial da BYD em Camaçari, Bahia. O projeto inclui sete pontos de cobertura externa e 63 equipamentos distribuídos em galpões e áreas operacionais, segundo as informações divulgadas pelo Mobile Time.
A rede deverá conectar funcionários, visitantes, sistemas industriais e os próprios carros durante o processo de fabricação. A expectativa das empresas é facilitar a circulação de informações em tempo real e apoiar a digitalização da produção.
Inaugurado em outubro de 2025, o complexo ocupa cerca de 4,6 milhões de metros quadrados e é a maior operação industrial da BYD fora da China. A unidade começou montando veículos como Dolphin Mini, King e Song Pro e passa por um processo de expansão da produção.
Em comunicado, o CEO da TIM Brasil, Alberto Griselli, associou o acordo à digitalização da indústria e à expansão da conectividade embarcada. O vice-presidente sênior da BYD no Brasil, Alexandre Baldy, destacou a intenção de oferecer serviços que continuem evoluindo depois da compra do carro.
As companhias não revelaram o valor do contrato nem estabeleceram publicamente uma data para concluir a instalação da rede dedicada.

articles.title: L'iPhone 18 et l'iPhone 18e auraient plus de points communs que prévu : pourquoi c'est une (très) bonne nouvelle
articles.text:
Début 2027, probablement entre mars et avril, Apple devrait sortir les iPhone 18, iPhone 18e et iPhone Air 2. La série 18 serait celle qui rapprocherait le plus le modèle de base avec le modèle « e » si l’on en croit une nouvelle fuite.
Même batterie, même écran : les points communs s’accumulent
C’est le leaker Fixed Focus Digital qui a publié cette fuite sur le réseau social chinois Weibo ce 7 novembre. Il y a publié une image de deux prototypes de ce qui seraient les prochains iPhone à venir. Tout d’abord, il confirme que la batterie serait plus grande que sur les versions précédentes pour les deux modèles. Une batterie de capacité identique avec 4 430 mAh. Une augmentation significative qui serait à prévoir donc, puisque l’iPhone 17 et l’iPhone 17e ont respectivement des capacités de 3 692 et 4 005 mAh. Et avec une meilleure puce, l’A20 gravée en 2 nm, ces modèles 18 devraient proposer une meilleure autonomie.
Côté photo, on apprend que le capteur principal de l’iPhone 18 serait légèrement plus petit, tout en conservant sa définition de 48 Mpx ; Apple gagnerait un petit peu de place avec. Malheureusement, le capteur ultra-grand-angle resterait absent du modèle plus abordable.
Autre point commun, l’écran : une dalle de 6,3 pouces dans les deux cas. Un point très intéressant : Apple n’a jusqu’à maintenant jamais proposé d’écran de cette taille avec une encoche. On peut alors laisser libre cours à son imagination : et si la marque l’abandonnait au profit d’un écran avec une Dynamic Island ? Ce serait une très belle amélioration pour l’iPhone 18e et cela ne donnerait pas du tout l’impression d’avoir un « iPhone au rabais ». Mais ce point n’est malheureusement que spéculation.
Faut-il croire cette nouvelle fuite ?
Cette fuite va à l’encontre des rumeurs précédentes à propos de l’iPhone 18e. Ces dernières racontaient que rien ne changerait sur l’écran : une dalle Oled de 6,12 pouces, limitée à 60 Hz. Pas de changement sur l’écran signifie aussi que l’encoche serait toujours là. À plusieurs mois de la sortie de ce smartphone, il est encore trop tôt pour savoir si Apple proposerait effectivement une nouvelle dalle.
Du côté de l’iPhone 18, on savait déjà que la batterie serait plus grosse. Une autre rumeur il y a quelques jours évoquait le chiffre de 4 056 mAh, une petite différence avec celle que nous évoquons ici. Mais pour ces deux téléphones (trois avec l’iPhone Air 2), il faudrait aussi et surtout s’attendre à des hausses de prix, comme sur les iPhone 18 Pro et 18 Pro Max.

articles.title: Ollama
articles.text:
Ollama is an open-source platform for running large language models (LLMs) locally on macOS, Linux, and Windows. It lets you download, manage, customize, and run models such as Llama 4, Qwen 3, Gemma 3, Phi-4, DeepSeek-R1, Mistral, and many others, without relying on cloud services. Ollama is free and open-source under the MIT License.
Do I need an internet connection to use Ollama?
Only to download models. Once installed, these models can operate entirely offline without sending prompts or responses to cloud servers. However, downloading models, accessing cloud-hosted models, and using online integrations require an internet connection.
Can I use Ollama with my own models?
Yes, Ollama supports custom models via GGUF format and lets you tweak prompts and parameters through a Modelfile.
Features
- Local-first and lightweight: Install and run LLMs via a simple CLI (ollama run ), leveraging your own CPU/GPU instead of cloud servers.
- Extensible and developer-friendly: Integrates well with Docker, REST API, and libraries in Python and JavaScript.
- Customizable models and prompts: Supports tweaking parameters, system messages (via "Modelfile"), and importing custom GGUF/Safetensors models.
What's New
- Added support for Ripple Preview, a 65B model designed for agentic coding.
- Reduced memory usage for Qwen3.8 Flash Next by approximately 27 GiB on Apple Silicon.
- Improved Claude Code integration through ollama launch claude.
- Added clearer messages when cloud models have been retired.
- Improved compatibility with the OpenAI Responses API.
- Added CUDA 13.5 support for Windows on ARM.
- Updated llama.cpp.
System Requirements
Platform & OS
- macOS: Big Sur (11) or later
- Linux: Ubuntu 18.04 / 20.04 / 22.04 or later
- Windows: Full support via native installer or WSL 2
CPU
- Minimum: Any modern x86-64 CPU supporting AVX2 (Intel/AMD)
- Recommended: 11th-gen Intel or AMD Zen 4 with AVX512 and ideally DDR5 memory
Memory RAM
- Minimum: 8GB
- Recommended: 16GB
GPU (Optional, but boosts performance significantly)
- Not required, but speeds inference dramatically
- Minimum recommendation: Nvidia or AMD GPU with 8 GB VRAM for 7B – 13B models
For large models:
- 30B model: 16 GB VRAM
- 65B model: 32 GB VRAM
- Very large models (70B+): 48 GB or more, possibly multi-GPU

articles.title: Pré-Black Friday Amazon : 5 mini PC en promotion jusqu’à -32%, dès 197,16€
articles.text:
À un peu plus de deux semaines du Black Friday, fixé au vendredi 27 novembre, Amazon affiche déjà des offres à durée limitée sur son rayon mini PC. Nous en avons retenu 5, de la petite machine de bureautique au modèle taillé pour le multitâche, en comparant chaque prix au plus bas des 30 derniers jours affiché sur la fiche.
Un mini PC tient derrière un écran ou dans un coin de bureau et suffit à la plupart des usages du quotidien : bureautique, navigation, visioconférence, streaming. Les cinq modèles relevés ce mardi 10 novembre chez Amazon répondent à deux besoins distincts : deux machines d’entrée de gamme à moins de 235 €, et trois configurations plus musclées entre 519,96 € et 619,99 €, avec 16 à 24 Go de mémoire vive.
Toutes ces offres portent la mention « Offre à durée limitée » sur leur fiche, sans date de fin indiquée. Elles sont proposées par des vendeurs tiers sur la marketplace d’Amazon, et non par Amazon directement. Le prix du NiPoGi H2, lui, suppose de cocher un coupon sur la fiche avant l’ajout au panier.
Les 5 mini PC en promotion chez Amazon avant le Black Friday
- Mini PC GMKtec NucBox M5 Ultra (Ryzen 7 7730U, 16 Go, 1 To) à 529,96 € au lieu de 629,96 €
- Mini PC GMKtec NucBox G3S (Intel N95, 8 Go, 256 Go) à 230,59 € au lieu de 268,96 €
- Mini PC GMKtec M3 Pro (Core i5-13500H, 16 Go, 512 Go) à 519,96 € au lieu de 639,96 €
- Mini PC NiPoGi H2 (Core 5 220H, 24 Go, 512 Go) à 619,99 € au lieu de 729,99 €, avec le coupon à cocher sur la fiche
- Mini PC GMKtec NucBox G5S (Intel N5095, 8 Go, 128 Go) à 197,16 € au lieu de 288,96 €
VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
5 mini PC, 5 usages : ce qu’il faut savoir avant de choisir
Sur ce type de machine, le processeur, la quantité de mémoire vive et la capacité du SSD décident de presque tout. Pour chacun des cinq modèles, voici l’usage auquel il répond et la limite à connaître, d’après les caractéristiques annoncées par les fabricants : nous n’avons testé aucune de ces configurations.
- GMKtec NucBox M5 Ultra : le plus complet du lot pour un poste de travail fixe. Son Ryzen 7 7730U à 8 cœurs est accompagné de 16 Go de mémoire vive et d’un SSD de 1 To, la plus grande capacité de la sélection. Il ajoute deux ports Ethernet 2,5 Gb/s, utiles pour un petit serveur maison. Il se contente en revanche d’une puce graphique intégrée : ce n’est pas une machine de jeu.
- GMKtec NucBox G3S : une machine de bureautique et de streaming, avec un Intel N95 à 4 cœurs, 8 Go de mémoire vive et deux sorties HDMI 4K. Ses 256 Go de stockage et son Wi-Fi 5 fixent ses limites. La baisse réelle est modeste : 5 % sous son prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, qui était de 242,73 €.
- GMKtec M3 Pro : son Core i5-13500H compte 12 cœurs et il peut piloter trois écrans 4K, ce qui le destine au multitâche de bureau. À 10 € de moins que le M5 Ultra, il n’embarque toutefois que 512 Go de stockage, soit moitié moins. GMKtec précise lui-même que sa partie graphique n’est pas conçue pour le jeu.
- NiPoGi H2 : le mieux doté en mémoire vive, avec 24 Go de LPDDR5 associés à un Core 5 220H à 12 cœurs. La fiche ne mentionne aucune extension possible de cette mémoire, contrairement au stockage, qui dispose de deux emplacements M.2. Sans le coupon, le prix reste à 659,99 €, et le port Ethernet se limite au Gigabit.
- GMKtec NucBox G5S : le plus petit et le moins cher : 7,1 cm de côté pour 207 g, de quoi le fixer derrière un écran ou le poser près d’un téléviseur. Son Intel N5095 et ses 8 Go de mémoire vive visent la navigation, la vidéo et les documents. Les 128 Go du SSD sont vite occupés : la fiche annonce un SSD remplaçable jusqu’à 4 To et un lecteur microSD pour compléter.
Des remises affichées plus fortes que les baisses réelles
Les pourcentages affichés par Amazon vont de -10 % à -32 %, mais quatre d’entre eux sont calculés sur un ancien prix ou un prix conseillé. Rapportée au prix le plus bas des 30 derniers jours, indiqué sur chaque fiche, la baisse est de 15 % pour le NucBox M5 Ultra, de 10 % pour le M3 Pro et le NiPoGi H2 (15 % avec son coupon), et de 5 % pour les NucBox G3S et G5S.
Aucune de ces fiches n’indique de date de fin, et rien ne garantit que ces prix baisseront encore le 27 novembre. Le choix dépend surtout de l’usage : un modèle à processeur N95 ou N5095 suffit pour la bureautique et la vidéo, quand 16 Go de mémoire vive et un processeur à 8 ou 12 cœurs apportent de la marge pour travailler sur plusieurs applications à la fois. Pour situer ces machines face au reste du marché, notre comparatif des meilleurs mini-PC passe en revue les critères à regarder, du processeur à la connectique.
Mini PC et Black Friday : vos questions
Quand a lieu le Black Friday 2026 ?
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre 2026. Amazon enchaîne les offres à durée limitée depuis la fin octobre, dont celles de cette sélection.
Que peut-on faire avec un mini PC à moins de 250 € ?
Les modèles à processeur Intel N95 ou N5095 et 8 Go de mémoire vive sont pensés pour la bureautique, la navigation, la visioconférence et la lecture de vidéos. Ils visent des usages légers, pas le jeu ni le montage vidéo.
Comment obtenir le prix de 619,99 € sur le NiPoGi H2 ?
Il faut cocher le coupon proposé sur la fiche Amazon avant d’ajouter le produit au panier : la réduction s’applique au moment du paiement. Sans cette case, le mini PC est facturé 659,99 €.
Comment profiter des offres exclusives du Black Friday ?

Pour les aficionados de X, n'hésitez pas à suivre notre compte Clubic Bons Plans pour être au courant en direct des meilleures offres.

articles.title: Seagate Launches the FireCuda Forge Powered by the New Alkemi Intelligent Platform
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
Seagate Launches the FireCuda Forge Powered by the New Alkemi Intelligent Platform
Seagate Technology Holdings plc, a mass-capacity data storage leader, today introduced the Seagate FireCuda Forge drive, representing the first Seagate hard drive powered by the Alkemi intelligent storage platform. With Alkemi, the FireCuda Forge combines solid-state drive (SSD) responsiveness and hard disk drive (HDD) capacity in a single drive, using adaptive intelligence to give gamers and creators the speed and space they need without added complexity.
A new platform for a new reality
From massive game libraries and 4K video to AI-powered animation, people are creating, working with, and keeping more data than ever. IDC projects annual global data generation will more than triple, from 218 zettabytes in 2025 to more than 718 zettabytes by 2030. As digital libraries expand, consumers need fast access to active content and the capacity to preserve growing collections.Engineered to improve with use, the Alkemi dynamic-caching technology learns how data is used in real-time and automatically prioritizes frequently accessed content from a user's SSD, while ensuring the HDD provides capacity for larger libraries. The result brings intelligent data tiering from the data center to the desktop, dynamically caching data based on activity patterns, to deliver fast and easy access without users having to manage where their data lives.
"For years, external storage has forced users to choose: speed or scale. Forge is built on the idea that they shouldn't have to," said Lance Ohara, VP of Edge IoT Marketing at Seagate. "Powered by our new Alkemi technology, it combines the responsiveness users want with the storage capacity they need in one intelligently managed system to give gamers and creators the best of both worlds."
FireCuda Forge is the first product to deliver the Alkemi experience, combining a user's NVMe SSD with the Forge's high-capacity HDD to onboard processing in a single box. Seagate engineers designed the FireCuda Forge to provide fast, seamless access to the content people use most, while offering the capacity to keep more of what matters, whether gaming, streaming, creating or managing everyday digital life.
Product highlights
- First product build on the Alkemi platform: Alkemi learns and adapts over time to keep high-demand content fast and accessible on a user's SSD, while the HDD provides space for growing libraries. Behind the scenes, Alkemi manages data placement, giving users the simplicity of a single storage drive.
- Performance for demanding workflows: Up to 2,500 MB/s read and 2,000 MB/s write performance.
- Choice and expandability: The FireCuda Forge contains an upgradeable HDD, and users select and provide their own NVMe SSD that is required for operational compatibility.
- High-bandwidth connectivity: USB4 supports gaming and creator workflows on compatible systems.
- Platform support: Designed to support Windows 11 and macOS 26 and above.
Availability:
The FireCuda Forge is available now through the Seagate on-line store and authorized partners in 8 TB and 20 TB configurations, starting at $699 (8 TB) and $899 (20 TB). Product availability may vary by market.
[Editor's note: The Seagate FireCuda Forge doesn't include an SSD, it's up to the user to add their own SSD.]
Source:
				Seagate

articles.title: Google Fi adds support for a second 5G network, won't say which one
articles.text:
Google has announced a “super network” upgrade for its Fi cell service. For the past few years, Google Fi has operated exclusively on the T-Mobile network, but now it’s adding support for a second 5G network. Oddly, Google refuses to say which one.
Google’s MVNO (mobile virtual network operator) launched in 2015 as Project Fi with support for both T-Mobile and Sprint service. The service initially only worked on Google’s Nexus phones, which would switch between networks based on signal strength. After T-Mobile absorbed Sprint, Fi switched to being a single-network service in the US while continuing to hop between networks for international travel.
With the super network, Google Fi is again a dual-carrier service stateside. Phones connected to Fi will be able to hop between T-Mobile 5G and a different 5G network to provide the best possible connectivity. Google’s blog post announcing the change conspicuously doesn’t mention either network, saying only that it supports “two of America’s best 5G cellular networks.”
We know one of them is T-Mobile, and the other must be either AT&T or Verizon. When reached for comment, a Google spokesperson declined to name the second network, which is odd. Looking at the Fi coverage map, my best guess for the super network partner is Verizon. The shape of unserved regions is a closer match than AT&T, but carriers do tend to fudge the fine details of these maps.

articles.title: Anthropic crea su propio Office con Claude y quiere cambiar tu forma de trabajar
articles.text:
Anthropic está a nada de salir a la bolsa y, como parte de su estrategia para la oferta pública inicial, la empresa ha lanzado su versión de Office impulsada por IA. En un evento para medios, el gigante tecnológico presentó nuevas funciones que convierten a Claude en una suite ofimática. Entre ellas se encuentra Claude Meetings, una herramienta que permite añadir la IA a tus llamadas para que tome apuntes en tiempo real.
De acuerdo con TechCrunch, Claude Meetings funciona como un participante más dentro de una videollamada. Los equipos pueden invitar a Claude a una reunión de Google Meet y la IA seguirá la conversación en tiempo real, registrando datos y respondiendo preguntas en el chat. Claude puede redactar planes de trabajo, crear cronogramas o revisar aplicaciones conectadas para extraer información relevante para la llamada, todo en tiempo real.
Una vez que concluye la reunión, todo el material que se generó queda disponible dentro del historial de Claude para usarlo en consultas a futuro. Anthropic afirma que Claude siempre se identificará como un participante de la reunión y no se unirá a llamadas con invitados externos, a menos que lo autorice el administrador. La compañía señala que su IA puede convertir las discusiones en acciones mientras se lleva a cabo la llamada, por lo que no es necesario colgar para comenzar a delegar responsabilidades.
Además de la IA en las videollamadas, Anthropic presentó Claude Sheets, una herramienta que compite directamente con Excel. En lugar de comenzar desde una plantilla vacía, los usuarios pueden pedirle a Claude que cree un presupuesto o que haga un seguimiento de campañas a través de una instrucción en lenguaje natural. Una vez que envías el prompt, la IA generará una hoja de cálculo con pestañas, fórmulas y menús desplegables.
Anthropic planta cara a Excel con Claude Sheets
Posteriormente, el usuario puede pedirle a Claude que edite las celdas, realice cambios y explique cada modificación para que todos sepan qué fue lo que hizo. Sobre esta línea, Microsoft ya ha integrado funciones similares en Excel y otras aplicaciones de Office como Word y PowerPoint. La diferencia con Claude Sheets es que la herramienta de Anthropic se integra con el flujo de trabajo de Claude para que no saltes entre aplicaciones.
Por último, Anthropic presentó Claude Whiteboards, una especie de pizarra colaborativa con IA. Esta herramienta permite desarrollar ideas en un espacio compartido, en donde los usuarios discuten un plan y Claude le da forma para convertirlo en un espacio de trabajo visual.
Al igual que vemos en Sheets, no es necesario usar otra aplicación para una lluvia de ideas, puesto que Claude convertirá todo el material en un documento o una presentación con diapositivas. Whiteboards se integra con Claude Meetings, por lo que los participantes pueden invocar la pizarra durante una videollamada.
Anthropic también lanzó otras funciones enfocadas a empresas, como Claude Data, que permite conectar a Claude con sistemas CRM y almacenes de datos. También existen nuevos conectores para aplicaciones de Adobe, Atlassian y HubSpot, con los cuales se pueden abrir versiones completas de algunas herramientas dentro de la interfaz de Claude para no salir de la conversación.
Claude Meetings estará disponible en fase beta para los usuarios de Team y Enterprise, pero solo funcionará con Google Meet en un inicio. Mientras tanto, Claude Whiteboards y Claude Sheet podrán usarse en cualquier plan de pago dentro de la web y las apps de escritorio o móvil. Estas últimas también se lanzan en fase beta con miras a mejorarlas sobre la marcha.

articles.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy: a timeline | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security.
United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)
Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China.
The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.
As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.
November 9, 2026: Huang pulls out of various speaking engagements
The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.
November 9-10, 2026: Details emerge about the business relationships between Nvidia and the alleged spy
Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became an Nvidia-preferred cloud partner, giving it priority access to chips, The Information reported. The Information also reported that Shanghai Century Litong facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.
Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 U.S. government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported. Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.
In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.
November 8, 2026: Trump shows support for Nvidia CEO, calls him a “fine person”
On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.
“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.
When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia, Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”
November 8, 2026: Huang admits to affair in public message to Nvidia employees; Nvidia board of directors begins investigation
Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.
“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”
Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”
“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.
Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.
November 5, 2026: Three Republican committee chairmen ask Huang for closed-door briefing
Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.
“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote. “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”
October 29, 2026: Jensen Huang publicly revealed to have developed ‘close relationship’ with suspected Chinese spy
U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.
An Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.
“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”
Spring 2026: A secret memo circulates in the Trump administration about Nvidia CEO’s alleged relationship with Chinese spy
U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers that warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.
Late 2025: President Trump briefed on U.S. surveillance of Alice Huang and her relationship to Nvidia CEO but does not take action
Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report, U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.
The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump, has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.
October 2025: U.S. and Singapore each investigate Megaspeed over possible Chinese export violations
Megaspeed was confirmed to be under investigation by both the U.S. and Singaporean governments in October 2025. As a customer of Nvidia, Megaspeed was suspected of helping Chinese companies get around American embargoes on chip exports.
Megaspeed, a neocloud that used Nvidia chips, had been renting computing power to Chinese internet giant Alibaba and other Chinese companies, the Times reported. A Commerce Department official who had visited Megaspeed’s data center in Malaysia in 2024 had found a hoard of Nvidia equipment that was still packed in boxes and the concern was that this equipment was being directly shipped somewhere else, like China, rather than installed and sold as a cloud service.
Jensen Huang had been spotted socializing with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang as early as 2024 in Taiwan, where the Nvidia CEO was born.
These investigations into Megaspeed highlighted concerns about the degree to which Nvidia is able to track its chip exports. At the time, an Nvidia spokesperson told press that the company did not have “any reason to believe products had been diverted.”
“NVIDIA visited multiple Megaspeed sites yet again earlier this week and confirmed what we previously observed — Megaspeed is running a small commercial cloud, like many other companies throughout the world, as allowed by U.S. export control rules,” the Nvidia spokesperson said at the time.

articles.title: Oman's 44.01 secures fresh investment from Holcim
articles.text:
Oman's 44.01 secures fresh investment from Holcim
- Omani climatetech company 44.01 has secured a strategic investment from Swiss building materials company Holcim through its corporate venture capital activities. The investment amount and equity stake were not disclosed.
- Founded in 2020 by Talal Hassan, Ehab Tasfai and Karan Khimji, 44.01 develops carbon mineralisation technology that injects captured carbon dioxide into reactive underground rock formations, converting it into stable carbonate minerals for permanent storage.
- The investment will support 44.01's commercial scaling and international expansion, building on its existing partnership with Holcim. Other investors in the company include JERA, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Equinor Ventures, Air Liquide Venture Capital and Siemens Financial Services.
- In July 2024, 44.01 closed a $37 million Series A funding round, led by Equinor Ventures with Shorooq Partners and other investors.
Press release:
Holcim has invested in 44.01, a developer of breakthrough mineralisation technology where captured CO₂ is injected into naturally reactive ultramafic rock formations and mineralised into stable carbonate rock. The investment will support 44.01's scaling and international expansion and marks the next step in an established commercial relationship between Holcim and 44.01.
Since July, the two companies have been running a pilot project under live industrial conditions at Holcim's Fujairah cement plant in the United Arab Emirates, where CO₂ is now being safely stored underground and mineralised into solid rock. Other investors in 44.01 include JERA, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Equinor Ventures, Air Liquide Venture Capital and Siemens Financial Services.
Ram Muthu, Head of Operational Excellence, Holcim: "Holcim’s investment in 44.01 builds on our existing project in the UAE, where together we are already storing captured carbon in rock formations near our Fujairah plant. 44.01’s breakthrough technology enables storage close to production given the right geological conditions, advancing decarbonisation in line with Holcim’s NextGen Growth 2030 strategy. This pathway can help us manage captured carbon at inland sites across our operations where access to offshore storage may be limited."
The investment is a valuable addition to Holcim's growing portfolio of digital and decarbonisation technologies, part of its open innovation ecosystem. Holcim has made 22 investments to date through Holcim MAQER Ventures, its corporate venture capital and open innovation unit, and is constantly working to scale groundbreaking technologies for the built environment.

articles.title: Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop
articles.text:
Google’s Pixel phones get an update every month, but most are just security patches and bug fixes. The bigger changes are bundled into quarterly Pixel Drops, and one is rolling out today. The update brings a few new things, and many of the Gemini features previously exclusive to the latest Pixel phones will also expand to Google’s Pixel 10 lineup.
The Pixel 11 was Google’s first foray into “Gemini Intelligence” branding, something we’ll see a lot more of going forward. Some of the features under that heading were limited to Google’s newest phones (and in some cases, Samsung’s phones). The November Pixel Drop will expand these AI features to the Pixel 10 lineup, but importantly, that doesn’t include the budget-oriented Pixel 10a.
For starters, the Pixel 10 series will get the improved personalized suggestions (previously known as Magic Cue) that debuted on the Pixel 11. This enables things like sending grocery lists to Google Keep from other apps and generating summaries from the context menu. Rambler, Google’s AI-assisted voice input system, is also coming to the 2025 phones. Likewise, Gemini app automation will roll out on Pixel 10 with this update. This feature is still limited to select apps in rideshare, food delivery, travel, and a few other categories.
The AI-powered icon theming that Google added to Pixels back in March is also getting an update. Initially, this feature just matched icon colors to the system theme when developers didn’t include the necessary theming assets. With this update, Google says it has moved the feature to a more powerful Nano Banana model, unlocking 10 new icon styles for your home screen.

articles.title: 5 lessons from Hospitality with a Heart by Amrita Tripathi
articles.text:
5 lessons from Hospitality with a Heart by Amrita Tripathi
Discover five powerful lessons from Hospitality with a Heart by Amrita Tripathi, a book exploring identity, acceptance, empathy and workplace inclusion.
The stories that deserve to be heard are not always the ones that get told. Some remain hidden behind societal expectations, fear of judgement and the struggle to find acceptance.
I recently attended the launch of Hospitality with a Heart, written by Amrita Tripathi, with an introduction by Keshav Suri, Executive Director of The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group. Held on October 31, 2026, at the Crystal Ballroom of The LaLiT New Delhi, the event brought together the people behind the book and those who have been part of the organisation's inclusion journey.
The book documents the personal journeys and lived experiences of queer team members at The LaLiT, exploring themes of identity, discrimination, resilience, acceptance and belonging.
The evening began with a welcome address by Dr Jyotsna Suri, Chairperson and Managing Director of The LaLiT Suri Hospitality Group, followed by a keynote address by Saurabh Kirpal. A panel discussion moderated by journalist Faye D'Souza, featuring Amrita Tripathi, Rithik Hukku, Shaurya and Shruti, explored workplace inclusion, queer representation and the importance of empathy.
The launch also featured the unveiling of the book by the Group's leadership and the people whose stories it captures, followed by drag performances by Hash Brownie and Hiten Noonwal.
Beyond the celebrations, what stood out was the larger message of creating spaces where people are not merely included but genuinely accepted.
5 Important lessons readers can take away from Hospitality with a Heart
1. True inclusion begins with acceptance
One of the central ideas explored in Hospitality with a Heart is that inclusion goes beyond simply allowing people to be part of an organisation.
For individuals from marginalised communities, finding acceptance can be a difficult journey. Social expectations, discrimination, bullying and fear of judgement can make it challenging to express one's identity openly.
The stories in the book highlight why acceptance matters. People should not have to hide parts of themselves to fit into a workplace or earn respect.
True inclusion begins when individuals are welcomed for who they are, without being expected to change their identities to meet someone else's expectations.
2. Everyone deserves to feel safe and valued at work
A workplace is more than a place where people earn a living. It is also where they spend a significant part of their lives, build relationships and develop their confidence.
Through the experiences of queer employees at The LaLiT, the book highlights the importance of creating environments where people can work without constantly worrying about discrimination or judgement.
It also reflects an important realisation in the organisation's inclusion journey: hiring people from marginalised communities is only the beginning. Organisations must also establish systems, policies and support structures that allow employees to feel protected and respected.
A truly inclusive workplace is one where everyone has the opportunity to grow without compromising their sense of identity.
3. Empathy can change the way we see others
People often form opinions about others without understanding the experiences they have lived through.
Hospitality with a Heart encourages readers to look beyond assumptions and recognise the human stories behind individual identities.
The experiences shared in the book include isolation, societal pressure, bullying and the struggle to find acceptance. These stories remind readers that everyone carries experiences that may not be immediately visible.
Empathy begins when we make an effort to listen instead of judge. By understanding another person's journey, we can build stronger relationships and create communities where differences are respected rather than questioned.
4. Every individual story deserves to be heard
Representation is important because it allows people to see their experiences acknowledged rather than overlooked.
The book brings together the personal journeys of queer team members whose stories reflect different struggles, milestones and experiences. By documenting their voices, Amrita Tripathi creates space for conversations that are often missing from mainstream narratives.
Sharing these experiences also challenges stereotypes and helps readers understand the realities faced by people from marginalised communities.
The lesson is simple: listening to people and giving them the space to tell their stories can help build understanding. Every individual deserves to have their experiences recognised, respected and heard.
5. Belonging is built through everyday actions
Perhaps the most meaningful lesson from Hospitality with a Heart is that belonging cannot be created through statements or policies alone. It is built through everyday actions.
An inclusive environment requires consistent efforts from leadership, colleagues and the wider organisation. It means treating everyone with dignity, challenging discriminatory behaviour, listening to different perspectives and ensuring that people feel comfortable being themselves.
The LaLiT's inclusion journey, as documented in the book, highlights the importance of moving beyond representation towards meaningful acceptance.
Whether in a workplace, a community or personal relationships, making someone feel that they belong is an ongoing responsibility.
Final thoughts
Hospitality with a Heart by Amrita Tripathi is a reminder that behind every conversation about diversity and inclusion are real people with individual stories, struggles and aspirations.
By documenting the lived experiences of queer employees at The LaLiT, the book explores what it means to move from representation to acceptance and from employment to genuine belonging.
The October 31 launch brought these ideas into focus through conversations involving the author, the organisation's leadership, speakers and the people whose experiences form the heart of the book.
Ultimately, the book leaves readers with an important thought: hospitality should not end with welcoming someone through the door. It should extend to making them feel respected, accepted and at home.

articles.title: Samsung ouvre enfin sa Galerie à Google Photos, voici pourquoi c'est une bonne nouvelle
articles.text:
Samsung ouvre enfin sa Galerie à Google Photos, voici pourquoi c'est une bonne nouvelle
Samsung ouvre les vannes à Google Photos. Alors que l'application était déjà préinstallée par défaut sur ses smartphones Galaxy, le fabricant inaugure la synchronisation automatisée des images et vidéos de sa Galerie avec le service de Mountain View.
Bonne nouvelle pour éviter la prolifération d’applications en doublon sur les smartphones, et surtout un nouveau pas en avant réalisé par Samsung envers son partenaire privilégié, Google. Le sud-coréen, qui avait mis un terme à la synchronisation des photos de sa Galerie propriétaire avec Microsoft OneDrive au printemps dernier, annonce aujourd’hui offir à ses clients la possibilité de synchroniser leurs images avec un autre service : Google Photos.
Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra
Concrètement donc, il suffit, lorsqu’un compte Google est paramétré sur un smartphone Samsung Galaxy, d’opter pour une synchronisation avec Photos, via une simple activation dans les paramètres de l’application Galerie. L’intérêt est évident : il permet notamment aux détenteurs d’un stockage en cloud payant auprès de Mountain View de continuer à y stocker leurs photos et vidéos, sans multiplier les points d’accès à leurs images ; pour ceux qui, en revanche, se contentent des 15 Go proposés gratuitement par Google, la saturation guettera rapidement. Néanmoins, sur le smartphone, s’il est possible d’éviter de multiplier les applications aux usages identiques (Galerie et Photos, donc), l’app de Google reste préinstallée. Il s’agit donc davantage de faciliter l’accès aux images depuis un autre terminal, quel qu’en soit la marque.
Gagner de la place en misant sur le stockage déporté
Samsung met enfin en avant une option cruciale en ces temps de pénurie de mémoire, particulièrement pour les détenteurs de smartphones à faible capacité de stockage. Son app Galerie intègre désormais une option de libération d’espace, un fois les images synchronisées avec Google Photos ; seul un aperçu peut ainsi être disponible dans l’application pour les images sélectionnées. Il suffit donc de les “appeler” depuis le cloud lorsqu’il est nécessaire à l’utilisateur de les ouvrir en plein écran. En revanche, les images disponibles sur Google Photos avant la mise en place de la synchronisation avec l’app de Samsung n’apparaîtront pas dans la Galerie ; le fonctionnement n’est pas tout à fait bidirectionnel, en somme.
La synchronisation de la Galerie Samsung avec le stockage Google Photos a vocation à être généralisée sur les produits du géant de la téléphonie, mais n’en est aujourd’hui qu’à ses débuts. Seuls sont pour l’heure éligibles les terminaux mobiles sous One UI 9 avec Android 17, soit les séries Galaxy S26 à S23, Z Flip et Fold 8 à 5, et les Galaxy A, des dernières générations (Galaxy A57 et A37 notamment) aux modèles A55 et A35.

articles.title: La Séptima necesitaba un 1,5% para ser rentable: ayer con Pedro Sánchez consiguió un 14,2%
articles.text:
El plan de negocio de La Séptima situaba su meta en un 3% de cuota dentro de dos años. La cadena ya lo rebasó en su primer fin de semana y ahora, tras una entrevista en plató con Pedro Sánchez, deja atrás a laSexta. Parte de la explicación está en un número: el 101, íntimamente relacionado con la resintonización necesaria para acceder al canal.
El dato. La entrevista de Javier Ruiz a Pedro Sánchez en 'La última hora' reunió el lunes 9 de noviembre a 2.160.000 espectadores y un 14,2% de cuota entre las 21:31 y las 22:39. Ese pico arrastró la media diaria de la cadena hasta el 5,8%, seis décimas por encima de laSexta. Lo más extraordinario es que estamos hablando de solo el quinto día de vida de la cadena.
El fin de semana. Las mejores cifras del fin de semana las firmaron espacios menos ligados a la actualidad dura: el 'Fin de semana' de Luján Argüelles alcanzó el sábado un 5,7% en su franja y superó a 'El precio justo' de Telecinco, que se quedó en el 4,3%. Ese mismo día, 'La comedia nacional' de Héctor de Miguel sumó un 4,5% y 373.000 espectadores, mientras que las dos películas con las que La Séptima afrontó el prime time, 'Infiltrada' y 'Bangkok Dangerous', se quedaron en un 1,5% y un 1,4%, las cuotas más bajas del canal ese día. Lo que da alguna pista muy clara sobre qué buscan los espectadores del canal.
Las previsiones. Las previsiones de la propia cadena eran mucho más modestas. José Miguel Contreras contó en la víspera del estreno que el plan de negocio, con 20 millones de inversión y pérdidas previstas en los dos primeros años, contemplaba un 1,8% de media en los dos primeros meses y no llegaba al 3% hasta 2028. En esa misma conversación dejó abierta la hipótesis de que el estreno tuviera "un aspecto de acontecimiento" y la audiencia bajara después.
Las cifras del plan son más prudentes que las que el propio Contreras había dejado caer unos meses antes, en julio, cuando decía que su idea era acercarse al 5% al cabo de tres años. El consejero delegado de La Séptima le dijo a EFE que un 1,5% en la jornada inaugural sería "un magnífico resultado para arrancar" y admitió que algunos técnicos situaban lo lógico entre el 0,5% y el 0,8%. Ahora posiblemente están recalculando todas esas previsiones: para empezar, el estreno del canal el pasado jueves 5 se saldó con un 2,8%.
El número 101. Para que un canal nuevo tenga audiencia, primero el televisor tiene que encontrarlo. SIETE, la sociedad que explota La Séptima, obtuvo la licencia el 26 de mayo, cuando el Consejo de Ministros resolvió el concurso frente a Mediaset, y que Vox recurrió en julio ante la Audiencia Nacional. Su llegada era además la pieza que desbloqueaba la primera fase del salto de la TDT a DVB-T2.
A mediados de octubre, la CNMC resolvió cancelar el valor 101 del identificador de servicio que Atresmedia usaba en el múltiple MPE5 y asignárselo a SIETE con efectos desde el 5 de noviembre, el mismo día del cambio de la TDT al UHD. Su objetivo declarado era minimizar el impacto en quienes aún no hubieran resintonizado. La misma resolución entregó a DKISS, el valor 102 que usaba Mediaset. Las dos grandes alegaron que el cambio confundiría a los receptores y pidieron seguir emitiendo uno o dos meses en el MPE5 con imágenes informativas; la CNMC rechazó lo segundo y respondió que, sin la reutilización, esos espectadores no verían ninguna señal.
El precedente. Consecuencia práctica de todo ello: algunos televisores sin resintonizar podían mostrar La Séptima en la posición de Atreseries. Hace 21 años hubo un caso parecido: Cuatro arrancó el 7 de noviembre de 2005 ocupando la frecuencia analógica de Canal+ y debutó, gracias a ello, con un 5,1%; laSexta, por comparar, marcó un 0,3% en su primer día medido, el 1 de abril de 2006. Una lectura posible de las dos cifras es que, en la televisión en abierto, heredar un sitio en el mando tiene un peso muy notable en la audiencia inicial.
Un mes hecho para la tertulia. Pero más allá de coincidencias técnicas, hay algo indicutible: la Séptima, una cadena construida casi por completo sobre la tertulia política, se estrena cuando faltan 24 días para unas elecciones generales, a pocos días del inicio de campaña.
El interés del público es indiscutible: a la misma hora que Sánchez, La 1 emitía la entrevista de David Broncano a Santiago Abascal, que logró un 33,6% de share, y Cuatro había entrevistado a Alberto Núñez Feijóo, con un 14% y 645.000 espectadores. En el conjunto de la noche, la entrevista de Ruiz quedó por encima de un monstruo de audiencia como 'El Hormiguero', que marcó un 8,3%. Y aún ni siquiera ha empezado la campaña (cuyo pistoletazo de salida lo dará Jordi Wild en términos informativos).

articles.title: Estafa de habitaciones a precios de ganga en el centro de Venecia, Booking reembolsa a los clientes hasta 263 euros: "Investigación para entender cómo han atacado los hackers"
articles.text:
Más de 3.500 reservas falsas en apenas 13 horas. Eso es lo que ocurrió en el hotel Antigo Trovatore de Venecia después de que aparecieran en Booking habitaciones a precios de auténtica ganga, ya que se encuentra a pocos pasos de la plaza de San Marcos. El problema es que detrás de aquellas ofertas había un presunto ataque informático… y los turistas no se enteraron hasta que llegaron al establecimiento.
Según explica el diario italiano Corriere del Veneto, las reservas se realizaron entre las diez de la noche del 6 de octubre y las once de la mañana del día siguiente. Los clientes habían recibido correos de confirmación y algunos llegaron a pagar 150 euros por dos noches para tres personas, cuando alojarse en aquel hotel durante la temporada alta podía costar varios cientos de euros.
Booking ofrece reembolsos, pero no todos los afectados han recibido la misma solución
Una de las turistas afectadas fue Floriana Bellitto, que había viajado desde Catania con su madre y su abuela para celebrar un cumpleaños. Tras descubrir que su reserva no existía, comenzó a llamar a Booking desde la recepción del hotel. A muchos clientes les ofrecieron inicialmente 30 euros, aunque Bellitto asegura que finalmente le comunicaron la posibilidad de recibir hasta 261,94 euros.
Otros viajeros fueron trasladados a establecimientos fuera de Venecia, incluso a Dolo, mientras que algunos aceptaron las primeras compensaciones. Por ahora, se desconoce qué criterios está utilizando Booking para determinar los reembolsos.
El director del hotel, Alberto De Toffoli, acudió a la Policía Postal italiana para denunciar lo ocurrido. Los investigadores todavía deben aclarar cómo se produjo el incidente y qué sistemas fueron comprometidos. También se investiga la posible sustracción de datos personales y bancarios, algo que todavía no está confirmado.
Booking, por su parte, asegura que está investigando las actividades ilícitas relacionadas con el incidente. La compañía afirma que suspendió el anuncio del establecimiento para evitar nuevas reservas fraudulentas y que está trabajando para realojar a los clientes afectados y prestar asistencia al hotel.

articles.title: Microsoft publie une mise à jour surprise pour Outlook classique
articles.text:
Alors même que Microsoft pousse de plus en plus les utilisateurs à embrasser le nouvel Outlook, la firme de Redmond est sur le point de déployer une mise à jour aussi surprenante qu’inattendue pour la version classique d’Outlook.
Ce rafraîchissement a pour but principal d’harmoniser l’interface d’Outlook classique avec les autres versions d’Outlook pour offrir une expérience d’utilisation plus cohérente sur l’ensemble des appareils.
Des changements esthétiques et fonctionnels
D’après le message publié par Microsoft dans le centre de messages Microsoft 365, cette mise à jour apportera donc principalement des retouches visuelles. Microsoft a prévu d’ajuster l’apparence des icônes, mais aussi l’espacement et l’alignement dans les différentes vues de la messagerie et du calendrier.
Cette mise à jour, qui n’a pas vocation à changer les fonctionnalités du client de messagerie, n’altère donc en rien les habitudes de travail des utilisateurs, et ne remplacera pas l’expérience d’Outlook classique. Microsoft précise que si d’autres changements à venir devaient avoir une incidence sur la navigation ou les habitudes de travail des utilisateurs, elle communiquera plus explicitement à ce sujet.
Pour accompagner l’arrivée des changements visuels à venir dans Outlook classique, Microsoft réintroduit la fenêtre contextuelle « Quoi de neuf » qui s’affichera automatiquement une fois par mois pour informer les utilisateurs des changements effectués par Microsoft.
Cette mise à jour concerne tous les utilisateurs de la version classique d’Outlook pour Windows. Microsoft précise qu’elle commencera à déployer ces modifications à compter de la mi-novembre, avec un déploiement progressif qui doit s’étaler jusqu’à la fin du mois de novembre. L’entreprise précise par ailleurs que les différentes améliorations peuvent arriver de manière individuelle tout au long de la période de déploiement.

articles.title: Accionistas demandaron a Nvidia y a Jensen Huang por ocultar su relación con una presunta espía china
articles.text:
Accionistas de Nvidia presentaron una demanda colectiva contra la empresa y su director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, a quienes acusan de engañar a los inversores al ocultar el vínculo del directivo con Alice Huang, una ejecutiva que, según The New York Times, Estados Unidos considera una agente de inteligencia china.
La denuncia fue presentada en un tribunal federal de San José, California, cinco minutos después del cierre de la bolsa, informó Reuters. El grupo de accionistas está encabezado por Mark Kistenmacher y reclama una indemnización sin monto definido.
Ese mismo día, las acciones de Nvidia cerraron con una baja de 4,3%. Según Reuters, la caída redujo el valor de mercado de la compañía en unos USD 190.000 millones.
Alice Huang, que no es pariente del directivo, fue ejecutiva de Megaspeed, una empresa de centros de datos con sede en Singapur. Jensen Huang dijo a los empleados de Nvidia que fue infiel a su esposa, sin dar detalles de la relación, según Reuters.
Qué sostiene la demanda
El texto acusa a Nvidia y a Huang de dar información engañosa sobre Megaspeed y de no revelar que la relación planteaba un riesgo de seguridad nacional para la reputación y el negocio de la empresa. Así lo describe Reuters a partir de la denuncia.
El sitio Unite.AI, que analizó el caso, precisa que la demanda cubre a quienes compraron acciones entre el 9 de octubre de 2025 y el 8 de noviembre de 2026. Invoca dos normas de las leyes federales de valores: una sobre declaraciones falsas u omisiones y otra que hace responsable a Huang como controlante de la empresa.
Entre las declaraciones cuestionadas figura la explicación que Nvidia dio en octubre de 2025 sobre su revisión de Megaspeed, según la cual la firma no tenía accionistas chinos ni señales de desvío de chips. También se objeta que un vocero describiera el trato con Megaspeed como normal y habitual.
Según Unite.AI, el título de Nvidia cerró el lunes en USD 178,67, con una baja de USD 7,97 por acción.
Una ola de estudios de abogados
El profesor Robert Bartlett, de la Facultad de Derecho de Stanford, dijo a TechCrunch que la declaración previa de la empresa fue “claramente engañosa” y que el conocimiento de un director ejecutivo se atribuye a la compañía.
También afirmó que el planteo es una demanda clásica por fraude al mercado: los inversores alegan que pagaron precios basados en información falsa o incompleta.
La teoría legal, explicó Bartlett, no depende de lo que descubra la investigación interna sobre la vida privada de Huang. Estos casos suelen durar años y terminar en acuerdos que pagan la empresa y sus aseguradoras, sin consecuencias personales para el directivo, agregó. Es un proceso civil, por lo que Huang no enfrenta prisión.
Bartlett dudó de que la Comisión de Bolsa y Valores de Estados Unidos (SEC), el regulador de los mercados, actúe, dado el respaldo del presidente Donald Trump a Huang. TechCrunch señala además que el estudio Schall, Brown & Schwartz, de Los Ángeles, y otros como Levi & Korsinsky anunciaron investigaciones el mismo lunes, y que un anuncio de investigación no prueba por sí solo que el caso sea sólido.
La junta directiva de Nvidia abrió el domingo 8 de noviembre una investigación independiente, a cargo de directores sin vínculos con la gerencia y asesorados por abogados externos. En un comunicado, dijo que no tiene motivos para creer que se haya puesto en riesgo la seguridad nacional ni los secretos de la empresa.
Según el anuncio del estudio que presentó la demanda, difundido por Unite.AI, los inversores que quieran ser demandantes principales deben pedirlo al tribunal antes del 8 de enero de 2027.

articles.title: AMD confirms GPU driver bug is writing data continuously, promises fix with next update
articles.text:
What we know so far: AMD has officially confirmed that a bug in its Radeon GPU drivers triggers a silent background process that continuously writes data to the system drive, even when the PC is idle, accelerating SSD wear and potentially shortening the drive's lifespan. The company added that a permanent fix is currently being validated and will be rolled out as part of the next driver update, scheduled for later this month.
The problem, which affects only Windows PCs, has been reported by multiple users on social media, online message boards, and official AMD forums for years. Some users have complained that the excessive disk activity was reducing their SSD's lifespan by around 1% every month. One user even claimed that their PC lost as much as 16% of its SSD health in just over a year due to the bug.
 – Tomasz Gawroński (@GawroskiT) November 9, 2026
AMD has acknowledged that the issue affects its External Events Utility service, which creates the "atieclxx.exe" process responsible for the continuous write activity. Official documentation reveals that the process handles several display-related functions for AMD GPUs, including monitor detection, FreeSync, and Radeon software hotkeys.
According to user reports, the buggy process writes data to log files stored on the system drive under Windows\System32\AMD\EEUDumps\, at speeds ranging from 0.3 MB/s to 5 MB/s. If this write activity continues indefinitely, it could potentially generate more than 400GB of data per day, or over 12TB per month, taking a considerable toll on consumer-grade SSDs.
Although reports of unusually high write activity have been circulating for at least a year and a half, the issue came to a head following last month's Adrenalin 26.10.1 and 26.10.2 GPU driver updates. The problem gained further attention after Redditor darklinkpower posted a series of possible workarounds users could try to temporarily mitigate the issue.
The most widely recommended workaround is to disable the External Events Utility service, although doing so also affects some display-related functionality. According to the Redditor, AMD FreeSync continues to work after disabling the service, but frame pacing could become significantly more erratic, particularly when using Lossless Scaling's 2x frame generation.
Thankfully, Radeon GPU users won't have to rely on temporary workarounds for much longer. Responding to a complaint on Reddit, AMD representative "Vik" confirmed that the problem stems from an erroneous interaction between the External Events Utility and Microsoft's PCIe filter driver. The company expects to roll out a fix with Adrenalin 26.11.1 before the end of this month.

articles.title: Rapidus Could Miss 2 nm Mass Production Timeline Amid SRAM Issues
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
Rapidus Could Miss 2 nm Mass Production Timeline Amid SRAM Issues
Japanese semiconductor maker Rapidus might miss the planned timeline for its 2 nm node production, as the company is reportedly struggling with its initial attempts at risk production and trial runs. According to a report by the Japan Times, 2 nm volume production at Rapidus facilities will likely be delayed by a few months due to difficulties in 2 nm production, specifically with SRAM. SRAM consists of tiny bitcells that serve as the foundational building blocks for designs operating on one node, and without functional SRAM, it is simply impossible to achieve normal volume production.
There are reportedly other problems, including dust and particle control, which are impacting Rapidus cleanrooms—where the actual silicon is manufactured—to a point where production may be jeopardized altogether. Engineers are working on fixing these problems with the cleanroom and SRAM cells, which should put Rapidus on the right track. Despite these challenges, the company claims that the 2 nm node will arrive on time without any delays, so we are yet to see how these issues will impact their product delivery pipeline.Rapidus successfully taped out a 2 nm GAA test chip at the IIM-1 fab back in mid-2025, with plans to enter high-volume production in Japan's fiscal 2027, which ends in March 2028. In under three years, Rapidus has completed its IIM-1 milestones: after breaking ground in September 2023 and finishing the cleanroom in 2024, the company had connected more than 200 of the world's most advanced semiconductor tools by June 2025. Keep in mind that Rapidus promises some extraordinary services like hot lots with a 15-day turnaround for the wafer, which is unprecedented, especially at a leading-edge node like 2 nm. Hence, the company aims to differentiate itself from other silicon makers, and achieving a working 2 nm node will be a huge milestone if Rapidus can overcome these challenges in time.
