articles.title: Anthropic nennt Preisspanne und Datum für Börsendebüt
articles.text:
Mega-Börsengang: Anthropic nennt Preisspanne und Datum für den Nasdaq-Start
Nach den Spekulationen der vergangenen Monate hat Anthropic am 10. November 2026 letzte Details zu seinem geplanten Börsengang offengelegt. Zuvor hatte der KI-Anbieter schon ein rekordverdächtiges Umsatzplus bekanntgegeben, musste aber zugleich Milliardenverluste und hohe finanzielle Verpflichtungen melden.
Aktien für IPO: Anthropic legt Preisspanne fest
Der aktualisierte Börsenprospekt enthält jetzt die anvisierte Preisspanne. Demnach will Anthropic 825 Millionen Aktien zu einem Preis zwischen 70 und 78 Dollar verkaufen und damit bis zu rund 64 Milliarden Dollar erlösen. Auf vollständig verwässerte Basis ergäbe sich daraus eine Bewertung von gut 1,4 Billionen Dollar, wie Der Aktionär vorrechnet.
Das bedeutet zwar einen deutlichen Aufschlag gegenüber der bis dato letzten Finanzierungsrunde im Mai 2026, bei der Anthropic mit 965 Milliarden Dollar bewertet wurde. Allerdings waren Beobachter:innen noch im Sommer davon ausgegangen, dass Anthropic im Rahmen seines Börsengangs eine Bewertung von zwei Billionen Dollar erreichen könnte. Zuletzt standen allerdings eher 1,5 bis 1,4 Billionen Dollar im Raum.
Zusätzliche Einnahmen durch Privatplatzierung
Dafür dass die IPO-Erlöse bei insgesamt knapp 100 Milliarden Dollar liegen und ein neuer Rekord in Reichweite ist, soll eine sogenannte Privatplatzierung sorgen. Dabei will Anthropic zusätzliche 26 Milliarden Dollar einsammeln. Zu den Investoren sollen Tech-Firmen wie Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, AMD und TSMC gehören. Eine sogenannte Greenshoe-Option, eine Mehrzuteilung der Konsortialbanken, soll weitere 9,6 Milliarden Dollar einbringen, wie Marketwatch schreibt.
Bei der zu erwartenden Bewertung von bestenfalls 1,4 Billionen Dollar läge Anthropic derweil deutlich hinter Elon Musks SpaceX, das bei seinem Börsengang im Juni 2026 1,78 Billionen Dollar wert war. Die Erlöse beliefen sich auf 86 Milliarden Dollar.
Börsengang als Stimmungstest für KI-Branche
So oder so gilt der bevorstehende Anthropic-IPO als wichtiger Test für die Stimmung in der KI-Branche. Unicredit-Chefanalyst Christian Stocker zufolge könnte an der Börse eine gewisse Zurückhaltung herrschen. „Fiele der Börsengang enttäuschend aus, könnte es zu einer systematischeren Neubewertung der KI-Story kommen“, so Stocker.
Die endgültige Klärung dieser Frage ist für den 19. November zu erwarten. Dann soll die Anthropic-Aktie unter dem Kürzel ANT an der Nasdaq starten. Der endgültige Ausgabepreis soll am Tag davor feststehen.

articles.title: Meta lanza una actualización urgente para sus gafas inteligentes: si tienes este modelo, descárgala cuanto antes
articles.text:
Meta ha lanzado una actualización de emergencia para algunas de sus gafas inteligentes. Luego de que decenas de usuarios reportaran problemas de sobrecalentamiento, la compañía desplegó un parche que corrige el aumento excesivo de temperatura. La medida afecta a determinados modelos de las Meta Glasses, una familia de gafas más baratas que las Ray-Ban y Oakley.
De acuerdo con 9to5Google, el gigante tecnológico envió un aviso a los propietarios de las Meta Glasses invitándolos a instalar la actualización de software lo antes posible. La compañía explica en el correo electrónico que el problema aparece cuando se filtra una cantidad excesiva de agua o sudor al dispositivo. Si usas tus gafas cuando llueve o mientras haces ejercicio, es posible que se calienten más de lo esperado.
Vale la pena mencionar que este problema es ajeno a las Meta Ray-Ban y las gafas desarrolladas junto con Oakley. El sobrecalentamiento se presenta en los modelos Adventurer, Fury, Starfire, Nova y Capri, que forman parte de la línea Meta Glasses que se lanzó como una alternativa más asequible. Estos dispositivos cuentan con funciones similares a los de gama alta, como la cámara de 12 MP con resolución 3K, autonomía de más de 8 horas, micrófonos y la posibilidad de graduar las micas.
El fallo de sobrecalientamiento no afecta a las Meta Ray-Ban
La compañía dejó claro que la incidencia no afecta a las Ray-Ban, que son sus gafas inteligentes más vendidas a la fecha. No obstante, existen rumores desde hace unos meses sobre el aumento de temperatura en las Meta Ray-Ban de segunda generación que debutaron hace dos años. Algunos usuarios avisaron desde hace meses que las Wayfarer Gen 2 se calentaban cuando se usaban en días soleados.
“Después de estar fuera de casa solo 1-2 minutos, intenté grabar y recibí un mensaje diciendo que estaban demasiado calientes para grabar”, dijo un usuario en Reddit, quien confirmó que los usó a una temperatura ambiente de 35 ºC. En otra publicación, un segundo usuario mencionó que el mismo modelo de gafas se calentó tanto al usarlo que el marco le quemó la nariz.
Meta no ha confirmado ninguno de estos problemas, por lo que la actualización más reciente solo va dirigida a los propietarios de unas Meta Glasses. Si tienes un modelo Adventurer, Fury, Starfire, Nova y Capri, puedes seguir estos pasos para instalar el parche y corregir el fallo del sobrecalentamiento de tus gafas.
- Abre la aplicación Meta AI en tu smartphone.
- Toca el icono de las gafas situado en la esquina superior derecha.
- Entra en la configuración de tu modelo de Meta Glasses.
- Selecciona las gafas vinculadas que aparecen en la lista.
- Accede al apartado Actualizaciones.
- Pulsa Buscar para revisar si está disponible una nueva versión y pulsa en Instalar.
Si no tienes unas gafas inteligentes y buscas comprar unas durante el Buen Fin (México) o Black Friday, tal vez deberías dar el salto a las Meta Ray Ban Gen 3. Estos modelos se lanzaron a finales de septiembre de 2026 con batería de 9 horas, cámara de 12 MP y micrófonos con reducción de ruido. Hasta ahora no hay reportes de fallos en esta generación, aunque recordemos que muchos de los problemas se reportaron durante el verano.

articles.title: Sundrop turns your endless baby photos into recaps, time lapses, and more — without AI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
New parents take a lot of pictures of their children, but those photos often end up languishing in photo galleries, never to be seen again after the initial snap and share.
A new app, Sundrop, aims to make those pictures more useful by turning them into weekly recaps, highlights, time lapses of the child growing up, and other cute scenes, like putting the child’s photo on a magazine cover or a rookie card.
While Google Photos and Apple Photos already provide extensive tools to organize and manage photos, Sundrop is taking aim at a particular niche: parents with a new baby (usually their first!) who take an overwhelming number of photos and want to do more with those pictures.
The app was developed over the past few months by the same team behind the read-it-later app, Matter: Ben Springwater, Sky Lan, and Rob Mackenzie (all dads themselves).
Notably, Sundrop claims it is designed to be private, and processes all photos locally on the device it is installed on. To make this possible, Sundrop taps into Apple’s Vision framework and on-device Core ML (machine learning) models instead of uploading photos to a cloud server or some other hosted AI service.
Both of the child’s parents can use Sundrop together by linking their accounts, which allows the app to sync their shared photos via Apple’s iCloud service. This feature, the company says, means the pictures aren’t sent to any external servers it runs.
In addition, the team notes that no generative AI is used in the creation of its scenes or highlights.
This differentiates it from many photo-editing apps on the market, including Google’s, which are increasingly tapping generative AI to create new versions of your photos.
To find highlights and recaps, Sundrop scans pictures in the parents’ respective Camera Rolls on their iPhones, skipping things like screenshots or duplicates. It then creates highlights or fun scenes, which it calls “drops.”
One of these is a recap of the week every Sunday, announced as a Lock Screen notification. Others can put two siblings side-by-side at the same age, generate a time-lapse series of photos or a video of a kid growing up, or cut out a photo of the child and place it into a layered template.
Parents can also manually edit the photos Sundrop uses to make its creations, or use the app to automatically organize the best photos into galleries with other similar shots.
The app costs $39.99 per year, and offers a week-long free trial. The annual plan also includes Family Sharing, so only one parent needs to purchase it.

articles.title: Apple TV debuts Sign Language interpretation feature on Friday
articles.text:
On Friday, Nov. 13, Apple TV will officially debut its new Sign Language interpretation feature. The streaming premiere of Being Heumann, a film based on the true story of disability rights activist Judy Heumann, will be one of the first with Sign Language interpretation.
Both American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will be available for the movie F1 as well. Later this year, Way of the Warrior Kid and Greyhound will follow. You can find the sign language interpretation in the Apple TV app settings, and then Sign Language option will show up on supported Apple Original titles.
There will be a Sign Language icon labelling each title to make it easy to know which one has Sign Language. Also you can search “with ASL” to more easily find titles that feature sign language.
As sign language becomes more widely available across streaming services, the new ‘Movies & Shows with American Sign Language ‘ collection.
Apple’s sign language experience was both designed and tested by Deaf and native signers. The performances are each crafted to fit and complement the Apple Original Film.
Ahead of Friday, viewers can add Being Heumann to their watchlist on Apple TV. Also on Friday, Apple’s HomeView and new Apple TV 4K officially release.

articles.title: Commvault unveils Recovery Studio, AgentRecover update and joint work with three partners - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Commvault unveils Recovery Studio, AgentRecover update and joint work with three partners
Data protection provider Commvault Systems Inc. today used its SHIFT 2026 customer event to unveil Recovery Studio, a new service that will automate the rebuilding of entire business applications after an outage or cyberattack.
Four other announcements cover recovery for artificial intelligence agents and joint work with Databricks Inc., Nvidia Corp. and Zscaler Inc.
AgentRecover, the company’s tool for reversing damage done by AI agents, is being extended to agents built on Microsoft Corp.’s Foundry and on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore from Amazon Web Services Inc. Databricks and Nvidia technology will draw on governed enterprise data from Commvault’s Data Activate service. The Zscaler agreement is a strategic partnership centered on AI security.
Recovery Studio goes after the manual work of restoring a business one piece at a time. Data alone does not get an application running again. Without the identities, configurations and infrastructure it depends on, an application can stay offline long after its files are back.
A large enterprise may have hundreds of applications and thousands of identities to bring up in sequence. Getting back to even a minimal level of operation takes 28 days on average under conventional approaches, according to Commvault research from last year.
In place of that manual work, the service uses automated runbooks that rebuild and validate each component in order. Commvault said the runbooks also restore identity systems and cloud configurations, firewall rules included. Threat scans can run inside a runbook on supported resources, and the results feed into the call on whether a service is ready to go back into production. Operational, disaster and cyber recovery all run from the same platform.
Pranay Ahlawat, Commvault’s chief technology and AI officer, called the launch “the DevOps moment for recovery.” He said one orchestrated flow can take over from the spreadsheets and war rooms that recovery teams lean on today.
The AgentRecover update moves the company’s agent protection onto the platforms where businesses build production agents. In September Commvault added protection for agent configurations that tools such as Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code store on employee laptops.
Phil Goodwin, research vice president at International Data Corp., said conventional recovery assumes a discrete set of data at one point in time. Agents break that assumption, because the agent, its data and the resources around it all have to come back “at machine speed,” he said.
On Bedrock AgentCore and Foundry, the software discovers each agent and maps the data, applications and infrastructure it interacts with. If an agent goes rogue, its activity log shows which systems it may have touched across platforms.
Restores target the agent and whatever it changed. Customers can also run AgentRecover with Commvault’s identity recovery and change auditing tools to trace the identities an agent acted through.
The Databricks and Nvidia announcements both build on Data Activate, which turns backup copies protected by Commvault into datasets for analytics and AI. Much of the data companies hold is unstructured and scattered across systems. In research from BARC published by DataHub in June, 70% of data and AI leaders said less than half of their unstructured data could be found and used for AI.
Commvault Data Activate for Databricks shares data under Commvault management into Databricks through OpenSharing. The data arrives as governed tables in Unity Catalog with its ownership, access permissions and lineage intact.
Updates keep flowing as source content changes or is deleted, and customers do not have to rebuild a connection to every original source. Alan Atkinson, chief business development officer at Commvault, said the aim is “turning protected data into an active business asset.”
Nvidia’s part, delivered as a reference design for software-as-a-service and software deployments, centers on retrieval. Nvidia NIM microservices and Nemotron Retriever, together with the Nvidia cuVS library used with Apache Solr, extract and organize Commvault-protected content so applications and agents can pull from it more easily. Data Activate keeps that content current as source files change, retention periods expire or permissions are revoked.
On the security side, Commvault and Zscaler listed AI discovery, runtime governance and agent detection and recovery as early areas of collaboration, and the companies did not announce a joint product or availability date. Zscaler’s Security for AI line polices how employees and agents use AI tools. Dhawal Sharma, Zscaler’s executive vice president of AI security and strategic initiatives, said organizations need to be “prepared to recover quickly if something goes wrong.”
Recovery Studio, AgentRecover’s Amazon Bedrock AgentCore support and the Databricks integration are all due to enter early access in December, the last of them in select Microsoft Azure regions. Foundry support comes sooner, with early access targeted for this month.
The Nvidia reference design is set to reach general availability in 2027 after an early release in December. Recovery Studio will be priced on the amount of data configured for orchestrated recovery, and Commvault plans general availability in the coming months.
A virtual edition of SHIFT follows on Nov. 18.

articles.title: $10 programmer saves BIOS-locked Lenovo ThinkPads from the dump — exploit bypasses supervisor passwords to save 4th- to 8th-gen Intel models from e-waste
articles.text:
$10 programmer saves BIOS-locked Lenovo ThinkPads from the dump — exploit bypasses supervisor passwords to save 4th- to 8th-gen Intel models from e-waste
More affordable ThinkPads for everyone.
Rebooted by Hileeq has shared how others can get cheap Lenovo ThinkPads and save them from becoming e-waste by using a simple BIOS unlock hack that only requires a $10 programmer and another laptop or PC. The technique is niche, known mostly by technicians, but Hileeq is the first to give this bypass mass attention with an easy-to-follow YouTube tutorial.
Rebooted by Hileeq's channel, dedicated to fixing cheap eBay finds, documents the process and what he learned while fixing the laptops. Three weeks ago, he posted a video explaining how to bypass locked Lenovo ThinkPads with Intel 4th- to 8th-generation CPUs using a cheap CH431A programmer to read, write, erase, and save EEPROM and SPI flash memory.
Companies often add supervisor passwords to the fleet of ThinkPads they hand out to their employees as an IT security measure. When these ThinkPads are disposed of, often with the storage removed and destroyed, it’s rare that the supervisor passwords are included and documented. These locked ThinkPads are then incredibly cheap because of the lack of access, ending up as e-waste most of the time. However, Victor Voinea shared a post in a Romanian forum containing his ThinkPad supervisor removal exploits.
Unfortunately, Voinea’s method generated a random password every time the exploit was run, requiring users to contact Voinea for the key specific to the generated hardware ID — and getting the password wasn’t free. However, in 2020, Knucklegrumble posted a free way to bypass the password in the Badcaps electronics repair forum. Mark Juvan, an Ethical Hacker, reverse-engineered Knucklegrumble’s exploit as his cybersecurity master’s thesis at Radboud University Nijmegen, Netherlands, which goes into deeper detail.
The exploit begins by extracting the BIOS from the EEPROM chip on the motherboard using the CH341A programmer and plugging it into a USB port of another PC or laptop. Hileeq then uses NeoProgrammer, a utility for CH341A programmers, and dumps the BIOS, saving a copy of it on the other laptop. NeoProgrammer then applies the same auto-patching workflow Knucklegrumble created.
When the patched BIOS is flashed onto the EEPROM, the laptop can then be turned on, and Hileeq goes through some steps requiring a few keystrokes which remove the password saved in the Embedded Controller (EC), a separate IC that stores security data, among other system tasks. The original BIOS can then be flashed back into the EEPROM, and with the supervisor password removed, the laptop is now usable.
Juvan states in his paper that the exploit takes advantage of a weakness in Lenovo’s firmware verification and driver architecture. Lenovo actually provides the EmulatedEepromDxe driver needed by the exploit, and the driver allows the EEPROM to be read and written to — and the EC’s supervisor password happens to be stored where it’s treated as EEPROM memory, allowing the supervisor password to be overwritten or removed.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The hard, complicated work has already been done by the electronics repair community, and now the process to bypass the supervisor password requires just a few steps and an inexpensive programmer tool. While the method may only be for ThinkPads with Intel 4th- to 8th-generation CPUs, this will still save plenty of usable ThinkPads from going to waste, as Hileeq’s popular post potentially encourages more people to attempt this themselves — who knows, this might cause a domino effect to unlock newer generations of ThinkPads.

Jhet Borja is a serial hobbyist who was taking apart toys from childhood and sketching inventions. He now loves doing DIY projects ranging from designing custom 3D-printed parts, building PCs and keyboards, all the way to woodworking. If he's not getting his hands dirty, he's probably brainstorming his next project.

articles.title: Skip the new model — this older Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is a smart budget buy in Amazon's early Black Friday sale
articles.text:
Here's your first Black Friday Kindle deal: get the Paperwhite Signature Edition for a record-low price
A best-ever discount with the new model coming soon
Whether it's for yourself or as a gift for a loved one, a Kindle is a popular Black Friday purchase. And if you want to get a head start on your end-of-year shopping, then Amazon has just dropped an early offer on one of its premium ereaders. Right now, the Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition is down to £139.99 (was £229.99).
• See all early Black Friday deals at Amazon
This is a record-low price for the 2024 version of the ereader, which features a few useful upgrades over the standard Kindle Paperwhite, including double the storage at 32GB, wireless charging support, and an auto-adjusting front light that adapts the display to suit your environment so you have ideal reading conditions.
Those improvements are in addition to the standard features found on the Paperwhite, such as a seven-inch glare-free display, a lengthy 12-week battery life, and a thin and light waterproof design.
Amazon is clearly cutting the price of this model as a brand-new Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition launches this month, with a new aluminium design, replaceable battery, and a higher contrast screen. Outside of that, though, all of the other key features are exactly the same. So, going for this older model is a smart budget buy as it's around £100 cheaper.
Today's best Kindle deal
With a new model on the way, the last-generation Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition falls to a record-low price on Amazon. Upgrades in the 2026 version are fairly minimal, mostly improving the design and offering a replaceable battery, so I'd be tempted to go for the older version while it's at a great budget price. You still get a bright and easy-to-read seven-inch glare-free display, an auto-adjusting front light, space for thousands of books, handy wireless charging support, and a thin, waterproof design. And it's all for around £100 less than the new model.
We awarded this ereader a respectable four stars in our Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition review.
We appreciated the improvements to the display and the extra storage space that enthusiastic readers will definitely find useful, while the faster interface and snappier navigation mean it's much easier to use overall as well.
If you really want the most premium reading experience, then you'll probably want to hold off for a deal on the Kindle Colorsoft instead, but it's difficult to fault what you get in the Paperwhite Signature Edition while it's at this excellent sale price.

articles.title: « C'est exactement ce que j'imaginais », une IA transforme les dessins d'un enfant en jeu vidéo
articles.text:
Un enfant, quelques dessins et une promesse difficile à tenir… Après des mois à tenter de créer le jeu imaginé par son neveu, un développeur a finalement fait appel à plusieurs outils d'IA pour un résultat étonnant : une aventure de douze niveaux à laquelle toute la famille peut désormais jouer.
Aiden avait déjà tout imaginé : les personnages, leurs pouvoirs, les ennemis et même le scénario. Il ne lui manquait que le jeu. Son oncle, Lex Toumbourou, ingénieur logiciel australien, avait accepté de le créer pour son anniversaire. Mais la première version n'avait rien de très convaincant. Et le garçon ne comptait pas abandonner son idée : à chaque visite, il demandait où en était son jeu vidéo. Jusqu'au jour où son oncle a décidé de tenter une nouvelle expérience, qu'il raconte sur son blog.
Un premier jeu trop court pour Aiden
Tout était parti d'une passion commune pour les jeux d'arcade, notamment Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Shredder's Revenge. Aiden voulait son propre jeu du même genre, avec cinq héros inspirés de sa famille et de leur chien, douze ennemis et une mission : sauver leur chiot Pudding.
Lex Toumbourou avait commencé à travailler sur le projet en janvier 2026. Pour l'anniversaire de son neveu, en juin, il avait réussi à produire une première version avec Claude Code. Le jeu fonctionnait, mais son contenu était limité à quelques minutes. Aiden avait remercié son oncle avant de lui expliquer tout ce qui manquait encore.
Quelques mois plus tard, Lex obtient un accès anticipé à Claude Fable 5.2, le nouveau modèle haut de gamme d'Anthropic, officiellement lancé le 9 novembre. Il décide de lui confier le projet avec une consigne : transformer ce prototype en un véritable jeu d'action, aussi amusant que possible, jouable à quatre et fidèle aux dessins de son neveu.
Il lance l'agent avant d'aller dormir. À son réveil, le jeu a été largement reconstruit. Nouveaux décors, animations, objets destructibles, scènes narratives : Claude a même développé un programme de test automatisé pour parcourir les douze niveaux et repérer certains problèmes.
Le lendemain, Lex branche quatre manettes à son ordinateur. Aiden et les autres enfants découvrent enfin Aiden's Revenge, un jeu dans lequel ils peuvent incarner les personnages qu'ils avaient imaginés. Selon son oncle, Aiden s'exclame que c'est exactement ce qu'il avait en tête.
Un jeu familial, mais aussi une démonstration des progrès de l'IA
L'expérience ne s'arrête pas à cette première partie. Les enfants demandent de nouveaux pouvoirs, puis les autres membres de la famille rejoignent progressivement l'aventure. Parents, grands-parents, oncles, tantes et même deux tortues deviennent des personnages jouables. Le jeu finit par en compter dix-huit.
Derrière ce résultat, l'IA n'a toutefois pas tout fait seule. Claude s'est chargé d'une grande partie du développement, tandis que ChatGPT Images a servi à créer les graphismes et ElevenLabs les éléments sonores. L'ensemble a nécessité environ 600 requêtes à Claude sur deux jours, quelque 500 générations d'images, onze morceaux de musique et une centaine d'effets sonores.
L'auteur évoque également 340 millions de tokens traités par Claude, dont l'immense majorité correspond à des lectures depuis le cache, facturées à un tarif réduit. Il ne communique pas le coût total de l'expérience, mais celle-ci a bien mobilisé plusieurs services payants et une quantité considérable de calcul.
Lex présente son expérience comme une réalisation en one-shot, mais la formule mérite d'être nuancée. L'IA est partie d'un prototype existant, et plusieurs retouches ont suivi les premières parties. Le résultat n'en reste pas moins impressionnant : quelques jours ont suffi pour accomplir un travail qui aurait probablement demandé des mois sur son temps libre, en mobilisant au passage des compétences en graphisme et en création sonore.
Et le résultat n'est pas qu'une démonstration vidéo. Aiden's Revenge est accessible gratuitement dans un navigateur, pour que chacun puisse découvrir ce qu'est devenu ce jeu imaginé sur quelques feuilles de papier.

articles.title: Disney entrenará con Adobe modelos de IA propios basados en sus personajes y parques
articles.text:
The Walt Disney Company y Adobe anunciaron una alianza de varios años para desarrollar modelos de inteligencia artificial generativa a medida de Disney. Los modelos se entrenarán con personajes, escenarios y estilos visuales de la compañía y se usarán en parques, estudios y ESPN, según informó Adobe.
El anuncio se hizo el 9 de noviembre en Adobe MAX, la conferencia anual de creatividad de la empresa de software. Adobe pasa a ser “socio oficial de innovación en IA” de Disney y le dará acceso anticipado a sus tecnologías, además de ingenieros e investigadores dedicados.
Entre las herramientas figuran Firefly, el generador de imágenes y video de Adobe, y Firefly Foundry, el servicio con el que la empresa crea modelos privados para un cliente. También se incluyen los programas de edición de video Premiere y de imagen Photoshop.
Según el comunicado, los modelos de Disney serán “centrados en las personas y dirigidos por artistas”. Estarán entrenados con información propia de la compañía, como atributos de personajes, entornos y estilos visuales, para producir resultados “comercialmente seguros” y listos para producción.
Imagineering ya usa la tecnología
Walt Disney Imagineering Research & Development, la división que diseña los parques y los cruceros de Disney, ya trabaja con Firefly Foundry. Adobe describe dos herramientas: un modelo que convierte bocetos dibujados a mano en arte conceptual en 2D terminado y otro que genera material gráfico fiel a las franquicias de Disney.
En una nota publicada por Disney en junio, Laughlin, de Imagineering, explicó por qué la división eligió este camino. “Buscábamos una manera de acelerar nuestro proceso”, dijo. Agregó que la herramienta permite comprimir “meses de trabajo en días y semanas”.
La misma nota indica que el modelo base se construyó con material licenciado y propio, y que luego se ajustó con más de 70 años de trabajo de Imagineering, desde arte conceptual hasta diseños técnicos.
Laughlin sostuvo que Disney buscaba un socio que respetara que es “una compañía impulsada por sus creadores”, y que el proceso creativo conserva un componente humano.
Estudios y ESPN, los próximos frentes
La alianza se extiende a StudioLAB, el centro de innovación de Walt Disney Studios, donde Adobe participará como socio. Según el blog de Adobe, los primeros proyectos se centrarán en modelos personalizados para posproducción y efectos visuales.
En ESPN Edge, el centro de innovación de la cadena deportiva, ambas empresas buscarán usos de la IA para atraer a los aficionados. Adobe menciona los resúmenes deportivos y los documentales, además de nuevas formas de aprovechar el archivo de ESPN.
El acuerdo incluye también un componente comercial: Adobe aumentará su presencia en las plataformas de Disney, con acciones de marketing en Walt Disney World, Disneyland, Disney Cruise Line, ESPN Edge y StudioLAB. Ninguna de las empresas publicó el valor del acuerdo ni su duración exacta.
Los proyectos de colaboración con StudioLAB y ESPN Edge ya están en marcha, según Adobe, que prevé más actividades durante los años de vigencia de la alianza.
Para qué sirve Adobe
Adobe Creative Cloud es un conjunto integral de aplicaciones y servicios diseñado para la creación visual, el diseño gráfico, la producción audiovisual y el desarrollo de experiencias digitales.
Sus herramientas cubren prácticamente todas las disciplinas del contenido multimedia: Photoshop e Illustrator lideran la edición fotográfica y la ilustración vectorial; Premiere Pro y After Effects son estándares de la industria para el montaje de video, la animación y los efectos visuales; mientras que aplicaciones como InDesign resuelven la maquetación editorial tanto impresa como digital.
Más allá de los programas individuales, la suite funciona como un ecosistema conectado que optimiza el flujo de trabajo entre profesionales y equipos creativos.
Gracias al almacenamiento en la nube, el acceso a tipografías profesionales con Adobe Fonts y la sincronización de recursos entre aplicaciones, permite compartir proyectos, gestionar versiones y colaborar en tiempo real.
Hoy en día integra además herramientas de inteligencia artificial generativa con Adobe Firefly, facilitando la automatización de tareas repetitivas y acelerando los procesos de diseño desde la fase de concepto hasta la entrega final.

National Startup Awards 6.0 opens applications; winners to receive Rs 25 lakh prize in 20 categories
The award exercise seeks to identify and recognise entrepreneurial ventures that make significant contributions across 20 sectoral categories, from agriculture to space technology.
The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has opened applications for the sixth edition of the National Startup Awards, offering a prize of Rs 25 lakh in each category to recognise innovative, scalable and impactful startups across the country.
These awards recognise startups demonstrating outstanding performance in innovation, scalability, sustainability and socio-economic impact, according to DPIIT.
The award exercise is organised under the Startup India initiative of the commerce and industry ministry. It seeks to identify and recognise entrepreneurial ventures making significant contributions across 20 sectoral categories, spanning areas from agriculture to space technology.
The awards also include special categories for women-led startups, North-East Startup Excellence, student innovators, and aspiring entrepreneurs.
This exercise will provide national-level visibility and recognition to selected startups, while also facilitating access to industry stakeholders and potential investors.
Further, the DPIIT-recognised startups are eligible to apply for these awards under the 20 sectoral categories and the specified special categories. Over 2.6 lakh units are recognised as startups by the department.
Students aged 10 and above can also submit applications for the award, provided their proposed solutions align with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 and 'Shakti Ki Sapta Dhara'.
On August 15, Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid out a seven-point reform framework, 'Sapta Dhara', aimed at accelerating India's journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047, with a focus on manufacturing, agro-food production and food processing, technology and innovation, logistics, defence, green and blue economy, and soft power.
Interested applicants can submit their applications through the Startup India portal at https://www.startupindia.gov.in/content/sih/en/nsa2026.html.

articles.title: L'iPhone Air 2 changerait de design : voici à quoi il pourrait ressembler
articles.text:
Une fois n’est pas coutume, les caractéristiques en fuite d’un smartphone permettent de réaliser des maquettes de ce dernier avant sa sortie, donnant un aperçu de la forme finale du produit. L’iPhone Air 2 et l’iPhone 18 ont profité de ce traitement. L’occasion de comparer les deux modèles et de voir les changements qu’Apple pourrait opérer.
Un double module photo et un design encore plus fin pour l’iPhone Air 2
Notre test de l’iPhone Air premier du nom a été l’occasion de mettre en avant ses forces et ses faiblesses. Parmi nos déceptions, nous avions notamment mentionné son unique caméra de 48 mégapixels, difficile à justifier compte tenu de son positionnement tarifaire. L’iPhone Air 2 pourrait ainsi corriger le tir en intégrant un second module ultra grand-angle de 48 mégapixels. De quoi offrir une meilleure polyvalence photo qu’aucun utilisateur ne refuserait.
 iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 https://t.co/BEGf7VHq0u
— Lusi Roy (@LusiRoy7) November 9, 2026
Côté dimensions, l’iPhone Air 2 ne volerait pas son nom, car Apple réussirait à le rendre encore plus fin que son prédécesseur, atteignant seulement 5,2 millimètres d’épaisseur, contre 5,6 millimètres pour le premier iPhone Air. Cela ne se ferait pas au détriment de la batterie, les dernières indiscrétions faisant état d’un accumulateur de 3500 mAh, soit légèrement plus grand que la génération actuelle. Ajoutez à cela une puce plus efficiente (l’A20 Pro ?) et cela devrait se traduire par une autonomie qui, espérons-le, serait revue à la hausse.
Des concessions et une commercialisation au printemps
Tout ne serait pas rose pour ce second modèle puisque les rumeurs évoquent toujours un unique haut-parleur. L’intégration d’un téléobjectif ne semble pas non plus être à l’ordre du jour. L’iPhone Air 2 miserait ainsi toujours sur le capteur de 48 Mpx pour découper l’image afin de préserver au mieux la qualité lorsque l’on zoome.
À lire : iPhone Air 2 : face aux critiques, Apple préparerait ces 3 changements
La date de sortie de l’iPhone Air 2 est toujours attendue au printemps 2027, avec une probable hausse de prix par rapport au modèle précédent. Apple ferait donc évoluer sa formule sans pour autant la révolutionner. L’iPhone Air 2 s’adresserait toujours au même public, à savoir les utilisateurs qui cherchent avant tout un smartphone plus fin et léger que les autres et qui sont prêts à faire des concessions pour profiter de ces deux caractéristiques.

articles.title: Soundcore Life Q30 : le casque à réduction de bruit très populaire passe sous les 50 €
articles.text:
Le casque à réduction de bruit Soundcore Life Q30 est à 47,99 € (-40 %)
Réduction de bruit active, très grande autonomie et format pliable : le casque Bluetooth Soundcore Life Q30 d'Anker passe à 47,99 € chez Amazon, soit 32 € sous son prix conseillé.
Vendu par AnkerDirect FR et expédié par Amazon, ce casque noir affiche 47,99 € contre 79,99 € pour le prix conseillé, soit une remise de 40 % dans le cadre des offres pré-Black Friday d'Amazon. C'est aussi 9 € de moins que son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours (56,99 €).
Une réduction de bruit efficace pour le prix
Lors de notre test, noté 3/5, sa réduction de bruit active s'est montrée très correcte, et nous avons apprécié son rendu sonore homogène et agréable, avec une belle largeur stéréo. Le casque propose trois modes de réduction de bruit, dont un mode transport pensé pour le bruit des moteurs.
Son autonomie est extrêmement généreuse : nous avons mesuré 40 heures avec la réduction de bruit activée.
Confortable, mais une finition perfectible
Nous avons aussi relevé un bon confort et une conception entièrement pliable, pratique en voyage. En revanche, la précision sonore reste très moyenne, le rendu se dégrade nettement lorsque la réduction de bruit est désactivée, et la finition est assez moyenne.
C'est l'un des casques les plus populaires d'Amazon : il dépasse les 97 000 évaluations, pour une note de 4,5/5, et Amazon indique plus de 300 achats le mois dernier.

articles.title: Pulsar “Sí, y no vuelvas a preguntar” en Claude Code parecía inofensivo. Ha acabado filtrando miles de contraseñas en GitHub
articles.text:
Si en algo son característicos los modelos de IA generativa es en su persistencia preguntando. Porque no pueden terminar una intervención sin decirte: "¿Quieres que haga algo más?". Lo llevan en su ADN, los LLM son sistemas predictivos que necesitan seguir adelante. Las herramientas actuales permiten restringir ese comportamiento, aunque el resultado podría no ser el que se espera.
El problema. Claude Code puede funcionar en modo automático, aunque siempre va a preguntarle al usuario cómo continuar si necesita tomar una decisión que sea trascendente. Para ser menos pesado, la aplicación incluye un selector de "Sí, y no vuelvas a preguntar", la típica opción que marcas cuando eliminas una carpeta y resulta que tiene demasiadas cosas dentro. "Sí a todo" y que pase lo que tenga que pasar.
En el caso de Claude Code, marcar la casilla de no volver a preguntar implicaba que el comando aprobado se guardaba tal cual, con las contraseñas que llevase escritas, en un archivo que podía acabar en el código elaborado por la IA. Como descubrieron en Apiiro, así se filtraban contraseñas de bases de datos, el login de los servidores SSH del usuario, claves privadas y hasta tokens de GitHub y claves de AWS.
Acceso público a datos sensibles. Imagina el alcance de la filtración: cualquiera que encontrase esos datos, como una clave API privada, podría acarrearle al desarrollador un importante agujero en la cuenta bancaria. Y la información estaba al alcance de cualquiera: en los propios repositorios públicos de GitHub.
Para recordar un permiso, Claude Code anota el comando literal en un archivo del proyecto, '.claude/settings.local.json'. Si el comando incluía una contraseña, esta se guardaba en texto plano. Dicho archivo no está pensado para compartirse, pero esto manda en el equipo del desarrollador, no en el repositorio. Si el archivo ya estaba subido previamente, o en el proyecto hay otro ordenador colaborando, el contenido viaja a GitHub junto con el resto del código.
El peligro del vibecoding. El comportamiento de Claude Code tiene sentido: para no molestar al usuario, y dado que ya tiene su permiso, guarda el comando exacto para reconocerlo la próxima vez. Si el desarrollador no supervisa lo que está subiendo, y manda directamente los archivos a GitHub, termina compartiendo un acceso a su propia información.
No es algo casual: el vibecoding ha elevado con creces el uso de GitHub. Según el informe Octoverse 2026 de GitHub, en los doce meses previos al 30 de septiembre se registraron 17.900 millones de pushes y 34.300 millones de commits. Esa cifra de pushes supera a la de 2024 y 2025 juntos. Y hay otro dato que demuestra el peso del vibecoding en GitHub: en septiembre de este año, más del 40% de las pull requests tenían como origen un agente IA. En marzo era el 17%.
¿Qué dice Anthropic? La empresa no publicó un comunicado, pero Boris Cherny, responsable de Claude Code, respondió en Hacker News. Admitió que la herramienta nunca ha limpiado los secretos de lo que guarda y defendió que el archivo está pensado para quedarse en local: como Claude Code lo excluye de Git al crearlo, sostiene que los archivos filtrados se crearon a mano y se subieron después.
Mientras Antropic encuentra una solución definitiva, Cherny recomienda usar el modo automático en Claude Code y activar el escaneo de secretos en el repositorio. También adelantó que el equipo está probando dos mejoras: que el modo automático detecte el filtrado de datos y un escáner básico de secretos integrado. No hay fecha para ninguno de estos dos cambios.

articles.title: José, español viviendo en Islandia: "Aquí está el famoso 3-2-2, que trabajas tres días, descansas dos y trabajas dos", con turnos de 11 o 12 horas
articles.text:
Si estás pensando en trabajar en el extranjero, quizá Islandia sea uno de los destinos que te pasan por la cabeza. Si este es el caso, el joven español Jose Esepe ha publicado su experiencia en TikTok trabajando en que es uno de los países europeos donde más se cobra, pero también uno de los más caros para vivir. Pero como explica Jose, todo depende de tu trabajo y de dónde vivas.
Un calendario que se da la vuelta. Lo primero que menciona en su vídeo es el llamado método local para organizar los días de trabajo: “Aquí está el famoso 3-2-2, que trabajas tres días, descansas dos y trabajas dos”, explica. Y a la semana siguiente el calendario se invierte, de manera que descansas tres días, trabajas dos y vuelves a librar otros dos.
Doce horas para sumar 172. La parte negativa de este método es que los turnos suelen durar entre 11 y 12 horas, de forma que vayas acumulando más rápido las horas del mes, que según los cálculos de Jose son unas 172. A cambio, al concentrar tanto trabajo en pocos días, cabe la posibilidad de que tengas libres una o dos semanas al mes, aunque esto depende de cómo se organice el calendario en tu empresa.
Porque este no es un horario que se aplique en todas las empresas, y él mismo ha podido comprobarlo: “Yo vine con esa condición, entre comillas, porque no tengo 3-2-2”. Por eso recomienda revisar bien las condiciones antes de aceptar una oferta, ya que el reparto de los turnos puede cambiar de un puesto de trabajo o una empresa a otra.
Sueldo, extras y pluses. En cuanto al dinero, José habla de unos 2.800 euros al mes, aunque insiste en que la cifra depende del empleo, del lugar y de las horas que hagas. Este sueldo es lo que él cobra, pero no tiene que ver con ningún tipo de salario mínimo, ya que en Islandia se negocian sector a sector en los convenios colectivos.
Las horas extraordinarias, según cuenta, se pagan al 190% de la tarifa habitual, algo que lleva a las empresas a vigilarlas para no disparar sus costes. Por eso mismo, José aconseja a quien tenga como objetivo ahorrar el negociar con el empleador la posibilidad de hacer más horas.
A eso se suman, según José, complementos por trabajar de noche, en fin de semana o en festivos. El convenio de los cocineros del sindicato Efling, por ejemplo, recoge pluses por turno y paga los grandes festivos al 1,375% del sueldo mensual por hora. José reconoce que no recuerda a partir de qué hora empieza a aplicarse el plus nocturno, pero destaca que estos conceptos pueden engordar la nómina. Aun así, esto también va a depender de cada puesto de trabajo y cada convenio.
Vivir en un pueblo pequeño. Más allá del sueldo, José también habla de la capacidad de ahorro, que depende sobre todo de dónde vivas y de lo que gastes. Él reside en una localidad islandesa de unos 1.000 habitantes, donde comparte habitación con otra persona y entre los dos pagan 800 euros al mes, 400 euros cada uno. Pero también dice que en ciudades como Reikiavik la puede llegar a cambiar mucho, puesto que los alquileres son bastante más caros.
También cuenta que algunas empresas descuentan el alojamiento directamente de la nómina, de manera que no tienes que pagarlo por separado. En su caso, el sitio donde vive le ayuda a recortar mucho los gastos del día a día: “Como vivo en un pueblo donde no hay nada que gastar, lo estoy ahorrando todo”.

articles.title: Your meditation headband may be feeding your brainwaves to an AI model
articles.text:
In brief: Companies that direct users' texts, emails, art, online behavior, and other work or private data to advertisers and AI training models have long been under scrutiny. However, a recent report highlights how similar practices in the brain-computer industry have largely flown under the radar. Some experts say consumer brain scanners can't collect much data, but others worry about what might happen if advertisers and AI companies can access users' brain activity.
A recent report from the journal Science outlines the relationship between the electroencephalography (EEG) industry and AI. It found that some companies selling brain-tracking devices aren't entirely forthcoming about where users' brain-signal data ends up.
InteraXon's Muse brain-sensing headband is a leading example. The $475 device tracks and charts users' brainwaves to help improve sleep and focus. But the company didn't inform users that it was using data from some headbands, supposedly anonymized, to train its AI model of the brain until after Science notified them.
Science also examined the privacy policies of dozens of other consumer-facing EEG companies and found that around one-third didn't clearly explain how they handle user brainwave data. Of those companies, 11 had policies that mentioned only how users interact with their websites, and four had no privacy policies at all.
A relatively little-known industry has been exploring EEG devices since long before the AI boom. InteraXon first unveiled what would become Muse in 2010 and spent the next decade promoting it as a project for brain-controlled devices and mental health. However, the AI industry's booming popularity and the investment flowing into it may change how companies use data from brain-tracking wearables.
InteraXon and other companies claim that training AI models on tens of thousands of hours of user data makes their products more helpful. For example, a brain model from AI neurotech startup Piramidal successfully identified nine out of 10 seizures in a pilot study last year.
Some experts note that the data collected by consumer EEG devices is limited in range and usefulness compared to data collected by medical-grade scanners. For instance, Muse headbands use only a handful of electrodes for user comfort, compared to the EEG caps used in labs, which are covered in up to two dozen electrodes. Furthermore, a 2018 study suggests that the research underpinning most EEG products does not meet a high standard.
Meanwhile, other experts are concerned about how much AI models could learn when trained on thousands of people's brainwaves. Although companies can already learn people's thought patterns from what they click, brain data might be the final frontier of privacy.

articles.title: AMD's RDNA 5 Inches Closer as GFX13 Support Lands in Linux Driver Patches
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
AMD's RDNA 5 Inches Closer as GFX13 Support Lands in Linux Driver Patches
AMD has begun integrating its next-generation graphics IP into the Linux kernel, releasing a series of eight patches that add GFX13 support to the open-source AMDGPU driver. These patches, submitted to the mailing list on November 9 by AMDGPU maintainer Alex Deucher, contain over 12,600 lines of code, excluding the typically large header files. GFX13 is anticipated to be the graphics core for RDNA 5, although AMD has not officially confirmed this connection. However, since GFX12 has been linked to RDNA 4, it is assumed that GFX13 is the correct codename for RDNA 5.
The patches introduce version 13 of three IP blocks: the "graphics" GFX block itself, the MicroEngine Scheduler (MES), and the IMU. On the compute side, the AMDKFD driver gains initial GC 13 support, a CWSR trap handler for saving and restoring compute wave state, and a temporary change that disables queue reset in the topology. The final patch enables the MGCG, CGCG, and CGLS clock gating features, which reduce power consumption when parts of the GPU are idle. Interestingly, the series mentions two specific targets, GFX 13.0.1 and GFX 13.0.4, indicating that AMD is preparing at least two graphics IP configurations. These version numbers do not correspond to any specific GPU models, so it is unclear which products they relate to. RDNA 5 is expected to be a significant advancement over RDNA 4, necessitating numerous patches to add support.GFX13 first appeared in LLVM compiler back-end patches in January 2026, and by August, AMD's Linux code had integrated the upcoming Display Core Next 6 (DCN6) display engine. AMD's DCN display engine manages various functions, including display output, image scaling, monitor ratio output, and pixel manipulation. This engine is a highly complex component essential for graphics output in AMD RDNA graphics cards. For the DCN6 version, AMD has introduced new scaling integrity and costing surfaces, a UPSP pre-scaler to sample 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 content before scaling, and new pixel formats within the display logic.

articles.title: Free video-streaming service Tubi lets users share curated watchlists now
articles.text:
Tubi users can now create and share playlists of movies and shows available on the streaming service.
Tubi is a free ad-supported streaming television (FAST) service that has both live channels and on-demand content.
Today, the Fox-owned company announced “Mixtapes” as a way for users to make watchlists from Tubi’s “nearly 400,000 movies and TV episodes,” Tubi’s announcement said, adding:
They can give each mixtape a title and description and arrange the entertainment inside in whatever order feels right to them. Viewers can build one entirely on their own, or describe what they’re looking for and let Tubi offer a starting place that they can edit, rearrange, or rebuild entirely. When their mixtape is finished, they can publish and share it with other people or keep it for themselves.
Tubi’s Mixtapes website already features numerous playlists, including: “Millennial Memory Lane”—with movies like Cruel Intentions (1999) and The Fifth Element (1997) and shows such as Everybody Hates Chris (2005–2009) and Degrassi: The Next Generation (2001–2015); and “Bald Baddies”—which includes Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw (2019) and Central Intelligence (2016).
Watching a Mixtape doesn’t require a Tubi account, but making one does.
Tubi’s Mixtapes comes at a time when streaming service providers are seeking a way to address the content fragmentation that’s frequently cited as a frustration among streaming users, as well as users struggling to find something to watch. Gracenote’s “2025 State of Play” report, for instance, surveyed 3,000 consumers in the US, Brazil, France, Germany, Mexico, and the UK and found that “nearly 33 percent of streaming users feel content and service fragmentation negatively impacts their TV experience.”

articles.title: 'GTA 6' estará en Xbox Cloud Gaming desde el primer día: gran noticia si tienes una Xbox One, pero no si usas un PC
articles.text:
GTA 6 estará disponible en Xbox Cloud Gaming desde el primer día, ha confirmado Rockstar Games. El estudio ha revelado que su nuevo (y muy esperado) título se incorporará al catálogo de Microsoft para jugar desde la nube el próximo 19 de noviembre, en simultáneo con su debut en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S. Aunque todavía no te emociones con accederlo desde un PC, un televisor, un móvil o cualquier otro dispositivo compatible con el servicio.
De acuerdo con el anuncio de Rockstar, GTA 6 estará disponible en Xbox Cloud Gaming a través de consolas Xbox Series X, Series S y Xbox One. Esto deja en claro que el acceso a este título desde la nube se limitará a los dispositivos en cuestión, lo cual tiene sus pros y sus contras.
La contra más notoria es que si usas Xbox Cloud Gaming desde un PC o cualquier otro dispositivo conectado que no sea una consola, no te quedará más opción que seguir esperando. Los que sí van a estar de parabienes serán los jugadores que todavía le saquen provecho a su vieja Xbox One, pues tendrán la posibilidad de jugar GTA 6 desde el día 1 sin tener que actualizarse a una Series X|S.
El otro punto a favor de esta historia es que los usuarios de Cloud Gaming en consolas Xbox no tendrán que comprar el juego por separado. Esto seguramente busque seducir a quienes quieren probar GTA 6, pero no son fanáticos o jugadores asiduos de la saga Grand Theft Auto. Tal vez la experiencia no sea 100 % idéntica a la de jugarlo de forma nativa, pero puede ser suficiente para quienes quieren saber por qué hay tanto alboroto en torno a este lanzamiento, sin tener que pagar 79,99 o 99,99 euros adicionales.
GTA 6 estará disponible en Xbox Cloud Gaming el 19 de noviembre
Un detalle crucial que menciona Rockstar respecto de la disponibilidad de GTA 6 en Xbox Cloud Gaming es que quienes accedan al juego a través de la nube estarán limitados a los ajustes gráficos de Xbox Series S. Esto vale tanto para la citada consola, como para la Series X y la vieja Xbox One.
"Al igual que ocurre con cualquier sistema de streaming en la nube, la velocidad de conexión y otros factores técnicos pueden influir en el rendimiento del juego de formas que no afectarían a una partida ejecutada localmente", indica también el estudio. Así, los responsables de GTA 6 están dejando en claro que la experiencia de jugar en la nube no será ni por asomo la misma que si se ejecuta de forma nativa.
Será interesante ver si esto ayuda a dar nuevo impulso a las suscripciones de Xbox Game Pass, que padecieron un éxodo de usuarios tras el último encarecimiento de la mano de Phil Spencer. Posteriormente, Microsoft recortó el precio del servicio pero le quitó los lanzamientos de nuevos Call of Duty desde el primer día. Vale recordar que Xbox Cloud Gaming ya no se limita a los suscriptores de Game Pass Ultimate, aunque en el caso de GTA 6 no hay precisiones sobre si su acceso desde la nube estará disponible en todos los planes o solo en el más caro.
Alimentando el hype antes del lanzamiento
La precarga de GTA 6 se ha iniciado hoy, 10 de noviembre, tanto en Xbox como en PlayStation. Rockstar ha publicado un breve tráiler alegórico, con un puñado de imágenes nuevas. Puedes verlo a continuación:
Asimismo, PlayStation ha compartido un vídeo en el que muestra con más detalles las características de GTA 6 con el mando DualSense. Entre ellas, el aprovechamiento de los gatillos adaptativos, el feedback háptico y el audio 3D.
GTA 6 estará disponible en PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X|S y Xbox Cloud Gaming el próximo 19 de noviembre.

articles.title: GTA 7 chegará mais rápido que GTA 6, diz CEO • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
GTA 7 chegará mais rápido que GTA 6, diz CEO
Strauss Zelnick, chefe da Take-Two, afirma que futuros jogos da franquia Grand Theft Auto terão ciclos de desenvolvimento mais curtos.
GTA 6 mal chegou, mas as expectativas para o desenvolvimento de Grand Theft Auto 7 já começam a surgir. Segundo Strauss Zelnick, CEO da Take-Two Interactive, o próximo jogo da franquia deve ter um ciclo de desenvolvimento mais curto. A empresa é controladora da Rockstar Games, responsável pela franquia.
Em entrevista à IGN, o executivo disse que a produção de futuros jogos da companhia deve passar por mudanças ao longo da próxima década.
“A natureza e a velocidade do conteúdo que veremos de nossas franquias icônicas, incluindo GTA, serão dramaticamente diferentes na próxima década”, declarou o CEO. Segundo Zelnick, a mudança está ligada ao compromisso da empresa com a qualidade dos jogos, a novas formas de alcançar os jogadores e à manutenção do engajamento após o lançamento.
A declaração ocorre após o longo intervalo entre GTA 5 e GTA 6. O quinto jogo principal da franquia chegou ao mercado em 2013, enquanto o próximo chegará no dia 19 deste mês – mais de 13 anos depois.
Mesmo citando o próximo jogo, a Take-Two e a Rockstar concentram seus esforços no lançamento de GTA 6. O pré-download foi liberado nesta terça-feira (10/11) e exige cerca de 212 GB de espaço livre no PlayStation 5 ou no Xbox Series S/X. Nos marketplaces, as entregas estão previstas para começar nesta quinta-feira (12/11).
O intervalo de mais de uma década entre os dois jogos principais da franquia tornou-se um dos mais longos da indústria. A produção de GTA 6 envolveu grandes equipes e um investimento elevado, embora a Rockstar não tenha divulgado oficialmente o custo total do projeto.
No Brasil, a edição padrão (Standard) custa R$ 449,90 e está em pré-venda desde junho. O jogo gerou controvérsia por ser o primeiro da franquia a não incluir um disco físico: quem comprar as versões comercializadas em marketplaces receberá uma caixa com um código para download.
Imagens de consumidores que supostamente já receberam o jogo começaram a circular na internet. Algumas delas mostram embalagens que incluem um pôster, mas ainda não há confirmação de que o item também será distribuído no Brasil. Até mesmo a edição de colecionador, vendida por cerca de R$ 2 mil, não inclui uma cópia do jogo.
O título se passa em Vice City, cidade fictícia inspirada em Miami, e acompanha os personagens Lucia Caminos e Jason Duval.

articles.title: Apple TV makes sign language interpretation a built-in accessibility feature | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Apple TV is making its content more accessible to Deaf audiences with the launch of a new Sign Language Interpretation feature, the company announced on Tuesday. The feature will initially be available across a limited set of titles, starting this Friday with the release of “Being Heumann,” a biopic about disability rights activist Judy Heumann.
American Sign Language (ASL) and British Sign Language (BSL) will also be made available for Apple’s hit movie “F1.” Later this year, other titles will follow, including “Way of the Warrior Kid” and “Greyhound.”
What makes Apple’s offering different from other platforms is that the sign language version of the film is not a separate product — that is, it’s not a separate film designed just for Deaf viewers. Instead, Apple’s support for sign language is just a setting you enable that’s integrated with the main title, similar to how you could turn on or off closed captions.
When a title with the sign language option is playing, an interpreter appears in the bottom right of the screen, translating the spoken words into signs. Apple says it has partnered with a group of DASLs (Directors of Artistic Sign Language) to ensure that the interpreter for each film fits the tone of the film. Notably, the company is not using any AI-generated interpreters, as Apple says that’s not what the Deaf community has said it needs.
The feature is shipping in the latest release of iOS 27.2, and can be turned on through a new sign language option in Settings. After being enabled, a new button will appear in the supported Apple Original titles on Apple TV indicating that sign language is available.
These titles are labeled with a sign language icon that appears on the title page alongside other features like closed captions or audio descriptions. There’s also a new section under languages that will list the specific sign languages that are available with the given title.
To make the titles more discoverable, Apple TV will highlight which titles include the sign language option in a “Movies & Shows with American Sign Language” editorial collection. Meanwhile, users can easily surface supported titles via search by typing in keywords like “with ASL,” for example.
The new feature builds on Apple’s other investments in accessibility features, which it builds itself.
“At Apple, we believe everyone should be able to enjoy great stories and entertainment,” said Sarah Herrlinger, Apple’s senior director of Global Accessibility Policy and Initiatives, in a statement about the launch. “Bringing sign language interpretation to Apple TV is an exciting step forward in making the viewing experience more accessible and inclusive for Deaf audiences. Accessibility is a core value at Apple, and we’re proud to continue creating experiences that allow more people to enjoy the content they love,” she added.

articles.title: Teleport makes Beams generally available to bring AI agents into production - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Teleport makes Beams generally available to bring AI agents into production
Infrastructure identity company Teleport today made Teleport Beams, its runtime for artificial intelligence agents that work on production infrastructure, generally available.
Beams goes after what Teleport sees as the main reason agents have stayed out of production so far. Most enterprises have not plugged agents into those systems at all, according to Ev Kontsevoy, Teleport’s co-founder and chief executive. He blamed gaps such as delegated identity and an audit trail that follows an agent from intent to action.
Sandboxes, the tool many teams reach for now, mostly isolate the agent in a virtual machine and handle its credentials. “When the cost of an error is high, traditional sandboxes don’t cut it,” Kontsevoy said ahead of the announcement.
Teleport calls each individual runtime a Beam, and every agent gets its own. A Beam carries a delegated identity inherited from the user or agent that launched it, while the agent inside starts with no standing privileges. Work begins with a proposed execution plan. That plan can be revised by a person or by a large language model acting as judge before a separate Beam runs it with only the approved roles. Reviewers then see new requests only for steps outside the plan.
Passwords never enter the agent’s environment. Everything the agent sends to a model is traced, and Teleport says that record lets Beams pick out a hijacked goal or agents coordinating in ways nobody planned. Each session also gets scored against the MITRE ATT&CK framework for a written risk summary. Seven of the detection rules come prebuilt, privilege escalation among them. Anything else a customer wants caught can be described in natural language and added to the set.
Each Beam is an ephemeral micro-VM on a virtualized network. Nothing gets in or out without passing Teleport’s controls, and the audit log keeps a copy of every protocol exchange. Snapshots taken by a feature named Phases carry the files and memory of an expiring Beam into the next one, so longer jobs do not have to start over.
Teams can also fork a Beam to try several approaches in parallel. When something goes badly wrong, a kill switch ends the agent’s activity and cuts all of its connections to production at once.
Teleport makes no promise about what a model will decide. A hijacked or mistaken agent inside a Beam can reach only what it was granted until its authority lapses at the end of the task, and every action it takes stays on the record.
Beams runs on top of the Teleport Infrastructure Identity Platform, which the company says is in production at more than 700 enterprises, Nasdaq Inc., DoorDash Inc. and Elastic N.V. among them. Cisco Systems Inc. became Teleport’s largest strategic investor in August.
Teleport first showed Beams in March, two months after publishing the Teleport Agentic Identity Framework that the runtime now puts into practice. Following a public beta, the product is available at beams.run.

articles.title: Software engineer Rickrolls his Prusa 3D printer via remote code execution exploit — one week of testing with Claude Opus uncovers 23 Prusa Buddy firmware defects
articles.text:
Software engineer Rickrolls his Prusa 3D printer via remote code execution exploit — one week of testing with Claude Opus uncovers 23 Prusa Buddy firmware defects
Prusa has patched all the vulnerabilities discovered ahead of a coordinated news release.
Software engineer Yannick Dixken spent a week attacking his Prusa MK4S 3D printer in the name of science. At the end of the relatively short but intense period, he produced a video demonstrating the ability to Rickroll the printer via remote code execution (RCE). Dixken shared the video and findings – charting “roughly 23 individual defects” with Prusa and published his amusing but detailed Never gonna print you up! blog in coordination with the 3D printer maker. Yes, all the vulnerabilities are now patched in the Buddy firmware versions >7.0.0.
Dixken is an experienced Freelance Cloud Architect, DevOps and Platform Engineer. Security research is more of a hobby, he notes in the blog post, but it is clearly a passion strong enough to spend a whole week probing the MK4S for vulnerabilities. The result is far more than the funny old Rickroll. The week of debugging, fuzzing and reverse engineering “armed with Opus 4.8 and a fuzzer” resulted in “14 findings, roughly 23 individual defects, and a chain that ends with the printer's main controller running code I sent it over the network,” noted Dixken. “Yup, fully fledged RCE.”
The headlining RCE scored 8.1 and is officially described as High Severity. This serious bug was in the cloud (or self-hosted) management platform called Prusa Connect. You can see proof-of-concept code Rickrolling the user in Dixken’s embedded video. He sent this video to Prusa.
The methods used to uncover these vulnerabilities are outlined in the source blog, if you’d like to know more. Meanwhile, there were many other vulnerabilities uncovered and cataloged. These include a USB filename attack, heap overflows triggered by malformed encrypted print files, and network denial-of-service flaws. Many of the bugs were probably symptoms of the original developers’ use of assert statements to enforce assumptions.
Happily for Prusa 3D printer users, Dixken has responsibly disclosed this multitude of vulnerabilities. The engineer says that within 24 hours of the Rickroll video being shared on social media, the 3D printing firm’s team coordinated professionally, efficiently, and kindly. Companies don’t always react so positively to those helping them find vulnerabilities in their wares.

articles.title: 'Connected data is transforming the fight against fraud': New report warns AI is fuelling a major rise in insurance fraud
articles.text:
'Connected data is transforming the fight against fraud': New report warns AI is fuelling a major rise in insurance fraud
AI is driving a rise in fake insurance claims
- Zurich analysis of insurance claims has found that AI is behind 20% of fake claims
- A complex pattern of seemingly unrelated false claims are believed to be coordinated by AI
- Generative AI has been employed by organized crime rings to create fake evidence for non-existent incidents
AI has been driving a worrying rise insurance fraud, new analysis by insurance giant Zurich and AI analytics experts at Quantexa has claimed, with complex, organized crime rings have employed generative AI to make to fabricate supporting evidence in 1 in every 5 fake claims.
Scams as diverse as crash for cash and serial claimants were intelligently analyzed with repeated elements flagged for investigation. AI’s use as both a generative tool for fakery and as a tool to detect patterns and highlight criminality demonstrates how the technology is taking criminality and detection into a new era.
The analysis has so far led to £17.9 million in fake claims detected, a small number when compared to the £1.34 billion of fraudulent claims made in 2025.
Fighting fraud
Incredible volumes of fraudulent insurance claims have been detected over the past 12 months. Zurich UK found £109.3 million in total of faked claims, with £17.9 million of that identified using advanced analytics and AI. Some 4,359 fraudulent claims were uncovered, in motor, property, and casualty insurance portfolios. Claims identified as fraudulent increased 22% from 2022’s figure of 3,562 claims to 4,359 in the past 12 months.
“Insurance fraud in the UK is becoming more sophisticated, more organized and increasingly technology-enabled," noted Scott Clayton, Head of Claims Fraud at Zurich UK and Chair of IFB. "Criminal networks are constantly adapting their tactics, whether that's staged accidents, ghost broking, fabricated claims or the use of AI-generated evidence.
Explaining how AI has helped combat the £109.3 million of fraud uncovered in 2026, he added “Connected data is transforming the fight against fraud, helping us expose hidden relationships, identify organized networks and protect honest customers from footing the bill for criminal activity.”
This appears to be an industry-leading combination of advanced analytics and human judgement by specialist investigators to tackle what is considered a rapidly evolving threat.

Clayton says that Zurich is the first insurance company in the UK to unify data from “Companies House, Equifax, industry intelligence and the Insurance Fraud Register to give us a much richer picture across every claim. That helps us identify crucial connections and information that might otherwise be difficult to spot.”
