articles.title: Strom für die KI: Anthropic sichert sich eigene Erdgasturbinen – für 3,4 Milliarden Dollar
articles.text:
Strom für die KI: Anthropic sichert sich eigene Erdgasturbinen – für 3,4 Milliarden Dollar
Der steigende Energiebedarf der KI-Branche bringt Anthropic dazu, von seiner bisherigen Zurückhaltung beim Erwerb physischer Infrastruktur abzurücken: Das Unternehmen investiert 3,4 Milliarden US-Dollar in Erdgasturbinen. Der Financial Times zufolge ist dies die bis dato größte bekannte Einzelinvestition eines KI-Unternehmens in Stromerzeugungsanlagen.
Laut der Financial Times erwirbt Anthropic Caterpillar-Generatoren, die bis zu 1,7 Gigawatt Strom erzeugen können. Caterpillar ist Hersteller von Bau- und Bergbaumaschinen, Diesel- und Erdgasmotoren und eben Gasturbinen.
Anthropic investiert erstmals in eigene Strominfrastruktur
Bisher setzte Anthropic darauf, Strominfrastruktur zu mieten, anstatt sie zu kaufen. Wie Techcrunch berichtet, geht aus dem im Mai eingereichten Börsenprospekt des Unternehmens hervor, dass es bis Mai 2029 monatlich 1,25 Milliarden US-Dollar für Rechenleistung an die SpaceX-Tochter xAI zahlen will. Mit dem Erwerb der Caterpillar-Generatoren hat Anthropic erstmals in eigene Infrastruktur für die Gewinnung von Erdgas investiert. „Durch den Besitz eines Teils ihrer Strominfrastruktur und die Verfügbarkeit der entsprechenden Kapazitäten im eigenen Haus glauben Unternehmen, sich besser vor Störungen schützen zu können, die außerhalb ihrer Kontrolle liegen“, sagt Arash Nazhad, Energieexperte, gegenüber der Financial Times.
Anthropic, OnePWR und ein Turbinen-Deal
Das KI-Unternehmen schloss die Vereinbarung mit der texanischen Firma OnePWR Solutions, die nicht nur die Turbinen liefert, sondern auch die Ressourcen für Planungs- und Bauarbeiten bereitstellt. Vor zwei Jahren bestellte die texanische Firma die Turbinen bei Caterpillar, konnte den Kauf laut Informanten der Financial Times aber letztlich nicht finanzieren. Anthropic habe die Gelegenheit genutzt und den bestehenden Auftrag bei Caterpillar übernommen.
Ursprünglich sei Anthropic daran interessiert gewesen, Kunde von OnePWR zu werden. „Anthropic wollte die Erzeugungskapazität wahrscheinlich lieber selbst behalten, anstatt einem Konkurrenten die Gelegenheit zu geben, sie sich zu sichern“, vermutet Techcrunch.
Fracking für die KI
Der massive Energiebedarf Künstlicher Intelligenz könne das von US-Präsident Trump befürwortete Fracking weiter in den Fokus rücken, wie Techcrunch schreibt. Fracking ist eine Methode, bei der unter hohem Druck ein Gemisch aus Wasser, Sand und Chemikalien in tiefe Gesteinsschichten gepresst wird. So werden Risse erzeugt und darin gebundenes Erdgas oder Erdöl freigesetzt. Wenn der Kaufrausch der KI-Unternehmen weiter voranschreitet, könnten allein die US-Rechenzentren bis 2035 mehr Erdgas verbrauchen als Deutschland und Japan zusammen.
Das Verfahren ist aufgrund seiner Umweltrisiken umstritten – dazu zählt etwa die Verunreinigung von Trink- und Grundwasser. In Deutschland gelten seit 2017 strenge Regeln und weitreichende Verbote für die Anwendung der Fracking-Technik.

articles.title: Bluetooth® High Data Throughput: The Future of Wireless - EE Times
articles.text:
The world is generating, sharing, and processing more data than ever before. Applications are becoming more sophisticated, and user expectations continue to rise.
More of the experiences people, businesses, and industries rely on every day are wireless. From premium audio experiences to immersive computing, industrial systems, advanced peripherals, and emerging AI-driven applications, wireless connectivity is increasingly required to support more devices, more data, and higher expectations with every new generation of products.
Keeping pace with these demands requires more than speed alone. It requires the capacity to communicate larger volumes of information with greater efficiency and reliability. Bluetooth® High Data Throughput (HDT) was designed to meet this opportunity.
What is Bluetooth® High Data Throughput?
Bluetooth HDT introduces a new physical layer (PHY) that significantly increases the amount of information devices can exchange while continuing to operate within the same channel bandwidth and spacing used by existing Bluetooth LE PHYs. Higher throughput is achieved primarily through greater spectral efficiency, using higher-order coherent modulation and forward error correction to support multiple data rates up to 7.5 Mbps.
By increasing the maximum supported bit rate to 7.5 Mbps, nearly four times that of the Bluetooth LE 2M PHY, HDT expands the Bluetooth performance envelope across speed, capacity, energy efficiency, and reliability.
These advances enable Bluetooth devices to transfer more data, make more efficient use of wireless resources, and perform more reliably across a broader range of applications and environments. Together, they open the door to richer experiences, more sophisticated applications, and new opportunities for innovation across the global Bluetooth ecosystem.
The Bluetooth LE PHY evolution
The introduction of Bluetooth LE enabled an entirely new generation of low-power connected devices, helping fuel the connected device revolution and ushering in an explosion of commercial and industrial applications. The Bluetooth LE 2M PHY and Bluetooth LE Coded PHY introduced higher speed and longer range, respectively, further expanding the role of Bluetooth technology in industrial and commercial environments.
Most recently, the Bluetooth LE 2M 2BT PHY enabled Bluetooth® Channel Sounding, a secure, fine-ranging feature that brings true distance awareness to billions of everyday devices.
Bluetooth HDT marks the next major milestone in this evolution, advancing Bluetooth performance across four critical dimensions: faster data transfer, increased capacity, better energy efficiency, and enhanced reliability.
The benefits of Bluetooth HDT
Faster data transfer
With a maximum supported bit rate of 7.5 Mbps, Bluetooth HDT can move substantially more data over the Bluetooth link than the Bluetooth LE 2M PHY. The data rate available to an application will depend on implementation and operating conditions, but the expanded PHY capability creates additional headroom for faster synchronization, shorter file transfer times, reduced delays, and more responsive wireless interactions.
Increased capacity
Higher data rates do more than shorten the time required to complete a transfer. They also increase the amount of information that devices can exchange within available wireless resources. By improving spectral efficiency and potentially reducing the airtime required to move a given volume of data, Bluetooth HDT creates additional capacity for richer and more data-intensive interactions.
This additional headroom better supports today’s most demanding applications as well as tomorrow’s innovations. From high-resolution and lossless audio to immersive computing, AI-enabled devices, and future applications yet to be imagined, increased capacity enables Bluetooth technology to meet growing expectations for wireless connectivity.
Better energy efficiency
Efficient use of spectrum, airtime, and energy is essential to supporting a future where billions of connected devices exchange increasing amounts of information. By moving more data in less time, Bluetooth HDT can allow the radio to spend less time actively transmitting and more time in lower-power states.
Enhanced reliability
Bluetooth HDT supports multiple data rates and can adapt transmission behavior as link conditions change, helping devices balance higher throughput with the robustness needed to maintain reliable communication across a broader range of operating environments.
Bluetooth HDT also introduces a packet format designed to move larger amounts of data efficiently and reliably. When this format is used, a payload can be divided into independently validated blocks, allowing devices to retransmit only missing or corrupted blocks rather than repeating the entire payload. This reduces unnecessary retransmissions and helps preserve throughput when part of a transmission is affected.
Key use cases
The first flagship application for Bluetooth HDT will be premium wireless audio, bringing standardized high-resolution and lossless audio capabilities to Bluetooth technology. But audio is just the first demonstration of what becomes possible when Bluetooth devices can exchange more information at greater speed and with greater efficiency and reliability. Those same advances create opportunities across immersive computing, AI-enabled devices, commercial and industrial solutions, everyday IoT devices, and future applications.
Premium wireless audio
With demand for higher-quality wireless listening experiences increasing, Bluetooth HDT provides the capacity, efficiency, and wireless performance needed to support high-resolution and lossless audio while creating new opportunities for surround sound, spatial audio, and other elevated audio experiences across the Bluetooth ecosystem.
Immersive and spatial computing
With extended reality (XR), spatial computing, and other immersive applications continuing to evolve, Bluetooth HDT enables more responsive experiences and increasingly complex device interactions, introducing new possibilities for innovation across this rapidly expanding application space.
AI-enabled devices
With more data being generated, processed, and exchanged at the edge, Bluetooth HDT provides additional capacity and performance for increasingly intelligent, context-aware, and adaptive AI-enabled experiences.
Commercial and industrial solutions
Across commercial and industrial environments, the reliance on wireless communication continues to grow. Bluetooth HDT delivers the capacity and reliability needed to enable more advanced automation, monitoring, and operational systems.
Everyday IoT devices
From wearables and health and fitness devices to smart home products, peripherals, and other connected devices, billions of products rely on Bluetooth technology to create everyday connected experiences. Bluetooth HDT enables these common data exchanges, from syncing information with smartphones to transferring files and receiving firmware updates, to happen faster, reducing wait times and keeping data transfer from getting in the way of the connected experience.
The opportunity extends well beyond any single use case. By expanding Bluetooth performance, Bluetooth HDT gives developers and manufacturers greater flexibility to create new products and experiences as wireless requirements continue to evolve.
Building a foundation for what comes next
As devices generate, process, and exchange more data, wireless connectivity must continue to evolve alongside them. Bluetooth HDT represents an important step in that evolution, simultaneously advancing speed, capacity, energy efficiency, and reliability.
Premium wireless audio may be the first flagship application, but the potential extends much further. Bluetooth HDT gives developers and manufacturers greater flexibility to create richer, more responsive, and more sophisticated wireless experiences. By significantly expanding what Bluetooth technology can deliver, Bluetooth HDT establishes a foundation for the next generation of wireless experiences.
To learn more about Bluetooth® High Data Throughput and the opportunities it creates, visit the Bluetooth HDT page on Bluetooth.com. For a deeper look at the technology and its implementation, read the Bluetooth® High Data Throughput technical overview.

articles.title: Why traction-first investing could make Africa miss its next category-defining companies - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African venture capital is becoming more disciplined, writes Amarachi Nwachukwu, is a tech investor at MARLVC, where she leads investment activities across Africa, from deal sourcing and due diligence to investment execution and portfolio support.
But I worry that in trying to avoid the mistakes of the last funding cycle, we may be creating another problem: becoming so focused on traction that we lose the ability to recognise exceptional opportunities before they become obvious.
Over the past few years, the conversation around early-stage investing has shifted significantly. Founders who could once raise capital on the strength of their vision, market opportunity and team are now being asked to demonstrate revenue, customer growth, retention and sometimes even profitability before investors are willing to write the first cheque.
I understand why. The funding boom of 2021 and 2022 taught us expensive lessons. Capital became harder to raise, follow-on funding slowed, and companies built around unsustainable growth struggled to survive. Investors became more selective, and founders were forced to prioritise stronger business fundamentals.
That correction was necessary.
Investing is fundamentally a judgment business. When we begin replacing judgment with rigid frameworks, we risk becoming exceptionally good at identifying what already works and increasingly poor at recognising what could work.
If we expect founders to eliminate most of the uncertainty before investing, what exactly are we underwriting?
The traction paradox
One of the biggest contradictions in African early-stage investing is that founders need capital to generate traction, yet investors increasingly demand traction before providing capital.
Consider a founder building financial infrastructure, an energy technology company or an AI product requiring specialised engineering and enterprise adoption.
These businesses may need regulatory approvals, technical development, distribution partnerships and significant product experimentation before meaningful revenue becomes possible.
Yet they are often evaluated using the same commercial expectations as software businesses operating in established markets.
The result is a difficult cycle: founders need funding to build, but must demonstrate the outcomes of that funding before receiving it.
And this changes what founders build.
When a founder is constantly worried about payroll, infrastructure costs and keeping the business alive, long-term product innovation can become secondary to immediate revenue.
Instead of pursuing an ambitious technology opportunity, they may pivot toward consulting, short-term commercial contracts or smaller business models that generate cash quickly.
There is nothing wrong with building a profitable small business. But venture capital is supposed to finance companies with the potential for outsized outcomes.
If our investment expectations consistently push founders toward what is easiest to monetise, we may be discouraging them from building what could become most valuable.
Traction is not the same as potential
In evaluating early-stage technology companies, I have become increasingly interested in the distinction between what a company has already achieved and what its achievements actually tell us about its future.
A company generating $30,000 in monthly revenue is not automatically a better venture investment than one generating $3,000.
The first may operate in a crowded market, with limited differentiation, expensive customer acquisition and little room to expand.
Revenue does not eliminate execution risk, competition, regulatory uncertainty or the possibility that a business will never achieve venture-scale returns.
For some companies, revenue is the strongest evidence of demand. For others, it may be product adoption, customer retention, successful technical deployment, signed commercial agreements or a measurable improvement in how customers operate.
Of course, a signed partnership is not equivalent to revenue, and a product demonstration is not proof of product-market fit.
But these signals should not be dismissed simply because they have not yet translated into substantial revenue.
Our responsibility as investors is to understand what each signal proves. AI has made this conversation even more interesting.
Today, with AI-assisted development tools and increasingly accessible software infrastructure, founders can build prototypes and minimum viable products at a fraction of what similar development might have cost a few years ago.
Investors know this. However an MVP alone is no longer particularly impressive in many software categories. If almost anyone can build a functional product, investors reasonably want evidence that customers need it..
But we should not confuse the declining cost of building software with the declining difficulty of building a meaningful technology company. Distribution, regulatory complexity, customer trust, proprietary technology and sustainable competitive advantages remain difficult to develop.
The question should not simply be whether a founder has built something and generated revenue.
It should be whether they are building something that matters, why they are uniquely positioned to succeed, and whether the market conditions support that opportunity.
Are we managing risk or avoiding it?
It would be unfair to discuss traction-first investing without acknowledging the position of fund managers.
Fund managers have fiduciary responsibilities, portfolio construction strategies, investment mandates and return expectations. Their ability to raise subsequent funds often depends on the performance of their existing investments and in Africa, those pressures are particularly significant. The ecosystem operates against a backdrop of currency volatility, limited exit opportunities, uneven consumer purchasing power, regulatory uncertainty and a relatively small pool of investors willing to fund companies through multiple stages. This explains why investors increasingly favour companies with measurable commercial progress.
However, there is a difference between managing risk and refusing to take the risks that define venture capital. If every fund eventually waits for the same revenue thresholds and growth metrics, we eventually compete for the same small pool of validated companies. And by then, the earliest opportunities to generate outsized returns may already have passed.
I believe investing is fundamentally a judgment business.
At pre-seed, I want to understand the founder’s insight into the problem, their ability to execute, the timing of the market opportunity, the strength of the technology and the evidence supporting their assumptions.
Most importantly, I want to understand what the investment will help them prove next.
There is a difference between managing risk intelligently and refusing to take risks that are central to the venture capital model.
Not every fund should invest before revenue. Fund mandates, portfolio strategies and LP expectations matter. But an ecosystem in which almost nobody is willing to finance that stage has a structural problem.
We are also shaping the kinds of companies Africa will produce.
Perhaps the most concerning consequence of traction-first investing is not the individual companies that fail to raise capital. The greatest consequence of traction-first investing may not be the companies that fail to raise capital. It may be the companies that never get built. Founders respond to incentives.
Founders pay attention to what investors fund. If capital consistently flows toward business models capable of generating immediate revenue, more founders will naturally pursue those opportunities.
We may end up with an ecosystem that produces an increasing number of commercially sensible startups but fewer companies attempting difficult technological breakthroughs or creating entirely new markets.
But where the potential for venture-scale outcomes exists, investors should be willing to evaluate the opportunity on its merits instead of rejecting it because its commercial progress does not resemble that of a conventional SaaS startup.
There is also a broader ecosystem effect. Every successful founder can create experienced operators, angel investors, new companies and future sources of capital. Supporting the right early-stage companies can therefore create value beyond the returns of an individual investment. But that future ecosystem cannot emerge if we consistently wait for someone else to take the earliest risks
But where the potential for venture-scale outcomes exists, investors should be willing to evaluate the opportunity on its merits instead of rejecting it because its commercial progress does not resemble that of a conventional SaaS startup.
The greatest consequence of traction-first investing may not be the companies that fail to raise capital. It may be the companies that never get built. Founders respond to incentives.
If investors consistently reward business models capable of generating immediate revenue, founders will naturally gravitate toward those opportunities. We risk producing more companies that are commercially sensible from day one, but fewer attempting difficult technological breakthroughs or creating entirely new markets.
I am not advocating a return to reckless investing, inflated valuations or funding ambitious narratives without credible evidence.
African venture capital needs discipline. We need better governance, stronger due diligence, realistic valuations and founders who understand capital efficiency.
Our responsibility is to recognise the difference between an unproven idea and an opportunity worth proving.
Because if we only invest when the outcome begins to look certain, are we still financing innovation, or are we simply financing its survivors?

articles.title: YouTube volverá a las listas de Billboard tras un cambio que da más peso a las escuchas gratuitas
articles.text:
YouTube volverá en 2027 a entregar sus datos de reproducciones a las listas de Billboard, la medición de éxito musical de Estados Unidos, luego de que Billboard modificara su fórmula para que las escuchas gratuitas con anuncios valgan más. Lyor Cohen, jefe global de música de YouTube, lo confirmó el 9 de noviembre.
Cohen añadió dos líneas a la publicación de diciembre de 2025 en la que había anunciado la salida. “Volvemos a las listas de Billboard a partir de 2027”, escribió. “La nueva metodología de Billboard refleja mejor cómo interactúan hoy los fans con la música, tanto en servicios de suscripción como con anuncios”.
Billboard había anunciado antes, ese mismo lunes, que reducía la diferencia entre ambos tipos de escucha. Hasta ahora, un álbum sumaba una unidad de consumo con 1.000 reproducciones de pago o con 2.500 con anuncios. Con la nueva proporción bastarán 1.500 reproducciones con anuncios.
El cambio rige para la lista Billboard 200 y sus listas de álbumes por género a partir de la edición con fecha del 16 de enero de 2027, que reflejará los datos del 1 al 7 de enero, según Music Business Worldwide. Billboard dijo que la revisión surge de un análisis anual con la empresa Luminate sobre los ingresos del streaming.
La medición de streaming también alimenta a la lista de canciones Hot 100 y a otras listas de álbumes y canciones, según Engadget. Billboard afirmó que busca mantener sus listas alineadas con la economía cambiante del consumo de música, y que las nuevas proporciones se basan en el análisis de los ingresos de las escuchas pagas y gratuitas.
11 meses de enfrentamiento
El conflicto comenzó el 16 de diciembre de 2025. Ese día Billboard estrechó la proporción de 1 a 3 a 1 a 2,5, y al día siguiente Cohen anunció que YouTube dejaría de enviar sus datos después del 16 de enero de 2026.
En su mensaje original, Cohen calificó la fórmula de “obsoleta” y sostuvo que ignoraba el interés de los fans sin suscripción. Afirmó además que el streaming representa el 84% de los ingresos de la música grabada en Estados Unidos. YouTube pedía que cada reproducción contara por igual.
Los datos de YouTube faltan en las listas desde la edición con fecha del 31 de enero, según Billboard. La plataforma se había incorporado a las listas de canciones en 2013 y a la Billboard 200 en 2019, de acuerdo con la propia Billboard.
Cuando Billboard dio mayor valor a las escuchas de pago en 2019, explicó que asignar valores según el nivel de acceso y de compensación económica reflejaba mejor la actividad de los usuarios. Esa postura se mantiene: las escuchas de suscripción siguen pesando más que las gratuitas.
Qué cambia para los artistas
TechCrunch señaló que el regreso puede beneficiar a músicos independientes y a artistas con muchos seguidores en el exterior, cuyos videos, presentaciones en vivo y videos de letras sumarán de nuevo a su posición en las listas.
La proporción final no coincide con la igualdad que YouTube pedía en 2025. Pitchfork indicó que no está claro por qué la plataforma aceptó 1 a 1,5, y que consultó a sus voceros sin respuesta hasta la publicación.
La primera lista con los nuevos criterios será la del 16 de enero de 2027. YouTube no precisó en qué fecha de 2027 empezará a enviar sus datos.

articles.title: OpenAI unveils a 'Control Room' safety feature that shuts down AI agents from going rogue in 35 seconds
articles.text:
OpenAI unveils a 'Control Room' safety feature that shuts down AI agents from going rogue in 35 seconds
OpenAI said Control Room will connect every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. It will work together with its misalignment monitoring systems.
OpenAI has introduced Control Room, a feature that halts any artificial intelligence (AI) output that raises safety or security concerns within 35 seconds, the company said in a blog post.
On the need for Control Room, the blog post said, “As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed. To solve this, we built Control Room.”
Control Room will be a central system to track model workloads across the research infrastructure of OpenAI.
OpenAI said Control Room will connect every research inference workload, including agentic sampling for model training and evaluation, data processing, and more. It will work together with its misalignment monitoring systems
The Control Room will be integrating a few systems: the workload, the inference engine and the centralised control room service.
The workload is the job being run, such as a reinforcement learning experiment, an evaluation, a high-volume sampling or data processing job. The inference engine is the key of any AI model. The Control Room service tracks jobs and controls whether they are allowed to continue generating model output.
The blog post noted that engines check with the Control Room service before fulfilling a request. If a job has been stopped, the service denies the request, preventing further output.
OpenAI said it runs continuous checks to detect unauthorised or modified inference engine implementations that may bypass Control Room.
“We additionally run continual agentic and programmatic sweeps to check that users are not accidentally or maliciously launching rogue engine implementations with Control Room unimplemented or disabled,” it noted.
OpenAI said it will continue to strengthen and expand the system over the coming months, alongside its investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.

articles.title: James Gunn et Peter Safran virés de DC Studios : le DCU en danger ?
articles.text:
James Gunn et Peter Safran virés de DC Studios : le DCU en danger ?
Coup de théâtre chez DC Studios : James Gunn et Peter Safran, aux commandes du DCU depuis quatre ans, quittent le navire et vont être remplacés par un ancien producteur de Marvel.
James Gunn et Peter Safran pensaient avoir survécu au rachat de Warner Bros. par Paramount mais le couperet est finalement tombé : ils ne vont plus être à la tête de l'univers DC. Les patrons de Skydance, David Ellison et Ynon Kreiz, en ont décidé autrement et c'est dorénavant Jeremy Latcham, un producteur qui jouait autrefois un rôle clé chez Marvel Studios, qui va les remplacer.
Ça sent le roussi chez DC
Après quatre ans à la tête de DC Studios, James Gunn et Peter Safran quittent leurs postes et repassent du côté créatif. Jeremy Latcham, qui a participé à la production d'Iron Man, Les Gardiens de la Galaxie ou encore Avengers chez Marvel, va ainsi prendre la relève.
Alors que, sous le nouveau régime de Skydance, Safran et Gunn souhaitaient continuer de ne répondre qu'aux patrons du studios, Ellison et Kreiz (comme cela était le cas du temps de Warner Bros. sous David Zaslav), afin de garder le contrôle sur les sorties DC, Latcham sera lui sous la direction de Dana Goldberg et Josh Greenstein, coprésidents de Skydance Motion Picture Group, et prendra ses fonctions le 1er décembre.
Si Gunn s'est montré quelque peu soulagé de pouvoir retourner pleinement à ses fonctions de réalisateur, lui et Safran demeurent liés à DC et assureront la production de divers projets. Ils travaillent actuellement sur la postproduction de la suite de Superman, Man of Tomorrow, dont la sortie en salles est prévue pour le 7 juillet 2027.
On ne sait pas encore si Gunn pourra ensuite achever ses ambitions autour de Superman, qu'il souhaitait transformer en trilogie.
Mais que s'est-il passé chez Skydance pour provoquer ce retournement de situation alors que le duo pensait conserver leur place ? Des sources proches de la situation ont indiqué plusieurs facteurs auprès de nos confrères du Hollywood Reporter.
Tout d'abord, le contrôle de Gunn et Safran sur les projets DC semblait poser problème aux têtes pensantes de Skydance, d'autant plus que le duo n'était pas suffisamment communicatifs au sujet de leurs projets et des détails de leur programmations, refusant aussi de montrer des images aux responsables de Skydance.
Ce manque de communication ajouté à l'échec massif au box-office de Supergirl, qui n'a rapporté que 126,4 millions de dollars au box-office mondial pour un budget de 186 millions, n'a pas aidé leur cause. D'autant plus que les boss de Skyfance considèreraient même les 618,7 millions de dollars de recettes de Superman comme insuffisantes, estimant que le film n'a pas eu d'impact marquant sur la pop culture.
En somme, Skydance semble vouloir que DC touche un public plus large et en embauchant Latcham, un producteur reconnu pour une approche grand public, l'idée est de faire de DC une franchise plus performante.
Certains au sein du studio ont cependant une crainte : à force de le voir changer de direction, les fans du DCU ne vont-ils pas finir par en avoir assez de s'investir dans ces films ?

articles.title: 164 395 dollars par an et une base sur la Lune : la NASA recrute ses futurs astronautes, mais pas n'importe qui
articles.text:
L’annonce ressemble à n’importe quelle offre d’emploi de l’administration américaine. Publiée sur USAJobs, elle affiche un salaire de départ de 164 395 dollars par an, pour un poste basé au Johnson Space Center de Houston. L’intitulé, lui, sort de l’ordinaire : candidat astronaute, pour « quelques postes vacants ». Selon l’administrateur de la NASA, Jared Isaacman, les personnes retenues lors de ce recrutement lancé samedi 7 novembre « pourraient marcher sur la Lune, vivre et travailler dans la base lunaire », avant de préparer les premières missions habitées vers Mars. Les candidatures sont ouvertes jusqu’au 3 décembre 2026 à 23 h 59, heure de la côte Est américaine.
Un passeport américain, un master et des nerfs d’acier
La première condition écarte d’emblée les lecteurs français, puisqu’il faut avoir la nationalité américaine. Pour les Européens, la voie passe par l’Agence spatiale européenne, qui a sélectionné Sophie Adenot, revenue de la Station spatiale internationale en octobre. Côté diplôme, la NASA demande un master scientifique (ingénierie, biologie, physique, informatique ou mathématiques), deux années validées de doctorat dans l’un de ces domaines, un diplôme médical ou un passage par une école de pilotes d’essai, à terminer avant juillet 2027. Nouveauté relevée par la radio publique NPR, les masters en soins infirmiers sont désormais acceptés. À l’inverse, les diplômes de technologie, d’aviation, de sciences sociales ou de psychologie (hors psychologie clinique, physiologique ou expérimentale) ne suffisent pas.
Il faut aussi justifier d’au moins trois ans d’expérience professionnelle après le diplôme. Les pilotes font exception, mais ils doivent afficher un nombre minimum d’heures de vol, par exemple 750 heures comme commandant de bord sur avion à réaction. Chaque candidat choisit une seule spécialité parmi sept. L’une d’elles, baptisée « opérations », vise les profils habitués aux environnements à haut risque, comme la plongée profonde, le contrôle de mission ou les sous-marins nucléaires.
Sept heures sous l’eau et aucune mission garantie
La suite de l’annonce détaille ce qui attend les recrues, et la liste a de quoi refroidir. Il faut d’abord réussir des examens médicaux et psychiatriques, une enquête de sécurité, un dépistage de drogues et, dès le premier mois, un test de natation. La vue doit être corrigeable à 10/10 à chaque œil, lunettes et chirurgie réfractive comprises. La formation, d’environ deux ans, comprend même des langues étrangères, et les candidats pourront y passer jusqu’à sept heures par jour sous l’eau en scaphandre pour simuler l’apesanteur. Le télétravail est exclu, les congés peuvent être refusés à certaines périodes et il faut accepter des séjours de douze mois ou plus dans l’espace. Rien ne garantit pourtant une affectation : la NASA prévient que les délais d’attente sont « inconnus ». Les élus devront même représenter l’agence devant le public, y compris quand le message « contredit leurs opinions personnelles ».
La sélection s’annonce féroce. Lors du précédent recrutement, plus de 8 000 personnes avaient postulé pour seulement 10 places, rappelle NPR. Le corps des astronautes de la NASA compte aujourd’hui 32 membres actifs. Les candidats retenus, attendus fin 2027, devront ensuite boucler leur formation avant de pouvoir être affectés à une mission.
Une base lunaire qui se construit contrat par contrat
Le même jour, la NASA a détaillé une série de contrats pour sa base au pôle Sud lunaire. Huit entreprises pourront se disputer les futures livraisons sur la Lune, dont SpaceX, Blue Origin, Lockheed Martin et Intuitive Machines. Ce contrat-cadre, baptisé CLPS 2, court sur dix ans et vaut jusqu’à 10 milliards de dollars. Boeing, dont la capsule Starliner a accumulé les déboires, ne figure pas dans la liste. L’agence lance aussi PROMISE, un rover à propulsion nucléaire conçu par le JPL à partir de pièces de rechange des rovers martiens Curiosity et Perseverance. Il pourra fonctionner pendant les longues nuits lunaires et dans les cratères plongés dans l’ombre, où de la glace pourrait se cacher. Son lancement est prévu fin 2028 à bord d’un atterrisseur de Blue Origin, pour une mission de 18 mois.
SpaceX lancera de son côté des satellites de communication vers l’espace cislunaire à bord d’un Starship en 2028. D’autres contrats, d’environ 1,3 milliard de dollars au total, financeront le transport de matériel entre la Terre et la Lune. La NASA vise un retour d’astronautes sur la Lune en 2028, une première depuis 1972. L’équipage d’Artemis II l’a déjà survolée en avril. Les astronautes recrutés cet hiver pourraient faire partie des équipages suivants. « Quand nos astronautes retourneront sur la Lune, ils y trouveront les premiers éléments de la base lunaire qui les attendront déjà », promet Jared Isaacman.

articles.title: Microsoft releases Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update
articles.text:
Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update, which includes this month's November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes and a few bug fixes and changes.
If you are running Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC or are enrolled in the ESU program, you can install this update as normal by going to Settings, clicking Windows Update, and manually running a 'Check for Updates.'
After installing this update, Windows 10 will be updated to build 19045.7846, and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 will be updated to build 19044.7846.
What's new in Windows 10 KB5131096
Microsoft no longer releases new features for Windows 10, and the KB5131096 update mainly includes security updates and bug fixes.
The update also includes fixes released as part of today's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, which addressed 1,235 vulnerabilities across Microsoft's products, including one actively exploited Outlook zero-day flaw.
The complete list of fixes and changes in KB5131096 is below:
- [Date and Time] This update adjusts daylight saving time (DST) rules for Cuba for the extended 2026-2027 DST period. Cuba remains on UTC-04:00 and doesn't observe the November 2026 and March 2027 transitions. It returns to UTC-05:00 in November 2027 and resumes its regular seasonal schedule in 2028. 
  - For the latest DST and time zone guidance, see the Daylight Saving Time & Time Zone Blog.
- [Printing] - Fixed: Adding a printer published in Active Directory through Settings > Bluetooth & devices > Printers & scanners > Add device might fail with error 87, "The parameter is incorrect." This issue was introduced by the October 2026 update and does not generally affect existing printers or printing.
- [Remote Desktop] 
  - Fixed: The “Specify thumbprints of certificates representing trusted .rdp publishers” policy could not be configured successfully through Microsoft Intune.
  - Fixed: Remote Desktop shadow connections might fail with an “Unspecified error” on Windows Server 2016 and Windows Server 2012 R2 after installing the October 14, 2026, update.
- [Windows PowerShell] This update strengthens security for PowerShell script signing and signature verification by introducing stricter encoding validation. As a result, scripts containing invalid UTF-8 encoding might fail signature validation, even if they were previously accepted. To resolve this issue, review the affected scripts, save them using valid UTF-8 encoding with a byte order mark (BOM), and sign them again. For further guidance, see Encoding Guidance for Signed PowerShell Scripts.
Microsoft says it has now resolved all known issues affecting USB Audio Class 1.0 devices introduced by the September 2026 Windows security updates.
The problems caused some devices to stop producing audio, fail to start with Code 10 errors, or experience unresponsive volume controls and sound settings.
Microsoft previously released an emergency out-of-band update on September 14 to fix issues affecting 8-channel and 3D audio modes.
The remaining audio issues have now been fixed in today's Windows 10 update.

articles.title: Google ya no quiere un solo chip de IA que haga de todo: lanza dos nuevas TPU especializadas para plantar cara a Nvidia
articles.text:
Google está ampliando su familia de procesadores de IA de diseño propio con dos nuevas variantes, una diseñada para computación que requiera proteger datos sensibles y la otra para cargas de trabajo exigentes en memoria. La compañía quiere seguir ampliando su oferta de chips en un contexto en el que Nvidia ha estado dominando todos estos años. Y con estos chips ya van cuatro configuraciones de sus TPUs en un solo año, todo un hito para la compañía.
Novedades. Los dos sistemas son el TPU 8tx y el TPU 8i Max. Se unen al TPU 8t, diseñado para el entrenamiento, y al TPU 8i, diseñado para el razonamiento, que la compañía presentó durante el Google Cloud Next de abril. Google afirma que el 8t ofrece un rendimiento de entrenamiento hasta 2,7 veces superior y el 8i una relación precio-rendimiento de inferencia hasta un 80% mejor en comparación con la generación anterior.
Google no ha revelado los precios ni las fechas exactas de lanzamiento, aunque su responsable de chips, Amin Vahdat, declaraba a Bloomberg que las nuevas variantes estarán disponibles el año que viene.
Por qué es importante. Tal y como comparten desde Bloomberg, Google ha estado lanzando nuevas TPUs una vez cada dos años. Esta vez ya van cuatro configuraciones en una misma generación, lo que demuestra el interés de la compañía por conseguir una mayor cuota en el mercado de hardware para IA. Desde hace tiempo, Nvidia ha sido la que vendía y cortaba el pescado. Pero las TPUs de Google entran con fuerza cada vez más. Vahdat señalaba que la estrategia responde a la tesis de que “el futuro va a girar en torno a la especialización”. En lugar de un único chip para todo, argumenta, las versiones personalizadas “aportan mucho más valor”.
La opción segura. El TPU 8tx está dirigido a gobiernos e industrias reguladas que desean ejecutar modelos y agentes de IA con datos confidenciales. Google explica que los datos suelen estar cifrados en el almacenamiento y en tránsito, pero deben desbloquearse en la memoria mientras un ordenador los procesa. La compañía afirma que el 8tx integra la protección directamente en el hardware, manteniendo los datos y los pesos de los modelos aislados incluso durante su uso.
Esta versión utiliza el mismo silicio que el TPU 8t y se combina con procesadores AMD EPYC de quinta generación. Además, Google afirma que ofrece una latencia hasta dos veces menor que el 8t, con una penalización de rendimiento casi nula ante esa seguridad adicional. La compañía también asegura que los clientes pueden ajustar los modelos con datos privados sin necesidad de moverlos entre clústeres.
La opción de memoria. El TPU 8i Max se centra en lo que Google denomina el “muro de la memoria”, es decir, cuando muchos agentes de inteligencia artificial trabajan en toda una base de código o en horas de vídeo, el ancho de banda de la memoria se convierte en el cuello de botella. La respuesta de Google consiste en colocar dos chips TPU 8i en un solo paquete. En comparación con el 8i estándar, afirma que esto duplica la capacidad de cálculo, la memoria SRAM integrada y el ancho de banda de la memoria. Asimismo, permite integrar el doble de silicio en el mismo espacio de rack, lo que permitiría a los centros de datos contar con más chips y más potencia en la misma superficie.
Vahdat contaba a Bloomberg que el sistema está pensado para aplicaciones de contexto largo, como el descubrimiento de fármacos o complejos problemas matemáticos, así como para programación.
Versiones mejoradas. Realmente no son chips completamente nuevos, pues el propio Vahdat indicaba al medio que ambas variantes son reconfiguraciones de silicio ya existente, adaptadas a las solicitudes de los clientes. Un chip nuevo requiere años de diseño y fabricación, mientras que un sistema construido a su alrededor (redes, memoria, empaquetado) puede ajustarse en cuestión de meses. Google prefiere aprovechar este enfoque para seguirle el ritmo al software de IA.
El mercado para las TPUs de Google. Según Bloomberg Intelligence, espera que las ventas de TPU, incluyendo el hardware y el software relacionados, superen los 135.000 millones de dólares para 2028, frente a los estimados 12.000 millones de este año. Entre los clientes se encuentran Apple, Meta y Oracle, que ha indicado que sus clientes en la nube podrán utilizar las TPU a partir del próximo año. Anthropic tiene la opción de comprar hasta 150.000 millones de dólares en TPU entre 2028 y 2031, según un documento regulatorio citado por Bloomberg, y el mismo medio ha informado de que OpenAI también planea adquirirlas.
Los obstáculos. Según comparte Bloomberg, haciendo alusión a la última presentación de resultados de Google, todas las TPU de las que dispone la compañía ya están contratadas por un cliente. Persisten la escasez de memoria y de capacidad de fabricación, y según los informes, Google está ampliando su base de proveedores más allá de Broadcom, incluyendo un acuerdo con Marvell.
También está surgiendo competencia, pues Tenspresso, una startup fundada por dos exingenieros de TPU, se centra en la inferencia de contexto largo, aunque Bloomberg informa de que su chip se encuentra a un año como mínimo de completar su diseño. OpenAI y Anthropic también están desarrollando chips propios con veteranos de TPU.

articles.title: Elon Musk dice que ahorrar a largo plazo es 'inútil' ya que espera un futuro de abundancia
articles.text:
Elon Musk ha vuelto a sacar el tema de ahorrar para el futuro. Escribió en X: “Con la llegada de la abundancia superinteligente, no tiene sentido ahorrar dinero para el futuro lejano”. Para que su argumento tenga sentido, debe cumplirse su previsión de que la combinación de inteligencia artificial (IA) y robótica llevará a una producción suficientemente grande de bienes y servicios como para que los ahorros pierdan relevancia en ese futuro.
Este comentario fue en respuesta a una usuaria de X (@battleangelviv) que explicaba que se atrevía a tomar “cuestionables decisiones financieras” porque cree en un futuro de abundancia. Incluso avisaba de que no hay que ser completamente imprudente, pero que en unos años gran parte de estas decisiones dejarán de tener importancia. Musk apoyó este argumento en su respuesta.
Ya había comentado esto en otras ocasiones. En diciembre de 2025, Genbeta recogía cómo Musk defendía que con un alto ingreso universal no sería necesario ahorrar. En esta ocasión es en respuesta a una charla sobre decisiones personales con el dinero.
Ahorrar para una jubilación que Musk imagina distinta
En un episodio de Moonshots con Peter Diamandis, Musk hablaba de no preocuparse por ahorrar para la jubilación en 10 o 20 años. “No importará”, decía. “Si alguna de las cosas que hemos dicho es cierta, ahorrar para la jubilación será irrelevante”.
Su argumento era que, con los avances en IA, energía y robótica, se va a disparar la productividad. Se podrá acceder a cualquier producto que uno quiera. Además de eso, se tendrá acceso a una atención médica mejor que la disponible entonces. También se podrá aprender de forma gratuita cualquier cosa y se acabará la escasez de bienes y servicios.
Varios expertos en finanzas personales e IA consultados sobre estos comentarios están de acuerdo en que hay que seguir ahorrando para la jubilación.
En otro momento (The Builders con Walter Isaacson) ha llevado el argumento más allá, hacia una economía multiplanetaria. En este caso, Musk defiende que los avances en robótica y viajes espaciales harán que el dinero deje de importar. Las monedas tradicionales dejarán de tener sentido.
También Bill Gates ha hablado de una verdadera abundancia futura. En el pódcast Decoder decía que los robots podrían construir casas, producir alimentos o hacer cirugías. Sin embargo, advertía que las dos décadas de transición pueden ser tan caóticas como cualquier otro momento de la historia humana. El motivo es que el trabajo humano dejará de ser necesario para la mayoría de los bienes y servicios.
Musk también admite que puede haber un camino accidentado. Para solucionar el problema de destrucción de empleo que genera la IA, propone que los gobiernos envíen dinero a todos.

articles.title: Apple lance ses premières recharges d’IA payantes, en supplément de votre abonnement
articles.text:
Apple commence à vendre des recharges permettant de dépasser les limites d’utilisation de certains outils d’intelligence artificielle de Creator Studio. Petite particularité : elles ne garantissent pas un nombre fixe de requêtes.
Les quotas d’utilisation sont une règle commune à quasiment tous les chatbots et autres outils d’intelligence artificielle. Après un certain nombre de requêtes, le quota est épuisé et il faut sortir la carte bancaire pour acheter de nouveaux crédits d’utilisation. Apple s’était tenue jusqu’ici éloignée de cette règle, jusqu’à aujourd’hui. Avec ses « intelligence usage packs », Apple propose un nouveau passage en caisse pour prolonger l’utilisation de certaines fonctions. Le principe rappelle celui d’une recharge prépayée, avec un compteur nettement moins facile à lire que celui d’un forfait téléphonique.
Une rallonge de 49,99 dollars pour continuer à utiliser l’IA
Selon 9to5Mac, la dernière mise à jour de Logic Pro sur Mac propose désormais d’acheter de l’usage supplémentaire depuis le menu consacré aux fonctions d’intelligence artificielle. Un seul pack apparaît pour l’instant, au prix de 49,99 dollars aux États-Unis, mais aussi en France ou au Royaume-Uni.
L’achat est ponctuel et ne se renouvelle pas automatiquement. La réserve supplémentaire n’est entamée qu’une fois le quota mensuel inclus épuisé. Le solde peut être conservé d’un mois sur l’autre, mais expire douze mois après l’achat.
Apple précise en outre que cette recharge IA ne peut pas être incluse dans le partage familial. Même si vous utilisez Logic Pro avec cinq autres membres de votre groupe, il faudra que chacun paie 50 dollars pour profiter de tous les outils d’intelligence artificielle.
Logic Pro est la première application dans laquelle cette possibilité a été repérée. Apple poursuit parallèlement le déploiement des nouveaux assistants et outils IA de Creator Studio, annoncés fin octobre pour ses logiciels de création et sa suite bureautique. L’arrivée des packs dans les autres applications devra être vérifiée à mesure de leurs mises à jour.
Du crédit supplémentaire, sans quantité de travail garantie
Les conditions d’utilisation publiées par Apple apportent une autre précision : la consommation peut varier selon la fonction employée, la complexité du résultat demandé et la sollicitation des systèmes. Plus concrètement, une recharge ne garantit donc pas un nombre précis de réponses ou de créations. Rien d’original, c’est la même chose sur un ChatGPT ou un Claude, où le quota peut s’épuiser plus rapidement lors d’un travail exigeant.
Ce mode de fonctionnement complique toutefois l’évaluation du coût réel pour un utilisateur, qui paie déjà 12,99 € par mois pour avoir accès à Logic Pro ainsi qu’à toutes les apps comprises dans Apple Creator Studio. Avant de repasser à la caisse, difficile de savoir combien de temps la recharge permettra de travailler. Apple précise même que l’affichage du solde disponible peut être approximatif.
Ces premiers packs concernent uniquement la suite Apple Creator Studio. Pour le moment, Siri AI n’est pas concerné mais cela arrivera sans doute prochainement. Apple a déjà évoqué la création d'un accès payant étendu à certains de ses outils exécutés sur serveur pour les utilisateurs avancés.
Apple tire aujourd’hui plus d'un quart de ses revenus dans les services, et ne compte certainement pas s’arrêter en si bon chemin.

articles.title: Kalshi user who lost $308,000 on sports bets sues to get back $580,000
articles.text:
The big picture: Over eight weeks this summer, a Bellevue, Washington, man moved $315,353.94 into Kalshi through 253 separate bank debits, and the platform turned that money over in more than $14.3 million worth of trades on baseball games, tennis matches and other sporting events. When it was over, Scott Bright had lost $308,781.62, while Kalshi had kept $89,651.76 in fees. He is now suing to recover more than $580,000, and his case raises a hard question: is software that matches buyers and sellers of event contracts a federally regulated exchange, or an online casino that Washington law has banned?
Bright filed his complaint in September in King County Superior Court. Kalshi wants the case heard in the US District Court for the Western District of Washington. It filed a motion to dismiss the following month and has also asked the court to put the case on hold.
The complaint lays out the account's activity in detail. Between June and August 2026, Bright funded his Kalshi account through his checking account, and the platform allegedly charged $5,589.05 in funding fees on those transfers. He appears to have put his winnings straight back into new positions. That would explain why the trading volume ended up about 45 times larger than what he deposited.
Bright alleges that the platform ran his deposits through $14,396,457.30 in transactions and took $84,062.71 in trading fees along the way. That works out to 26.7% of everything he put in. When he stopped, $983.27 was left in the account.
Kalshi describes itself as "a neutral exchange platform" with no financial stake in how any event turns out. It makes its money from transaction fees. In its motion to dismiss, the company argued that Bright's positions were matched with other traders and settled on the real-world results, so his losses went to those counterparties, not to Kalshi. It also pointed out that the complaint never alleges that either KalshiEX or its parent, Kalshi Inc., was on the other side of any of his trades.
That neutrality claim runs into how the platform's market making works. Kalshi's rulebook says a trading affiliate supplies liquidity by placing orders on one or both sides of a market at competitive prices. Kalshi says the affiliate sees only the same public information as every other trader.
Bright alleges that the affiliate took the opposite side of many of his positions. If so, he argues, Kalshi was a player winning his money rather than a neutral venue. He admits he can't prove it from where he sits. "The identity of the participant on the opposite side of each of Plaintiff's positions, and the profit each such participant realized, is information exclusively within Kalshi's possession," the complaint says. That means the exchange's own order-matching records could end up deciding a key part of the case.
Bright's legal theory depends on state law. Washington has banned internet gambling since 2006. Under a much older statute, anyone who loses money at illegal gambling can sue to get it back from the operator who profited from the game.
Kalshi says that statute doesn't apply because what Bright traded were event contracts covered by the Commodity Exchange Act. In Kalshi's view, those contracts fall under the federal Commodity Futures Trading Commission, not state gambling regulators. The company also noted that Bright does not claim anyone misled him about how the platform worked, what it charged or the chance that a position might lose.
The federal appeals court that covers Washington has already weighed in on a similar question. In August, the Ninth Circuit ruled that Nevada can regulate Kalshi under its gambling laws, and Bright's complaint quotes that ruling's finding that "placing sports bets, even when called by another name, is still gambling."
The size of his demand stems from a 1950 Washington Supreme Court decision, Heitfeld v. Benevolent and Protective Order of Keglers. Bright argues that under the ruling, wins on separate events can't be netted against losses on others. Counting each event on its own gets him to $580,544.98. If the court rejects that method, Bright wants back everything he deposited plus all the fees, a total of just over $405,000.
Bright's trading happened before Washington managed to restrict the platform. The state attorney general had already sued Kalshi and is trying to recover all the money Washington residents lost on the platform. Kalshi tried to move that case to federal court, but it was sent back to King County in May. In August, a county judge granted a preliminary injunction that requires Kalshi to use geofencing and to stop offering contracts "related to sports, elections, politics, entertainment, culture, tech and science, or mentions" in Washington. Contracts on commodities, climate, economics and finance were not affected.
In mid-September, Bright tried to open the app and got a message saying "using this app in your current location is prohibited," according to his complaint.
Kalshi now wants Bright's case paused until the US Supreme Court decides whether to take up the broader dispute. New Jersey has asked the justices to rule on whether states can regulate the platform under gambling laws. Federal appeals courts have mostly sided with states so far, but not in every case. Kalshi told the federal court that a Supreme Court ruling would settle or simplify every claim and make sure similar lawsuits are treated the same way. It also noted that the state is pursuing the same theory, and seeking the same recovery for Bright, in its own case.

articles.title: Anthropic's Fable 5.2 One-Shots a Playable FPS Game in Just 8 Hours
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 10th 2026
Anthropic's Fable 5.2 One-Shots a Playable FPS Game in Just 8 Hours
The power of frontier AI models is increasing, and the gaming realm has already experienced what AI can do in terms of mods, changes, bug fixes, and many other aspects when a powerful model is put to work. Late last night, Anthropic released its most powerful frontier model, Fable 5.2, which brings the best intelligence from the company's offerings into an API. As a demonstration of this model's capabilities, we are seeing a relatively complex first-person shooter developed from scratch today. This includes models, sounds, and textures, all created by Fable 5.2. It took about eight hours, 445 million input tokens, and about 2.7 million output tokens, totaling around $550 if done through an API. The result is a game called "Saltline," which can be played entirely in a browser through Claude Artifact, a platform used to showcase creations.
Below you can find the "Saltline" game, where the objective is a simple mission to cut three relays while being constantly attacked by an army of robot dogs and drones. After completing the objective, the main character reaches a boat, and the mission is complete. While this is a very simple task, the fact that Fable 5.2 accomplished all of this from a prompt is an amazing achievement. It can deploy thousands of agents to get one thing done, and with better descriptions, it can perform tasks much closer to what you have imagined.For users interested in trying out "Saltline," there is a Claude Artifact available that you can use without a subscription as a demonstration of what the model is capable of. Additionally, if you want some modifications, you can create your own duplicate and ask Claude to add more features if you have a subscription. Quickly creating interesting games and modifying them at home might be the next big project for the gaming community, and the technology implementation is only getting easier. At this point, the power lies within one's imagination, as AI models can easily implement anything.

articles.title: Steam Deck performance gets a reality check with Valve's new FPS data
articles.text:
Since Valve announced its Steam Deck Verified program in 2021, players have found that a game’s “Verified” status doesn’t always match how well it actually runs on the handheld. Now, new Steam Deck frame rate data being shared by Valve itself can help players dig deeper into the performance they can expect from many Steam Deck games.
Valve has been collecting anonymized frame rate data from Steam players who opt in since February. Yesterday evening, the company announced it has started sharing that data on many Steam Store pages as averages and histograms for both the Steam Deck and Steam Deck OLED.
Valve acknowledges that players enabling VSync or frame rate limits can bias the collected data somewhat and that the measurements don’t account for custom in-game settings that Steam Deck users may tinker with to get a game running. Regardless, Valve says it has nonetheless “found that the framerate data consolidates around relatively narrow ranges.”
Beyond the badge
This kind of data can be extremely useful for distinguishing between the wide range of performance levels that can exist among “Verified” Steam Deck games. Both Cyberpunk 2077 and Skyrim: Special Edition earn the same Steam Deck Verified badge, for instance, but the former sees average Deck frame rates in the 30–40 FPS range, while the latter usually achieves 50–60 FPS on the hardware.
Valve’s frame rate data is even more useful for games that the company insists are “Unsupported” on Steam Deck because their “graphics setting cannot be configured to run well” on the hardware or because Valve is “still working on adding support for this game.” Despite warnings like these, games like Starfield, Silent Hill 2, and Assassin’s Creed Syndicate, to name just a few, all show extremely playable frame rates reported by actual Steam Deck users. Assassin’s Creed Syndicate in particular approaches a 60 FPS average on the Steam Deck OLED hardware despite its “Unsupported” status.

articles.title: Google lanza Gemini 4 Carbon para todos: así es su modelo más potente
articles.text:
Google ha anunciado el lanzamiento de Gemini 4 Carbon, la nueva versión de su IA que ya está disponible para desarrolladores, empresas, científicos y... usuarios en general, por lo que si eres usuario de la IA de la compañía, ya puedes probarlo. Hasta ahora, solo estaba disponible a través del Programa Fairwind y limitado para expertos en ciberseguridad.
Según Google, es la evolución de Argon, siendo mucho más potente, pero la compañía afirma que Gemini Argon continúa siendo la opción idónea para la gran mayoría de las tareas, sobre todo en lo que a ingeniería de software y conocimiento; siendo Carbon un modelo mejor diseñado para tareas que, según Google, "desafían los límites de la inteligencia de un modelo", especialmente en lo que se refiere a la programación y depuración complejas.
Respecto a los benchmarks del nuevo modelo, Gemini 4 Carbon ocupa el primer puesto en CursorBench 4.0, WANDR de Perplexity y AutomationBench de Zapier, y lo hace además con un coste por tarea mucho menor que el segundo modelo dentro del ranking, por lo que Google parece haber dado con la clave en cuanto a potencia y eficiencia.
Si hablamos de costes, Gemini 4 Carbon llega con el mismo precio (de momento promocional y por su lanzamiento) que Gemini 4 Argon: $2 por millón de tókenes de entrada y $10 por millón de tókenes de salida. Una vez finalizado este período promocional, pasará a costar $4 dólares por millón de tókenes de entrada y $20 dólares por millón de tókenes de salida. Además, Gemini 4 Carbon también estará disponible para todos los suscriptores de Google AI Ultra en Google Antigravity, la aplicación Gemini y el Modo IA en la Búsqueda.
Una cosa interesante de Gemini 4 Carbon son sus funcionalidades y capacidades extras de ciberseguridad, según Google, las mejores hasta la fecha, en especial en lo que se refiere a la seguridad de la inteligencia integral para el software crítico. Carbon lidera las principales evaluaciones comparativas en localización (SEC-bench Pro), explotación (ExploitGym) y corrección (CWE-bench v1) de vulnerabilidades. Es capaz de inspeccionar software, rastrear cómo pueden encadenarse los fallos a través de diferentes sistemas y generar parches verificados para subsanar la causa raíz.

articles.title: James-Webb-Teleskop: Warum einige „Little Red Dots“ älter sein könnten als die ersten Sterne
articles.text:
James-Webb-Rätsel um „Little Red Dots“: Stammen die frühen Schwarzen Löcher direkt aus dem Urknall?
Hinter einigen der sogenannten „Little Red Dots“ könnten primordiale Schwarze Löcher stecken, also urzeitliche Objekte aus den ersten Sekundenbruchteilen nach dem Urknall. Entdeckt wurden die kleinen roten Lichtpunkte mit dem James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop der US-Weltraumbehörde Nasa. Während gewöhnliche Schwarze Löcher erst aus ausgebrannten Sternen hervorgehen, hätten sich solche Urknall-Relikte noch vor dem ersten Stern direkt aus verdichteter Materie gebildet.
Wie diese Objekte heranwachsen konnten, zeigen Modellrechnungen im Fachjournal Physical Review Letters. Beteiligt waren Wissenschaftler:innen der Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore im US-Bundesstaat Maryland, des dortigen Space Telescope Science Institute und der italienischen Universität Padua. Demnach könnte ein anfangs leichteres Schwarzes Loch über Jahrmillionen hinweg Gas angezogen haben, auch wenn die Studie noch keinen Beobachtungsbeweis liefert.
Abell 2744-QSO1: Ein Schwarzes Loch ohne passende Heimatgalaxie
Als Prüfstein diente den Forscher:innen das rund 13,1 Milliarden Lichtjahre entfernte Objekt Abell 2744-QSO1 aus einer Zeit etwa 700 Millionen Jahre nach dem Urknall. Sichtbar wird diese ferne Quelle, weil die Schwerkraft eines vorgelagerten Galaxienhaufens ihr Licht wie eine Lupe verstärkt und dreifach abbildet. Im Zentrum kreist Gas um ein Schwarzes Loch von rund 50 Millionen Sonnenmassen, das mindestens doppelt so schwer ist wie alle umliegenden Sterne zusammen. Ermittelt hat diesen Wert ein Team um den Astrophysiker Ignas Juodžbalis von der britischen Universität Cambridge in einer Untersuchung, die auf der Forschungsplattform Arxiv nachgelesen werden kann.
Im heutigen Universum erreicht ein zentrales Schwarzes Loch üblicherweise nur etwa ein Tausendstel der Sternmasse seiner Heimatgalaxie. Zudem besteht die Umgebung von Abell 2744-QSO1 fast nur aus Wasserstoff und Helium, während schwerere Elemente nahezu fehlen. Solche schwereren Stoffe entstehen erst im Inneren von Sternen und bei deren Explosionen, weshalb dort zuvor kaum Sterne gelebt haben können.
Stephen Hawkings Urknall-Theorie im Härtetest der Kosmologie
Um dieses Missverhältnis zu klären, griffen die Studienautor:innen eine Idee auf, die der britische Physiker Stephen Hawking in den 1970er-Jahren formuliert hatte. Demnach waren manche Materieansammlungen kurz nach dem Urknall so dicht, dass sie durch ihre Schwerkraft direkt zu Schwarzen Löchern kollabierten. „Sie entstammen der Physik des frühen Universums noch vor den ersten Sternen, als sich der Kosmos in Raum und Zeit exponentiell ausdehnte“, erklärt Studienautor Valerio De Luca laut einer Mitteilung der Johns Hopkins University.
In ihren Berechnungen schlossen die Forscher:innen zunächst aus, dass solche Urzeit-Löcher schon bei ihrer Geburt Millionen Sonnenmassen wogen. Derart große Materieverdichtungen hätten messbare Spuren in der kosmischen Hintergrundstrahlung hinterlassen, dem noch heute empfangbaren Strahlungsecho aus der Frühzeit des Alls. Da Satellitendaten keine solchen Abweichungen zeigen, durften primordiale Schwarze Löcher anfangs höchstens etwa 1.000 Sonnenmassen erreichen.
Auch ein zweiter Weg, bei dem tausende dieser leichteren Schwarzen Löcher schrittweise miteinander verschmelzen, scheitert in fast allen Modellvarianten. Kollidieren zwei Schwarze Löcher, erzeugen sie Gravitationswellen in der Raumzeit, die dem verschmolzenen Objekt oft einen starken Rückstoß versetzen. Dieser Stoß schleudert das wachsende Schwarze Loch fort, sofern es nicht von einer besonders schweren Wolke aus Dunkler Materie festgehalten wird. Solche massereichen Wolken waren im frühen Kosmos jedoch zu selten, um die hohe beobachtete Zahl der „Little Red Dots“ zu erklären.
Wachsende Schwarze Löcher und das fehlende Röntgenlicht der „Little Red Dots“
Tragfähig blieb in den Simulationen allein ein dritter Pfad: Ein rund 1.000 Sonnenmassen schweres Urzeit-Loch zieht über hunderte Millionen Jahre hinweg Wasserstoff- und Heliumgas an. Das einströmende Gas sammelt sich in einer rotierenden Scheibe und lässt das Schwarze Loch bis auf die bei Abell 2744-QSO1 gemessenen 50 Millionen Sonnenmassen wachsen. Voraussetzung ist allerdings, dass sich in dieser Gasscheibe kaum neue Sterne bilden, weil sonst jene schwereren Elemente entstünden, die dort fehlen.
Dieses Wachstumsmodell erklärt zugleich, warum die „Little Red Dots“ anders als gewöhnliche wachsende Schwarze Löcher kaum Röntgenstrahlung aussenden. Normalerweise heizt sich einströmendes Gas kurz vor dem Verschlucken stark auf und sendet Röntgenlicht aus, dessen Druck weiteren Nachschub bremst. Stürzt jedoch in kurzer Zeit besonders viel Materie ein, bläht sich die innere Gasscheibe auf und schluckt die Röntgenstrahlung, bevor sie entweichen kann.
Warum für primordiale Schwarze Löcher weiter jeder Nachweis fehlt
Auch wenn das Modell rechnerisch aufgeht, liefert die bereits im Juni 2026 erschienene Studie keinen Beweis dafür, dass primordiale Schwarze Löcher existieren. Die Rechnung setzt eine stark gebremste Sternentstehung voraus, und viele der rund 100 katalogisierten „Little Red Dots“ dürften ohnehin gewöhnliche Schwarze Löcher enthalten. „Die Tür für diese Theorie, dass Little Red Dots primordiale Schwarze Löcher sein könnten, stand offen“, ordnet Mitautor Loris Del Grosso das Ergebnis ein. Die Studie habe diese Tür lediglich ein Stück weiter geöffnet, indem sie zeige, welche Szenarien wahrscheinlicher seien als andere.
Zudem konkurriert die Urknall-Hypothese mit Erklärungen, die ohne Relikte aus den ersten Sekundenbruchteilen auskommen. So beschreibt ein Team um den Astronomen Rohan Naidu vom Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge im US-Bundesstaat Massachusetts in einer Facharbeit zu „Schwarzloch-Sternen“ jüngere Schwarze Löcher in dichten Gashüllen. Ebenso könnten später im jungen Kosmos große Gaswolken direkt kollabiert sein, wie der Astrophysiker Fabio Pacucci von der US-amerikanischen Harvard University in einer Modellstudie untersucht hat. Um primordiale Schwarze Löcher eindeutig zu belegen, müssten Astronom:innen erst ein Objekt finden, das nachweislich vor den ersten Sternen entstand oder leichter ist als jeder kollabierte Stern.

articles.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google is notching up its chipmaking game as the company seeks to reduce its dependence on chips made by other companies for its cloud computing business. Google on Monday unveiled two new variants of its tensor processing units (TPUs), in-house-developed chips meant for AI workloads, that broaden its chip portfolio to additional use cases: confidential inference and more memory capacity for large workloads.
The new units, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, are part of the company’s eighth generation of chips introduced in April this year, and build on what those chips offered, which was more inference capacity and support for large training requirements.
TPU 8tx, designed with AMD, is based on the TPU 8t chip, and is geared specifically for confidentially training and running AI models, Google said in a blog post. The chip “builds security directly into the hardware layer, keeping sensitive data and model weights protected and isolated even while in active use,” the company wrote.
The chip also has a custom inferencing network that lets it run reasoning alongside training, so it can be used to distill and train small models on the fly. That ability, according to Google, could prove useful for cases where a company might want to train a model on its proprietary data without having to move the data between devices.
Meanwhile, TPU 8i Max basically combines two of the inference-focused TPU 8i chips the company launched in April, doubling the memory capacity, processing power and bandwidth, but in a single package. The result is a chip that lets AI models handle a larger range of information during queries.
The chip launch comes as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and even AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are working on their own lines of AI-specific semiconductors and accompanying software in order to reduce their reliance on the dominance of Nvidia.
The news also comes at a particularly vulnerable moment for Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend admitted to having an affair with someone alleged to be a Chinese spy.

articles.title: I tested Ninja’s spill-proof Belgian Waffle Maker in the name of consumer research — and ended up eating my body weight in desserts
articles.text:
I fell in love with Ninja’s genius Belgian Waffle Maker, and now I have a serious, out-of-control waffle problem
Seriously, send help. I’m now 56% waffle
For years, I’ve been envious of folks in the US as they’ve had access to a kitchen gadget I desperately wanted here in the UK. But the envy has turned to glee, as the Ninja Belgian Waffle Maker has finally made it to British shores, three long years after its US debut.
What initially attracted me to this particular waffle maker was its apparent simplicity. Instead of the traditional horizontal pan, Ninja has given the humble waffle iron a 90 degree spin, standing it vertically with a spout at the top for you to pour batter in.
Pour, select your shade level (one thorough five, depending on how dark you like your waffle), and wait. Waffles in an instant. It sounded almost too easy, and for $99.99 / £99.99, it’s not exactly going to break the bank — although it’s still on the pricier end of the waffle iron market. It’s no doubt an indulgent purchase.
So I’ve finally managed to get my hands on it, and in the name of consumer research, have eaten an awful lot of waffles to determine whether the Ninja Belgian Waffle Maker can live up to my heady expectations. Spoiler - I can’t stop eating these damn waffles. So yeah, it’s pretty good.
Stand up
Another good thing about Ninja’s decision to go vertical is it saves on counter space. At 6.5 x 9.25 inches / 16.5 x 23.5cm, its footprint is small, allowing you to tuck it away in a corner or slide it into a cupboard when not in use. Plus, at 5.7lbs / 2.6kg, it’s easy to move and lift. It stands just 11.9 inches / 30.2cm high too, so it really isn’t taking up much space.
Ninja includes a handy 'Inspiration Guide' in the box, with a few batter recipes, plus its Precision Pour Cup so you get the right amount of batter each time. If you find yourself needing another one of these cups, they’re currently available in the US for $17.99 (around £14). There's no word yet on whether we’ll get the same option to buy replacements in the UK.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Whipping up my first batch of batter using Ninja’s classic recipe, and my mouth is already watering. I’ve got my M&Ms, freshly sliced bananas, nutella, cream and chocolate sauce at the ready. The guide suggests setting the shade dial to three (bang in the middle), which I think is a fair shout as it’ll help get a gauge on how toasted things get.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
I need to let the waffle maker warm up first - the red light will switch to green when it’s ready to add the batter. After around two minutes, the light changes and I get an audible beep signifying we’re ready to pour.
I carefully tip some of the batter into the cup (the recipe reckons I’ve got enough for four to five waffles), and then pour it through the spout at the top of the iron. By what I can only assume is pure witchcraft, the batter doesn’t leak out the bottom.
Now I wait. I close my eyes, hoping for waffly goodness, as the batter sizzles away inside. After a little over four minutes the light changes again and I get the beep I’ve been so eager to hear. It’s waffle time. I press the release button on the side of the waffle maker and gently open the iron up to its horizontal position.
Success! Sort of. I followed the instructions to use three quarters of a cup of batter initially. The result? Three quarters of a waffle. Wonderfully cooked, but I'm a hungry boy.
We go again
We go again, this time on level 4 as I'd like a touch more bite to my waffle, and a cup full to the brim with batter goes into the waffle maker when the preheat buzzer chimes.
I wait, patiently, and I’m rewarded with perfection. I’ve got a whole waffle, with a little bit of excess where the batter has risen up the spout. I cut this off and snack on it while adding my toppings. The waffle itself is light and airy, and wonderfully cooked.
It’s not enough though. I return to the kitchen, turn the shade level all the way up to five — I’ve got to be thorough — and pour another cup of batter into the machine. A few more minutes tick by, and we’re ready.
This time the waffle is a bit browner, thanks to the higher setting. It’s still perfectly pleasant, but my personal preference certainly lies at level four.
And there’s more good news. The waffle leaves very little in the way of mess on the waffle maker, meaning clean-up is super easy. Once it’s cooled down, grab a damp cloth and give it a quick wipe and you’re done. Simple, quick cleaning is my kind of cleaning.
And remember to use silicon tipped tongs to remove the waffle. Don’t use anything metal as it will damage the nano-ceramic cooking surface.
Mixing it up
So the Ninja Belgian Waffle Maker can make excellent, classic waffles. Thank goodness really, because if it didn’t we’d have a serious issue. But sometimes a standard waffle doesn’t cut it.
There are times I must up my waffle game. Give me flavor, I bellow across the kitchen to no one in particular. The cat doesn’t even bother to look up. Thanks mate.
Because I’m a bit of a sugar sicko, I have a penchant for M&Ms in my waffles when I visit certain dessert establishments who play to my whims. Unfortunately, the Ninja Belgian Waffle Maker won’t put up with that.
This is strictly a liquid only waffle iron. No solids allowed in the batter. I can understand why — solids will likely clog the top of the iron, making it difficult for the batter to make its way evenly down. A shame, but by no means a deal breaker.
So instead I opt to try out the cake batter method. I've got a box of Betty Crocker red velvet cake mix in the cupboard. Adding some oil, eggs and water, and I've got a silky red batter ready to roll.
Ninja's booklet suggestions to set the shade to level one. I dutifully comply, wait for it to get to temperature, add the batter, and wait. I was skeptical about how well this method would work, but the batter rose and cooked.
The result? Essentially, a waffle-shaped cake, fluffy and soft. If you’ve got kids and they’re demanding cake, this is possibly the quickest way to answer their calls. Tasty, yes, but I have a hankering for waffles.
So back I return to the classic batter, but this time I’m infusing it with lemon peel and juice, for a tangy, refreshing finish. Excellent. I make more batter, adding apple sauce and cinnamon to the mix for another taste sensation. The flavors you can add extend as far as your imagination. Whether sweet or savory, the Ninja Belgian Waffle Maker complied.
Send help
Would I recommend the Ninja Belgian Waffle Maker? Absolutely. It delivers on the promise of easy, quick, and delicious waffles. So long as you make a good batter and pour in the correct amount, you can’t go wrong.
Is it a must buy? Well, it’s certainly not as versatile as an air fryer, it does just make waffles. Sure there are cheaper options on the market, but as far as indulgent purchases go, for waffles fans it feels like a home run. The only trouble is, I can’t seem to stop eating them.
