articles.title: Anthropic was going to rent power for its data centers, then decided to spend $3.4 billion buying the generators
articles.text:
The big picture: AI companies usually rent their power rather than own the machines that generate it. Anthropic was planning such a deal with a supplier in Texas, too. But the Claude maker reportedly scrapped that plan and went after the supplier's generators instead. It agreed to pay roughly $3.4 billion to take them over. That's enough gas-fired equipment to produce 1.7 gigawatts of power.
The deal makes it the largest known purchase of power-generation gear by any AI lab, according to the Financial Times. Anthropic signed the agreement back in late September with San Antonio-based supplier OnePWR Solutions. OnePWR had ordered the generators from Caterpillar about two years earlier, but it was still short on the financing needed to complete the purchase.
Along with the hardware, the company picked up the engineering and construction work needed to install it. It didn't buy OnePWR itself, though, so none of the supplier's staff moved over.
Because those orders were already sitting in Caterpillar's production schedule, the generators should start arriving soon, with deliveries continuing over the next two years. The FT notes they were also ordered before generator prices started climbing, so Anthropic may have locked in older pricing as well.
Placing a fresh order today would likely mean waiting years longer. That's because turbine makers can only build an estimated 60 to 70 GW of capacity annually. Global orders, meanwhile, have reportedly blown past 100 GW. That's why some new US orders are already being pushed out to 2030 or 2031.
The grid isn't much help either, since hooking up a new data center can take up to seven years. Some developers have even resorted to running old jet engines on site.
Elon Musk's xAI, for one, spent $2 billion on mobile gas turbines earlier this year to keep its data centers running. Anthropic actually rents computing capacity from xAI's parent company, SpaceX – a bill that's expected to hit $3.1 billion a month by the end of the year. The entire generator deal costs only a little more than one month of that rent.
Running all those generators will take a lot of gas, though. The company's IPO filing, made public last month, already warned that competing with hyperscalers for the same supply and pipelines could increase fuel prices. For now, there's no word on where the generators will actually end up.

articles.title: One space station company sues another for copying its work
articles.text:
In this long exposure shot, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket soars upward after lifting off from NASA Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39A in Florida on May 21, 2023, for the Axiom Mission 2 to the International Space Station.
Credit:
NASA/Cory S Huston
In this long exposure shot, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket soars upward after lifting off from NASA Kennedy Space Center’s Launch Complex 39A in Florida on May 21, 2023, for the Axiom Mission 2 to the International Space Station.
Credit:
NASA/Cory S Huston
NASA’s competition for the development of private space stations that will take flight in the 2030s is already nearing crunch time. But a recently unsealed lawsuit may spice things up even further.
The lawsuit involves two of the most prominent companies in this competition, Houston-based Axiom Space and Long Beach, California-based Vast Space. And it is surfacing as final proposals for private space stations are due from companies to the US space agency a little more than one month from today, on December 14.
According to the court filings unsealed by a November 4 order from US District Judge Charles Eskridge, Axiom is pursuing a False Claims Act case against Vast in which Axiom accuses Vast of presenting NASA with a fraudulent mission-planning document that incorporates Axiom’s proprietary information.
“Axiom Space filed this false-claims action on behalf of the government because public-private partnerships in human spaceflight depend on candor, capability, original work, and integrity,” an Axiom Space spokesperson told Ars. “Presenting another company’s hard-won experience as its own does not meet that standard.”
In response, Vast said the lawsuit was about competition, not fraud.
“NASA opened private astronaut missions to more than one provider because competition drives innovation, delivers better value for taxpayers, and keeps America leading in space,” a Vast spokesperson said. “Misusing litigation against a competitor works against all of that.”
About Private Astronaut Missions
So what happened? Let’s unpack this further to understand what we do and don’t know at this point.
The dispute revolves around a program called Private Astronaut Missions, launched in 2019, through which NASA allows private companies to organize missions of up to four astronauts to visit the International Space Station. The missions are part of NASA’s effort to increase commercial activity in low-Earth orbit and allow private companies to gain some operational experience as they develop their own commercial space stations. As such, these missions are viewed by some as a stepping stone toward private station contracts with NASA.
Axiom became the early leader in the program, winning contracts to organize the first four private missions. The first, Axiom-1, launched in April 2022, while the most recent, Axiom-4, launched to the International Space Station in the summer of 2025. Then, in January, NASA awarded the fifth private astronaut mission to Axiom, followed by the sixth to Vast Space in February and the seventh to Voyager Technologies in April.
As part of these agreements, private companies generally purchase mission services from NASA, including food, storage, and other supplies. In return, NASA buys the capability to return scientific samples to Earth that must remain cold during transit.
The private astronaut mission agreements include contractual deliverables that providers must submit for NASA’s review. According to Axiom’s lawsuit, one such deliverable under its contracts is a Mission Integration and Operations Management Plan, or MIOMP, essentially the operational blueprint for the entire mission. Axiom alleges that Vast’s contract contains a similar requirement and that NASA’s acceptance of the document is a condition for a milestone payment.
What triggered the lawsuit?
According to the lawsuit filed by Axiom, prior to June 3, Vast submitted its mission-planning document for the private astronaut mission to NASA. Then, on June 3, NASA notified Axiom “that its sensitive information had been improperly included in a deliverable submitted by Vast.”
On page 11 of the Axiom lawsuit, the company alleges: “NASA advised that Vast’s submission in some locations substituted ‘the PAM Provider’ for Axiom’s name, while in other instances retained Axiom’s name and company details instead of replacing it with Vast’s name. That the document retained residual references to Axiom in certain sections demonstrates that the underlying text originated with Axiom and was not independently authored by Vast.”
Axiom said its mission planning documents are “sensitive and proprietary” information. These documents represent years of work and significant investment, a company spokesperson said.
“A Mission Integration and Operations Management Plan is not paperwork,” the Axiom spokesperson said. “It is the document that demonstrates to NASA the company understands and can execute every step required to keep a crew safe from launch to return. When human lives depend on a plan, the company submitting it must have developed it, understood it, and be able to stand behind it.”
What has happened since
Axiom filed a lawsuit in a Houston federal court, where the company is based, on June 19. The False Claims Act complaint seeks civil penalties, treble damages, litigation costs, and a statutory whistleblower award.
There are plenty of unanswered questions at this point. Principal among them is how Vast obtained Axiom’s planning document and how it was inserted into Vast’s submission to NASA.
What does seem notable is that Axiom sued under the False Claims Act rather than bringing a conventional trade-secret misappropriation case. The False Claims Act imposes a demanding burden of proving fraud against the government, but successful cases can produce substantial civil penalties and damages. A finding of fraud could also complicate Vast’s ability to compete for future NASA contracts, potentially including the commercial space station competition.
Additionally, by filing a False Claims Act case in federal court and essentially framing the issue as one of fraud against NASA, Axiom triggered a federal review that gave the US Department of Justice the opportunity to investigate the allegations and decide whether to take over prosecution. However, the Department of Justice declined to intervene on October 23, according to the court documents. Axiom is therefore pursuing the allegations independently.
“The Department of Justice’s decision not to intervene does not mean that what happened was acceptable,” the Axiom spokesperson told Ars.
However, Vast officials said the government’s decision not to intervene reflects the merits of the case.
“The Department of Justice reviewed Axiom’s allegations and declined to intervene,” the spokesperson said. “We think that decision speaks for itself. Axiom’s complaint does not describe a fraud on the government, and it does not meet the basic requirements of the False Claims Act.”
The Justice Department’s decision does not establish whether Vast improperly used Axiom’s materials. In False Claims Act cases, federal prosecutors may decline to intervene for a variety of reasons, including doubts about the case’s legal merits, the availability of evidence, or the potential recovery. The government provided no explanation for its decision in the court filing. Axiom remains free to pursue the lawsuit on its own.
And the company appears poised to do so. Vast said it would defend itself “vigorously” in legal proceedings. The company also said its work with NASA on the sixth Private Astronaut Mission—for which customers have already been announced—is proceeding without difficulty or interruption.
The timing is important
NASA now finds itself the central witness in a case involving two of the leading companies chasing private space station contracts that could ultimately be worth billions of dollars. Other potential contenders include Voyager, Blue Origin, and possibly SpaceX.
The agency declined to provide a substantive comment for this article. “NASA is aware of the matter but does not comment on litigation,” agency spokesman George Alderman told Ars.
The commercial space stations program, which dates back half a decade, has been a rough-and-tumble contest as private companies have jostled for favor with NASA. Ultimately, the space agency is expected to pick only a few winners to finish their space stations in low-Earth orbit and pay handsomely for NASA astronauts to visit there in the 2030s.
At times, this contest has turned personal. In September 2025, for example, far-right political activist Laura Loomer shared an in-depth post on the social media site X purporting to link Vast chief executive Max Haot, who was born in Belgium, and Vast with Chinese interests. These allegations, which raised national security concerns, were wholly unsubstantiated. A recent Washington Post investigation reported that Loomer has received payments for some political posts on X.
It is also not the only lawsuit Axiom has filed this year. In April, after policy advisor Ramzi Masri-Elyafaoui left the company to work for rival Vast, Axiom sued to stop him, alleging he violated a non-compete agreement. In June, a Houston federal judge dismissed the case with prejudice.
Eric Berger is the senior space editor at Ars Technica, covering everything from astronomy to private space to NASA policy, and author of two books: Liftoff, about the rise of SpaceX; and Reentry, on the development of the Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon. A certified meteorologist, Eric lives in Houston.

articles.title: Cloudflare Makes Basin Serverless Analytics Generally Available
articles.text:
Cloudflare has announced the general availability of Basin, a serverless analytics platform built on Apache Iceberg and R2 Object Storage. The managed service supports open data formats and integrates with tools such as DuckDB, Snowflake, and Apache Spark, with no data egress fees.
Introduced in preview as "Cloudflare Data Platform" just over a year ago, Basin combines data ingestion and SQL-based transformation, managed table maintenance, and distributed SQL queries, allowing developers to analyze large datasets without managing infrastructure. Marc Selwan, senior product manager at Cloudflare, and Micah Wylde, principal engineer at Cloudflare, explain why eliminating egress costs is central to the design:
A large driving force in the development and adoption of Basin is the continued growth we are seeing in the open Apache Iceberg ecosystem. (...) With Basin, you can read and write your data using any Iceberg-compatible engine, including PyIceberg, DuckDB, Snowflake, and Apache Spark. That kind of data portability is only possible with free egress, which allows developers to access their data in Cloudflare from the wide variety of tools in the ecosystem, regardless of region or cloud.
The platform combines three services: Basin Pipelines, formerly Cloudflare Pipelines, ingests events from Workers, HTTP endpoints, and Logpush, applies SQL transformations, and writes data to Apache Iceberg tables or R2; Basin Catalog manages Iceberg metadata and automates table maintenance; and Basin SQL provides a serverless, distributed SQL engine for querying Iceberg tables.
Basin aims to make analytics more accessible to smaller teams by running data ingestion, preparation, and queries on Cloudflare’s global network. This reduces the need to manage server clusters or move data between services, lowering the operational overhead of building and maintaining analytics pipelines. Selwan and Wylde explain the renaming:
Why Basin? A basin is where rivers from many sources come together to a single point. We felt that Basin perfectly captures how the platform is used: Pipelines brings data into Basin Catalog while Basin SQL makes it instantly queryable.
While some practitioners describe Basin as "open analytics infrastructure without the warehouse cathedral," Ramin Muradov, lead data analyst at PashaPay , comments:
I don't think it will knock Snowflake off its spot, at least not anytime soon. Cloudflare itself says Basin isn't a replacement for every warehouse workload. But there's a big layer of the market made up of teams whose data is too small to justify dedicated infrastructure and too big to fit in Excel. They now have an option.
Cloudflare is not the only cloud provider targeting unified analytics: as separately reported on InfoQ, AWS recently acquired DuckLabs and integrated DuckDB into Aurora PostgreSQL, aiming to simplify analytics across transactional and object storage data, while Google repositioned over the years BigQuery as the "single, unified AI-ready data platform."
Since its preview, Basin has increased ingestion capacity to 3 GB/s per stream, expanded SQL capabilities, improved Iceberg table maintenance, and added Logpush integration and Terraform support. Planned features, with no committed release dates, include real-time processing capabilities, support for the latest Iceberg specification, adaptive table-maintenance, and additional controls for data sovereignty and access management.
Cloudflare's Basin tutorial explains how to ingest events with Basin Pipelines, store them in Iceberg tables managed by Basin Catalog, and query them using Basin SQL.

articles.title: Las ventas de 'GTA 6' han sido más bestiales de lo que Take-Two esperaba: "Los números hablarán por sí solos"
articles.text:
Entramos en la recta final hacia el lanzamiento de GTA 6 y el panorama no podría ser más prometedor para sus responsables. Con expectativas tan altas detrás del juego, Take-Two Interactive ha confirmado que la preventa ha sido todavía más exitosa de lo que se esperaba.
En la más reciente presentación de sus resultados financieros, la casa matriz de Rockstar Games fue determinante en tal sentido. La compañía indicó que las reservas de GTA 6 han sido muy superiores a lo que estimaban inicialmente. Y si bien puede sonar un tanto vago, es una perspectiva bastante interesante pensando en el desempeñó que logrará el título cuando llegue al mercado.
"Las reservas de Grand Theft Auto VI están muy por encima de nuestras expectativas iniciales y sabemos que, dentro de poco, las cifras hablarán por sí solas", indicaron desde Take-Two Interactive en su presentación financiera. Como complemento, Strauss Zelnick, CEO de la firma, remarcó que la preventa de GTA 6 está alcanzando "niveles sin precedentes".
Por lo pronto, los dueños de Rockstar Games no indican datos precisos sobre cuánto dinero ha generado el juego, ni cuántas copias digitales se han vendido hasta la fecha. Aun así, todo apunta a que los números serán bestiales.
GTA 6 habría generado más de 750 millones de dólares antes de su lanzamiento, según cifras extraoficiales
Según estimaciones extraoficiales, GTA 6 habría generado unos 750 millones de dólares en reservas hasta principios de la semana pasada. Datos de Sensor Tower apuntaban a que ya se habían vendido más de 7,7 millones del nuevo juego de Rockstar Games. De ser ciertas, es lógico pensar que ambas cifras ya han quedado totalmente desactualizadas.
Es importante recordar que a principios de 2025 ya existían estimaciones que hablaban de que GTA 6 podría generar unos 1.000 millones de dólares durante la etapa de reservas. Las cifras que se han divulgado hasta ahora de forma no oficial parecen ir por la misma vía.
Hoy, martes 10 de noviembre, GTA 6 ha iniciado su etapa de precarga tanto en Xbox Series X|S como en PlayStation 5. Esto significa que los compradores del juego ya pueden instalarlo en su consola, pero los archivos están cifrados e inaccesibles hasta el próximo 19 de noviembre, cuando se produzca su debut formal.
Es lógico pensar que con la descarga anticipada en marcha, las ventas de GTA 6 continuarán disparándose con notoriedad. Además, Rockstar espera que las versiones en "físico" del juego comiencen a estar disponibles en cadenas minoristas a partir de este jueves 12 de noviembre. Todavía es un misterio cuánto puede aportar este formato a las ventas generales del juego, considerando que la caja no trae un disco, sino un código de descarga.

articles.title: N-able takes its remote access service offline after researcher publishes dozens of zero-day bugs | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Remote access company N-able has confirmed it took down its cloud-hosted offering to fix a slew of security vulnerabilities that were published online this week, giving the company no advance notice to fix them.
In a status update on its website, the company said its hosted N-Central offering for customers is now offline “while we take the necessary actions to secure the environments and implement appropriate remediation.” The company also urged customers to take down their own self-hosted deployments of N-Central, fearing that attackers could use the publicly disclosed exploits to hack into customer networks.
N-able said during this time customers will not be able to use their N-Central service, which allows corporate customers to remotely access and manage other devices and systems on the same network. Remote access technologies are a frequent target of hackers, as these systems can grant vast access to a company’s network and internal data.
Security researcher Ben Bales released the “zero-day” bugs on GitHub on Sunday. In a post on X, Bales dubbed the bugs Able2Shell, describing them as a mix of vulnerabilities capable of stealing credentials, creating new administrative accounts, and gaining root access to affected N-able systems.
Bales told Bleeping Computer that he publicly released the bugs as the company allegedly failed to patch the flaws reported in a different product.
N-able said that it has no evidence of successful exploitation against any of its customer environments. A spokesperson for the company did not respond to a request for comment about whether it has the ability to check, such as server logs, or if it has no way to check.

articles.title: PitchBook opens its platform to startups for free and debuts Origin deal sourcing service - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
PitchBook opens its platform to startups for free and debuts Origin deal sourcing service
Private markets data provider PitchBook Data Inc. today opened its platform to startups for free at Web Summit in Lisbon.
Those that sign up have to share their financials. Some of that information will reach investors through the company’s new deal sourcing service, PitchBook Origin.
The launches come as more startups than ever are landing a first round. In the U.S., the 2021 record for first-time financings had already fallen by the end of September, PitchBook and the National Venture Capital Association found in their latest Venture Monitor report.
PitchBook credits artificial intelligence with part of that growth, since the technology has made companies easier to start. AI tools have also compressed investor diligence from weeks to days. Sourcing has not kept pace, the company argues, particularly where the signals are not public.
Free access for startups runs through a program called PitchBook for Startups. Founders who have bootstrapped or raised only from angels, grants or accelerators qualify as long as they are now seeking a first institutional round and can show at least a mockup of their product.
Once a startup has handed over its financials and details on its leadership team and product, its founders can use the PitchBook platform to research which firms are actively writing checks in their sector and stage. Investor research tops PitchBook’s own list of what founders can do with the access.
That founder data lands in a much bigger pool on the Origin side, where coverage starts at about 25 million companies and 250 million people profiles. Bootstrapped businesses and companies that have not yet raised money or announced what they are building are part of that count, and some 15 million of the companies are new to PitchBook.
Third-party data enrichment and PitchBook’s own machine learning models supply part of the coverage. PitchBook said it has not had founder-verified data at scale before.
Each company gets a score, and investors can tune relevance filters to their own criteria. Real-time alerts, saved searches and customer relationship management integrations are meant to replace the manual monitoring that deal teams do now.
Chief Solutions Officer Paul Santarelli said the missing piece for investors has been visibility into “the stage before a company raises, when the most important signals are the hardest to see.” Every company that joins the startup program and contributes verified information sharpens that picture, he said.
PitchBook “was once a startup itself, working to get in front of the right backers,” President and Chief Operating Officer Rod Diefendorf said. Founded in 2007, the Seattle company now serves more than 100,000 clients worldwide. Morningstar Inc. has owned it since 2016.
Startups can apply for the program now. Origin is available as a standalone product or as an add-on to the main PitchBook platform.

articles.title: France accuses Iran of supermarket freezer hacking, slams 'the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory'
articles.text:
France accuses Iran of supermarket freezer hacking, slams 'the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory'
France calls attack 'an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness'
- France blames Iran for recent cyberattacks against supermarket freezers
- October 2026 attack saw food ruined and multiple fires across France
- Iran denies involvement, but France orders its ambassador to Paris to explain
The French government has accused Iran of being behind the recent cyberattacks which hit freezers in supermarkets across Europe.
More than 700 grocery stores were affected by the attack in October 2026, spoiling food and even causing fires as fridges and freezers saw their temperatures hiked up to over 50C.
France has now laid the blame for the attack at the Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), saying the incident was "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression".
Iran blamed for attacks
“This is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory,” France’s Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot said.
He added that the incident, "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".
The attacks affected French supermarket chains Casino, Leclerc, Coopérative U, Metro, Carrefour, and Intermarché groups, with food losses estimated in the tens of millions of euros, a report by France’s Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre (C4) found.
The attacks were followed by a second incident a few days later, with supermarkets in other European countries hit, before a third attack saw French blood plasma reserves targeted.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The latter incident saw Coolworld, which supplies the French Blood Establishment (EFS), targeted. The EFS is responsible for collecting, preparing and distributing blood and blood products in France, many of which are used in essential surgeries and medical operations.
Fortunately, the cyberattack did not result in any serious operational consequences because the temperature spikes were noticed quickly and corrected.
Iranian hacking groups such as the IRGC have been blamed for several high-profile cyberattacks in recent months, many of which have targeted industrial facilities and systems.
This includes a UK power generation plant being taken offline for several days in August 2026, and in the same month, more than 30 Minnesota water utilities were hit in a coordinated attack blamed on Iranian-affiliated actors.
“The Iranian cyber threat against French interests is not new,” the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs added. “Iran has already carried out several destabilizing acts against us, notably targeting the weekly magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and the organization of the Paris Olympic Games in 2024.”
Barrot said the French government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".
Iran has yet to respond officially, but some Iranian media outlets have dismissed the allegations as baseless.

articles.title: Steam Store adds average FPS data so you can see game performance before making a purchase — Steam Deck only for now, with desktop PC support planned
articles.text:
Steam Store adds average FPS data so you can see game performance before making a purchase — Steam Deck only for now, with desktop PC support planned
The current feature is a beta and only available for Steam Deck, but it's coming to all users eventually.
Valve is adding framerate telemetry data to games so you can see what your hardware will manage in a given game before you buy it. The new initiative will start with the Steam Deck, but Valve has promised to bring the feature to more hardware in the future, presumably not only its Steam Machine but desktop gaming PCs more generally. The new feature shows players' average FPS on Steam Deck while playing the title, so customers can decide whether to invest without risking a purchase.
Valve already added the option to insert your hardware specifications when you write a review for a game, but an extremely small fraction of players actually write reviews, and from looking at reviews on recent Steam games, it seems like an even smaller fraction actually select to include their hardware specifications, for whatever reason.
So this is a pretty interesting idea, not least because Valve is debuting it for the Steam Deck first. Notably, the framerate data Valve is using is sourced from users who opted into sharing this data, so there's no privacy concern here. It appears to be as simple as it sounds: Valve will capture your performance while playing a game on the Steam Deck, and then show that performance to other users—anonymously, of course.
The clever among you may have realized "but wait, PC games have settings you can adjust, so even the same hardware might deliver really different performance levels." Correct! And it's also exactly why Valve is doing this. Its Steam Deck Verified program requires a certain level of performance, and games can get marked as "Unsupported" if they don't reach that level, but some people may find them playable regardless. In other words, there's no one perfect standard for "playable performance," and thus Valve wants to let users decide for themselves.
Valve says that, at least for this early trial with Steam Deck data, that data is being filtered to only show data from Decks that are set to the default frame limit. The firm doesn't make any attempt to account for custom in-game settings, yet it says that "despite this, [Valve has] found that the framerate data consolidates around relatively narrow ranges," after accounting for the unusual effects of vertical sync.
So what if you don't have a Steam Deck? Well, Valve says it sees this update (adding the Steam Deck framerate data) as "a stepping stone toward providing framerate data for more devices than just Steam Deck." Obviously, that includes Valve's own Steam Machine mini-desktop and Steam Frame VR headset, but presumably it will extend to folks on standard gaming PCs (whether desktop or laptop)
It's not clear whether desktop performance data will be matched by graphics card, some combination of GPU and CPU, or multiple factors, but either way, there's no question that this is yet another feature that sets Steam as a storefront above its competitors. If you'd like to opt in, you'll have to join the Steam Client Beta for now; Valve says the feature is coming to all users "in the future," though.

articles.title: Preload von GTA 6 lässt Datenverkehr ansteigen: So bereiten sich Internetanbieter auf den Release vor
articles.text:
Preload von GTA 6 lässt Datenverkehr ansteigen: So bereiten sich Internetanbieter auf den Release vor
Am 19. November 2026 fällt der Startschuss für ein Spiel, auf das viele Zocker:innen schon seit Jahren warten. GTA 6 öffnet die Tore des neonbeleuchteten und chaotischen Vice City. Neu für die Reihe ist, dass das Spiel ausschließlich als Download angeboten wird. Damit im besten Fall niemand am Release-Tag enttäuscht wird, weil die Download-Server in die Knie gehen, lässt Rockstar den Preload von GTA 6 seit dem 10. November zu.
GTA 6 im Preload: Erste Vorzeichen für den Start?
Wie Golem berichtet, vermelden schon jetzt erste Internetanbieter, dass GTA 6 den Datenverkehr beachtlich erhöht. So verzeichnete etwa 1&1 in der Nacht vom 9. auf den 10. November einen Verbrauch, der etwa zehnmal so hoch lag, wie an normalen Tagen. Auch Vodafone berichtet von kleineren Anstiegen. Allerdings will der Anbieter den Datenverkehr in den kommenden Tagen nach dem Start des GTA-6-Preloads noch im Blick behalten, um endgültige Aussagen zu treffen.
Für den Release-Tag wollen beide Internetanbieter gut gerüstet sein, sodass es nicht zu Ausfällen kommt. Und auch in den USA rüsten sich die Anbieter für den Release von GTA 6. Comcast bietet über seine Untermarke Xfinity etwa erhöhte Download-Raten für alle Kunden und das ohne Aufpreis. So sollen sich die mehr als 200 Gigabyte, die GTA 6 im Download beanspruchen wird, dank Verbindungen mit bis zu zwei Gigabyte pro Sekunde schnell abhandeln lassen.
Gegenüber Gamesindustry berichteten mehrere Branchenexpert:innen, dass der Release von GTA 6 zwar eine Herausforderung für den Datenverkehr sein wird, aber es aktuell keine Anzeichen dafür gäbe, von flächendeckenden Ausfällen auszugehen. Sie gehen davon aus, dass der Preload die Last vom Playstation Network und vom Xbox Store nimmt. Ohne eine neuntägige Vorlaufzeit hätten sonst alle Vorbesteller:innen direkt zum Launch den Download angeworfen und hätten die Server damit überfordert.
Neil McRae, Chief Technology and Innovation Officer beim britischen Internetanbieter Cityfibre, schlägt indes etwas vorsichtigere Töne an: „Es gibt keinen Weg daran vorbei, dass am Launch-Tag extrem viel los sein wird. Das liegt daran, dass viele Leute bis zum Launch mit dem Kauf warten.“ Doch in den vergangenen Jahren sind digitale Events und ausschließlich per Download angebotene Spiele immer mehr zum Standard geworden. Internetanbieter konnten sich laut McRae auf ein solches Großereignis also vorbereiten.
Er sagt dazu: „Egal, ob es der Launch von GTA 6 oder ein großes Update für Fortnite oder Call of Duty ist: Netzwerkspitzen sind mittlerweile ein normales Ereignis statt einer Anomalie. Die Anbieter sind in der Lage, sie zu handhaben.“ Gordon Thornton, der 17 Jahre bei Sony gearbeitet und dort das Playstation Network mit aufgebaut hat, findet ähnlich optimistische Worte für die Server der Playstation: „Sie wissen, wie viele Vorbestellungen es gab und welche Bandbreiten nötig sind, um die Vorbestellungen bereitzustellen […] Es ist der größte Titel und die größte Möglichkeit für die PS5, sie müssen es also hinbekommen.“

articles.title: Black Friday 2026 bei Amazon, Mediamarkt und Otto: Diese Termine solltest du kennen
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 bei Amazon, Mediamarkt und Otto: Diese Termine solltest du kennen
Viele Menschen warten mit größeren Anschaffungen gespannt auf den Black Friday. Denn Jahr für Jahr locken zahlreiche Onlineshops mit scheinbar unschlagbaren Angeboten und nie dagewesenen Rabatten. Auch wenn diese Versprechen nicht immer gehalten werden können, gibt es immerhin Sparpotenzial. Damit du den Beginn des Black Fridays und der Black Week nicht verpasst, findest du hier die Starttermine der größten Händler. Sollte es Updates geben, aktualisieren wir den Artikel entsprechend.
Wann findet der Black Friday 2026 statt?
Der Black Friday findet in diesem Jahr am 27. November statt. Schon ab dem 23. November dürften viele Händler:innen mit der Black Week erste Angebote an Kund:innen ausspielen. Das Ende der Rabattzeit setzt dann wie immer der Cyber Monday, der in diesem Jahr auf den 30. November fällt. Dort werden die letzten Angebote herausgehauen, um noch einmal alle Kund:innen zum Kaufen zu animieren.
Wie in jedem Jahr zeigt sich aber, dass die Zeiträume für Deals zum Black Friday und der Black Week von manchen Shops sehr großzügig ausgelegt werden. Schon Anfang November gibt es zahlreiche Anbieter, die mit Pre-Black-Week-Deals werben. Das hat einen einfachen Grund: Die Shops, die ihre Angebote zuerst anbieten, haben eine erhöhte Chance darauf, dass die Kund:innen bei ihnen ihr Geld ausgeben. Wer schon jetzt zuschlägt, sollte deshalb auf Bestpreisgarantien achten, um nicht zum echten Black Friday von einem besseren Angebot überrumpelt zu werden.
Black Friday bei Amazon
Bei Amazon steht der Start der Rabattaktion schon fest. Vom 19. bis 30. November können Kund:innen im Rahmen des Black Fridays und der Black Week shoppen. Das Unternehmen verspricht dabei Deals zu Produkten von Samsung, Bosch, Philips, Braun und vielen mehr. Prime-Kund:innen sollen zudem exklusive Angebote und täglich neue Angebotsartikel präsentiert bekommen.
Aber auch Amazon lässt es sich nicht nehmen, noch etwas früher mit der eigentlichen Rabattaktion zu starten. Denn während alle anderen auf der Plattform des Shopping-Giganten ab 19. November ihre Produkte vergünstigt anbieten, legt das Unternehmen selbst bei „ausgewählten Amazon-Geräten“ schon ab dem 16. November los. Dadurch dürfen interessierte Kund:innen wohl einige Tage vorher Kindle-E-Books, Echo-Lautsprecher und Fire-TV-Sticks günstiger einkaufen.
Black Friday bei Otto
Otto setzt Anfang November noch auf den Singles Day, der am 11. November stattfindet. Dementsprechend finden sich noch kaum Hinweise zum Black Friday 2026 auf der Seite des Shops. Kund:innen sollen lediglich „gespannt“ auf die Deals sein und bis dahin die aktuellen Angebote nutzen. Im vergangenen Jahr startete Otto allerdings auch vor dem richtigen Black Friday. Dieser fiel auf den 28. November 2025. Erste Black-Friday-Angebot gab es bei Otto schon ab dem 18. November.
Black Friday bei Mediamarkt und Saturn
Mediamarkt und Saturn gehören zu den Anbietern, die schon jetzt auf den Black Friday 2026 und erste Vorangebote setzen. Bis zum 13. November um 9 Uhr sollen zunächst erste Angebote in diversen Kategorien stattfinden. Wer schon jetzt zuschlägt, darf bis zum 31. Dezember 2026 die gekauften Produkte umtauschen. Die Rückgabe darf dabei auch im Markt vor Ort oder per Post abgewickelt werden. Ein genaues Datum für die „echten“ Black-Friday-Deals haben Mediamarkt und Saturn noch nicht bekannt gegeben.
Black Friday bei Notebooksbilliger
Auch Notebooksbilliger ist Anfang November schon in Black-Friday-Stimmung. Im Gegensatz zu anderen Anbietern wird hier aber schon ein genauer Zeitraum vorgegeben. Vom 4. November bis 6. Dezember 2026 können Kund:innen mit Rabatten rechnen. Das Angebot wechselt dabei aber etwas durch. So gibt es etwa limitierte, tägliche Black Deals, die Kund:innen immer wieder auf die Seite zurückbringen sollen. Und zum Start der Black Week dürfte sicherlich der eine oder andere Deal noch hinzukommen.

articles.title: Grab this GameSir Super Nova wireless controller at a record-low Amazon price, now under $40 — 20% discount on PC and Switch gamepad that ships with drift-free Hall Effect sticks and a customizable layout
articles.text:
Grab this GameSir Super Nova wireless controller at a record-low Amazon price, now under $40 — 20% discount on PC and Switch gamepad that ships with drift-free Hall Effect sticks and a customizable layout
A budget-friendly and appealing controller for PC
There's nothing that can improve the gaming experience on a PC more than a brand new controller, and this deal on a wireless gamepad is one you won't want to miss. For a limited time only, you can pick up GameSir's Super Nova wireless gaming controller for $39.99. That's a record low from Amazon directly, and one that knocks 20% off its list price.
There are a lot of cheap controllers out there at this price point and lower, but they won't come with the specs that this GameSir controller has. For under $40, you're getting Hall Effect sticks and triggers, along with three different connectivity methods and a charging dock. It's also got an Xbox-style layout, although annoyingly, it isn't compatible with Xbox. It will work with your PC, however, along with smartphones, and even a Nintendo Switch.
The GameSir Super Nova wireless controller is compatible for use with PC, Nintendo Switch, iOS, and Android devices. Its mix of Hall Effect thumbsticks and triggers means accurate control while eliminating stick-drift buildup. The Super Nova controller features subtle RGB lighting, swappable ABXY buttons, a detachable faceplate, a 1000mAh battery, and a charging dock.
You won't be too surprised by the GameSir Super Nova's design, and it's a comfortable and familiar option for gamers, with rubberized grips on the handles and the Xbox button layout for the thumbsticks and buttons. It's instantly recognizable if you've used a recent Xbox controller, making it perfect for PC gaming.
There are three different ways to connect the GameSir Super Nova to a device. You can use it wired, so you won't have to worry about battery life, or you can connect wirelessly using a 2.4 GHz dongle or via Bluetooth. The wired and wireless 2.4 GHz connections will ensure ultra-low latency with a 1,000Hz polling rate, which you'll want if you play competitive-style FPS games, for instance. Bluetooth will give you better battery life while using its 1,000 mAh battery. The combination also makes it easier to switch between using different devices, too.
The GameSir Super Nova is fitted with Hall Effect switches for the controller's trigger buttons, and also uses Hall Effect thumbsticks. These magnetic switches reduce physical wear and tear, avoiding the stick-drift issues that have plagued plenty of older controllers. You've also got trigger stops you can engage for a hair-trigger feel, giving you faster response times in FPS games. There's also 6-axis gyroscopic movement that you can use in Nintendo Switch games, along with vibration motors in both handgrips for haptic feedback.
It's possible to remove the magnetic faceplate and swap the ABXY button layout for your own preference, while vibration settings, button mapping, and dead zone adjustment can be made using GameSir's own app.
The $39.99 sale price for this GameSir Super Nova game controller is a good one, and it's the lowest we've seen on Amazon before. Expect this deal to sell out fast, as there's no guarantee that this limited-time deal will stick around for very long.

How to watch the Golden Joystick Awards 2026 tomorrow — including start times and what to expect
Games like 007 First Light, Big Walk, and Resident Evil Requiem lead the nominations
- The Golden Joystick Awards 2026 will air on November 11 at 10AM PT / 1PM ET / 6PM GMT / 7PM CEST
- Fans can tune in and watch the event live, which will be hosted by Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis actor Alix Wilton Regan
- The ceremony will announce winners for 25 categories, including Ultimate Game of the Year
The winners of the Golden Joystick Awards 2026, one of the biggest ceremonies of the year that celebrates the best games of this year, will be revealed this week - here's when you can tune in.
The show is scheduled to begin on November 11 at 10AM PT / 1PM ET / 6PM GMT / 7PM CEST and can be watched live via YouTube, Twitch, TikTok, X, Future Games, and more.
Hosted by Dragon Age: Inquisition and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis actor Alix Wilton Regan, the event will also feature guest presenters from the industry, including Rare composer Chloe Kwok, art and creative director Rex Crowle, Paddle Paddle Paddle developer Mateo Covic, and interviewer, actor, and presenter AlicesPixels.
More guest presenters include Resident Evil Requiem actor Nick Apostolides, Star Wars: Galactic Racer actor and Wrestling’s Mr. Charles Crowley, Richard Summers-Calvert, CD Projekt Red production director Malgorzata Mitrega, composer Richard Jacques, and Control Resonant actor, Frankie Kevich.
"I’m absolutely thrilled to be your host for this year’s Golden Joystick Awards on November 11th," said Wilton Regan. "We’re celebrating the greatest games of the past 12 months - and, more importantly, the incredibly talented teams who made them happen. The people who put in thousands of hours creating virtual worlds for us to get hopelessly lost in. Get ready for an evening of special guests, spectacular games, and plenty of silly jokes. See you on November 11th when we will unveil your winners!'"
Games like 007 First Light, Resident Evil Requiem, Dispatch, Forza Horizon 6, Big Walk, Crimson Desert, and more are leading this year's nominations across 25 categories, including Ultimate Game of the Year, 22 of which are voted for by the public.
"This year’s shortlist offers a fascinating cross-section of our industry in 2026, with the work of small teams of indie developers sitting shoulder to shoulder with titanic gaming franchises like Pokémon and Resident Evil, as well as huge IPs like Star Wars and James Bond," said content director Daniel Dawkins.

articles.title: Vous n'avez pas besoin de PS5 ou de Xbox séries pour jouer à GTA 6
articles.text:
Alors que le pré-téléchargement de GTA 6 a ouvert ce mardi 10 novembre, neuf jours avant la sortie officielle du 19 novembre, Rockstar a glissé dans son communiqué une annonce destinée aux joueurs restés sur Xbox One.
Pensé et développé de fond en comble pour la génération actuelle de consoles (PS5 et Xbox Series X|S), GTA 6 semblait définitivement hors de portée des machines sorties en 2013. Mais l’éditeur américain a trouvé une parade technique pour ne pas laisser sur le carreau les millions de possesseurs de l’ancienne console de Microsoft.
Le Cloud Gaming à la rescousse de la Xbox One pour GTA 6
Rockstar le précise dans son communiqué publié ce mardi 10 novembre : GTA 6 sera jouable sur Xbox One dès le premier jour via le service Xbox Cloud Gaming. Une bonne nouvelle, qui ne change rien au fait que le jeu tournera à 30 images par seconde partout.
Le jeu ne s’installera pas sur la console. Il tournera sur les serveurs de Microsoft, qui enverront l’image en streaming jusqu’à l’écran du joueur. Sur le plan visuel et technique, cette version déportée s’appuiera sur les paramètres graphiques de la Xbox Series S, bridée elle aussi à 30 images par seconde comme l’ensemble des versions consoles.
Une solution de secours… à condition d’avoir une connexion irréprochable
Si l’initiative évite d’acheter une nouvelle console (plusieurs centaines d’euros) pour profiter de l’État de Leonida, Rockstar prend soin d’émettre un avertissement clair dans son communiqué. Comme pour tout jeu en streaming, la qualité de la partie dépendra de la vitesse et de la stabilité de la connexion internet du joueur. Latence, image qui se dégrade ou baisses de débit peuvent perturber la partie, des soucis qu’on n’a pas quand le jeu est installé sur la console.
Pour les joueurs PlayStation 4, en revanche, Rockstar n’annonce aucune solution équivalente. Sony propose bien du streaming dans le cloud avec son abonnement PS Plus Premium, mais il ne permet pas de jouer à des jeux PS5 sur une PS4.
Rockstar accompagne cette annonce d’une nouvelle vidéo sur le morceau Blood in Your Eyes de Tove Lo, tiré de l’album officiel du jeu. Le communiqué confirme aussi la prise en charge du Remote Play (lecture à distance) sur PS5 et Xbox Series, qui permet de jouer depuis sa propre console sur un autre écran, la PlayStation Portal par exemple.
Rendez-vous le 19 novembre pour vérifier si le streaming sur Xbox One tiendra la route face au titan de Rockstar.

Si vous hésitez à acheter une imprimante 3D, c’est le moment de sauter le pas ! Pendant le Black Friday chinois, l’Anycubic Kobra 4 Combo passe sous les 200 euros grâce à un code promo. Elle est livrée avec le module ACE 2 Pro, qui gère quatre bobines pour imprimer en quatre couleurs et sèche le filament pendant l’impression.
Pourquoi imprimer avec l’Anycubic Kobra 4 Combo ?
- Pour son volume d’impression de 260 x 260 x 260 mm
- Pour sa vitesse d’impression maximale de 600 mm/s
- Pour le pilotage à distance grâce à l’application Anycubic
En entrant le code 11FR40 sur le site d’AliExpress, vous pourrez acheter l’Anycubic Kobra 4 Combo pour 191,99 euros au lieu de 231,99 euros.
Une imprimante qui a besoin de son espace
La mention Combo dans le nom de cette imprimante 3D n’est pas anodine puisqu’elle est vendue avec un module ACE 2 Pro, qui permet d’imprimer en quatre couleurs. Pour monter à huit couleurs, il faut acheter un second ACE 2 Pro et un hub dédié. Ce boîtier sèche aussi le filament pendant l’impression, en chauffant jusqu’à 65 °C.
Avant de l’installer, pensez au bruit. Anycubic annonce 48 dB en mode standard et 45 dB en mode silencieux, des mesures faites dans son propre labo. C’est discret sur le papier, mais une impression peut durer plusieurs heures, donc mieux vaut placer la machine dans une pièce où elle ne vous gênera pas.
Il est aussi préférable de ne pas la laisser fonctionner de nuit puisque vous n’êtes pas à l’abri d’un défaut d’impression. Anycubic propose donc un pilotage à distance. Depuis l’application Anycubic, vous suivez l’impression en direct grâce à la caméra 720p intégrée. Celle-ci repère les impressions ratées (le fameux « spaghetti ») ou un objet oublié sur le plateau, et vous envoie une alerte.
Une imprimante
Une fois l’Anycubic Kobra 4 Combo dans un espace adapté, vous pourrez imprimer des objets avec des dimensions maximales de 260 x 260 x 260 mm. Vous pouvez suivre l’avancée de votre création depuis l’application, mais un écran tactile de 3,5 pouces permet aussi d’ajuster les paramètres directement sur la machine avant de lancer l’impression.
En activité, l’imprimante 3D se démarque par sa vitesse d’exécution puisqu’elle possède une vitesse d’impression maximale de 600 mm/s et de 300 mm/s par défaut. Anycubic promet jusqu’à 80 % de temps d’impression en moins, sans préciser face à quelle machine. C’est un chiffre de labo, à prendre avec des pincettes.
Côté précision, Anycubic mise sur LeviQ 3.0, son système de nivellement automatique du plateau sur 49 points. Il corrige les petits écarts qui peuvent fausser la première couche, sans réglage manuel.

articles.title: Diese Webseite zeigt dir, welche Satelliten über deinen Wohnort geflogen sind – und was sie aufgenommen haben
articles.text:
Diese Webseite zeigt dir, welche Satelliten über deinen Wohnort geflogen sind – und was sie aufgenommen haben
Der Orbit der Erde ist voll mit Flugkörpern, die von Menschen geschaffen wurden. Die mehr als 16.600 Satelliten, die noch im Betrieb sind (via Orbital Radar) ziehen jeden Tag ihre Bahnen über unsere Köpfe hinweg und nehmen dabei eine Vielzahl von Bildern auf. Diese Aufnahmen sind normalerweise über mehrere Archive hinweg verstreut. Doch eine Webseite möchte Weltallbegeisterten die Arbeit ersparen, sie alle zusammenzusuchen.
Welche Satelliten fliegen über Area 51?
Die Webseite trägt den Namen „Watched“ und hat zunächst einen eher ominösen Unterton. So steht auf der Seite als Begrüßung: „Etwas hat dich diese Woche beobachtet“. Es handelt sich dabei allerdings nur um eine Zusammenstellung aller aktiven Satelliten, deren Bahnen und vorhandener Aufnahmen. Die Seite scannt alle sechs Stunden die Tracker der US Space Force und bringt sie dann mit den Archiven der Nasa, Element 84 und Microsoft Planetary Computer in Verbindung.
Für dich heißt das, dass du einfach nur einen bestimmten Ort in die Suchleiste der Webseite eingeben musst oder einen vorgefertigten Vorschlag aus der Leiste darüber auswählen kannst. Wählst du etwa Area 51 aus, siehst du, dass mehr als 250 Satelliten in den vergangenen sieben Tagen über das Areal geflogen sind. Standardmäßig zeigt „Watched“ dabei immer zuerst die Aufnahme mit der höchsten Zoomstufe. Bei Area 51 stammt sie etwa vom Satelliten Sentinel-2B der Esa.
Daneben gibt es aber noch viele weitere Aufnahmen des Areals, die du dir anschauen kannst. Die Suche nimmt im Grunde jeden Ort auf der Erde an und zeigt alle Satellitenverläufe und -aufnahmen der vergangenen sieben Tage. Die Verantwortlichen hinter der Webseite betonen, dass es sich dabei nicht um Live-Daten handelt. Flugbahnen und Bilder werden erst ein bis zwei Tage, nachdem sie entstanden sind, in die Datenbank eingefügt.
Zudem werden nicht alle Satelliten erfasst. Logischerweise sind die Daten von „militärischen und Spionagesatelliten“ nicht öffentlich verfügbar. Was sie aufnehmen, ist also nicht bekannt. Bei den verfügbaren Aufnahmen muss allerdings niemand Sorge haben, ungewollt abgelichtet zu werden. Die höchste Zoomstufe ist gerade so detailliert, dass ein Pixel etwa zehn Metern entspricht. Eine einzelne Person erkennen zu können, ist also unmöglich.

articles.title: Microsoft November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235 flaws, Outlook zero-day
articles.text:
Today is Microsoft's November 2026 Patch Tuesday, with security updates addressing a record-breaking 1,235 flaws, including one actively exploited Microsoft Outlook zero-day vulnerability.
This Patch Tuesday addresses 66 "Critical" vulnerabilities, 48 of which are Remote Code Execution (RCE), 15 are Elevation of Privilege (EoP), and three are Use-After-Free in Microsoft Edge.
The approximate number of bugs in each vulnerability category is listed below:
- 536 Elevation of Privilege Vulnerabilities
- 27 Security Feature Bypass Vulnerabilities
- 296 Remote Code Execution Vulnerabilities
- 157 Information Disclosure Vulnerabilities
- 46 Denial of Service Vulnerabilities
- 22 Spoofing Vulnerabilities
- 142 Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) Vulnerabilities
Of the 1,235 vulnerabilities, approximately 639 are categorized under Windows or Microsoft Windows products/components.
When BleepingComputer reports on Patch Tuesday security updates, we only count vulnerabilities released by Microsoft on Patch Tuesday itself.
Therefore, today's total excludes 108 flaws fixed earlier this month, including one Entra Device Registration, 82 Mariner, and 25 Microsoft Edge flaws.
November's Patch Tuesday comes after a record-breaking 1,411 flaws in the October updates as Microsoft continues to use AI to find and patch vulnerabilities.
To learn more about the non-security updates released today, you can review our dedicated articles on the Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates and the Microsoft Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update.
Microsoft patches 1 zero-days
This month's Patch Tuesday fixes one zero-day vulnerability in Microsoft Outlook that was exploited in attacks.
Microsoft classifies a zero-day flaw as publicly disclosed or actively exploited when no official fix is available.
The actively exploited zero-day vulnerability addressed in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday updates is:
CVE-2026-124194 - Microsoft Outlook Spoofing Vulnerability
Microsoft patched a Microsoft Outlook Spoofing zero-day vulnerability that was actively exploited in attacks to steal NTLM account hashes.
"An unauthenticated attacker could send a specially crafted message file and convince a user to open it in an affected version of Microsoft Outlook," warns Microsoft.
"Opening the file could cause Outlook to connect to an attacker-controlled network location without displaying the usual external-content warning, potentially disclosing authentication information that could be used to impersonate the user. Exploitation requires network connectivity and user interaction."
This type of vulnerability is known as an NTLM credential disclosure flaw, where a malicious attachment, when opened, causes Windows to connect to an attacker-controlled network share.
When connecting, Windows may automatically attempt to authenticate to the remote server, exposing the user's NTLMv2 authentication hash, which can then be captured by the attacker and potentially cracked offline.
The recovered credentials could then be used to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts.
Similar vulnerability have been exploited in the past, typically through malicious attachments sent in phishing campaigns.
Recent updates from other companies
Other vendors who released updates or advisories in November 2026 include:
- Barracuda Networks released security updates for two vulnerabilities that can let attackers run commands with root privileges. A week later, these flaws were exploited in attacks.
- Cisco released security updates for numerous products, including critical vulnerabilities Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Secure Email Gateway, and Meraki.
- Google released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks.
- Ivanti released security updates to patch two Connect Secure (ICS) remote access gateway flaws that have been chained in zero-day attacks since at least October 1.
- N-able is working on a hotfix for an alleged 30+ zero-days that were publicly disclosed yesterday, causing the company to take its hosted N-central environments offline.
- Linux distributions released security updates to fix an authentication bypass flaw involving OpenSSH and musl, dubbed "*sshole".
- SAP released the November security updates, which include fixes for four maximum-severity vulnerabilities.
- SonicWall released security updates for seven vulnerabilities in SonicOS firewalls, including an SSL-VPN authentication bypass flaw exploited in attacks.
- Vates released security updates for a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks.
- Zyxel patched a zero-day vulnerability in its GS1900 series network switches that was exploited to compromise nearly 1,000 devices worldwide.
The November 2026 Patch Tuesday Security Updates
Below is the complete list of resolved vulnerabilities in the November 2026 updates. Note, this report does include the flaws fixed earlier this month.
To access the full description of each vulnerability and the systems it affects, you can view the full report here.

articles.title: From conversations to action: How Cogover is addressing commitment leakage in Indian enterprises
articles.text:
NetApp Excellerator
View Brand Publisher
From conversations to action: How Cogover is addressing commitment leakage in Indian enterprises
Selected for NetApp Excellerator, Cogover is connecting customer conversations, business workflows, and AI agents to help enterprises turn commitments into accountable action.
At 11 am, a borrower tells a collections agent they will make a payment on Friday. The conversation is recorded, the agent moves to the next call, and the account may be handled by someone else days later. When Friday arrives, does the team know what was promised, who owns the follow-up, and whether payment was received?
This is the problem Cogover calls ‘commitment leakage’: customer commitments that lose context, ownership, or follow-through as work moves between people and disconnected systems.
For Indian enterprises managing large volumes of calls, approvals and customer requests, the cost is not simply missed tasks. It is repeated conversations, delayed resolutions, and limited visibility into whether work actually gets done.
The gap between a conversation and an outcome
Most enterprises already have tools to store customer records, manage calls, and track tasks. The difficulty arises when employees must manually connect them.
In lending, a promise-to-pay may be recorded without a clear next action. In brokerage, a customer seeking help with KYC can wait while teams coordinate. In real estate, a promised site visit may never become a confirmed appointment.
Managers can see call volumes but may struggle to identify unresolved commitments. Employees piece together notes and messages, while customers repeat information they have already shared.
Cogover is addressing that operational gap with an Agentic Enterprise Platform that brings CRM, built-in calling, workflows, and AI agents into one environment. Its central proposition is straightforward: a customer interaction should lead to a visible, accountable next step.
What makes the approach agentic?
An AI summary can save time, but it does not by itself assign an owner, approve an exception, or ensure a follow-up happens.
In Cogover, AI agents are designed to participate in defined business processes. They can help extract information from a conversation, propose a record update or prepare a task. Permissions and workflow rules determine what can proceed automatically and what requires human review.
Because calling is built into the same platform, an employee can dial from a customer record and access the relevant history, disposition, and subsequent work without moving between separate tools. A supervisor reviewing an exception can trace a task back to its originating interaction.
The goal is not to replace employee judgment. It is to make the context, responsibility, and next action available to the right person at the right time.
A promise-to-pay, followed through
Consider a collections workflow. An agent calls a borrower from the account record. AI helps identify the proposed amount, payment date and intent. The employee checks those details before confirming the commitment.
The workflow then assigns a follow-up with an owner and deadline. If the borrower requests an arrangement beyond the agent’s authority, the request moves to an approver with the conversation context attached. If a relevant payment-status integration is available, that update can guide the next action.
When a deadline passes, the unresolved item becomes visible to the responsible supervisor instead of disappearing into personal notes.
Crucially, the process distinguishes what the customer promised, what the employee must do, and whether the business outcome occurred. A completed follow-up is not the same as a received payment. Both need to be measurable.
The same design can support brokerage KYC resolution, real-estate site-visit coordination and service escalations, each with its own ownership, approval and exception rules.
Building around real enterprise processes
Enterprise workflows rarely match a rigid template. An approval may depend on transaction value, customer type, or branch. A service exception might involve sales, operations, and finance.
Cogover combines AI-assisted application creation with low-code configuration so teams can shape fields, stages, permissions, and escalation paths around those realities. They can review an initial working application and refine it against actual cases rather than relying solely on a static specification.
That flexibility matters in enterprises where formal systems coexist with conversations, messaging and cross-functional decisions. To operate reliably, those informal handoffs must become explicit business rules.
Why NetApp Excellerator matters
Cogover’s selection for NetApp Excellerator creates an opportunity to connect this application-led approach with a broader enterprise data perspective.
One customer request may depend on a recording, CRM history, an approval policy and a transaction update. For AI to assist responsibly, it needs relevant data and controlled access. For the organization to trust the process, actions need ownership and traceability.
NetApp brings an enterprise data infrastructure perspective; Cogover brings the customer interactions and operational workflows where data is translated into decisions and actions. Participation in the program provides a setting to explore that connection further.
Measure actions, not just activity
For businesses evaluating agentic AI, Cogover suggests starting with a specific workflow rather than a broad automation target.
Can managers identify every commitment made yesterday and its owner? Can approvers access the original context? How many follow-ups are overdue? How often must customers call again for an update?
A focused pilot can measure ownership coverage, approval turnaround, missed deadlines, repeated data entry, and customer follow-up rates. Teams should also monitor errors and human corrections, not merely processing speed.
For simple, low-volume work, shared task tracking may be sufficient. As customer interactions, handoffs, and approvals multiply, a connected system becomes more valuable.
Cogover’s argument is that enterprise AI delivers practical value when it moves beyond generating information to helping people complete work with clear permissions, accountability, and evidence of outcomes.

articles.title: Espanha exige que TikTok suspenda operações por conteúdo de abuso sexual infantil
articles.text:
O governo da Espanha exigiu que o TikTok suspenda suas operações no país até eliminar conteúdos de abuso sexual infantil da plataforma. A cobrança foi anunciada nesta terça-feira (10), após uma investigação identificar mais de mil publicações explícitas que, juntas, acumularam dezenas de milhões de visualizações na rede social.
A ministra da Juventude espanhola, Sira Rego, acionou o Ministério Público e a Agência de Proteção de Dados para que as autoridades adotem providências contra a empresa. Segundo comunicado do ministério, Rego afirmou que as redes sociais não podem funcionar como territórios sem regras.
A exigência veio depois de uma investigação publicada pela organização espanhola de checagem de fatos Maldita.es. O levantamento identificou 1.183 publicações com material explícito de abuso sexual infantil no TikTok.
Os vídeos foram visualizados pelo menos 48 milhões de vezes. Além disso, mais de 26 mil perfis comentaram ou compartilharam esse conteúdo.
TikTok restringiu buscas, mas material continuou acessível
- Após a divulgação da investigação, o TikTok restringiu dois termos de pesquisa identificados pela Maldita.es como caminhos para encontrar conteúdo de abuso sexual infantil na Espanha;
- Entretanto, uma atualização da investigação, publicada na terça-feira, apontou que as mesmas publicações ainda podiam ser encontradas por meio de pesquisas realizadas em outros países europeus;
- A situação reforçou as cobranças sobre a capacidade da plataforma de identificar e remover conteúdos ilegais, mesmo depois de receber alertas sobre sua circulação;
- Procurado pela Reuters, o TikTok não respondeu imediatamente ao pedido de comentário.
Leia mais:
- Dono do TikTok acumula R$ 540 bilhões e vira o mais rico da China
- TikTok enfrenta ação de R$ 200 milhões por mensagens racistas no Brasil
- Google, Meta e TikTok processam Califórnia para barrar lei de proteção a menores
Governo espanhol já investigava grandes plataformas
A nova exigência ocorre meses depois de o governo espanhol solicitar investigação sobre X, Meta e TikTok por supostamente disseminarem material de abuso sexual infantil gerado por inteligência artificial (IA).
A iniciativa faz parte de movimento mais amplo de fiscalização das grandes empresas de tecnologia na Europa, onde reguladores têm intensificado a pressão sobre as plataformas por causa da circulação de conteúdos prejudiciais e ilegais.
A ministra Sira Rego, porém, não tem autoridade para determinar sozinha a proibição da operação do TikTok na Espanha. Por isso, o governo recorreu ao Ministério Público e à Agência de Proteção de Dados para que sejam tomadas medidas contra a empresa.
A exigência espanhola representa mais um capítulo da pressão europeia sobre as redes sociais para que assumam maior responsabilidade pelo conteúdo publicado e compartilhado em seus serviços.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Emmanuel Macron fait signer un engagement international aux rois de l’IA
articles.text:
Ce 9 novembre 2026, à la veille de la 9e édition du Forum de Paris sur la Paix, Emmanuel Macron a réuni en visioconférence plusieurs grands dirigeants du secteur, dont Sam Altman (OpenAI), Dario Amodei (Anthropic), Brad Smith (le président de Microsoft) et Arthur Mensch (Mistral AI).
Nous pouvions également noter la présence de représentants de huit pays (Canada, Japon, Norvège, Pays-Bas, Royaume-Uni…), de Scott Bessent (secrétaire américain au Trésor), ainsi que de représentants de deux organisations internationales : l’ONU et l’OCDE. Sous l’égide du président de la République, tous se sont engagés à respecter une charte destinée à encadrer l’intelligence artificielle à l’échelle mondiale.
Trois engagements pour mieux contrôler l’intelligence artificielle
Cette charte, baptisée « Appel de Paris pour la sécurité de l’IA », est articulée en trois axes. Premièrement, les décideurs publics, les développeurs et les chercheurs s’engagent à établir un cadre commun d’évaluation et de gestion des risques liés aux modèles de pointe. Ce cadre d’évaluation doit être indépendant et public. Il est plus précisément ici question des risques de cyberattaques et des cas de pertes de contrôle de puissants modèles par leur concepteur.
Deuxièmement, les signataires s’engagent à renforcer les dispositifs existants de signalement et d’alerte « afin de partager rapidement les informations relatives aux incidents graves, cyber ou de perte de contrôle », comme l’explique l’Élysée. Les décideurs publics s’engagent par ailleurs « à offrir des canaux sécurisés et confidentiels permettant aux lanceurs d’alerte de signaler des risques systémiques sans crainte de représailles ».
Enfin, troisièmement, la charte appelle les concepteurs des modèles de pointe à davantage de responsabilité. Ceux-ci s’engagent « à rendre publiques les capacités, limites et risques connus de leurs modèles ». Sur X, Emmanuel Macron a déclaré : « L’idée, ce n’est pas de refuser ces innovations mais de réussir à créer un cadre qui prend en compte les dangers, qui sont de trois ordres : nos enfants, la sécurité démocratique et les grands enjeux de sécurité nationale ».
Emmanuel Macron envisage d’interdire certains outils d’IA aux plus jeunes
Lors d’une interview accordée au quotidien Les Echos, Emmanuel Macron a déclaré : « S’il y a un risque pour les enfants avec certains usages de l’IA, alors il faut l’interdire ». Il précise ensuite : « Ce n’est pas parce que c’est de l’IA que ce doit être le Far West. Ce système n’est pas tenable, il faut le changer jusqu’à l’interdire s’il est mauvais ». Après avoir voulu interdire l’accès aux réseaux sociaux pour les moins de 15 ans, le président de la République envisage désormais de restreindre l’accès des plus jeunes à certains outils d’intelligence artificielle.
Quoi qu’il en soit, les appels à réguler l’intelligence artificielle se sont multipliés en l’espace de quelques mois. Donald Trump a fait signer un code de bonne conduite aux principaux acteurs américains de l’IA, tandis qu’OpenAI, Google et Anthropic travailleraient sur l’élaboration de leur propre gendarme de l’IA. Il reste maintenant à voir quel poids pourrait avoir la charte signée sous l’égide d’Emmanuel Macron.
