articles.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"
articles.text:
Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark.
DeepMind’s physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There’s the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that’s Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5.
DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate.
Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.
That’s an impressive showing compared to previous robotic AI systems, but it’s still probably not enough for a company like Mercedes-Benz. A human doing that sort of repetitive task will get it right virtually every time, and DeepMind director Kanishka Rao notes that closing that last 4 percent gap will be a “steep road.”

articles.title: Google Finds that Technical Debt Can Derail Coding Agents Through "Agent Distraction"
articles.text:
In a recent article, Google senior staff software engineer Sam Saccone and senior staff data scientist Madhuri Garikapati highlighted the cost of agent distraction, where AI coding agents get derailed by stale technical debt, such as old TODO comments, obsolete bug references, and outdated specs, leading them to embark on unrequested "side-quests".
Obsolete specs, long resolved bugs, and lagging documentation no longer rest in long forgotten corners of the codebase, but rather are unintentionally ingested as context indirecting and misdirecting the next wave of coders - the agents.
According to the authors, at best, agent distraction increases token consumption and execution time; at worst, it can lead agents to "incorrect logic and decisions". To investigate this impact, they focused on TODO(bug/...) comments, which, as they note, "tend to be left behind long after the underlying bug is resolved or abandoned".
By cross-referencing every TODO an agent encounters against the TODO's bug status and the user's prompt, we can automatically separate valid work from wasted detours at scale.
Using distributed traces from thousands of engineers and hundreds of millions of agent steps, Google found that approximately 13% of sessions exposed agents to inline TODO/FIXME references, leading agents to take action targeting the reference bug in 6% of those cases. In most cases, the prompt did not even mention the referenced bug. Furthermore, in 41% of these unprompted detours, the agent worked on tickets that were already closed; in 57% of them they worked on bugs that were still open, but fell outside the scope of the developer's request, which the investigators classified as "scope creep".
Using a multi-way fixed-effects regression with developer-clustered standard errors, the investigators found that these detours add substantial overhead per session, with 70% more steps, 77% more tokens, and 105% more wait time.
To address this issue, Google developed scanner agents to identify and clean up obsolete TODOs across the codebase. In some cases, the agents had to inspect years of git history to be able to confirm that both the TODO and the intent behind it were obsolete. However, only once confirmed this, they submitted a PR to remove the outdated reference from the codebase.
As a result of this multi-layer approach, our todo cleaner has been able to remove thousands of actually obsolete references over the last 6 months exceeding 95% acceptance from human reviewers.
The investigators conclude that tools such as presubmit analyzers, codebase scanners, and automated agents can help mitigate "agent distraction" and thus improve the effectiveness of AI coding agents.
Commenting on the finding, X user Tulasiram noted that "this is a useful reminder that comments are context too". Ryan White emphasized:
This is just junior dev behavior at machine speed. Leave a misleading comment and someone chases it for a day. Except now it happens 40 times an hour and you're paying for the tokens.
On LinkedId, user Awais Raza expressed optimism about the potential to mitigate agent distraction:
The 95%+ human acceptance of the todo cleaner is telling: it shows cleanup can be automated without losing human judgment.
Finally, Muhammad Zohaib extended this perspective, pointing out that "the same probably applies to websites: outdated pages and conflicting info make it harder for AI systems to pick the right answer."

articles.title: Quién es Alice Huang, la exdirectiva de Megaspeed que ha puesto contra las cuerdas a Jensen Huang y Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang está en una posición extremadamente delicada. Ha reconocido públicamente en un mensaje dirigido a los empleados de Nvidia que ha sido infiel a su esposa. Aunque no ha identificado a la persona con la que ha estado, parece tratarse de Alice Huang, una exdirectiva de la compañía singapurense Megaspeed International. Para rizar aún más el rizo, los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses siguen a esta empresaria desde hace al menos dos años porque sospechan que trabaja para los servicios de inteligencia de China.
Parece el hilo argumental de una película de espionaje, pero es absolutamente real. Y está teniendo repercusiones muy profundas en Nvidia. Sus acciones han caído un 4,3% durante la sesión bursátil del 9 de noviembre, lo que ha provocado una reducción de la capitalización bursátil de la compañía de aproximadamente 190.000 millones de dólares. La confianza del mercado en Jensen Huang y Nvidia se está resintiendo, lo que ha desencadenado que un grupo de accionistas presente una demanda colectiva ante un tribunal federal de San José (California).
En el centro de toda esta trama no está solo Jensen Huang; le acompaña Alice Huang, el detonante de este escándalo. Su apellido coincide, pero no tienen ninguna relación de parentesco. Sea como sea, ¿quién es esta ejecutiva y cómo ha conseguido acercarse tanto al líder de una de las compañías de tecnología más importantes del planeta? Su nombre original es Huang Le (Alice es su nombre occidentalizado), y se acercó a Jensen Huang cuando ella formaba parte de la cúpula directiva de Megaspeed International.
De filial de una empresa china de videojuegos a gran cliente de Nvidia
Antes de llegar a Megaspeed, Alice Huang, ciudadana china que actualmente tiene 43 años, ocupó varios puestos directivos en los bancos HSBC y CITIC Securities. Un apunte interesante: HSBC es un banco occidental cuya sede está en Londres y para el que Hong Kong y China representan su principal fuente de ingresos. Sin embargo, CITIC Securities es el mayor banco de inversión de China y está vinculado al Estado chino a través de su matriz.
Alice Huang se incorporó a Megaspeed como directora general en marzo de 2023. Su llegada se produjo en el mismo momento en el que esta compañía, que había sido constituida en Singapur, en 2015, como 7Road International, cambió su nombre a Megaspeed International. Este cambio se produjo apenas unos meses después de que el Gobierno de EEUU liderado por Joe Biden aprobase las primeras restricciones a la exportación de semiconductores avanzados a China.
En octubre de 2025 The New York Times describió a 7Road International como una firma de juegos y computación en la nube
7Road, la matriz de la compañía, se fundó en 2008 en Shenzhen (China), y se dedica a desarrollar y distribuir internacionalmente juegos de navegador y para móviles. No obstante, 7Road International, su filial singapurense, fue constituida como una desarrolladora de videojuegos. Curiosamente, en octubre de 2025 The New York Times describió a esta empresa como una firma de juegos y computación en la nube respaldada por inversores estatales.
En su página web, Megaspeed International se presenta como Nvidia Cloud Partner en Asia-Pacífico con una infraestructura que aglutina el hardware más potente de Nvidia, como los sistemas GB200 NVL72 y HGX H100. Esto es muy importante: Megaspeed tiene acceso a las GPU para inteligencia artificial (IA) más avanzadas de Nvidia. Además, hay otra conexión que merece la pena que no pasemos por alto: en la década de 2010, Alice Huang trabajó en Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, que tenía lazos de inversión con 7Road.
Alice Huang permaneció como administradora y directora general de Megaspeed hasta noviembre de 2023, aunque The Wall Street Journal sospecha que continuó dirigiendo el negocio tras su dimisión. Sea como sea, están documentados varios encuentros públicos entre ella y Jensen Huang tanto durante su mandato en Megaspeed como meses después. De hecho, fueron fotografiados juntos en un bar de Taipéi (Taiwán), en junio de 2024, durante una reunión en la que también participaron otros ejecutivos del sector tecnológico.
Como he mencionado en las primeras líneas de este artículo, los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses sospechan que el interés de Alice Huang en Jensen Huang no fue estrictamente romántico. Temen que esté vinculada a la inteligencia china y que haya aprovechado su cercanía al líder de Nvidia tanto para entregar información confidencial a la Administración china como para mediar en el tráfico de chips restringidos para IA a China. No obstante, estas hipótesis están siendo investigadas, por lo que todavía no podemos aceptarlas como sólidas.

articles.title: Perros robot para detener los ataques de lobos a los rebaños
articles.text:
En la Universidad de Padua están trabajando en un sistema para proteger a los rebaños de los ataques de lobos. Y para ello han puesto en marcha un proyecto en el que participan además la región italiana del Véneto y Veneto Agricoltura.
En él están desarrollando un perro robot que sea capaz de moverse en terrenos accidentados. Además de este elemento, están realizando un sistema de protección que combina sensores y dispositivos que emiten ultrasonidos y luces parpadeantes para intentar disuadir al depredador cuando se aproxima a los animales que pastan.
El proyecto ha generado polémica por su coste. El consejero regional de Futuro Nazionale, Stefano Valdegamberi, ha criticado que gasten 70.000 euros en un “perro robot”. Ha pedido saber de qué sirven estos dispositivos y qué resultados han obtenido. “Es ciencia ficción pagada con el dinero de los contribuyentes”, ha dicho.
Esta es la cantidad total del proyecto experimental que financia la región. El coste previsto del prototipo del perro robot es de unos 5.000 euros. El proyecto también trata de la integración de los sistemas disuasorios en una plataforma móvil. Este será el robot.
Luz y sonido para evitar que el lobo se acostumbre
El equipo está liderado por los profesores Nicola Trivellin, Alessandro Pozzebon y Michele Scotton. Los proyectos en los que trabajan son HEIMAT (financiado por la región del Véneto) y MELKEN (por Veneto Agricoltura), según informa la Universidad de Padua.
Una de las problemáticas de los sistemas tradicionales de protección (como vallas eléctricas o dispositivos acústicos) es que, aunque en un principio funcionan (disminuyen los ataques), los estímulos poco variados llevan al lobo a la habituación. Los investigadores están analizando qué tipo de estímulos visuales y auditivos pueden hacer que el lobo retire su presencia. También qué se puede hacer para evitar la habituación.
En esta primera fase están probando un prototipo llamado Remo. Desde noviembre de 2025 está instalado en un parque de la provincia de Grosseto. Los primeros indicios son buenos. Se trata de unas pruebas de los estímulos disuasorios. Los dispositivos están alimentados con energía solar.
En una fase posterior estaría el uso de perros robots. Se trata de llevar la tecnología de luz y sonido por el terreno. También servirían para orientar el sistema disuasorio hacia el sitio en el que se detecte al lobo.
Por ello, está previsto que el robot tenga un papel móvil. Su integración está prevista tras las pruebas de disuasión. Los resultados iniciales no demuestran que ya haya un perro robot que evite los ataques a los rebaños.

articles.title: Ugreen Nexode Air 65 W : ce chargeur compact et son câble passent sous les 24 €
articles.text:
Le chargeur USB-C Ugreen Nexode Air 65 W avec câble est à 23,99 € (-31 %)
Assez puissant pour un MacBook Air et livré avec un câble USB-C de 100 W, le chargeur Ugreen Nexode Air 65 W passe à 23,99 € chez Amazon, soit 11 € de moins.
Vendu par Ugreen et expédié par Amazon, ce chargeur gris affiche 23,99 € contre 34,99 € pour le prix conseillé, soit une remise de 31 % dans le cadre des offres pré-Black Friday d'Amazon. C'est aussi 4 € de moins que son plus bas prix des 30 derniers jours (27,99 €).
65 W pour un smartphone comme pour un ordinateur
Ce chargeur USB-C délivre jusqu'à 65 W et gère de nombreux protocoles de charge rapide, dont le Power Delivery et le PPS. Ugreen annonce 50 % de batterie en 15 minutes pour un iPhone 18 Pro et 55 % en 30 minutes pour un MacBook Air.
Le câble USB-C vers USB-C fourni supporte jusqu'à 100 W, ce qui évite d'en racheter un.
Compact et protégé contre la surchauffe
Grâce à sa technologie GaN, Ugreen annonce un encombrement réduit de 74 % par rapport à un chargeur classique de 65 W, avec un rendement allant jusqu'à 93 %. Un système de surveillance de la température adapte la charge pour limiter l'échauffement. Il ne dispose en revanche que d'un seul port USB-C : impossible de recharger deux appareils en même temps.
C'est un accessoire très demandé : Amazon indique plus de 400 achats le mois dernier, et il est noté 4,7/5 par plus de 580 acheteurs.

articles.title: Anthropic wants Claude to be the front end for your entire enterprise app stack
articles.text:
Anthropic wants Claude to be the front end for your entire enterprise app stack
Anthropic is expanding Claude’s ability to work directly inside enterprise applications; it can now open full software interfaces, retrieve information, and make changes without requiring users to move between applications.
At The Briefing: Work at the Frontier in San Francisco on Tuesday, the company announced expanded interactive connectors, along with new tools for meetings, spreadsheets, shared workspaces, and business data.
“For years, we’ve learned to work around software. Now Claude works around you,” said Ami Vora, Anthropic’s chief product officer, in remarks prepared for the event.
“For years, we’ve learned to work around software. Now Claude works around you,”
Full apps open inside Claude
Anthropic’s interactive connectors previously let users see a small preview of a connected app in Claude. Now, they can open and work in the full application within the conversation, starting with Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot.
For example, Claude can edit a Confluence page directly or update an Adobe design using assets from a company’s brand kit. Users do still need to approve those changes before Claude executes.
Built on MCP Apps
The expanded connectors are built on MCP Apps, which lets MCP servers provide interactive interfaces instead of relying solely on tool calls. Developers can bring existing application interfaces into Claude using app tools and embedded websites, without rebuilding them for the assistant. The new capabilities are in public preview and aren’t limited to Claude, since other AI clients that support MCP Apps can use them too.
The new capabilities are in public preview and aren’t limited to Claude, since other AI clients that support MCP Apps can use them too.
Anthropic says Claude Marketplace now includes more than 9,000 connectors and plugins, continuing the effort to connect AI systems with enterprise infrastructure. For applications without a supported connector, Claude can use its built-in browser to interact with them.
Existing permissions still apply
The company says connectors respect the permissions employees already have in the underlying application. For example, a user who cannot access a particular Google Drive document cannot retrieve it through Claude.
Administrators can also restrict individual connector capabilities, including allowing Claude to read Slack messages without permission to send messages.
Additionally, Anthropic is introducing Claude auto-connect in beta, a ten-minute setup that lets administrators enable connectors across an organization without requiring employees to configure them individually. Smart Reports, meanwhile, gives administrators visibility into team usage, completed work, and spending.
Claude Data gets certified queries
Anthropic is also making Claude Data generally available, following its October launch as Claude Dashboards.
The update introduces certified queries, allowing data teams to approve the queries Claude uses for reporting so different teams get consistent numbers from the same data.
The update introduces certified queries, allowing data teams to approve the queries Claude uses for reporting so different teams get consistent numbers from the same data. A second feature, live sharing, lets employees access updated dashboards without needing direct access to the underlying data source.
Both features are still in beta. Anthropic hasn’t detailed how it handles versioning for certified queries or changes to the source data’s schema.
Task delegation moves beyond engineering
Claude Meetings, which Anthropic says is coming soon, will join video calls to create project plans, answer questions, and retrieve information from connected applications. The feature is planned for Team and Enterprise customers but won’t be available to organizations using zero data retention, HIPAA-ready configurations, or customer-managed encryption keys.
Another feature, Claude Whiteboards, gives teams a shared space to develop projects with Claude, while Claude Sheets lets them build and edit spreadsheets together. Both are available in beta on paid plans.
Enterprise adoption moves beyond engineering
At Datadog, product managers are using Claude to develop product requirements documents and testable prototypes. Uday Tennety, the company’s head of technology partnerships, said the approach has shortened the time between an initial idea and a working prototype.
Anthropic also reports that Mercado Libre has deployed Claude to more than 26,000 employees, with 78% using it weekly. These figures have not been independently verified.

articles.title: Microsoft patent describes paying you to train AI on your idle GPU
articles.text:
In a nutshell: The AI boom needs every spare gigabyte of RAM and GPU cycle it can get. Just a few days after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman controversially complained about memory sitting idle in consumer devices, Microsoft filed a patent describing how it might pay users to train AI on their idle devices.
Filed earlier this month and quickly noticed by Patentlyze, the patent would monitor consenting users' devices and assign them AI training workloads during periods of low or no usage. Users might receive store credit or advanced access to AI models as compensation.
As the patent explains, training AI models requires massive processing power, and GPUs are uniquely suited to these tasks. Furthermore, the computational cost of training models is growing with their complexity.
Those costs are also straining GPU manufacturing capacity. Memory shortages from the AI data center buildout aren't the only reason consumer GPUs are becoming unaffordable. The situation has also made server GPUs a more lucrative use of wafers for GPU manufacturers than manufacturing RTX 5090s. AMD CEO Lisa Su recently described the GPU builder as a data center-first company.
The RAM market is experiencing a more extreme version of the problem, increasing prices of various consumer devices. Manufacturing capacity is becoming so strained that Sam Altman recently claimed RAM is more useful in AI companies' servers than in home devices, where it often sits idle. The comments drew widespread anger. Microsoft's patent would claw back some of that idle GPU capacity.
Its first diagram shows a training network consisting of servers, desktop PCs, and smartphones, suggesting Microsoft's system could also tap into idle mobile devices.
Microsoft would monitor their CPU and GPU utilization, memory usage, temperature, power consumption, memory bandwidth, and compute queue depth to determine how much they can spare and when.
Training workloads would be divided into micro-tasks and assigned to subscribed devices based on availability and their reputation for accurate results. Users who consent to lending their spare cycles to AI training might receive monetary compensation, software credits, or access to the models they help train.
It remains unclear whether this patent will see the light of day, but AI-related patents have become a trend in the years since the boom started. A recent one from Microsoft proposes editing livestreams in real time to rewrite or translate words while adjusting speakers' lip movements to match.

articles.title: Meta's AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meta is bringing its Muse AI agent to the Apple Watch and Android’s Wear OS, the company announced on Monday. With the launch, users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation directly on their smartwatch.
The smartwatch launch comes just a month after Meta introduced a dedicated iPad app for Muse. First launched on the App Store in September, the AI assistant’s expansion across Apple devices signals Meta’s growing ambitions for its consumer AI product and its focus on making Muse a central part of its ecosystem.
Muse is now one of dozens of consumer-facing AI agents competing for users’ attention. Like many of its competitors, it allows users to connect their accounts to manage email, meetings, bills, and more, while also handling tasks such as booking reservations, ordering groceries, setting goals, and making purchases.
Users can also personalize their Muse avatar to their liking and change it into something that resembles a person, an animal, or another type of character.
Despite being a relatively new product, Meta has wasted little time introducing new capabilities to Muse.
A few days ago, Meta launched Spaces, a new way to communicate and collaborate with Muse. Spaces function as dedicated conversations around specific topics, which Meta describes as “custom experiences” as they’re mini apps that are built on the fly. They appear in the sidebar of the Muse interface and bring up a focused conversation where the AI agent works toward a particular goal on the user’s behalf.
Last week, Meta rolled out the ability for users in the U.S. to video chat with their Muse AI avatar. Meta said Muse will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that reflect the tone and context of the conversation as it speaks. It’s worth noting that Muse doesn’t actually see users, but can hear them and respond in real time.
Shortly after its launch, Muse became one of just 12 mobile apps to have surpassed 10 million U.S. downloads within their first 40 days in the App Store. Only 11 other apps have achieved this milestone, with Meta’s Threads being the most recent in July 2023.

articles.title: Reducing Lithography Learning Cycles To Accelerate FOPLP Ramps
articles.text:
How yield prediction technology can reduce trial-and-error in advanced packaging lithography.
For manufacturers scaling advanced AI packages, pressure is mounting from every direction.
On one side, demand continues to rise.
While on another, AI packages are growing larger and integrating more high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and high-performance chips.
And that’s to say nothing of the production teams who face increasing pressure to ramp new processes quickly.
While achieving high yield remains a critical goal, success increasingly depends on how quickly manufacturers can establish stable process conditions and transition from development to high-volume manufacturing (HVM).
Fan-out panel-level packaging (FOPLP) has emerged as an attractive path forward for manufacturers looking to scale advanced packaging production.
Compared with traditional wafer-based approaches, FOPLP can significantly improve substrate utilization while increasing the number of packages produced per substrate. In one study comparison, a 300mm wafer achieved approximately 55% substrate utilization with six packages per wafer, while a 300mm panel achieved 86% utilization with 12 packages per panel and a 510 × 515mm panel achieved 74% utilization with 30 packages per panel. This enables manufacturers to improve manufacturing efficiency and reduce costs per package.
However, realizing those benefits requires overcoming significant lithography challenges.
As panel sizes increase, manufacturers must contend with pattern distortion, die shift, and resulting overlay errors across the substrate. These effects directly impact yield and make process optimization substantially more difficult.
Unlike traditional wafer-based processes, panel-scale variation does not behave uniformly. Instead, distortion patterns can vary significantly across the panel, creating localized challenges that are difficult to correct using conventional approaches.
Ultimately, process engineers must identify the “sweet spot” between overlay yield and throughput. To compensate for panel-level distortion, manufacturers typically rely on a range of correction strategies.
Global correction maintains throughput but often leaves localized overlay errors uncorrected. Zone correction can improve yield, with field data in our study indicating yields between 40% and 80%, but at reduced throughput. Die-by-die correction can further improve yield but introduces a significant throughput penalty. Site-by-site correction offers a compromise, balancing yield improvement with higher throughput.
However, finding that balance is rarely straightforward.
Identifying the optimal operating window often requires repeated experimentation across variables, such as exposure field configurations, die layouts, panel layouts, and overlay thresholds. Each adjustment can require another trial run and another round of data analysis. The result is increased engineering effort, additional material consumption, longer development cycles, and delayed production ramps.
For manufacturers under pressure to bring capacity online quickly, every additional iteration delays the path to production.
By combining offline metrology data with yield prediction algorithms, manufacturers can evaluate process performance before committing to extensive physical trials. Instead of repeatedly testing possible operating conditions on production hardware, engineering teams can assess likely yield outcomes in advance and identify promising process windows earlier in the development cycle.
The process begins with detailed metrology measurements that capture panel-scale variation, including pattern errors and die shifts. Yield prediction algorithms then evaluate this information alongside process variables, such as exposure field configuration, panel layout, die layout, and overlay thresholds. Using these inputs, manufacturers can estimate expected yield performance and compare alternative process strategies without executing full production experiments.
The value extends beyond simple prediction. Visualization tools such as heat maps, vector plots, histograms, and yield dashboards help engineers understand process sensitivities, isolate sources of variation, and identify root causes more quickly (Figure 1). This enables more targeted process optimization and faster decision making.
Fig. 1: Yield prediction analysis tools showing 1) parameters for analysis, 2) X-axis overlay error and 3) Y-axis overlay error. A comparison of these maps reveals that the Y-axis exhibits the most significant overlay errors, which directly contribute to yield loss. This insight enables users to pinpoint the root cause of the issue and take corrective actions effectively, thereby improving overall process performance.
Yield prediction technology has also been evaluated using production substrates in an HVM process. In the initial assessment, differences between predicted and measured yield ranged from 1.2% to 2.7%. Further analysis showed that variability in manual inspection judgments was the primary source of the discrepancies. After the inspection process was standardized, prediction errors were reduced to 0.2% to 0.8%.
During process development, manufacturers can use yield prediction technology to evaluate process conditions through simulation before running qualification substrates (Figure 2). Rather than relying exclusively on physical experimentation, engineers can evaluate multiple parameter combinations, identify promising operating conditions, and then use qualification substrates to validate the predictions. This approach can reduce trial-and-error iterations while accelerating process refinement and shortening development timelines.
Fig. 2: Residual overlay error vector maps generated under various process conditions help accelerate process refinement, reduce trial-and-error iterations and improve efficiency during R&D.
Just as important, it helps engineering teams focus their efforts on optimization rather than repetitive trial-and-error experimentation.
The benefits of yield prediction technology can also extend beyond process development. In mass production, the technology can be integrated into the lithography workflow for real-time, in-line process monitoring and earlier defect detection.
A standard lithography workflow includes multiple process steps before final inspection determines overlay yield. Errors introduced along the way can result in rework or permanent yield loss. By integrating yield prediction earlier in the workflow, manufacturers can identify potential problems before final inspection, enabling earlier intervention while reducing the manpower, time and costs associated with rework (Figure 3).
Fig. 3: Yield prediction technology can be integrated into the production workflow to support real-time, in-line process monitoring and earlier defect detection.
This extends the role of yield prediction from accelerating process development to supporting process monitoring and early defect detection during mass production.
As demand for advanced AI packages continues to rise, manufacturers face growing pressure to establish stable processes, protect yield, and move from development to HVM more quickly. FOPLP offers compelling economic advantages, but pattern distortion, die shift, and yield/throughput tradeoffs can lengthen process learning cycles and delay production ramps.
Yield prediction technology gives manufacturers a way to address these challenges from process development through mass production. During development, this technology can reduce trial-and-error iterations and accelerate process refinement. In mass production, real-time, in-line monitoring can support earlier defect detection and intervention. By incorporating these capabilities into their FOPLP lithography strategies, manufacturers can spend less time finding the right process conditions and advance more efficiently toward stable, high-yield production.

articles.title: L’Europe a tranché : refuser le Linky n’est pas un droit, la facture des réfractaires flambe — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les compteurs communicants, comme Linky, sont déployés à travers l’Union européenne pour contribuer à la modernisation des réseaux électriques. Ils permettent également aux consommateurs de suivre leurs usages et d’adapter leurs habitudes de consommation en conséquence.
Mais ces boîtiers intelligents n’ont pas que des adeptes. Leur déploiement suscite encore de nombreuses contestations, les principaux arguments avancés étant les craintes liées aux ondes électromagnétiques et à la protection des données personnelles.
Les réfractaires sont-ils pour autant en droit de refuser l’installation d’un compteur communicant ? Dans un arrêt rendu le jeudi 5 novembre, la Cour de justice de l’Union européenne (CJUE) a répondu par la négative, et sa lecture du droit européen vaut pour tous les États membres, France comprise.
Refuser Linky n’est pas un droit garanti
À la suite d’une affaire portée devant la justice autrichienne, concernant une cliente qui refusait le remplacement de son ancien compteur électrique, la CJUE a rendu un arrêt le 5 novembre 2026. La Cour estime que le droit européen ne garantit pas aux consommateurs la possibilité de conserver indéfiniment un compteur électrique classique. En d’autres termes, les gestionnaires de réseaux, comme Enedis en France, ne sont pas tenus de se conformer aux demandes des particuliers qui souhaitent conserver leur ancien équipement. « La CJUE siffle la fin du match sur le prétendu droit à s’opposer à Linky », résume l’avocat français Alexandre Archambault dans un message publié sur X.
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le YUKA mini 2 500 passe à 599 € au lieu de 799 € ! Plug & Play, sans fil périmétrique à enterrer, zéro installation prise de tête. Bref, déballez, lancez, et dites adieu à la tonte !
Le litige opposait une cliente au gestionnaire de réseau autrichien Netz Niederösterreich, qui voulait remplacer son vieux compteur mécanique, dont la période de vérification avait expiré, par un compteur numérique réglé en mode « opt-out ». Selon le gestionnaire, ce réglage se limite à un relevé à distance une fois par an. La CJUE ne tranche pas le litige elle-même : saisie par le tribunal régional de Sankt Pölten, elle interprète le droit européen, et c’est la justice autrichienne qui statuera sur le fond. Cette interprétation s’impose en revanche aux tribunaux de tous les États membres.
En France, il reste des opposants au Linky, même si Enedis affirme avoir presque achevé son déploiement, entamé en 2015. Le gestionnaire revendique 38,7 millions de compteurs installés en 2026, soit plus de 95 % des foyers qu’il dessert, ce qui laisse au plus 2 millions de foyers environ avec un ancien compteur.
En France, l’article L. 341-4 du Code de l’énergie impose aux gestionnaires de réseau de moderniser les compteurs pour favoriser la transition énergétique. La pose du compteur Linky est donc obligatoire pour les foyers raccordés au réseau d’Enedis.
La justice française avait déjà tranché dans le même sens. Dans un arrêt du 9 avril 2025, la Cour de cassation a donné raison à Enedis face à deux clientes qui refusaient la pose d’un Linky, en estimant que les usagers « ne pouvaient s’opposer à l’installation d’un compteur Linky sur leur propriété ».
La directive européenne 2019/944 sur le marché de l’électricité, que la Cour a interprétée, protège le droit des consommateurs à une mesure exacte de leur consommation, mais n’en tire aucun droit général de s’opposer à l’installation d’un compteur communicant.
L’arrêt traite aussi de la question des données, que soulèvent de nombreux opposants. La Cour estime que la règle de consentement de la directive « vie privée et communications électroniques », celle qui encadre les traceurs en ligne, ne s’applique pas au réseau électrique qui transmet les relevés du compteur. Les données de consommation restent en revanche protégées par le RGPD : leur collecte, leur conservation et leur sécurité doivent toujours reposer sur un cadre légal adapté.
Refuser l’accès au logement reste possible, mais pas sans conséquences financières
Si, en droit, les consommateurs ne peuvent pas refuser l’installation d’un compteur Linky, certains invoquent la propriété privée pour empêcher les techniciens d’entrer chez eux. Enedis ne peut effectivement pas forcer l’entrée d’un particulier pour procéder au remplacement du compteur.
Lorsque le compteur se trouve à l’extérieur du logement ou dans un local commun accessible, le technicien peut procéder à son remplacement sans avoir à obtenir l’accord du propriétaire. En revanche, si le dispositif est situé à l’intérieur du domicile et que l’occupant refuse d’y laisser entrer le technicien, son remplacement ne peut être imposé de force. Ce deuxième cas sera considéré comme un refus et des frais seront appliqués en conséquence.
Depuis le 1er août 2025, les consommateurs qui refusent l’installation du Linky sans justification technique doivent en effet payer une composante tarifaire supplémentaire. Revalorisée au 1er août 2026, elle atteint désormais 40,08 € HT par an (contre 38,88 € HT l’an dernier), facturée 6,68 € HT tous les deux mois. Ce surcoût s’applique même aux foyers qui transmettent régulièrement leurs relevés de consommation.
Si aucun relevé réel n’a été communiqué depuis plus de douze mois, des frais de relevé de 4,27 € HT tous les deux mois s’y ajoutent, soit 25,62 € HT par an, ce qui porte la note à 65,70 € HT par an. L’ensemble de ces frais est suspendu dès la demande de rendez-vous pour poser un Linky, et jusqu’à son installation effective.

articles.title: Google corrige en urgence une faille zero-day dans Chrome, déjà exploitée par des pirates
articles.text:
Google vient de publier une nouvelle mise à jour de sécurité pour Chrome. Elle corrige neuf vulnérabilités, dont une faille zero-day déjà exploitée dans des attaques. Le correctif est disponible sur Windows, macOS et Linux.
Trois jours. C’est le temps qu’il aura fallu à Google pour corriger une faille de Chrome signalée le 6 novembre par un chercheur anonyme. Bien que cette vulnérabilité ne soit pas classée critique, son exploitation dans des attaques est déjà confirmée. Il faut donc mettre à jour son navigateur sans attendre, d’autant que le patch corrige six autres failles de gravité élevée et deux de gravité moyenne.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Un exploit confirmé, des détails encore sous clé
Référencée CVE-2026-125350, la vulnérabilité touche le composant chargé du traitement des données XML dans Chrome. Il s’agit d’une erreur de type use-after-free, qui survient lorsqu’un programme continue d’utiliser une zone de mémoire après l’avoir libérée. Selon les circonstances, ce défaut peut provoquer un plantage ou permettre à un attaquant de corrompre la mémoire du navigateur pour y exécuter du code malveillant.
Google n’a pas détaillé la manière dont les pirates exploitent la faille. On ignore donc si la simple consultation d'une page web piégée suffit à déclencher une attaque, et aucune information n'a été communiquée sur les cibles visées. L’entreprise limite également l’accès aux détails techniques tant qu’une majorité d’internautes n'a pas installé le correctif, pour contenir le risque de nouvelles exploitations.
Une seconde faille de même nature a aussi été corrigée dans le traitement du XML, sans exploitation signalée cette fois. Les autres failles touchent des fonctions différentes de Chrome : V8, qui exécute le JavaScript des pages web, FileSystem, qui gère certains accès aux fichiers, et plusieurs composants chargés de l’affichage et du rendu graphique. Elles concernent notamment des erreurs de gestion de la mémoire et un défaut de contrôle des autorisations. Deux vulnérabilités de gravité moyenne affectent par ailleurs la partie graphique du navigateur.
Chrome est-il à jour ? Les versions à vérifier
Google a intégré ces correctifs aux versions 157.0.8103.50 et 157.0.8103.51 de Chrome pour Windows et macOS, ainsi qu’à la version 157.0.8103.50 pour Linux. Le canal Extended Stable, principalement destiné aux entreprises, bénéficie également du patch de la faille exploitée avec la version 156.0.8078.96 sur Windows et macOS.
La mise à jour est en cours de déploiement et pourrait prendre plusieurs jours pour atteindre l’ensemble des internautes. Pour vérifier votre version, ouvrez le menu de Chrome, puis rendez-vous dans Aide > À propos de Google Chrome. Le navigateur recherchera les mises à jour disponibles et vous proposera de le relancer pour appliquer les correctifs. Sur Linux, vous pouvez aussi passer par le gestionnaire de paquets de votre distribution.
Enfin, les autres navigateurs reposant sur Chromium, comme Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera ou Vivaldi, pourraient être concernés par cette vulnérabilité. Leurs utilisateurs et utilisatrices devront vérifier la disponibilité des patchs propres à chaque éditeur.

articles.title: Grants aren’t a consolation prize: rethinking non-dilutive capital for early-stage founders - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Ask an African founder how they funded their first year and you will often hear a slightly apologetic answer: “We did some grants while we figured out the VC side”. The tone matters. It suggests grants are what you take when the real money says “no” – a holding pattern, a consolation prize for not yet being fundable.
That framing is out of date, and it is costing founders. With venture capital still selective after the funding correction of the last few years, a growing number of early-stage startups across the continent are being built on government grants, foundation programmes, fellowships, cloud credits and small cheques from Web3 ecosystem funds.
The founders who will come out ahead are not the ones who tolerate this capital until a seed round arrives. They are the ones who stack it on purpose.
The recovery didn’t reach the bottom of the funnel
On paper, African tech funding has bounced back. Total investment into the African tech startup ecosystem increased by almost 50 per cent to US$1.64 billion in 2025. Q3 figures for 2026 were up 70 per cent on the corresponding period in 2025, suggesting 2026 will equal or surpass 2025 in terms of funding raised.
That is a healthy sign for scaled fintechs and energy businesses. It is far less comforting for a two-person team in Kigali or Lagos with a prototype and 10 paying customers. Investors are rewarding traction and clear paths to profit, which means the gap between “idea” and “venture-backable” has widened, not narrowed.
Founders have filled that gap with whatever capital doesn’t ask for equity: national innovation agency grants, foundation-backed programmes, fellowships with stipends, prize money from pitch competitions, hyper-scaler cloud credits, and – increasingly – grants and small cheques from blockchain ecosystem funds looking for builders in emerging markets. What began as survival has quietly become a funding layer of its own.
Why “consolation prize” is the wrong frame
The case for taking grants seriously starts with arithmetic. A founder who gives up 10 to 15 per cent of the company in a pre-seed round to buy 12 months of runway has paid for that time with the most expensive currency they own. A founder who buys the same 12 months with three grants and a credits package has paid in paperwork. That is not a lesser outcome. On a cap table, it is a better one.
The second argument is about control. Early VC money arrives with expectations about market size, speed and exit that can push a startup into a shape it isn’t ready for. Grant money gives founders room to do the slow, unglamorous work – regulatory approvals, pilots with public health systems, agri-tech field trials – that many African businesses need before they can scale at all. In sectors such as climate, health and agriculture, the patient capital is often the right capital.
Third, grants are increasingly a signal, not a stigma. Getting through a competitive government or foundation process means a third party has vetted the team, the problem and the budget. Smart investors read that as reduced risk. A startup that walks into a seed conversation with US$150,000 in non-dilutive funding, a pilot and a clean cap table is negotiating from strength, not asking for rescue.
How to stack it on purpose
The difference between a founder who “did some grants” and one who built a non-dilutive capital stack is intent. The second founder treats grants the way a CFO treats a funding plan: mapped, sequenced and tied to milestones. In practice, that looks like five habits.
- Give every source a job. Cloud and software credits cover infrastructure. Research and innovation grants pay for product development and pilots. Fellowships buy founder time and networks. A Web3 ecosystem grant funds a specific integration or open-source component. When each pot has a defined purpose, they complement each other instead of overlapping.
- Sequence from small to large. A US$5,000 competition win or an accelerator stipend is rarely life-changing, but it is evidence. Use the smaller, faster awards to build a track record that makes the larger, slower government or foundation grants easier to win.
- Run it like a pipeline, not a lottery. Keep a calendar of deadlines, eligibility rules and reporting dates across the year. Many founders apply reactively to whatever lands in a WhatsApp group. The ones who win consistently plan 6-12 months ahead and reuse a core application they sharpen each time.
- Tie grants to the milestones investors care about. Work backwards from the seed round you eventually want. If investors will ask for a regulatory licence, a paid pilot or a first 1,000 users, point grant money directly at those proofs. Non-dilutive capital is most powerful when it de-risks the next equity cheque.
- Read the fine print as a stack, not one by one. Matching-fund requirements, IP clauses, exclusivity terms and restrictions on other funding sources can clash. Check how each new award interacts with the ones you already hold before you sign.
Free money isn’t free
None of this means grants are costless. The most common failure is the professional applicant: a startup that becomes very good at winning programmes and much less good at winning customers. African tech has had its fair share of these. If a founder spends more hours on application forms than on sales calls, the stack has become a crutch.
Reporting is the second hidden cost. Several concurrent grants can mean several sets of quarterly reports, audits and site visits, each in a different format. For a team of three, that overhead is real and should be budgeted for, in time and sometimes in a part-time grants manager.
Third is mission drift. Funders have their own priorities, from gender inclusion to climate impact to digital public goods. Those are often worthy, but a founder who bends the product to fit each new call ends up with a company built to satisfy funders rather than a market.
Web3 money deserves its own warning. Ecosystem grants can be generous and fast, but they may be paid in volatile tokens, tied to building on one chain, or come with expectations about promotion and community activity. Convert what you can, understand any lock-ups, and make sure the protocol’s fortunes are not quietly becoming your own.
Stop apologising for it
The ecosystem has a part to play too. Governments and foundations could make stacking easier by harmonising reporting templates and being explicit about which other funding they allow alongside their own. Investors could stop treating a grant-heavy history as a red flag and start asking the more useful question: what did this founder achieve with the money?
But the biggest shift has to come from founders themselves. Non-dilutive capital is not what you settle for when VCs say no. Used well, it is how you get to a VC conversation on your own terms – or, for some businesses, how you avoid needing one at all. Stack it deliberately, point it at real milestones, and stop apologising for it.

articles.title: Netflix despide a unos 1000 empleados
articles.text:
Netflix anunció el despido de unos 1.000 trabajadores, una cifra que representa cerca del 6 % de su plantilla mundial. Este es el mayor recorte de personal que realiza la compañía desde 2022 y llega en un momento clave en el que la atención por captar la atención de los usuarios crece, e incluso ante plataformas gratuitas como YouTube.
Según adelantó The Wall Street Journal, los consejeros delegados Greg Peters y Ted Sarandos comunicaron la decisión a los empleados mediante un correo electrónico. La mayoría de los despidos se concentran en los departamentos de producto, tecnología, asuntos jurídicos y recursos humanos, aunque los responsables de Netflix aseguran que la empresa sigue creciendo y que cumplirá sus previsiones económicas para este año.
Netflix perdió la oportunidad de comprar Warner Bros. frente a Paramount
Los despidos también llegan después de que Netflix perdiera frente a Paramount Skydance la puja por los estudios y el negocio de streaming de Warner Bros. Discovery. Paramount completó la adquisición en octubre por una operación valorada en unos 110.000 millones de dólares, dando lugar a uno de los grandes grupos de entretenimiento del sector.
Mientras tanto, Netflix intenta ampliar su negocio más allá de las suscripciones tradicionales, apostando por los videojuegos, los eventos en directo y los planes con publicidad. Eso sí, sus responsables han dejado claro en el correo que seguirán invirtiendo en las áreas que consideran prioritarias, aunque para ello hayan decidido reducir su plantilla.

articles.title: Beyond the cloud: Why businesses are turning to on-device AI
articles.text:
Beyond the cloud: Why businesses are turning to on-device AI
At TechSparks 2026, Brilyant CEO Akash Saxenaa explained how running AI models locally can help businesses control costs, protect sensitive data, and reduce their dependence on the cloud.
AI tools have made it easier for businesses to analyze documents, generate content, and automate tasks. But how much do companies know about where the data they enter into these tools goes?
At TechSparks 2026, Akash Saxenaa, CEO of Brilyant, discussed why businesses should consider moving routine AI workloads from the cloud to local devices. He argued that on-device AI can help organizations manage costs, protect data, and reduce their dependence on internet connectivity.
The costs of taking AI to the cloud
The economics of AI are changing. While the cost of individual tokens may be falling, Saxenaa pointed out that inference costs could rise as businesses deploy more AI agents and consume more tokens. Citing Gartner, he referred to predictions that inference costs could increase more than fivefold.
Cost is only one concern. When employees use cloud-based AI tools, sensitive business information may leave the organization’s own environment. This raises questions about data privacy, intellectual property protection, and compliance with data protection requirements.
Saxenaa cited India's Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act as another reason for businesses to review their AI infrastructure.
“If you look at 83% of Indian enterprises, they have not yet begun comprehensive DPDP implementations, or they are not even aware. What is the cost? Rs 250 crore. Now, if you are a large company, 5,000 employees, that’s a budget line. But if you are an SMB, that's a company,” he said.
For smaller businesses, in particular, the financial consequences of non-compliance could be significant.
Saxenaa’s recommendation is to bring the model to the data rather than take the data to the model.
Not every task requires a frontier model
Saxenaa compared cloud-based AI tools such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude with on-device AI, where models run locally.
Cloud-based tools can involve recurring input and output token costs, latency, and less direct control over where data is processed. On-device AI, by contrast, can operate without an internet connection and does not incur recurring token charges for local inference.
“Almost 60-70% of your workload can move on to on-device. But the balance 30%, you will have to use large, complex, latest front-end AI models," Saxenaa said.
He stressed that the two approaches are not mutually exclusive. Businesses can use larger cloud-based models for complex tasks while moving suitable everyday workloads to local devices.
On-device AI: From the office to the factory floor
Saxenaa outlined several areas where businesses could use on-device AI, including endpoint security, support operations, internal search, and finance.
“There are these beautiful use cases out there for on-device: you look at endpoint security or support operations. All those things can be done on-device. You look at finance, local rack, internal search, finance, operations. Everything can be done on-device,” he said.
For software development teams, keeping code on local devices can reduce the risk of intellectual property being exposed through cloud-based tools.
In contact centers, on-device AI can support real-time call translation, note-taking, and product recommendations. These functions can operate locally, reducing dependence on network connectivity.
Saxenaa also highlighted devices equipped with neural processing units (NPUs), which allow AI models to run locally. This can help reduce recurring cloud costs while supporting data governance and operational resilience.
During his keynote, Saxenaa presented a case study involving Tech Paramount Solutions to show how on-device AI could be used in an industrial setting.
The company’s TP Smart Sol platform combines visitor and vehicle management, asset management, energy monitoring, surveillance, and workforce management.
With Brilyant's support, Tech Paramount Solutions explored using Apple's Mac mini as an edge-computing device to process video analytics locally, while keeping its platform connected to the cloud for alerts, dashboards, and remote access.
The setup can process live AI video analytics from around 100 on-premise cameras.
Tech Paramount Solutions' co-founder shared that deployment reduced annual security overhead by more than Rs 12 lakh, cut lifetime compute costs by over Rs 11 lakh per Mac mini compared with comparable GPU-based options, and increased factory machine uptime by more than 240 hours a month.
Making on-device AI work at scale
Moving AI workloads to local devices involves more than installing a model. Businesses also need to consider device management, security, governance, and the infrastructure required to support large-scale deployments.
Saxenaa explained how Brilyant works with partners including Apple and Jamf to provide device provisioning, AI setup, and lifecycle management. Leasing and financing options can help businesses spread the upfront cost of devices over time.
For organizations managing hundreds of laptops, Brilyant also offers containerized runtimes and governance measures designed to keep data within controlled environments.
The larger challenge is deciding which AI workloads should run locally, which require cloud-based models, and how to manage data and devices across an organization.
On-device AI will not eliminate the need for the cloud. However, as more capable models become available for local hardware, businesses have more options to balance cost, privacy, and performance.
For Saxenaa, the shift is not about using AI everywhere in the same way, but deciding where workloads should run and where business data should remain.

articles.title: Windows 11 KB5132061 & KB5131087 cumulative updates released
articles.text:
Microsoft has released the Patch Tuesday Windows 11 KB513261 and KB5131087 cumulative updates for versions 26H2/25H2/24H2 and 23H2 to fix security vulnerabilities and bugs and add new features.
Today's updates are mandatory as they contain the November 2026 Patch Tuesday security patches for hundreds of vulnerabilities discovered in previous months.
You can install today's update by going to Start > Settings > Windows Update and clicking on 'Check for Updates.'
You can also manually download and install the update from the Microsoft Update Catalog.
This is the eleventh 'Patch Tuesday' release in 2026, and it's based on 24H2, which means 25H2 or 26H2 get the same update. There are no exclusive or special changes. You'll get the same fixes across the two versions of Windows 11.
What's new in the November 2026 Patch Tuesday update
With today's update, Microsoft is adding new customization options to Windows 11 and fixing minor issues with File Explorer.
Here's the full list of improvements and fixes:
- [Context menu in File Explorer] 
  - New! This update introduces an updated context menu that is faster, simpler, and more customizable. The updated menu opens more quickly, reduces clutter, and gives you more control over the commands and app extensions that appear when you right-click.
		
    - You can now customize the context menu to better fit how you use Windows. Select Customize menu at the bottom of the context menu to open its Settings page.
			
      - Turn built-in Windows commands, such as Send to and Create shortcut, on or off.
      - Add commands such as Print to the context menu.
      - Choose which app extensions appear in the main menu or a submenu or hide the app extensions submenu.
      - Display Cut, Copy, Paste, Rename, Delete, and Share directly in the menu instead of as a row of icons.
      - Move Properties to the bottom of the context menu.
    - To personalize the context menu, right-click and select Customize menu, then choose the commands, app extensions, and layout you prefer. No action is required to use the default configuration. To see more options, hold down Shift and right-click on your desktop.
- [Modernized AutoPlay experience] 
  - New! This update modernizes the AutoPlay dialog that appears when you connect devices such as a phone, camera, or removable drive to your PC. The updated experience supports dark mode, responds better to text scaling and display settings, and makes AutoPlay notifications available in notification center for easier access.
- [File Explorer] 
  - New! Key file information, such as name, location, and date, now appear in a consistent layout on the File Explorer search results page, making search results easier to scan.
  - New! Address bar now supports ~, making it quicker to navigate directly to your user profile folder and subfolders (for example, ~\AppData).
  - New! This update enables dark mode support in the Folder Options dialog in File Explorer.
- [XBOX mode] 
  - New! This update introduces a refreshed Gaming Task View experience in XBOX mode, featuring a new navigation bar that provides quick access to Exit to Desktop and Power Options, making key system actions easier to access while gaming. 1
- [Settings] 
  - New! This update improves the Privacy & security page in Windows Settings by grouping related Camera, Microphone, and Location privacy controls and elevating usage information from linked pages onto the main page.
  - New! The Device Info card on the Settings Home page, first introduced in the March 2026 preview update KB5079391, is expanding to additional markets. Available to users signed in with a Microsoft account, the card provides a quick view of key PC specifications and usage, with more detailed device information available under Settings > System > About. 1
  - This update makes some small visual refinements to the design of the temporary files section under Settings > System > Storage.
- [Phone Link] 
  - New! You can now hover over a recent message or notification in the Recent section to preview its content directly in Start without opening the item. This experience can be managed under Phone Link > Settings > Start menu personalization.
- [Taskbar] 
  - New! The update improves animations of app window previews when mousing across app icons in the taskbar.
  - This update improves the underlying state persistence of taskbar settings related to multiple monitors across monitor connections and disconnections.
- [Magnifier] 
  - New! Magnifier now includes a contrast theme toggle that can reduce screen glare while keeping the original colors in photos, videos, and charts. The toggle applies a dark contrast theme by default and is available from the Magnifier toolbar. To choose a different contrast theme, go to Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier. Color inversion remains available as a separate option.
  - New! Magnifier now supports per-monitor zoom, allowing each display to use its own zoom level while keeping the magnified view within that display. To use per-monitor zoom, set your displays to Extend under Settings > System > Display.
		
    - To adjust a display, move your pointer to it and press Windows key + Plus (+) or Windows key + Minus (-), use Ctrl + Alt with the mouse wheel or move the Magnifier toolbar to that display and use its controls.
    - Per-monitor zoom is on by default. You can turn it off or adjust individual zoom levels from the Magnifier toolbar or under Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier.
  - New! Magnifier now supports viewport locking for multi-monitor setups with per-monitor zoom turned on. It keeps the magnified view on a display in place while you move the pointer to another display. The locked display remains interactive. Point to a display and press Ctrl + Windows key + K to lock or unlock its view.
		
    - Press Windows key + Esc to release all locked displays.
    - You can change the lock shortcut to Ctrl + Alt + P under Settings > Accessibility > Magnifier.
- [Live Captions] 
  - New! This update improves Live Captions with a new Include screen reader audio setting, which is off by default. With the setting off, Live Captions will not transcribe audio from screen readers such as Narrator, JAWS, and NVDA, keeping captions focused on microphone and system audio. To turn on this setting, go to Settings > Accessibility > Captions.
- [Narrator] 
  - New! Narrator now supports reading and navigating math equations in supported Microsoft 365 apps, including Word and PowerPoint, and supported web content in Microsoft Edge (version 153.0.4234.32 and later) and Google Chrome (version 153.0.8010.18 and later). This makes it easier for users who are blind or have low vision to understand and explore equations, formulas, and scientific notation.
		
    - Press Narrator key + Alt + N to turn on math navigation and use the arrow keys to explore parts of an equation. Press Esc to exit.
    - Math reading supports English (United States), English (United Kingdom), Traditional Chinese, Finnish, German, and Spanish. You can change the language and other math reading preferences in Narrator settings (Accessibility > Narrator > Math reading).
- [Family Safety] 
  - New! The update improves family safety messaging when applications are blocked because of age-restricted parental controls.
- [Recovery] 
  - New! This update enables Windows recovery (WinRE) to automatically reuse eligible Wi-Fi profiles already saved in Windows, including supported certificate-based networks. Devices can now get online automatically during recovery scenarios such as quick machine recovery or cloud rebuild, without preconfiguring Wi-Fi credentials in WinRE. This capability is on by default, and IT admins can disable it. This feature was previously disclosed last month and is now beginning to roll out.
  - To learn more, see Networking in WinRE.
- [Cloud rebuild] 
  - New! This update introduces Cloud rebuild, a new recovery option that reinstalls Windows 11 using a Windows image and device drivers downloaded from Windows Update, including when Windows is unable to start. No USB media or custom image is required. Cloud rebuild includes:
		
    - Drive sanitization: Choose to remove your files or securely erase data using the storage hardware’s erase capability before Windows is reinstalled. Sanitization is irreversible.
    - Remote management: IT administrators can configure and start a Cloud rebuild remotely through the Recovery CSP using either the currently installed build or a specified target build.
  - To start Cloud rebuild:
		
    - In Windows, go to Settings > System > Recovery, and then select Rebuild PC. The device restarts into the Windows Recovery Environment and starts Cloud rebuild.
    - Alternatively, if Windows can't start, the device enters the Windows Recovery Environment automatically after repeated boot failures. From the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE), select Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud rebuild.
    - Connect to a wired Ethernet or Wi-Fi network.
    - Review the target Windows build, edition, and language, and then confirm the data loss warning before the rebuild begins. You can choose whether to remove files or remove and sanitize files prior to Windows reinstalling.
  - To learn more, see Cloud rebuild.
- [Windows settings backup and restore] 
  - New! This update introduces a Restore Summary that appears after you restore a backup profile to a new device. The summary gives a clear overview of what was successfully restored, including Windows settings and the list of Microsoft Store apps. This improves transparency during device transitions and helps you validate your restore results and continue setup on your new device with confidence.
  - For more information see, Windows settings backup and restore overview.
- [Adaptive hibernate policy] 
  - New! This update improves the adaptive hibernate policy to provide more instant-on resumes from Modern Standby while helping preserve battery life when the charge is low. Noticeable changes include less hibernation while the battery is above 80% and hibernating sooner when the battery is below 10%.
- [Security] 
  - New! This update expands memory integrity protection across eligible devices. Supported PCs may now have memory integrity (HVCI) enabled during updates to help improve security and prepare devices for advanced Windows security features, while respecting existing user or IT administrator choices. For more information, see Expanding memory integrity protection across Windows devices.
- [Windows IPv6 networking support] 
  - New! Windows now supports IPv6 CLAT for Wi-Fi and Ethernet network interfaces, adding client-side 464XLAT translation so IPv4-only applications can continue reaching IPv4 services from IPv6-only networks. This helps organizations advance IPv6-only deployments while preserving compatibility for legacy IPv4 application scenarios.
		
    - Prefix discovery: PREF64 is discovered through Router Advertisements (RA) by default, with DNS ipv4only.arpa available as a fallback.
    - Requirements: CLAT requires SLAAC-based IPv6 addressing. DHCPv6 Prefix Delegation and Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL) are not currently supported.
    - Configuration: Enable CLAT by using netsh interface clat set global permit=enabled pref64fromdns=enabled pref64fromra=enabled or Group Policy under Network > TCPIP Settings > IPv6 Transition Technologies.
- [Data Protection API (DPAPI)] 
  - New! This update adds a warning before prompt-based protect and unprotect operations. The warning explains that this prompt-based experience will be retired in April 2027. If you or an app use these prompts, stop creating new prompt-protected data, use a supported non-interactive protection flow, and decrypt or migrate existing prompt-protected data before retirement. DPAPI operations that do not use the prompt-based flow aren't affected. For more details, see CRYPTPROTECT_PROMPTSTRUCT structure (dpapi.h).
- [Windows Spotlight] 
  - This update makes underlying platform changes to generally improve Windows Spotlight reliability on the lock screen.
- [Unicode] 
  - This update provides Windows text shaping support for Unicode 17.0, helping Windows correctly display and shape newly encoded characters and scripts. Unicode 17.0 added 4,803 characters, including support for four newly encoded scripts: Beria Erfe, Sidetic, Tai Yo, and Tolong Siki. These updates help keep Windows text support current as the Unicode Standard evolves and improve support for languages and writing systems used by people around the world.
Microsoft is not aware of any new issues with this month's Patch Tuesday, and it also patched a long-standing issue that broke USB audio on some PCs.

articles.title: China ha inventado un Frankenstein para sus cementerios de palas eólicas: una descarga de medio segundo para resucitarlas como grafeno
articles.text:
Con la energía eólica ocurre una cosa: tiene un problema del que se habla mucho menos que de sus beneficios. Nos referimos a qué hacer con sus gigantescas estructuras cuando dejan de funcionar, especialmente esas enormes palas aparentemente inútiles. China lleva tiempo buscando una respuesta, y un grupo de científicos acaba de demostrar que la solución podría ser tan brutal como sorprendente.
El cementerio de los gigantes verdes. Qué duda cabe, los aerogeneradores son uno de los grandes símbolos de la transición energética, pero esconden una paradoja: sus enormes palas son extraordinariamente difíciles de reciclar. Fabricadas con fibras de vidrio y resinas termoestables, están diseñadas para resistir décadas de viento y esfuerzos mecánicos.
El problema llega cuando terminan su vida útil, porque esas resinas no pueden fundirse y moldearse como los plásticos convencionales. Las alternativas pasan por enterrarlas, triturarlas o someterlas a tratamientos térmicos y químicos costosos que pueden deteriorar los materiales. Con millones de toneladas de residuos previstos para las próximas décadas, el sector necesita algo más que espacio para seguir acumulándolos.
El Frankenstein chino: 2.000 grados en medio segundo. Así, un equipo de la Universidad de Tsinghua, dirigido por Bing Deng, ha desarrollado una técnica que parece sacada de una novela de ciencia ficción: destruir las palas viejas mediante una descarga eléctrica para convertir sus restos en materiales con los que fabricar otras potencialmente mejores. ¿Cómo? Primero trituran las palas hasta convertirlas en polvo y lo mezclan con negro de carbono para hacerlo conductor.
Después aplican un pulso eléctrico mediante calentamiento Joule ultrarrápido que eleva la temperatura hasta unos 2.000 °C en apenas 0,5 segundos. La sílice de la fibra de vidrio se transforma en carburo de silicio y los compuestos carbonados de la resina generan grafeno. Lo sorprendente es que no necesitan separar previamente ambos materiales ni utilizar disolventes o catalizadores.
Resucitar una pala para fabricar otra mejor. La verdadera sorpresa llegó cuando incorporaron el material recuperado a una resina epoxi nueva. Con apenas un 0,3% en peso, consiguieron aumentar un 27% su rigidez a tracción y un 9% su rigidez a flexión, mientras que una proporción del 0,1% mejoró un 41% su difusividad térmica. El carburo de silicio aporta dureza y resistencia térmica, mientras que el grafeno destaca por sus propiedades mecánicas y conductoras.
Esta combinación podría permitir fabricar palas más resistentes y duraderas, e incluso ayudar a combatir la acumulación de hielo, explican. Con todo, un inciso: todavía no se han construido palas completas y los resultados proceden de ensayos con resinas de laboratorio.
La factura también podría salir a favor. Sí, el procedimiento promete recuperar materiales valiosos con una economía potencialmente mejor que otros métodos. Según los cálculos del equipo, procesar una tonelada de residuos podría generar unos 80 dólares de beneficio, frente a pérdidas estimadas de 460 dólares mediante pirólisis y 1.800 dólares con determinados tratamientos químicos.
El análisis ambiental también apunta a una reducción de emisiones del 83% respecto a la pirólisis y del 92% frente a la disolución química. La clave está en el calentamiento eléctrico ultrarrápido, que evita la combustión directa y transforma los residuos en productos de mayor valor. Eso sí, las estimaciones todavía excluyen gastos como la trituración, los equipos y otros costes operativos.
De diez gramos a montañas de residuos. El principal obstáculo es la escala. La mayoría de los experimentos se realizaron con apenas 0,3 gramos de material y los investigadores lograron aumentar los lotes hasta 10 gramos, manteniendo la producción de carburo de silicio y grafeno. También han diseñado un reactor para procesar 200 gramos, pero todavía deben demostrar que funciona con cantidades mucho mayores.
El desafío, por tanto, es considerable: las palas retiradas de un solo aerogenerador pueden sumar decenas de toneladas. Dicho esto, Deng aspira a desarrollar una instalación piloto capaz de procesar 100 toneladas como objetivo principal. También será necesario comprobar el consumo energético real y la durabilidad de los nuevos materiales.
EEUU también ve potencial en la descarga eléctrica. Porque el interés de esta tecnología no se limita a China. James Tour, químico de la Universidad Rice y pionero del calentamiento Joule ultrarrápido, considera que el experimento demuestra cómo transformar residuos difíciles de reciclar en materiales valiosos, aunque advierte de que todavía falta comprobar su eficacia industrial.
El procedimiento aprovecha tanto la fibra de vidrio como la resina, evitando tener que separarlas previamente y reduciendo la necesidad de tratamientos químicos. Su siguiente gran prueba será demostrar que el compuesto funciona en estructuras completas y que conserva sus propiedades durante años de funcionamiento. De ser así, la técnica podría abrir una nueva vía de reciclaje para materiales compuestos que hasta ahora resultaban especialmente problemáticos.
La segunda vida de los molinos podría empezar en sus propias ruinas. El descubrimiento va más allá de encontrar una forma de deshacerse de las palas viejas. Si funciona a escala industrial, permitiría convertir un residuo problemático en materia prima para fabricar nuevos componentes eólicos, reduciendo la dependencia de materiales vírgenes por el camino. Además, ofrecería una alternativa a los cementerios de palas que se acumulan conforme envejecen los parques eólicos.
Como vemos, todavía quedan obstáculos técnicos y económicos, pero la paradoja resume perfectamente el proyecto, el de una tecnología diseñada para producir energía limpia que podría encontrar parte de su futuro en los restos de sus propias máquinas, transformados mediante una descarga eléctrica de apenas medio segundo.
