articles.title: Acecore, Supplya and Navidyn are betting Nigeria can build, lend and dive for itself
articles.text:
A battery manufacturer, a lender serving small retailers, and a developer of underwater robots took the top three spots at TechCabal (TC) Battlefield during Moonshot in Lagos on October 29. Two of the three winners are building hardware in a country that relies heavily on imports for its technology products.
The annual competition brought ten startups before a panel of judges to pitch their businesses. Acecore won the $10,000 first prize, followed by Supplya, which received $5,000, and Navidyn, which took home $2,500. Supplya and Navidyn also earned places in Antler’s residency programme, giving them access to a potential $250,000 in pre-seed funding.
Acecore
Acecore started in Oyigbo, a town in Rivers State, where founder Caleb Iwuoha, an agricultural engineer with certificates in electrical and mechanical engineering, was assembling battery systems in a shed in 2024. He says monthly output has grown from 8kWh to more than 320kWh, and the company now runs a workshop and showroom. Iwuoha told the judges the casing and battery software were “all built here in Nigeria by our very own hands.”
The PowerCell is a battery backup that stores electricity from the grid or solar panels and powers a home or business when the grid goes down. A wall-mounted cabinet holds the battery, an inverter that turns the stored power into the kind of power appliances use, and a charge controller that protects the battery from overcharging.
Most buyers would otherwise wire those parts together separately or run a generator. An app called PowerCore tracks consumption and flags maintenance. A 5kVA, 10kWh unit, which can power several appliances at once while holding 10kWh of energy, starts at $5,250, and Sterling Bank, SunFi and Earthbond finance customers who cannot pay upfront. The company holds MANCAP certification and says it has $164,000 in purchase orders from buyers including Chopbox, PartyRice and Skydiamond Homes.
It names Lumos and Greenage Technologies among its rivals and says it undercuts the market by 10% to 20%. Its own comparison, $5,250 against $6,200 for a competitor’s cabinet of the same size, works out at roughly 15%, and one judge noted that imported Chinese systems land in Nigeria at a similar price. Iwuoha put his margin at 62%, leaving about $2,000 to build each unit.
The stronger case is local manufacturing in an imports-heavy market. Nigeria imported 1,721MW of Chinese solar panels in the year to June 2025, the second-highest in Africa, according to Ember.
Acecore does not say where its battery cells come from. The company projects 170 units and $892,000 in revenue for 2026, a figure that is consistent with its stated unit price. But it also reports $2.58 million from 340 units over ten months, implying a much higher average price than its own pricing supports. At its stated price, those 340 units would generate closer to $1.79 million. The $138,000 it reported for 2025 represents local purchase orders (LPOs)—commitments from buyers to purchase, not cash the company has collected.
Supplya
Founded in 2021, Supplya is led by chief executive Opeyemi Kehinde, who has a decade of experience in sales operations, and chief operating officer Joy Adeniran, an e-commerce entrepreneur.
It began as a marketplace where small retailers order directly from manufacturers and pay 30 days later at no interest. Chief technology officer Osama Okunbo previously worked at Access Bank, one of Nigeria’s largest commercial lenders. The company dates its current lending record from October 2024 and now calls itself a credit layer for informal commerce.
Retailers order stock through the platform, often over WhatsApp, and the credit attaches to the goods and not to cash, which the company says stops borrowers from diverting loans. Repayment comes from daily sales, and field officers who collect payments also sign up new shops. Ten manufacturers supply the platform, including Planet Bottling Company and Flour Mills of Nigeria.
The repayment record is the strongest of the three. Supplya claims it has financed more than $150,000 of inventory since October 2024, with 98% repaid over 18 months and defaults below 1%, across more than 120 monthly active retailers. These are encouraging figures on a small book, and Nigerian lenders know a portfolio can look excellent until it grows or the economy turns.
The World Bank said in December 2025 that fewer than one in 20 Nigerian small businesses can access bank credit, and PwC’s 2024 survey put the figure at about 4%. Omnibiz and TradeDepot, which Supplya names as rivals, supply goods, while the company wants retailers to buy from several vendors.
Supplya currently earns a 3% to 8% margin on the stock it sells. The company says its next revenue lines will be a 2% fee on credit used and a 1% commission on each marketplace sale. It is raising $250,000 in pre-seed funding and plans to put 45% of it, about $112,500, into expanding its credit pool. This would add roughly three quarters to the more than $150,000 of inventory it has financed since October 2024.
Navidyn
Navidyn built the robot before the company. Mechatronics engineer David Ojabo, according to the company, led core development of the prototype, which finished second at the 2025 Coderina University Challenge, known as COUCH, under the name Neuronaut Robotics at Nile University of Nigeria. The team says it also won first place at the 2025 SPE Africa Energy Challenge and placed second at the Red Bull Basement Nigeria final in April 2026.
Atabot is an observation-class remotely operated vehicle, or ROV, rated to 50 metres with a battery that lasts 36 minutes. Navidyn plans to rent it at $4,000 a day, add lump-sum fees for bigger jobs, and sell machines later. It will start with small and medium-sized offshore operators in shallow water, and wants $800,000 to finish a product, land a first recurring contract, and fund 18 months. It forecasts profit in year two and $1.82 million in operating profit by year five.
“Now it’s time to invest in advanced AI and robotics,” the cofounders told the judges.
Navidyn’s case rests on a shift in who owns Nigeria’s oil. Shell, ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies, Eni and Equinor have sold onshore and shallow water assets worth about $6 billion across 26 oil blocks to mostly Nigerian buyers since 2023, according to the Nigeria Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative. The local content regulator wants Nigerian firms to supply 70% of the industry’s goods and services by 2027, and it puts the current level at about 61%.
Its own competitor map lists Marine Platforms, Tilone, GOSL, Tallsea and Subsea 7, and Marine Platforms ordered two work-class ROVs from UK-based Forum Energy Technologies last October. Renting by the day puts Navidyn in the same business as operators that already own vessels, crews and imported fleets, and work-class machines handle jobs Atabot cannot yet do.
Navidyn’s list of 50 target companies splits into 23 small, 22 medium and 13 large, which adds up to 58. Ogaji also works as a lead engineer at a Texas-based drone manufacturer. At the pitch, the founders said that a Sahara Group representative offered a $5,000 inspection job before the product was ready. Securing more commitments like this will be important as Navidyn moves towards commercialising its technology.
The verdict
Acecore looks closest to a working business. It has orders, a workshop, and banks willing to finance buyers. What it has not shown is cash. Its $164,000 in purchase orders are promises to buy, and a price only slightly below imports leaves little room for error. It is worth backing if those orders turn into paid and delivered units.
Supplya has the best repayment record of the three, but $150,000 of financing is a small book. We do not yet know how borrowers will behave once it starts charging fees. It is worth watching closely.
Navidyn has the boldest idea and the least to show for it. It has a prototype rated to 50 metres, no reported revenue, and a team that only formed this year. A first paid inspection job would change that.

articles.title: Robot aspirateur ou aspirateur laveur : lequel choisir pour garder un logement toujours propre ?
articles.text:
Entre le travail, les loisirs et les obligations du quotidien, les journées peuvent vite ressembler à une course-contre-la-montre et il est souvent difficile de trouver du temps pour faire le ménage. Et quand vous avez un instant pour vous, il va de soi que vous avez mieux à faire que sortir votre aspirateur et votre serpillière. Pourtant, il faut bien que quelqu’un s’y colle. Heureusement, les aspirateurs nouvelle génération permettent de simplifier l’entretien des sols, de limiter les efforts et de gagner du temps au quotidien.
Aujourd’hui, deux grandes familles d’appareils se distinguent. D’un côté, il y a les robots aspirateurs qui travaillent de manière autonome. De l’autre, on retrouve les aspirateurs laveurs, pour ceux qui veulent garder la main sans faire trop d’efforts pour nettoyer leurs sols en profondeur. Mais lequel choisir ? La réponse dépendra de vos habitudes et de vos besoins. Alors que le Black Friday approche, c’est le moment idéal pour vous pencher sur la question. Comme ça, vous allez pouvoir choisir votre allié du quotidien avec toutes les cartes en main.
Robot aspirateur ou aspirateur laveur : deux appareils, deux usages
Le robot aspirateur, c’est le roi de l’autonomie. Vous allez pouvoir lui déléguer une bonne partie du ménage. Il se déplace seul dans votre logement pour aspirer les sols et n’a pas besoin que vous soyez constamment derrière lui. Encore mieux ? Vous pouvez programmer des cycles de nettoyage pour qu’il se mette au boulot en votre absence. Comme ça, vous rentrez chez vous et vos sols sont impeccables. Le robot aspirateur est donc la meilleure solution pour les personnes qui désirent avoir un logement toujours propre sans y consacrer du temps. Aujourd’hui, les aspirateurs robots sont de plus en plus sophistiqués et évolués avec des stations multifonctions qui automatisent certaines opérations d’entretien tandis qu’ils peuvent même passer la serpillière.
Contrairement au robot aspirateur, l’aspirateur laveur s’utilise manuellement. Il combine aspiration et lavage afin d’éliminer la poussière mais aussi les saletés sèches comme les taches incrustées et les traces du quotidien. C’est l’appareil parfait pour les personnes qui veulent limiter leurs efforts au quotidien mais qui souhaitent tout de même garder le contrôle. C’est notamment intéressant pour les zones de passage, les accidents domestiques comme une tasse de café qu’on renverse ou tout simplement les sols qui ont besoin d’un nettoyage plus ciblé. Vous pouvez le dégainer quand vous en avez besoin.
Ainsi, le choix va surtout dépendre de votre logement, de vos besoins, de vos attentes et de vos modes de vie.
Quels critères prendre en compte avant de choisir ?
Entre aspirateur laveur et robot aspirateur, il faut maintenant choisir. Plusieurs éléments sont à prendre en compte. La superficie de votre logement n’est pas à négliger. Effectivement, un robot aspirateur est redoutablement pratique dans une maison ou dans un grand appartement alors qu’un aspirateur laveur s’avère plus intéressant pour cibler certaines surfaces. Ensuite, il faut penser à la configuration de vos pièces. Présence de meubles, de tapis, d’obstacles, de seuils ou de passage étroits… Tout ça est à prendre en compte. L’intelligence de navigation et la capacité à franchir certains obstacles peuvent faire la différence pour un robot aspirateur.
De même, il est important de s’assurer que l’appareil est adapté à la nature de vos sols (carrelage, parquet, sols durs ou tapis). Enfin, vous devez considérer votre quotidien, notamment si vous avez des enfants ou des animaux de compagnie. Certains foyers ont besoin d’un entretien régulier et automatisé alors que d’autres nécessitent un nettoyage plus ciblé.
Roborock : des solutions adaptées à différents besoins
À l’heure actuelle, Roborock est un acteur incontournable quand on parle de ménage. Il est aujourd’hui le leader mondial en robotique domestique ultra-intelligente conçue pour simplifier la vie quotidienne. Fort de 10 années d’expérience, Roborock s’efforce d’être toujours en adéquation avec les besoins et les attentes des consommateurs et de répondre véritablement à leurs problématiques. Le Roborock Saros 20 et le Roborock F25 Ultra sont deux références qui répondent à des usages bien distincts.
Pour celles et ceux qui veulent déléguer au maximum le ménage, le Roborock Saros 20 mise sur l’autonomie et l’intelligence de navigation. Ce robot aspirateur embarque notamment le système StarSight 2.0, capable de cartographier précisément les pièces et de reconnaître plus de 300 types d’obstacles. Il peut ainsi adapter ses déplacements afin d’éviter les objets qui se dressent en travers de son chemin. Son châssis AdaptiLift 3.0, lui, permet de franchir les seuils à deux niveaux pouvant atteindre 8,8 cm. Avec une puissance d’aspiration HyperForce de 36 000 Pa et son double système anti-enchevêtrement, il est également conçu pour récupérer efficacement la poussière, les cheveux et les poils d’animaux. Sa station RockDock automatise par ailleurs plusieurs opérations d’entretien, que vous n’avez donc pas à gérer. De quoi profiter d’un nettoyage régulier sans avoir à sortir soi-même l’aspirateur à chaque fois.
À l’inverse, si vous préférez garder la main sur le nettoyage de vos sols, le Roborock F25 Ultra constitue une option plus intéressante. Cet aspirateur laveur combine l’aspiration et le lavage en un seul et unique passage, avec une particularité : il propose deux technologies de nettoyage à haute température. VaporFlow utilise de la vapeur pouvant atteindre 180°C pour s’attaquer aux taches les plus incrustées tandis que WaveFlow diffuse de l’eau chaude à 86°C pour dissoudre notamment les salissures grasses. Avec ses 22 000 Pa de puissance d’aspiration, le Roborock F25 Ultra prend aussi en charge les déchets secs et humides du quotidien. Sa technologie SlideTech 2.0 facilite les déplacements alors que FlatReach 2.0 permet de nettoyer sous les meubles en inclinant l’appareil à plat. Cerise sur le gâteau ? Son rouleau bénéficie d’un système d’auto-nettoyage et de séchage à l’air chaud pouvant atteindre 95°C. C’est un vrai plus pour éviter de devoir entretenir manuellement l’appareil après chaque utilisation.
Robot aspirateur ou aspirateur laveur… En vérité, il n’existe pas de réponse universelle. Comme nous l’avons vu ensemble, tout dépend de vos besoins et de vos habitudes. L’essentiel reste de choisir un appareil qui facilite réellement l’entretien de votre logement. Avec des références comme le Saros 20 et F25 Ultra, Roborock propose différentes solutions pour y parvenir. À l’approche du Black Friday, c’est donc le bon moment pour découvrir sa gamme et découvrir les offres exceptionnelles de Roborock.

articles.title: France says Iran was behind supermarket refrigerator cyberattacks
articles.text:
What just happened? France has accused Iran of being responsible for the recent cyberattacks that targeted its supermarket refrigerators. The incidents affected more than 700 stores in October, before other European countries were also hit. France says it will take action using "all available means of response."
On October 11 and 12, stores across France experienced cyberattacks that took control of their refrigeration controllers. The hackers remotely overrode the settings on freezers, fridges and chiller cabinets, in some cases raising temperatures to 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit), spoiling food and causing at least 15 fires. France put the cost of food losses alone in the tens of millions of euros.
At a press briefing following a G7 ministerial meeting in Paris, France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said, "Thanks to the remarkable efforts of government agencies, I am able to confirm that the Islamic Republic of Iran's Revolutionary Guards are responsible for this attack."
France identified the group behind the attacks as Shahid Kaveh, an offensive cyber unit affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards. It operates through several online personas, including CyberAv3ngers, a name previously linked to attacks on US water facilities.
According to a joint report from France's cyber crisis coordination body, C4, infrastructure used in the supermarket attacks was also probing Schneider Electric equipment at energy and water facilities. That reconnaissance used the Modbus industrial communications protocol over port 502, matching techniques associated with Shahid Kaveh since at least April 2026.
Investigators also identified use of FOFA, an internet-connected device search and scanning tool regularly used by the unit. They found traces of Farsi in the attack infrastructure, while CyberbanNews, an outlet French authorities link to the group, publicized the attacks as early as October 13.
Earlier this month, similar attacks subsequently hit stores in at least seven European countries. One Belgian Delhaize store estimated its losses at €100,000 ($112,196).
The disruption also reached France's national blood service through a refrigeration supplier. Fortunately, alarms alerted staff, who moved the stock before any biological materials were lost.
French prosecutors have opened a judicial investigation and requested international arrest warrants against members of Shahid Kaveh, meaning there will be a criminal case in addition to the diplomatic and potential cyber response.
France summoned Iran's ambassador on November 10 and is pushing for EU sanctions. Barrot has also left open the possibility of further measures that would remain undisclosed.
France's attribution points to Iran, despite earlier reports that Russia-aligned hacking groups had claimed responsibility for refrigeration attacks in Europe.

articles.title: Google says Gemini 4 Carbon proved Signal’s encryption in weeks
articles.text:
Google says Gemini 4 Carbon proved Signal’s encryption in weeks
Google released Gemini 4 Carbon to paying developers Tuesday, positioning its newest frontier model above Gemini 4 Argon for complex software engineering, cybersecurity, and scientific reasoning.
Argon remains Google’s recommended model for everyday engineering and knowledge work. while Carbon is designed for more demanding tasks, including multi-package migrations, cross-subsystem debugging, and long-horizon agentic workflows.
Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP of Google DeepMind and Google’s chief AI architect, described Carbon in the launch announcement as the company’s strongest model for complex, multi-step work.
The release also introduces /swarm, a preview feature in Google Antigravity that coordinates multiple coding agents from a single prompt.
Multi-agent coding arrives
Carbon can build, test, and debug full-stack applications, checking both the code and rendered UI. Google says it performs particularly well on multi-package migrations and debugging across subsystems.
What Google hasn’t explained is how /swarm shares context between agents, handles conflicting changes, or decides which tasks need Carbon instead of a lighter model.
Google claims Carbon ranks first on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity’s WANDR and Zapier’s AutomationBench, completing tasks at less than half the cost of the next-best model.
What Google hasn’t explained is how /swarm shares context between agents, handles conflicting changes, or decides which tasks need Carbon instead of a lighter model.
Pricing doubles November 30
The company hasn’t provided enough detail to independently verify those cost comparisons. Carbon launches at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, matching Argon, before doubling to $4 and $20 after November 30.
Whether Carbon’s performance offsets those higher costs, including the overhead of multi-agent orchestration and verification, remains to be seen in production.
Proving Signal’s code
One of the more technically ambitious examples in Google’s announcement involves AlphaProof Code, a new agentic framework for formal verification.
Google researchers used Carbon alongside other models to mathematically prove key security properties of the code underlying Signal’s cryptographic protocol.
The researchers translated security requirements into mathematical theorems and used AlphaProof Code agents to generate millions of lines of Lean, a language used to express and check mathematical proofs.
Google says the work took weeks, compared with the years that similar verification efforts have historically required from expert teams.
The announcement doesn’t specify the full scope of the verified properties, how much human intervention it required, or whether Google will make the proof artifacts publicly available.
Google says the work took weeks, compared with the years that similar verification efforts have historically required from expert teams.
Security that cuts both ways
Google initially made Carbon’s cybersecurity capabilities available to selected defenders through its Fairwind Program in late October.
The company says Carbon leads on SEC-bench Pro, ExploitGym and CWE-bench v1, benchmarks covering vulnerability discovery, exploitation and patching.
In Project Fortify, Google’s autonomous scanning, triage and remediation system, Carbon achieved 100% scanning recall and 95% triage precision on an internal benchmark. Google also reports a relative improvement of more than 25% over Argon’s recall rate when testing open-source repositories.
Google’s Cloud Vulnerability Research team used Carbon to confirm that two bugs in a popular open-source project could be exploited, prompting maintainers to classify them as critical and release patches. Google says the vulnerabilities were comparable in severity to the recent PHP2Shell exploit, but hasn’t named the affected project while the disclosure process is still underway.
Separately, Wiz used Carbon through its Scan for Good program to uncover zero-day vulnerabilities in two major SaaS providers in under two hours. The affected organizations worked with the researchers on remediation.
Cybersecurity’s double edge
The stronger exploitation capabilities also raise misuse concerns. Google says Carbon’s safeguards blocked 99% of attack trajectories attempted by an adaptive red-teaming agent in simulated environments, reducing the per-attempt breach rate to 0.8%, compared with 3.1% for Argon.
The company also reports a 0% attack success rate on Gray Swan’s indirect prompt-injection benchmark, while acknowledging that more sophisticated attacks remain an area for improvement.
These results come from specific evaluation environments and don’t establish that Carbon is resistant to all real-world attacks.
Getting access to Carbon
Gemini 4 Carbon is available through the paid Gemini API tier in Google AI Studio and Android Studio, as well as Google’s enterprise offerings.
Google AI Ultra subscribers can access Carbon through Antigravity, the Gemini app, and AI Mode in Search. The /swarm orchestration feature remains in preview.
Access to Carbon’s advanced cybersecurity tools still requires approval through Fairwind. Google is also giving selected scientists six months of free access to Carbon through Antigravity, with applications open and new researchers added each week.
Google has published an updated Gemini 4 developer guide covering migration and implementation.

articles.title: Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Autonomous treasury agents: How Trovata built an AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore
Corporate treasury teams face a persistent challenge: fragmented banking data scattered across dozens of bank portals, manual reporting trapped in spreadsheets, and legacy Treasury Management Systems (TMS) that can’t scale for modern enterprise needs. For treasury teams these manual processes create delays, errors, and an inability to make real-time cash decisions when they matter most.
Trovata is an AI-native cash and liquidity management platform with direct connections to over 10,000 banks, serving enterprises globally from a single cloud-based platform. In 2023, Trovata launched the first generative AI built specifically for treasury. Now, with Trovata’s latest AI-native updates, they’ve evolved from delivering insights to deploying autonomous agents that act on behalf of treasury teams.
Trovata’s customers have seen measurable results: $1M+ in annualized cost savings, over 5 hours per day saved per accounting team, a 77 percent reduction in annual TMS costs, and treasury reporting reduced from hours or days to under a minute.
In this post, we explore how Trovata built autonomous treasury agents on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, the architecture secured with role-based access control (RBAC) that supports bank-branded AI deployment, and how agentic workflows are transforming corporate treasury from manual operations to real-time decision-making at enterprise scale.
Solution overview
Trovata operates as an AI-native treasury operating system, providing direct connections to over 10,000 banks through a single system for cash reporting, forecasting, analysis, and money movement.
Treasury teams today face a three-pressure problem:
- Fragmented banking data across multiple portals, requiring manual aggregation and reconciliation.
- Manual reporting and reconciliation consuming hours or even days of skilled team members’ time.
- Legacy TMS applications that lack cloud-native architecture and AI capabilities needed for modern operations.
Trovata’s evolution from its first generative AI for treasury in 2023 to its AI-native capabilities with autonomous agents represents a fundamental shift. The solution moves from static insights to persistent agentic workflows that operate continuously on behalf of treasury teams. Critically, Trovata AI is built directly into the treasury operating system. It’s not a generic chatbot layered on top, but embedded intelligence tied to real treasury objects with a governed path to automation through agents.
Trovata chose AWS for this transformation for three reasons. Its serverless, cloud-native infrastructure supports real-time execution, Amazon Bedrock provides large language model (LLM) inference for natural language queries and AI features, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore handles agent orchestration with RBAC security, rapid deployment, and global scale.
The core AWS services powering Trovata’s AI-native solution include:
- Amazon Bedrock – LLM inference for natural language understanding and generation.
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Agent orchestration, agentic workflows, and RBAC security.
- Serverless AWS infrastructure – Real-time execution at enterprise scale.
Architecture diagram
The Trovata AI architecture centers on autonomous treasury agents operating within a bank-branded, RBAC-secured framework. The solution comprises several key components working together:
- Trovata AI Chat – Natural language querying of multi-bank treasury data, so users can ask questions like “What was our net cash position across all accounts yesterday?” and receive instant, accurate responses.
- AI Insights – Automated anomaly detection, variance explanation, and trend analysis that surfaces critical information proactively.
- AI Agents – Persistent workflows running on schedules, triggers, or rules to monitor activity, explain variance, detect anomalies, and deliver updates automatically, without human intervention.
- Agent Builder-Configurator – A management console for building and configuring treasury agents, giving teams full control over agent behavior and scope.
- Enterprise RBAC – Role-based access control securing agentic workflows, making sure that agents operate within the same permission boundaries as human users.
Technical implementation
Trovata built its AI-native solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, combining autonomous agents, natural language querying, and enterprise access controls. The following sections describe what the team built, the primary use cases, and the AgentCore capabilities behind it.
What Trovata built: AI-native solution
Trovata AI delivers autonomous treasury management agents embedded directly within the Trovata treasury operating system. These AI agents turn repeatable operational work into persistent workflows that run continuously. This is the work that consumes hours of skilled professionals’ time.
Agents operate on schedules, triggers, or rules to monitor activity, explain variance, detect anomalies, and deliver updates automatically. The entire system runs on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a secure, isolated environment purpose-built for enterprise AI. When a user asks a question, the AI retrieves data through Trovata’s own verified API layer, analyzes it, and presents the response within that secure infrastructure.
Primary use cases
- Cash forecasting – Automated cash flow forecasting across multi-bank environments with scenario modeling, replacing manual spreadsheet-based projections.
- Natural language querying – Enterprise users query bank data in plain English. For example: “What was our net cash position across all accounts yesterday?”.
- Anomaly detection – Real-time detection of unusual transactions, balance changes, or cash flow patterns that might indicate errors, fraud, or operational issues.
- Automated reconciliation – AI-powered reconciliation summaries across hundreds of accounts, reducing what previously took hours to seconds.
- Agentic workflows – Persistent agents that run autonomously by monitoring, analyzing, and reporting without human intervention on an ongoing basis.
Ten agent patterns from real customer deployments
Treasury teams have already started building AI agents in production. Trovata’s AI Agents Playbook provides a working library of ten agent patterns drawn from real customer deployments, covering the most common and high-value treasury workflows. Most treasury teams have 5–15 workflows that are ready for AI agents today.
AgentCore capabilities Trovata uses
Trovata’s implementation takes advantage of several key Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capabilities:
- Agent orchestration – Multi-step agentic workflows for complex treasury operations that require sequential reasoning and action.
- RBAC security – Role-based access control securing agent actions, making sure agents respect organizational permission boundaries.
- Real-time execution – Serverless infrastructure that delivers sub-minute treasury reporting across hundreds of bank accounts.
- Bank-branded deployment – Agents embedded within bank-branded tools, so banks can offer AI-powered treasury capabilities without needing to build AI themselves.
Security and governance architecture
| Control | Implementation | 
| Enterprise RBAC | Role-based access control securing agentic workflows and data access | 
| Verified API layer | AI retrieves data only through Trovata’s own verified API layer — no direct database access | 
| Secure isolated environment | AgentCore provides a secure, isolated runtime for AI agent execution | 
| Bank-branded deployment | Agents operate within bank-branded applications, preserving enterprise security and supporting compliance efforts | 
| Multi-bank data governance | Direct connectivity to over 10,000 banks | 
| Audit trail | AI queries and agent actions logged for compliance review | 
Results
| Metric | Result | Context | 
| Annualized cost savings | $1M+ | Based on customer case studies | 
| Time saved per accounting team | 5+ hours/day | Manual reporting and reconciliation avoided | 
| Annual TMS cost reduction | 77% | Compared to legacy TMS tools | 
| Treasury reporting time | Hours/days → <1 min | Real-time cash visibility across hundreds of accounts | 
| Bank connectivity | 100+ enterprise; 2,000+ business | Direct connections — single system | 
| Production status | Live | AI with autonomous agents in production | 
| Agent patterns available | 10 | From real customer deployments (Agents Playbook) | 
Key differentiators
| Differentiator | Detail | 
| First generative AI for treasury | Launched 2023. Evolved to autonomous agents with latest AI updates | 
| Embedded, not bolted-on | AI built directly into the treasury operating system, not a generic chatbot layer | 
| Bank-branded deployment | Banks deploy AI agents under their own brand without building AI themselves | 
| Verified API layer | AI accesses data only through Trovata’s verified API — no direct database access | 
| Ten production agent patterns | Working library from real customer deployments | 
| Multi-bank at scale | Over 10,000 banks on a single system | 
Prerequisites
To explore a similar architecture, you will need:
- An AWS account with access to Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
- Familiarity with treasury management operations (cash forecasting, reconciliation, multi-bank connectivity)
- Understanding of agentic AI architectures and enterprise RBAC models.
- Knowledge of financial services compliance requirements.
Cleanup
If you deployed any example resources while exploring this architecture, remember to delete them to avoid incurring future costs. Remove any Bedrock agents, AgentCore configurations, and associated infrastructure that were created for testing purposes.
Conclusion
Trovata’s journey from manual treasury operations to autonomous AI-powered treasury management demonstrates the transformative potential of agentic AI in financial services. With over $1M in annualized cost savings, over 5 hours per day saved per accounting team, a 77 percent reduction in annual TMS costs, and reporting reduced from hours or days to under a minute, the impact is measurable.
The bank-branded deployment model is especially effective. Banks and enterprises get production-ready AI without building it themselves. Trovata AI shows how, with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, independent software vendors (ISVs) can embed governed, autonomous AI agents directly into vertical software as a service (SaaS) applications, delivering AI with the security and compliance-awareness that financial services demands.
Looking ahead, Trovata plans to expand its agent patterns, deepen enterprise resource planning (ERP) integrations, and extend global bank connectivity. The company continues to advance what autonomous treasury management can achieve.

articles.title: Anthropic lanzó Claude Fable 5.2, una IA más rápida y capaz de diseñar un sistema operativo desde cero
articles.text:
Anthropic lanzó Claude Fable 5.2 y Claude Mythos 5.2, nuevas versiones de sus modelos de inteligencia artificial más potentes. Según la empresa, generan respuestas hasta un 30% más rápido que las versiones 5.1 y cuestan un 20% menos para los desarrolladores que las usan en sus propios productos.
Fable 5.2 ya está disponible en todos los planes de pago de Claude, en la plataforma para desarrolladores de Anthropic y en las nubes de Amazon, Google y Microsoft. Mythos 5.2 es el mismo modelo con menos salvaguardas en ciberseguridad y biología, y solo lo recibirán organizaciones que superen un proceso de verificación.
El precio pasó de USD 10 a USD 8 por millón de unidades de texto de entrada (los fragmentos en que el modelo divide lo que lee) y de USD 50 a USD 40 por millón de salida. Un modo rápido opcional, hasta 2,5 veces más veloz, cuesta el doble: USD 16 y USD 80.
Para los suscriptores, la empresa anunció uso adicional de Fable durante esta semana. Los planes que incluyen el modelo reciben entre uno y tres reinicios de sus límites, según el tiempo de suscripción, y en el plan Pro Fable cuenta hasta el 50% del uso semanal permitido.
Qué dice Anthropic que puede hacer
En su comparación, Fable 5.2 obtuvo 49,1% en una prueba de programación basada en cambios reales de proyectos de código abierto, el puntaje más alto entre los modelos publicados que la empresa evaluó. El modelo anterior, Fable 5.1, había logrado 32,4%, y GPT-6 Astra, de OpenAI, 42,8%. Son mediciones de la propia compañía.
La empresa afirmó que más del 90% de los cambios incorporados a su código principal ya los escribe Claude, con guía humana. Para probar el modelo, un ingeniero le pidió diseñar un sistema operativo desde cero: el modelo coordinó más de 1.000 subagentes durante ocho días y produjo uno que arranca en una computadora portátil.
Anthropic también informó que el modelo resolvió dos problemas abiertos de la física de los agujeros negros y formalizó la demostración del último teorema de Fermat en 30 horas durante las pruebas previas. En tareas de control de robots en simulación, Fable 5.2 alcanzó 64,9%, frente a 27,6% de la versión anterior.
Para la mayoría de las tareas de programación y trabajo con conocimiento, la propia empresa recomienda empezar por otro modelo, Claude Opus 5.5, y subir a Fable o Mythos solo ante trabajos más complejos.
Las advertencias que acompañan el lanzamiento
Es el primer lanzamiento de Anthropic desde un informe del grupo evaluador independiente METR. Según TechCrunch, el informe indicó que los modelos internos de la compañía aceleran su propio progreso en torno a 2 veces, lo que sugiere que podría acercarse a la automejora recursiva, es decir, a que una IA entrene a la siguiente sin ayuda humana. El medio aclaró que persisten muchas incertidumbres.
Las notas de lanzamiento reconocen otro problema. Según el texto citado por TechCrunch, ambos modelos expresan sospecha de estar siendo evaluados más a menudo que cualquier modelo reciente de la empresa, lo que dificulta anticipar cómo actuarán en situaciones reales.
La ficha técnica de Mythos 5.2 indica que el modelo muestra capacidades de actuar de forma encubierta más fuertes que las de modelos anteriores en varias pruebas, sobre todo cuando su razonamiento queda oculto para el monitor. Anthropic sostiene que los niveles absolutos de esas capacidades son bajos y que los riesgos graves por desalineación siguen siendo reducidos.
Dianne Penn, responsable de producto de investigación de Anthropic, dijo a Bloomberg, según Investing.com, que la empresa extendió los períodos de prueba. “Ir más despacio no es lo mismo que detenerse”, afirmó.
En septiembre, el director ejecutivo Dario Amodei había pedido a las principales compañías de IA reducir el ritmo de desarrollo de sus modelos más avanzados, según esa misma fuente.
El lanzamiento llega cuando Anthropic prepara su debut en bolsa. Bloomberg informó, según The Next Web, que la salida podría ocurrir este mismo mes.

articles.title: Nvidia has a Jensen Huang problem—and no obvious successor
articles.text:
The investigation of Jensen Huang by Nvidia’s board threatens the future of one of Silicon Valley’s longest-serving executives and a key enabler of the AI boom, who has no obvious successor as leader of the world’s second-most-valuable company.
Huang is fighting for survival after admitting to an extramarital affair, believed to be with an executive at a large Nvidia customer whom US officials also allege was working as a Chinese spy.
The prospect that Huang could be forced out as chief executive of the US chipmaker he co-founded more than 30 years ago has alarmed investors and allies in the tech industry. Shares in Nvidia, which late last month ceded its position as the world’s most valuable to Apple amid a broader sell-off in AI stocks, had fallen more than 5 percent by midday trading on Monday.
“Jensen is irreplaceable for America’s AI leadership,” said Shaun Maguire, partner at early Nvidia investor Sequoia Capital, in a social media post.
Nvidia’s chips were instrumental in the creation of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and now sit at the center of Big Tech’s $1 trillion AI infrastructure frenzy. Huang has personally stood behind investments and guarantees running into hundreds of billions of dollars for dozens of AI start-ups and data center providers, as well as lobbying US President Donald Trump for looser AI regulation.
“Nvidia is not an ordinary company and Jensen is not an ordinary CEO; he IS Nvidia,” analysts at Bernstein said in a note to clients.
With policymakers in Washington pressuring Huang to appear before congressional committees to explain himself, the spotlight is on Nvidia’s board, which said on Sunday it would conduct its own “independent” investigation into the scandal that exploded over the weekend.
The investigation will probably be led by board member and former Cooley chief executive Stephen C. Neal, according to people familiar with the probe.
“If information was compromised, the implications are a lot bigger than if it was just an affair, which obviously isn’t welcome news,” said a fund manager with a large Nvidia position. “Nvidia would survive [Huang leaving] but there’s no better person than Jensen to run the company; it would be very different without him.”
In contrast to other leading Big Tech companies, Nvidia’s annual reports and corporate governance paperwork make no specific reference to “succession planning” and set out no details for how it would replace its CEO, even in an emergency, beyond noting that the company “believe[s] in extensive leadership development.”
Huang’s unusually large number of direct reports, numbered at more than 60 according to a 2024 disclosure, present Nvidia’s board with a “pool of excellent candidates for future promotion,” recent filings say.
Huang leads a small core executive team at Nvidia, including Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, Operations Chief Debora Shoquist and general counsel Tim Teter. He has become one of Huang’s closest lieutenants since joining in 2017 and has lobbied Washington on export controls.
Jay Puri, a close lieutenant who led Nvidia’s sales operations and deputized for Huang on international visits, stepped down in August and was replaced on the executive team by Microsoft veteran Nick Parker.
Huang, who has cultivated an air of infallibility inside Nvidia, has given no indication he will step down from the role of CEO.
Recent biographies of Huang and Nvidia, including Tae Kim’s The Nvidia Way and Stephen Witt’s The Thinking Machine, portray him as having a rare combination of technical depth and forward-thinking leadership.
He is known to be able to inspire extraordinary productivity inside a company whose 42,000 employees each generated an average of more than $7 million in annual revenue over the past 12 months, far more than any other Big Tech group. But Kim also notes that Huang represents the company’s “single point of failure,” functioning as its head of marketing, sales, and product development.
His influence in the wider tech industry is also unique. Endorsements by Huang of companies in the AI semiconductor supply chain can supercharge their share prices, while his offhand dismissal early last year of the near-term commercial prospects for quantum computing sent stocks in the sector spiraling.
Despite his imperial stature, Huang owns just 3.6 percent of Nvidia. That stake makes him Nvidia’s largest individual shareholder and is worth more than $150 billion. However, Huang lacks the special voting rights held by many Silicon Valley founders, including Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg and Google’s Larry Page and Sergey Brin, that would allow him to control the board or face down outside investors who might attempt to oust him.
Huang’s total compensation last year of $36.3 million, of which the vast majority came in the form of stock awards, included some $4 million for security paid for by Nvidia, which filings say is “due to the exceptionally high public profile and prominence of our CEO.”
These costs included protection at home and during “personal travel,” as well as using private aircraft for all business trips, according to filings. Huang reimburses Nvidia for personal air travel on private aircraft arranged by the company, according to filings.
Nvidia’s board, whose individual members have until now kept a low profile, confirmed they would appoint a special committee composed of sitting board members assisted by outside counsel to examine the allegations surrounding its CEO.
Neal joined Nvidia’s board in 2019 and is chair emeritus and senior counsel at Cooley, after serving as the law firm’s CEO from 2001 to 2008.
Nvidia’s board is unusual among the largest US companies in having no designated chair. A 2025 report by law firm Fenwick found that only one company in S&P 100—which would be Nvidia, according to its own filings—had no chair.
In its proxy filings, Nvidia states that this set-up “ensures that each member has an equal voice in the affairs and management of Nvidia.”
The other nine members of Nvidia’s board—excluding Huang, who is himself a director—include four men who have been with the company since the 1990s, a former Taco Bell executive, a professor of aeronautics, and a former Goldman Sachs executive who joined only this year.
The board’s public statement on Sunday said it had “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team” and that it had “no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised.”
Nonetheless, his admission of an affair on Sunday shocked employees and former colleagues who spoke to the FT.
Madison Huang, Jensen’s daughter who serves as a senior director in Nvidia’s product marketing team and has become an increasingly visible presence at the company’s conferences, canceled a planned appearance at a company event in South Korea on Monday.
The law in Delaware, where Nvidia is incorporated, says executives have certain fiduciary duties including a duty of care and loyalty to their company.
Nvidia’s code of conduct requires executives to “conduct themselves with the highest degree of integrity, ethics and honesty. Our credibility and reputation depend upon their good judgment, ethical standards and personal integrity.”
Even if Huang is found to have breached those guidelines, his defenders in Silicon Valley argue that he is too big to fire.
“Yes he should have known better,” Sequoia’s Maguire said. “But let’s also not nuke our AI industry because China ran a successful intel op.”

articles.title: Pinterest and Intel Take Open-Source Profiling to Internet Scale
articles.text:
Pinterest has partnered with Intel to extend gProfiler, an open-source continuous profiler that provides production performance visibility across an internet-scale fleet of infrastructure.
Pinterest claims it operates hundreds of thousands of instances supporting 640 million monthly active users, with services written in Java, Python, C++, Go, and Node.js. At that scale, even a small efficiency improvement can have significant infrastructure and cost implications. The challenge was that engineers were using separate tools such as perf, async-profiler, and py-spy, producing fragmented profiles that were difficult to correlate across languages and machines.
Rather than building another proprietary profiling platform, Pinterest worked with Intel to extend gProfiler and contribute those capabilities back to the open-source project. The collaboration adds dynamic profiling, hardware-level telemetry, wall-time profiling, and performance-counter flame graphs, while also hardening the system for large production fleets.
gProfiler acts as an orchestration layer over several existing profilers. It combines system-wide perf data with runtime-specific tools such as async-profiler for Java and eBPF-based profiling for Python, producing a unified flame graph across the processes running on a host.
This is important for modern services where application execution crosses multiple layers. A Java application may spend time inside the JVM, native libraries, or the Linux kernel, while a Python service can involve interpreter, native, and kernel activity. Instead of requiring engineers to select and manually correlate separate profilers, gProfiler combines those views.
The agent discovers processes, starts the appropriate profilers, merges their stack traces, and uploads the resulting profile without requiring application code changes.
The new capability allows engineers to select services, hosts, or clusters and trigger profiling remotely through the UI or API. Agents normally remain dormant, consuming less than 1% CPU and 100 MB of memory, and receive profiling instructions through periodic heartbeats. You can change profiling frequency, duration, and the profilers used without redeploying the agent.
This effectively turns profiling into an operational capability rather than something that requires engineers to gain shell access to individual machines.
Integration with Intel PerfSpect allows gProfiler to collect hardware-level information such as cache behaviour, memory bandwidth, and CPU stalls. Pinterest also added PMC flame graphs, which correlate functions with hardware performance events such as cache misses and branch mispredictions.
Another addition is wall-time profiling. CPU profiling shows where processor time is being spent, but a service can still be slow while consuming relatively little CPU because threads are waiting on I/O, locks, or remote procedure calls. Wall-time profiling makes those waiting periods visible.
The gProfiler architecture separates collection from analysis. Agents run on individual hosts, while gProfiler Performance Studio aggregates and visualises the resulting profiles.
Profiles are stored in S3, passed through SQS for asynchronous indexing, and stored in ClickHouse for analytical queries. A React frontend provides flame-graph exploration, while aggregated data allows engineers to compare profiles across hosts, services, and time periods.
Pinterest and Intel also hardened the platform for production, addressing issues involving agent resource consumption, disk usage, and multi-terabyte ingestion before deploying it across the fleet.
gProfiler sits in an increasingly crowded continuous-profiling landscape. Parca and Grafana Pyroscope use eBPF and related sampling technologies to provide fleet-wide profiling, while commercial platforms such as Datadog offer continuous profiling alongside broader observability capabilities.
The distinction with gProfiler is its emphasis on system-wide, multi-runtime profiling and open-source extensibility. Rather than replacing tools such as perf or async-profiler, it orchestrates them. It also adds hardware-level profiling through Intel's tooling.
Intel's VTune provides much deeper processor and application performance analysis, but it was designed primarily as a performance-engineering tool rather than a cloud-native fleet profiler. Pinterest specifically notes that this difference influenced the decision to build on gProfiler rather than adapt VTune for its environment.
At small scale, profiling is usually something an engineer enables when a performance problem appears. At Pinterest's scale, the cost of waiting for engineers to reproduce problems or manually profile machines becomes too high. Continuous profiling provides a baseline, while dynamic profiling allows teams to investigate specific anomalies when they occur.
By combining runtime profiles, system behaviour, and hardware performance data under an open-source platform, Pinterest is effectively making profiling another layer of production observability.

articles.title: Platform Calgary and Ax.c launch reciprocal access for startups | BetaKit
articles.text:
Tech startups based in Calgary and Montréal will now have a place to build and network when they visit either city.
The news: Local innovation hubs Platform Calgary and Montréal-based Ax.c announced a one-year reciprocal agreement on Tuesday that will give associated startups access to the spaces and activities run by both organizations.
Ax.c member startups will be welcome to work out of Platform Calgary’s Innovation Centre, while the inverse will be true for Calgary startups visiting Ax.c. They’re also sharing access to expert sessions and networking events.
From the source: “Our startups have everything to gain from getting to know the ecosystems of Calgary and Western Canada, and the reverse is just as true,” Ax.c director Geneviève Leclerc said in a statement. “We want to make interprovincial collaboration simple, natural, and concrete.”
The context: Ax.c has branded itself as a hub to host international delegations. It’s aligned with the mission of the provincially backed non-profit Québec Tech, which has sought to help startups sell globally. Alongside renewed funding from the city of Montréal, Ax.c recently partnered with Toronto’s DMZ to provide office space at its headquarters, plus in New York City and Tokyo.
It’s now taking that outward-facing approach to boost collaboration within Canada, particularly with Calgary, which was recently named the fastest-growing tech ecosystem in the country. Platform Calgary, which has new leadership under CEO Jennifer Lussier, hosts a litany of events, including this month’s Calgary Innovation Week that features workshops, seminars, and networking get-togethers.
Final thought: Café co-working and booking WeWork-style workspaces can be expensive for budding startups hoping to keep their costs down. Free access at Ax.c and Platform Calgary for visiting startups could encourage usage of the spaces and free up more money for key costs, such as AI token spend.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.
Feature image courtesy Platform Calgary.

articles.title: La amante de Jensen Huang habría ayudado a desviar 7.500 millones de dólares en chips de NVIDIA a China
articles.text:
La aventura extramatrimonial de Jensen Huang con la supuesta espía china Alice Huang no solo está ocupando titulares en todo el mundo, sino que ha disparado tanto una revisión interna de NVIDIA como una investigación del FBI. Y las implicaciones del escándalo amoroso son cada vez más notorias.
Según reporta The Information, la relación entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang dataría al menos desde 2023. Pero no solo eso, sino que la amante del CEO de NVIDIA habría ayudado a desviar unos 7.500 millones de dólares en chips avanzados hacia el gigante asiático, a pesar del bloqueo de Estados Unidos.
El citado medio indica que Alice Huang habría montado una red de empresas en China y Singapur junto con su esposo y su hermana, destacando una firma llamada Shanghai Century Litong. Esta se fundó en junio de 2023 y apenas meses después, en octubre, se convirtió en socio preferente de NVIDIA para servicios en la nube.
Ser socio preferente de NVIDIA le daba a la compañía acceso prioritario a sus chips. No obstante, la situación se habría complicado tras la entrada en vigor del veto de Estados Unidos a la exportación de hardware avanzado para servidores de IA hacia China. No obstante, Alice Huang habría sacado provecho de su cercanía con Jensen Huang para mover hilos y evadir el bloqueo.
La aventura de Jensen Huang con una supuesta espía destapa el desvío de chips de NVIDIA hacia China
Puntualmente, The Information indica que Alice Huang habría utilizado sus vínculos con NVIDIA y los distribuidores de la empresa para garantizarse el acceso a sus chips avanzados y enviarlos a China. Se menciona en tal sentido que la estrategia habría facilitado el envío de 240.000 placas gráficas H100, H200 y A100 hacia el gigante asiático. Así, se estima que la amante de Jensen Huang habría logrado movilizar hardware por al menos 7.500 millones de dólares desde 2023.
El culebrón por la relación entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang está muy lejos de finalizar. La historia se destapó a finales de octubre, cuando The New York Times publicó que el CEO de NVIDIA mantenía una "relación cercana" con la presunta espía china. El citado medio no explicitó si se trataba de un vínculo romántico, pero las especulaciones no se hicieron esperar.
El reporte original sostenía que Jensen Huang no sabía que Alice Huang estaba enviando información hacia China. También decía que Donald Trump conocía sobre el tema desde hacía un año, pero que había optado por no tomar cartas en el asunto. En una conferencia de prensa que realizó ayer en la Casa Blanca, el presidente de EE. UU. dijo que el jefe de NVIDIA le confesó que no estaba al tanto de que su amante era una espía china.
Si bien NVIDIA negó inicialmente que el vínculo entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang fuese problemático, la historia cambió en los últimos días. El domingo, el propio líder y fundador de la empresa reconoció haber tenido una relación extramatrimonial, y la firma anunció la puesta en marcha de una investigación interna.
Durante la jornada bursátil del lunes, la acción de NVIDIA cayó un 5 %. Así, la empresa perdió unos 190.000 millones de dólares de valor de mercado en un solo día. Al momento de redacción de este artículo, el gigante verde tiene un marketcap de 4,3 billones de dólares. Esto ha dejado a Apple como la única empresa del mundo que vale más de 5 billones de dólares.

articles.title: Reddit is turning user conversations into AI-powered product reviews | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Shortly after announcing a plan to transition its site to a logged-in experience, Reddit is debuting a feature that could help make it more of a destination for people doing product research via the web. The company on Tuesday introduced “Reddit Reviews,” a feature that organizes conversations about products into dedicated reviews that include the highlights and key takeaways from users across its communities.
The company notes that the new experience builds on one of the ways people are already using Reddit: to learn from others what products are really like, and how they fit into their everyday lives. These first-hand accounts and recommendations can help consumers determine whether or not a particular product is right for them.
However, given the rise of generative AI and bots, it’s an area that’s also ripe for “astroturfing” — a term that refers to when a brand fakes public support. With Reddit now effectively turning what was casual online research into more of a structured product, it could become a larger target for these types of fake reviews and recommendations than before.
To address this, Reddit’s announcement points to its rules and its latest measures to combat automated abuse and spam, as well as its practice involving community moderators, as tools it will use to keep the reviews on the site legit.
The Reddit Reviews feature itself taps into AI to organize the conversations people are having where they describe their product experiences. These posts will often see users discussing how a product works for them, or why it fails, or what the trade-offs are that someone should consider before buying.
The company has been testing the product reviews feature since February, initially with U.S. users in areas like Electronics, Video Games, and Health & Beauty products. In September, Reddit expanded the test to include the Home & Garden and Fashion & Apparel categories as well.
Now, the company says Reddit Reviews is rolling out to all U.S. users on iOS, Android, and web, with an initial selection focused on around 10,000 products. Over time, it will roll out to more categories and expand beyond the U.S.
To use the feature, Reddit users can search for a product or category in the app’s search bar or click on a highlighted product name they see in someone’s comment. From there, the user is taken to a screen where important conversations are summarized under a “what people are saying” heading. This will also include a visual breakdown that shows how many of those comments are positive, negative, or mixed, and what sort of things people said they liked or disliked about the item.
For instance, a user considering buying an espresso machine might want to know about things like how much counter space it takes up or whether it’s easier for beginners to understand how to use it, says Reddit. Users can then browse the comments, filter them by topic, or click to be taken to the original conversation, where they can ask more questions or get advice.
Users can also move from one product review back to the full category to weigh other, similar products that have been discussed to compare their options, the company said.
The feature arrives just ahead of the busy holiday shopping season, when people spend a lot more time doing online product research ahead of their bigger purchases.

articles.title: The telecoms industry needs to think differently about climate resilience
articles.text:
The telecoms industry needs to think differently about climate resilience
Building climate resilience into the UK’s telecoms infrastructure
Ten years ago, one of the telecoms industry’s biggest infrastructure challenges was rolling out 4G. Since then, telecoms has transformed – and the environment our infrastructure operates in has changed with it.
Summer 2026 was the UK’s hottest on record. In the first nine months of 2026 alone we’ve faced heatwaves, droughts, wildfires, and flash-flood warnings. And climate projections suggest conditions like these will become increasingly familiar.
For those of us responsible for the critical national infrastructure people rely on every day, that means thinking about resilience in an entirely different way – shifting the focus from a single network to the continuity of the service people rely on.
Chief Sustainability Officer at Virgin Media O2.
In telecoms, the physical impacts of climate change can quickly become real issues for our customers. And while operators are already taking steps to prepare their networks – from backup power and cooling to flood protection and longer-term climate risk planning – resilience doesn’t begin and end at the boundaries of an individual network. It has to be thought about in the context of the UK’s digital infrastructure system.
The Telecommunications Security Act has already required operators to take a more systemic approach to identifying risks and preparing for disruption. Climate risk now needs the same operational discipline to ensure the connectivity that keeps our economy and national security running stays reliable.
We need to think beyond the resilience of individual networks
Our networks don’t exist in isolation. We are all connected to a much wider digital ecosystem, and increasingly dependent on other critical infrastructure too. Transport is an obvious example. Telecoms networks depend on roads and transport links remaining accessible so engineers can reach critical sites.
That means we need to look beyond the resilience of individual networks and think about the resilience of the system as a whole.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Climate risks don’t arrive neatly one at a time, and the impact of an event in one part of our critical national infrastructure can quickly be felt elsewhere. We’ve seen this come to life in extreme weather events. A heatwave can increase cooling demand at the same time as the power system is under strain, and flooding can damage equipment and prevent engineers from reaching it.
Each individual operator – whether that be the telecoms company or highways authority – has plans for each disruption scenario. The challenge is that those plans need to work when the same event puts several dependencies under pressure at once.
Working together, with government, regulators and the other infrastructure industries we depend on is therefore more vital than ever. Climate adaptation is a strategic national issue. We need to start treating it as one.
Adaptation has to change the infrastructure decisions we make today
Thinking differently about climate resilience also means thinking differently about the decisions we make today. Identifying climate risks is important, but simply recognizing or reporting them isn’t enough. The real value comes when those risks start to influence how businesses plan, invest and operate.
Telecoms infrastructure is built to operate for years, often decades. We can’t predict the exact weather at a particular site in 2040, but we can make decisions now that remain sensible across a credible range of future conditions and identify what would trigger a different course through climate scenario planning.
Climate considerations therefore need to be part of long term decisions from capital investment and network planning to executive governance. That isn’t always straightforward.
One of the challenges with climate change is its unpredictability. We can see patterns in the science and data, but there isn’t a neat, linear pathway that tells a business exactly what conditions its infrastructure will face in five, ten or twenty years’ time. A lot of the impact we are experiencing today is unchartered territory for humanity as a whole, let alone infrastructure.
Part of the answer is translating climate risk into the language businesses already use to make decisions. For telecoms, that means talking about resilience, reliability, efficiency and investment – and recognizing that these priorities are often more closely connected than we might think.
We’ve seen that with net zero. Many of the actions needed to decarbonize networks are also ones that can make them more efficient, more reliable and more resilient. Reducing energy consumption is an obvious example: it can lower emissions while improving efficiency and reducing exposure to energy costs. Rather than treating net zero, adaptation and network resilience as separate agendas, we should increasingly look at where the same infrastructure decisions can help deliver all three.
After all, telecoms is first and foremost an infrastructure business. And if we are investing in infrastructure that will be operating for years to come, resilience to a changing climate needs to be part of how we decide what – and where – to invest.
Uncertainty is often treated as a reason to wait. But when investing in long-lived infrastructure, I believe it should be a reason to keep our options open.
Adaptation needs greater priority
For years, the climate conversation in telecoms has rightly focused on how we reduce our impact on the climate. But as its physical effects become increasingly visible, we need to give the other side of that conversation much greater attention too: how a changing climate will affect the infrastructure we all rely on.
No individual operator has the full picture. The systems telecoms depend on span different companies, sectors and regulatory frameworks, which makes climate resilience a shared challenge as well as an individual one.
A more collaborative approach could help strengthen resilience across sectors. That could include common climate scenarios, cross-sector stress testing, agreed restoration priorities, clearer protocols for sharing information during disruption.
In the event of a storm, power resilience is an example. Imposing a higher duty of cooperation and data sharing between Distribution Network Operators and telecoms companies would help mitigation to be deployed appropriately.
Government and regulators also have a role in convening this work – however, we cannot wait for climate adaptation to become another compliance exercise. We should compete on service and innovation, while collaborating on risks no company can manage alone.
We can’t know exactly what conditions our networks will face in the decades ahead. But we do know that the climate they operate in is changing. The challenge now is to make sure the infrastructure we invest in today is ready for the world it will need to operate in tomorrow.
