articles.title: Alexa Plus: So steuerst du dein Smarthome jetzt über den Browser
articles.text:
Amazon hat die Browser-Version seines KI-Systems Alexa Plus am 10. November für Deutschland freigeschaltet. Bislang war die Sprachassistenz hierzulande nur über Echo-Lautsprecher, Fire-TV-Geräte und die Alexa-App erreichbar. Zugriff auf alexa.com haben aber nur Teilnehmende des deutschen Early-Access-Programms, also der frühen Testphase von Alexa Plus.
Chatfenster plus Smart-Home-Steuerung
Die Weboberfläche funktioniert wie ein klassischer KI-Chatbot: Nutzer tippen ihre Anfragen in ein Chatfenster. Laut Amazon soll Alexa Plus dort nicht nur antworten und Texte schreiben, sondern auch Aufgaben übernehmen – etwa To-do-Listen und den Familienkalender pflegen oder Restaurants reservieren. Direkt neben dem Chat sitzt die Smart-Home-Steuerung. Darüber lassen sich Lampen schalten, die Temperatur regeln und Bilder von Sicherheitskameras abrufen.
Nach Angaben von Amazon übernimmt alexa.com bisherige Chats, Einstellungen und Personalisierungen von den anderen Geräten. Unter „Letzte Chats“ erscheinen auch Unterhaltungen, die auf einem Echo-Gerät oder in der App begonnen haben. Sie lassen sich im Browser fortsetzen.
Dokumente hochladen – und gespeicherte Daten
Auf alexa.com können Nutzer zusätzlich Dokumente, E-Mails und Bilder hochladen. Alexa Plus soll daraus die wichtigsten Details ziehen, Termine in den Kalender eintragen und Informationen auf Abruf bereithalten. Zum Deutschlandstart im Mai hatte Amazon mitgeteilt, hochgeladene Dateien und die daraus gewonnenen Inhalte bis auf Widerruf zu speichern. Auf Wunsch erstellt die Assistenz auch einen Essensplan für eine ganze Woche und berücksichtigt dabei Vorlieben, etwa eine eiweißreiche Ernährung oder den Verzicht auf Zucker.
In den USA legt Alexa Plus die nötigen Zutaten direkt in den Warenkorb der Amazon-eigenen Lebensmittelanbieter Fresh oder Whole Foods. Diese Funktion erwähnt Amazon in der deutschen Mitteilung jedoch nicht – hierzulande kooperiert der Anbieter unter anderem mit Knuspr. Ob das auch via KI gehen wird, bleibt abzuwarten. In den USA steht alexa.com allen Early-Access-Kunden bereits seit dem 5. Januar offen.
Während des „Early Access“-Zeitraums ist Alexa Plus gratis. Danach gehört die KI-Assistenz zum Prime-Abo, das 9 Euro im Monat oder 90 Euro im Jahr kostet. (Ohne Prime: 23 Euro im Monat.) Wer an der Testphase teilnehmen möchte, meldet sich mit einem kompatiblen Echo- oder Fire-TV-Gerät hier auf Amazon an.

articles.title: Test Struggles To Keep Pace With AI
articles.text:
Rapidly changing workloads, more test insertions, and fragmented data complicate chip testing.
Key Takeaways:
The rapid pace of change in AI models and approaches is creating confusion over what to test, when to test it, and what to monitor once chips are in the field.
Until recently, test targets and the timing for test insertions generally were determined by fab processes and the laws of physics, and the results of those tests were deterministic and quantifiable. But starting with the rollout of generative AI and the ensuing explosion of data centers, the gap has widened between the rollout of new algorithms and use models and the time it takes to deploy a chip in the field.
An increasing number of high-performance processors used in data centers, and many at the edge, are multi-die assemblies. The chips are more complex and take longer to design, manufacture, package, and assemble, and the workloads for which they are designed often change by the time those chips leave final test. Along the way, there are more test insertions along the way, each of which generates more data.
The tests are more complex and varied, as well. In addition to electrical tests, these chips need to be analyzed for mechanical integrity. AI workloads can stress one part of a multi-die assembly more than others, and they can change quickly as algorithms and use cases evolve. That, in turn, requires increasingly complex multiphysics simulations and more real-time monitoring of processor and memory utilization, thermal gradients, and datapath throughput, along with accelerated aging that can affect signal integrity.
“It’s a huge challenge,” said Scott Segura, vice president of sales at Advantest. “People are starting to put more active components into the substrate, and moving things closer to each other, as well, so it’s turning into more test insertions. What shifts left? What shifts right? There are substrate testers today that are just trying to make sure you have contact, but now we’re seeing functional testing moving into substrate testing. And at the die level, we’re probing performance. We’ve got to control thermal. For known good dies, they have to be able to handle 3 kilowatts at the die level, so now we’re testing singulated dies. There’s going to be a shift in how you slice up where things go, and packaging is the key. As you’re putting more and more stuff in the package, into the substrates, whatever you’re stacking this stuff on, you’re going to have to start testing those different steps. Silicon photonics has five insertions right now.”
It only gets more challenging from here with the transition from wafers to panels, which will require entirely new equipment and processes. At the same time, packaging and assembly, which used to be done in one location, is now being split between fabs and OSATs. That creates ongoing challenges around who sees what data, when they see it, and how much of it can be shared with other companies.
“Test insertions typically are done at different locations,” said Jeorge Hutarte, senior director of product marketing in the Semiconductor Test group at Teradyne. “For example, from wafer sort to singulated die probe could be done at a fab. They have their data collection workflows. They have their own test programs. And they gather failure mechanisms as a result of the testing done at wafer sort and singulated die probing. When it comes to the next step, which is where we put together a compute die plus a stack of HBMs, plus perhaps other chiplets into an interposer — and it’s going to panels today from round wafers to optimize the utilization of equipment and putting as many dies as possible on a 310 × 310mm panel — this wafer/panel interposer substrate test will likely be done by the OSAT. That’s a different location with a different test program and a different data collection environment or workflow. They don’t necessarily talk to the previous test insertion data. And unfortunately in the fabless world, people don’t share data unless the customer owns everything.”
Fig. 1: Evolving test strategies and emerging test insertions. Source: Teradyne
Testing gets more complicated
It took slightly more than two years from the introduction of ChatGPT in November 2022 to widespread commercial adoption of agentic AI systems. That’s roughly the time it takes to design, verify, and validate a chip, get that design onto a shuttle in a fab, package it, and integrate that chip into a functional system. But during that time, the industry shifted from arrays of GPUs for massively parallel multiply-accumulate operations to a combination of GPUs, CPUs, and customized and programmable accelerators for orchestrating how agents work and interact. Those involve very different optimization and prioritization schemes — hierarchies that are constantly being re-evaluated as workloads shift.
Hyperscalers and large chipmakers have been pushing EDA vendors to reduce the time it takes to design these mini-systems. But even if the chip design cycle could be shrunk from today’s 18 to 24 months to as little as 6 months — a stated goal by some large chipmakers — there would still be a significant gap between the time it takes to get to working silicon and the time it takes to roll out new training and inference models. And that could change again if recurrent self-improvement lives up to its promise.
“We have customers now that will tape out chips, run their models on them, or look at what the end application is, and they’ll end up not going to market with them,” said Advantest’s Segura. “They’ll do a derivative of it, or they’ll do a different version of it. That could change how much memory they’re stacking on it, how many cores it has, how much cache it has, and the overall architecture. It totally changes depending on whether you’re training a frontier model or whether it’s a CPU hosting something. Even our customers sometimes guess wrong. They go through a chip development cycle, get the silicon out, start to run models on it, and they find out the use model has shifted, or they didn’t put enough memory in, or it’s too expensive. They’ve got to be pretty nimble about what they develop, as well. You see a lot of chiplet designs because it lets them scale a different number of cores, for example. If they originally planned for 256 cores, they may only need 192.”
Breaking down data silos
The reasons underlying the gap between hardware and software schedules are complex. Algorithms can be updated in hours or days. Chip architectures can take years to optimize. The goal is to make every process step bulletproof. Achieving that requires more testing, more data, and a clear plan for making sense of that data.
“Not only are there more tools, but they’re all generating more data — and pretty rich modes of data with lots of images,” said Jim Schiely, chief of staff for Calibre Semiconductor R&D at Siemens EDA. “Over time, customers had been building their own local systems for managing revisions, trying to develop context, because you can’t just have a bunch of models floating around without knowing what the provenance of all that data is.”
In some cases, this involves multiple companies. In others, it involves different groups within the same company.
One big challenge here is breaking through silos that have been controlling this data. “There are two aspects to that,” said Schiely. “One is on the technical side, and the other has to do with the relationships between the entities that control that data. On the technical side, the good news is that it’s sort of AI to the rescue. Waiting for everybody to define the format is going to take a long time. But you can very easily take these digital threads of information and turn them into a model or representation with the help of AI tools, even if there’s a slightly different data model being used by another department. That stuff can be handled more or less automatically. So that’s an area where some of the old problems might start to dissolve.”
Battles over who controls critical data intensified in the 1990s, when manufacturing began shifting from vertically integrated companies to foundries. To get designs to work, the foundries instituted restrictive design rules. Those rules have proven very effective for improving yield, but they also limit design freedom. The so-called design rule deck also has become thicker at each new process node, and the amount of data that needs to be processed and analyzed by different groups has ballooned.
“This needs to go from historical analysis done by a group to analytics that are site-wide or maybe group-wide to now being effectively networked analytics either across your own supply chain, or collaboration with your partners,” said Kimon Michaels, co-founder and executive vice president of products and solutions at PDF Solutions. “We’re driving toward how you can have a standard platform that enables the efficient sharing of data and pulling it together and reaching into different facilities, but the obfuscation of the protection of the IP. We’re not there yet as an industry for sure.”
The orchestration required by agentic AI has further blurred the lines of what belongs to whom. “The complexity in our industry is beyond coming up with the latest, greatest model,” said Michaels. “It’s about dealing with the geographical dispersion across the customer-vendor relationship to manage, collect, and understand what model, what data has to be at what place at the right time.”
This matters because chips are increasingly becoming assemblies of heterogeneous components.
“You have active components sitting on a substrate that are very difficult to access, so now they’re building BiST into it,” Segura said. “They’re looking at how different dies are talking to each other. And not just dies. You could have inductors, capacitors, or some type of voltage regulator. How do we self-test that, because it’s really hard to get access to that on the substrate level? All of that’s changing how you’re going to test when you don’t have access to it. Some of these dies have CPUs in them, so they already have built-in self-test for burn-in. But in cases where you can’t get access, either you don’t test it, or you use something that’s connected to it. It’s getting more and more complicated, and people are making this up as they go.”
That was considered business as usual when developing a chip was relatively inexpensive, and field failures were manageable. But in a complex collection of chiplets with HBM memory running mission-critical or safety-critical systems, those costs can quickly spiral out of control. Avoiding them requires more simulations, more testing, and more analysis of live systems.
“In some cases, because of silent data corruption and other potential defects, you may want to do system-level tests, as well,” said Teradyne’s Hutarte. “Some companies are asking to insert between wafer sort and singulated die a wafer-level burn-in stage, where you can accelerate infant mortality before you actually commit it to the interposer as a stack-up. What’s changed in the AI accelerator world, as compared to the mobility era, is that every wrong screening translates to thousands of dollars of loss because of failures at the data center. So the trend is toward more and more shift-left screening and added insertions. The test intensity has at least doubled over the AI era, because once they hit the rack assembly, they could be worth $30,000 to $50,000. We cannot throw away $30,000 because of a defective chiplet.”
Longer lifespans, changing workloads
As a result, chipmakers are increasingly looking at rework rather than scrapping dies or full chips, and their customers are looking at extending the life of these chips.
Some of this can be improved with more data, including synthetic data that is being used where real data is unavailable. But more data also requires more planning as to how to use that data effectively.
“One of the new trends involves workload scheduling,” said Rahima Mohammed, distinguished engineer and semiconductor technical advisor at Vinci. “How do you move the workloads in a way that you don’t heat it up as much and keep it safe? You also need to really think through all the applications very carefully.”
Efficiencies can be gained at multiple points in a system-level architecture, whether that’s access to memory, understanding which data needs to be processed in real-time, and how to parse the processing across a system to ensure that, and how and where to reroute data if data pathways become slower due to electromigration. The list goes on, but all of these decisions also need to take into account structural changes inside customized packaging, the degradation of dielectrics, and the effectiveness of the cooling architecture, any of which can impact how a system behaves over time.
“When you think about chiplets and the smallest processes, how do the transistors come together? Where is the self-heating coming from? You have to think about this from the nanometer level all the way up to the package level,” Mohammed said. “With chiplets, how do you bring those into the package? In a previous time, PCB packaging was just about adding layers. You didn’t have to think about all the copper lines or vias. We just kind of winged it. You don’t have that option anymore. You have to get power through all the possible layers that you can think about, whether that’s horizontal, vertical, or lateral, and you have to do all these ‘what ifs.’ If I change the location of the metal lines here, what happens?”
Conclusion
Test is no longer a fixed step in chipmaking. Historically, test represented a small percentage of manufacturing costs, and test schedules were more predictable. But as leading-edge chips become increasingly heterogeneous collections of chiplets and other components in a customized advanced package with high utilization rates and very specific applications, test is no longer cookie-cutter. It is a unique process that is tailored to a specific design, and one that is increasingly costly and time-consuming. On top of that, the use case for these chips is changing so quickly that by the time a chip is fully tested and ready for work, it may already be outdated.
AI may be used to design better AI chips and help integrate data from various processes, such as test, but keeping up with the changes within AI is a much tougher challenge. And until the technology settles into a pattern of use that isn’t uprooted every month or so, the chip industry is likely to face some hard choices about how much customization is needed to remain competitive, and how long it’s expected to last.

articles.title: GTA 6 sera jouable sur une console à 65 € : est-ce vraiment une bonne affaire ?
articles.text:
Certains ont acheté une console rien que pour lui. GTA 6 sort le 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, et l’attente a poussé une foule de joueuses et de joueurs à s’équiper, et ce au pire moment. Avec la flambée de la mémoire vive, le prix des consoles s’est envolé aussi bien chez Sony que chez Microsoft, qui a relevé ses tarifs le 1er août (la Xbox Series X 1 To s’affiche à 799,99 €).
Les autres offres sur les Xbox One :
- 39,99 € chez Easycash (occasion, parfait état, manette incluse)
- 129,94 € chez Fnac (reconditionnée, vendeur partenaire)
- 144,99 € chez Amazon (occasion, vendeur partenaire)
- 156 € chez Back Market (reconditionnée, manette incluse)
Celles et ceux qui ont résisté ont désormais une option. En ouvrant le préchargement ce mardi 10 novembre, Rockstar a confirmé que GTA 6 serait aussi jouable via Xbox Cloud Gaming sur Xbox One. La console de 2013 ne fera pas tourner le jeu elle-même. Elle affichera une partie calculée sur les serveurs de Microsoft, avec les réglages graphiques de la Xbox Series S.
Contrairement aux Xbox Series, une Xbox One d’occasion se trouve pour quelques dizaines d’euros. Micromania vend par exemple la Xbox One 500 Go d’occasion à 64,99 €, avec une manette sans fil et un câble HDMI. Petite contrainte : la console se retire en boutique, et le stock varie d’un magasin à l’autre. Mais il y a d’autres offres ici et là, qui devraient d’ailleurs aussi rapidement disparaître avec l’effet d’annonce.
Pour 25 € de plus, la Xbox One S 500 Go passe à 89,99 € au lieu de 109,99 € chez Micromania. En plus d’être plus compacte, elle peut recevoir le cloud jusqu’en 1440p avec le Game Pass Ultimate, sur les jeux compatibles, quand la Xbox One d’origine reste bloquée en 1080p.
GTA 6 en cloud sur Xbox One : ce qu’il faut savoir avant de foncer
Avec le cloud, rien ne s’installe sur la console. Il sera inutile de libérer les 212 Go réclamés par le jeu, ou de remplacer le vieux disque dur de 500 Go. Sur le cloud, le jeu utilisera les paramètres graphiques de la Xbox Series S. Rockstar vise de toute façon 30 images par seconde sur PS5 et Xbox Series (même sur PS5 Pro).
Mais tout repose sur votre connexion. Microsoft recommande au moins 20 Mb/s pour jouer en cloud sur une console Xbox, et la stabilité compte autant que le débit. Une box fibre reliée en Ethernet est idéale. Faute de câble, Microsoft conseille un Wi-Fi en 5 GHz ou 6 GHz. Un Wi-Fi capricieux à l’autre bout de l’appartement, lui, se paiera en image qui bave et en temps de réponse qui s’allonge. Rockstar le reconnaît lui-même : en cloud, les performances dépendront de la qualité du réseau. Avant d’acheter, faites un test de débit depuis le salon.
Si vous êtes encore en ADSL, ou si votre abonnement fibre a quelques années, c’est peut-être aussi le moment d’en changer : utilisez notre comparateur des meilleures offres fibre du moment. Visez une offre jusqu’à 8 Gb/s. Longtemps réservées au haut de gamme, elles se trouvent désormais à un prix bien plus raisonnable.
Attention toutefois, le cloud ne vous fera pas économiser GTA 6. Le jeu n’est pas annoncé dans le Game Pass, il faut donc l’acheter, puis disposer d’heures de streaming. Le calendrier fait bien les choses (pour Microsoft du moins), c’est justement ce mois-ci que le cloud cesse d’être illimité dans le Game Pass.
- L’Ultimate (20,99 € par mois) inclut désormais 15 heures par mois,
- le Premium (12,99 €) 10 heures,
- l’Essential (8,99 €) 5 heures.
Comme l’a rapporté Xboxygen en septembre, Xbox a toutefois prévenu par e-mail certains abonnés français que leur abonnement en cours garderait le cloud illimité tant qu’il reste à renouvellement automatique. Une résiliation suivie d’un réabonnement fait basculer sur les nouveaux quotas.
Microsoft prépare aussi des packs d’heures sans abonnement comme le rapporte le Journal du Geek (deuxième coïncidence). Ils sont testés par les membres du programme Xbox Insider à partir de 3,99 $ les 10 heures, mais leur prix en euros n’est pas encore connu. Pour arpenter Leonida pendant des dizaines d’heures, prévoyez ce budget en plus.
Pour résumer, il vous faudra une Xbox One d’occasion, le jeu, un Game Pass et une bonne box. Comptez un peu plus de 150 € pour démarrer avec un mois d’Ultimate (sans compter l’abonnement fibre). Si les 15 heures mensuelles ne suffisent pas, il faudra compter sur des heures supplémentaires, si Microsoft maintient son système de forfaits, à un tarif qui reste à annoncer en France.
Pour les joueurs, le bilan reste à faire. Des heures de cloud comptées, des forfaits au temps de jeu… Microsoft teste une nouvelle façon de facturer les joueurs, à un moment où beaucoup sont déjà excédés par les hausses de prix successives et l’avènement du dématérialisé porté par Sony.
La Xbox One soufflera ses treize bougies le 22 novembre, trois jours après la sortie de GTA 6. Drôle de cadeau d’anniversaire pour une console qui doit ce sursis non pas à sa puissance, mais à sa connexion internet. C’est une belle affaire pour Microsoft qui était pour l’instant resté assez discret sur la sortie du jeu comparé à Sony qui a mis le paquet.

articles.title: Free Mobile, c'est bientôt fini ! La fusion avec Free se fera le 1er décembre, l'opérateur s'explique
articles.text:
Free Mobile fusionnera avec Free le 1er décembre 2026. L'opérateur l'annonce à ses abonnés mobiles dans leurs factures et promet que les forfaits et tarifs ne changeront pas. Leurs données personnelles, en revanche, seront transférées.
La fusion entre Free Mobile et Free s'annonce sans tambour ni trompette, au détour d'un encadré apparu sur les dernières factures mobiles de l'opérateur. Repérée par Univers Freebox, la nouvelle marque symboliquement la fin d'une ère, puisque la société qui avait largement bousculé le marché mobile à son lancement il y a quatorze ans maintenant deviendra, dès le 1er décembre, une entité juridique à part entière. Pour les 15,8 millions d'abonnés concernés, rien ne change au quotidien, à une nuance près, qui touche à leurs données.
Free Mobile disparaît le 1er décembre et Free prévient ses 15,8 millions d’abonnés
Jusqu'ici, l'opérateur de Xavier Niel reposait sur deux sociétés distinctes, avec Free pour le fixe et ses Freebox, et Free Mobile pour le mobile, par définition. Mais à compter du 1er décembre 2026, elles n'en feront plus qu'une, officiellement pour simplifier la gestion des services. Sur le papier, c'est l'organisation juridique de l'opérateur qui évolue. Pour les utilisateurs, le changement devrait rester relativement invisible.
On pourrait même dire qu'il coïncide avec une autre fusion, survenue en début d'année, celle de ses applications Freebox Connect et Free. Les abonnés peuvent, depuis plusieurs mois, accéder aussi bien aux services Freebox que Free Mobile depuis la même interface mobile, l'appli Free.
Free l'écrit noir sur blanc sur les dernières factures mobiles. « Vous n'avez rien à faire », tout se fait automatiquement. Les forfaits, tarifs, services et conditions du contrat restent les mêmes. Même chose pour les clients qui ont souscrit un contrat de location avec option d'achat Free Flex, qui conservent leur contrat tel quel. Les moyens de paiement déjà enregistrés continueront aussi de fonctionner normalement. Voilà qui est rassurant.
Avec la fusion Free Mobile, gare aux faux messages
Le changement le plus concret, c'est en fait celui des données personnelles des abonnés, qui seront transférées de Free Mobile vers Free. L'identité, les coordonnées, les informations de facturation ou encore l'historique de consommation font partie du voyage. Ce transfert repose sur « l'intérêt légitime » des deux sociétés à assurer la continuité des services. Free promet évidemment de respecter ses engagements en matière de confidentialité et de sécurité.
L'opérateur rappelle en outre qu'il ne demandera jamais vos coordonnées bancaires par e-mail ou par SMS. Si un tel message arrive, on ne clique sur aucun lien, et on le supprime. Une fusion pourrait bien offrir un prétexte commode aux arnaqueurs, d'autant plus que Free a déjà été victime d'une cyberattaque, il y a deux ans, avec récupération d'un grand nombre d'informations. Les abonnés qui veulent en savoir plus sur l'usage de leurs données, ou exercer leurs droits, sont renvoyés vers les politiques de confidentialité de Free.

articles.title: How Bout India built a travel company without selling packages
articles.text:
How Bout India built a travel company without selling packages
By refusing the cookie‑cutter tour, Himanshu Maru and his co‑founders turned personalization into a moat, earning 970+ glowing reviews and a loyal global clientele.
Himanshu Maru started Bout India in 2013 with a simple bet: that international travellers to India wanted something built around them, not a fixed itinerary sold off a brochure. Thirteen years later, that bet has become the foundation of a distinctive inbound travel business.
Most travel companies begin by asking how many packages they can sell. Bout India took a different route. Founded in Jaipur in 2013 by Himanshu Maru, Managing Director; Bhupender Rana, Director, Operations; and Vinod Jhajharia, Director, Marketing, the company built its offering around a simple proposition: international travellers visiting India should not have to fit themselves into a pre-designed itinerary.
Each journey is planned around the traveller’s interests, pace and practical requirements. The company’s model centers on 100% tailor-made trips, with no fixed group packages and a direct relationship between the traveller and the person responsible for planning the experience.
Why tailor‑made mattered more than packages
Planning a trip to India can be complex for a first-time international visitor. The country’s geographic scale, distinct cultural regions, transport options, and local logistics require decisions that go beyond booking flights and hotels.
A traveller interested in Rajasthan may want heritage sites and local experiences, while someone visiting Ladakh may need planning around altitude, road conditions, and acclimatization. A wellness traveller heading to Kerala may prioritize retreat quality and time for rest.
Maru’s founding insight was that travellers would value a company that removed this complexity while preserving the feeling that the journey belonged to them. Rather than selling a standard route, Bout India positioned itself as a planning partner.
That approach is reflected in the company’s Destination Expert model. Each client is assigned a named expert who manages the relationship from the initial enquiry through the trip.
Reviews published on the company’s website frequently mention individual team members by name. While testimonials are not independent audits of service quality, this pattern illustrates the personal accountability the company seeks to build into its operating model.
Zero negative reviews and repeat travellers According to Bout India’s reported company information, its traction includes:
- 4.9/5-stars average rating across 970+ reviews on TripAdvisor and Google Maps
- A claimed zero-negative-review and 100% happy-customer record
- Travellers served from over 50 countries
- References to repeat customers who have booked second or third trips
The distinction between company-reported claims and independently verified performance is important. Review platforms can change, ratings can fluctuate, and customer-satisfaction records should ideally be assessed through the underlying reviews. Nevertheless, the reported figures indicate the reputation Bout India has sought to build.
For a services business, repeat and referral behavior can be especially valuable. A returning traveller is placing trust in the company’s ability to understand their preferences and deliver consistently.
Keeping personal involvement at the core
Bout India’s positioning continues to emphasize founder involvement. Company testimonials reference Maru personally checking in with clients, responding to concerns, and remaining involved in the travel experience.
Its Destination Expert structure combines individual ownership with a broader team. The company has also expanded across categories, including heritage travel, luxury experiences, wellness and Ayurveda retreats in Kerala, high-altitude adventure travel in Ladakh and Spiti, wildlife safaris, spiritual circuits, honeymoon and family travel, and corporate/MICE travel.
Why bespoke journeys beat standardized tours
Bout India’s model reflects a broader shift in the experience economy. As travellers gain access to online booking platforms and standardized packages, the value of a specialist may increasingly lie in interpretation, judgement, and reassurance.
A booking platform can compare prices, but a specialist can help a traveller decide whether a route is realistic, whether a destination suits their interests, or how to balance sightseeing with rest.
That is particularly relevant to inbound travel, where customers may be unfamiliar with local distances, seasonal conditions and operational realities. A tailor-made approach can address those concerns before they become problems.
Personalized travel does require skilled staff, detailed communication, and careful execution. The company must, therefore, demonstrate that the additional service creates enough value to justify the model.
Lessons in trust, service, and differentiation
Bout India is not a technology startup in the traditional sense. Its core proposition is built around people, destination expertise, and service delivery. Yet its approach offers a lesson relevant to India’s wider services economy.
In high-trust, high-consideration purchases such as international travel, radical personalization can be a durable differentiator. Customers may compare prices, but they also evaluate how confidently a company understands their needs and responds when plans change.
For founders, the lesson is to identify which parts of the customer experience should remain personal as the business grows. Technology can improve communication and operations, but the underlying relationship still depends on judgement and accountability.
Bout India’s journey illustrates one possible answer: build a system in which personal attention is not an exception, but a defining part of the product itself.

articles.title: "Si vous n’avez pas retiré vos crypto-actifs au 31 décembre 2026..." : Binance France prévient ses utilisateurs avant qu'il ne soit trop tard
articles.text:
Binance : les comptes français seront fermés le 31 décembre 2026, récupérez rapidement vos crypto-actifs
S'il vous reste des crypto-actifs sur la plateforme Binance, ne traînez pas trop pour les retirer, car sinon elles seront perdues ou il vous faudra payer des frais.
Si vous êtes un utilisateur de Binance et que son récent piratage massif ne vous a pas déjà incité à mettre vos cryptomonnaies ailleurs, l'annonce du jour devrait terminer de vous décider. Via un email envoyé à ses utilisateurs, la plus importante plateforme d'échange de cryptomonnaies au monde rappelle que "votre compte Binance France sera clôturé à compter du 31 décembre 2026". Faisons le point sur la situation.
Sans agrément Mica, Binance France s'en va
Depuis le 1er juillet dernier, les sociétés proposant des services crypto en Europe doivent respecter le règlement Mica (Markets in Crypto-Assets). Faute d'avoir pu obtenir cet agrément à temps, Binance restreint depuis cet été la plupart de ses services sur le continent, y compris en France. Impossible d'y ouvrir un nouveau compte, mais aussi d'acheter ou de vendre des cryptos ou de faire du trading, laissant seule la possibilité de retirer ses fonds.
Binance a désormais annoncé que la plateforme allait totalement cesser ses services en France, et que les utilisateurs ont jusqu'au 29 novembre pour retirer leurs cryptos sans frais. En effet, passée cette date les personnes retirant leurs cryptos "se verront appliqués des frais mensuels de 0,025% du solde", avec un minimum de 10 dollars.
	
Si vous n’avez pas retiré vos crypto-actifs au 31 décembre 2026, ce message constitue une notification de notre intention de considérer votre compte comme inactif, conformément à nos Conditions d’Utilisation.
De plus, si les crypto-actifs ne sont pas retirés au 31 décembre 2026, Binance considerera le compte comme inactif et que "cela peut entraîner la conversion, le transfert ou tout autre traitement de vos crypto-actifs."
En somme, s'il vous reste des cryptos sur Binance, il est préférable de bouger ces fonds vers une plateforme agréée Mica ou sur un portefeuille auto-hébergé avant le 29 novembre pour ne rien perdre dans l'opération. Reste à voir quand Binance parviendra à revenir en Europe, puisque la société souhaite toujours obtenir cet agrément.

articles.title: Samsung Galaxy S27, S27+, S27 Pro et S27 Ultra : les configurations photo fuitent et déçoivent déjà
articles.text:
Attendus au tournant sur le terrain de la photo, les Samsung Galaxy S27 voient aujourd’hui les caractéristiques techniques de leurs blocs caméras dévoilées dans les grandes lignes par SammyGuru. Entre des modèles classiques qui font du surplace et des versions haut de gamme qui laissent de côté certains objectifs, les premiers détails ne sont pas très encourageants pour les futurs smartphones haut de gamme de Samsung.
|  | Galaxy S27 | Galaxy S27+ | Galaxy S27 Pro | Galaxy S27 Ultra | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grand-angle (principal) | 50 Mpx : Sony IMX955 ou Samsung S5KGNG | 50 Mpx : Sony IMX955 ou Samsung S5KGNG | 200 Mpx : Samsung S5KHP6 | 200 Mpx : Samsung S5KHP6 | 
| Ultra-grand-angle | 12 Mpx : Sony IMX564 | 12 Mpx : Sony IMX564 | 50 Mpx : Samsung S5KJN3 ou Sony IMX855 | 50 Mpx : Samsung S5KJN3 ou Sony IMX855 | 
| Téléobjectif | 12 Mpx, 3x : Samsung S5K3K1 | 12 Mpx, 3x : Samsung S5K3K1 | 50 Mpx, 3x : Samsung S5KJN3 ou the Sony IMX855 | 50 Mpx, 5x : Samsung S5KJN3 ou the Sony IMX855 | 
| Selfie | 12 Mpx : Samsung S5K3LU ou Sony IMX874 | 12 Mpx : Samsung S5K3LU ou Sony IMX874 | 16 Mpx : Samsung S5K2P5 | 16 Mpx : Samsung S5K2P5 | 
Les caméras des Galaxy S27 et S27+ feraient du surplace
Si l’on en croit les dernières indiscrétions partagées, les Galaxy S27 et S27+ ressembleraient comme deux gouttes d’eau sur le plan de la photo aux Galaxy S26 et S26+, avec un capteur principal de 50 mégapixels Sony IMX955 ou Samsung avec le S5KGNG. Sur ces deux modèles, on retrouverait également le même capteur ultra grand-angle de 12 mégapixels (Sony IMX564) que celui utilisé sur le Galaxy S23.
Du côté du zoom et de la caméra frontale, de nouveaux capteurs feraient leur apparition avec un module téléobjectif de 12 mégapixels offrant un zoom 3x (Samsung S5K3K1) et un capteur selfie de 12 mégapixels (Samsung S5K3LU ou Sony IMX874). Rien de neuf, donc, pour les modèles de base.
Des Galaxy S27 Pro et S27 Ultra décevants ?
Les Galaxy S27 Pro et S27 Ultra recevraient un nouveau capteur principal de 200 mégapixels (Samsung S5KHP6) épaulé par un ultra grand-angle de 50 mégapixels (Samsung S5KJN3 ou Sony IMX855). Affichant seulement 12 mégapixels pour le téléobjectif, les deux modèles proposeraient respectivement un zoom optique 3x pour le Pro et un zoom optique 5x pour l’Ultra, actant la disparition pure et simple d’un second téléobjectif comme on le retrouve actuellement sur le Galaxy S26 Ultra.
Pour compléter cette configuration, la caméra selfie grimperait à 16 mégapixels avec un capteur Samsung S5K2P5. Samsung est évidemment soumis à la contrainte de l’augmentation du coût des composants, mais c’est aussi le cas de ses concurrents, qui ne ménagent pourtant pas leurs efforts côté photo. On pense notamment à l’Oppo Find X10 Pro Max que nous avons récemment testé et qui nous a fait forte impression sur ce point.

articles.title: Critical Xen Orchestra auth bypass flaw exploited to hijack VM servers
articles.text:
A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Xen Orchestra is being actively exploited in attacks that could grant administrator privileges and allow takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts.
Xen Orchestra is a web-based management platform developed by French software company Vates, used to manage XCP-ng virtualization environments, including virtual machines, hosts, and pools.
The vulnerability, tracked as VSA-2026-062, affects Xen Orchestra and the Xen Orchestra Appliance (XOA) and allows remote attackers with network access to the management interface to bypass authentication using a specially crafted cookie. A CVE identifier and CVSS score have not been assigned yet.
According to a Vates security advisory, the flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication tokens sent through REST API requests.
The flaw stems from how Xen Orchestra processes authentication cookies.
By sending a specially crafted cookie (authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D) containing an empty JSON object ({}), attackers can trick the platform into retrieving an existing authentication token and logging them in as its owner, without requiring actual credentials.
Once authenticated, attackers can retrieve "reusable login token IDs" through the /rest/v0/users/me/authentication_tokens REST API endpoint, which can be used for further access.
"An adversary can bypass authentication and perform actions with 'Admin' privilege. Xen Orchestra compromise can lead to arbitrary code execution on managed pools and a full XCP-ng node takeover as root," warns Vates.
The company has released Xen Orchestra 6.9.1 (stable) and 6.10.0 (latest), including patched xo-server packages 5.211.2 and 5.213.1 to fix these security vulnerabilities.
Administrators should install the update immediately, and if not possible, restrict Xen Orchestra access to dedicated management networks and block known malicious IP addresses.
Security researchers Filip Magic and Christoffer Olsen of TDC NET Security discovered the vulnerability.
Exploited in attacks
Vates confirmed that the vulnerability is being actively exploited and shared the following indicators of compromise (IOCs) to help administrators identify attacks:
- Attacker's infrastructure: Connections to 91.211.251.112:8001 or ustar3rqxgnskzgnwkgpofgtvxevm6cx3lxdbwt4mndtveqyaohid.onion:3333.
- Suspicious authentication cookies: HTTP requests containing authenticationToken=j:%7B%7D or authenticationToken=j:{}.
- Virtual machines: A VM named pivot2.
- Modified VM configurations: Virtual machines configured with the hvm_serial: file parameter.
- Unusual files: /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar, /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar2, /.ustar5, and /.ustar6.
Administrators can also run the following commands on XCP-ng hosts to check for unusual VM configurations, virtual machines configured to use a file for its serial port, and malicious files:
xe vm-list params=name-label,platform | grep -B1 'hvm_serial: file'
zgrep -- '-serial file:' /var/log/xensource.log*
ls -la /etc/ld.so.preload /.ustar* /etc/cron.d/zz-ustar*
However, Vates warns that exploitation will not generate any identifiers in logs, such as the use of specially crafted cookies, and instead must be detected through HTTP monitoring.
The company also says these IOCs are only associated with this known attack campaign and may differ for other threat actors.
Companies that believe they are compromised should rotate passwords and secrets used by their virtualization environments.

articles.title: El creador de clones gratuitos de Adobe presenta replicaciones de Microsoft Office Excel, PowerPoint y Word de código abierto; herramientas de Autodesk y otros servicios basados en suscripción pueden ser los próximos
articles.text:
Brandon Thomas llevaba unas semanas llamando la atención por desarrollar alternativas gratuitas a programas de Adobe como Photoshop, Illustrator o Premiere Pro utilizando la IA de Claude para escribir buena parte del código. Ahora, el programador (que acumula unos 15 años de experiencia) ha decidido ampliar su proyecto ArtCraft al presentar sus propias versiones de Word, Excel y PowerPoint.
Según recoge Tom’s Hardware, las nuevas aplicaciones se llaman WordCraft, GridCraft y DeckCraft y ya están publicadas en GitHub. La idea es ofrecer programas de código abierto que cualquier persona pueda utilizar sin pagar una suscripción, pero todavía se encuentran en una fase temprana de desarrollo y necesitan muchas funciones para competir con los originales.
No quiere quedarse en Adobe y Microsoft: Autodesk también está en el punto de mira
Lo más curioso es que Thomas no es un principiante que haya descubierto cómo programar con inteligencia artificial. Tras 15 años trabajando como ingeniero de software, respondió en X a las críticas por utilizar Claude para crear sus apps recordando que sí, que sabe programar, pero que estos modelos permiten asumir una cantidad de trabajo que normalmente requeriría todo un equipo.
Por otro lado, una de las ventajas que busca con ArtCraft es que sus programas funcionen en Windows, macOS y Linux, y así cubriría un nicho que Adobe ha descuidado. Además, el código de WordCraft, GridCraft y DeckCraft está disponible para que otros desarrolladores puedan revisarlo y contribuir a mejorarlo, una de las bases de los proyectos de código abierto.
Así, el proyecto también ha despertado el interés de usuarios que quieren alternativas a otros programas de pago. De hecho, dentro de su comunidad ya se habla de desarrollar herramientas de diseño asistido por ordenador que puedan competir con Autodesk y seguir la misma idea de crear versiones gratuitas de aplicaciones que requieren licencias o suscripciones.
Eso sí, conviene tener en cuenta que los programas de Thomas todavía están lejos de ofrecer todas las funciones de las herramientas que pretenden sustituir. Sus repositorios describen las aplicaciones como versiones alfa, por lo que pueden presentar errores y limitaciones importantes. Por ahora, lo que ha conseguido es publicar una colección de alternativas abiertas a programas muy conocidos, aunque queda bastante trabajo antes de poder utilizarlas como sustitutos completos.

articles.title: Equity turns to AI to predict staff exits and retain talent
articles.text:
Equity Group, Kenya’s second-largest lender by assets, is developing an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to forecast staff departures, as it seeks to retain specialist employees and give managers more time to fill critical roles.
The Nairobi-based group said in its 2025 sustainability report that it was developing “predictive analytics to forecast attrition and identify risk windows.” Equity said earlier warnings would help it decide when to intervene to retain employees and where to prepare for staffing gaps.
Equity’s move to use AI to predict staff departures reflects a challenge for Kenya’s banks. As fintechs, telcos, and rival lenders compete for the same pool of digital and payments talent, keeping experienced staff has become as important as hiring them.
“Early insight into potential employee turnover would support targeted retention actions and sustainable staffing strategies to ensure reinforcement and retention of critical talent and preparation for such situations in a sustainable way,” Equity said in the sustainability report.
Net employment turnover fell to 10.6% last year from 11.1% in 2024. The decline was smaller than the improvement in the previous year, when Equity reported turnover falling from 17% in 2023 to about 11% in 2024.
The bank nearly doubled hiring to 3,198 people in 2025, while its overall workforce grew by 2.2% to 13,370. Its permanent workforce rose by nearly 1,000, while temporary employees fell by almost 700. Staff costs rose 18% to KES 39.5 billion ($303.9 million) from KES 33.4 billion ($257 million) a year earlier.
The push to retain specialist staff comes as Equity’s businesses outside Kenya account for a growing share of its earnings. Its regional banking subsidiaries generated 48% of banking profit after tax in 2025, with the Democratic Republic of Congo alone contributing KES 24.7 billion.
The group already sends specialists from its head office on secondment to subsidiaries that need their expertise and is bringing workforce records and performance data from across its markets into a single human resources system.
Equity advertises vacancies internally first and offers incentives for employees with critical skills and those in leadership roles. It is also formalising career paths that allow technical specialists to advance without taking on management duties.
Average training time rose to 74 hours per employee in 2025 from 45 the previous year, and the lender made some generative AI courses mandatory for all staff.
The group gave no launch date for the forecasting tool. Its report describes the approach as predictive analytics and leaves open how the model will work, what employee data it will use, and whether it will flag individuals or forecast turnover across teams and markets.
