articles.title: Black Friday: Warum die Rabattschlacht schon jetzt tobt
articles.text:
Frühe Black-Friday-Angebote: Lohnt sich der Kauf schon jetzt?
Wir schauen auf den Kalender und reiben uns verwundert die Augen: Der Black Friday ist erst am 27. November – und doch wirbt gefühlt schon die halbe Branche mit dem Schnäppchen-Schlagwort, das die preisbewussten Kund:innen in Wallung bringen soll. Und die Geschäfte sind erfinderisch: Pre-Black-Friday-Angebote, Early-Black-Friday-Deals und Black Weeks sind nur ein paar der kreativen Wortschöpfungen, die allesamt nur eins suggerieren sollen: Billiger wird’s so schnell nicht mehr.
Man könnte fast glauben, der Handel hätte Angst, den Black Friday zu verpassen. Doch in Wahrheit laufen vor allem die Händler dem Geld ihrer Kund hinterher. Dass sie damit seit Jahren immer früher anfangen, hat einen Grund, der insbesondere in diesem Jahr eine große Rolle spielen könnte: Die Kund:innen können ihr Weihnachtsgeld, so sie es überhaupt noch bekommen, schließlich nur einmal ausgeben.
Und wer hier früher dran ist als die anderen, so das Kalkül, hat größere Chancen darauf. Wer also sein Budget bereits Anfang November bei Händler A gelassen hat, fällt Ende November womöglich als Kunde für Händler B aus.
Die Angst, zu früh gekauft zu haben
Doch gerade in wirtschaftlich angespannten Zeiten überlegen Verbraucher:innen genauer, wofür sie ihr Erspartes ausgeben. Schon länger beobachten Marktforscher:innen gar nicht mal so sehr eine Kaufzurückhaltung, wohl aber, dass die Verbraucher:innen bis zum November mit wichtigen Anschaffungen warten – wohl wissend, dass in dieser Zeit das Rennen um die Rabatte besonders ausgeprägt ist.
Eher neu ist hier aber neben der verlängerten Rückgabefrist bis in den Januar, mit der Amazon schon seit Jahren den Markt zum Mitziehen motiviert, ein weiterer Faktor: Immer mehr Händler:innen bieten automatisch oder auf Anfrage eine Bestpreis-Garantie für all jene, die sich jetzt für einen Kauf entscheiden. Die Idee dahinter: Wer heute kauft, soll sich in zwei Wochen nicht ärgern, wenn das gleiche Produkt am eigentlichen Black Friday plötzlich noch günstiger angeboten wird.
Dabei lohnt sich dennoch ein Blick ins Kleingedruckte, denn nicht bei allen Händlern bedeutet das, dass man automatisch davon profitiert. In einigen Fällen müssen Kund:innen selbst aktiv werden, den günstigeren Preis entdecken und die Differenz beim Kundenservice beantragen. Eine weitere Einschränkung: Während die Preisgarantie in vielen Fällen branchenweit gilt, bezieht sie sich manchmal auch lediglich auf die Preise beim selben Händler.
Aus Sicht der Logistik ein gutes Geschäft
Dass viele Händler:innen den Black Friday entzerren wollen, hat aber auch noch einen weiteren, durchaus vernünftigen Grund: die Logistik. Denn die letzten Jahre haben gezeigt, dass innerhalb weniger Tage Lager, Versanddienstleister und Kundenservice übermäßig strapaziert wurden. Auch können die Händler:innen so ihre Ads-Kampagnen über einen längeren Zeitraum ziehen, anstatt an einem einzigen Wochenende mit allen anderen um die Aufmerksamkeit der Kund:innen zu buhlen.
Aus dem Black Friday wird so eine Art vorweihnachtliche Dauerschleife der Kaufverführung. Noch sieht es nicht danach aus, dass die Händler:innen das Thema überreizt hätten, auch wenn das Risiko durchaus besteht, dass dabei die Aufmerksamkeit irgendwann auf der Strecke bleibt.
All das ist aus Sicht vieler Händler nachvollziehbar. Denn wer abwartet, bis die Mitbewerber ihre Rabattaktionen starten, muss nicht nur gegen deren Preise ankämpfen, sondern riskiert auch, dass viele potenzielle Kund:innen längst eingekauft haben und aus dem Rennen sind.

articles.title: ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
articles.text:
ChatGPT is going to let you chat with verified “Business Agents” that represent a brand to help you with things like comparison shopping. The feature, available first to “eligible” e-commerce and online service businesses in the US, is launching as part of a suite of business-focused features in ChatGPT being announced today in beta.
ChatGPT is getting verified AI ‘Business Agents’
ChatGPT’s new AI agents represent companies and can help with things like comparison shopping.
You can start talking with a Business Agent if a business that has created one appears in a response from ChatGPT. While chatting with a custom agent, you can ask about a business’s offerings and ask follow-up questions, like asking about differences between two different products. Businesses can specify a Business Agent’s instructions and provide business context so that the agent knows how to respond.
Chats with Business Agents will be clearly labeled and separate from your main ChatGPT conversation, OpenAI says. To help people know that they’re talking with an agent that actually represents the business, companies will be able to claim their organization and get verified through a feature called Business Hub. (OpenAI isn’t sharing specifics about its verification methods because there are different methods for different businesses, VP of monetization Benji Shomair said in a press briefing.) Business Hub will also let companies see insights such as mentions in ChatGPT responses and top “discovery topics” where their business pops up.
“Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT,” OpenAI says in a blog post. “We’re starting with the foundations: accurate business information, useful insights and conversations that help people make informed decisions.” As things evolve, “we’ll explore more ways for businesses to connect with customers — directly or through agents and in ChatGPT and beyond. Our goal is to make ChatGPT more useful for people making decisions, and give businesses new ways to participate and grow.”

articles.title: Agent Substrate: Advancing Kubernetes for Agents at Scale | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
AI agents spend most of their time idle, waiting on a human prompt, a tool result or a model response. Kubernetes wasn’t built for that. Running one Pod per session holds memory for sessions that aren’t doing anything, and deleting Pods between turns pays a multi-second cold start every time and loses the agent’s state. RL post-training hits the same wall.
Agent Substrate, now donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox, is an open-source, security-hardened, zero-trust runtime for sandboxed agents, engineered to safely run millions of agents and tools with 10x higher density than standard containers. It multiplexes many sessions over a small pool of worker Pods. Idle sessions are checkpointed, memory and filesystem included, and restored onto whichever worker is free when the next request arrives. As agentic infrastructure fragments into proprietary runtimes that bypass Kubernetes, NVIDIA is contributing upstream to keep this work open.
This post covers which workloads suit Agent Substrate, what is being built upstream, and how the project works with KAI Scheduler and NVIDIA Dynamo components in the DSX AI Factory Platform.
The shape of an agent workload
Traditional web services run as a relatively small number of long-lived instances. Agents follow a different pattern: they wake up and take one step, running a shell command, editing a file, calling a test suite or calling an LLM. Then they wait, sometimes for milliseconds and sometimes for minutes, before the next step. The agent’s state (its filesystem, its processes, its working directory) has to continue between steps.
Kubernetes struggles because spinning up a compute Pod for an agent means a trip through the API server, admission, etcd, the scheduler, the kubelet, image pulls and network setup. That takes seconds, which is fine for a service that runs for weeks. It’s far too slow for a sandbox that must appear, run a 10 ms bash command and get out of the way, hundreds of times per second.
This leaves platform teams with two suboptimal choices: either keep one Pod warm per agent and pay for compute that is idle almost all the time, or create Pods on demand and pay a cold start penalty on every step.
How Agent Substrate works
Agent Substrate uses Kubernetes for running a pool of ready pods. It creates a separate control plane that maps a large set of actors (agents and their environments) onto that smaller pool of workers. When an actor goes idle, it is snapshotted out of its sandbox (gVisor or a microVM) and its worker is freed. When the actor is called again, it is restored into whichever worker is free, with its memory and filesystem state intact.
Waking an actor doesn’t require a new trip through the API server, scheduler or kubelet. Agent Substrate restores the actor onto an existing worker instead. The worker pods are still ordinary Kubernetes Pods, so cluster scheduling, quotas and placement policies still apply as we describe later.
The use cases driving demand
We see three kinds of workload driving demand for Agent Substrate:
- Coding assistants and agent serving: A coding agent alternates between LLM calls and work in its own environment: cloning a repository, editing files, running builds and tests. Users expect the environment to persist between turns and to respond immediately. A platform serving thousands of these sessions can’t afford a dedicated warm sandbox for each one.
- Reinforcement Learning (RL) post-training with agentic environments: RL with verifiable rewards runs GPU trainers and generation servers alongside a fleet of CPU-heavy environments (code sandboxes, compilers, browsers, simulators) that execute actions and check results. Sandbox demand arrives in bursts as rollout batches dispatch actions. A training run can grow from a few hundred sandboxes in early experiments to many hundreds of thousands in production. The slowest environment determines when the trainer gets its next batch, so cold starts on that path leave GPUs idle.
- GPU sandboxes for research: A researcher’s coding agent needs a GPU, not to serve a model but to compile CUDA code, benchmark a kernel or run a numerical calculation. It launches a GPU sandbox on a shared cluster, runs the job and deletes the sandbox. Supporting this across an organization requires many short-lived, isolated GPU sandboxes that start quickly and share a limited pool of GPUs fairly.
Upstream work: What’s landed and what’s next
Each contribution below started from one of those use cases. All of this work is public in the Agent Substrate repository:
- When every worker is busy, the next request waits instead of failing: In an oversubscribed system, such as a coding-assistant platform at peak or an RL rollout burst, a user’s next turn can arrive while every worker is busy. Agent Substrate used to return an error immediately, even though another actor would usually free a worker a moment later.
Request parking in the Agent Substrate router (#221) holds the request and retries the resume until a worker frees up, with a bounded wait and a cap on how many requests can wait at once. A follow-up (#1229) makes sure requests to already-running actors never get stuck in that line.
- Giving agents a GPU inside their sandbox: The research GPU sandbox described above, along with GPU-backed RL environments such as simulators.
We are working on device-pluggability that adds device support on Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA). Device vendors plug in their devices through a profile, each container in a sandbox requests only the devices it needs (#752), and the same model works for both gVisor and microVM sandboxes. NVIDIA GPUs will be the first supported device.
- One container can’t starve or kill its neighbors: An agent sandbox often runs the agent’s workload next to helper containers for logging, proxying or metrics. Some of those may be untrusted. A runaway container shouldn’t consume the whole sandbox’s memory and take the agent down with it.
Per-container CPU and memory limits for microVM sandboxes (#859) addresses that issue. A container that exceeds its memory limit is stopped on its own, and the rest of the sandbox keeps running.
Preserving GPU sandboxes across suspend and resume
When an agent pauses to wait for human review, its sandbox should release the GPU and resume later with its compiled artifacts and loaded data still in place. Supporting that requires saving and restoring both the agent’s state and the GPU state.
Restoring GPU state introduces hardware compatibility constraints. A GPU checkpoint can usually be restored only onto the same GPU model, and sometimes only with the same driver version. Agent Substrate proposes a design to address this.
Device vendors describe how to pause their devices safely and which device properties a snapshot depends on. Agent Substrate records those properties with each snapshot and restores the sandbox on a matching device, or falls back to a clean cold start if none is available. The design is vendor-neutral and builds on DRA. NVIDIA GPUs are the first target; the design can be extended to other hardware types.
NVIDIA Dynamo: Connecting the agent loop to the inference loop
Agent Substrate manages where agents act; inference runtimes manage where they think. Both face a similar efficiency challenge: keeping idle sandboxes warm wastes CPU and memory, while rebuilding model context on repeated model calls wastes GPU cycles. Scaling each layer independently improves utilization. Coordinating them can also reduce latency and preserve reusable context as agents move between tool execution and model calls.
NVIDIA Dynamo, the open-source distributed inference framework, provides that coordination. Agent Substrate activates, suspends and restores stateful agent environments across a pool of warm sandbox workers. Dynamo orchestrates inference across GPU workers. The Dynamo router sits between them and connects what the agent is doing with what is happening on the GPUs.
Making inference agent-aware
Traditional inference routing treats every model call as an independent request. In an agent, each request is one step in a longer loop, and consecutive requests often reuse the same system prompt, tool definitions, conversation history and earlier observations.
Dynamo’s router sees where reusable key-value (KV) cache lives, which workers are busy with prefill or decode, and how load is spread across the GPU fleet. Agent Substrate and the agent harness add signals such as session identity, request priority, expected output length, tool-call boundaries and lifecycle events.
With both, Dynamo can:
- Keep related model calls on workers that already hold reusable KV cache, without creating overloaded GPU hot spots
- Prioritize interactive turns over background agent work when the inference pool is under pressure
- Keep system prompts, tool definitions and conversation history available across tool-call gaps
- Drop cache state from terminated subagents, closed reasoning branches or summarized contexts first
- Prepare likely context as a tool call approaches completion
Feeding GPU intelligence back to Agent Substrate
The most important part of the integration is that Dynamo exposes inference signals to Agent Substrate, helping it decide when to keep agents running, suspend them or resume them.
Dynamo is closer to GPU execution than the agent runtime. It has visibility into cache readiness, queue pressure, active prefill and decode work, and how long an LLM request is likely to take. That information can inform both inference routing and how Agent Substrate schedules agent sandboxes.
Dynamo can return signals such as projected time to first token, projected completion time, request progress, cache readiness, and GPU-pool saturation. Agent Substrate can use this feedback to decide whether to keep an Actor resident, suspend it during a longer inference wait, or resume it as the model response approaches completion.
At fleet scale, the same feedback can help tune warm-worker capacity, regulate agent and subagent fan-out, and avoid activating CPU sandboxes that would otherwise sit idle behind a saturated GPU queue.
This integration establishes a simple division of responsibility. Agent Substrate manages the high-frequency lifecycle of agent environments. Dynamo manages the high-performance lifecycle of inference. Dynamo connects the two around the loop that defines agentic computing: model call, tool call, observation, and model call again.
Get started: A coding assistant with Dynamo and Agent Substrate
This guide provides step-by-step instructions for deploying a coding assistant on Dynamo and Agent Substrate.
You’ll learn how to:
Guide link placeholder – add when supplied
- Run Pi coding agents as Substrate Actors: giving each agent an isolated, stateful environment to inspect repositories, edit code, and run tests.
- Connect the agents to GLM-5.3-Flash served through NVIDIA Dynamo: completing the loop between model inference and tool execution in Substrate-managed sandboxes.
- Use Harbor to orchestrate evaluations on SWE-bench Verified: running agents against software issues and collecting results to assess whether their changes resolve the tasks.
Agent Substrate is still evolving. Its APIs are still changing, GPU support is being rebuilt on the new DRA foundation, and parts of the Dynamo agent integration are experimental. Now is a good time to contribute and help shape the core design.
Running Agent Substrate with KAI Scheduler and Dynamo
Agent Substrate runs above Kubernetes and works alongside the NVIDIA software that serves models and places workloads. Substrate manages stateful agent environments, KAI Scheduler places the Kubernetes workloads, and Dynamo serves the models and exchanges inference-state signals with the agent runtime.
Together, they coordinate CPU-side tool execution with GPU-side inference so shared cluster capacity is used more productively.
Table 1, below, shows where each piece sits. Dynamo, KAI Scheduler and the Kubernetes foundation components are part of NVIDIA DSX OS.
Agent Substrate is an independent, open-source CNCF Sandbox project and not a named DSX OS component, though NVIDIA is contributing upstream and developing interoperability with DSX OS components.
| Architectural layer | Technology | Role | DSX relationship | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Agent and RL framework | NeMo RL, NeMo Gym, your agent harness | Agent loops, rollout orchestration, and environment requests | Application layer above DSX OS | 
| Agent execution | Agent Substrate | Stateful, isolated sandboxes multiplexed across warm workers | External open-source runtime integrating with DSX OS components | 
| Model serving | NVIDIA Dynamo ( ThunderAgent, Grove, ModelExpress) | KV-aware, agent-aware routing; prefill/decode coordination; topology-aware placement of inference pods | DSX OS model serving | 
| Workload orchestration | KAI Scheduler | Placement, queues, gang scheduling, topology awareness, and fair share | DSX OS workload and GPU orchestration | 
| Kubernetes foundation | AI Cluster Runtime, GPU Operator, Network Operator, Topograph | Validated runtime and GPU, network, and topology management | DSX OS accelerated Kubernetes foundation | 
Table 1. Where Agent Substrate fits in the stack for running AI agents and RL environments on Kubernetes: each layer’s technology, role, and relationship to NVIDIA DSX OS.
KAI Scheduler and Agent Substrate operate at different scheduling levels: Substrate worker Pods are ordinary Kubernetes Pods. KAI Scheduler can place them today alongside the GPU trainers and inference servers they support. Coordinating worker-pool autoscaling with KAI’s queues and fair-share policies could extend resource sharing across tenants to the environment layer.
Build agent infrastructure with us at KubeCon
- Agent Substrate Community Party—Tuesday, Nov. 10, Salt Lake City. An informal evening for maintainers, contributors, and anyone in the ecosystem to connect. Join us to talk about all the contributions we mentioned in this blog and meet with the people building the future of agentic infrastructure on Kubernetes.
- Lightning session—Wednesday, Nov. 11, 1-1:15 pm at Google Cloud Booth #122: “Talk From Pods to Actors : GPU-Aware Infrastructure for Agentic Workloads”
- NVIDIA booth #170 at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America—Nov.10–12. Come talk to our experts about agent platforms, RL post-training on Kubernetes, Substrate, Dynamo and KAI Scheduler.
- Meet with Experts at NVIDIA booth #170—Wednesday, Nov. 11, from 3:15–3:35 p.m. MT to discuss Agent Substrate and running agent workloads on Kubernetes.
- Explore the full Meet the Experts lineup—NVIDIA at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026
Going further
If you’re building agent platforms, coding assistants or RL environments on Kubernetes, we want to hear about your workload. Find us at the event, check out the Dynamo guide or open an issue agent-substrate/substrate or ai-dynamo/dynamo. Join the community meetings and get involved in what comes next.

articles.title: Shrinking Hybrid Bonding Pitches Push Inspection Limits
articles.text:
Existing inspection tools struggle to capture defects, especially those hidden at the bond interface.
Key Takeaways:
Hybrid bonding represents a paradigm shift in advanced packaging, replacing 35 µm off-chip microbumps with 10 µm pitch or smaller pad-to-pad interconnects on-chip. It can be used to join silicon-to-silicon, as in DRAM-DRAM bonding in future HBM devices, or even disparate materials like GaN-on-silicon.
This elegant process, which is available on wafer-to-wafer or die-to-wafer platforms, reduces signal delay to negligible levels while enabling smaller, thinner packages with unmatched memory/processor speeds and bandwidth. It also consumes significantly less power.
Hybrid bonding’s success depends on the performance of advanced bonding equipment, as well as metrology’s ability to verify critical alignment, cleanliness, planarity, and surface properties — both before and after bonding. Solving these challenges is proving essential to realizing the vision of true 3D integration at the bonded-chip level.
But as hybrid bonding pitches continue to scale down below today’s production levels of 4 to 9 µm, some inspection and metrology methods are struggling to meet the spatial resolution and sensitivity needed to catch all relevant defect types, especially ones buried at the bond interface. Particles, voids, overlay errors, roughness, CMP defects, and warpage threaten the bond quality between chips. Even a single particle can delaminate the top wafer from the one below, resulting in catastrophic failure.
At times, conventional metrology fails to differentiate a killer defect from minor topographical variation. A handful of tools, including non-destructive optical, IR, X-ray, profilometry, AFM, and acoustic inspection tools, are working to resolve critical defects smaller than 100 nm. These are some of the most stringent requirements ever imposed on a semiconductor process.
“Particles and surface contamination are among the most critical defects in hybrid bonding, as they can prevent contact between bonding surfaces and lead to the formation of voids,” said Burhan Ali, product marketing director at Onto Innovation. “Smaller interconnect pitches reduce the tolerance for defects, making even nanoscale particles capable of causing bonding voids. For leading-edge hybrid bonding processes, defect size requirements can be as low as 50 nm.”
Cracks and delamination can be particularly insidious problems, especially in the early stages of process development, but also in full-scale production. “For cracks and delamination, acoustic micro-imaging (AMI) using ultrasound in the 200MHz range provides the highest resolution,” said Bryan Schackmuth, AMI product manager at Nordson Test & Inspection. “Ultrasound does not travel through air gaps that have a thickness down to about 0.1 µm. If a crack or delamination is around the 5 µm to 10 µm size (x and y) and is at least 0.1 µm thick (z), there is a good chance that it can be detected with acoustic micro-imaging.”
Figure 1, below, shows some of the most challenging defects to capture.
Fig. 1: Hybrid bonding defects and the methods used to capture them. Source: Laura Peters/Semiconductor Engineering
Four pivotal steps
The performance and reliability of hybrid bonds largely depend on the precision and across-wafer uniformity of the four main processes: surface planarization, surface activation, precision alignment, and thermal bonding.
Chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP), which combines mechanical and chemical removal, must achieve nanometer-scale control of surface topography and copper-pad recess, with negligible surface roughness (0.5nm RMS). Otherwise, dielectric-to-dielectric voids can form during bonding.
Wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding begins with the wafer processed to the final BEOL interconnect level. Next, a suitable dielectric (either SiCN or SiO2) is deposited and then etched to create vias to the metal below. Next, barrier and copper seed layers are deposited, followed by copper plating. Copper pads are typically square. Copper CMP then polishes the overburden to provide a slight dishing (several nm) below the planar feature. That minuscule gap will be filled when the copper expands during annealing. Next, wafer cleaning removes all contaminants.
Next, the exposed dielectric is activated in a plasma vacuum chamber to create an optimized bonding surface with many dangling Si-O– bonds. This is followed by a DI water rinse to hydrate the dielectric. Face-to-face (or face-to-back) bonding of the second wafer, processed up through copper CMP in the same manner as wafer 1, is then aligned with and bonded to wafer 1. Then the wafer pair is brought into intimate contact to form the initial bond, followed by furnace annealing at 350° C for two hours to expand the copper and form permanent Cu-Cu and dielectric-dielectric bonds.
Pre-bond inspection
Prior to bonding, CMP needs to be fine-tuned to provide a flat dielectric surface with a specific run-off profile at the wafer edge. Improper edge roll-off can distort alignment marks, leading to poor contact or voids, which compromise bond strength. The roll-off region must be perfectly smooth and free of microcracks, scratches, or handling damage.
Before micro-inspections, a full-wafer macro-inspection is often performed to catch scratches, large particles, or wafer edge damage. Macro-inspection complements micro-inspection findings and creates a detailed wafer map for every wafer in the lot. Scanning of every single wafer provides the necessary record-keeping for mission-critical devices.
“By inspecting 100% of the wafers at each mask level, our macro-inspection tool provides a great complement to the micro-inspection tools on the market,” said Errol Akomer, applications director at Microtronic. “Because they’re slow, they typically only sample each lot, looking at maybe two to five wafers per lot, so in many cases, they’re missing some really big defects that could affect the long-term reliability of the chips. In some applications, like data centers or aerospace, the customers may select only the best chips that come out of the lot. They don’t use the marginal ones that we like to call the walking wounded.”
After cleaning, automated optical inspection (AOI) is usually performed using brightfield and darkfield modes. Darkfield inspection, which collects scattered light from defects, is particularly effective for particles and scratches, while brightfield, which collects reflected light, is useful for isolating residual material like slurry, pattern defects, and topographical surface damage.
Fig. 2: Submicron defects prior to hybrid bonding must be accurately classified to distinguish nuisance defects from killer defects. Source: Onto Innovation 
Topographical variations, both local and global, affect bondability. “In advanced processes, localized topography can be more yield-critical, but both global and localized height variations are important in hybrid bonding because they create different process failure mechanisms,” explained Maruko Wu, senior director of product marketing at Onto Innovation. “Interferometric technologies are generally applicable to measure wafer-level or die-level planarity, while OCD (optical CD) and AFM (atomic force microscope) are the best approaches for enabling extremely fine control of just a few nanometers local height variations. White-light or phase-shifting interferometry, as well as AFM, are used to measure copper recess levels.”
White-light or phase-shifting interferometry tools are provided by Bruker, KLA, Onto Innovation, and Zygo, and some companies offer double-sided inspection systems.
“Pre-bond defect inspection is commonly performed using advanced optical inspection systems, which offer high-throughput, full-wafer inspection capabilities, and can detect surface defects and particles with high sensitivity,” said Ali. The details of copper pad morphology require AFMs. “Surface roughness and copper pad topography are typically characterized using AFM, which provides nanometer- to sub-nanometer-scale resolution for accurate measurement of surface features such as roughness, dishing, and protrusion.”
AFMs are finding increasing application in the hybrid bonding process, particularly when just one nanometer of material can make a significant difference in determining whether or not the copper-copper pads fuse together during annealing. After CMP, the copper pads are recessed just 2 nm to 5 nm below the dielectric. Process control needs to keep this specified thickness within 2 nm across the wafer.
Both AFM and atomic force profilometry (AFP) are critical for surface characterization and process optimization. AFM delivers localized, high-resolution surface measurements of recess depth while illuminating pad divots or protrusions (see figure 3). AFP provides complementary large-area topography scans spanning nanometer-scale features to full wafer dimensions, including the bevel edge. AFP can reveal excessive topography at different points across a 33 × 26 mm large-area scan (see Figure 4), even when local AFM scans confirm in-spec dielectric roughness and copper pad recess. AFP is also a useful tool for monitoring wafer edge roll-off.
Fig. 3: AFM topography scans after three different CMP steps produce different recess depths. Source: Bruker
Fig. 4: Atomic force profilometry shows out-of-spec topography, despite earlier AFMs that indicated in-specification copper recess and roughness. Source: Bruker
“We are currently focused on failure analysis and three-dimensional (3D) imaging of existing bonds and potential identification of failed bonds,” said Thomas Rodgers, senior director of market strategy at Zeiss Microscopy. “Though it is outside our application scope, we are often asked to detect voids in the hybrid copper bonding interconnect, which can give insights into reliability and potential failure points.”
The company is also taking a novel approach to solving topographical issues in hybrid bonding. “Our colleagues in the Zeiss Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology business unit developed a solution for measuring and correcting surface planarity by inducing local strain in the wafer prior to backside thinning. We see increasing market interest in this solution, especially as HCB is used on multi-layer stacked die devices such as those seen in high bandwidth memory,” said Rodgers.
Post-bond metrology
After bonding, IR metrology tools verify alignment between the top and bottom copper pads because the infrared beam can penetrate the silicon. Just as too much copper recess on the pads can cause problems, too little recess can also cause problems. “Excessive copper dishing or protrusion can hinder proper Cu-Cu and dielectric-to-dielectric bonding, resulting in degraded electrical connectivity and reduced bond yield. Likewise, elevated surface roughness reduces the effective contact area between bonding surfaces, leading to lower bond strength and increased risk of bonding defects,” said Ali.
“Alignment also can be measured using 3D X-ray, both in classical computed tomography (CT) and laminography modes, giving a clear picture of the alignment and any overlay errors. We have shown some excellent results here with our tool,” said Rodgers.
For post-bonding, many engineers are turning to high-resolution X-ray imaging to inspect the bond interface, especially during early stages of process development. Advanced X-ray methods, such as laminography, allow 3D sub-micron inspection and quantification of defects, aiding in process optimization and failure analysis. High-resolution X-ray imaging is an essential technique for the development and failure analysis of hybrid bonds. A resolution of 150 nm has been demonstrated. [1]
“XRDI tends to be used for fully automated leading-edge wafer processing where the process steps can be more aggressive, and the cost of wafer loss and disruption to the line is more significant,” said John Wall, site manager at Bruker JV UK. “We can detect subsurface critical defects on patterned/metalized wafers with zero edge exclusion. Full wafer inspection can be performed at ~20wph, thus enabling in-line/at-line inspection for these critical defects.”
“When it comes to detecting cracks, delamination, and warpage, 3D X-ray is the tool of choice,” said Rodgers. “Our systems can show warpage and planarity of the bonds, while providing 3D image of cracks and voids without physically cutting the sample. Ultimately, this is used for localizing such defects.”
Acoustic microscopy, widely used to detect voids in microbumps, is now being applied to hybrid-bonded wafer stacks. “Currently, acoustic micro imaging (AMI) inspection is done after the device is fully assembled,” said Schackmuth. “With traditional microbumps, the pitch of 20µm to 40µm would normally become the critical defect size for a delamination or void. Hybrid bonding’s pitch in the 5µm to 10µm range drives the need for higher resolution capabilities in the AMI inspection.”
In acoustic imaging, the resolution is a function of the transducer’s wavelength, but at higher frequencies, the acoustic signal has shallower penetration. Higher frequencies can improve lateral resolution to distinguish two closely spaced voids and detect smaller voids, provided the signal-to-noise ratio is acceptable.
Schackmuth described the differences between resolving and detecting voids with AMI. “We can go up to our 165 MHz transducer, which gets you down to a resolution of 12 microns. But there’s resolution and detection. So if you had a 12-micron defect, 165 MHz could measure it accurately. But if you had a 5-micron defect, we could detect it, but not measure it accurately. So we’re in the process of developing higher frequency transducers to improve that resolution.”
Conclusion
Hybrid bonding is enabling denser, faster, and more power-efficient 3D semiconductor integration, but shrinking interconnect pitches are placing extraordinary demands on inspection and metrology. Particles, surface contamination, copper dishing, roughness, alignment errors, and buried voids can compromise bond quality, electrical performance, and long-term reliability.
To address these issues, manufacturers are combining optical inspection, interferometry, AFM, X-ray imaging, and acoustic microscopy to characterize bonding surfaces before assembly and detect hidden defects afterward. Yet no single technique provides the resolution, sensitivity, wafer coverage, and throughput required to identify every yield-critical defect.
As hybrid bonding scales toward finer pitches, the central challenge is developing faster, more sensitive, and complementary metrology methods that can distinguish yield-killing defects from harmless variations while also supporting high-volume manufacturing.

articles.title: Se busca a quien quiera vivir gratis en una casa de Málaga con piscina y jacuzzi. A cambio pide cinco horas de trabajo al día
articles.text:
Un estudio independiente junto a la piscina. Un amplio jacuzzi. Vistas a 700 metros de altitud y a 15 minutos del centro. Y todo gratis. Parece un anuncio porque las condiciones son demasiado buenas. El precio: cinco horas de trabajo al día, cinco días a la semana. Tampoco es para tanto, según se mire. Jaqui y David, una pareja de Comares, en la Axarquía malagueña, buscan voluntarios a través de la aplicación Workaway. No hay mucha letra pequeña, pero sí algunos matices a tener en cuenta.
Qué se ofrece. Alojamiento gratuito en un estudio “muy bonito y autónomo”, según los anfitriones. Está junto a la piscina de una casa unida a otras tres unidades independientes, en la parte más baja del pueblo. Ellos gestionan un alojamiento turístico y allí caben coches y autocaravanas, salvo las muy grandes, que deben quedarse a 30 minutos. Y aquí llega el primer pero: la piscina y el jacuzzi están a disposición de los voluntarios siempre y cuando no haya huéspedes. El que paga tiene prioridad.
Qué piden. Cinco horas diarias, cinco días a la semana: 25 horas semanales (como máximo). Las extra, si hicieran falta, se compensan en otro día. Las tareas incluyen jardinería básica, mantenimiento, cocina para la familia, ayuda doméstica, ayuda informática y proyectos creativos. El anuncio también menciona construcción. En un mes, son unas 100 horas de trabajo.
Evidentemente, cocinar para la familia no es cocinar para uno mismo, pero entre todos se reparte. Prefieren estancias de al menos un mes y parejas; también buscan practicar idiomas y compartir cultura. La privacidad, por ambas partes, es importante.
Lo que no dicen. Sin embargo, no se especifica si la comida está incluida ni si los voluntarios pagan gastos, aunque se asume que toda la compra corre a cargo de los anfitriones. Tampoco menciona contrato ni seguro. Eso sí, para contactar hay que pasar por caja: Workaway cobra una membresía anual de 59 euros para una persona y 69 para la pareja, que sale más rentable.
A cambio se da acceso a más de 50.000 ofertas en más de 170 países y un servicio de mensajería. Por otro lado, como prefieren parejas, serían 50 horas semanales para la casa, más de una jornada completa, a cambio de un estudio. No es un sueldo pero sí trabajo regular.
Casos similares. En Xataka hemos contado varias ofertas similares y casi todas comparten condiciones: 25 horas semanales piden en una casa con piscina cerca de Alicante, a cambio de mover heno y cuidar caballos. Otras 25 en un albergue del Camino Primitivo, incluye tres comidas, pero es un negocio privado, no una ONG. 24 horas en un santuario de Gredos y entre los requisitos piden dieta vegana y transporte propio. 20 horas en un santuario de cerdos en Hawái, con tres meses de estancia mínima. Comida, vuelos y seguro corren por cuenta del voluntario. Y hasta 30 horas en una isla griega con gatos, incluyendo en el gratis alojamiento y desayuno. Comida y cena, aparte. Con 25 horas, Málaga está en la media. Es más, un texto del blog de la propia plataforma lo presenta como lo habitual.
La ley, en una línea. Según la Ley 45/2015 de Voluntariado, que ya citamos, el voluntariado debe ser gratuito, con acuerdo por escrito y seguro de accidentes y enfermedad a cargo de la organización. Lo que distingue voluntariado de empleo, advierten los laboralistas, no son solo las horas, sino la compensación. Aquí quien pide es un alojamiento turístico, no una entidad de voluntariado. Así que antes de ir, es recomendable pedir por escrito tareas, horas, gastos cubiertos, comida y seguro. Incluso preguntar cuándo se puede usar el jacuzzi. Y recordar que “gratis” casi nunca significa “sin coste”. Entre la membresía, el desplazamiento y la comida, la casa gratis también tiene una factura que tener en cuenta.

articles.title: Nvidia probes whether foreign intelligence targeted Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Nvidia probes whether foreign intelligence targeted Jensen Huang
Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The company has said its board had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security had been compromised.
Dear Readers,
Nvidia’s board has opened an independent investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The move follows a New York Times report alleging that a business executive with whom Huang had a close relationship passed information to Beijing.
The company shares slid sharply on Monday following this news.
Nvidia said its board had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security had been compromised.
In other news, Sashikumar Sreedharan, the former MD for India at Google Cloud, has joined AI company Sarvam as President and Chief Business Officer. He will also be on the company’s board. Sreedharan will run Sarvam’s business across enterprises and government and expand its work with digital-native companies, developers and partners.
Meanwhile, the India subsidiary of travel booking platform MakeMyTrip has received Sebi’s approval to launch an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO is expected to comprise a sale of equity shares in MMT India by its parent MakeMyTrip and its wholly-owned subsidiary, ibibo Group Holdings (Singapore) Pte Ltd.
Lastly, 2026 is on track to be one of the four warmest years on record, according to the World Meteorological Organization.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- How Bariflo uses AI to help factories treat wastewater
- How these Mothers of Courage are fighting to keep girls in school
Here’s your trivia for today: What was Henry Ford’s original design for a car called? (Scroll down for the answer)
In-focus
How Bariflo uses AI to help factories treat wastewater
Bariflo Cybernetics wants factories to get more use out of their wastewater treatment plants. The Odisha-based startup combines sensors, AI software, and automation to adjust treatment processes, aiming to reduce the energy and chemicals needed to clean water for reuse.
It recently secured Rs 2 crore in milestone-linked funding from energy innovation platform MC² Plus, an initiative led by the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, and is preparing for a pilot with Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), according to founder and CEO Mrityunjay Sahu. The funding comes as Bariflo moves from developing and testing its technology towards commercial deployments. That means persuading industrial customers to invest in upgrades that promise lower operating costs.
Key takeaways
- Founded in 2018, Bariflo initially focused on monitoring and cleaning municipal waterbodies. It subsequently explored aquaculture, including shrimp and fish farming, before concentrating on industrial wastewater treatment and reuse. It is now engaged in making existing treatment infrastructure smarter and more efficient.
- Bariflo’s proprietary IoT sensors monitor wastewater parameters such as pH, total dissolved solids, and flow. Its AI models use the readings to determine chemical dosage and treatment processes at different stages. This automates some decisions that operators would otherwise make manually and helps plants respond as the characteristics of incoming wastewater change.
- The company has conducted pilots with Indian Oil Corporation’s R&D centre in Faridabad. Its planned BPCL pilot will test treatment efficiency, energy consumption, and chemical use in an industrial setting. Founder Sahu hopes successful validation will pave the way for a commercial work order.
Social impact
How these Mothers of Courage are fighting to keep girls in school
Mothers of Courage, a documentary on girls’ education in Bihar, recently won the 2026 UN SDG Action Award in the Creativity category. It captures how women in rural Bihar are challenging social norms to keep girls in school.
Directed by Vandana R Jaikumar and produced by Butterfly Effect Media, the documentary was chosen from more than 7,000 applications from 190 countries and territories.
Key takeaways
- In rural Bihar, mothers are at the centre of a quiet revolution. They are negotiating with their families so their daughters can keep studying. Others are standing up for daughters-in-law who want to return to school. This quiet, stubborn conviction and resilience is the subject of the documentary.
- Mothers of Courage is part of Shikshagraha, a national movement to strengthen public education championed by Infosys Co-founder and former CEO S D Shibulal, and supported by Bengaluru-based non-profits ShikshaLokam and Mantra4Change.
- Urmila Kumari, State Head for Shikshagraha in Bihar, is the living embodiment of the movement. She has spent nearly three decades working for the rights and education of girls and young women. She says the UN recognition belongs to “thousands of women and adolescent girls whose courage and determination have driven the fight for girls' education and rights.”
News & updates
- New GCC: SplashBI, a Georgia (US)-headquartered enterprise data intelligence platform, has opened its global capability centre in Hyderabad. The company plans to invest over $100 million over five to seven years in infrastructure, technology and talent to scale the Hyderabad centre and strengthen its global product engineering and delivery capabilities.
- Age checks: Meta Platforms plans to expand its AI age-estimation technology globally to move millions more teens on Instagram into Teen Account protections, even if they have given birth dates showing they are adults. This comes as the company faces lawsuits alleging its platforms harm young users.
- AI guardrails: US President Donald Trump said the risks posed by artificial intelligence can be managed but signalled an openness to safeguards, telling CBS’s 60 Minutes that he “doesn’t mind guardrails.”

articles.title: BYD lance un SUV électrique tellement lourd qu’il nécessiterait le permis poids-lourd en Europe
articles.text:
On pensait les Américains champions au petit jeu de la démesure automobile. Mais ce titre est aujourd’hui battu en brèche par les Chinois, qui poussent le gigantisme toujours plus loin depuis l’avènement de la voiture électrique. Dans les SUV délirants, BYD vient justement de sortir une sacrée perle. Avec ses 5,27 mètres de long, 2,03 mètres de large et 1,83 mètre de haut, le Denza N9 étonne déjà par ses dimensions.
Mais ce qui est réellement horripilant est en réalité ailleurs. C’est bien lorsqu’il s’agit de monter sur la balance que le chinois choque sans faillir. Avec une masse à vide homologuée de 3 105 kg, l’engin est déjà extrêmement lourd. Alors imaginez maintenant si l’on rajoute des humains et leurs bagages à bord… Denza indique un poids total à charge de 3 760 kg, que l’on choisisse la version électrique ou hybride rechargeable.
Le poids de la démesure : pourquoi le permis B ne suffit plus
Si le véhicule devait arriver chez nous, il dépasserait alors la limite légale des 3 500 kg admis par le permis B. Il faudrait donc passer le permis poids-lourd et se limiter à 90 km/h au maximum. Ce serait franchement frustrant, raison pour laquelle l’Union Européenne songe à relever le plafond pour les véhicules disposant de motorisations alternatives. Le permis B donnerait ainsi droit à des engins pesant jusqu’à 4 250 kg, ce qui handicaperait moins les modèles électriques.
Alors, qu’est-ce qui fait la masse phénoménale du Denza N9 ? On s’attend à une batterie massive, bien entendu. Hélas, aucune donnée technique n’a été communiquée à son sujet, mais on suppose que sa capacité devrait très aisément dépasser les 100 kWh. On sait uniquement qu’il s’agit de packs en chimie lithium fer phosphate. Ce qui est en revanche certain, c’est qu’ils alimenteront trois machines électriques.
Le monstre électrique en chiffres : 1 210 ch sous la pédale
Un premier bloc situé à l’avant développera 367 ch quand deux électromoteurs placés à l’arrière produiront chacun 422 ch. On obtient au bout du compte une puissance cumulée de 1 210 ch. C’est un peu beaucoup, même vraiment beaucoup pour un usage sur route. On passera ensuite le style éléphantesque pour se concentrer brièvement sur l’équipement, dont une maigre partie a été rendue publique.
Le N9 embarque ainsi la conduite autonome par LiDAR, les jantes forgées de 22 pouces, la peinture bicolore, les roues arrière directrices et les suspensions pneumatiques. Bien entendu, la liste complète risque d’être autrement plus fournie… Il y a peu de chances que le Denza N9 arrive en France, même si le Zeekr 9X, un de ses principaux concurrents en Chine, a bien osé pousser les portes du Vieux Continent.

articles.title: Peut-on repasser le lin et le jean sans régler la température ?
articles.text:
| Puissance | 3120 W | 
| Débit vapeur | 170 g/min | 
| Débit vapeur réglable | Oui | 
| Pression | 8.5 bar(s) | 
| Temps de chauffe annoncé | 120 s | 
| Poids à vide | 4.69 kg | 
| Capacité du réservoir | 1.5 L | 
| Bac à eau amovible | Oui | 
| Centrale illimitée | Oui | 
| Collecteur de tartre | Oui | 
| Fonction pressing | Oui, 650 g/min | 
| Pose verticale du fer | Non | 
La Philips PerfectCare 7000 PSG7300 a pour particularité de déclencher la vapeur au mouvement du fer. Nous avons sorti un jean épais et une chemise en lin pour voir ce que ce mode automatique change au repassage, puis mesuré le temps de chauffe et la consommation.
Sur la plupart des centrales vapeur et fers à repasser, il faut presser une gâchette pour envoyer de la vapeur. Avec sa PerfectCare Série 7000 PSG7300, Philips laisse le choix. On peut garder cette habitude ou laisser un capteur déclencher la vapeur lorsqu'on déplace le fer sur le linge. La température, elle, se passe de molette. Avec le système OptimalTEMP, on peut passer d'un tissu repassable à l'autre sans toucher au réglage de la chauffe.
Philips annonce une puissance de 3 120 W, une pression de 8,5 bars et un débit continu pouvant atteindre 170 g/min. S'y ajoute un effet pressing de 650 g annoncé pour venir à bout d'un pli récalcitrant. La centrale permet aussi de défroisser à la verticale, par exemple pour reprendre une veste sur cintre.
La centrale Philips adopte une robe noire et dorée qu'on voit parfois dans d'autres types de produits de la marque. Le fer repose en biais sur le socle et se verrouille par la pointe.
Ce détail compte au moment de sortir la centrale du placard. Le fer reste en place quand on déplace l'ensemble, qui pèse 4,69 kg à vide. Le fer seul ne pèse que 900 g. Nous l'avons trouvé facile à guider.
Le flexible de 1,7 m s'enroule autour de l'appareil pour le rangement. Dommage que Philips n'ait pas aussi prévu quelque chose pour le cordon d'alimentation. Le collecteur de calcaire est situé sur le côté de l'appareil.
Son talon ne permet pas de le faire tenir debout sur la planche. On peut le reposer sur son socle ou le laisser à plat sur la housse même en chauffe, comme l'indique Philips. Le manuel conseille toutefois d'éviter de le laisser longtemps au même endroit pour ne pas décolorer la housse.
Le réservoir de 1,5 l se retire pour passer sous le robinet et peut être rempli en cours de repassage. Le flexible vapeur se range dans une gorge au pied du socle, tandis que me cordon secteur demande un peu plus de patience au rangement. Il faut le replier à la main et le maintenir avec sa bande autoagrippante.
La centrale démarre en mode Normal. Pour obtenir davantage de vapeur, on maintient le bouton de mise en marche enfoncé 2 s. Un second appui long donne accès au mode Éco. Le voyant est blanc en Max et vert en Éco.
Pour l'effet pressing, la commande est sur le fer. Deux pressions rapides sur la gâchette déclenchent trois jets successifs. Le bouton Auto Steam se trouve sous le pouce. Une fois le mode enclenché, la vapeur arrive quand on déplace le fer et se coupe dès qu'on l'immobilise ou qu'on le soulève. À l'usage, c'est la commande que nous avons le plus appréciée. On peut enchaîner les passages sur une jambe de pantalon sans garder le doigt sur la gâchette, qui reste disponible quand on préfère décider soi-même du moment où envoyer de la vapeur.
Le bruit du souffle de la vapeur est celui qu'on attend d'une centrale. La pompe, en revanche, se fait davantage remarquer. Elle se met en route par intermittence pour réalimenter la chaudière en eau. Pour l'entretien, un voyant et un signal sonore indiquent quand vider le collecteur de tartre Easy De-Calc, accessible sur le côté du socle.
Nous avons attendu exactement 2 min avant de pouvoir repasser, comme annoncé par Philips. Au centre de la semelle, la température oscille entre 140,5 et 146,1 °C. Sur les cinq points contrôlés, les valeurs relevées s'étendent de 135,8 °C au milieu de l'arrière à 146,1 °C au centre, la pointe atteignant 137,3 °C. Notre indice d'homogénéité s'établit à 94,2 % pour un écart de 10,3 °C entre les deux points extrêmes.
Sur notre jean épais, le fer a bien lissé la toile. Le résultat est tout aussi convaincant sur notre chemise en lin. On peut s'occuper de l'un puis de l'autre à la suite, sans laisser le fer monter ou redescendre en température entre les deux.
Lors de notre essai de 10 min avec émission continue de vapeur, la centrale a utilisé 404 g d'eau.
Nous avons relevé 0,470 kWh sur notre cycle qui comprend la mise en chauffe, puis 10 min de vapeur continue. C'est plus que d'autres modèles sur le même protocole, mais cette consommation est logique au vu de la puissance proposée. En repassage courant, la consommation dépendra du temps passé et de la quantité de vapeur demandée.
La Philips PerfectCare Série 7000 PSG7300 nous a séduits avec sa fonction qui permet de profiter de la vapeur automatique. Le fer se guide facilement et l'on peut enchaîner les passages sans garder le doigt sur la gâchette. Seul bémol, la pompe émet un bruit pas très agréable à l'oreille par intermittence. Le résultat sur la planche est bon et notre jean épais et notre chemise en lin sont tous deux ressortis bien lisses, sans avoir à régler la température entre les deux.
La Philips Série 8000 AIS8540 intègre une planche orientable pour passer du repassage à plat au défroissage vertical et s'est montrée moins gourmande en électricité sur notre cycle de test. La Philips PerfectCare Elite Plus GC9682 déclenche elle aussi la vapeur au mouvement du fer et offre un réservoir plus grand de 1,8 l.

articles.title: Google patches eighth Chrome zero-day exploited in attacks this year
articles.text:
Google has released emergency security updates to patch a new Chrome vulnerability exploited in zero-day attacks, the eighth such flaw since the start of the year.
"Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," the company said in a Monday security advisory.
As Google explained, this flaw stems from a Use-After-Free (UAF) weakness in the XML component of the Google Chrome web browser, which occurs when the browser's XML parser processes data, deletes an object from the computer's memory, but fails to clear the pointer referencing that object.
Attackers can exploit this high-severity memory corruption vulnerability when the browser later tries to use or read that "freed" memory space to manipulate the memory layout and execute malicious code.
While Google has found evidence of attackers exploiting this zero-day bug in the wild, it has not shared additional details about these incidents.
"Access to bug details and links may be kept restricted until a majority of users are updated with a fix. We will also retain restrictions if the bug exists in a third party library that other projects similarly depend on, but haven't yet fixed," it noted.
Google has now fixed the zero-day for users in the Stable Desktop channel, with new versions rolling out to Windows, macOS (157.0.8103.50/.51), and Linux users (157.0.8103.50). Although Google says the security update could take days or weeks to reach all Chrome users, it was available immediately when BleepingComputer checked for updates today.
If you don't want to update the web browser manually, you can also let Chrome check for updates on its own, as it will automatically install them after the next launch.
Since the start of the year, Google has addressed seven other actively exploited zero-day vulnerabilities:
- An iterator invalidation bug (CVE-2026-2441) in CSSFontFeatureValuesMap (Chrome's implementation of CSS font feature values), which Google addressed in mid-February.
- Two other Chrome zero-day bugs exploited in attacks were patched in March: an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Skia 2D graphics library (CVE-2026-3909), and an inappropriate implementation vulnerability in the V8 JavaScript and WebAssembly engine (CVE-2026-3910).
- A use-after-free weakness in Dawn (CVE-2026-5281), the underlying cross-platform implementation of the WebGPU standard used by the Chromium project, which Google patched in April.
- An out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine (CVE-2026-11645), exploited in the wild and patched in June.
- And out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-87491) and type confusion (CVE-2026-85046) flaws in the V8 JavaScript engine, fixed in September.
Google fixed eight more zero-days exploited in attacks in 2025, many of them reported by the company's Threat Analysis Group (TAG), which tracks zero-day exploits used in spyware attacks.

articles.title: HBO Max et Paramount+ : à quand la réunion des deux plateformes ? On a un début de réponse
articles.text:
Skydance (ex-Paramount Skydance) a finalisé le 6 octobre le rachat de Warner Bros. Discovery, une opération à 110 milliards de dollars (environ 98 milliards d’euros).
Le groupe réorganise désormais ses services de streaming. David Ellison, CEO de Skydance, a donné le calendrier de ce rapprochement ce lundi 9 novembre comme le rapporte Deadline, dans la lettre aux actionnaires qui accompagne les premiers résultats trimestriels du groupe depuis le rachat. Ces chiffres du troisième trimestre n’intègrent pas encore Warner Bros. Discovery, l’opération ayant été conclue après la fin du trimestre.
Une offre groupée, sans prix pour l’instant pour HBO Max et Paramount
Interrogé par les analystes de Wall Street, David Ellison a qualifié cette offre conjointe de « première étape vers l’unification des deux services ». Skydance n’a donné ni prix ni nom ni date précise pour cette offre. Sa lettre aux actionnaires promet seulement de s’abonner aux deux services « à un prix encore plus avantageux », sans chiffrer la réduction.
Ensemble, Paramount+, HBO et HBO Max comptent 203 millions d’abonnements dans le monde, selon Skydance. Ce total additionne les abonnements sans retirer les personnes abonnées aux deux services. À titre de comparaison, Netflix revendiquait 325 millions d’abonnés payants au début de l’année 2026. L’offre groupée réunira notamment l’univers Harry Potter et The Pitt côté HBO Max, Mayor of Kingstown et Landman côté Paramount+.
Une intégration progressive avant la fusion totale
David Ellison a présenté les deux plateformes comme complémentaires, car elles attirent des publics différents aux États-Unis. Skydance espère ainsi garder ses abonnés plus longtemps et augmenter ses revenus d’abonnement et de publicité.
Skydance veut faire tourner HBO Max et Paramount+ sur la même infrastructure technique dans l’année qui suit le rachat, donc d’ici l’automne 2027. Le groupe rappelle qu’il lui avait fallu environ 18 mois pour intégrer Pluto TV à Paramount+. Les prix évolueront par étapes, en fonction des retours des abonnés, a précisé David Ellison. D’ici 2030, Skydance veut tirer la majorité de son chiffre d’affaires et de ses bénéfices du streaming et de ses studios plutôt que de la télévision classique, dont les recettes publicitaires ont encore reculé de 8 % au troisième trimestre.

articles.title: Banco pour le propriétaire de Betclic, qui va pouvoir racheter 33 vrais casinos en France
articles.text:
Le propriétaire de Betclic va s’implanter dans les casinos physiques. Le rachat de JOA, deuxième opérateur français avec 33 établissements, vient d’obtenir l’aval de l’Autorité de la concurrence, confrontée à un dossier d’un genre nouveau.
C'est dans une certaine discrétion, au vu de l'ampleur du dossier, que le rachat des casinos JOA par le propriétaire de Betclic a reçu le feu vert de l'Autorité de la concurrence. Le deuxième réseau de casinos français s'apprête à rejoindre un groupe qui, dans l'Hexagone, ne connaissait jusqu'ici les jeux d'argent qu'à travers un écran. La décision, rendue publique le 4 novembre 2026, concerne 33 casinos, plus de 2 000 salariés et environ 430 millions d’euros de chiffre d’affaires brut l'an dernier. Elle éclaire aussi la façon dont l’institution envisage le poker et le casino en ligne, dont la légalisation lui paraît encore trop incertaine.
Betclic pose ses jetons dans le monde réel
L'affaire s'est à l'origine nouée le 6 juillet dernier, quand Banijay Gaming s'est engagé à racheter 100 % de JOA aux fonds Blackstone et Kings Park Capital. Le prix reste sous le tapis, Banijay ne le dévoile pas et évoque seulement un financement mêlant dette et capitaux propres. Notifié le 7 octobre, le dossier a été bouclé en moins d'un mois, sans le moindre engagement réclamé à l'acheteur.
Le groupe JOA, basé à Lyon et présent uniquement en France, est tout simplement le deuxième opérateur de casinos du pays par le nombre d’établissements. Il accueille plus de 4,6 millions de visiteurs par an. L’essentiel de cette somme vient des casinos eux-mêmes, exploités en délégation de service public, c'est-à-dire que la commune confie leur gestion à JOA par contrat. Le reste provient notamment des restaurants, bars et hôtels installés sur place. Son président, Laurent Lassiaz, restera à la tête du groupe après le rachat.
En face, son acheteur a pris du volume. Filiale de Banijay Group, dans le giron de Lov Group, Banijay Gaming n'était présent en France qu'en ligne, avec les paris sportifs, le poker et les paris hippiques de Betclic. Depuis avril, il coiffe aussi Tipico, poids lourd des paris en Allemagne et en Autriche, et la marque Admiral. Lors de l'annonce, la finalisation, prévue au second semestre 2026, était aussi suspendue à la consultation du personnel de JOA et aux autorisations propres aux casinos.
Bientôt des deux côtés de la table
Pour la première fois, l'Autorité de la concurrence devait se prononcer sur un opérateur actif à la fois sur internet et en dur, et c'est le poker qui a retenu son attention. Aucune activité ne se chevauche, mais le poker en ligne et les tables de casino peuvent être considérés comme connexes, autrement dit voisins. Malgré des manières de jouer différentes, l'enquête auprès des concurrents et de l'Autorité nationale des jeux fait ressortir une clientèle en partie commune, que le rajeunissement du public des casinos resserre encore, d'autant plus que cette clientèle est prête à passer de la salle à l'écran, ou l'inverse.
On imagine que le groupe réfléchit à une stratégie omnicanale, avec des offres commerciales associant les deux activités, au risque qu'un groupe s'appuie sur un marché pour peser sur son voisin. L'Autorité a étudié ce scénario sans y voir de danger pour la concurrence, au vu des parts de marché des parties, de la présence de concurrents importants et du faible poids du poker dans l'activité des casinos JOA.
Il faut toutefois comprendre que le casino en ligne, interdit en France, n'entre pas dans l'équation. Sa légalisation, débattue depuis des années, paraît encore trop incertaine à l'Autorité. Fin octobre 2024, le gouvernement avait retiré un amendement au budget 2025 qui devait l'autoriser, sur fond de tribune de plus d'une centaine de maires chiffrant à 15 000 les emplois menacés. Si la porte s'ouvrait, Banijay aurait un pied de chaque côté de la table, à la fois chez les opérateurs en ligne qui la réclament, et chez les casinos physiques qui la redoutent.

articles.title: "Novo patamar”: os bastidores de produção de celulares Oppo na China • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
“Novo patamar”: os bastidores de produção de celulares Oppo na China
O Tecnoblog viajou a Dongguan para conhecer de perto as operações de pesquisa, desenvolvimento e montagem do próximo smartphone topo de linha da Oppo
Quando alguém diz que comprou um “celular chinês”, qual é a sua primeira impressão? Se você ainda imagina um smartphone baratinho, com recursos básicos para o dia a dia, já é hora de repensar seus conceitos. Afinal, gigantes da tecnologia já investem esforços massivos para produzir dispositivos cada vez mais avançados.
É o caso da Oppo, que convidou o Tecnoblog para conhecer sua fábrica de celulares em Dongguan, nos arredores de Shenzhen, cidade conhecida como o “Vale do Silício” da China.
O objetivo? Acompanhar os bastidores de desenvolvimento da principal linha de smartphones da marca – a série Find X – e entender o que há por trás do conceito de “Next Level of Making”, ou “Outro patamar de fabricação”, em tradução livre.
O primeiro contato com o ambiente de pesquisa da Oppo foi na sede da empresa, no Binhaiwan Park. Trata-se de um grande complexo populado por prédios de arquitetura imponente e moderna, além de uma ampla área verde, com árvores, lagos e até pequenas cascatas.
A recepção ocorreu no Centro de Exposições de Marca, onde tivemos acesso a alguns dos principais produtos da empresa, incluindo um novo smartphone premium cujo nome não posso mencionar – mas que chega em breve ao Brasil —, relógios inteligentes, fones de ouvido, celulares dobráveis e tablets.
Na primeira palestra do dia, nos encontramos com Hope Liu, gerente-geral do Centro de Design Industrial e vice-presidente assistente da Oppo, e uma equipe de especialistas responsável pelo desenvolvimento da linha Find X.
Por lá, eu pude conhecer um pouco melhor o que acontece antes do smartphone entrar em linha de montagem – e o trabalho vai muito além de escolher a cor mais bonita ou a textura mais exótica do mercado.
Você já parou para pensar na importância do design da traseira de um smartphone? Afinal, essa é a primeira coisa que você vê quando considera comprar um produto: o celular fica exposto na vitrine ou é reproduzido em zilhões de cópias no material de marketing da empresa, e essa imagem inicial pode atrair a atenção ou repelir o consumidor logo de primeira.
Sem contar, é claro, que também é esse design que acompanha o usuário no dia a dia: precisa ser confortável, se adequar ao estilo de vida, resistir aos pequenos acidentes diários e acomodar de forma funcional todo o conjunto de hardware do aparelho.
Por isso, o desenvolvimento de um smartphone como esse envolve muita pesquisa: é preciso entender o comportamento e necessidades dos consumidores, pensar ergonomia, observar tendências e realizar uma série de testes para avaliar como cada escolha influencia a experiência de uso.
Teoricamente, já me parece exaustivo desenhar diversos modelos e escolher o mais adequado. Mas o trabalho desses especialistas precisa ir além do campo das ideias e ganhar vida no mundo real. É nesse momento que são produzidas dezenas de unidades de protótipos para partes específicas do smartphone.
Muitas vezes, as peças testadas são tão semelhantes entre si que é difícil notar o que muda de fato. Confesso que eu mesma não consegui perceber diferenças entre vários dos componentes exibidos na visita, apesar dos esforços dos especialistas para explicar as especificidades técnicas de cada coisa.
Mas essas diferenças existem, e eles medem o impacto de cada ajuste. Nesse processo, todo detalhe importa. As dimensões do aparelho, a textura dos materiais e até a maneira como ele se encaixa na mão precisam fazer sentido em conjunto.
A Oppo parece levar muito a sério a abordagem “Limpa e Sofisticada” (em tradução livre). A ideia é encontrar um equilíbrio entre estética, funcionalidade e experiência de uso — e transformar tudo isso em um produto viável.
“A qualidade é a base de todo o portfólio de produtos da Oppo, e nosso controle sobre o processo de criação dos dispositivos é o que nos permite cumprir esse compromisso em larga escala” — Ling Liu, CMO da Oppo para mercados internacionais.
Depois de entender como o corpo do smartphone é planejado, chegamos a uma das partes mais legais de toda a viagem: hora de conhecer os laboratórios de teste de câmera da linha Find X.
Eu estava empolgadíssima! Afinal, não é todo dia que você se depara com os bastidores de uma empresa com importância histórica na fotografia.
Para quem não está familiarizado, a Oppo mantém uma parceria com a Hasselblad desde 2022 para o desenvolvimento de sistemas de imagem de alto desempenho. Isso envolve desde calibração de cores até a criação de motores de imagem avançados, passando por kits de acessórios profissionais, projetados para os mais entusiastas.
Em um dos laboratórios, acompanhamos um exemplo de comparativos de textura e resolução de imagem. Máquinas seguravam e moviam painéis com o objeto a ser fotografado. As capturas eram feitas primeiramente com uma câmera Hasselblad e posteriormente com um smartphone da Oppo em condições controladas de iluminação.
Os resultados são analisados lado a lado por meio de um software dedicado, e os cientistas avaliam a necessidade de ajustes ou correções.
Em outro laboratório, acompanhamos os testes do tão popular modo retrato, que desfoca o fundo da imagem, dando um toque profissional à composição. Apesar de já ser visto em smartphones há pelo menos uma década, a dedicação da Oppo a esse tipo de recurso deixa evidente que ainda há espaço para aprimoramentos.
Foi especialmente interessante observar de perto os experimentos feitos em modelos com cabeças humanas realistas. Tom de pele, linhas de expressão, contorno e textura de cabelos – esses e outros detalhes são observados profundamente e processados com extremo cuidado para um resultado o mais natural possível.
O desempenho em HDR, o brilho dos rostos e a gradação dos tons de pele são avaliados em 40 condições diferentes de iluminação. Na calibração de cores, a Oppo utiliza uma referência com 140 tons, em vez da cartela de 24 cores, padrão da indústria. O objetivo é alcançar uma reprodução mais precisa.
Ela não é a única a se preocupar com isso: vale lembrar que marcas como Motorola, Xiaomi, Apple e Samsung também têm perfis próprios de calibração científica para tons de pele inclusivos.
Mas outro nome importante apareceu enquanto andávamos entre os corredores do gigantesco Centro de Imagem da Oppo no Binhaiwan Park. Uma das despretensiosas portas verdes abriga nada menos do que um laboratório do DXOMark, referência absoluta quando o assunto é ranquear as melhores câmeras de smartphones. Mais um ponto pro meu bingo tecnológico.
Concluindo a imersão em câmeras, a Oppo nos levou até um imenso laboratório onde faz simulações de shows ao vivo. O intuito dessa sala é testar, por meio de braços robóticos e softwares avançados, movimentos similares ao de humanos quando estão em grandes eventos musicais, com condições de iluminação bastante específicas e distâncias variadas do palco.
É muito interessante perceber o quanto a indústria de smartphones tem que se adaptar para entender a realidade de seu público-alvo. Um celular super premium não precisa ser apenas ágil e resistente, ele precisa de câmeras que funcionem bem à noite ou em situações de pouca luz, em vídeos com muito movimento e fotografando à distância, porque isso faz parte da vida do consumidor que está disposto a pagar caro para registrar suas experiências.
Falamos de design, câmeras e agora chegou a hora de tratar do terceiro e último pilar de desenvolvimento dos smartphones Oppo: o software.
Quem acompanha meus testes aqui no Tecnoblog já sabe que virei fã do ColorOS depois de experimentar o Find X9 Pro. Na versão 16, o sistema me chamou a atenção pela fluidez: a navegação é rápida, os comandos respondem bem, as animações são suaves e até os efeitos sonoros são agradáveis. É uma experiência que me lembra bastante a do iOS, algo que ainda considero raro de encontrar em smartphones Android.
Agora, no ColorOS 17, a inteligência artificial ganha mais destaque. A empresa nos apresentou seu novo agente de IA, desenvolvido com tecnologia Manus, que roda diretamente no dispositivo, podendo acessar fotos, vídeos e outros arquivos para realizar tarefas de forma mais autônoma, compreendendo contextos complexos e executando fluxos de trabalho com várias etapas em tempo real.
Não faltaram demonstrações da IA em ação: desde recursos de edição e processamento de imagem até um novo sistema antifraude da Oppo projetado para identificar deepfakes e alertar o usuário sobre possíveis golpes. Tudo parece rodar muito bem, mas a gente só vai ter certeza disso depois de testar por conta própria, é claro.
Para manter seus serviços rodando com disponibilidade de 99,9%, a Oppo conta com uma robusta infraestrutura global de computação, distribuída por nove Centros de Dados de Internet (IDCs) localizados em seis regiões do mundo, cada um implementado de acordo com os requisitos regulatórios específicos, a infraestrutura de rede e os serviços de nuvem de cada mercado local.
Nós tivemos acesso a um desses data centers em uma área mais restrita do campus da Oppo em Binhaiwan Bay. Após a passagem por algumas catracas e controles de acesso, entramos em uma sala com dezenas de racks enfileirados, armazenando servidores refrigerados a ar.
Para os mais curiosos: não havia muito mais informações. Os racks até tinham painéis de LED, mas eles estavam escurecidos e, obviamente, os dados tratados ali não foram identificados por questões de segurança e privacidade.
Em outra sala, encontramos GPUs de alto desempenho mergulhadas em um tanque de resfriamento por imersão. A técnica utiliza um composto líquido fluorado, que não conduz eletricidade, para absorver o calor gerado pelos componentes.
Esse líquido é conduzido por meio de uma tubulação até um trocador de calor, onde transfere a energia para outro circuito de refrigeração e, enfim, retorna ao tanque.
O processo visa reduzir as emissões de carbono e cumprir metas de sustentabilidade da Oppo, mas também resultou em uma melhoria na eficiência energética, segundo a empresa.
No último dia de imersão, passamos pelo maior crivo de segurança de toda a viagem para conhecer de perto a linha de produção de smartphones Oppo. Aqui, sem mais experimentos ou protótipos – apenas os produtos em sua linha de montagem, ficando prontos para serem embalados e comercializados.
Nesse espaço, celulares não eram permitidos aos jornalistas e influenciadores, e cada pessoa só podia entrar com uma câmera na mão para registrar as operações. Passamos por detectores de metal na entrada e na saída, e também tivemos que usar trajes adequados para acessar as instalações, incluindo jaleco, boina e pantufas.
A fabricação de um smartphone envolve diferentes etapas, e uma delas é a tecnologia de montagem em superfície, conhecida pela sigla SMT (Surface Mount Technology). É nesse processo que componentes eletrônicos minúsculos, como chips, resistores e capacitores, são posicionados e soldados diretamente nas placas de circuito impresso do aparelho.
Com as placas prontas, o processo avança para a montagem final. É quando elas são integradas aos demais componentes, como tela, bateria, câmeras, alto-falantes e estrutura externa. Depois, o smartphone passa por máquinas de testes para verificar se tudo funciona corretamente antes de seguir para a embalagem e distribuição.
A poucos metros de distância, tudo parecia um grande circuito muito bem orquestrado, onde a sinergia homem-máquina é impressionante: desde a agilidade nas mãos que entregam e recebem peça a peça de máquinas, aos robôs que circulam livremente para entregar componentes e materiais, passando por máquinas de altíssima complexidade, responsáveis por testar cada tecnologia presente no celular.
No mesmo galpão, nos deparamos com uma grande sala de vidro que abriga os materiais que compõem as embalagens dos smartphones, bem como itens que acompanham a caixa, como carregadores, cabos e manuais.
A Oppo foi uma das primeiras fabricantes de smartphones a implementar a fabricação automatizada, ainda em 2017. Hoje, segundo a empresa, mais de 95% das linhas de produção SMT são automatizadas, assim como, em média, 85% das linhas de montagem final.
Apesar desses números, fiquei surpresa com a quantidade de pessoas trabalhando nas estações. Minha principal referência anterior era a fábrica de semicondutores da Intel, na Costa Rica. Vi bem menos humanos andando por lá em 2024 – logicamente, pela natureza mais delicada do produto.
Chegando ao fim da nossa viagem ao outro lado do mundo, ficou claro que a Oppo quer brigar pelo lugar mais alto do pódio no segmento topo de linha. Para isso, a marca não parece poupar esforços na construção de um produto de qualidade: há uma cadeia enorme de decisões, pesquisas, testes e procedimentos industriais por trás de cada detalhe que chega às mãos do consumidor.
E o mais legal de ver os bastidores desse processo, desde o desenvolvimento do design até a fabricação dos componentes e a montagem dos aparelhos, é ter uma dimensão mais concreta do trabalho necessário para colocar um produto desse nível no mercado. E, ao menos para o smartphone que eu testei, os investimentos parecem ter surtido efeito.
Mas o desafio da Oppo não termina quando o aparelho sai da fábrica. No Brasil, ela precisa transformar essa capacidade de desenvolvimento em reconhecimento e preferência do consumidor. A marca chegou por aqui em 2022 e intensificou os esforços em 2024. Mas somente em 2026 começou a vender seu primeiro flagship da linha Find X no mercado nacional — com preços difíceis de defender.
E a disputa não é simples: competir em preço e popularidade com empresas que fabricam localmente há muitos anos exige mais do que desenvolver bons smartphones. Marcas como a Samsung já têm uma operação consolidada no Brasil, reconhecimento entre os consumidores, presença no varejo e uma estrutura de distribuição que ajuda a tornar seus produtos mais acessíveis.
Para a Oppo, conquistar espaço significa superar essa vantagem e mostrar, na prática, o que seus aparelhos oferecem de diferente.
Por aqui, seguimos torcendo pela entrada e o crescimento de novos fabricantes, o que também tende a ser positivo para o mercado. Afinal, quanto mais empresas disputam a preferência do consumidor, maior é a pressão para que todas invistam em tecnologia, aprimorem seus produtos e encontrem maneiras de oferecer mais por preços competitivos. Isso vale tanto para recursos de câmera e desempenho quanto para bateria, software, suporte e experiência de uso.
No fim, é justamente essa concorrência que pode fazer diferença para quem está do outro lado do balcão. Quanto mais opções relevantes existirem, maior será a pressão para que as fabricantes não se acomodem. E, se essa disputa resultar em smartphones melhores e preços mais competitivos, quem ganha é o consumidor.
Ana Marques viajou para a China a convite da Oppo
