articles.title: SAP Patches Critical ICM2SHELL, ProxyGate Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Enterprise software maker SAP on Tuesday announced the release of 42 new and updated security notes, including nine that resolve critical-severity vulnerabilities.
Four of SAP’s new security notes address maximum-severity flaws in NetWeaver (Internet Communication Manager (ICM) and SAML2 Service Provider), Web Dispatcher, and Gateway.
The ICM and Web Dispatcher flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-76964 and CVE-2026-89126, are a single weakness in the SAP kernel component that receives HTTP, HTTPS, and WebSocket traffic.
According to Onapsis, which calls the security defect ICM2SHELL, the issue is related to reassembling large WebSocket messages, which may be split into fragments during a server-browser exchange and then put together by the receiver.
“A specially crafted sequence of WebSocket messages makes the ICM or the WD write attacker-controlled data past the end of the memory it reserved for the connection. Depending on how that data is shaped, the result is either an immediate crash of the process or controlled corruption of its memory,” Onapsis explains.
ICM2SHELL, the enterprise application security firm says, could allow an attacker to execute operating system commands with <sid>adm privileges.
“This is not a theoretical outcome. The Onapsis Research Labs provided SAP a working exploit that achieves full, unauthenticated remote code execution end to end, running arbitrary commands as <sid>adm on the target system. The denial-of-service condition, in turn, reproduced on every SAP Kernel release tested,” Onapsis says.
The max-severity SAP Gateway flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-89103 and referred to as ProxyGate, could be exploited by unauthenticated attackers to achieve remote code execution (RCE) without user interaction.
It is related to the prxyinfo access-control list, which should restrict requests to trusted networks only. However, if left open, it allows an attacker to send a series of requests that appear to be originating from an internal network, tricking the gateway into accepting them.
This allows an attacker to execute OS commands with the <sid>adm privileges and gain full control over the SAP system, without providing a username, password, or certificate.
“Because the flaw is in the SAP kernel, it affects a broad range of releases, including kernel versions that are already out of maintenance. Further, the gateway runs not only on ABAP but also on AS Java, dual-stack, and standalone-gateway systems,” Onapsis explains.
SAP also resolved a max-severity missing authentication bug in NetWeaver (CVE-2026-120017) that, in certain configurations, could allow unauthenticated attackers to submit specially crafted data and impersonate arbitrary users, which could lead to full system compromise.
The remaining five critical notes in SAP’s November 2026 bulletin address vulnerabilities in NetWeaver (CVE-2026-109803 and CVE-2026-76965), S4CRM (CVE-2026-109795), Web Dispatcher (CVE-2026-89119), and BusinessObjects (CVE-2026-109798).
Additionally, SAP published 17 high-severity fixes, including for multiple memory corruption, denial-of-service (DoS), and information disclosure bugs.
Since the scheduled October 2026 security patches, SAP released new notes dealing with the recently disclosed PHP2Shell and Node2Shell vulnerabilities in its Business AI Platform and updated several other notes and advisories. This brings the total to 43 new and updated notes released this month, Onapsis notes in its analysis of the patches.

articles.title: AI tax research platform Blue J raises $176-million USD Series E
articles.text:
Toronto-based Blue J has raised a $176-million USD ($249-million CAD) Series E round after more than doubling its annual recurring revenue in just over a year.
The round, which Blue J announced on Tuesday morning, values the AI-powered tax research software provider at more than $700 million USD. US-based growth equity firm JMI Equity led the round, with existing investors Oak HC/FT, Sapphire Ventures, and Intrepid Growth Partners also participating.
Blue J CEO Ben Alarie told BetaKit in a Monday interview that the round featured a secondary capital component, buying out “long holders” and a small amount for long-term employees, but did not disclose how much of the round this included.
“I’m excited about building Canada’s next great tech company right here from Toronto.”
Founded in 2015 by Alarie, CTO Brett Janssen, Anthony Niblett, and Albert Yoon, Blue J aims to make the law more transparent and accessible for tax practitioners. Blue J claims its AI-powered platform can answer questions about federal, state, and local taxes in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom.
The company said the proceeds will help it scale its agentic AI for tax work feature, Workflows, as well as expand in the UK and internationally. While Blue J’s platform is versed in UK tax law, Alarie said the company still doesn’t have “boots on the ground” in the country.
“This will be about establishing a UK office and making a more concerted effort to take Blue J to market in the UK,” Alarie said, adding with a smirk that the office will be “probably big, in time.”
Alarie foresees the forthcoming upgrade to Blue J’s Workflows fundamentally changing his business. He wants Blue J to be able to produce hundreds of deliverables, from helping its accountant users draft a memo to responding to a notice of assessment from the Canada Revenue Agency. With these features, Blue J will move from an AI-powered tax research platform to a tax research and advisory platform.
“Our ambition is, by the end of next year, to have built out all of these workflow capabilities to effectively assist with just about any kind of work product that a tax professional routinely does in their practice,” Alarie said. “So it’s a big build.”
RELATED: Blue J raises $167.4-million CAD Series D after AI tax research platform more than doubles revenue
The Series E round comes just 15 months after Blue J raised a $122-million USD ($167.4-million CAD) Series D round, which was also on the heels of rapid growth, to expand its team, product, and market reach. While specific revenue figures weren’t disclosed (Alarie only said it’s in the “mid eight-figures”), Blue J claims its annual recurring revenue grew 165 percent since the Series D round, and that its revenue has grown 529 percent in the last three years. Blue J has added roughly 2,500 customers since the end of 2025, bringing it up to a total of 6,500 customers; growth that Alarie credits to Blue J’s effectiveness as a product.
“Tax technical stuff is really, really hard to research, and I can tell you this as somebody who’s been a tax professor for 22 years,” Alarie said. “It’s a painful problem to solve, and Blue J makes it, I like to think, rather delightful.”
As Alarie prepares Blue J to take flight, he said he’s excited to work with lead investor JMI, which has backed multiple scaling Canadian tech firms, including Clio, Safe Software, PointClickCare, Vena, and Jane.
“They’ve done a phenomenal job at helping companies like Blue J scale from where we are today to being much, much larger businesses,” Alarie said. “They really excel [at] helping people like me, a first-time founder, navigate as we scale this business to the next level.”
To support its growth, Blue J has doubled its head count over the past year, and expects to exceed 200 employees by year-end. While some of these may be in the UK or the US, Alarie expects the majority to be based in Blue J’s “center of gravity.”
“Our hearts are in Toronto,” Alarie said. “I’m excited about building Canada’s next great tech company right here from Toronto.”
Feature image courtesy Blue J.

articles.title: Ring, da Amazon, lança Ring Robotics com drone voador e robô de segurança
articles.text:
A Ring anunciou a Ring Robotics, linha de dispositivos autônomos de segurança que inclui uma câmera voadora para residências e um robô móvel para empresas. Os equipamentos realizam patrulhas, investigam ocorrências e se integram ao ecossistema de câmeras e alarmes da companhia.
Os primeiros modelos são o Ring Drone Cam e o Ring Rover Cam. Ambos utilizam inteligência artificial para mapear ambientes, identificar pontos de interesse e navegar de forma autônoma.
Como funciona a tecnologia
Os dois dispositivos utilizam o AI Pilot, sistema desenvolvido pela Ring, empresa adquirida pela Amazon em 2018, que combina câmeras, modelos especializados de visão computacional, sensores e processamento em nuvem para permitir a navegação independente.
Durante a configuração, o usuário pode carregar o Drone pelos ambientes para que ele registre o espaço. O Rover, por sua vez, consegue explorá-lo sozinho. A partir dessas informações, o sistema cria uma planta do local, identifica cômodos e sugere pontos para patrulhamento, como portas, janelas, caixas registradoras e corredores. Também é possível adicionar locais personalizados.
Quando uma ronda começa, o AI Pilot calcula uma rota até os pontos selecionados e desvia de obstáculos, como móveis e prateleiras.
Drone Cam leva a vigilância para ambientes internos
O Ring Drone Cam é uma câmera voadora que monitora diferentes cômodos sem exigir a instalação de equipamentos fixos em cada ambiente. Quando não está em uso, permanece em uma base, com a câmera desligada.
Entre suas características estão:
- Rotas de voo personalizadas, com horários programados para patrulhas automáticas ou acionamento manual.
- Resposta automática quando uma câmera, um sensor ou um alarme Ring é acionado, com deslocamento até pontos de patrulhamento predefinidos.
- Campo de visão de 148 graus e rotação de 360 graus.
- Gravação em resolução 2K, com duas luzes LED ativadas automaticamente em ambientes pouco iluminados.
- Integração com o Alexa Home Map, além de compatibilidade com câmeras, campainhas, sensores e alarmes Ring.
Rover Cam foi desenvolvido para empresas
O Ring Rover Cam foi projetado para a segurança de estabelecimentos comerciais. O robô percorre os ambientes e realiza rondas programadas, além de verificar ocorrências identificadas pelos dispositivos conectados.
O projeto aproveitou experiências com o Amazon Astro. Segundo a Ring, clientes do robô doméstico destacaram a patrulha de segurança como um de seus recursos preferidos. A equipe decidiu, então, desenvolver um equipamento dedicado à proteção de espaços comerciais.
O Rover conta com câmera que transmite vídeos em até 4K e realiza varreduras de 360 graus ao chegar aos pontos de patrulhamento. Um mastro ajustável permite visualizar áreas acima de balcões e prateleiras.
Outros recursos incluem:
- Sirene e torre de luz para sinalizar a presença do robô.
- Áudio bidirecional, que permite conversar com pessoas no ambiente remotamente.
- Gravação contínua durante deslocamentos e patrulhas, não apenas nos pontos programados.
- Detecção de movimento de pessoas, inclusive quando o equipamento está estacionado na base.
Privacidade e disponibilidade
A Ring informa que o Drone desliga a câmera enquanto permanece na base. No Rover, o modo Sleep recolhe o periscópio e desativa o microfone. Os dois aparelhos possuem indicadores LED de gravação, e o Rover também exibe essa informação na própria tela.
Os vídeos serão protegidos pelo Throw Away the Key Encryption (TAKE), sistema apresentado pela empresa como seu padrão de criptografia mais forte até agora.
Os lançamentos estão previstos inicialmente para os Estados Unidos:
- Ring Rover Cam: envios a partir de 16 de dezembro de 2026, por US$ 999,99 (aproximadamente R$ 5.549,94).
- Ring Drone Cam: envios a partir de 27 de janeiro de 2027, por US$ 249,99 (aproximadamente R$ 1.387,44).
A empresa não informou quando os dispositivos chegarão a outros mercados.
Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

articles.title: Spotify's AI DJ gets new voices, personalities, and an option for less chatter | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Spotify’s AI DJ, one of the company’s earlier efforts in embracing AI technology to connect people with their favorite music, is getting an upgrade. On Tuesday, the streamer announced that users will now be able to customize their DJ more like they can an AI assistant, by choosing between different voices and personalities. Those who like the feature, but not all the chatter, can also now opt for an experience with less commentary in between sets.
Since first launching the AI DJ in 2023, Spotify has leveraged AI to improve all areas of its app. Most recently, that has included updates that allow users to chat with a conversational AI agent about music, fine-tune their recommendations with prompts, create playlists with AI, and work with third-party agents like ChatGPT and Claude. However, the DJ remains one of Spotify’s most popular AI features, as it’s used by over 94 million Spotify Premium listeners.
Now, it’s revisiting one of its first major AI features, taking a cue from the personalization options other AI assistants routinely offer.
With the update, Spotify Premium subscribers will be able to choose from an expanded set of AI DJ voices in both English and Spanish. The voices include seven English options with British, American, Irish, Australian, and Indian accents, and two new Spanish options.
The different voices will have their own unique personalities as well. For instance, users can pick between three American voices, one of which is laid-back and warm (Casey), another that’s direct and has an edge (Tess), and a third that has a Southern accent and a youthful energy (Lane). In addition to the other various regional accents, there are also two new Spanish voices, one that’s more down-to-earth (Nico) and one that’s more witty and friendly (Fabi).
The voices will not replace the AI DJ’s original voice, “X,” which was based on that of a Spotify employee’s real voice recordings. However, DJ Fabi and Nico will now be the only Spanish voices available, replacing the earlier “Livi.”
The other change allows users to toggle off the commentary between songs, reducing the DJ’s interruptions. While typically, the AI DJ introduces different selections of music, explaining what it picked and why, users can now limit it to brief acknowledgements when they first start the DJ feature and when they turn it off. Spotify says this would allow people to use the DJ at times they may have turned to a playlist instead, like when hosting a party where they want music in the background, but not the chatter.
To access the DJ, users can search for the term “DJ” in the search bar of the Spotify app on their device, then tap the three-dot menu to pick their voice and commentary settings. To change genres, artists, or recommendations while the DJ is driving things, you simply tap the DJ button again.
Spotify says the new voices begin rolling out today, November 10, to Premium users in the markets where DJ is already supported. Currently, that includes over 95 global markets, where the DJ is supported in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Brazilian Portuguese.

articles.title: Jensen Huang: FBI ermittelt zur Affäre des Nvidia-Chefs – warum ihm Aktien zum Verhängnis werden könnten
articles.text:
Das FBI ermittelt nach Worten von US-Präsident Donald Trump im Fall der Affäre von Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang mit einer möglichen chinesischen Spionin. Die US-Bundespolizei prüfe den Fall, sagte Trump auf einer Pressekonferenz im Weißen Haus. Welche Rolle genau das FBI dabei spielt, ließ der Präsident offen.
Huang selbst beteure, keine Ahnung gehabt zu haben, dass die Frau eine Spionin sein könnte, sagte Trump. Er habe den Nvidia-Chef in einem Gespräch am Montag danach gefragt. „Er sagte, dass er keine Ahnung gehabt habe, dass sie eine Spionin war, und ich glaube ihm das wirklich.“
Trump hatte bereits am 9. November nach dem Eingeständnis der Affäre durch Huang dem Nvidia-Chef den Rücken gestärkt. Huang sei „ein feiner Mensch“, der sich um die USA verdient gemacht habe, sagte Trump. „Ich denke, er hat vermutlich eine Entschuldigung dafür.“ In den vergangenen Jahren hatte Huang ein enges Verhältnis zu Trump aufgebaut.
Bei Nvidia läuft nichts ohne Huang
Huangs Affäre wirft ein Schlaglicht darauf, dass Nvidia für ein Unternehmen dieser Größe eine außerordentlich stark auf den Chef zugeschnittene Struktur hat. Jede wichtige Entscheidung läuft über den 63‑Jährigen. Rund 60 Nvidia-Manager berichteten direkt an ihn, schrieb der Finanzdienst Bloomberg. Huang beantworte ihre kurzen E-Mails mit „fünf zentralen Punkten“ zu allen möglichen Zeiten.
Nach Huangs Eingeständnis der Affäre unterstützte ein anderer Tech-Milliardär – Elon Musk – auf seiner Online-Plattform X die Ansicht, dass der Nvidia-Chef für das Unternehmen unersetzlich sei. Musk ist mit dem KI-Bereich seiner Weltraumfirma SpaceX ein großer Nvidia-Kunde. Nvidia-Chips wurden zu einer unverzichtbaren Technik für die Entwicklung Künstlicher Intelligenz.
Huangs heikle Aktionärs-Position
Trotz seiner scheinbar allmächtigen Rolle im Tagesgeschäft ist Huang nicht unangreifbar, denn ihm gehört der Konzern keineswegs allein. Er hält nach offiziellen Börsenunterlagen rund 3,6 Prozent der Nvidia-Aktien. Damit ist er zwar der mit Abstand größte private Einzelaktionär, das Gros der Anteile liegt jedoch bei mächtigen institutionellen Fondsgesellschaften wie Vanguard und BlackRock.
Vor allem aber unterscheidet sich Nvidia fundamental von anderen Tech-Riesen im Silicon Valley. Es gibt keine Mehrstimmrechtsaktien, wie sie etwa Mark Zuckerberg beim Facebook-Mutterkonzern Meta schützen. Während Zuckerberg trotz eines Minderheitsanteils über Spezialaktien die uneingeschränkte Stimmenmehrheit kontrolliert und von Anlegern praktisch nicht abberufen werden kann, gilt bei Nvidia das klassische Prinzip: eine Aktie, eine Stimme.
Sollten die Vorwürfe eskalieren, haben die Großanleger und der unabhängige Verwaltungsrat juristisch das letzte Wort. Eine Mehrheit im Board of Directors könnte Huang jederzeit abberufen. Anders als Zuckerberg ist Huang dem Willen der Märkte und seiner Mitdirektoren institutionell ausgeliefert.
Atemberaubender Aufstieg – aber kein „Kronprinz“
Die bisherige Geschichte und der jüngste Aufstieg von Nvidia sind gleichwohl untrennbar mit Huang verbunden. Er war nicht nur ein Mitgründer, sondern auch gleich der erste Chef der Chipfirma. In den vergangenen 33 Jahren wuchs Nvidia mit ihm an der Spitze – und um ihn herum. Und es war ein atemberaubendes Wachstum: Im laufenden Geschäftsjahr dürfte der Umsatz als Folge des KI-Booms die Marke von 400 Milliarden US-Dollar knacken. Vor vier Jahren waren es noch 27 Milliarden Dollar.
Die Management-Struktur blieb dabei schlank. Es gibt zwar Top-Manager, die einzelne Bereiche verantworten. Aber sie sind eng auf ihre Themen spezialisiert, während nur Huang das große Ganze überblickt. Einen designierten Kronprinzen lehnte Huang stets ab. Er hoffe auf einen Nachfolger aus den eigenen Reihen, würde den Job aber gern noch 20 Jahre selbst machen, hatte er jüngst erklärt.
Wer im Notfall übernehmen könnte
Sollte der Druck von Behörden und Anlegern Huang dennoch zum Rückzug zwingen, stehen laut US-Branchenexperten vor allem interne Lösungen im Raum. Als naheliegende Wahl für eine Interimsführung gilt Finanzchefin Colette Kress. Die 58-Jährige leitet die Finanzen seit 2013 und ist an der Wall Street das vertrauteste Gesicht neben Huang. Nach dem Vorbild anderer Tech-Schwergewichte könnte sie beruhigend auf die Märkte wirken.
Geht es hingegen um die technologische DNA des Unternehmens, fällt unter Beobachtern regelmäßig der Name von Ian Buck, der das Geschäft mit Rechenzentren und Künstlicher Intelligenz leitet. Buck gilt als Miterfinder der Programmierplattform Cuda, die Nvidias Vormachtstellung im KI-Zeitalter erst begründet hat, und genießt bei Softwareentwicklern hohes Ansehen.
Nvidia-Untersuchung
Die Schlüsselrolle Huangs für das Unternehmen dürfte das bislang vorsichtige Vorgehen des Nvidia-Verwaltungsrates erklären. Schließlich deuten Dementis der Firma, die nach ersten Medienberichten noch von gewöhnlichen Kundenkontakten sprach, darauf hin, dass Huang auch seinen Konzern hinters Licht geführt haben könnte. Für viele Chefs wäre hier Endstation. Vom Nvidia-Aufsichtsgremium hieß es aber bei der Einleitung einer Untersuchung der Affäre, man habe weiterhin Vertrauen zu Huang und dessen Führungsteam.

articles.title: Ableton Live 13 announced with a step sequencer, new drum synth, and more
articles.text:
Today, Ableton announced Live 13, which is expected to arrive in early 2027 with a slew of new features. Most of the changes are seemingly minor on paper, but when combined, they make for the biggest update to the digital audio workstation (DAW) in years.
Ableton Live 13 announced with a step sequencer, new drum synth, and more
Live 13 is one of the biggest updates to Ableton’s music-making suite in years.
The feature most likely to draw attention is the addition of a proper step sequencer. While Ableton’s Push controller had a dedicated step sequencer, and you could effectively use the piano roll as one, the desktop app never included one. Ableton didn’t phone this feature in either — it’s a powerful sequencer. You can change velocity, timing, chance, length, and repeats for each step in the grid. Each track can have its own length, playback rate, and direction, letting you create something complex and evolving.
The addition of ARA plugin support will also likely excite pro producers and vocalists. This means compatible plugins can now be used directly on audio in the DAW. For example, pitch correction and time-stretching tool Melodyne previously required you to import audio from Ableton into Melodyne, then render it back out to a track in your DAW. Now it can clean up messy vocal takes directly in Live’s UI.
Ableton has also added a new mixer view that lets you see all the loaded devices on a track in a compact vertical view. Here you can drag and drop them between tracks, or copy and paste them. It also makes it much easier to navigate a sprawling 30-track session quickly at a glance.
My personal favorite new addition is Looplet, an experimental looping instrument with four playheads and a ton of options for manipulating your audio. It offers granular processing, filtering, pitch and speed control, and each playhead can be routed to individual tracks for additional processing. It’s a powerful tool for ambient and soundtrack work.
The full list of new features is sprawling, so here are just a few more highlights:
- A new drum synth with more than 20 different models across nine categories spanning classic drum machines and experimental abstract percussion.
- Capture now includes not just MIDI notes but automation as well.
- Contextual browsing lets you swap instruments and presets directly in the device view, reducing the need to open the main browser.
- Multiband racks for processing different frequencies through different effect chains.
- A bread-and-butter transient shaper for tightening up drum sounds.
- Envelope clips on return tracks for automating effects.
- Racks can now have up to 32 macros and custom mapping curves.
- Custom layouts on Push 3 for combining mixers, note grids, step sequencers, and more.

articles.title: Fireworks AI discloses new breach after cloud provider hack
articles.text:
AI infrastructure startup Fireworks has disclosed a new security breach in which attackers accessed its development machines after breaching a third-party cloud provider.
FireWorks provides a high-performance inference platform for developers who want to deploy and run open-source artificial intelligence models (such as Mistral, Meta's Llama, or Google's Gemma) without worrying about hardware bottlenecks and complex infrastructure tasks.
The company notified law enforcement and customers of another security incident in early October after attackers accessed environment variables containing API keys and tokens stored as secrets for a limited number of accounts.
"The evidence indicates links to a cybercriminal threat actor group, which is financially motivated and aimed at selling tokens from unauthorized access to Large Language Models (LLMs) to illicit routing gateways, known as 'LLMJacking'," Fireworks said at the time.
After revoking compromised internal credentials, affected Fireworks API keys, and keys created by the attackers, Fireworks discovered another security incident on October 23.
In the new breach, the threat actors accessed resource metadata (e.g., Fireworks resource identifiers, display names, descriptions, creation time), billing information (e.g., billing and shipping addresses, invoice and payment history, account balance, and credit usage), and incomplete model weights and datasets for some customers.
However, the company said the attackers couldn't access customer payment card numbers because Fireworks doesn't store them.
"A third-party cloud provider that hosted Fireworks R&D machines experienced a security incident on October 23. On October 24, the unauthorized third party used it to reach Fireworks development machines and then run an unauthorized workload that led to additional customer data impact," Fireworks noted in a Monday advisory.
"We detected this activity on the same day, and followed our incident response processes to take immediate remediation measures and close known critical vulnerabilities. As of October 25, we have not detected further evidence of successful unauthorized access by the threat actor on the Fireworks platform customers use."
Since the attack, Fireworks revoked and replaced credentials and service accounts, restricted unauthorized network pathways, isolated affected systems, and tightened access to data storage and analytics systems to block public or unauthorized access to stored data.
The company is now working with Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 incident response division to secure its systems against future attacks and further investigate the incident's full scope and impact.
One week ago, researchers at Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant reported that large language model hijacking attacks (also known as LLMjacking) are driving record costs for compromised organizations, with cloud AI charges reaching as high as $1 million due to fraudulent calls using stolen API keys.

articles.title: 31 ans d'agacement : Windows 11 teste une option pour faire taire les touches rémanentes
articles.text:
Cinq appuis rapides sur la touche Maj, et une fenêtre s’invite par-dessus la partie ou le document en cours pour proposer d’activer les touches rémanentes. Le scénario se rejoue à l’identique, ou presque, depuis Windows 95. Microsoft teste désormais, dans les versions d’essai de Windows 11, la case qui permet de ne plus jamais revoir cette boîte de dialogue.
La faute à un flipper de 1995
Les touches rémanentes rendent un vrai service : elles maintiennent virtuellement Ctrl ou Maj enfoncées, comme une pédale qui resterait appuyée, le temps de presser la touche suivante. La fonction s’adresse à celles et ceux qui tapent d’un seul doigt ou à l’aide d’une tige tenue en bouche. Les touches filtres, elles, ignorent les frappes brèves ou répétées pour amortir les tremblements. Deux raccourcis les déclenchent depuis trois décennies : cinq appuis sur Maj pour les premières, la touche Maj droite maintenue huit secondes pour les secondes.
Lire aussi : Windows 11 27H2 pourrait être la mise à jour majeure que vous attendez tous
Charles Oppermann, arrivé chez Microsoft en 1994 pour piloter l’accessibilité de Windows, raconte avoir écrit ces boîtes de dialogue début 1995. Les enfants de Brad Silverberg, le patron de Windows 95, activaient la fonction à répétition en martelant la touche Maj dans Space Cadet Pinball, le flipper culte de l’époque. La fenêtre de confirmation est née là, présentée dans la documentation de l’époque comme une « précaution contre l’usage accidentel ». Son équipe avait même envisagé une case pour ne plus poser la question ; elle a préféré garder les options d’accessibilité bien en vue.
Une case minuscule, trente et un ans plus tard
Les versions d’essai diffusées le 6 novembre, bâties sur Windows 11 26H2, ajoutent au dialogue des touches rémanentes une case à cocher inédite, libellée « Never turn on Sticky Keys with this shortcut » dans l’interface anglaise. Une fois cochée, le raccourci cesse définitivement d’ouvrir la fenêtre. Les touches filtres reçoivent leur équivalent. Le déploiement s’effectue par vagues au sein du programme de test, sans date encore pour le grand public.
L’option existait en réalité depuis toujours, enfouie dans les réglages d’accessibilité du clavier, où il fallait penser à aller la chercher. Chez Microsoft, une ingénieure de l’équipe Windows glisse d’ailleurs que « ça a toujours été possible ». La nouveauté tient à l’endroit : la case s’affiche au moment exact de l’agacement, dans la fenêtre fautive. Par défaut, rien ne change d’ailleurs pour les personnes qui dépendent de ces fonctions, puisque la question continue de s’afficher tant qu’on ne l’a pas congédiée.

articles.title: La première Ferrari électrique déjà épuisée pour 2027 : un succès qui fait taire les sceptiques
articles.text:
Vivement (c’est peu de le dire) critiquée lors de sa présentation, la première Ferrari 100 % électrique, la Luce, affiche complet aussi pour 2027, avant même que les premiers clients aient pu prendre son volant. De quoi donner quelques arguments au cheval cabré face à ses détracteurs.
Il y a quelques mois, la présentation de la première Ferrari électrique suscitait surtout des interrogations, voire quelques moqueries chez les amateurs de la marque italienne. Mais les premières réactions n’ont visiblement pas refroidi les acheteurs. Bien au contraire, puisque la Luce continue d’enregistrer des commandes à un rythme qui semble donner raison au constructeur italien.
La Ferrari Luce affiche déjà complet pour 2027
Comme le rapporte Bevolt, c’est Benedetto Vigna, le patron de Ferrari, qui a confirmé la nouvelle le 3 novembre dernier, à l’occasion de la présentation des résultats financiers du troisième trimestre.
Tous les exemplaires de la Luce prévus pour 2027 ont déjà été attribués à des clients. En d’autres termes, les nouveaux acheteurs, dont vous faites peut-être partie, devront donc patienter au moins jusqu’en 2028.
Un scénario qui rappelle celui de cet été. Dès juillet, nous rapportions que les quelque 500 exemplaires prévus pour 2026 avaient déjà tous trouvé preneur, alors que la voiture venait tout juste de dévoiler ses lignes pour le moins controversées.
Quoi que l’on pense de son look, la Luce ne manque pas d’arguments sous le capot. Cette première Ferrari 100 % électrique embarque quatre moteurs électriques développant une puissance cumulée de 1 050 chevaux. Elle dispose d’une batterie de 122 kWh, d'une autonomie annoncée de 530 km et promet un 0 à 100 km/h en seulement 2,5 secondes.
Une première Ferrari électrique qui ne laisse personne indifférent
Bien sûr, il est important de souligner que Ferrari n’a pas communiqué le nombre exact de voitures qui seront produites en 2027. Il convient donc de relativiser ce succès, la rareté faisant aussi partie de la stratégie commerciale du constructeur italien, véritable maître en la matière.
La Luce a néanmoins déjà démontré qu’elle pouvait susciter un intérêt pour le moins considérable, et en août dernier, son tout premier exemplaire, un modèle unique baptisé « Chassis 0 », avait été adjugé 40 millions de dollars lors d’une vente aux enchères caritative organisée par RM Sotheby’s.
Pour les intéressés, les premiers essais destinés aux clients sont prévus en 2027. Benedetto Vigna estime d’ailleurs que la perception de la voiture évolue de manière considérable lorsqu’on la découvre en personne.
Et vous, que pensez-vous de cette première Ferrari électrique Luce ?

articles.title: Start and Restore GPU Workloads in Seconds with NVIDIA Snapshot | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
NVIDIA Snapshot, a new open-source component of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, makes initialized GPU workloads reusable across inference replicas—speeding startup and recovery.
When inference demand spikes or a replica fails, available GPUs don’t translate immediately into serving capacity. Initializing an LLM workload—a process known as a cold start—can take minutes, delaying scaling and recovery.
Snapshot is a checkpoint and restore system for GPU workloads on Kubernetes. It captures a fully initialized workload—including CPU and GPU memory—and restores that state on compatible infrastructure, bringing inference capacity online in seconds instead of minutes. Figure 1 shows the startup sequence. Snapshot skips repeated workload initialization; infrastructure provisioning and container image loading remain outside the measured restore path.
This post explains how Snapshot checkpoints and restores GPU workloads, how platform teams can integrate it, and how restore times compare with cold starts across three inference engines.
Snapshot for AI factory operations
Originally developed for NVIDIA Dynamo inference workers, Snapshot provides checkpoint and restore capabilities that other inference engines, schedulers, controllers, and platforms can integrate.
Snapshot provides two operations for GPU Pods:
- Checkpoint: Once a workload is fully initialized, capture its CPU and GPU memory as a portable artifact.
- Restore: Start a new Pod from that artifact on any node with the same GPU model and driver. The process continues from where it was checkpointed, so weight loading, compilation, and graph capture are skipped.
Both operations use Kubernetes custom resources. To checkpoint a Pod that is already running, create a PodSnapshot that names it. To start a Pod from a template and checkpoint it as soon as it is ready, create a SnapshotJob instead. To restore, add the annotation nvidia.com/restore-from to a new Pod, naming the PodSnapshot to restore from. The workload only needs a small handshake to pause before the checkpoint and resume after the restore. The repository has ready-made examples for vLLM, SGLang, and NVIDIA TensorRT LLM.
Snapshot can checkpoint and restore compatible workloads that span multiple GPUs on a single node as a single checkpoint artifact across ranks. This supports fast startup for large mixture-of-experts (MoE) models using parallelism strategies such as tensor parallelism (TP), data and expert parallelism (DEP), and decode context parallelism (DCP). Workloads must meet Snapshot’s checkpoint/restore and runtime compatibility requirements. See the example configurations.
Benchmarks
Design partners have also evaluated Snapshot on their own workloads:
- Crusoe, an upstream contributor to Snapshot, reduced GLM-5.3 Pod readiness time from roughly 8 minutes to 31 seconds on NVIDIA HGX B300.
- Saturn Cloud, a token factory platform, benchmarked NVIDIA Snapshot for scale-from-zero inference, cutting vLLM startup from 2–8.5 minutes to 6–34 seconds on NVIDIA HGX B300.
The following benchmarks show how Snapshot accelerates inference startup across vLLM, SGLang, and NVIDIA TensorRT LLM (TRT-LLM)—with models from 600 million parameters to mixture-of-experts (MoE) models with 1 TB checkpoints on 8 GPUs. Across all tested configurations, Snapshot brings a replica back in under 45 seconds, 8x to 36x faster than a cold start.
Methodology
Each configuration was tested using two strategies on the same hardware and software stack:
- Cold start: The workload starts from scratch. The clock runs from process launch until engine initialization returns, before inference. The measurement is divided into four phases (Table 2):
  - Startup: Starting the engine and worker processes, importing Python libraries, and setting up communication between GPUs. Some just-in-time (JIT) kernel compilation also happens here.
  - Model load: Reading the model weights and constructing the model’s tensors, including any engine-specific conversion or repacking done while loading.
  - Initialization: Preparing the loaded model to serve: memory profiling, allocating the key-value (KV) cache and runtime buffers, and other kernel and runtime preparation.
  - Compilation, autotuning, and graph capture: Compiling kernels (for example, with torch.compile), autotuning them for the GPU, and capturing CUDA graphs.
- Snapshot: The workload is restored from its checkpoint. The clock runs from the moment Snapshot is asked to restore until the workload is serving again. The measurement is divided into four stages (Table 3):
  - Agent setup: The Snapshot agent on the node locates the checkpoint artifact and prepares the target Pod and GPUs.
  - Checkpoint/Restore in Userspace (CRIU) restore: CRIU, the standard Linux tool for checkpointing processes, reads the process image from storage into host memory. Speed is set mostly by the storage backend.
  - CUDA restore: Copying GPU state back into GPU memory.
  - Wake/remap: Adapting the process to the new node and waking the engine.
Both measurements exclude pulling the container image and setting up the container runtime. The KV cache release is triggered before every checkpoint, so it is not part of the artifact.
Table 1 also reports checkpoint time and size: how long it takes to capture a fully initialized replica and how much storage the stored artifact requires. This is a one-time cost per model and configuration.
Setup
- GPU: NVIDIA B200
- NVIDIA driver: 615.71.09
- Storage backend: VAST (NFS)
- Inference engines:
  - vLLM 0.31.0
  - SGLang 0.5.21
  - TensorRT LLM 1.3.0
Results
The benchmarks show four main findings.
- Restore times stayed under 43 seconds: Across all tested configurations, Snapshot restored replicas in 3.6 to 42.7 seconds—8x to 36x faster than cold start. The largest MoE models, with checkpoints of about 600 GB to 1 TB across eight GPUs, restored in under 43 seconds compared with cold-start times of 6 to 19 minutes.
- Restoring skips more than weight loading: Cold-start time includes loading weights, compiling and autotuning kernels, and capturing CUDA graphs. Snapshot restores the initialized workload, skipping these repeated steps.
- Checkpointing pays off with the first restored replica: In every tested configuration, checkpoint time plus restore time was shorter than a single cold start. Checkpoint creation took 15 seconds to 5.5 minutes, depending on the model and configuration.
- Moving GPU state dominates large restores: For the eight-GPU MoE configurations, restoring GPU state took 18 to 29 seconds. Restoring CPU process state with CRIU took 4.2 to 10.8 seconds.

articles.title: VC exits show year-over-year improvement as acquisitions ramp up: CVCA report
articles.text:
The disclosed value of VC exits in Canada has more than doubled so far compared to last year as the ecosystem eagerly anticipates an influx of capital in the coming years.
The total amount invested hit $4.3 billion CAD across 397 deals through the first three quarters of 2026.
According to the Canadian Venture Capital & Private Equity Association’s Q3 2026 report on Canadian venture deals, mergers and acquisitions accounted for 26 out of the 28 venture-backed exits during the year’s first three quarters. There were only 29 exits in total last year. Proceeds totalled $744 million CAD across 10 disclosed transactions, which is more than double the $355 million in disclosed exit value for all of 2025.
But while 2026 venture-backed merger and acquisition (M&A) activity has already surpassed 2025 numbers, last year was far below 2023 and 2024, which both recorded more than 30 exits.
Some of the largest acquisitions included an $850-million CAD go-private deal for Calgary’s Blackline Safety and the reported $400-million USD purchase of Montréal amateur sports streamer LiveBarn. Meanwhile, one of 2026’s largest exits—the semiconductor company Taalas, which chip giant AMD has agreed to buy for $2.9 billion USD—has yet to close, meaning that it’s not included in CVCA’s exit total. The $4.75-billion USD deal to acquire CoolIT Systems, which passed from KKR to Ecolab, was classified as a private equity transaction, and was also therefore not added to the total.
“Having more liquidity in the market is overall positive,” said CVCA director of data and product David Kornacki in an interview on Monday, adding that seeing that liquidity reinvested in the market is positive as well. He added that this facilitates returning capital to limited partners and raising new funds.
No venture-backed initial public offerings (IPOs) have been recorded since 2023, the report says. That absence has created knock-on effects for Canada’s VC industry in general. While companies stay private longer, it takes longer to return capital to limited partners (LPs), making it more challenging to fundraise as a general partner (GP) and leaving less money out there for emerging managers.
RELATED: Canada to implement QSBS-style tax incentive and “level playing field” with US
Kornacki said that alternative routes to the public markets, like reverse takeovers and special-purpose acquisition company (SPAC) deals, have become more active exit avenues this year. Xanadu and General Fusion both made public debuts via SPAC to raise more capital for their quantum and fusion technologies; space communications company NorthStar went public earlier this year, and aspiring defence prime Juno Industries also listed in October.
“We’re still seeing companies going public, but not through the traditional route anymore,” Kornacki said.
Overall, the report said that capital continued to concentrate around a handful of megadeals larger than $50 million, continuing a trend of deal count dropping every year since 2021.
VC activity was broadly on par with last year’s numbers: the total amount invested hit $4.3 billion CAD across 397 deals through the first three quarters of 2026, which is just one percent less than at this point last year. Notably, the recently announced $7-billion CAD Cohere Series E deal will nearly double that year-to-date total once it closes.
That deal could eventually uplift the growth stage, which faltered this quarter. While early-stage, later-stage, and growth-stage deals were all below their five-year averages, growth stage was the lowest, at 66 percent below its five-year average of $1.16 billion for the first three quarters of the year. At $396 million, growth-stage investment was down 55 percent compared to this point last year.
CVCA has been advocating for an increased focus on growth-stage investment in Canada. The organization recently got its wish when the feds revealed that the majority of a $750-million envelope for its Early and Growth Stage Investment Strategy was earmarked for the “later and growth-stage,” in addition to a new iteration of the Venture Capital Catalyst Initiative (now called Growth VCCI).
But details remain to be announced for that strategy, and the Growth VCCI funding will likely take at least 12 to 18 months for the capital to reach fund managers.
“It’s too early to expect any immediate improvements,” Kornacki said. “But let’s press on the gas, let’s get this money deployed as quickly as possible.”
Feature image courtesy Chris Robert via Unsplash.

articles.title: The indie game community is in disarray over AI and Big Walk
articles.text:
Some Independent Games Festival (IGF) jurors published a statement yesterday saying they would not vote for games that use generative AI in “any capacity.” Soon after, the developer of indie hit Big Walk has published a statement saying it “sparingly” used AI in the “final stretch” of the game’s development to “help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs.”
The indie game community is in disarray over AI and Big Walk
Big Walk’s developers said that they used AI ‘sparingly’ to help work through ‘difficult technical challenges.’
According to the jurors’ statement, a copy of which was posted by Austin Walker, while this year’s IGF entries have been “incredible,” there has been “a significant increase” in the number of games “developed with generative AI tools,” leading to “fairly intense discussion and disagreement” with no “universal consensus.” The statement includes a list of beliefs, including that generative AI has “negative effects,” that AI-generated code is “not an exception to these harms,” and that use of AI tools is “not a forgone conclusion in our industry.”
IGF jurors that signed include Telling Lies and Immortality creator Sam Barlow and Celeste composer Lena Raine. The jurors say that the statement doesn’t speak for IGF as an organization or for all IGF jury members, noting that some voiced concern about being able to safely sign “without professional blowback.”
One contentious title was apparently Big Walk, the co-op adventure game from Untitled Goose Game developer House House. In a statement to Aftermath and posted on its website, House House said that “In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code—we’d estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.”
House House said its “primary use case” of LLMs was “to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code,” including fixing an issue with shadows by modifying LLM-suggested code. House House noted it turned to the “LLM chatbot” after researching the problem “extensively” and even speaking to an engineer at Unity.
The studio said it disclosed its AI usage as part of its IGF submission, though it has not disclosed AI usage on Big Walk’s Steam page because “the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage.”
“This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal,” House House said. “We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as ‘inevitable’. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.”
House House didn’t have an AI policy in place when it developed Big Walk, which it described as a “failure,” and said it will “work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards.”
Barlow said after we published this post that Big Walk was not the “impetus” for the IGF’s discussion, but it became the “tricky edge case — well what about this minimal use of AI, what about when your favorite game, or team uses it?” Barlow added that “This is not a call to boycott a certain game, or to economically hurt a team — this was about a single award’s show of many and what that award should mean to reflect our ‘indie’ alternative to mainstream and larger scale game development.” Walker also shared a long blog post that’s worth reading about his position on AI and the IGF awards.
Update, November 10th: Added posts from Barlow and Walker.

articles.text:
Solopreneure in Gefahr: Experten erklären größtes Cybersecurity-Risiko und wie du dich als Einzelunternehmer schützt
Über 330.000 registrierte Cyberstraftaten bei einem geschätzten Schaden von 200 Milliarden Euro für die deutsche Wirtschaft in 2025: Das Bundeslagebild Cybercrime für das vergangene Jahr zeichnet ein düsteres Bild. articles.title: Manage Kubernetes Clusters for GPU Infrastructure with NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
NVIDIA is announcing two open source projects for building and operating managed Kubernetes services on GPU infrastructure—NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR). Both are new projects available in public preview.
AI Factory customers often want to consume GPU capacity through the Kubernetes APIs, tools, and ecosystem they already use, with the factory operating their clusters. Delivering this service requires API-driven provisioning, tenant isolation, upgrades, and recovery, backed by service commitments. It also requires qualifying GPU hardware, networking, drivers, and runtime software across GPU generations and Kubernetes versions.
NVKE and NVKR divide this work between cluster management and reproducible software builds. NVKE provides the software to run a managed Kubernetes service, installed on the factory’s infrastructure, with APIs to provision and manage clusters. NVKR builds the operating system images, container images, and packages those clusters need, using recipes that define validated combinations of software versions and GPU generations. AI Factories retain control of their software, operations, service, and customer experience. Teams can adopt NVKE and NVKR projects together or independently.
Both NVKE and NVKR are components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform, which helps AI factories design, build, and operate GPU infrastructure. Both projects are available on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license, so teams can inspect the code, develop in parallel, and contribute improvements. During the public preview, APIs, configuration, and behavior may change between releases. NVKE and NVKR are not yet recommended for production workloads. See preview status and known limitations.
This walkthrough covers building a node image with NVKR, deploying the NVKE management plane, and provisioning a customer Kubernetes cluster.
How NVKE and NVKR work together
- NVKR builds the software: It produces node images, binaries, container images, and Helm charts from specific source versions and records the build inputs.
- NVKE manages the clusters: It uses those artifacts to provision and operate Kubernetes clusters.
Teams can use the projects together or separately. NVKE has no runtime dependency on NVKR, and NVKR can build artifacts for other Kubernetes management systems.
nvkectl starts a temporary seed cluster on a bootstrap host and uses it to form a management cluster. The NVKE management plane, including the REST API and controllers, runs on the management cluster. The management plane creates workload clusters for AI factory customers, each with its own Kubernetes control plane, etcd, and node pools. Machines come from NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo), which manages bare-metal lifecycle, through CAPNICo, the Cluster API infrastructure provider for NICo.
A node must present an attested SPIFFE identity before it receives join credentials. The NVKE telemetry pipeline, an OpenTelemetry-based Helm chart, collects logs, metrics, and traces and exports them over OTLP to a monitoring backend.
Inside each workload cluster, teams add the GPU-accelerated runtime with AI Cluster Runtime (AICR), node packages with NodeWright, and break-fix automation with NVSentinel.
NVKE is a Certified Kubernetes AI Platform and Certified Kubernetes Installer, conformance tested on Kubernetes 1.36.
From bare metal to a customer cluster
This walkthrough describes how to provision a customer Kubernetes cluster starting from servers installed in a rack by building a node image with NVKR, deploying the NVKE management plane with nvkectl, and creating a customer cluster through the NVKE API. The NVKE documentation lists every flag and option, along with the most up-to-date steps.
Walkthrough prerequisites:
- Three CPU servers for the management cluster, plus a separate Linux bootstrap host on the site network with containerd, nerdctl, kind, Helm, and kubectl
- Three CPU servers for the workload cluster control plane
- A pool of GPU servers for worker nodes
- A NICo installation with enrolled capacity
- A Linux build host with Docker and KVM support
- An HTTP server for the node image, a container registry for the controller image, and internet access to download the open source images and Helm charts used during installation
Build the node image
NVKR defines the Kubernetes software configuration that NVIDIA validates for NVKE and provides the reproducible pipeline that turns that definition into deployable artifacts. NVKR builds node images from version-pinned sources and records every input, so teams can identify the software included in each image and can rebuild it later. The management cluster and each node pool can run different images, such as one per CPU architecture or GPU generation.
Teams clone the NVKR repository on the build host. They then run the quickstart script to build nvkectl, the NVKE controller image, and its Helm chart, and a second script to build the node image, named node-image-01 in this walkthrough.
$ git clone https://github.com/dsx-ai-factory/nvkr.git && cd nvkr
$ bash scripts/nvkr-quickstart.sh
$ NVKE_OS_ARCH=amd64 scripts/nvke-os-local.sh node-image-01
The node image build compiles the NVKE node agent and OVN-Kubernetes from source and adds checksum-pinned upstream releases of the Kubernetes 1.36 packages and the SPIRE agent. It then boots a virtual machine from the Ubuntu installer, installs the agents, and stages the Kubernetes and networking packages on the disk. The result is a QCOW2 disk image. Teams push the controller image to a registry, copy nvkectl to the bootstrap host, and put the QCOW2 on an HTTP server.
Deploy the NVKE management plane
The NVKE management plane runs on a Kubernetes cluster called the management cluster. Teams run the following command on the bootstrap host to begin creating the management cluster:
$ nvkectl bootstrap site -f site-a.yaml \
    --nvke-controller-image registry.example.com/nvke/nvke-controller:<tag>
The site specification file, site-a.yaml, includes the inputs that NICo needs to provision the three servers for the management cluster. The bootstrap command starts a temporary Kubernetes cluster on the bootstrap host. This temporary cluster uses kind to run a single Kubernetes node and hosts the NVKE software needed for the setup.
The NVKE controller asks NICo for three servers, which NICo boots from the previously built node image. When all three nodes have joined, the bootstrap process deletes the temporary cluster, leaving the management cluster. Teams then install the NVKE management plane on the management cluster and run nvkectl config set-site to connect the command-line tool to the NVKE API.
Publish a release set that customers will run
Customers choose a release by name from those that the AI factory publishes. They do not work directly with operating system images or cloud-init configuration.
A release set has three components:
- A machine image holds the iPXE script NICo runs to boot a server.
- A cluster release pairs a machine image with the cloud-init configuration that prepares a control plane node and records the Kubernetes version that cloud-init installs.
- A node pool release provides the corresponding image and configuration for worker nodes.
$ nvkectl create machineimage -f machineimage.yaml
$ nvkectl create clusterrelease -f clusterrelease.yaml
$ nvkectl create nodepoolrelease -f nodepoolrelease.yaml
Create a customer cluster
A customer cluster request includes the same NICo inputs as the site specification, plus a Kubernetes version. The control plane and each node pool have their own instance types, VPC prefix, and release. In this example, the control plane and GPU node pool reference releases named k8s-1.36.3-amd64.
name: customer-a
controlPlaneKubernetesVersion: 1.36.3
etcdEncrypted: true
controlPlaneVIP: 10.0.20.10
nico: {orgID: <org-id>, siteID: <site-id>, vpcID: <vpc-id>}
controlPlaneConfig:
  desiredCount: 3
  nico: {instanceTypePreference: [<cpu-instance-type>], vpcPrefixIDs: [<prefix-id>], release: k8s-1.36.3-amd64}
nodePools:
  - name: gpu
    nodeNamePrefix: gpu
    desiredNodeCount: 4
    nico: {instanceTypeID: <gpu-instance-type>, vpcPrefixIDs: [<prefix-id>], release: k8s-1.36.3-amd64}
Teams save the request as customer-a.yaml, then run the following command to submit it to the NVKE REST API through nvkectl.
$ nvkectl create cluster -f customer-a.yaml
The cluster status remains Provisioning until the first control-plane node has run kubeadm init and NVKE has installed OVN-Kubernetes and NodeLocal DNSCache. The status then changes to Provisioned.
Give the customer access
The customer accesses the cluster’s Kubernetes API through a kubeconfig, while the AI factory continues managing it through the NVKE API. To give the customer access, the team retrieves the cluster’s kubeconfig from the management cluster and shares it securely.
$ nvkectl get kubeconfig customer-a --output-file customer-a.kubeconfig
kubeconfig written to customer-a.kubeconfig
AI factories and partners building with NVKE and NVKR
NVIDIA Cloud Partners Firmus and SK Telecom are integrating NVKE and NVKR into their AI Factories to build and deploy Kubernetes clusters that host AI workloads.
Additionally, NVIDIA Partners Mirantis, Rafay, Spectro Cloud, OpenNebula Systems, and vCluster are integrating components of NVKE and NVKR into their managed Kubernetes offerings to help their AI factory customers run AI workloads on Kubernetes. Netris is enabling NVKE for its network automation solution.
Available today in public preview
NVKE and NVKR are in public preview and are not yet recommended for production workloads. These projects are evolving rapidly, and the NVKE API may change between releases. The preview status page lists current limitations.
Teams can evaluate the projects against their infrastructure requirements and review planned work on the public NVKE and NVKR roadmaps. Feedback and contributions can help shape NVKE, NVKR, and the rest of the DSX AI Factory stack.
Get started
NVKE and NVKR are open source components available through the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory GitHub organization, alongside CAPNICo. Start with the NVKE documentation or try the local quickstart on a single machine—no GPU or NVIDIA account needed.
- Join the conversation in #nvke on the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Slack workspace using the Slack invitation link. Share what you build with the community.

articles.title: Overcoming Silicon Photonics Process Control Challenges in the AI Era
articles.text:
How connected inspection, metrology and software can help manufacturers move SiPh and CPO toward high-volume production.
More bandwidth. Lower latency. Less power consumed and less heat generated.
These are three of the challenges facing manufacturers as AI pushes electrical interconnects toward their limits. Silicon photonics (SiPh) and co-packaged optics (CPO) offer a path forward by using light to transmit data rather than relying solely on electrical signals. But realizing those benefits at production scale introduces another challenge: maintaining precise process control across the optical structures, materials and integration processes that ultimately determine device performance and yield.
At the same time, traditional copper interconnects face increasing resistance, electromigration and power challenges as semiconductor architectures scale (Figure 1). For manufacturers, the shift toward silicon photonics places greater importance on precise control of optical structures and materials.
Fig. 1: In the AI era, interconnects (within die and die-to-die and board-to-board) become the bottleneck. Source: Onto Innovation
One of the fundamental differences between conventional semiconductor manufacturing and silicon photonics is what manufacturers need to control.
Photonics yield and performance depend on critical dimensions and tight control of geometry, films and defects. Optical performance can be highly sensitive to relatively small process variations, with consequences for device performance and yield.
That makes several areas particularly important:
The result is a process control challenge that extends across multiple inspection and metrology steps. Manufacturers need visibility into the different variables that influence optical performance throughout fabrication and integration.

articles.title: Mazda promet 703 km d’autonomie sur sa nouvelle 6e, mais lisez bien les petites lignes
articles.text:
C’est la pire électrique que nous ayons essayée jusqu’à maintenant chez Numerama. Lors de mon essai publié en février, j’avais relevé un amortissement manquant de cohérence (tantôt souple, tantôt sec), une autonomie juste pour une berline routière, une recharge trop lente sur la version Grande Autonomie, des aides à la conduite à revoir et un système multimédia à la ramasse.
Le millésime 2027, que Mazda a présenté ce lundi 9 novembre, corrige une partie de ces défauts avec sa nouvelle (et unique) batterie, sa suspension recalibrée et ses ADAS revues. Le tout pour un prix toujours aussi intéressant : à partir de 43 900 €.
703 km d’autonomie, mais en ville
Pour mémoire, la 6e imposait jusqu’ici un choix absurde. La version de base, avec sa batterie LFP de 68,8 kWh acceptait 165 kW en recharge rapide mais plafonnait à 479 km WLTP. Quant à la Grande Autonomie de 80 kWh, elle allait jusqu’à 552 km, mais était bridée à 90 kW et demandait 47 minutes pour passer de 10 à 80 %, soit deux fois plus que la petite batterie.
Le millésime 2027 remplace les deux accumulateurs par une seule batterie LFP de 78 kWh, qui accepte jusqu’à 200 kW. Elle est alimentée par le même moteur de 258 ch (placé à l’arrière) de l’ancienne version à petite batterie.
Attention à la lecture de la fiche technique. Le communiqué français met en avant « jusqu’à 703 km d’autonomie en cycle urbain ». La « vraie » autonomie théorique en cycle mixte de la 6e est 560 km WLTP, comme le confirme Mazda dans son communiqué allemand et autrichien.
Finalement, c’est donc 8 km de plus que l’ancienne Grande Autonomie et 81 km de plus que l’ancienne version de base. Côté recharge, Mazda annonce un temps de 24 minutes pour passer de 10 à 80 % de batterie. On retrouve cette fois le temps de l’ancienne petite batterie, mais avec plus d’énergie à remplir. À en croire nos confrères de Caradisiac qui ont pu roulé avec la version évoluée de la 6e, les promesses de recharge semblent se tenir avec un 2-80 % en 25 minutes.
Le châssis et les aides revus, le logiciel à peine
Mazda ne s’est pas arrêté au couple batterie/recharge et dit avoir recalibré la suspension pour mieux équilibrer confort et stabilité. Le constructeur a également retravaillé la réponse de la pédale d’accélérateur et augmenté la puissance du freinage régénératif, sans toutefois annoncer l’arrivée d’un mode One Pedal. Dommage, cela faisait partie des points à revoir.
Niveau aides à la conduite, le Smart Cruise Assist, qui gère la vitesse et maintient la voiture dans sa voie, fonctionne désormais jusqu’à 160 km/h. Mais surtout, l’aide au maintien dans la file se veut plus souple. Bon point.
Le logiciel était le gros point noir de notre essai. Pourtant, il n’a droit qu’à une mise à jour du planificateur d’itinéraire, qui filtre et recherche mieux les bornes de recharge compatibles. C’est déjà ça, mais le communiqué ne mentionne aucune autre évolution du système multimédia.
Un prix d’entrée en hausse, sans bonus écologique
La 6e 2027 démarre à 43 900 € en finition Takumi. C’est 1 000 € de plus que l’ancienne version de base et 600 € de moins que l’ancienne Grande Autonomie. Au niveau supérieur, la Takumi Plus coûte 45 900 €, comme la nouvelle finition Homura Plus, avec ses boucliers noir brillant et sa sellerie cuir et suédine à surpiqûres rouges.
Fabriquée en Chine par la coentreprise Changan Mazda, la berline n’obtient pas le score environnemental donnant droit au coup de pouce de l’État pour l’achat d’une électrique. Seule une prime CEE de 400 € s’applique. La nouvelle Mazda 6e est déjà dans les concessions depuis le début du mois de novembre.

articles.title: Drone d’intérieur et robot de patrouille : Amazon recycle deux projets enlisés — Frandroid
articles.text:
Voici Ring Robotics qui recycle deux projets qu’Amazon n’a jamais su vendre, avec un nouveau nom et une IA en partie hébergée dans le cloud. Un Rover, un robot, ainsi qu’un drone.
Ring remet en vitrine une caméra volante à 249,99 dollars, le prix exact qu’il annonçait déjà en 2020. Entre-temps, l’appareil n’a jamais dépassé le stade du programme sur invitation. Le robot Astro, qu’Amazon n’a jamais réussi à installer dans les salons, revient lui aussi avec un nouveau métier : vigile de nuit pour entrepôts. La marque parle d’une nouvelle catégorie de produits, on y voit surtout deux projets que le groupe refuse d’enterrer.
Panos Panay, patron des appareils et d’Alexa chez Amazon, a présenté Ring Robotics sur X ce 10 novembre.
Le premier modèle, le Ring Drone Cam, est un petit quadricoptère d’intérieur qui filme en 2K avec un angle de 148 degrés. Il couvre ainsi une bonne partie d’une pièce, sans caméra vissée dans chaque coin. Il suit des trajets programmés, décolle à la demande ou part inspecter une pièce dès qu’une alarme Ring se déclenche.
Le Ring Rover Cam, lui, roule et filme jusqu’en 4K. Son mât-périscope voit par-dessus les étagères, et une sirène complète un système audio pour interpeller un intrus à distance. Selon Amazon, le robot arrive le 16 décembre à 999,99 dollars, le drone le 27 janvier 2027 à 249,99 dollars. Les deux restent réservés aux États-Unis (prix américains, hors taxes).
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1000 passe à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 499 €, support de lavage offert ! Vision IA tri-caméra, sans fil périmétrique, tonte des bordures, adaptation à toutes les conditions de luminosité… Bref, il a tout pour tondre à votre place !
Un Astro reconverti, un drone qui s’appuie sur le cloud
Ring ne cache pas la filiation du Rover. Le constructeur dit avoir repris le meilleur de l’Astro lancé en 2021, dont les propriétaires appréciaient surtout la fonction de ronde. La nouveauté technique se trouve dans le drone et son système de navigation AI Pilot.
Selon Ring, il combine capteurs embarqués et traitement dans le cloud pour cartographier le logement et contourner les meubles. Jamie Siminoff, fondateur de Ring, explique avoir déporté une bonne part du calcul sur les serveurs de l’entreprise pour tenir le prix. Résultat, d’après les détails publiés aux États-Unis, le drone a besoin d’internet pour naviguer.
Jamie Siminoff assure que ses équipes se sont « accrochées jusqu’à y arriver ». Pour le moment, le drone n’a pas encore reçu l’autorisation de la FCC, le régulateur américain des télécoms, et ne peut donc pas être vendu.
Les vols programmés du drone et la consultation des vidéos du Rover exigent un abonnement Ring Protect, sans que Ring précise la formule. Le prix d’appel ne dit rien du coût réel sur un an.
Le drone se pilote aussi depuis Alexa Home Map, la carte 3D du logement que Panos Panay a dévoilée fin octobre. Elle accompagnait la nouvelle fournée d’Echo et l’écran Echo Show 16. Amazon dessine une maison où les appareils voient tout, et où certains se déplacent.
    Pour aller plus loin
Amazon dévoile l’Echo Show 16, un écran connecté avec une caméra qui voit la nuit et Fire TV
            
Ne l’attendez pas tout de suite
Pour le moment, le drone est surtout à destination du propriétaire américain d’une maison à étage, déjà équipé de l’alarme Ring. Il peut vérifier la cuisine sans y visser une caméra fixe. Le Rover pourrait intéresser un gérant d’un commerce ou d’un entrepôt qui veut une ronde nocturne sans payer de vigile. En France, la question ne se pose pas encore : aucune date ni aucun prix n’est annoncé hors des États-Unis.
Ring promet que la confidentialité est « le réglage par défaut », avec une caméra éteinte au dock. Les vidéos seront protégées par TAKE, un chiffrement que la marque détaille dans une note technique. Ring garde une copie des clés dans une enclave sécurisée, un compartiment isolé de ses serveurs, et la supprime au bout de 24 heures.
Pendant ce délai, l’entreprise peut donc déchiffrer les images pour les fonctions activées sur le compte. Le chiffrement de bout en bout, qui l’en empêche, reste optionnel et prive de ces fonctions. La note ne dit rien du drone, et la marque traîne un passif chargé avec la police américaine.
Les derniers propriétaires d’Astro, vendu 1 449,99 dollars, n’ont aucune évolution annoncée pour leur robot. Amazon a pourtant racheté la start-up new-yorkaise Fauna Robotics en mars et recrute pour un robot domestique « inédit », selon ses offres d’emploi. Autrement dit, le vrai robot de maison serait encore dans les cartons.
En France, Amazon vient de glisser une caméra dans l’Echo Studio, et l’Echo Show 16 voit dans le noir.
    Pour aller plus loin
Amazon met une caméra dans l’Echo Studio, fait de l’Echo Dot un répéteur Wi-Fi et lance l’Echo Time, un réveil connecté

articles.title: Amazon n'attend pas le Black Friday et fait chuter le prix de l’iPhone 17 Pro Max
articles.text:
Depuis la sortie de l’iPhone 18 Pro Max en septembre, la génération précédente devient nettement plus abordable. À quelques semaines du Black Friday, Amazon affiche l’iPhone 17 Pro Max 256 Go à 1 241,10 €, soit près de 390 € de moins que le prix de lancement de son successeur, pour un smartphone qui reste l’un des plus complets du marché.
L’iPhone 17 Pro Max a marqué un vrai changement de cap chez Apple avec son châssis monocoque en aluminium, sa chambre à vapeur et son triple appareil photo 48 Mpx. Il embarque un écran de 6,9 pouces, la puce A19 Pro et la plus grande autonomie jamais proposée sur un iPhone à sa sortie.
Amazon le propose à 1 241,10 € au lieu d’un prix conseillé de 1 479 €, son prix de lancement, soit 237,90 € d’économie (-16 %), en version 256 Go Orange cosmique. Le coloris Bleu intense est affiché au même prix. Le smartphone est vendu et expédié par Amazon, et ce tarif rejoint le prix le plus bas relevé récemment sur la plateforme.
Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max à 1 241,10 € au lieu de 1 479 €
Pourquoi choisir l’iPhone 17 Pro Max ?
- Un écran de 6,9 pouces à 120 Hz, lisible même en plein soleil
- La puce A19 Pro refroidie par une chambre à vapeur, pour des performances qui tiennent dans la durée
- Trois capteurs 48 Mpx, avec un téléobjectif capable de zoomer jusqu’à 8x en qualité optique
- Jusqu’à 39 heures de lecture vidéo, un record pour un iPhone à sa sortie
- 256 Go de stockage pour les photos et vidéos en haute définition
Le Pro Max qui a rompu avec la routine
Avec l’iPhone 17 Pro Max, Apple a revu sa copie en profondeur. Le titane laisse place à un châssis monocoque en aluminium, et le module photo s’étend désormais sur toute la largeur du dos. Ce choix a permis d’intégrer une chambre à vapeur qui dissipe nettement mieux la chaleur, ainsi qu’une batterie plus grosse. L’écran ProMotion de 6,9 pouces atteint 3 000 nits en pointe, une luminosité qui le rend parfaitement lisible en extérieur, comme le relevait Clubic dans son test de l’iPhone 17 Pro Max. Le verre Ceramic Shield protège désormais l’avant comme l’arrière.
Ce smartphone a aussi ses défauts. Il est le plus épais jamais conçu par Apple et reprend du poids, avec environ 231 g en main, ce qui se ressent à l’usage. Les nouveautés logicielles restaient limitées à sa sortie, et il a été remplacé en septembre par l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, qui apporte la puce A20 Pro et une autonomie supérieure. Enfin, aucun chargeur n’est fourni, seulement un câble USB-C tressé.
Un appareil photo et une autonomie taillés pour durer
Trois capteurs 48 Mpx et un zoom qui va loin
Le système photo Pro Fusion aligne trois capteurs 48 Mpx : principal, ultra grand-angle et téléobjectif. Ce dernier, doté d’un tétraprisme et d’un capteur plus grand, propose un zoom 4x natif et monte jusqu’à 8x en qualité optique, avec des clichés qui conservent un bon niveau de détail. À l’avant, la caméra Center Stage de 18 Mpx recadre automatiquement les selfies de groupe, et la fonction Dual Capture filme simultanément avec les caméras avant et arrière. Les vidéastes exigeants profitent en prime du ProRes RAW, de l’Apple Log 2 et du Genlock.
Une endurance qui change le quotidien
L’autre point fort reste l’autonomie. Apple annonce jusqu’à 39 heures de lecture vidéo, soit plusieurs heures de mieux que l’iPhone 16 Pro Max, de quoi tenir sans difficulté une grosse journée, voire davantage avec un usage modéré. La recharge rapide permet de récupérer 50 % en une vingtaine de minutes avec un adaptateur USB-C de 40 W, et la recharge sans fil MagSafe ou Qi2 grimpe jusqu’à 25 W.
✅ Les points forts
- Un nouveau design aluminium réussi
- De beaux progrès sur la chauffe
- Les meilleures performances du marché
- Très grande autonomie
- L'iPhone le plus polyvalent en photo
- Écran toujours plus lumineux
❌ Les limites
- Peu de nouveautés logicielles cette année
- Il reprend du poids et de l'épaisseur
Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max à 1 241,10 € au lieu de 1 479 €
L’iPhone 17 Pro Max reste un smartphone haut de gamme redoutable, avec un écran, une autonomie et un appareil photo qui n’ont pas à rougir face à son successeur. À 1 241,10 €, il devient une alternative sérieuse à l’iPhone 18 Pro Max pour ceux qui veulent un grand iPhone Pro sans payer le prix fort du dernier modèle.

articles.title: “Cette attaque revient au corps des gardiens de la révolution de la République islamique d’Iran” : le piratage des supermarchés français s'éclaircit
articles.text:
Cyberattaque contre des supermarchés : la France pointe l'Iran du doigt
Un mois après la vague de cyberattaques à l'encontre de centaines de supermarchés en France, la justice et les services de renseignements français pensent avoir trouvé le coupable : des hackers iraniens du régime des mollahs.
Ce lundi 9 novembre, soit environ un mois après des attaques informatiques visant à faire grimper la température des réfrigérateurs de plus de 700 magasins en France, les choses commencent à se préciser. D'après une information du Figaro, depuis confirmée par la procureure de Paris, Laure Beccuau, l'Iran serait derrière ces cyberattaques.
"Une attaque d’une ampleur inédite et d’une agressivité inédite"
Le parquet de Paris a annoncé l’ouverture d’une information judiciaire pour "atteintes frauduleuses à un système de traitement automatisé de données en bande organisée" et "dégradations par un moyen dangereux pour les personnes en bande organisée" contre "le chef du groupe iranien Shahid Kaveh, unité cyber offensive affiliée au Centre électronique et cyber du corps des gardiens de la révolution [CGRI-CEC], contre ses deux adjoints et contre toute autre personne qui serait identifiée." La délivrance de mandats d’arrêt internationaux contre plusieurs Iraniens a également été requise.
Toujours selon Laure Beccuau, l'enquête "a mis au jour, avec l’appui des services spécialisés de l’Etat, un mode opératoire d’attaque caractéristique de cette unité, l’utilisation du farsi et des adresses IP renvoyant vers des terminaux localisés en Iran." L'enquête est également venue confirmer que les hackers ont profité de failles de sécurité sur des appareils des marques Danfoss et Dixell, dont les logiciels n'étaient plus à jour et souvent obsolètes.
	
C’est une attaque inédite par son ampleur et ses effets, menée purement à des fins de sabotage. Cela constitue une escalade assez grave, mais ce n’est pas du tout la première fois que l’Iran s’en prend à nos intérêts par la voie cyber.
Du côté du gouvernement, lundi le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Jean-Noël Barrot, a déclaré : "Je suis en mesure de confirmer que la responsabilité de cette attaque revient au corps des gardiens de la révolution de la République islamique d’Iran. C’est une attaque d’une ampleur inédite et d’une agressivité inédite." Il compte "protester très vivement contre cet acte extrêmement grave" devant l'ambassadeur d'Iran, mais aussi que "nous prendrons des sanctions à l’échelle européenne contre tous les responsables de cette attaque."
Des hackers prorusses s'en mêlent
En revanche, les responsables de la seconde vague d'attaques qui a visé quelques jours plus tard des réfrigérateurs de supermarchés ailleurs en Europe, ainsi que l'EFS en France, restent inconnus. Selon Le Figaro, "en coulisses, diplomates et agents de renseignements français n’ont pas de doutes sur l’origine similaire de cette opération".
Des groupes de hackers prorusses, à savoir NoName057(16) et Z-Pentest, ont pourtant revendiqué cette cyberattaque. Cependant, leurs propos sont à prendre avec des pincettes, car ils revendiquent aussi la première attaque, et tout cela ressemble beaucoup à du simple opportunisme.

articles.title: Over a Dozen Organizations Hit in Qubole Supply Chain Attack
articles.text:
A threat actor used the compromised IAM credentials for an AWS account associated with big-data platform Qubole to steal data from over a dozen organizations, cybersecurity researchers discovered.
The credentials allowed the attackers to assume IAM roles organizations had set up for Qubole’s AWS account and access their AWS environments.
Cross-account IAM roles are normal for SaaS platforms that operate within customers’ AWS environments. During onboarding, customers create a role for Qubole, and the vendor’s AWS account can assume the role when needed, typically via an External ID.
The leaked Qubole credentials allowed the threat actor to assume this role and pull data from the AWS environments of over a dozen companies.
“The doors the attacker used were old ones. Qubole roles were still in place long after companies had stopped using Qubole, and those roles could read nearly all of the data the attacker went after,” cybersecurity firm Sentra notes.
The roles stayed dormant until the campaign kicked off on October 14. They were used until October 26 to enumerate resources, collect secrets and configurations, and access data.
The attacks came from a rented OVH server and the Mullvad VPN, and none of the observed activity originated from Qubole’s network, Sentra says.
“The threat actor used role session names that followed a consistent format of the prefix quiam-, followed by a suffix describing the actions taken. This includes session names such as quiam-enum and quiam-scope-full,” Wiz, which analyzed the campaign alongside Sentra, says.
Following enumeration, the attackers harvested secrets from common AWS storage locations, then used TruffleHog to test the credentials. Next, the threat actor exfiltrated data from the victims’ S3 buckets.
“The threat actor appears to have been opportunistic. Rather than looking for specific data, it read from whatever buckets each role could reach, in some cases downloading entire buckets in a single session,” Wiz says.
The cybersecurity firm also identified an ISO file designed to be remotely booted on victim machines to harvest data, but has no evidence of its deployment.
“Wiz has not identified any ties between this campaign and other publicly reported activity. The targeting and data theft appear opportunistic and do not match typical state-backed priorities; however, we don’t have any direct insight into the motivation of the threat actor or how they may use the stolen data,” the company says.
Wiz also discovered a separate campaign involving Qubole integrations, active between October 8 and October 11, in which customer-owned AWS access keys were tested against victim environments, and in some cases used for compromise.
