articles.title: Robô constrói estrutura no espaço sem controle humano direto pela primeira vez
articles.text:
Um robô conseguiu montar autonomamente uma estrutura em órbita da Terra pela primeira vez na história. O experimento, financiado pela Agência de Projetos de Pesquisa Avançada de Defesa dos Estados Unidos (DARPA, na sigla em inglês) e conduzido por pesquisadores do Instituto de Tecnologia da Califórnia (Caltech), demonstrou que máquinas podem realizar trabalhos de construção no espaço com pouca intervenção humana.
Batizado de Autonomous In-Space Tensioned Reflector Assembly (ASTRA), o projeto utilizou um equipamento robótico para montar uma antena refletora de 1,4 metro de largura. A estrutura foi construída com filme de Kapton, tubos de fibra composta e juntas de alumínio.
Segundo Sergio Pellegrino, professor de engenharia aeroespacial e civil do Caltech e líder da equipe, esta foi a primeira vez que uma estrutura foi construída autonomamente no espaço.
A demonstração representa um passo importante para futuras missões espaciais, nas quais robôs poderão montar equipamentos de grandes dimensões ou até reparar satélites diretamente em órbita.
Como o robô construiu a estrutura no espaço?
- O equipamento foi desenvolvido para manipular peças e posicioná-las corretamente durante a montagem;
- O sistema recebeu comandos dos engenheiros em janelas de comunicação que, somadas, totalizavam apenas 15 minutos por dia;
- Nesse intervalo, os pesquisadores enviavam instruções e acompanhavam o progresso da máquina, que recolhia os componentes, preparava as peças e realizava a montagem sobre uma plataforma;
- O experimento foi transportado pela empresa espacial Momentus, a bordo do rebocador orbital Vigoride 7. O lançamento aconteceu em 30 de março, durante a missão Transporter-16, da SpaceX;
- Apesar de enfrentar alguns imprevistos, a equipe conseguiu demonstrar o funcionamento do sistema. Entretanto, limitações de tempo impediram a conclusão de todas as seções planejadas para a estrutura.
Leia mais:
- Robô humanoide acerta até 90% dos chutes ao gol em testes reais
- Robô humanoide suspeito de assédio é apreendido na Alemanha
- Cães-robôs enfrentam mais de 3 mil degraus em competição na China
Robôs podem construir estruturas gigantes no espaço
O experimento ASTRA faz parte de iniciativa mais ampla da DARPA, chamada Novel Orbital and Moon Manufacturing, Materials, and Mass-efficient Design (NOM4D).
O objetivo do programa é desenvolver tecnologias capazes de viabilizar a construção de estruturas muito maiores em órbita, com dimensões que podem chegar a centenas de metros ou até quilômetros.
Atualmente, equipamentos enviados ao espaço precisam caber dentro da carenagem dos foguetes, estrutura que protege a carga durante o lançamento. A montagem em órbita poderia contornar essa limitação, permitindo a construção de equipamentos que seriam grandes demais para serem transportados já prontos.
Entre as aplicações imaginadas estão antenas de comunicação, grandes painéis solares e telescópios espaciais mais avançados.
Para Pellegrino, a tecnologia também poderá beneficiar projetos de astronomia e astrofísica, além de sistemas de comunicação e futuras estruturas voltadas à geração de energia solar no espaço.
A demonstração ainda está longe de permitir construções gigantescas, mas representa uma prova de conceito importante: máquinas já conseguem realizar tarefas de montagem estrutural fora da Terra com autonomia.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Ring, known for its doorbell cameras, launches a home security drone and an enterprise security robot | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Ring, the Amazon-owned home security company, is launching its own robotics division, with an eye toward automating security at both the home and the office. The company announced Ring Robotics on Tuesday, debuting two new devices that are sure to stir more than a little bit of controversy.
The first new device is a home security drone that users will be able to deploy to patrol their domiciles when they’re out. The other item that the company is launching is a roving enterprise security robot, designed for businesses.
First, the drone. Ring calls the device a “flying indoor security camera” — which should give you a pretty good idea of what it’s supposed to do and how it’s supposed to work. Ring Drone Cam is designed to fly from room to room, inspecting what is happening in a user’s house and, if there’s trouble, to alert them. It has been built to integrate with Ring’s other home security devices, so, for instance, if a Ring alarm goes off in a particular part of the home (say, the back door), the bot will supposedly fly to that location and investigate. When it’s not in use, the drone stays inactive in a docking bay.
The drone shoots video in 2K and it also comes equipped with LED lights so that it can keep watch at night and record video in low light. It can be controlled via Amazon’s Alexa Home Map, and the bot can also be scheduled to patrol the house at specific times — so, if you know you’re going to be out for the night or even on vacation, the drone can keep you apprised of what’s happening while you’re away.
Now let’s turn to Ring Rover Cam. Like the drone, this roving robot can be set to patrol specific routes, at specific times, within the user’s business. The robot streams video in continuous 4K, which is viewable via Ring’s mobile app, and a trigger can be set to automatically record if it detects a human. It also comes with a periscope camera, which can be adjusted to see over specific obstacles, and it includes two-way audio — meaning that, should the remote user need to communicate with a person at the store (be that an employee or a burglar), they can speak to them through the robot.
Ring says that both devices are powered by the same proprietary AI system, known as AI Pilot. The company says this system leverages “specialized vision models, sensors, and cloud processing to see, think, and navigate autonomously.” Both devices, using this software, are designed to develop a detailed schematic of your house or office purely by exploring the space for themselves, the company says.
“Together, it’s like having a guard on patrol who never clocks out,” the company claims of its new devices. “Ring Rover can do a sweep of the floor after close and investigate when sensor trips at 2 a.m. — streaming it all to your phone, wherever you are.”
Automated security is one space the tech industry has never quite cracked. In 2021, Amazon launched its own home security robot, known as Astro. Astro, which resembles Ring’s new robot (the company says that it was inspired to create the bot because of “feedback from Amazon Astro customers”), was first announced as a kind of nebulous domestic helper before being repurposed as an enterprise security product. The device never took off, however, and seven months into the robot’s glow-up as a small business security guard, Amazon put the device out to pasture.
Privacy concerns have long dogged Ring — with critics frequently alleging that the company’s cameras have created unofficial surveillance networks that police departments can (and routinely do) tap into. It seems natural to assume that similar complaints will be lodged about the company’s newest products, given the invasive potential of both.
However, Ring claims that both devices have been built with “privacy and security” baked into them. The company notes that the videos recorded by both devices are protected by TAKE (Throw Away the Key Encryption), which the company calls its “strongest default encryption yet.” It’s unclear whether there will be an option for local video storage. Ring cameras generally record their videos to the cloud.
The Rover is being made available starting on December 16, and it will retail at a whopping $1,000. The drone, meanwhile, won’t launch until next year, on January 27, and will be made available for $270.

articles.title: Google Fi is bringing back multiple cell network support for better coverage
articles.text:
Google Fi is launching a new “super network” that can automatically switch users between two different 5G networks depending on which one has better connectivity. The feature is rolling out starting today on Pixel 9 and newer phones that have Google Fi active on eSIM and have any non-Fi SIMs disabled.
Google Fi is bringing back multiple cell network support for better coverage
Google Fi will swap users between two 5G networks, but only if your phone is a Pixel 9 or newer.
When Google Fi first launched in 2015, users were originally able to switch between T-Mobile and Sprint’s networks. But those two networks eventually became one when T-Mobile acquired Sprint in 2020, and so the network switching stopped there. Jane Harnett, Google Fi Wireless senior product manager, told The Verge that Fi stopped offering the feature because “the wireless landscape consolidated via mergers and limited our ability to offer multiple networks within the US.” (Networking switching has continued to be available internationally.)
Now the feature is returning to the US, with Fi once again hopping between two networks. Harnett declined to share which networks Fi will be working with to make this happen. Google Fi’s FAQs say it currently provides coverage through T-Mobile’s network.
According to Harnett, Google Fi’s new approach to network switching is faster than what it offered before, and uses eSIMs’ ability to connect to multiple carriers at once:
“Previously Fi’s switching was single-SIM switching which could only connect to one network at a time, so your phone had to wait until service dropped completely before performing a slow SIM profile swap into another network without knowing if coverage was actually better there. Fi also tried dual-SIM iterations that required both a physical SIM and eSIM which could be slower to transition.
Now we are back with added networks domestically. We have rebuilt the experience from the ground up for the modern era. With our new switching on newer Pixel devices, your phone keeps two eSIM network profiles on standby at the same time (via MEP technology) and uses the Android OS to monitor live connection quality. It also lets your phone transition faster and more fluidly with minimal battery impact—knowing a better connection is available before it switches.”

articles.title: Windows 11 wird effizienter: Microsoft optimiert RAM-Verbrauch für 8-GB-Systeme
articles.text:
Mehr Leistung für 8 GB RAM: So verbessert Windows 11 den Arbeitsspeicher
Seit August 2026 arbeitet Microsoft daran, Windows 11 effizienter zu gestalten. Damals hatte das Unternehmen versprochen, dass gerade Geräte mit acht Gigabyte RAM davon stark profitieren sollen. Wie genau diese Speicheroptimierung aussehen sollte, verriet das Unternehmen damals noch nicht. Jetzt zeigen sich aber schon die ersten Auswirkungen. Seit dem Update auf Windows 11 26H2 verbrauchen die besagten Systeme deutlich weniger RAM.
Windows 11 26H2: So gut funktioniert die RAM-Optimierung
Den Test dazu hat Windows Latest zunächst mit zwei Windows-Geräten durchgeführt. Eines davon lief noch mit der „alten“ 25H2-Version von Windows 11, das andere mit 26H2. Die ältere Systemversion benötigte im normalen Gebrauch schon etwas mehr als fünf Gigabyte der vorhandenen acht Gigabyte RAM. Nach dem Update auf Version 26H2 sank der Arbeitsspeicherverbrauch auf 3,3 Gigabyte.
In einem zweiten Test wurde Windows 11 in einer virtuellen Maschine installiert. So, als hätten User:innen das System komplett neu aufgesetzt. In diesem Zustand verbrauchte das Windows-System mit dem Oktober-Update von 25H2 rund 4,1 Gigabyte Arbeitsspeicher während des Normalbetriebs. Nach dem Update für die virtuelle Maschine lief das System mit einem RAM-Verbrauch zwischen 2,8 und 3,2 Gigabyte.
In einem Blog-Post erklärte Navjot Virk, Corporate Vice-President of Windows Experiences, wie diese Optimierung zumindest teilweise zustandekommt: „Windows kann jetzt bis zu zwei Gigabyte mehr von deinen aktiven Daten im Speicher behalten, statt sie an langsameren Speicher weitergeben zu müssen. Das hilft dabei, dass dein PC reaktionsschnell bleibt, während du mehr Apps und Browser-Tabs öffnest.“
Zudem werden Widgets auf Windows-PCs mit acht oder weniger Gigabyte RAM jetzt nur noch geladen, wenn sie wirklich geöffnet werden. Dadurch sollen allein 200 Megabyte Speicher für andere Apps und Aufgaben freigeworden sein. In den Fällen, die Windows Latest gezeigt hat, erklären diese Änderungen nicht die gesamte Verbesserung. Dementsprechend dürfte Microsoft auch noch einige weitere Änderungen am Speicherverbrauch von Windows 11 vorgenommen haben, die es nicht in die offizielle Erklärung geschafft haben.

articles.title: Speech Processing Pioneer Bishnu Saroop Atal Dies at 93
articles.text:
Bishnu Saroop Atal
Acoustics and signal processing pioneer
Life Fellow, 93; died 19 August
Atal was an acoustics and signal processing researcher at Bell Labs in Murray Hill, N.J., and later at AT&T’s Shannon Laboratory, in Florham Park, N.J. His pioneering work on voice-coding techniques became the foundation for efficient, high-quality voice transmission over cellular networks. He received the 2013 IEEE Jack S. Kilby Signal Processing Medal for “fundamental and pioneering contributions to speech coding.”
He joined Bell Labs in 1961 as a communications researcher, and his early work there focused on speaker identification technology. During the 1960s he helped develop linear predictive coding, a powerful method for analyzing and compressing speech. LPC is now the most widely used method for encoding speech at a low bit rate.
Atal developed increasingly sophisticated low-bit-rate speech-coding techniques. They included multipulse LPC, which improved the quality of compressed speech.
Bishnu Saroop AtalNokia Bell Labs
He also worked with his colleague Manfred R. Schroeder to develop code-excited linear prediction, a method for producing high-quality speech at very low bit rates. CELP became a foundational technique in modern speech coding, letting digital communications systems carry voice using less bandwidth. The extra efficiency expanded cellular capacity, allowing wireless networks to handle more simultaneous calls.
Later in his career, he led the acoustics and speech research departments at Bell.
The company named him a Fellow in 1994. When AT&T Bell Laboratories split into separate research organizations in 1996, Atal continued his career at the AT&T Florham Park headquarters, and he was named a Fellow the following year.
He retired in 2002 and became an affiliate professor of electrical engineering at the University of Washington, in Seattle. There he continued his research in speech processing, speech recognition, and high-dimensional computing.
Atal was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1987 and the National Academy of Sciences in 1993. He received numerous awards including the 2018 International Speech Communication Association Medal for Scientific Achievement and a 2003 medal from the Franklin Institute.
He received a bachelor’s degree in physics in 1952 from the University of Lucknow, in India, and a master’s degree in 1955 in electrical engineering from the Indian Institute of Science, in Bengaluru. While working full time at Bell he earned a Ph.D. in EE in 1968 from the Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn (now New York University’s Tandon engineering school), in New York City.
Darryl Palmer Jr.
Chair of the IEEE Central Illinois Section
Senior member, 55; died 30 August
Palmer was a dedicated IEEE volunteer, serving as chair of the Central Illinois Section and as the government relations chair of Region 4. He was a member of the IEEE Industrial Electronics Society and its industrial activity committee. He also served as associate editor of the IEEE Transactions on Industrial Informatics.
In 1986, at age 16, Palmer completed a summer internship at NASA’s Glenn Research Center, in Cleveland. He helped develop FoilSim, an interactive educational software program that introduces aerodynamic engineering to preuniversity students.
While studying computer science at Cleveland State University in 1996, he joined the university’s Allen-Bradley PLC lab as a research assistant. He designed hardware and software systems for the Glenn Research Center to collect and process thermal wave imaging data. He also designed software for General Motors’ North American robotic and welding division.
In 1999 he completed a second internship at the research center and helped develop EngineSim, an educational software program that models jet engine design and testing.
For his work, NASA recognized him with a Space Act Award.
In 2000 he earned his bachelor’s degree in computer science and became a software engineer at the Danfoss Drives manufacturing facility in Loves Park, Ill. He worked on embedded control systems for variable-frequency drives and high-power equipment. He also developed sensorless control technology for beam pumps used in the oil and gas industry.
In 2014 Palmer and his wife, Alexandra “Sasha” Goodwin, founded Janus Choice, a health technology platform that matches hospital patients with post-acute care facilities. He served as its CEO until the company closed in 2020.
From 2018 to 2023, he was a lead software engineer at Adept Coalescence, a startup in Rockford, Ill., focused on developing front-end software for control systems. He then worked in Peoria, Ill., as a control systems team lead at Caterpillar, a manufacturer of construction and mining equipment.
Henry Leopold Richter
Telecommunications engineer
Life senior member, 99; died 12 August
Richter was a spacecraft engineer at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, in Pasadena, Calif., before starting his own public safety communications consultancy.
He earned a bachelor’s degree and a Ph.D. at Caltech in 1952 and 1956, respectively. In 1955 he joined JPL as an engineer and supervisor of its new circuit elements group. Later, he was assigned to NASA’s Explorer program as project manager for satellite design, serving as a liaison between the organization’s satellite instrumentation group and its operations and data groups. Since 1958 the program has launched more than 90 missions for physics, geophysics, and astrophysics research.
As NASA prepared to launch Explorer 1 in January 1958, Richter worked with the San Gabriel Valley Radio Club in Los Angeles to set up stations across the United States to track the satellite.
He eventually was named JPL section chief and was responsible for scientific instruments on the lunar Ranger, Surveyor, and Mariner programs. He also helped develop NASA’s Deep Space Network, an international tracking and communications system.
Richter left NASA to become vice president and technical director of Xerox Electro-Optical Systems, in Pasadena, Calif.
In the mid-1970s, he joined the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department as a communications engineer, overseeing the department’s microwave and mobile radio networks.
He later ran a telecommunications consulting practice for more than 20 years. His clients included federal, state, and local government agencies, school districts, universities, and organizations. His work covered strategic technology planning and the design and implementation of public safety radio, microwave, CCTV, and paging systems.
He wrote several books including America’s Leap Into Space: My Time at JPL and the First Explorer Satellites (2015), a personal account of his experience working on the Explorer 1 and America’s space program.
In 2019 the Radio Club of America presented him with its Lifetime Achievement Award for “significant achievements and a major body of work that has advanced the art and science of wireless technology.”
Raymond L. Giordano
Former RCA engineer
Life member, 91; died 19 July
Giordano was an electrical engineer who designed integrated circuits and defense electronics at companies including Harris, Intersil, and RCA.
After earning his bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering in 1956 from the Newark College of Engineering (now the New Jersey Institute of Technology), Giordano joined RCA in Moorestown, N.J., as an engineer. He helped develop a video formatter for the company’s missile and surface radar division, and he taught in-house engineering courses, eventually attaining the rank of senior technical staff member.
Later he developed technologies for General Electric (which acquired RCA in 1986), Intersil, and Harris. He designed the circuitry for Kodak’s Cameo cameras and one of its laser printers.
Giordano was awarded several patents for his designs including a smoke detector chip for Siemens, a speed control chip for Ford, an engine control system for Delco Remy, and a control component for Chrysler.
He earned a master’s degree in EE in 1964 from the University of Pennsylvania, in Philadelphia.
Delano D. Wilson
President of Power Technologies
Life Fellow, 92; died 26 May
Wilson was president and CEO of Power Technologies, a consulting firm in Schenectady, N.Y., that specialized in electric power systems.
He was a director of R&D at General Electric in Schenectady until he joined Power Technologies in 1974 as a principal engineer. He developed utility systems and software for the company.
Wilson authored six books and 65 technical papers, and he held two patents.
Outside of his engineering work, he served on the boards of several hospitals, YMCAs, Rotary clubs, and chambers of commerce.
After returning to his hometown of Great Falls, Mont., in 1995, he volunteered as a court-appointed advocate, a trained community volunteer appointed by a judge to represent the interests of children in foster care.
Daniel I. Amey Jr.
Electronic packaging engineer
Life Fellow, 84; died 12 March
Amey was an electronic packaging engineer, working at several companies including General Dynamics, Sperry Univac, and E.I. du Pont de Nemours (now DuPont). His research interests included connectors, chip packages, and high-frequency materials.
He began his career in 1963 as an engineer in the General Dynamics electronics division, where he designed military electronic hardware including analog and digital support equipment for aerospace applications.
In 1967 he joined Sperry Univac in Blue Bell, Pa. From 1972 to 1981 he was engineering manager of packaging techniques, responsible for interconnection hardware for small and medium computer systems. His work focused on large-scale integration packages, hybrid circuits, connectors, and printed wiring board processes.
He left the company to serve as director of electronics technology at Thomas & Betts of Raritan, N.J. He led research and development of packaging and interconnection products there.
In 1986 he became a director of Elco, an electrical component manufacturer in Huntingdon, Pa., where he was responsible for the design and development of connector and packaging hardware.
In 1988 he joined E.I. du Pont de Nemours as director of its electronics and communications technology group in Research Triangle Park, N.C. He worked on packaging technology development, high-frequency materials characterization, and applications engineering. He retired from there as a research fellow.
Amey wrote or cowrote more than 70 technical papers and held more than 14 patents. He developed courses on electronic packaging and printed wiring technology for education companies McGraw-Hill and Cobblestone (formerly the Center for Professional Advancement).
He received the International Microelectronics Assembly and Packaging Society’s 2004 Wagnon Technical Achievement Award and the Electronic Industries Association’s 1984 Distinguished Engineering Contribution Award.
After receiving a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering and a master’s degree in engineering science from Pennsylvania State University, he earned an MBA from Lehigh University, in Bethlehem, Pa.

articles.title: Así logró China engañar al empresario más poderoso de la IA con una operación de seducción
articles.text:
Así logró China engañar al empresario más poderoso de la IA con una operación de seducción
Jensen Huang, fundador de Nvidia, ha admitido que le fue infiel a su esposa con una mujer que, según EE UU, es una espía
La guerra tecnológica por lograr chips avanzados de IA entre China y EE UU es enorme. Silicon Valley lleva ventaja y EE UU restringe su exportación a China. Para saltarse ese control, en un mundo dominado por la IA y los hackeos, China ha encontrado otro agujero mayor con uno de los trucos más viejos de la humanidad: la debilidad humana. Una aparente espía china, Alice Huang, logró seducir al empresario más poderoso del mundo de la IA, Jensen Huang, fundador de Nvidia y su presidente ejecutivo desde hace 33 años, supuestamente para que vendiera chips por valor de 2.000 millones a una empresa tapadera y quizá influyera en favor de China ante el presidente Donald Trump.
“He sido infiel a mi esposa. Mis acciones la han herido a ella y a mis hijos. No hay excusa para lo que he hecho”, ha escrito Jensen Huang a los empleados de Nvidia. Huang, de 63 años, se casó muy joven con Lori, su pareja de la universidad. Tienen dos hijos treintañeros que trabajan en Nvidia. Es una ironía sin precedentes y la historia tecnológica del año que el hackeo más comprometido haya sido sin usar ni una línea de código.
China ha rechazado este lunes las acusaciones de que Alice Huang trabajara para sus servicios de inteligencia: “Las afirmaciones sobre una supuesta espía china son puras especulaciones sin fundamento y constituyen calumnias y difamaciones”, ha declarado Guo Jiakun, portavoz del Ministerio de Exteriores, en una comparecencia rutinaria. Nvidia, la compañía, también ha anunciado que inicia una investigación sobre esta relación.
Alice Huang se convirtió en 2023 en directora general de una empresa radicada en Singapur llamada Megaspeed, que está en el centro de la trama. Megaspeed surgió cuando 7Road, una empresa china de videojuegos y la nube impulsada por inversores gubernamentales chinos, separó su filial en Singapur y la rebautizó como Megaspeed.
Hay solo un currículum en chino de Alice Huang en internet. No pone su edad, pero sí que trabajó como reportera en varias cadenas chinas de televisión. Una de ellas era Hunan TV, en una provincia de China central. “Nunca he oído hablar de ella”, dijo a New York Post un ejecutivo anónimo de esa cadena. Tampoco hay rastro online de ese trabajo.
Luego fue presuntamente gestora de banca privada, pero tampoco hay apenas evidencia de esa ocupación. Solo coinciden varias fuentes en colocarla en un fondo de inversión en Shanghái llamado Hexi, que pudo haber invertido en 7Road, justo antes de saltar a Megaspeed. Toda esta falta de evidencias hace que surjan las especulaciones, como que en realidad trabajaba desde el principio para el Ministerio de Seguridad Estatal chino, el servicio de inteligencia nacional, y que se inventó una carrera plausible. Pero por el momento son solo eso, rumores.
Cómo se conocieron
No está claro cuál es el origen de la relación entre Alice y Jensen Huang, pero fue, con toda probabilidad, antes de junio de 2024. Aquella noche en Taipéi, Alice Huang dijo una de las frases más inquietantes de su periplo. Pasada la medianoche, en un ambiente “húmedo”, según The New York Times, Alice estaba con un grupo de directivos del sector en un bar con vistas cuando dijo: “Os apuesto a que consigo que Jensen venga”. Y así fue: “Jensen apareció enseguida”, explica Parker Schmitt, ejecutivo de una empresa estadounidense. Huang usó el nombre de pila del poderoso ejecutivo. La empresa de Schmitt, NetThunder, colgó unas fotos en LinkedIn donde se veía a Huang con un chupito de whisky junto a Alice Huang.
Así que ahí ya se conocían y es entonces cuando aparecen meses después en un restaurante de pasta, también en Taiwán. En una de las fotos, ella aparece colocando el brazo sobre los hombros de Huang. Alice Huang colgó varias fotos de sus días con Jensen en WeChat, la principal red social china. Podría ser algo descuidado para una espía profesional, pero hacer algo que un espía nunca haría también puede ser de espía.
Photos said to be shared by Alice Huang (Huang Le) from her own WeChat feed - almost like she was showing off and wanted people to know that she had special relationship with Jensen.
Shouldn’t a spy be more low-key and cautious than this? pic.twitter.com/LtvRwBAjVM
— Vivi (@vivilinsv) November 9, 2026
Nvidia siempre ha negado que Huang revelara información confidencial a Alice. Pero lo que sí ocurrió es que Nvidia vendió chips por valor de 2.000 millones de dólares a Megaspeed y Huang abogaba por reducir las restricciones que imponía EE UU a China. En una entrevista con Bloomberg hace un mes, Jensen Huang dijo esto: “He sido muy claro, aunque compitamos con China, no son nuestros enemigos. Si nos preocupa la seguridad del mundo con la IA, claro que debemos abrir diálogos. Tenemos que trabajar con ellos de todas las maneras”. Huang no necesita de espías para decir eso porque sacaría más beneficios si China pudiera comprar Nvidia libremente, pero ahora que se sabe de la relación, son declaraciones más jugosas.
Last month, I followed Jensen Huang across Europe for an upcoming episode of The Circuit. In light of recent events, we’re sharing some unreleased footage. https://t.co/SHeOy9qbwG
— Emily Chang (@emilychangtv) November 9, 2026
La inteligencia estadounidense se preocupó por el papel de Alice Huang, sobre todo por la capacidad de Jensen de influir en el presidente Trump. El pasado mes de mayo, Trump viajó a China con una comitiva de empresarios. Huang no estaba inicialmente, pero el presidente le invitó a que se uniera en una de las paradas que hizo el Air Force One en Alaska.
La utilidad de una espía que accede a la vida privada de alguien con mucha influencia va más allá de lo que se conoce: ¿Le dijo algo a Alice sobre lo que creía Trump? ¿Tuvo acceso privado a los dispositivos digitales de Jensen Huang? Es probable que Jensen Huang tenga que ir al Congreso —ahora en manos de los demócratas— a explicar todo lo que ocurrió, de lo que quizá aún sabemos poco.
Todo esto, sin embargo, ya se sabía hace un año. Marco Rubio, secretario de Estado, preparó un documento clasificado en primavera para que altos cargos estuvieran al corriente, incluido el presidente, que ya había sido informado. The New York Times reveló la existencia de Alice Huang y Megaspeed en octubre de 2025, cuando todavía no se conocía que tenían una relación romántica. Ya entonces Alice Huang había dejado su presunto cargo en la compañía. Desde entonces no se sabe nada de ella.

articles.title: Mauvaise surprise, Notion découvre que des conversations avec son IA ont été volées chez un prestataire
articles.text:
Votre discussion avec Notion AI est-elle dans la nature ?
Dans un communiqué publié sur son site le 9 novembre 2026, Notion a indiqué que moins de 1 % des espaces de travail pourraient être concernés par un incident de sécurité survenu chez Fireworks AI, l’un de ses fournisseurs.
Si Notion insiste sur l’ampleur limitée de la fuite, le contenu, lui, n’a rien d’anodin pour cet outil de prise de notes et de travail collaboratif très utilisé en entreprise. Les données dérobées contiennent des transcriptions de conversations entre ses utilisateurs et l’assistant IA intégré au logiciel.
Des conversations envoyées à un prestataire pour mesurer l’usage de l’IA
C’est en réalité la chaîne de sous-traitance de l’IA que ce piratage met en lumière. Le point d’entrée des hackers a été Fireworks AI, une plateforme américaine qui fait tourner des modèles d’IA pour d’autres entreprises. Selon le prestataire, l’attaque s’apparente à du « LLMjacking », une pratique où les cybercriminels revendent l’accès à des modèles d’IA détournés.
Notion s’en servait pour proposer des modèles open-weight dans son produit, mais aussi pour classer les conversations de ses utilisateurs avec Notion AI. Ce classement alimentait Insights, une fonctionnalité qui permet aux entreprises de voir comment leurs équipes utilisent l’IA.
Mais voilà, le 9 octobre, Fireworks a annoncé qu’un tiers avait utilisé des identifiants internes de l’entreprise pour lire des variables d’environnement, des paramètres qui contiennent souvent des clés d’accès, sur un nombre limité de comptes clients.
Prévenu de possibles incidents, Notion a coupé par précaution toutes ses connexions avec le prestataire. Le 6 novembre, Fireworks est revenu vers Notion pour signaler que des données clients avaient peut-être aussi été consultées, avant de le confirmer deux jours plus tard.
En analysant ce nouveau lot, Notion y a trouvé des conversations envoyées pour Insights. Pour la grande majorité des espaces touchés, elles ne portent ni le nom de leur auteur ni l’espace de travail d’origine, et ne contiennent pas les résultats des outils, c’est-à-dire les extraits de documents que l’IA va chercher pour répondre.
Ce que les conversations disent de leurs auteurs
Reste que le contenu des conversations peut suffire à identifier leurs auteurs. Notion le reconnaît d’ailleurs à demi-mot en précisant que rien ne relie les conversations à un utilisateur « au-delà de ce que contient la transcription elle-même ».
En d’autres termes, si quelqu’un a collé dans le chat le nom d’un client, un contrat ou une clé API, le texte permet de remonter jusqu’à la personne ou l’entreprise.
C’est pourquoi Notion recommande de « traiter ces données comme si elles avaient été exposées ». L’entreprise ajoute que « si vous ou un membre de votre équipe avez collé des informations sensibles comme des mots de passe, des clés API ou d’autres identifiants dans Notion AI pendant cette période, nous vous recommandons de les changer immédiatement ».
Depuis, l’entreprise a suspendu Insights et a annoncé ne plus passer par Fireworks pour ses modèles open-weight. Les propriétaires des espaces touchés peuvent consulter les données concernées dans la barre latérale de Notion, en passant par le menu « ? » puis « Security incident review », uniquement sur ordinateur.

articles.title: AMD EPYC 9006 Results Are Here and AMD Delivers a Knockout Part Deux
articles.text:
At long last, the day is here. Today, we finally get to share with you our first look at AMD’s EPYC “Venice” series, or the EPYC 9006 processors. Following AMD’s biennial CPU development roadmap, the highlight of the year for AMD’s CPU teams is the launch of the EPYC 9006 processors and the Zen 6 CPU architecture that underlies them. Amid an unprecedented explosion in demand for server CPUs for AI systems driving both host nodes and agentic workloads, AMD is in a commanding position, bringing to market a new generation of even more powerful server hardware right when the industry needs it most. All the while, AMD has ambitions of becoming the undisputed market leader for server CPUs, ambitions that Venice seems primed to help AMD reach.
As far as server CPU launches go, today’s launch is remarkable on multiple levels. Besides taking a look at a wholly new server platform from AMD (socket and all), which would normally be a big event in and of itself, the server boom has turned the CPU development cycle on its head, and now it is a server CPU where we will see AMD’s latest CPU architecture. So along with our first benchmarks of Venice, today also marks our first chance to evaluate the Zen 6 CPU architecture that will be driving so many AMD products over the coming two years – everything ranging from server chips like Venice and Verano to consumer desktops, laptops, and more. There is a lot to unpack with today’s launch.
| AMD EPYC: Generation on Generation |  |  |  | 
|  | EPYC 9004 | EPYC 9005 | EPYC 9006 (SP7) | 
| Codename | Genoa | Turin | Venice | 
| Microarchitecture | Zen 4 | Zen 5 | Zen 6 | 
| Core Manufacturing | 5nm | 4nm/3nm | 2nm | 
| Max Cores/Threads | 128/256 | 192/384 | 256/512 | 
| Core Complex | 16 + 32MB | 16 + 32MB | 32 + 128MB | 
| Memory Support | 12x DDR5-4800 | 12x DDR5-6400 | 16x DDR5-8000 / MRDIMM-12800 | 
| Memory Capacity | 6TB | 6TB | 8TB | 
| PCIe (1P) | 5.0 x128 | 5.0 x128 | 6.0 x96 | 
| Socket | SP5 | SP5 | SP7 | 
| Peak Power | 400W | 500W | 600W | 
With so much to do and so little time to do it all, we are going to have a lot more content to follow. But to get things started, for today’s launch piece we are going to run the flagship EPYC 9996 through not only our agentic-workload-focused AgentSTH V7 benchmark suite, but we are also including bits and pieces of what is essentially a preview of 2027’s AgentSTH V8. For some context, we are going back roughly a decade in server architectures to not just blindly pick up benchmark suites, but to profile workloads on dozens of platforms for inclusion in the suite.
We have lots of numbers for this one and some neat comparison points. The headline feature is that we now get up to 256 cores per socket, a new PCIe Gen6 I/O subsystem, and more than twice the memory bandwidth to go along with a revised Zen 6 microarchitecture and SoC design. AMD is also splitting its lineup into multiple families for different applications with two primary sockets, a return of the -X high-cache parts with Venice-X, and the LPDDR5X Verano. The new series covers a lot more and is by far the most ambitious innovation in the EPYC line since the switch to an I/O die, which allowed the EPYC 7002 to deliver a knockout. This is the Knockout Part Deux.
I also wanted to recognize Ryan, Sam, and Vic for helping us turn this around quickly. We will have Ryan cover the Zen 6 microarchitecture and SoC portion before I take back over on performance. Regular STH readers may have noticed this, but many of our pieces are much longer than they used to be, and doing these reviews has become a team effort.
AMD EPYC 9006 “Venice”: The Story So Far
Over the summer, AMD held a proper unveiling for its EPYC 9006 “Venice” server CPU platform at the company’s annual Advancing AI event. In what has become AMD’s marquee event of the year – and a reflection of the importance of server parts to their bottom line – the company laid out an aggressive plan for 2026 and beyond. Spearheaded by the Venice CPU platform, AMD has ambitions to deliver not only its most powerful and most capable server platform to date, but to iterate on that over the next year or so to deliver a broad portfolio of server chips that covers everything from rank-and-file servers to mighty HPC systems, and of course lots of AI nodes.
Now in its sixth generation of Zen-architecture server chips, Venice is in some respects AMD’s most aggressive design yet. AMD is making heavier use of chiplets than ever before, and the company is now relying on advanced packaging techniques to tie them all together. This has allowed AMD to fully leverage TSMC’s N2 (2nm) process node, their first GAAFET-based node, to the best of their abilities, tapping it to not only devote more transistors than ever to the Zen CPU cores to boost their performance, but to pack in more CPU cores than ever before.
For high-throughput workloads, the highlight of Venice is that there are now up to 256 CPU cores in a single socket, a 33% improvement over EPYC 9005 “Turin” only a generation ago, and with 20% higher IPC and higher clock speeds on top of that. Meanwhile, for workloads where single-threaded performance and latency are more critical, AMD is bringing the 5.3GHz EPYC 9686F to market to double down on Zen 6’s IPC improvements with the highest clock speeds yet for an EPYC server chip.
AMD is keen to tap into the agentic era of computing. And there are a lot of improvements to Venice and the Zen 6 CPU architecture that are going to help them get there. But do not underestimate the chip in other areas, either. AMD has invested in features such as PCIe Gen6, new virtualization and security features, and it has even picked up a software engineering firm in recent months to develop software to replace DRAM with flash memory. AI is certainly the highlight of the Venice story, but it is not the only story.
With any luck, AMD expects that over the next 12 months they will finally reach the point where they capture leadership of the server CPU market. As we saw with AMD’s earnings last week, the company’s data center division is already projecting that its revenues will surpass Intel’s in Q4 of this year. Meanwhile, AMD already holds 46% of the x86 server CPU revenue share, and the company seems confident that Venice will push it above 50% for the first time.
EPYC 9006 SP7 Product Stack: Venice HF Gets a Spec Bump
Alongside its initial summer announcement of the EPYC 9006 lineup, AMD also published the complete specifications for its full stack of chip SKUs. This was for both the high-end SP7 platform launching today, as well as the more restrained SP8 platform that is launching early next year.
As it turns out, AMD was sandbagging things a bit. Whereas their flagship high-frequency chip, the EPYC 9686F, was originally announced to ship with a peak frequency of 5.0GHz, that is no longer the case.
Instead, the 9686F is now a 5.3GHz chip. Making this a notable improvement just ahead of the launch of the hardware, and admittedly a bit of a point of pride (or at least bragging rights) for AMD.
In talking with AMD, the company has found that the final silicon for their big Zen 6 CCD has turned out even better than the company was expecting. Consequently, their earlier SKU stack was a bit conservative, and they can do a bit better than 5.0GHz – and allow the fastest Venice to clock higher than the fastest Turin after all.
So here is what the final, shipping SP7 chip stack looks like.
| AMD EPYC 9006 SP7 SKUs |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
|  | CPU Cores | Threads | Max Boost Clock | Base Clock | L3 Cache | TDP | 
| AMD EPYC 9996 | 256 | 512 | 4.1 GHz | 2.55 GHz | 1024 MB | 600W | 
| AMD EPYC 9966 | 192 | 384 | 4.0 GHz | 2.9 GHz | 768 MB | 600W | 
| AMD EPYC 9846 | 168 | 336 | 3.7 GHz | 2.85 GHz | 768 MB | 500W | 
| AMD EPYC 9756 | 128 | 256 | 4.0 GHz | 3.15 GHz | 512 MB | 500W | 
| AMD EPYC 9G76 | 96 | 192 | 4.8 GHz | 3.4 GHz | 384 MB | 500W | 
| AMD EPYC 9656 | 96 | 192 | 3.7 GHz | 3.05 GHz | 512 MB | 400W | 
| AMD EPYC 9686F | 96 | 192 | 5.3 GHz | 3.4 GHz | 384 MB | 500W | 
| AMD EPYC 9556 | 64 | 128 | 4.3 GHz | 2.75 GHz | 384 MB | 300W | 
| AMD EPYC 9586F | 64 | 128 | 5.3 GHz | 3.75 GHz | 384 MB | 500W | 
Only the EPYC 9686F is getting a specification bump here. The rest of the lineup is unchanged from before. Notably, this means the 64-core EPYC 9586F does not get to share in the gains. So if customers want AMD’s highest clocked Venice chip, they will need to buy the 96-core version.

articles.title: Anthropic Rolls Out Mythos 5.2 With Improved Bug Hunting, Fewer Sandbox Escapes
articles.text:
Anthropic on Monday released Claude Mythos 5.2, the latest version of its access-restricted AI model, and Mozilla says it roughly doubled the vulnerability discovery results of Mythos 5.1 in Firefox.
Mythos 5.2 and Claude Fable 5.2, which was released alongside it, share the same underlying model. The difference lies in the guardrails: Fable, which anyone can use, carries protections against cybersecurity and biology misuse, while Mythos ships without some of them.
Direct access to Mythos is reserved for vetted organizations, which can apply through Anthropic’s Cyber and Life Sciences Verification Programs.
“We’ve worked closely with the Anthropic team all year to harden Firefox with successive generations of Claude models, and each round has left fewer, subtler bugs to find. Even so, Mythos 5.2 roughly doubled the vulnerability discovery metrics of Mythos 5.1 across respective scanning campaigns,” said Brian Grinstead, distinguished engineer at Mozilla.
Internally, Anthropic measures progress with CVE Rediscovery, which gives a model the code of a project from before a known CVE was patched and checks whether the model spots the flaw without help.
In an October run covering 1,829 CVEs, Mythos 5.2 achieved a success rate of 89.6%. Mythos 5.1 scored 78.3%, and Opus 5.5, tested without safeguards, scored 81.3%.
Anthropic also shared results from testers, including a security company that found that one in six confirmed bugs uncovered by Mythos 5.2 had gone unnoticed by every other frontier model it ran.
In a footnote, however, Anthropic noted, “On our own evaluations, vulnerability identification is roughly on par with Opus 5.5.”
Claude Enterprise customers who are not part of the Cyber Verification Program have another route to the latest Mythos. Claude Security, Anthropic’s code vulnerability scanner, now uses Mythos 5.2 among other models.
In Fable 5.2, classifiers stop penetration testing, exploit generation and other risky cyber tasks, and users get a response from Opus 4.8 instead.
Anthropic says these protections are as robust as those in Fable 5.1 but are triggered less often by legitimate work. Early testing showed roughly 60% fewer cybersecurity blocks compared with Fable 5.1.
The company tested how readily the model escapes containment in an experiment of more than 1,800 scenarios. The sandbox contained an intentional flaw, and most tasks could only be completed by getting out of it.
Mythos 5.2 relied on credentials or files that Anthropic had left outside the sandbox in 3.1% of scenarios. That is a sharp drop from Mythos 5.1 (21%) and Mythos 5 (39%), and close to the 3.3% rate for Opus 5.5.
Related: Anthropic Fast-Tracks AI Bug Reports to OSS Maintainers, Taps 11 Firms for OT Security
Related: Anthropic Acquires Confidential AI Startup Opaque Systems
Related: Risks Spelled Out for Anthropic Investors Include Possible Harms From Runaway AI

articles.title: Vol IFT-15 : ce vendredi, le double rattrapage du Starship sera un défi d'ingénierie absolu
articles.text:
Starship 15, le 13 novembre : déroulé complet et double capture, Musk estime le succès “probable”
La date est fixée au 13 novembre et l'heure (française) est connue. À 23h45, SpaceX engagera la manœuvre la plus audacieuse de l’histoire aérospatiale : rattraper les deux étages d'une fusée super lourde tombant du ciel. Elon Musk estime la probabilité de succès de la mission d'essai Starship 15 supérieure à celle d'un échec.
SpaceX s'apprête à franchir une étape cruciale dans l'histoire spatiale. Le régulateur étasunien (FAA) finalisant les autorisations, la firme d'Elon Musk vise un décollage ce vendredi 13 novembre 2026 depuis la Starbase (Texas). Pour ce 15e vol d'essai (IFT-15), l'entreprise ne se contentera plus de tester la résistance et la fiabilité de son monstre d’acier ; elle veut prouver la maîtrise totale de son cycle de réutilisation opérationnelle.
Les essais statiques au sol ayant tous été concluants, les voyants sont au vert pour le plus ambitieux test de SpaceX depuis octobre 2024 et la première capture en vol du booster.
Ship 42 static fires complete. The Starship preparing for Flight 15 performed a full duration, six-engine static fire, and fired a single Raptor engine to simulate a deorbit burn pic.twitter.com/I7Ip89Bmey
— SpaceX (@SpaceX) October 28, 2026
Voici un lien pour suivre le décollage et le vol en direct, prévus à 23h45, heure française.
Vol IFT-15 : une course d'endurance de 22 h et 14 orbites
Contrairement aux premiers — et brefs — essais suborbitaux, le déroulé de l'IFT-15 s'étirera sur plus de 22 h. Le Starship restera en orbite terrestre durant 14 révolutions complètes afin d'évaluer la tenue de ses systèmes embarqués et de son bouclier thermique face à des expositions solaires prolongées et répétées.
Au cours des premières minutes de vol, le vaisseau déploiera une grappe de 26 satellites Starlink V3 opérationnels, confirmant la capacité de la soute du Starship à acheminer d'importantes charges commerciales en orbite basse.
Le déroulé du vol Starship IFT-15 minute par minute
Voici le fil conducteur de la mission tel qu'il a été planifié par les équipes d'ingénierie de SpaceX :
- T+00:00 – Décollage Allumage des 33 moteurs Raptor du premier étage Super Heavy (version Block 3) et séparation du pas de tir.
- T+02:21 – Hot-staging Séparation “à chaud” des deux étages. Les moteurs du Starship s'allument alors qu'il est encore attaché au booster.
- T+06:35 – Première capture (Super Heavy) Après sa manœuvre d'inversion d'impulsion (boostback burn), le booster revient vers la Starbase. La tour de lancement, Mechazilla de son petit surnom, attrape le premier étage au vol à l'aide de ses bras métalliques.
- T+26:10 – Insertion orbitale Allumage de confirmation et circularisation de la trajectoire pour le Ship.
- T+35:01 à T+01:17:40 Déploiement Starlink Ouverture de la soute et largage progressif des 26 satellites Starlink V3.
- T+21:35:57 – Rallumage de désorbitation Après 22 h en orbite, le Ship rallume ses moteurs Raptor pour entamer sa rentrée atmosphérique contrôlée.
- T+22:32:34 – Seconde capture (Starship) Une fois l’entrée atmosphérique effectuée et la manœuvre de bascule finale exécutée, le Ship vient se placer au millimètre pour être attrapé à son tour par les bras de la tour de lancement.
Double capture de Mechazilla : le défi technique absolu pour SpaceX
	
Je dirais que la probabilité de succès est supérieure à celle de l'échec.
Rattraper le booster Super Heavy est désormais une manœuvre que SpaceX commence à maîtriser. En revanche, faire de même avec l'étage supérieur (le Starship) directement à la Starbase constitue une première mondiale théorique extrêmement risquée.
Pour réussir ce pari, SpaceX a revu le design des tuiles thermiques recouvrant le ventre du vaisseau afin de combler les espaces résiduels et éviter que le plasma ne fragilise les structures de fixation lors de la rentrée à Mach 25. Si les deux captures réussissent, SpaceX validera l'architecture 100 % réutilisable de la plus puissante fusée jamais construite ; un prérequis indispensable avant les missions lunaires du programme Artemis de la NASA.

articles.title: 5 887 km en voiture électrique : la nouvelle BMW i3 met 7 heures à Tesla sur la recharge — Frandroid
articles.text:
Depuis l’avènement de la voiture électrique, les records en tout genre vont bon train. Le dernier en date est celui de la YangWang U9 Xtreme, la supercar électrique chinoise de plus de 3 000 ch qui a franchi les 500 km/h en vitesse de pointe, en améliorant le 1er novembre son propre record de voiture de série la plus rapide du monde, avec 503,17 km/h sur une autoroute fermée d’Abu Dhabi.
Loin de ces records de vitesse, BMW a annoncé ce mardi 10 novembre, pour accompagner le lancement commercial de sa berline i3, un record plus parlant pour un conducteur ordinaire : celui du temps de recharge cumulé sur la Paneuropeana.
Ce tracé, lancé par Rafael de Mestre, tient en une phrase : traverser l’Europe d’un point extrême à l’autre, via des étapes imposées, en cumulant le moins de temps possible à la borne. Ici, du cap Nord, en Norvège, jusqu’à Tarifa, pointe sud de l’Espagne. Soit 5 886,7 km à travers 8 pays, sur autoroute, route de campagne et en ville.
Les arrêts, eux, ne sont pas imposés. À l’équipe de choisir où et quand recharger, en composant avec la météo, le trafic et l’état des réseaux. La même équipe de BMW avait déjà fait une autre démonstration avec un iX3 50 xDrive, qui avait enchaîné 1 007 km d’une seule charge entre Debrecen et Munich. Cette fois, la i3 a cumulé 2 heures, 45 minutes et 54 secondes de recharge sur des bornes publiques, soit plus de 7 heures de mieux que l’ancien record, établi en 2017 par une Tesla Model S avec 9 heures et 51 minutes de recharge.
Pour garder les proportions en tête, la phase de conduite a duré 3 jours, 2 heures et 41 minutes, à 79,7 km/h de moyenne. La recharge représente donc moins de 4 % du temps passé sur la route.
Du 10 au 30 novembre, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500 passe à 1 399 € au lieu de 1 899 €, support de lavage offert ! Sans fil, navigation LiDAR 360°, évitement précis des obstacles, tonte des bordures… La tonte sans effort, même pour les jardins les plus complexes.
Précisons que La Chaine EV a réalisé un autre record en 2023 : relier le Cap Saint-Vincent au Portugal au Cap Nord, en Hyundai Ioniq 6, avec 5h57 de recharge.
Une voiture taillée pour consommer peu et recharger fort
La i3 est la première Série 3 100 % électrique de BMW, bâtie sur la plateforme Neue Klasse. Sa batterie offre 108,7 kWh utilisables, pour 814 à 912 km d’autonomie WLTP annoncés selon la configuration. Deux moteurs développent 469 ch et 645 Nm, de quoi passer de 0 à 100 km/h en 4,7 secondes.
En France, la i3 50 xDrive du record démarre à 65 400 €, puis passe à 69 400 € en finition M Sport et 72 100 € en M Sport Pro. La i3 40 xDrive, vendue à partir de 59 900 €, se contente de 300 kW en recharge rapide, contre 400 kW pour la 50 xDrive.
Pour ce record, deux chiffres comptent surtout. Le premier : 12,5 kWh/100 km de consommation moyenne, soit sous la fourchette WLTP annoncée (13,4 à 18 kWh/100 km). Un bon résultat, à relativiser : une moyenne de 79,7 km/h reste raisonnable, et la norme WLTP n’est de toute façon qu’un cadre de comparaison. Le second : 275 kW de puissance de charge en moyenne pendant les arrêts, pour un pic annoncé à 400 kW.
Rappelons que la i3 fonctionne en 800 volts. Pour une même puissance, doubler la tension divise l’intensité par deux, ce qui limite l’échauffement des câbles et de la batterie. BMW annonce ainsi de quoi récupérer jusqu’à 423 km WLTP en 10 minutes sur une borne adaptée.
Côté efficience, le constructeur met en avant un Cx de 0,21, des pneus à résistance au roulement meilleure que le niveau « A » de l’étiquette, des moteurs aux pertes réduites de 40 % par rapport à la génération précédente, et une récupération d’énergie qui gère plus de 95 % des freinages.
Un record qui parle de la voiture, moins de votre quotidien
Ce record reste une opération organisée par BMW avec sa propre équipe EfficientDynamics, la même que pour le trajet de l’iX3. Un seul ingénieur était au volant, suivi par une seconde i3 identique et un iX3 50 xDrive en assistance.
BMW précise aussi que la i3 roulait sur des jantes aérodynamiques de 19 pouces, un choix qui favorise la consommation. Le trajet n’a pas été facile pour autant : dans la partie scandinave, partie par environ 1 °C, la batterie a dû être préchauffée avant chaque arrivée à la borne pour accepter la pleine puissance.
La marque assure que « les voitures étaient strictement conformes à la série », mais les conditions restaient plus favorables que celles d’un trajet du quotidien.
Pour un acheteur, cette moyenne de 275 kW suppose des bornes capables de délivrer cette puissance, et surtout disponibles au bon endroit. Branchée sur une borne de 50 kW, une voiture capable d’encaisser 400 kW ne rechargera pas plus vite qu’une autre.
Le défi consistait justement à optimiser les arrêts, ce que peu d’automobilistes feront en vacances, avec des enfants et un horaire de réservation d’hôtel. D’autant qu’il faut désormais composer avec l’affluence aux bornes, loin de l’époque où les premiers « électromobilistes » les avaient pour eux seuls.

articles.title: Les physiciens ont vu un événement subatomique qui ne se produit qu’une fois sur 10 milliards
articles.text:
Le grand collisionneur de hadrons (LHC) du CERN a beau être un tunnel immense de 27 kilomètres de long, ce qu’on y observe est infiniment petit. C’est le cas d’une particule subatomique dite « de beauté », composée d’un quark down et d’un antiquark « beauté » (aussi appelé bottom). La collaboration LHCb lui consacre une étude mise en ligne le 30 octobre sur le serveur arXiv et présentée au CERN le 3 novembre, qui doit encore être relue par d’autres chercheurs avant de paraître dans une revue scientifique.
Comme le détaille l’université de Cambridge, une équipe d’une vingtaine de physiciens britanniques, allemands, italiens, espagnols et néerlandais, menée par Harry Cliff, du laboratoire Cavendish de cette même université, a obtenu les premiers indices solides de la désintégration de cette particule en deux muons, un événement extrêmement rare qui ne se produit qu’une fois sur 10 milliards.
Mais de quoi s’agit-il exactement ? Lorsque cette particule nommée Bd (ou B0) se désintègre, ce qui se produit environ 1,5 millième de milliardième de seconde (1,5 picoseconde) après son apparition, l’antiquark beauté qu’elle contient se transforme le plus souvent en antiquark charmé, plus rarement en antiquark up. Ce sont des cousins plus légers, avec une charge électrique différente.
À la recherche de l’évènement ultra rare
Seulement, une fois sur 10 milliards, le Modèle standard de la physique des particules prévoit que Bd se désintègre différemment, par une voie très détournée qui rend ce scénario extrêmement rare. À la place, elle produit deux muons, µ+ et µ-, des cousins plus lourds de l’électron, de charges opposées. On nomme cette désintégration « Bd to mu mu ».
Depuis 1984, les physiciens cherchaient à mettre la main sur ce processus, car il peut trahir l’existence de nouvelles particules qui ne rentrent pas dans le Modèle standard.
Le raisonnement est le suivant : si cette désintégration survient plus ou moins souvent que ne le prévoit le Modèle standard, c’est que d’autres particules s’en mêlent : des particules hypothétiques, trop lourdes pour être produites directement par le LHC, mais dont l’influence se manifesterait dans cette fréquence.
La traque avait déjà avancé, notamment en 2015, lorsque les expériences CMS et LHCb, en combinant leurs données, avaient observé une désintégration similaire mais un peu moins rare (environ trois fois sur un milliard) : celle de la particule Bs, qui contient cette fois un quark étrange. Ces mêmes données livraient déjà un premier indice, encore fragile, de « Bd to mu mu », que les analyses suivantes n’ont pas confirmé.
Dans leur article publié par la revue Nature, les deux équipes misaient alors sur la reprise du LHC à plus haute énergie, qui devait à peu près doubler la production de ces particules et affiner les mesures.
Ce qu’a changé la mise à niveau de LHCb
La donne a changé avec une importante mise à niveau de LHCb, l’une des expériences installées sur l’anneau du LHC et conçue pour étudier les quarks beauté. Le détecteur a été en grande partie remplacé pendant l’arrêt technique du LHC, entre 2018 et 2022. Les données récoltées en 2024 et 2025, triées avec des outils d’apprentissage automatique pour écarter le bruit de fond, ont permis de faire ressortir cette désintégration. Le LHC peut analyser des structures qui ne dépassent pas une centaine de zeptomètres (un zeptomètre valant un trilliardième de mètre). En mesurant finement ces désintégrations, LHCb permet de sonder de façon indirecte des distances encore plus courtes.
À ce stade, malgré des concepts physiques un peu abscons, on a compris l’essentiel : détecter cette désintégration relève de l’exploit technique.
Mais à quoi ça sert ? Pour l’instant, le résultat colle aux prédictions du Modèle standard et ne trahit donc aucune particule inconnue. Chaque mesure plus précise de cette fréquence réduit pourtant l’espace où de nouvelles particules pourraient se cacher, et indique aux physiciens lesquelles chercher avec les futurs accélérateurs. Parmi les pistes figurent les particules qui composeraient la fameuse matière noire, ces particules encore insaisissables mais qui seraient omniprésentes autour de nous jusqu’à donner leur forme aux galaxies.
Ces particules encore inconnues pourraient aussi être la clé pour comprendre comment la matière ordinaire et la matière noire sont apparues lors du Big Bang et ont pu coexister jusqu’à nos jours.
Les physiciens devront patienter, car LHCb a enregistré fin juin 2026 les dernières collisions de protons de la campagne en cours, avant l’arrêt du LHC pour travaux. La suite se jouera, toujours au CERN, dans les décennies à venir. Une nouvelle mise à niveau de LHCb, prévue vers le milieu des années 2030, pourrait multiplier par dix environ le rythme de collecte des données, et le successeur du LHC est attendu dans la seconde moitié du siècle.

articles.title: N-able Takes N-central Offline as Researcher Drops Over 30 Zero-Days
articles.text:
N-able on Monday took hosted N-central environments offline in response to a security researcher’s public disclosure of more than 30 alleged zero-day vulnerabilities.
“As a precautionary measure, we are temporarily taking our Hosted N-central environment offline while we take the necessary actions to secure the environment and implement appropriate remediation,” the company said.
While N-central and the related services remain inaccessible, N-able says it has made progress validating the flaws and creating a fix, which should roll out around midday on November 10.
On-premises N-central deployments should also be kept offline until patches are released, the company says.
“N-able Engineering continues to make progress on the N-central hotfix and associated validation activities. The work remains on track with no setbacks, and our teams are progressing as quickly as possible while maintaining the validation required for a safe remediation,” the company said.
N-able also pointed out that it has no evidence that the vulnerabilities have been exploited against its N-central environments.
The zero-day bugs were published on GitHub on Sunday by security researcher Sean Bales and have yet to be assigned CVE identifiers. Bales dubbed the flaws Able2Shell.
According to the researcher, the weaknesses could be exploited to achieve remote code execution (RCE) with ‘nable’ or root privileges, to execute arbitrary commands, create unauthorized administrative accounts, or leak sensitive data, such as configurations and credentials.
Additionally, Bales describes four exploit chains that could also lead to RCE with ‘nable’ or root privileges.
The security researcher released proof-of-concept (PoC) code targeting every flaw and reportedly explained that the zero-days were dropped after N-able failed to patch security defects he previously reported in another product.
